modules.name: eb.caststack.jsonstack
modules.summary: Turn a cast-stack profile's rows into the entries the combat engine runs, and hold them live.
modules.description:
A cast-stack PROFILE is the character's list of rows: what to cast (name, Type, Target) and when (its gates: encounter size, health and power windows, named-only, threat, renew-before-it-runs-out). build() turns each row into an ENTRY - slot order becomes priority (slot 1 = 99), the row's Type becomes its group and tag, its gates become the entry's gates - and holds back, with a reason, any row EB cannot run exactly as written. Nothing is guessed: a field neither the row nor EB's class facts can supply is counted, never made up.

THE ROW (what EB reads from an imported profile, and what you can write yourself): { slot, name, ability, type = "CA" | "NamedCA" | "NonNamedCA" | "Debuff" | "NamedDebuff" | "Combat" | "Heal" | "Res" | "Cure" | "CureCurse" | "PowerHeal" | "Buff" | "NonCombatBuff", target = "@Me" | "@Tank" | "@Group" | "@DPS1" | ... | a name, disabled, isItem, itemName, cond = { Tag = a custom tag, "#" = encounter size, "HP<" ..., ID = renew only when it runs out } }.

THE ENTRY (what the engine reads): { name, ability, group = "dps" | "upkeep" | "heal" | "cure" | "buff" | "item", priority, tags, target, gates, disabled, precast }. A row's custom Tag stays with its entry so setTagEnabled can switch every row that carries it.

How to write a cast stack by hand: 1) list the rows in priority order, slot 1 first, each { slot, name, ability, type, target, cond }; 2) put each row's conditions in cond (the keys are listed under ROW); 3) local result = jsonstack.build({ castStack = rows }, { class = "warden", facts = require("eb.caststack.classfacts").forClass("warden") }) and read result.held - each row it could not run as written, with why; 4) hand it to EB's holder: eb.app.combat.holder.rebind(result) (the switches carry across).

WHAT A ROW NEEDS. A row says when and on whom, so a Heal, Cure, Res or PowerHeal row is built from its own words when EB has no class fact for the ability: its Target, its % (a heal's trigger; left blank it is 80, and the entry says so) and its # (how many members must need it - two or more makes it a group spell). A spell built that way is a single-target one at the default weight, never an emergency heal. The class facts (eb.caststack.classfacts) refine it: a group spell, its weight, a cure's types.

WHAT HOLDS A ROW. A row is held, with its reason in result.held, only when EB cannot run it as written: a * alias target that the profile's Aliases do not define (or the profile has aliases switched off) - it names nobody until an alias is defined; a condition key the cast stack has no rule for; a NonNamedCA row that can never fire; a Type Custom row for anything but Balanced Synergy; an item row that names an adornment's click effect (EB cannot use an adornment by name). Every other condition is read, and means the same on every kind of row (see ROW).

functions.name: ROW
functions.signature: row = { slot, name, ability, type, target, disabled, isItem, itemName, cond = { ["#"], ["HP<"], ["HP>"], ["MP<"], ["MP>"], ["N_HP<"], ["N_HP>"], ["Aggro<"], ["Aggro>"], ["RW<"], ["%"], ID, Named, RD, ["Fervor<"], ["Fervor>"], Sav, ["D<"], ["D>"], MAX, RIE, Tag, ATag, AType, ETag, EType } }
functions.desc: One cast-stack row, the shape build() reads. cond keys: "#" = at least that many mobs in the encounter (members, on a heal, cure or res row); "HP<" / "HP>" = MY health below / at or above; "MP<" / "MP>" = my power; "N_HP<" / "N_HP>" = the mob's health; "Aggro<" / "Aggro>" = my share of the mob's threat (100 = it is on me); "RW<" = renew a ward under this much absorb; "%" = a heal's trigger (the health of the member it aims at); ID = renew only when your own effect runs out; Named = named mobs only; RD = after the row casts it is not cast again for that many seconds (the row's own timer, on top of the game's recast); "Fervor<" / "Fervor>", Sav and "D<" / "D>" = a class's own resource (Fervor, Savagery, Dissonance); MAX = an attack only once the class's stacking effect is full; RIE = an item row only while the item is worn; Tag = a custom tag (the switch); ATag (+ AType "Trigger Only") = cast only while the tag is raised; ETag (+ EType) = held while the tag is raised. A value of 0, "" or false is unset.
functions.notes: A Heal, Cure, Res or PowerHeal row is built from its own Target, % and # when there is no class fact for its ability (see the module description); with the class facts the same row builds as the class's own group spell, with its weight and cure types. Real class abilities have facts in eb.caststack.classfacts; for anything else, record a class module of your own (eb.caststack.jsonstack_facts). A % on an attack row, a # on a buff row, RW< on an attack or MAX on a heal belong to other kinds of row: they change nothing and are noted once. Fervor, Savagery and Dissonance rows wait until the game layer reads that resource.

functions.name: RESULT
functions.signature: result = { entries, held, unknown, skipped, gaps, notes, unused, precast, precastByKey, stealth, prefix, settings }
functions.desc: What build() returns. entries = every built entry in slot order; held = { slot, name, type, why, entry } for a row built but not runnable as written; unknown = rows with no Type or one EB does not run; skipped = empty rows, separators, an @Raid copy of an @Group row, and everything below an end-of-stack fence; gaps = { field = count } that nothing could supply; notes = one line per thing worth knowing; precast = the pre-cast rows; stealth = the stealth openers.

functions.name: HANDLED
functions.signature: jsonstack.HANDLED -> { dps = { ID, "#", Named, "Aggro<", "Aggro>", "HP<", "HP>", "MP<", "MP>", "N_HP<", "N_HP>" }, upkeep = { ID, "RW<", "MP<", "MP>" }, heal = { ID, "#", "%", "RW<", "MP<", "MP>" }, cure = { "#", "MP>" }, buff = { "Aggro<", "Aggro>", "MP>" }, item = {} }
functions.desc: Which conditions each kind of entry reads in its own builder. Every kind also reads RD, HP, MP, N_HP, Aggro, Named, Fervor, Sav and D, so the only key that holds a row is one the cast stack has no rule for; a key that belongs to another kind of row changes nothing and is noted once.

functions.name: TYPES
functions.signature: jsonstack.TYPES -> { CA, NamedCA, NonNamedCA, Debuff, NamedDebuff = dps; Combat = upkeep; Heal = heal; Res, Cure, CureCurse, PowerHeal = cure; Buff, NonCombatBuff, UseChannelerTab = buff }
functions.desc: Every row Type EB runs and the kind of entry it becomes (typeOf(name) answers one of them). Res rows carry the tag REZ, Cure CURE, CureCurse CURE_CURSE, PowerHeal POWER_HEAL, CA CA, Debuff DEBUFF, Combat COMBAT_UPKEEP; NonCombatBuff is a buff refused in combat; UseChannelerTab is a Channeler's Construct's Sacrifice, kept up on your own pet in a fight while the pet's health is at or above the Channeler tab's line.
functions.notes: Type Custom is not in this table: it casts Balanced Synergy only (the whole group casts it on one count) and builds as an attack row; a Custom row for any other ability is held, with why.

functions.name: ALIAS_UNDEFINED
functions.desc: The reason a row is held when it aims at a * alias that the profile's Aliases do not define: it names nobody until one is. Match on this constant, not on the words.

functions.name: ALIAS_SWITCHED_OFF
functions.desc: The reason a row is held when it aims at a * alias but the profile has Enable Aliases off: it names nobody.

functions.name: BLANK_HEAL_PCT
functions.desc: The % a Heal or PowerHeal row gets when it has none (the value EB's cast stack loader fills in): the row casts when its target is at or under it. The entry says so (entry.from.fields) and the build notes it once.

modules.name: eb.caststack.jsonstack_live
modules.summary: The live cast stack: the SAME entries every engine step, and the switches a fight script uses - one row by name, or every row carrying a tag.
modules.description:
The engine reads holder.entries() every step and skips any entry whose disabled flag is set, so a switch takes effect on the very next step and STAYS (nothing rebuilds the stack behind your back). Hold ONE holder per character - in a running EB that is eb.app.combat.holder - and rebind it when the profile is read again: every row's on/off state is carried across by its name.

A switch's on is true (on), false (off) or nil (flip). Each answers true and a line ("2 row(s) tagged 'burn' off"), or false and why ("no cast-stack row carries tag 'x'").

modules.description: EB finds a character's stack in the imported cast-stack profiles it knows about: the JSON profile named for the server and the character, else an older XML save, never another character's. modules.name: eb.caststack.jsonstack_facts
modules.summary: Class facts from a class module: record what a class module defines, index it by ability line, and read a fact with its template.
modules.description: A cast-stack row says what to cast and when; it cannot say what kind of spell it is (a heal's template, single or group, a cure's types, a taunt). A CLASS MODULE can: a Lua function that defines the class's entries on four category managers - M.Heals, M.Dps, M.Cures, M.Buffs - with DefineAbility(def, disabled), Enable(name, { priority }), Disable(name) and, on M.Dps, SetStealthOpeners(openers, freeLines). record() runs a class module against recording managers, so nothing reaches the game, and hands back the facts jsonstack.build takes as opts.facts. A definition whose name starts with T_ and has no ability is a heal TEMPLATE other entries inherit through their baseAbility. eb.caststack.classfacts ships ready facts for every class.

modules.name: commands.accounts
modules.summary: Console commands for your characters: the roster, the mercenary, hirelings, a new character, the daily chores runner, and logging in and launching game sessions.
modules.description: Type them as eb <command> in the console, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to <who> <command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch. login and launch are EB for InnerSpace's. roster, hirelings, createchar, login and launch are for this box only.

functions.name: roster

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (default), status, account or window. Default: list.

functions.desc: Your characters, from EB's own sources: list shows this PC's boxes in their order (the lead marked) and every other character EB has seen, with class and level; status shows who is online now and where; account reads the game's own list of the characters on the account this box is logged into; window opens the Roster window.
functions.notes: No login detail is ever shown: EB reads your logins' safe view only (box ids and characters). account is held until its game read is proven live, and says so; a deleted character is left out. A list that did not read is "could not read", with why - never "no character" (only the game's own 0 says that), and nothing is dropped on it; what did not read for list / status (a box list file that does not parse, the crew ...) is said under the list. Answered by eb.roster.roster. This box only.

functions.name: features

params.name: what
params.desc: nothing: what this character's account has; refresh: read the game's own list now; import: your other bots' files - the AccountFeatures_<server>_<char>.json snapshots and the account-features.json flags; why <zone>: the expansion that zone needs, where that was read and what this account says; forget: drop this character's list.

functions.desc: The account's features - its unlocked expansions and membership unlocks - for the character on this box, in plain words: the expansions it has, the unlocks tied to no zone (a membership unlock, a pack EB's data has no zones for), the expansions it lacks, and its flags (a key your other bot keeps, such as a guild hall teleporter's friends and family unlock). Every trip uses what is kept: a zone of an expansion the account lacks is planned around and the trip says why ("needs Rise of Kunark - not on this account"); a trip to such a zone stops at once and says so.
functions.notes: Kept per character on this PC (eb-account-features.local.json beside EB: never shipped, never uploaded). The game is read on your press only (nothing kept yet, or refresh) - a trip never reads it. Not known never holds a trip back: no list for this character, a list not known to be whole, a zone whose expansion is not known (a dungeon, a classic zone), an expansion no feature name the game gives stands for. A zone's expansion is read from its name (a region or a city carries its expansion's number, and EB's expansion list names that number). EB for InnerSpace reads the game's own list (EQ2:GetAccountFeatures); EB Boxer asks the game (/show_account_features) and reads its answer, held until its live proof. The imports read only those files, under each InnerSpace folder this PC runs EB from. Answered in a task (the answer follows on the console). Answered by eb.features.cmd. Also typed as: accountfeatures, acctfeatures. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> features ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: membership

params.name: nonmember
params.desc: nonmember: only a character that is not a member says it (on a crew line a member says nothing) - a quick look at which characters have lapsed.

functions.desc: This character's membership level, as the game's own Persona window shows it (All Access, Free ...), said on this box's console with what it means (a member, not a member). eb all membership asks every box: each says its own on its own console.
functions.notes: One read of the game's value a press, never on a timer. EB has not read this value in the game yet, so it is held until a proof run lets it out (eb proof open), and the answer says so. A level word EB does not know is said as the game shows it. Also typed as: memberlevel. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> membership ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: mercenary

params.name: cmd
params.desc: summon, dismiss, buff, status, suspend, list or swap. Default: status.

params.name: query
params.desc: summon / swap: words of the mercenary's name, class or kind (every word, any order).

functions.desc: Your mercenary: summon it (one merely suspended comes back), check its buffs, status; suspend the one that is up; list shows your roster as the Persona window lists it (the current one first, each one's class, suspended or restricted said); summon <words> brings up the one mercenary those words fit (its name, class or kind) when none is up; swap <words> puts the one that is up away first, waits the game's minute and brings that one up. Several fitting, none fitting or a restricted one: said, nothing sent. EB never dismisses or hires one from a contact (dismiss says so).
functions.notes: The roster is read from the Persona window's mercenary page (open it once so the game fills it); a roster row is brought up by the line the row itself carries. The roster read, the suspend, the resume and that line go through the gate until their live proof (eb proof open lets them out for a proof run). An instance run alone with merc=on brings up the one eb set ic.mercSolo <words> names (eb set ic.mercBack <words>: the one to go back to when the run, or its queue, ends). Also typed as: merc. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> mercenary ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: hirelings

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (default), run, collect, send, look, stop, band, deposit or auto. Default: status.

params.name: band
params.desc: The harvest level to ask for: ts (your tradeskill level, the default), adv (your level), top, or a number; band / send: a hireling's name first (gatherer, miner, hunter) for its own band or its send on or off; after deposit or auto: on or off.

functions.desc: The guild hall's harvest hirelings (gatherer, miner, hunter), visited in turn while you stand in your guild hall: run takes what each brought back and sends it out again, collect only takes back, send only sends out, status says what each did last, the level groups it offered and when it is due back. look walks to each one, hails it and reads its state and the levels it offers, pressing only its way out - nothing taken, nothing sent - then says which of them are in sight, the band, each one's own switches, the deposit and the auto visit (out of the hall: what each did last, no walk); stop ends a visit under way; band <level> keeps the band every visit sends them out at, band <hireling> <level> that one's own (same: back to every visit's; the line's own band still comes first); send <hireling> on or off: whether a visit sends that one out (off: what it brought is still taken, it is left in); deposit on or off: after a visit the harvest goes in the hall's Harvesting Supply Depot (on unless set off); auto on or off: a visit every 2 hours 1 minute while this box is idle in its guild hall.
functions.notes: EB walks up to each hireling, hails it and answers its talk in its own words; a talk whose words EB does not know is left unanswered and said. One job takes about two hours. The auto visit waits while an economy chore or a walk is under way, in a fight, while this box is played by hand (paused), or when no hireling is in sight (outside the hall), and its next time is kept per character. A crew line never starts a visit on a box played by hand. EB Hirelings shows each one's Send out and its band, and changes them with these words. Also typed as: hireling. This box only.

functions.name: createchar

params.name: spec
params.desc: A class, and a race if you like, for example "warden".

functions.desc: Help making a new character: with nothing after it, the steps at character select and what EB does once the character exists; with a class (and a race), the class checked against the game's own and its archetype.
functions.notes: You make the character yourself: EB types nothing at character select and never presses Create. EB holds no race list, so a race is the game screen's to check. This box only.

functions.name: tasks

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (default), list or run. Default: status.

functions.desc: This character's chores in one place: the chore loops EB has (the overseer's daily round, errands and writs, the trainer, the mercenary, the collections turn-in) and the task lists made in the Tasks window. status says how each stands and what it needs on this box; list adds the task lists; run starts the overnight chores.
functions.notes: run runs the task list called overnight when this character has one (eb tasklist run overnight), else the overseer's daily round (eb overseer run); each says what it does. eb chores is the same command. Also typed as: chores. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> tasks ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: tasklist

params.name: cmd
params.desc: run, stop, status (the default), lists, trigger, triggers (the triggers listed), level, resume or forget. Default: status.

params.name: name
params.desc: The task list, by its name in the Tasks window (any case), then the command's words: run <list> [stagger <seconds>]; trigger add <list> login | zonein [<zone words>] | every <hours> (90m, 1h30m work too), trigger list | on <n | all> | off <n | all> | remove <n> | test <n>; level <list> <min>[-<max>] [adv | ts], level <list> off.

functions.desc: Run a task list of the Tasks window whole on this box, step after step: a quest line (until it ends), an instance run (until it ends), a command (and the chore it starts), a wait. Stop it, see where it is, or list this character's lists. Run a list by itself on login, on a zone-in or every few hours; say the levels a list is for; pick up a list EB went down in the middle of.
functions.notes: A run that stops ends the list (the steps after it wait); a command EB refuses is said and skipped. stop ends the wait in hand and an instance run the list started; a quest line it started runs on (eb ql cancel ends it). eb stopall ends it too. eb all tasklist run <list> runs each box's own list of that name - never on a box played by hand (paused) or with EB stopped; with stagger <seconds> the box it was typed on starts at once and every other box that long after the one before. A trigger is this character's, kept across restarts: login runs when it comes into the world (not when EB comes up again with it already there), zonein when it zones into a zone (any, or one whose name holds the words), every N hours after its last run; it never starts over another run or on a box played by hand (a login or zone-in one is skipped and said; an every-N one waits its turn), and a fight holds it. A level limit holds for every start: a character under or over it skips the list and says so. A list EB went down in the middle of is picked up by itself when EB is back within ten minutes (the step in hand; a wait with the time it had left; an instance step it stands inside of goes on from the nearest step); later EB offers it (resume, or forget). The list called maintenance is the chore an instance run does between its runs when maintenance is one of its chores (eb ic loop <ic> ... maintenance, or the instance queue's run); it is never picked up on its own. Also typed as: task. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> tasklist ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: login

params.name: what
params.desc: A box (its id or character name) with -s <server> and -c <class> if you want them, or <character>:<server>:<class>; boxes, boxes save or check.

functions.desc: EB for InnerSpace: log this session in from your saved logins - the box its launch named, or the box you name. With no word it says where the login is. boxes lists the box list (boxes save writes it in your logins' order); check reads the login form and types nothing.
functions.notes: -s <server> picks that character's login on that server (a character saved on more than one; a short form works: ior). -c <class> logs it in as that class: the session stops at character select, the class is picked from the page's own list after the character's row and before Play, and a pick that cannot go (held until it is proven live, or the class not in the list) is said and Play is NOT pressed - never a login as another class. A launch profile's row (eb autologin) carries its server and class the same way. eb login healer -s ior -c templar. This box only.

functions.name: launch

params.name: what
params.desc: A box, with on x,y,w,h and avoid-primary if you want them; or set <team>. Nothing is every box of the box list.

functions.desc: EB for InnerSpace: open game sessions that log themselves in - one box, every box of the box list, or a whole team you set up in your multiboxing tool (set <team>). A window goes where you say (on x,y,w,h), else where the game puts it; avoid-primary keeps it off the main monitor.
functions.notes: eb help launch lists every form of the line. On EB Boxer the boxes start from EB Boxer's own launcher, outside the game: EB Setup's Play (a character, or Play ticked - one box after another, each logged in before the next starts, each window on the monitor you picked for it, never taking the focus) or its Play ticked shortcut; typed in an EB Boxer game it says so and does nothing. This box only.

functions.name: persona

params.name: cmd
params.desc: open (default), status, as, rules, rule, char, remove, fix, later, gear, bags, noswap, adorn or stop. Default: open.

params.name: arg
params.desc: A class; rule: <server | all> <class> <file | clear>; char: <class> <file | clear>; remove / fix: the rule's number; gear: save, restore or clear and a class or all; bags: the bags' numbers 1 to 6, or all; noswap: on or off; adorn: on, off, recheck, stop or status.

functions.desc: Persona - one character, several classes. open (the bare form) opens the Persona window; <class> (or as <class>) changes the class of the character in the world through the game's own Persona window, the class it leaves keeping what it wears first; status says the classes this character is known in (each with its level), the cast-stack profile each one loads and why, the gear kept for each, and the switches. rules lists the profile rules, numbered; rule <server | all> <class> <file> says which profile file a class loads on one server or on every server (the server by its name or a short form - the first letters of its words, or the start of its name when only one server fits), rule ... clear removes it; char <class> <file> is this character's own rule on this server and wins over every class rule. remove <n> takes a rule away, fix <n> does the same and opens the Cast Stack window, later puts the Profile not found view away. gear save | restore | clear [<class> | all] keeps what a class wears, puts it back on from the bags, or forgets it (nothing is taken off); bags <digits> are the bags that hold persona gear (all: every bag); noswap on | off is Do not swap gear when changing personas; adorn on | off switches Move adornments onto bare gear (on to start), adorn recheck does the same for the gear worn now, adorn stop (or stop) ends the persona chore under way.
functions.notes: A rule takes effect the next time that class loads: the cast stack asks the Persona rules first (a character's own rule, then the server's class rule, then the class rule for every server), then the character's own file (<Server>_<Char>.json), and a character with neither starts from the class sample EB ships for its archetype. A rule whose file is gone is passed over (the next one loads) and opens the Profile not found view; a class rule is flagged as one that hits every character of that class. No file is ever deleted. The rules are the PC's (eb-persona.json beside EB); a character's classes, gear and switches are its own (eb-persona-<character>.json): both private, never shipped. After a class change the old class's worn gear is kept for it, each bare piece of the new class's gear gets the adornments of the character's other piece for that slot (another class's, the same archetype first, never a piece above the level) and the new class's gear goes back on from the ticked bags: a piece the game refuses is listed once and kept in the bags, and the next best piece for that slot is tried. A move a zone or a stop cut short is finished after the next zone. The class change in the world, the class pick at character select (eb login <toon> -c <class>) and the steps after a class change are each held until their live proof, and say so. Answered by eb.persona. Also typed as: personas. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> persona ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: autologin

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (default), show, dry, start, save, delete, set or shortcut. Default: list.

params.name: rest
params.desc: The profile's name, then: start [pause <s>] [login <s>] [only is1,is2]; save <rows> [pause <s>] [login <s>] [overwrite], or save <name> from boxes; set <pc | this> <character set | none>.

functions.desc: Launch profiles: named lists of boxes to log in, kept in the box list's own file on this PC (a row names a box, nothing secret). list (the bare form) names them; show <name> its rows; dry <name> says what start would do and does nothing; start <name> opens this PC's rows, one session a pause apart; save makes one; set picks a PC's character set of your multiboxing tool; delete removes one; shortcut says how to make a shortcut that starts it from Windows.
functions.notes: A ROW is <session>=<box> (is1=main), any=<character>@<server>/<class> (a character saved on more than one server picks the one named; a server's short form works: ior), or <pc>:<session>=<box> for another PC, each optionally followed by lead, on x,y,w,h and fill as eb launch takes them. The class is played at character select. A profile keeps its pause between two sessions opening (pause, in seconds: 20 unless set) and between two logins (login); the words after start's name change that ONE run and are never saved. A row for another PC is that PC's to launch (dry says so); a PC whose character set is named launches that set instead of its rows. save refuses a name that is saved already unless you add overwrite; from boxes copies your box list. Rows go nowhere but this PC's own file beside the EB install (eb-boxes.local.json "profiles"); the Windows launcher reads the same profiles (eb_isx_launch.ps1 -Profile <name>, -ListProfiles, -Shortcut). Over IRC a nick you allow may list them (-List_AutoLoginProfiles) and start one (-LaunchAutoLogin <profile>): that answer gives counts, never a box. eb autologin save raid is1=main lead is2=healer any=Bardname@ior/troubador pause 15; eb autologin dry raid. Also typed as: launchprofile. This box only.

modules.name: commands.broker
modules.summary: Console commands for the broker and buying: price your listings, buy an item or the best upgrade, the shopping list, spell upgrades, and collections.
modules.description: Type them as eb <command> in the console, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to <who> <command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a status line, a chore under way or a refusal in plain words. The Lua behind them is eb.economy.broker (reprice, buy, buyBest, buyMasters, listFromBags, addFromInventory) and eb.economy.vendor (merchant buys). Every buy answers the game's purchase question only for the exact item.

functions.name: broker

params.name: cmd
params.desc: buy, masters, sweep, list, listings, setprice, unlist, coin, repeat, replenish, history, log, status. Default: status. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: buy: the item. list: bags [box], unlisted, reprice, or <box> <index> [price]. setprice: <box> <index> <price>. unlist: <box> <index>. repeat: check, beat, match, smart or unlisted, then the shortest and longest wait in seconds; off; status. history: how many days, or readlog. log: how many lines.

functions.desc: The broker, for a buyer and a seller: buy an item, buy the spell scrolls of a tier (masters), put the bags up, list or unlist one listing, set its price, take the coin out of the sale boxes, reprice on a timer, and keep what was sold, bought and taken in coin.
functions.notes: A price is written 5g, 20s 5c, 1p, or a bare number of copper. eb broker listings names each listing by its sale box and its index there - the two numbers setprice, unlist and list take. Everything that prices uses EB Broker's own rules (its mode, its friends, its sale boxes; the PC's price defaults): eb broker list bags searches each item and prices it FIRST - with no other seller and no default it stays in the bags and is named - then puts it in its default's sale box (or the one you name, else the first with room) and lists it. eb broker list reprice holds a big drop (under half the price) for EB Broker to show you. eb broker repeat beat 60 180 runs the pricing round again 60 to 180 seconds after each one ends, only while the broker window is up; repeat off stops it. eb broker history keeps every sale the game says, EB's own buys and the coin taken, per character on this PC (never a buyer's name); history readlog reads the market's Sales Log page for the sales made while EB was not there, and once that has worked it is read again a few seconds after the broker window opens. eb broker log shows each act of the broker jobs and whether its price read back (OK / NOT SET). eb broker status says what the broker is doing ("broker: idle" when nothing is). Every buy waits for the broker's search to be read to its end (on InnerSpace it is read a few rows at a time) and buys only the row named exactly so - never a longer name that holds the words, and never over the cap; a search that does not read through ends the buy in words, nothing bought. Never a buy at any price: the cap is the price on the line (eb broker sweep 5g, eb brokerbuy <item> <qty> <max>), else the broker's own (broker.maxCopper in EB's settings); with neither, buy, masters, sweep, brokerbuy and eb spells buy are refused in words and nothing is bought. eb broker masters says what it bought, what was already had and what had none under the cap. eb broker sweep [tier] [<min>-<max>] [the most a scroll may cost] [max <n>] takes every spell of this character's book below that tier (Master by default) in the level band and buys its scroll of that tier, one per spell, at most n a sweep; an ability with no tier word is never asked for. eb broker replenish add <item> puts an item on the replenish list: what of it sold since the last count goes onto the craft queue (eb craftqueue add), each sale once - now counts at once, on counts every 10 minutes; an item not on the list (a looted drop) is never asked of the crafter, and a queue that did not answer is said and counted again next time. From a script: eco.broker:buy / buyMasters / listFromBags. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> broker ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: buybest

params.name: what
params.desc: gear, spells or adorns. Default: gear. Default: gear.

functions.desc: Buy the best gear, spells or adornments the broker has for this character.
functions.notes: From a script: eco.broker:buyBest{ slot = ... }. Also typed as: brokerbuybest. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> buybest ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: brokerbuy
functions.desc: Buy a named item from the broker, a number of them, under a price cap.
functions.notes: From a script: eco.broker:buy(item, { count = qty, maxCopper = max }). Also typed as: brokerbuyitem. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> brokerbuy ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: purchase

params.name: cmd
params.desc: add, run, repeat, status, clear, grab, locate, known, go, expect, confirms, stop. Default: status. Default: status.

params.name: item
params.desc: add: the item. repeat: the shortest and longest wait in seconds (60 300), off or status. grab: a name to keep the spot under (else your target's own name). locate, go: the merchant. expect: the item, quoted when it has several words, then how many seconds (5 to 600).

functions.desc: The shopping list (merchant and broker): add an item, run it, repeat its broker lines on a timer, show it, or clear it. Each merchant line is bought one unit at a time under the line's price cap; a "broker" line is bought up to its quantity (what the bags hold counts) from a listing between its floor and its cap; a Krono is never bought. Merchant spots kept on this PC and a walk there: grab, locate, known, go. A buy you make yourself: expect, confirms.
functions.notes: Each character has its own list (EB Shopping List: a broker line's floor is stepped under its cap). The run says what it really bought; a line it could not buy is named and the run is not reported done. eb purchase repeat 60 300 buys the broker lines again a random 60 to 300 seconds after each run ends; repeat off stops it. MERCHANT SPOTS: eb purchase grab keeps your target's spot - its name as the game names it, the zone, x / y / z - in ONE list for every character on this PC; it is refused in words with no target, a player targeted, or a spot that did not read. eb purchase locate <merchant> says the best spot this PC knows: one you grabbed first, then a shopping list line that carries one (EB Shopping List's Grab gives a line its merchant and spot), then a merchant window EB itself opened (each one is kept as it opens), newest first in each; a name is matched in any case, its spaces squeezed. eb purchase known lists every merchant with a spot, where it came from and how long ago. eb purchase go <merchant> walks THIS character there: its zone first by EB's own travel (never the fast-travel map), then the mesh walk up to it; one walk at a time, never in a fight or dead, never while EB's hands are busy or a goal runs, and a crew line (eb all purchase go <merchant>: each box its own way) never moves a box played by hand. eb purchase stop ends the walk, the shopping-list run and what is expected. EXPECTED BUYS: eb purchase expect "<item>" [seconds] is for a buy made outside EB's own buy code (by hand, from a script): while it is expected (20 s by default, 5 s to 10 minutes, as long again after each Yes - a run of buys) EB answers the game's "Are you sure you want to purchase <item>?" Yes only when it names exactly that item; any other question is left for you; a Krono or real money is never Yes (refused at expect, No at the question); an answer this box may not give yet is said and never counted. eb purchase confirms says what is expected and for how long. Nothing is read while nothing is expected. From a script: eco.vendor:buyFromMerchant and eco.broker:buy(item, { count, maxCopper, minCopper }). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> purchase ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: spells

params.name: cmd
params.desc: buy or scribe. Default: scribe. Default: scribe.

params.name: arg
params.desc: buy: the spells, <spell>|<spell>; nothing = the masters list in your settings (broker.masters).

functions.desc: Spell upgrades: buy the Master scrolls you name from the broker, scribe every spell scroll in your bags, then write the ability export again - one run. scribe does the scribing and the export only.
functions.notes: The export (eb export abilities) is written only when at least one scroll was scribed, so a run that scribed nothing leaves it as it was. A buy the proof gate holds back is said, and the scribe still runs. From a script: eco.broker:buyMasters, then the bags' scrolls through the drive's bags.use. Also typed as: scribescrolls. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> spells ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: collections

params.name: cmd
params.desc: fill, list, depot, examine, scan, buy, acquire. Default: list. Default: list.

params.name: arg
params.desc: A collection word (a collection's name or a category; all); examine takes all; buy and acquire take the most a piece may cost (5g, 1p) after the word, and buy needs go to buy.

functions.desc: Collections: list what your collections still miss, scan the journal, add the collectibles in your bags (examine / fill), take pieces from the Collectible Depot, buy the missing ones on the broker, or acquire them all in one run.
functions.notes: scan counts the incomplete collections and what each still misses. buy shows the plan (what the broker would be asked for) until it is given the most a piece may cost and go; a piece already in the bags is never bought. acquire: the bags first, then the Collectible Depot, then (with the most a piece may cost) the broker, then the bought pieces added - every step said; a piece still missing at the end is named and the run is not reported done. The Lua behind it is eco.collections. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> collections ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.combat
modules.summary: The combat commands - eb combat, eb mez, eb cures, eb ho, eb cs ... - what each does, and the engine calls that do the same from a script.
modules.description:
Type them in the console after the console word (eb mez off), send them to the crew with a scope word (eb all mez off, eb to is2 mez off), or run them from a script with reg:dispatch("eb mez off").

EB answers the combat commands itself: each says how the engine stands or what it did. Two are still declared only: eb acs and eb rotation say "not wired yet", and reg:unattached({ domain = "combat" }) lists what waits. The engine behind the commands is scriptable - each command below names the engine calls that do its job - and a script may take over a command by attaching a handler to its id ("combat.<verb>") with replace = true.

EB casts only through the cast stack's rows, only at a mob it may fight, and never at a guard. A cast the game does not take rests before it is tried again, and a hostile ability never goes at a citizen or a merchant.

How to answer a combat command from your own helper: 1) local reg, engine = eb.app.reg, eb.app.combat.engine; 2) reg:attach("combat.mez", function(args) engine:toggle("mez", args.state ~= "off"); return true, "mez " .. tostring(args.state) end, { owner = "my-helper", replace = true }); 3) type eb mez off - or send eb all mez off to the crew. args holds each argument by name, already read as its type (on|off arguments arrive as "on", "off" or "status").

functions.name: combat

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off, or status (the default) - the engine's cast stack and whether it casts. Default: status.

functions.desc: Turn the combat engine's casting on or off, or say how it stands.
functions.notes: Script: engine:setCasting(on) pauses or resumes every cast; eb.app.combat.describe() is the status line. Also typed as: fight. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> combat ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: autohunt

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, status (the default), list (the saved hunt lists), area / route / patrol (how to roam), import (your old Auto-Hunt routes), rename, move (a list into a folder of yours: <list> to <folder>, none = out of it), folders (the lists by folder; list shows them so too) or options (a list's hunt options: options <list> says them; options <list> <option> <value> sets one - pulls (abilities split by |, the first ready opens each fight), group_hp / group_power (no pull while anyone of the group is under that %), pause_chest (no pull while an Exquisite Chest lies within 50 m), delay_after (seconds after a fight; on = 3), prebuff, ignore_collision (kept: EB reads no sight line)). Default: status.

params.name: list
params.desc: The saved hunt list, then its words: kills:<n> and minutes:<n> for this hunt, until:<n>:<item> (until the bags hold that many; _ for a space), until:quest or until:quest:<quest> (until a quest of yours updates), deaths:<n> (0 = no death ends it), group (the others follow this box), reach:<metres> (only what can be reached within that many metres walked on the mesh, the nearest that way first; reach alone = 60), pull:body (each pull is walked at until it comes for this box - never an attack - then back to the camp, or to where the pull began; one that does not come is pulled as before). import: an old route's zone, then overwrite to replace a list of that name. rename: <list> to <new name>.

functions.desc: Hunt by a saved list (the Auto Hunt window's): pull the nearest mob EB can win against - the list's names first, and with no names any mob it may kill, never a guard - rest, move on around where it started, along its waypoints (patrol) or inside its area (area), and stop at its kills or minutes or a zone line. No pull while anyone of the group is down (the dead check rezzes; each box releases by itself after its wait); one up again in another zone is called back; the third death in the group ends it.
functions.notes: Script: facade.brain.isWinnable before a pull, facade.brain.engage(target) and poll facade.brain.clear(); the engine never picks a guard and gives up a fight it cannot win. Also typed as: ah, hunt. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> autohunt ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: cures
functions.desc: Automatic cures on or off: arcane, noxious, elemental, trauma and curse detriments, by priority. With several healers in the crew, one healer cures each detriment.
functions.notes: Script: engine:toggle("CURE", on) and engine:toggle("CURE_CURSE", on) switch the cure rows (they carry those tags); an override's cureScope limits cures to group or single ones; facade.ic.cure(q) cures now. Also typed as: cure. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> cures ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: interrupts
functions.desc: Automatic interrupts and dispels on or off, for the casts and buffs being watched.
functions.notes: Script: engine:setInterruptList({ names }) or engine:setInterruptAll(on) for interrupts; engine:setDispelOn(on) for dispels; engine:dispel(q) strips a buff on cue. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> interrupts ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: rez

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off, status, toggle or now.

functions.desc: Automatic rez of fallen members on or off. When several boxes could rez, one does. now rezzes a dead member at once, whatever the switch says.
functions.notes: In a fight a rez the game takes only out of one (Revive, Supplication of the Fallen) never goes; a cast stack row that names several rezzes keeps the others - the in-combat one is cast - and is held only when every one is such a rez. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> rez ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: ho

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, status (the default), do (start one now), exclude (keep an ability out) or cancel (close the starter that is up). Default: status.

functions.desc: The heroic-opportunity part: on, off, its status, start one now, keep an ability out of them, or cancel a starter that is up.
functions.notes: status also says when this box cannot read the wheel yet (the window reads; the book's wheel icons wait for their live proof). cancel is held back until its live proof, and says so; eb all ho cancel closes it on every box. Script: engine:toggle("ho", on); engine:setHOExcludes({ names }); engine:setHOOffensiveOnly(on); engine:hoCancel(). See eb.combat.ho for what that part needs from the game. Also typed as: heroicop. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> ho ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: mez
functions.desc: Crowd control on or off: mez or root the adds in the mez list's order, renew a mez before it breaks, and never touch the mob being killed or a guard.
functions.notes: The profile's Crowd Control tab drives the mez when it lists abilities: they are the mezzes, top first (one turned off on the tab is skipped; one that is no row of the cast stack is cast from the book), and they never go in the damage pass - the mob being killed is never mezzed. The tab's Enable Crowd Control box unticked holds the mez (this switch stays the master); its Allow Epics box lets an epic add be mezzed. With no list, the stack's rows tagged as a mez are used, as before. Also typed as: cc, crowdcontrol. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> mez ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: embargo

params.name: kind
params.desc: item, ability or tag; list (the default) shows the holds, clear ends them. Default: list.

params.name: secs
params.desc: How long the other boxes hold it, in seconds.

functions.desc: Turn-taking across the crew: when one box uses an item, an ability or a tag, the other boxes hold it for some seconds. List or clear the holds.
functions.notes: Script: engine:tagFor(tag, secs, "Embargo") holds a tag's rows on a box for that long, and puts them back by itself; send it to the others with events.crew or reg:dispatch("eb others ..."). A bare tag (eb embargo <tag> [secs]) raises that tag as an embargo so the cast-stack rows carrying it are held while it is up. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> embargo ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: allow

params.name: secs
params.desc: For how long, in seconds (10 when left out).

functions.desc: Open an ALLOW tag for a while: the cast-stack rows that wait for it (their ATag) cast only while it is up, then it is as it was. Opening it on one box reaches the group. eb tags explains every tag; set a row's tags in the Cast Stack editor.
functions.notes: Script: engine:tagFor(tag, secs, "Allow"). An opener row (an ATag "Trigger Only") does this by itself when it casts. Fan it with a scope word: eb all allow Burn 15. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> allow ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: listen

params.name: tag
params.desc: The cast-stack tag to fire (one word).

functions.desc: Fire a tag now so its LISTEN rows cast: the rows held waiting for it go once, on this box and the group. An opener row does this by itself when it casts; this is the by-hand version.
functions.notes: Script: engine:fireListen(tag, "group"). The LISTEN rows are the ones whose Allow role is "Listen Only" (set in the Cast Stack editor's Tags sub-tab). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> listen ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: tag
functions.desc: Switch one cast-stack tag on or off by hand: its rows are held when it is off. Nothing or status says its state. eb tags lists them and explains each; eb allow / eb embargo raise a tag for a while instead.
functions.notes: Script: engine:toggle(name, on). This is the plain on/off switch; the timed raises are eb allow / eb embargo. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> tag ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: dnc
functions.desc: The do-not-cancel list: maintained spells the engine must never drop. A name puts it on the list or takes it off; nothing lists them.
functions.notes: game.Maintained() lists what you keep up; game.CancelMaintained is the one call that drops one. Also typed as: donotcancel. This box only.

functions.name: stance
functions.desc: A fighter's stance alone: def, off, subtle, or status (eb go also sets the damage rows and the tank).
functions.notes: Script: facade.brain.setPreset("instance" | "openworld" | "afk") sets the engine's presets. Also typed as: ts. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> stance ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: go

params.name: what
params.desc: tank, dps, subtle, heal, swap or status. Any other word is a place: it travels there, as eb goto.

functions.desc: One word sets the part this box plays. tank: a fighter's defensive stance and its threat proc on, its offensive stance and Subtle Strikes off (the stance rows of the cast stack are switched, an effect that must go is cancelled, one that must come up is cast once when its row cannot go out now). dps: a fighter's offensive stance on, its defensive stance and threat proc off; every class's damage rows go. subtle: as dps, with Subtle Strikes on. heal: a priest's damage rows wait, so heals, cures and buffs go first. swap: tank, or from tank back to the damage preset it had last (dps or subtle). status (or nothing): what this box is set to.
functions.notes: A swashbuckler or brigand may tank too: its defensive stance (Fancy Footwork, Blackguard) goes up, its taunts are switched on and go first in its damage list, and its dehates are switched off (cancelled when up). Which ability is a taunt or a dehate is read off its own effect text in the character's ability check (eb abilities export): with none, the stance and the tank's part are done and the rows are left as they are, and the answer says so. Any other preset puts every row back as it was. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> go ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: assist

params.name: who
params.desc: tank, me, a name (in quotes when it has several words) or off.

params.name: follow
params.desc: follow: this box goes with that one too (a camp spot it holds lets go first).

params.name: dist
params.desc: with follow: how many metres behind, 2 to 20; nothing: this character's own follow distance.

functions.desc: Fight what that one fights: tank (the group's tank - the one eb go tank names, else the group's first fighter), me (the box the line came from), a character's name, or off for no one; nothing says who this box assists now.
functions.notes: The one followed stays where it is: on the tank's own box eb assist tank follow follows nobody. eb relay mygroup assist tank follow is the MCP's Follow + assist tank button: every box of your group goes with the tank and fights what it fights. eb assist tank; eb assist off; eb all assist tank follow 3. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> assist ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: rogue

params.name: cmd
params.desc: tank, dps or status (the default). Default: status.

params.name: name
params.desc: tank: the rogue's character. Nothing: this box when it is a swashbuckler or brigand, else the group's first one.

functions.desc: A swashbuckler or brigand takes the tank's part. tank: on the rogue's box its defensive stance goes up, its taunts go first and its dehates off (read off its own ability check), and the crew heals it as the tank and points its hate buffs on the tank at it; typed on another box, the line goes to the rogue's box. dps: every row back as it was, the stance off, and the box that tanked before takes the part back. status: what this box is set to.
functions.notes: Script: engine:loadThreat(name, { fresh = true }) reads the facts; engine:tankRows(holder, true) / engine:tankRowsBack(holder) switch the rows; require("eb.combat.threat").ofEffects(lines) says what an ability's effect lines do to hate. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> rogue ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: encounter

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, status (the default), load, list, fight or fights. Default: status.

params.name: name
params.desc: The encounter file to load. With load and no name: the setup for the named this box fights, else for the nearest named within 60 m (a setup's mob is a part of the named's name, any case). With fight or fights: the boss's name.

functions.desc: The scripted encounter engine: load an encounter file and react to its mechanics (triggers, conditions, actions), list the files, say its status, switch it on or off.
functions.notes: Script: an instance's encounter files (eb.ic) carry the mechanics; engine:setEncounter(name) and engine:addOverride({ match = { encounter = name }, ... }) shape combat for one. Also typed as: enc. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> encounter ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: setups

params.name: kind
params.desc: heroic, raid, all (the default: both) or status. Default: all.

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off or toggle; nothing says how both stand and what this zone is.

functions.desc: Whether your encounter setups run by themselves, by the kind of zone this box stands in. heroic is every zone that is not a raid zone (heroic and solo instances, overland zones, cities); raid is a zone whose name carries the game's raid tag. In a zone whose kind is on, every encounter setup installed on this box is laid on, each while its named is the mob (as eb flag autosetups on does); going into a zone whose kind is off takes them off again.
functions.notes: Both are off until you switch one on, and then EB keeps eb flag autosetups in step with the zone each time this box zones; with both off it leaves that switch alone. A setup you load by hand (eb encounter load <name>) is never taken off. Kept for this character. The MCP's Enable Heroic Setups / Enable Raid Setups lines run it. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> setups ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: raidreact

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, status (the default), list, view, edit, test, rec, grab, import, upload, arm, stop or timer. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: test / on / off: a reaction's place in the list, or its name; timer: <n> <every seconds> [<seconds early>] or <n> off; import: a file's number or all; grab: a detriment's number.

functions.desc: Raid reactions: ready answers to a boss's moves. on and off switch every rule that reacts to a mob (its cast, its emote or its own timer) - or one, by its place in the list; status or list lists them; view or edit opens the Raid React window; test <n> sets one off now (to see what it does); rec starts the fight scanner, where a cast is picked into a reaction. stop holds every reaction that is on until arm brings exactly those back (one switched by hand meanwhile stays as it is). timer <n> <every> [<early>] makes that reaction also go off on its own clock in a fight - so many seconds early, every so often from the pull and from each time it was seen - and timer <n> off takes it away. import lists your old reactions files (each zone's .react files and the older settings XML, read in your InnerSpace folders) and import <n> | all brings their mechanics in, off; grab lists the detriments that landed on you here (EB Scanner's record) and grab <n> makes a reaction (off) to the cast seen just before one. upload says why sharing them through the hub stays off.
functions.notes: Script: react to the boss's emotes and announcements with eb.events (IncomingText, Announcement) and move with eb.nav - see the named-fight recipe. Also typed as: rr. This box only.

functions.name: mobcasts

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, record, watch, or list (the default). Default: list.

functions.desc: Watch and record what the mobs around you cast.
functions.notes: Script: game.MobCasts(radius) lists the casters near you; engine:mobCasting(ctx) is what the kill target casts. Also typed as: tc, npccasts. This box only.

functions.name: helpers

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list, add, remove, on, off, status, window, test, up, down, export, import or chains.

params.name: arg
params.desc: add: the helper in words; remove / test / up / down / on / off: its number on the list (or its ability); export: one number (none: all your own lines); import: the code (none: this class's share file); chains: test <n> for a dry run of one chain.

functions.desc: Class helpers in plain words - "when X, cast Y on Z": when someone drops under a share of health or power, is down, or is feared, stunned, mezzed or rooted; when a buff of yours is not on; when a named, an epic or the mob drops under a share; when my pet drops under a share; when my savagery is at a level; when the fight starts. list numbers them (your own first, then the ones your class tab switches on), add one, remove one by its number, on, off (all of them, or one by its number or ability - kept for this character), test one (a dry run: what it would do now and why, nothing sent), up / down (the order your own are tried in), export / import a share code, chains (the chains made in Tags & Helpers), status (the last one that went out); nothing (or window) opens the Tags & Helpers window.
functions.notes: "when the game says <words>" arms a helper for a few seconds after a line of the game's own holding the words (one line, one cast): eb helpers add when the game says "Fixture flare ignites", cast "Fixture Strike" on the mob. Also typed as: helper. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> helpers ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: classtab

params.name: option
params.desc: An option of this character's class tab (list, or nothing: every one; window: the Cast Stack window).

params.name: value
params.desc: on, off or toggle; the pick, the words or the number it takes; reset.

functions.desc: This character's class tab as EB's own settings. Nothing (or list) says every box of the tab EB acts on: its value, whether it is set in EB, the profile's or the default, and what EB does with it - and what it is doing now (the Warlock's Negative Void up or down, the last rotation call heard). An option alone says that one; an option and a value sets it for this character and the fight takes it at once; reset puts the profile's own box back. window opens the Cast Stack window on its Class tab.
functions.notes: eb classtab potm Fixture call - the words to listen for; eb classtab potm off - not listened for; eb classtab myth reset - the profile's box again. Script: eb.combat.classtab (view, set, read, write, changed). Also typed as: classopts. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> classtab ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: scan

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, status (the default), mark, clear, adds or lines. Default: status.

functions.desc: The fight scanner: record what the mobs cast and what lands on this box (on / off), mark the actors to watch during a fight, or clear the marks. Each detriment that lands is kept with the casts seen just before it, the mob that likely put it on (who cast those most) and its icon on this box (eb canceldet <icon>); a mob that joins a fight already going is an add - adds says the ones seen in this zone. While recording it also keeps the lines the fights here said (a mob's words, its emotes, the warnings on the screen) as patterns - numbers read #, a name of the crew * - and lines lists them; a player's chat and the game's own combat and loot lines are never kept. EB Scanner shows this fight or the whole zone, this box or every box (the crew's scans of the zone, asked over the relay while shown).
functions.notes: Script: game.EngagedMobs and game.EngagedNamed list what is engaged; game.ActorsNear finds actors by a query. Also typed as: fightscan. This box only.

functions.name: flag
functions.desc: The fight's named switches (ae, pbae, encounter, nothreat, namedca, dumbfires, petassist, casting, cures, rez, interrupts, mez, ho, joust, hooffensive, face, dispel, combos, smartae, smartencounter, los, selectivecures, selectivegroupcures, autosetups, chatevents), any cast-stack tag, or one cast-stack row by its name: switch it on or off, or say what it is set to.
functions.notes: joust says who may joust; hooffensive makes heroic opportunities use offensive arts only; face turns this character to face the mob it fights (off by default: one box is often played by hand); petassist sends the pet in; dispel holds or lets go the cast stack's dispel rows (the profile's No dispels box is the same switch); combos is the ascension chain (eb combos, which also goes to the crew); smartae and smartencounter are smart area attacks (the profile's two smart-nukes boxes): smartae holds a point-blank or targeted area row until 2 or more mobs of the fight stand within its effect radius - around me, or around its target for a targeted one (the book's radius, 10 m when it does not say); smartencounter holds an encounter row until its target's own encounter has 2 or more. The profile's "Targets for Smart AEs / Encounters" replace the 2 when the stack carries them. The counts come off the fight's own look; a targeted row's count asks where the mobs stand once a tick. los is the line-of-sight check before an attack (off by default: the game says what it cannot see). selectivecures and selectivegroupcures cure only the types switched on - stcure_arcane, stcure_elemental, stcure_noxious, stcure_trauma for single-target cures, groupcure_<type> for group cures; a cure goes only for a type switched on that it removes (with none, it is not cast at all), a curse cure is not touched, and a group cure's # counts only the members with a type switched on; eb flag lists the types beside each. autosetups lays on every encounter setup installed, each while its named is the mob; off takes back only those (one set up by hand with eb encounter load stays). chatevents switches the coordination's rules that answer a line someone says (a mob's emote is left alone). The profile's own boxes - Disable Ability Collision Checks (ticked = los off), the two smart-nukes boxes with their Setup counts, the selective cures and each type - are applied as its cast stack loads; a switch set by hand this session stays as it is. Script: engine:toggle(name, on) switches a tag and every row carrying it; engine:raiseTag(name, sec) raises a timed tag for allow rows. This box only.

functions.name: cs

params.name: cmd
params.desc: show (the default), profile, archive, share, import, infuse, camp, rcs (re-camp), clear or filter. Default: show.

params.name: arg
params.desc: archive: a name, or crew and a name (the whole crew as one set); share: the share's name; import: a share file's name from the received folder; infuse: all (every box, each its own); profile: a profile's name in this character's cast stack file (any case), or default.

functions.desc: The character's cast stack: show it (the Cast Stack window), archive it, share it, import a share file; camp, re-camp, clear and filter.
functions.notes: The Cast Stack window has three tabs. Cast order: every row with its icon, the words it wears (front, behind, flank, threat, dehate, stun ...), a hover card of what it does, a filter (a chip once = only, twice = hide), separators named after what is under them, + Add from this character's, the group's or everyone's ability book, items worn and in the bags or by name. Other stacks: every character's cast stack file on this PC by server, the archive (this character or the crew, with the AA builds, a name and an expansion; who buffs whom), share files (character names left out unless kept; sending through the EB hub is not open yet), the starter stacks; a row, every row or a whole profile is copied in (Undo takes it back, Save keeps it). AA builds: the game's own AA saves, archived and shared ones, beside the default build with every difference marked; a build goes into the game's AA list under a new name, never over one there. archive / share / import act on that same window (eb.ui.castcreator.cscmd.run); import adds the share as a profile and saves (refused while the window has unsaved edits). infuse swaps every Mount / Mercenary / Familiar Infusion row of the shown list for the infusion of that kind this character holds now (the first row of a kind takes it and keeps its Type, Target and conditions; any other row of that kind goes; a kind it holds none of stays) and saves - refused while the window has unsaved edits; infuse all asks every other box to do its own (eb others cs infuse). The window's Infusions button does the same as an edit (Undo, Save). Script: eb.app.combat.describe() is the stack's status; eb.app.combat.holder.entries() its rows; eb.app.combat.reload() reads it again (switched rows keep their state). Also typed as: caststack. This box only.

functions.name: acs

params.name: xpack
params.desc: A word that takes only that set: an expansion's key, name or initials (RoK, exp04, Rise of Kunark, TSO), a preset (TSOx2), or your own family's name or code. Nothing: the class set in EB's settings when there is one, else the expansion set your level allows (never a preset or your own family).

functions.desc: Put this character's class adornment set on. The set is picked for its class, else its class group, else its archetype, at the highest level its own level allows (a set above its level still goes on when it is the only one, and the answer says the adornments above the level will not). What the bags lack comes out of the Adornment Depot in reach.
functions.notes: eb all acs puts on, on every box, the set of that box's own class. Your own families are made with eb adorn own and in the Class Sets window. Script it with eb.economy.classsetpick (who, candidates, pick) and eco.adornments:applyProfile. Also typed as: applyclassset. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> acs ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: rotation

params.name: words
params.desc: <name> [once | start], stop, status, list, board, save <name>: <abilities>, delete <name>.

functions.desc: A saved rotation order: the abilities this box casts in that order, each through the checked cast (aimed and paced like any cast). save <name>: <ability>, <ability>, ... keeps one (again = replaced); <name> (or <name> once) casts it once, on demand; <name> start goes round and round until stop; list, status, delete <name>; board opens the Rotation Board (every box's rotation: the caster, the ability it casts next, its role and when that is ready).
functions.notes: The board reads this box's next ability's readiness once a second while a rotation runs here (and every 2 s while the board is closed, for the other boxes' boards); the other boxes answer its ask over the crew relay. Script: eb.ui.rotboard.model (the board), eb.combat.verbs_rotation.rotation() (this box's rotation object). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> rotation ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: abilities

params.name: cmd
params.desc: export, research, details, tracker, or list (the default). Default: list.

params.name: options
params.desc: For export, any of: merge (the default: the lines read now replace their old copies, every other line of your file stays), fresh (a new file) or new (only the lines your file does not have yet); dry (say what it would write, write nothing); reread (read the book from the game again first); nopassives, noascension, notradeskill (leave those lines out); tier:<tier> (the lowest tier kept: apprentice to celestial); levels:<from>-<to> (the levels the lines were learned at); quiet (the Ability Export window does not open by itself); only:<name>, <name> (just these abilities, by name or id - the rest of the line). Or stop (end the running export: nothing is written) or status (how far it is).

functions.desc: Knowledge-book tools: export your own ability check (what to export and how, with its progress), research the next tier, an ability's details, a usage tracker, the list.
functions.notes: export writes YOUR OWN ABILITY CHECK: this character's book as JSON, one entry per ability line with what it needs (flanking or behind, stealth, a bow), to data\exports\abilities\<character>.json - EB ships none, and reads that file for the position checks (the fights read the new file at once). It reads the book first when it is not in yet - a few abilities at a time, never beside the read EB makes at login (it waits for that one) - then builds and writes the file a slice at a time. While it runs the Ability Export window (eb windows abilityexport) shows a bar: what it reads now, how many of how many, and Stop - it opens by itself on the box that runs it and goes again a few seconds after a good end (quiet: no window); the console says how far it is every few seconds and what it wrote at the end. A line whose tier, level or book type this box did not read is kept by the filters, and the end line says which reads this box does not have. eb all abilities export runs it on every box, each with its own bar. list, details and tracker answer; research says in words what it waits for. EB reads the book once at start (a minute or so on a full book). Script: game.LoadAbilities (its 4th argument: { step, stop }), game.BookProgress, game.AllAbilities and game.FindAbility read the book; eb.exports.abilityrun runs an export, eb.exports.progress says how far it is, eb.exports.abilitycheck writes and reads the file. Also typed as: abilexport. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> abilities ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: cast

params.name: ability
params.desc: The ability, in quotes when it has several words.

params.name: who
params.desc: on <member>: a heal or a buff on that member.

functions.desc: Cast one ability now, by name, as a button of EB's MCP does. A row of this character's cast stack says what kind of spell it is; an ability that is no row goes only when this character has it in its own book. An attack goes only at the mob EB fights (never a guard, a merchant or a citizen), a beneficial spell on this box, and on <member> on that group or raid member alone. It is paced like any cast of the stack: a cast the game does not take rests before it is tried again.
functions.notes: eb cast "Mending Touch" on Tank. With no fight of EB's own, an attack is refused in words. eb all cast "<ability>" makes every box cast it for itself. Script: engine:castNow(ability, who). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> cast ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: rebuff
functions.desc: Rebuff now: every wait EB was keeping on a buff or an item is forgotten and the cast stack's buffs are cancelled so they are cast fresh, never one on the do-not-cancel list. Whatever buff is down goes out again on the next casts.
functions.notes: Where the game layer holds the cancel back until it is proven, only the waits are forgotten, and the answer says so. A row's own recast delay keeps running: it is the rule you set on that row, not a guess of EB's. Script: engine:rebuffNow(). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> rebuff ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: revive
functions.desc: When this character is dead: release to the first revive point - EB's own release; the death window's paid instant revive is never pressed. It says the release was sent, then "up again" once this character reads alive.
functions.notes: When the character is not dead it says so and does nothing. Until its live proof the release is held back, and it says so (release by hand meanwhile). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> revive ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: autorelease

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off or status (the default). Default: status.

functions.desc: Whether this box releases by itself when it dies. on (the default): solo or a wipe releases at once; with someone else up it waits for a rez first. off: it never releases by itself and waits for a rez.
functions.notes: The wait for a rez is the brain's revive wait (two minutes). In a raid, a group that is all down waits while someone else of the raid is up in this zone. Off never fails a run for it: the box waits, and eb revive releases by hand. Kept per character (the setting death.autorelease); eb all autorelease off sets the crew. Also typed as: releaseauto. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> autorelease ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: deadcheck

params.name: what
params.desc: now (the default), on, off, toggle, status, healers, tanks, send, first, hp, say, popup, scream, speed, test, or a dead member's name (that member only: the Raid window's click on a dead row sends this; a second click on the same body within 4 seconds is ignored).

params.name: arg
params.desc: healers / tanks / say / popup / scream / speed: on, off or status. send / first: a list of words, or default. hp: 0-100.

functions.desc: Every dead member in this zone (the group and the raid) gets ONE rezzer. One that already stands in reach of the body with a rez rezzes from where it stands - nobody runs (a tank in reach too; a healer only when healers go); else the send list's first kind up runs: a dirge, then a necromancer, healers when switched on, a tank last of all - of one kind the nearest to the body, never the window you play. That box runs to the body on the mesh, rezzes from its rez's max range, runs back and brings the member along (eb rezrun). Which body first: a dead healer, then a dead rezzer.
functions.notes: WHEN SOMEONE DIES (eb.combat.deathwatch): a member of the group or raid seen up in this zone and dead now has just died. say on: it is said out loud - "<name> died", then "<rezzer> is on the way to <name>" when a rezzer takes the body, or "<name> is dead, and nobody up can rez them" once a death (off by default). popup on: the Raid window shows it across the top for 10 s (on by default). scream on: EB's own scream plays first and the words wait for it (off by default); your own sound instead: put scream.wav in EB's data folder's sounds\ folder. One voice a PC: however many boxes of a PC see it, the PC screams once (once for a wipe) and says each sentence once. Streamer Mode says no name ("Someone died"). test: the scream, "Your tank is dead, sending your dirge" and the banner, whatever is on. Keys and Alerts' row "A member died" is the same choice (Sound = the scream, Spoken = the words). Each kept per character (deadcheck.say, .popup, .scream). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> deadcheck ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: autotarget

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status, on, off, add, remove, clear, radius, height, rescan or scan. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: add / remove: a mob's name; radius / height: metres; rescan: seconds; scan: on or off.

functions.desc: The kill-first list: the mobs this box fights first, by name, top first. add puts a mob on it (and switches it on), remove takes one off, clear empties it; off leaves the list but fights what the box is pointed at (enable and disable mean on and off, as on every switch of EB; yes / no, true / false and 1 / 0 do too). The scan that finds them: radius (a candidate stands within that many metres; 30 by default), height (within that many metres above or below the box; 0 = no limit) and rescan (a pick holds that many seconds before another candidate takes its place; one that dies goes at once). scan on also looks at mobs not in a fight yet. Said alone, it says the list and the scan.
functions.notes: eb autotarget add a fixture boss puts the boss first; eb autotarget height 8 passes over a mob on the floor above. The height is read only while one is set, at most once a step. Also typed as: killlist. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> autotarget ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: deathsave

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (the default), propose, clear, stagger or auto. Default: status.

functions.desc: The group's death-save plan: who saves whom and at what health, so two saves never go out together. A death save is an emergency heal row on one member. propose makes this box's part: the group's healers (its priests, A-Z - the same order on every box) share one ladder, every healer's first save before anyone's second - with two healers, 30% and 16% for the first, 23% and 9% for the second. A planned save waits for its target to fall to its % (the row keeps its own target). status says who does what; clear drops the plan (each save as its row says, one box a member at a time); stagger <top> <step> moves the ladder; auto on makes it again when the group changes.
functions.notes: eb all deathsave propose plans every box at once; each box plans only its own part, and the parts never meet. Also typed as: saves, deathsaves. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> deathsave ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: autocure

params.name: words
params.desc: <member> [cure | curse | cursed | off], or off, or nothing.

functions.desc: One member cured first, again and again: whenever that member carries what a cure row removes, this box cures them before anyone else. curse: only a curse cure puts them first. cursed: one curse cure on them, then the mark goes. <member> off takes their mark off; off alone takes every mark off; nothing says who is marked. The cure rows, the selective-cure switches and the crew's claim (one box a member at a time) decide as always.
functions.notes: eb all autocure Fixtank curse: every healer of the crew cures the tank's curse first, one at a time by the claim. Also typed as: curefocus. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> autocure ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: canceldet
functions.desc: A detriment on me cancelled, found by its icons - one a fight says to click off. The detriment whose icon (and backdrop, when given) match is cancelled; a beneficial effect with the same icon is never touched. The Target window shows an effect's icons.
functions.notes: Held until its live proof (eb proof: effect:Cancel) - until then it says so and cancels nothing. Also typed as: canceldetriment, canceldetrimental. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> canceldet ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: blockers

params.name: cmd
params.desc: now (the default), cycle, stop or status. Default: now.

functions.desc: The group's AE blockers - each class's own group ward against area damage: a druid's Tortoise Shell, a bard's Bladedance, a swashbuckler's Advance Warning, a channeler's Shield of Blackwood. now (or nothing): this box's own, cast now through the checked cast (eb all blockers: each box its own). cycle: the group's, one box after another, ten seconds apart (druids, bards, swashbucklers, channelers, A-Z) - the box it is typed on casts its own in its turn and tells the others theirs. stop ends a cycle; status says who has one and where a cycle is.
functions.notes: Only a box whose book holds the ability casts it; a class with none says so and casts nothing. Also typed as: aeblockers, cycleblockers. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> blockers ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: aa
functions.desc: The AA slider: what share of adventure XP goes to AA XP - 0 to 100, on (100) or off (0); nothing is 0 (every bit of XP to adventure levels). Sent as the game's own slider line.
