functions.notes: eb all aa 100 sets every box of the crew. Held until its live proof (eb proof): until then it says so and sends nothing. Also typed as: aaslider. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> aa ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: castin

params.name: seconds
params.desc: In how many seconds; or list, or clear.

params.name: ability
params.desc: The ability, in quotes when it has several words.

functions.desc: One cast, later: in so many seconds (600 at most) this box casts the ability - a row of its cast stack, or its book - aimed and paced like any cast, on the member named when one is. What happened is said when it goes. list says what waits; clear drops it.
functions.notes: eb castin 5 "Fixture Ward" on Fixtank casts Fixture Ward on Fixtank five seconds from now; eb castin list says what waits and how long each has left. Also typed as: castlater. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> castin ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: citycombat

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off, toggle or status. Default: status.

functions.desc: No casting or fighting in a city unless called for. Off (the default): in a city zone this box casts nothing, picks no target and attacks nothing; a press by hand still goes, and so does a run that fights (a quest line, a hunt, an instance run). On: it fights in a city as anywhere. Kept per character.
functions.notes: A city is a zone the travel data lists as a city (the bind cities and their districts); a guild hall or a house is none. The city is worked out once a zone. eb citycombat status says whether this box is in a city now and whether it is held there. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> citycombat ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: guards

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (the default) or check. Default: status.

functions.desc: The guard rule on this box. A mob with a guard word in its name or title (guard, sentinel, sentry, watchman, militia, warden, protector) is never fought, pulled or caught in an area attack - except the one mob a quest step or an instance run names to kill (its words, "fifteen Blades guards", name "a Blades guard"), and only outside a city. status: what stands now. check: each damage row of the cast stack and how EB knows whether it hits an area.
functions.notes: An order that is only a guard word ("guards") names nothing, a city never lets one through, and a zone EB cannot tell is a city keeps every guard a guard. An area attack waits while any other guard stands within 30 m. A row is known as an area attack by its AE tag or #, by the book, or by this character's own ability check (eb abilities export) - a row known by none of them may go off beside a guard. Script: engine:orderGuardName(words) gives a run's order, engine:guardRuleLines() / engine:guardRuleCheck() are the two answers. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> guards ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: readycast

params.name: ability
params.desc: The ability, in quotes when it has several words.

params.name: seconds
params.desc: How long to wait for it to be ready.

params.name: tag
params.desc: tag <id>: the crew hears that it went (or that it did not).

functions.desc: Cast an ability the moment it is ready: this box watches its own ability for up to the seconds given (0 = now or never, 10 when unsaid, 60 at most) and casts it through the fight's own cast - a row of its cast stack, or its book - then tells the crew. An ability this character does not have is refused at once.
functions.notes: eb readycast "Fixture Dance" 15. An instance run's step "wait until <ability> is ready on <who> (at most N s), else use <fallback>" sends this to that box (on the group: to every box - the first one that casts it tells the others, who stand down), waits on the crew's answer, and when the ability was not ready in time sends the fallback to every box that has it ready (eb all readycast "<fallback>" 0). The run's own stop ends the wait at once. Script: require("eb.combat.waitready").wait{ dispatch, coord, sleep, now, abort, ability, who, seconds, fallback }. Also typed as: castwhenready. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> readycast ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: rezrun

params.name: who
params.desc: the dead member to run to (irc may follow: EB's crew and EB IRC carry it anyway), stop, status (the default), comeback <x,y,z> <rezzer> [<member>], claim <body> <rezzer>, unclaim <body> <rezzer>.

functions.desc: This box runs to a dead member's body and rezzes them: a long way (25 m or more) first casts its in-combat speed buffs (eb deadcheck speed); out of a fight with Gather Remains in its book and the body within 100 m, Gather Remains first (the body comes, no walk); else a walk on the zone's mesh that stops half a metre inside where its rez may be cast (MAX range: 14 m for a 15 m rez), a quarter second still, then the rez from its own cast stack - the one that gets the most of the group up (a group rez) and reaches, never one tried on this body already while another may go - and the dead box is asked to take it every 3 seconds. Then, in that same moment, the walk back to where it stood.
functions.notes: Sent by another box (a crew line), a rez run is never run on a paused box (played by hand: a box someone plays is the one EB is paused on, never "its window is the one in front"): it is refused there in plain words ("type eb rez now yourself"), and the crew hears it, so the dead check sends another rezzer at once and does not pick that box again for a minute. The dead check itself never picks the window in front or a box the crew shows paused (its Pause switch, in an instance run too). A box that keeps its camp spots in tiers gets every tier back after the run, the top one held. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> rezrun ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: pet

params.name: cmd
params.desc: attack, backoff, assist or status (the default). Default: status.

functions.desc: The pet: attack my target (only a fight that is ours, or an aggressive mob - never a guard, a merchant or a citizen), back off, or assist on or off (EB then sends it at every mob it fights). status says the switch.
functions.notes: Pet assist is on by default wherever a pet of yours is seen, and never where there is none. The same switch is eb flag petassist. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> pet ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: mount

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, toggle, best or status (the default). Default: status.

functions.desc: Mount or dismount: on, off, toggle; status says which. best (the best mount you own) is held back until the game layer's mount swap has been proven.
functions.notes: eb all mount best asks every box for its best mount. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> mount ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: joust

params.name: cmd
params.desc: in, out or status (the default). Default: status.

functions.desc: Step out of melee for a mechanic (out: 25 m along the line from the mob) and back in (in: 3 m), walking on the mesh. status says where this box stands.
functions.notes: It needs a mob in a fight of EB's own, and says so when there is none. The walk is the one mover: a spot the mesh has no way to is not walked to. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> joust ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: ranged

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off or status (the default). Default: status.

functions.desc: The game's ranged auto-attack: on, off, or status. off is sent only while it is on (it stops the melee auto-attack too).
functions.notes: Until its live proof, on is held back and says so. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> ranged ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: position

params.name: cmd
params.desc: behind, flank, off or status (the default). Default: status.

params.name: metres
params.desc: How far past the mob's edge to stand (3 when left out).

functions.desc: Where this box stands in a fight: behind (at the mob's back), flank (at its nearer side), off (where it stands), or status. Unset, the cast stack profile's Move behind mob box decides (behind). The tank - the box the mob is on, or the group's tank - faces the mob and never walks round it.
functions.notes: The walk is EB's one mover on the zone's mesh: a spot the mesh has no way to is not walked to (said once, tried again a few seconds later). It starts only in a fight, with the cast bar idle, and never while this box jousts out or another walk runs (an eb walk, a follow's step, a leash): that walk wins and the fight's walk waits a few seconds. It is re-aimed as the mob turns, and ends with the fight. A spell with a cast time waits while the box moves; instants go on. Script: engine:setPosition("behind" | "flank" | "off", metres); engine:fightPosition() says what applies; engine.positionIntent is the last plan (its spot, or why it holds). Also typed as: pos. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> position ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: beltadorn

params.name: what
params.desc: stun, stifle, mez, fear or medic (a rune of that type), any other word, the adornment's own name, or status.

functions.desc: Put the belt rune a fight calls for on the belt, out of a fight. A word is first the item you named for it (eb set beltadorn.<word> <the item's name>). Stun, stifle, mez, fear and medic are rune TYPES: a rune's type is the end of its name (Adamant Defiance is Stun, Adamant Resolve Stifle, Astral Dominion Mez, Blinding Gleam Fear, Field Medic Medic), so eb beltadorn stun puts on the rune in your bags whose name ends in Adamant Defiance - typing those words does the same. With several runes of the type, the best one this character can wear: the highest level it may use, then the highest tier. Any other word is the one usable item in the bags whose name holds it; two or more are named and refused. Several words are an item's own name. status (or nothing) says what is going on.
functions.notes: Asked in a fight or on the move, the box waits until it is out of the fight and standing still (asked again each second, 10 minutes at most), then swaps; a new ask takes the waiting one's place. The swap takes a few seconds; the answer follows on the console. It is held back until its live proof, and says so. A fight's setup (an encounter or an instance) can call for a word: the box then puts it on once, out of a fight, before the pull. The Adornments window's Belt Runes tab sends the same for your group, an archetype or this box, and lists every rune by type. Script: engine:beltAdorn(word, say); engine:beltItem(word) says which item a word means. Also typed as: belt. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> beltadorn ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: combos

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off or status (the default). Default: status.

functions.desc: The ascension chain: on, an ascension starter that went out at a mob is followed by its combo before the other damage rows (never ahead of a heal, a cure or a rez); off, each ascension row casts where the cast stack puts it. status (or nothing) says how it stands and how many starter and combo rows the stack has.
functions.notes: The rows are the cast stack's own: a row's tag says it is an ascension starter or an ascension combo. Unset, the profile's ascension combos box decides. No second starter goes while a combo is due; the chain lets go when the combo went out, after a few seconds, or when the mob dies. The same switch as eb flag combos; this one goes to the crew (eb all combos on). Script: engine:setAscensionChain(on); engine:ascensionState(). Also typed as: ascension. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> combos ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: fightto

params.name: spot
params.desc: x,y,z (or x y z), then group to bring the others along; status (the default); off.

functions.desc: Walk to a spot in this zone on the zone's mesh and fight what is met on the way - a mob within 20 m that EB can win against, never a guard, a named, a heroic or an epic - then stop there. group: the others follow this box.
functions.notes: It is the hunt's own loop (one hunt at a time: eb autohunt off or eb fightto off ends either), and it ends on arrival, at a zone line, a death, eb stop, or when the mesh has no way to the spot after three tries - each said. group sends eb others follow me from the box it was typed on (eb others follow off ends that); a crew line calls nobody. Script: require("eb.combat.verbs_extra").hunter() is the running hunt (status, snapshot, stop). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> fightto ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: lazytank

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (the default), on, off, allow or unallow. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: on: the camp spot's metres (none: the camp spot it holds, else one here); allow / unallow: a member's name (allow alone lists them).

functions.desc: The lazy tank: this box holds a camp spot and takes back every mob that gets loose on someone who is not the tank - a taunt of its cast stack at that mob, sent like every cast of the fight (aimed at that mob, then back on the kill mob). The member worst off first; an area taunt first when two or more got loose. The tank is the crew's declared tank (eb go tank), else this box. A taunt is a row the class facts call one, or one this character's own ability check (eb abilities export) says raises its threat.
functions.notes: Script: engine:setLazyTank{ on = true, allow = { [name] = true } } and engine:lazyTankStatus() (require("eb.combat.lazy_engine") installs it); the judgment alone is require("eb.combat.lazy").loose(hostiles, group, o). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> lazytank ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: lazyheal

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (the default), on or off. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: on: the reach in metres (20 when none; 3 at least).

functions.desc: The lazy healer: in a fight (this box in it, a mob of it near, or the tank's own crew state says it fights), when the tank stands farther away than the reach, this box walks back within it - to a spot 0.7 x the reach from the tank on the line back to where it stood - by EB's one mover, with the fight walk's holds (the cast bar, another walk, a stop). In reach again, the box's own fight position is as before; out of a fight a follow does the rest.
functions.notes: The tank is the crew's declared tank, else the group's first fighter by name. Where it stands: its own crew state (every EB box says where it is every two seconds), else one actor read at most each second. A box played by hand never walks for it. Kept for this session. Script: engine:setLazyHeal{ on = true, range = 25 }, engine:lazyHealStatus(). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> lazyheal ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: formation

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (the default), on, off, show, melee, healer, ranged, group, role or avoid. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: on: behind, flank or front (the melee's side; behind when none); melee / healer / ranged: a side, then its ring in metres past the mob's edge (3 / 12 / 18 when none); group: 1 to 4; role: <name> tank, melee, healer, ranged or auto; avoid: here [metres], <x> <z> [metres], or clear.

functions.desc: The raid formation: in a fight every box works out its own spot round the mob from what every box sees alike - the group's members by name, each one's role (its class off its own crew state, else the group's read), the tank, the mob and the side of it the tank holds - and walks there itself with the fight walk. The tank holds the front and faces the mob; the melee stand behind it (or on the flanks, or in front), the healers and the ranged on rings further out, every spot 2.5 m from every other one and never inside an avoid circle; a raid's groups take rings of their own.
functions.notes: Script: require("eb.combat.formation").solve(req) -> answers, meta (pure); engine:setFormation(cfg) and engine:formationStatus() (require("eb.combat.formation_engine") installs the fight position "formation"). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> formation ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: pullplan

params.name: cmd
params.desc: scan (the default), plan, body, stop or status. Default: scan.

params.name: arg
params.desc: scan / plan: metres on the mesh (60 when none; 5 to 300); body: a mob's name, then here to fight it where it comes.

functions.desc: Pull planning by the hunt's own rules (never a guard, never another player's fight, never what proved too strong). scan says the mobs this box can reach walking on the zone's mesh - a mob behind a wall is as far as the way round it - nearest that way first, and what was passed over; plan says the order to pull them in (each next the nearest to the one before); body <name> walks at the nearest one of that name in reach until it comes for this box - never an attack - then back to where this box stood.
functions.notes: Script: require("eb.combat.pullplan").reach(actors, me, o), .sweep(list, from) and .body(env, mob). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> pullplan ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: flagrot

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), set, remove, removeall, is, next, clear (sync is the crew's own). Default: list.

params.name: words
params.desc: set / remove / is: <name> [<mark>] (me = this box's character; remove <name> all: every mark); removeall / list: [<mark>]; next: <mark> [<who>] [again] [do <eb line>] - who = names in your order (a|b|c), fighter / priest / mage / scout, a class, group (the default) or raid, by name A-Z (the same order on every box).

functions.desc: Flag rotation, for a fight's "next one takes it": marks 1 to 8, each the characters flagged on it in the order they were flagged, and the one flagged last. next flags the next one not flagged yet on that mark; again starts the mark over once every one had a turn; do <eb line> has that character's box run the line. set / remove one, removeall, is, list, clear every mark.
functions.notes: Script: local R = require("eb.combat.flagrot").shared(); R:isFlagged(name, mark), R:list(mark), R:last(mark), R:next(mark, candidates, { again = true }). Also typed as: flagrotation. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> flagrot ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: intent

params.name: cmd
params.desc: fire (the default: eb intent <name> fires it), save, list, status, delete (go is what a fire sends the other boxes). Default: fire.

functions.desc: Intents: a named list of abilities for one job (a burn, a group ward, a big heal). Fired, the first box of its scope with one of them ready casts it: the list's earliest ability any box has ready, cast by one box only.
functions.notes: Script: require("eb.combat.intents").pick(engine, abilities) -> place, ability (this box's earliest ready one). Also typed as: intents. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> intent ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: npccast

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (the default), on, off, toggle, list or reload. Default: status.

params.name: words
params.desc: list: a zone's name (nothing: this zone).

functions.desc: The mobs' cast lists, answered in a fight: per zone, the mobs to watch and what to do when one of them starts a listed spell - the lists shipped in your InnerSpace scripts and your own (read only; yours deep-merged over the shipped: a mob or a spell set to false drops it, noMerge keeps yours alone). on / off (kept for this character; off by default), status, list [<zone>] (each mob and spell in words: which are interrupted, which run lines), reload.
functions.notes: Script: require("eb.combat.npccast").load(files, { <InnerSpace folder> }, zone) -> the merged list; .find(list, mob, castId). Also typed as: castlists. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> npccast ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: cancel

params.name: spell
params.desc: The spell's name as the game shows it (no quotes needed).

functions.desc: Cancel a spell of yours that is up now (a stance, a toggle, a buff), by its name, any rank.
functions.notes: unbuff is the same. Only a cancel the game took is said as done; a spell that is not up says so. On EB for InnerSpace the game's cancel waits for its live proof: until then it says so and cancels nothing (eb proof evidence lets it out for the session). A box played by hand is left alone. Also typed as: unbuff. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> cancel ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: tagfor

params.name: tag
params.desc: The tag, one word (in quotes when it has several).

params.name: how
params.desc: embargo (the default) or allow. Default: embargo.

functions.desc: A cast-stack tag for a while: embargo holds back the rows that carry it, allow lets the rows that wait for it go - for so many seconds, then it is as it was.
functions.notes: eb all tagfor Burn 30 allow lets every box's Burn rows go for 30 seconds. eb flag <tag> off holds a tag back until it is switched on again. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> tagfor ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: curereq

params.name: cmd
params.desc: cure, curse, group, cancel, clear or status (the default). Default: status.

params.name: rest
params.desc: The member, then kinds, count <n>, secs <s>, tag <t>; for cancel the member or the tag.

functions.desc: Cure requests: ask this box's curers for a cure that gives up after a while. cure <member> [kinds]: while they carry a kind named (none named: arcane, elemental, noxious and trauma; curse; confrontfear = Confront Fear on them once), the first ready cure row that removes it goes on them - a single-target row first, else a group one - until they carry none. curse <member>: the same for a curse. group [kinds] [count <n>]: the group cure once, when at least n of the group (you included; 1 if not said) carry a kind named, each kind counted on its own - never on a guess. secs <s> gives up after that long (8 if not said, at most 300); tag <t> names it. cancel <member or tag> drops their requests, clear drops them all, status (or nothing) lists the live ones and the last few that ended.
functions.notes: A request goes past the cures switch (eb cures off) - asked for, it is cast - but never while the box is dead or paused, and never on top of a cast bar; the crew's claim still gives each cure to one box. eb all curereq group count 3 secs 10 tag wave: every curer of the crew casts its group cure once three of you carry a detriment of one kind, for ten seconds. A new request for the same member (or a group one with the same tag) replaces the old one. Also typed as: curerequest. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> curereq ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.coord
modules.summary: Coordination from the console: the ability tags of a cast stack, the claim arbiter that makes one box cure or rez, and the plain-language rules.
modules.description: The same engines a script drives through eb.coord.rules and eb.coord.arbiter. EB starts the coordination on every box, so all three commands answer.

functions.name: tags

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (default) or set. The other words of the schema (add, remove, sync, cs, check, auto, backup, restore, status) show the list; the Tags & Helpers window is where tags are edited. Default: list.

params.name: arg
params.desc: For set: the tag and on or off, for example "BURN off".

functions.desc: The ability tags the cast stack's rows carry: list them with their switch (the default), or set one on or off - every row that carries the tag switches together.
functions.notes: eb.coord.tagimport turns a cast stack's tags into rules from a script. Also typed as: tm, tagmanager. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> tags ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: claim

params.name: action
params.desc: The action to release: cure, rez, groupcure ... (nothing: every claim).

functions.desc: Show who holds a claim (the cure, the rez, the group action), or release this box's claims.
functions.notes: Answers "claims: none open" when nobody holds one. arb:statusOf and arb:list read the same from a script. This box only.

functions.name: rules

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (default), add, edit, remove, enable, disable, show, status, fired, reload, import, fire, run, lift, words or builder. Default: list.

params.name: arg
params.desc: The rule, its id, a tag (fire), what to lift (a tag, an ability or all), or for add and edit the rule's words, for example: when=cast who=@tank ability=Rescue then do=assist for=group.

functions.desc: Rules in plain words: when <something happens> do <something> for <who>. eb rules lists them, one sentence each, with what is wrong where a rule has a typo; add makes one, edit changes its fields, remove, enable and disable switch it, show prints one with its fields, status says what the service holds (rules, claims, holds), fired says what happened last, reload reads the saved file again, import turns this character's cast-stack tags into rules, fire sets a tag off by hand, run sets a rule off now, lift lifts a hold, words lists the words a rule may use, and builder opens the Coordination window.
functions.notes: when=landed ability=<ability> - a cast of THIS box has landed: cast to the end of its bar with its recast running (one readiness read), an instant on its recast a moment after it went, or its line on the target in the fight's own look; an interrupted or refused cast never lands. A chain's step that follows "once it has landed" waits on this (Tags & Helpers, the Chains tab); "right after it is cast" goes at the send. eb helpers chains shows each chain's last run: when each step was sent and when it landed. This box only.

functions.name: chain

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), show, save, run, stop, resume, status or delete. Default: list.

params.name: words
params.desc: show / run / delete: <name>; save: <name>: <step> | <step> | ...; resume: <name> [at <checkpoint>]; stop: [<name>].

functions.desc: Chains: step lists run beside the fight, one step a tick - cast an ability, wait, wait until a condition holds, stop unless a condition holds, say a line, fire a coordination tag, run an eb command, keep a checkpoint. save keeps one, run starts it, stop ends it (or every one), resume starts it again after the last checkpoint it passed or the one named, status says what runs and what it waits for, show its steps, delete.
functions.notes: Script: local C = require("eb.combat.verbs_chain").runner; C.run(name, require("eb.coord.chainsteps").parse(text)); C.stop(name); C.snapshot(). Also typed as: chains. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> chain ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.core
modules.summary: The commands every box answers: help, status, stop, end, pause, resume, afk and reload - typed in the console as eb <command>, sent to the crew as eb all <command>, or run from a script with eb.dispatch("eb <command>").
modules.description:
Type a command after the console word: eb status. Put a crew word in front to send it: eb all pause (every box, this one too), eb others pause (every box but this one), eb to is2 pause (just box is2; who may also be a character, a class or an archetype). A line that reaches a box from the crew runs there and is never sent on.

How to drive EB from a script: 1. local ok, text = eb.dispatch("eb pause") runs a line exactly as if it was typed (eb.app.dispatch). 2. Read the answer text; ok is false with a plain reason for an unknown word, a bad argument, a call EB has not proven in the game yet (it says so) or a command that is not answered on this box yet. 3. eb help lists every domain; eb help <command> prints its usage, its arguments and whether the crew may be sent it.

EB for InnerSpace answers one more console word before the commands: eb proof, the proof gate. EB sends the game only members and commands it has proven to work; a call that is held back says "held back until it is proven live" and answers false. eb proof (or eb proof <mode>) shows or sets the mode: tested (the default: only what is proven), evidence (also what working scripts are known to use) or open (everything, for a proof run, with the console watched for errors). eb proof alone says the mode and how much waits for a live proof; eb proof list [<word>] lists the steps that wait, eb proof probe <id> runs one of them and eb proof last shows the last answer. eb gate is not this: it opens a door (eb door is the same word).

functions.name: help

params.name: topic
params.desc: A domain (core, nav, combat ...) or a command; nothing lists the domains.

functions.desc: Print the help: with no topic the command domains, with a domain its commands, with a command its usage line, its arguments, other spellings and whether it can be sent to the crew.
functions.notes: EB Help (the window eb help opens) also has How do I... - the common jobs step by step, which window, which tab, what to type, the window one click away (EB Main's How do I... button opens it there) -, New this week (what the last patch added, each with a line to try), Window buttons (each EB window's own presses, pressed from Help; what writes your files, handles logins or keys or runs any line it is handed stays out and says why) and Script reads and calls (what a script can read and call, made from this reference). Enter in its search opens the first match; Enter in a Try it field runs the line, Esc there goes back to the list. Also typed as: h, ?. This box only.

functions.name: status

params.name: what
params.desc: bot, crew, goal, nav, combat or patch. Default: bot.

functions.desc: Print this box's state. bot (the default) is the version, the target, what came up at start and what did not, then the crew, combat, instance and brain lines; crew is every box this one hears; goal the instance runner and the brain; nav the walker; combat the engine; patch the quick live read after a game patch - PASS, FAIL or NOTE for the build gate, name, level, health, power, a position that follows you, the zone, the target, the actors around, the server, then the reads with no value on this build. It only reads.
functions.notes: Also typed as: s. This box only.

functions.name: stop
functions.desc: The kill switch. Typed on this box's console, eb stop ends EB on this box. Sent to the crew (eb all stop) or typed as eb stopall, every box it reaches halts its brain: quests, instances, walks and goals stop, while the combat engine still keeps the character alive. eb resume starts again.
functions.notes: Also typed as: stopall, abort. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> stop ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: freeze
functions.desc: Everything stops at once and stays stopped: the walk, the follow, a run or a quest line end (eb stop), the cast going now is cancelled, and nothing is cast until eb resume lets it all go again. Typed as eb halt too.
functions.notes: eb relay mygroup freeze stops every box of your group (a box you play by hand is left alone): the Stop group button of the MCP and of the mini; Go on there is eb relay mygroup resume. A casting that was off before the freeze stays off after eb resume. eb all freeze stops every box of the crew. Also typed as: halt. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> freeze ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: end

params.name: system
params.desc: quest, ic, nav, hunt, craft, harvest, all or irc.

functions.desc: End one engine and leave the rest running: quest, ic, nav, hunt, craft, harvest, or all. irc leaves the IRC channel and server this box is on (eb irc end).
functions.notes: eb end quest answers quest: ql: nothing is running when there is nothing to end. Sent with eb to <who> end ... it ends that box's engine. eb end all leaves IRC as it is; eb relay all end irc takes every box off IRC. Also typed as: kill. For the crew: eb to <who> end ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: pause

params.name: state
params.desc: pause, resume, toggle or status. Default: toggle. Default: toggle.

functions.desc: Pause: goals, quests, instances and walks freeze where they are; a fight still runs in the combat engine. Pause again, or eb resume, carries on from the same place.
functions.notes: Also typed as: hold, holdup. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> pause ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: resume
functions.desc: Carry on after eb pause or eb stopall, from where everything stopped (the same as eb pause resume).
functions.notes: Also typed as: letsgo, go!. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> resume ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: afk

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off, toggle or status. Default: status. Default: status.

functions.desc: Away mode: keep the character from being logged out for idling (a keep-alive at a random time every two to five minutes), and let the crew see this box as away.
functions.notes: eb afk status says whether the keep-alive is on, when the next one is due, and how many were sent or skipped. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> afk ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: reload

params.name: module
params.desc: nav, invites, stack, poi or cancel; nothing loads EB itself again.

functions.desc: Load EB again in this session without restarting the game or logging out: the client and the character stay, only EB's own scripts and data load again. With a word, one part only: nav (the mesh corrections, door lines, marks and places), invites (the roster and login results the invite reads), stack (this character's cast stack) or poi (the game's map points, read again at the next eb poi). A box in the middle of a run (an instance, a quest line, a power-level route, a queue) does not stop: it says so, keeps the ask and loads EB again by itself once the run is over; the word cancel drops that kept ask.
functions.notes: eb stopall drops a kept reload too (it ends the run and the ask with it). eb all reload: each box decides for itself. Also typed as: r. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> reload ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.craft
modules.summary: Console commands for crafting: the craft bot (EB Craft) - its setup queue, its runs (the queue, writs, a quest's craft steps, Auto Tinkering, Low Level Leveling), its settings - and recipe books, tinkering by its bands, crafting luck.
modules.description: Type these in the console as eb <command>, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to <who> <command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch(line) or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a run under way, a status line or a refusal in plain words. Every press in EB Craft is one of these lines, so a press and a typed line do the same thing. A crafting step that is not proven live on this box is held: a run is not started, and the answer says what waits and how to let it out for a proof run. The crafting itself is scriptable through the economy's Lua pillars (eb.economy.craft, eb.economy.writs, eb.economy.skilllevel) and the craft bot (app.economy.craftbot).

functions.name: craft

params.name: recipe
params.desc: A word above, or a recipe (its name or its id) and how many: eb craft Fixture Pie 3. For import, an old queue file's name.

functions.desc: The craft bot. With no word it opens EB Craft and says what the bot is doing. Runs: start (the setup queue), writs [n], quest <quest>, tinker, lll, stop, pause [on|off]. The setup queue: add <recipe> [n], remove <recipe>, qty <recipe> <n>, clear, queue, save <name>, load <name>, queues, forget <name>. Old saved queues: import list [words] shows the queue files your other craft tools left on this PC, import <file> [as <name>] saves one of them as a queue here, import all [words] saves every one (one a step). Settings: set <setting> <value> (set alone lists them), savesettings, reload; set campWhenDone on camps this character out to character select after a run that finishes (never one you stop; off by default). Also: scan (read the recipe book again), lite on|off (answer the reactions of a combine you start by hand), recipes <words>, parse <a writ or quest step's text>, proof on|off (EB Boxer: let its unproven crafting steps out for a proof run), shop books | sell <item> | destroy <item> (the named items in the bags sold to the merchant in reach, or destroyed - several split by | - never a protected one), minimize (EB Craft rolled up to its run row; eb craft brings it back). Any other words are a recipe crafted now.
functions.notes: A recipe's parts - its station, its fuel and the parts with their counts - come from the game's own recipe read first. When that read does not come (the server never answers for some recipes, the read waits for its live proof, or this box has no such read), they come from the recipe table EB ships, by the recipe's own id, and the run says where they came from: the Resources count, the fuel bought for the queue and for Low Level Leveling, and app.economy.craftbot:recipeParts (its from field says which). A recipe the table does not have is left as before, with both reasons said. A read still coming in is waited for, never filled. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> craft ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: craftqueue

params.name: cmd
params.desc: add, start, handout, status, stop, clear, remove, save or load. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: The recipe (and how many, and for <who>) for add; the recipe for remove; the queue's name for save and load.

functions.desc: The setup queue - the same one as EB Craft's Queues tab: add a recipe (and how many), remove one, start it, show it, stop it, clear it, save it or load a saved one by name, or hand the finished items out. add <recipe> [n] for <who> makes it for another box (a row of its own); handout trades each recipe made for another box to it - the economy's hand-over, one recipient at a time - and that box then scribes what it got (eb to <who> spells scribe).
functions.notes: eb craftqueue status lists the queue with each row's recipient ("craft: the setup queue is empty" when nothing is queued). The same as eb craft add / remove / start / save / load; a saved queue keeps its recipients. The hand-out gives what the last run made of each row (else what the bags hold, up to its count); a row for this box stays in the bags. EB Craft's Spell Upgrades sends its queue to the crafter with each upgrade's box as the recipient. Also typed as: cq. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> craftqueue ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: craftsetup
functions.desc: Low Level Leveling: a new crafter from level 1 to 9, then 10 to 19 - rounds of the highest recipe at or under the tradeskill level, what is made sold or destroyed as EB Craft's Low Level Leveling tab says, until the trainer's level. start [class] applies the class and options then runs it; plan says what it would do; stop ends it.
functions.notes: It does not run when the tradeskill level cannot be read. Stand at a station with the parts in the bags. The class is picked at the trainer at level 9, so start needs no class upfront; city:<city> sets the trainer's city, where:<where> is where it crafts, potion and xp prefer those recipes, and until:<level> stops it before the level-19 class choice. The same as eb craft lll (which keeps the settings as they are). Also typed as: csetup. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> craftsetup ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: recipebooks

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list, scribe, plan, prices or buy. Default: list.

params.name: arg
params.desc: plan / prices / buy: a class (else your set one), known or unknown, level:<n>; buy also takes broker or merchant, guildhall or nogh, and noscribe.

functions.desc: Recipe books: list = how many recipes this character's book holds (the book is read in the background); scribe = use every recipe book in the bags, then read the book again; plan = the books your crafting class still needs, at or under your tradeskill level; prices = the plan with each book's broker and merchant cost; buy = walk to the recipe merchant and buy then scribe the planned books.
functions.notes: plan reads which recipe books teach the recipes you do not have, for your class and the two tiers that feed it (artisan, its archetype, itself), capped at your tradeskill level. known lists the books you already hold in full; unknown (the default) the ones with a recipe still to learn. buy buys each by name at the recipe merchant (EB's own purchase question only) and scribes it. eb craft books does the same for the recipes in the setup queue; eb craft addlast adds the newest recipe your book gained. Also typed as: rbooks. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> recipebooks ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: craftjunk

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list, go, add or remove. Default: list. Default: list.

functions.desc: Low Level Leveling's leftovers: the items such a run is known to make. list says which bag stacks would go and which stay; go destroys them; add and remove keep your own names beside EB's list.
functions.notes: Only a handcrafted copy never worn goes (a copy worn once, or not handcrafted, stays and is said), and never a protected item. A Low Level Leveling run clears the same names when it cleans up, together with everything the whole run made (only what the bags gained of it). Script it with eb.economy.llljunk (names, pick). Also typed as: llljunk. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> craftjunk ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: tinker

params.name: arg
params.desc: on, off or status; or 'adorning' first to level adorning (eb tinker adorning on).

functions.desc: Level a secondary skill by its bands to the cap - tinkering (the default) or adorning: on = the recipes of each band (and the band's books, bought at the broker under a cap) until the skill is maxed; off = stop; no word = where it stands. eb tinker adorning on levels adorning instead. EB Craft's Auto Tinkering (eb craft tinker) is the other way: rounds of the highest tinkering recipe in the book.
functions.notes: It does not run when the skill cannot be read. eco.skilllevel:level("tinkering") or :level("adorning") levels the skill from a script. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> tinker ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: writs

params.name: cmd
params.desc: craft, rush or commission. Default: craft.

functions.desc: Crafting writs as EB Craft's Writs tab says (how many, which reply takes the writ): craft = from where the tab says (the rush order agent or the work order clipboard), rush = from the rush order agent; commission = accept commissions on or off.
functions.notes: It refuses in words when no writ giver is in reach. Script it with eco.writs:run(opts). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> writs ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: luck

params.name: cmd
params.desc: show, on (it pops up by itself while one levels), off (only on eb luck) or reset. Default: show.

functions.desc: The Luck window: while a skill that levels by chance climbs (tinkering, adorning, transmuting), how many crafts, how many skill-ups, the percent and the longest dry run.
functions.notes: This box only.

functions.name: craftgm

params.name: words
params.desc: [<range> | all] [scan | start | queue | status | stop] [depot | nodepot].

functions.desc: Craft Grandmasters: the (Master) spell scrolls in your bags turned into (Grandmaster) crafts, one craft per scroll. scan (the default) says what would be crafted and what is left out and why; start crafts them; queue only puts the recipes in the setup queue (eb craft start crafts it) and never uses the depot; status says where a run stands; stop ends it (a scroll taken out and not crafted stays in your bags). A level range is the (Grandmaster) recipe's level: 131-135, 131 135, level 131-135 or one level; all (the default) is every level, and a scroll with no readable level is left out of a ranged run. depot also takes the nearest Scroll Depot's scrolls, in batches that fit your bags; nodepot is bags only.
functions.notes: Nothing walks: stand at the Scroll Depot (and the crafting station) first. eb craftgm 131-135 queue then eb craft start crafts the queued recipes through the craft bot. The Craft Queue window shows the setup queue with what it needs. Also typed as: grandmasters. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> craftgm ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.depot
modules.summary: Console commands for bags, depots, the bank, mail and repairs: depot top-ups and keep lists, the inventory hub, deposits and withdrawals, restocking, buying, handing items out, food and drink, the protect list, item search, clearing raws, transmute and salvage runs, krono, the ledger, and mending gear.
modules.description: Type them as eb <command> in the console, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to <who> <command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers: a chore under way (a long job runs as a chore, one at a time, and eb economy stop ends it), a status line, or a refusal in plain words. A call the game layer holds back until EB has proven it in the game says so and answers false - it never says "done" for what it did not do. The Lua behind each one is named in its notes: eb.economy.inventory, eb.economy.vendor, eb.economy.depot, eb.economy.bank, eb.economy.mail and the rest of eb.economy.

functions.name: depot

params.name: cmd
params.desc: index (list the contents), here (the depot in reach), topup, keep, deposit, everywhere (walk to every depot of the hall and deposit at each), status, list (the PC's withdraw lists). Default: status. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: The depot or the item the action is about. A depot kind (scroll, harvest, food, ammo, fuel, adorn, collectible, lore, poison) picks the bag items that ARE that kind into that depot. list: a withdraw list's name (nothing names every list).

functions.desc: Depots: list what the depots in reach hold, top an item up from a depot, keep an item out of every deposit, deposit by rule, or show the depot status.
functions.notes: The withdraw lists are one catalogue for the PC (EB Depot > Withdraw lists makes them; eb.economy.withdrawlists reads them): a depot list brings each item up to its count - only what the bags lack, so a second run takes nothing more - and a bank list takes each item out of the personal or shared bank by name. eb all depot list <name> runs it on every box, each for itself. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> depot ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: inv

params.name: cmd
params.desc: show, tidy, move, sell, destroy, restock, trade, quiver, preset. Default: show. Default: show.

params.name: arg
params.desc: What the step is about: for move, <item> to <bag 1-6 | a bag's name> [slot <n>] [qty <n>]; for tidy, go (without it a dry run); a preset, an ammo name, an item and the member to give it to, or for preset: save <name> <action> <item>|<item>, run <name> [go] [to <who>], list, show <name>, delete <name>.

functions.desc: The inventory hub: show the bags, tidy them, move one item into a bag, sell by rule, destroy junk by rule, restock, hand items over, or fill the quiver - one after another.
functions.notes: move takes the whole stack (a part of a stack has no proven move: refused, nothing moved) into the slot asked (slot 1 = the bag's first; bag 1 = the first bag of the bag bar), else the bag's first empty slot - only ever an empty slot, never onto another item - and is done only when the game shows the item there. tidy gathers the empty slots at the end: an item of a later bag goes into an empty slot of an earlier bag, the last bag's last item first; it says what would move unless you add go. Nothing moves while a bag's or an item's place does not read. EB for InnerSpace holds both until their live proof; EB Boxer has no item move yet and says so. From a script: eb.economy.bagtidy (moveWords, plan) over drive bags.move. An inventory preset is a named list of items with what to do with them (sell, transmute, salvage, extract, destroy, depot, mail), kept for every character on this PC. A run takes only the bag items it names, each through the same gate as any bulk action (a protected item, a Krono, a bound one is never taken); a sell needs a merchant in reach; a destroy says what would go and destroys only with go; a mail preset needs who gets it (to <who>). A name with spaces is quoted. From a script: eco.inventory and eco.vendor; eb.economy.invpresets. Also typed as: inventory, im. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> inv ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: bank

params.name: cmd
params.desc: deposit, withdraw, coin, move, status. Default: status. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: [personal|shared|guild] all, an item, or the pick words. Withdraw takes several exact names joined by "|", or a pick: -name <part of the name>, -tiers <a,b>, -level <n> or <n>-<m> (-min / -max), -class <class that can use it>, -stat <stat> <n> and -resolve <n> (at least; < at most, = exactly), -pages <1,2> (the guild bank's pages), -qty <how many of each>. Deposit takes the T.S.E's pick words (-tiers -bags -min -max -novalue -notrade -heirloom -attuned) or names; deposit guild <page 1-4> [all | <item>] names the guild bank's page; coin deposit | withdraw <copper> [personal|shared|guild [<page 1-4>]] moves coin (the guild bank takes whole silver: an amount with copper over is refused, never rounded; coin put in is the guild's); move <from> <to> takes everything on one guild bank page and puts it on the other.

functions.desc: The bank: deposit bag items by rule, withdraw by name or by a pick, move coin, move a guild bank page onto another, or show what the banks hold.
functions.notes: Deposit all moves every bag item but the bags themselves and the never-deposit list at once; the protected list, the never-deposit list, the always-kept items and the Krono rule stay on every path. A withdraw pick reads the rows to the end first, and their tier and level when the pick needs them (a few items at a time: each is a question to the server). A pick the bank's rows on this box cannot judge - no tier read, or a guild row with no name - takes nothing and says so; a guild page is always taken by -pages. eb bank move 1 2 takes each stack off page 1 and puts that very stack on page 2: a stack of the same name you already carried stays in the bags. From a script: eco.bank:deposit / withdraw / coin / move / scan. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> bank ... (who after 'to').

functions.desc: Auto-consume named potions, elixirs, scrolls or poisons in the bags on or off, by the game's own Auto Consume flag: on uses one at once when its effect is not up. status reads them (no names: the ones EB switched). The AUTO-CONSUME LIST keeps that flag on for its items on every box - and off while the character is idle.
functions.notes: The list is one for every character on this PC. Each box looks every 5 seconds: an item is kept on while the list is on, the item is on (enable / disable) and the box is not idle; idle = no move of 2 m, no fight and no cast for the idle minutes (10 by default; idle off turns the rule off). Only a difference is flipped, one item a look; a flip that does not take after 3 tries is left alone for the session and said once. An item that cannot auto-consume is never turned on, and an item not on the list is never touched. apply counts as active and looks at once. Also typed as: pot, potions. functions.name: itemgate

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status, on, off or reload. Default: status. Default: status.

functions.desc: The item gate: a worn clicky whose effect shows only in a Persona stat - Dragon's Temper's Whirlwind is only seen as AE auto-attack - is not clicked again while that effect is on: its cast-stack row is held off, and on again when it may be used.
functions.notes: Every half second, per rule: held while the stat says the effect is up, out of a fight (combat only), or for the rule's wait after it stood open in a fight without the effect coming on (a fight's end gives the next fight a fresh try); open otherwise. Only a row the gate itself switched off is switched back on - a row you turned off stays off; off, a piece no longer worn, or no row for it puts everything back. The rules: built in (Dragon's Temper), or data\ebitemgate\gates.json { "gates": [ { "item", "stat" (a Persona stat word: aeauto, haste ...), "on_at", "combat_only", "retry_s" } ] } when it holds a good one (reload reads it again). This box only.

functions.notes: A crew line (eb all itemsearch ...) searches that box only. The characters that are not logged in are found too, as EB last read them on this PC (their bags and bank, this server's), each line saying how long ago that was; the shared bank once. A character's bags and bank are read a few minutes after it logs in, then every ten minutes while nothing else is going. From a script: eco.inventory:search(words, index). Also typed as: isearch. functions.notes: The shared bank belongs to the account, so it is counted once however many characters read it alike. A character never logged in on this PC since EB came is not known here; its box answers for itself when it is on. This box only.

functions.notes: A destroy typed by hand asks for go; without go it is a dry run that says what would go. A saved destroy runs with go. An item whose No-Trade, Heirloom or Attuned flags are not read on this box is not taken: the answer says so. The run itself is eco.tse and eco.transmute. Also typed as: transmutesalvage. functions.desc: The ledger: what every box sold, deposited, unadorned, transmuted and looted, day by day. It is kept on this PC and only your own boxes see it. open and close its window (EB Ledger: the days on the left, newest first, each with its coin and its counts); status says every box's coin and counts today, one line a box, each naming its character - the boxes of this PC from the day files here, a box of yours whose ledger is on another PC asked to say its own; a day (YYYY-MM-DD) or the last 12 hours reads the rows; loot says who got the loot (each character, how many, and what); clear <day> forgets that day and clear all forgets everything, every box's on this PC.

modules.name: commands.gear
modules.summary: Console commands for gear: gear a character or the group up, adornments, gear sets, temporary adornments, the best-gear list, worn gear, the at-a-glance card, Transmuting levels.
modules.description: Type these as eb <command>, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to <who> <command>, or run them with reg:dispatch(line) or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a chore under way, a status line or a refusal in plain words. The work behind them is scriptable through eb.economy.gearup, eb.economy.adornments, eb.economy.gearsets and eb.economy.transmute.

functions.name: gearup

params.name: arg
params.desc: max:<the most a piece may cost> lvl:<the highest level> skip:Name,Name.

functions.desc: Gear a fresh character from the broker: each empty slot gets the best listing for it under the cap, then the upgrades are worn. group: every box not paused gears itself up.
functions.notes: Never a buy without a cap: max: on the line, else your broker cap (broker.maxCopper); with neither it is refused. At most the character's level (lvl: lowers it). It says per empty slot what it bought and what not and why. group sends eb gearup self with the same words to every box not paused; a box named in skip: leaves itself out. Script it with eco.gearup:fillFromBroker and eco.gearup:aup. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> gearup ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: aup

params.name: who
params.desc: self or group. Default: self. Default: self.

params.name: arg
params.desc: self: [slots or kinds] [-1h | -2h | -any] - kinds are armor, weapons, jewelry, charms and all; slots as the game says them (head, ring, left ring ...). group: plan, scan, export, trade, cancel, status, priority <roles>, scope me | group.

functions.desc: Wear the upgrades in your bags, or (group) work out who in the crew should wear which spare piece and hand them over.
functions.notes: Every bag piece is judged against what is worn in its slot: Resolve first, then Fervor, then Potency, then the role's main stat, then your own weights (gear.<role> in EB's settings). The stat lines are read under one key set whatever the game calls them; a piece whose stats did not read is not judged and is counted in the answer (unknown is never taken for nothing). A ring is held against the weaker of the two worn, the same for ears and wrists; a two-hander against the primary and the secondary together. The weapon pick: one-handed for a plate tank, two-handed for a brawler, either for the rest; -1h, -2h or -any on the line wins. The best upgrade is put on by the gear job (worn by its own bag id, the old piece's adornments carried across), then the next, until nothing in the bags is better; one that does not go on is named and the run is not a done. group: each box shares its gear on this PC (eb aup group export; scan writes this box's and asks every other box), the bare form shows the plan (a dry run): each spare piece goes to the member it upgrades most, by the role order (priority tank,healer,dps,utility: of two members it upgrades, the role that comes first gets it); a bound piece (No-Trade, Heirloom, Attuned) or one whose flags did not read never moves; scope me sends every piece to this character only. trade hands them out one at a time per member: the member it is for takes the holder's trade (eb trade accept) and wears it (eb gearjob take), the holder trades it (eb trade item); status says how each went, cancel stops sending. Script it with eb.economy.gearscore, eco.gearup:aup / planGroupTrades and eb.economy.groupgear. Also typed as: adornup. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> aup ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: adorn

params.name: cmd
params.desc: guide, apply, missing, fill, contents, own, adopt, take, buy, unadorn or export. Default: guide.

params.name: arg
params.desc: apply / fill: [a set] [-depot | -broker | -auto | -craft] [the most one may cost]. No set means this character's class set, picked as eb acs picks it; a set is a gear set's name, your own family's name, or a class set's word for this character's class (RoK, exp04, TSOx2). adopt: <member> and the same words. contents / missing: [a set]; contents worn lists the adornments on the worn gear. own takes: <family> (what this box wears, saved as its class's set in your own family), list, copy <family> <set> [<class>], add | remove <family> <class> <slot> <adornment>, delete <family> [<class>]. take: <adornment> [how many].

functions.desc: Adornment sets: put a set on (apply), put it on and buy what is missing (fill), copy a member's adornments (adopt), say where each adornment of a set is (contents, missing), keep your own sets, take adornments from the depot, buy one, strip old gear, or show the guide.
functions.notes: Where a missing adornment comes from: the bags first, then -depot the Adornment Depot only, -broker the broker only, -auto (fill's default) the depot and then the broker; apply takes the bags and the depot and never buys. The broker is used only under a cap - 5p, 2g50s, a bare number in copper, or the four numbers platinum gold silver copper (5 0 0 0); with none on the line your broker cap stands in, and with neither the broker part is skipped and said. -craft puts the ones that are neither on nor in the bags in this character's craft queue (eb craftqueue add, one each), crafts the queue (eb craftqueue start) and, once that run has ended, puts the set on from the bags. A run that could not get an adornment, or one that did not go on, ends naming it, its slot and where it was looked for - never done; a slot with nothing worn is skipped and said. adopt <member> copies what that member wears, from the gear it shares on this PC (its Gear or Gear At-A-Glance window writes it); an adornment whose read never came is never copied. contents says for each adornment of the set: on (and on which piece), in the bags (how many), in a depot EB has read (the depot index, this zone's first, any zone), or nowhere; missing says it for the ones that are not on. An adornment with its tier in its name - X (Superior) - that the Adornment Depot does not hold is taken a tier lower, X (Greater) then X (Lesser), and that is said; take and apply / fill alike. A slot's several adornments (white, turquoise, black) each go on. Your own families are one file for the PC, one set per class; a family never takes an expansion's word (RoK, TSO). Script it with eb.economy.adornments (applyProfile with method depot | broker | auto | bags and maxCopper, unadorn), eb.economy.adornsets, eb.economy.adornwhere and eb.economy.ownsets. buy set [<set>] [-cap <coin>] buys what the set still needs - each adornment neither on its slot nor in the bags, one each, by its name, under the cap (the line's, else the broker's own; never without one) - and puts nothing on (eb adorn apply does). Also typed as: adorns, adornments. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> adorn ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: tempadorn

params.name: state
params.desc: apply, check, status, restock, find, on or off. Default: apply. Default: apply.

params.name: arg
params.desc: apply: dry (only say what it would do) or force (fresh ones everywhere, also where one is still on); restock: how many of each to keep in the bags (10, or tempKeep in EB's settings); find: a part of a name (none: the plan's own).

functions.desc: Temporary adornments by the Temp Adorns window's plan: put them on, a dry run, fresh ones, what is on, the status, a restock from the Adornment Depot, a find, and keep them on.
functions.notes: The plan is EB's own adorn.temp, else the Temp Adorns window's plan for the install: this class's picks over Everyone's, the two-handed pick on a two-handed primary. apply leaves a slot whose temporary adornment is still on, takes what the bags lack from the Adornment Depot in reach, never buys, and names what it could not get. check says what of the plan is on now (a piece whose adornments do not read yet is said). status shows the switch, the plan, how many of each the bags hold and how long each one EB put on has left. restock [n] takes from the depot up to n of each; one the depot does not hold is named and the run is not a done. find [words] the catalogue's temporary adornments named so: the slots each fits, how long it lasts, how many the bags hold, the depot EB saw it in. on keeps them on: out of a fight and calm for a few seconds, with no other economy chore under way, a planned one is put back when it is gone, the piece in its slot changed, or it is in its last tenth (at least 3 minutes before its end) - timed from when EB put it on and how long it lasts (the game has no time-left read), kept per character on this PC; a slot that did not take is tried again after 90 s and left after 3 tries on the same piece. off stops it. Script it with eb.economy.tempadorns and eb.economy.tempkeep. Also typed as: tempadorns. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> tempadorn ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: bestgear

params.name: cmd
params.desc: shop, buy, goals or status. Default: status. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: shop: slots:head|chest|all stat:<stat> stat2:<stat> need:a+b lvl:<min>-<max> max:<coin> count:0 upgrade:1 bags:1 wear:1 tiers:a|b. buy: <slot> [stat:<focus>] [stat2:<stat>] [max:<coin>]. goals: set <stat>=<n>,<stat>=<n> | clear | run [the shop's words].

functions.desc: The best gear on the broker: a shop ranked by the stats you pick, a buy for one slot by a focus stat, the stat goals and a run toward them, or where you stand.
functions.notes: Each slot's listings are ranked by stat, then stat2, then EB's gear scorer; need: keeps only the listings that carry those stats; tiers: only those tiers; the best one is bought BY ITS NAME under the cap (max:, else your broker cap; never without one - the purchase question answered Yes only when it names that item). count:0 only lists the three best per slot; upgrade:1 only what beats the worn piece; bags:1 puts a better bag piece on first; wear:1 puts what was bought on with the old piece's adornments carried across. A listing whose stats did not read (EB for InnerSpace's result rows today) is never judged nor bought, and counted in the answer. buy <slot> = the shop for that slot with upgrade:1 wear:1. goals are stat targets (multiattack=116, abilitymod=1300) held against the worn gear's totals; goals run shops the slots for the stat furthest from its goal (then the next), upgrades only, worn. Script it with eb.economy.gearshop (words, rankScore, run, totals). Also typed as: gearshop, geargoals. This box only.

functions.name: gearjob

params.name: cmd
params.desc: look, take, best, upgrade, status, cancel, dismiss. Default: look. Default: look.

params.name: arg
params.desc: look: the member. take: the piece this box is to wear. best: [a slot or kind] [-1h | -2h | -any].

functions.desc: Look at a member's worn gear (or this box's own), or run the gear job on this box: take a piece, wear it and carry the old piece's adornments across.
functions.notes: eb gearjob take <item> waits up to two minutes for the piece to reach the bags (a loot assign or a trade takes a moment), wears it, then moves the adornments of the piece it pushed off onto it - the game's own move where the box has one, else they are reclaimed off the old piece and put on the new one, each by its own bag id. A slot that was empty, or an old piece with no adornment, ends once it is worn. Each step is said in eb gearjob status and written for the leader: EB Loot Assign's Assign+ hands the drop over and starts this job on the box it went to (eb to <who> gearjob take <item>), and its progress column shows how far that box got. eb gearjob best [slot] lets the scorer pick the bag piece that gains this box the most (as eb aup judges it) and runs the same job on it. look reads another member's gear from what it shares on this PC when the crew feed has none. eb gearjob cancel stops it; dismiss clears what it said. eb gearjob upgrade (the MCP's Upgrade Item) is the same job from the bags: put the piece you wear now in bag 1 slot 1 and its upgrade in bag 1 slot 2 - the old piece's adornments go onto the new one, the old piece to the end of bag 1 (its last empty slot; a box with no bag move leaves it in slot 1), the new one is worn. Nothing moves when a slot is empty or did not read, the two are for different slots, or the new one carries an adornment already. Also typed as: gearworn. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> gearjob ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: glance

params.name: cmd
params.desc: card, presets, preset, run, join, retry, stop or status. Default: card. Default: card.

functions.desc: At a glance: one line of this character's gear, bags and coin (card, the bare form), or a RUN - a preset's steps done on several boxes, each box its own part - with its presets, retry, stop and status.
functions.notes: A preset's steps, joined by ";": withdraw <adornment> [n] (eb adorn take: the Adornment Depot, a tier lower when it lacks one), adorn [word] (eb acs: the class set), coin <from> <amount> (that box hands this one the coin: eb trade coin, and this box takes that trade), check (what this box wears, with its adornments, shared for the windows), buy (eb gearup). The presets are one file for the PC. run <preset> [boxes] writes the run for this PC and tells each box eb glance join: each box does its own part one step after the other, each step followed to the end of the chore it starts, the boxes 8 s apart and a coin step 40 s apart (one depot, one giver); a step that fails skips the rest on that box (a check still runs). Each box writes how each step went where every box of this PC reads it; status says it per box (waiting its turn, a step under way, done, or not done at which step and why). retry runs the boxes not done again, each from its first step not done (a step done before is never done again); stop ends every box's part (the step under way finishes). EB Gear At-A-Glance's Runs part (folded under the grid) shows the presets with a Run each (on the boxes shown), the newest run's boxes, Retry and Stop. Script it with eb.economy.glancerun. Also typed as: ataglance. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> glance ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: transmutelevel

params.name: cmd
params.desc: level, scan, stop or status. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: level: [stone words] [-max N] [-cur a|b] [-keep N] [-dry N].

functions.desc: Level the Transmuting skill: level, scan the stone merchant, stop, or show where it stands.
functions.notes: level buys a Transmuter's Stone at the stone merchant and transmutes it, round after round, until Transmuting is at its max. The stone words name the stone it starts from (else the cheapest); -max N stones at most (2000); -cur a|b only the currencies named, ~ for a space in one (none named: any the merchant takes); -keep N bag slots left free (4); -dry N transmutes with no skill-up before the next stone up (50; 0 = never). scan says what the merchant sells and for what, the currency held and the skill, and buys nothing. It does not run when the Transmuting skill cannot be read. Script it with eco.transmute:levelTransmute / scanStones. Also typed as: tmlevel. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> transmutelevel ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: gearset

params.name: cmd
params.desc: save, adorn, equip, list or delete. Default: list. Default: list.

functions.desc: Gear sets: save what is worn (the pieces and their adornments) under a name; put the adornments or the pieces back; list the sets; delete one.
functions.notes: equip polls each piece until the game shows it on before the next one goes. Also typed as: gearsets. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> gearset ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: unadorn

params.name: tiers
params.desc: The tiers, for example treasured legendary. Nothing means every tier. Then -name <part> to take them off only the pieces whose name holds that part.

functions.desc: Take the adornments off the bag items of the tiers named. They stay in the bags; protected items are skipped.
functions.notes: Each piece's take-off is followed to its end before the next. A piece whose adornments do not read here is left as it is and said - the run never says done over it. eb adorn buy <adornment> [the most it may cost] buys one more of an adornment from the broker, never over that price (else the broker's own cap). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> unadorn ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: checkgear
functions.desc: Worn gear: the worst piece's condition, and what is under the repair line.
functions.notes: For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> checkgear ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.harvest
modules.summary: Console commands for harvesting: nodes near you and gather routes, shinies, crafting materials, saved gather routes, the pack pony.
modules.description: Type these as eb <command>, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to <who> <command>, or run them with reg:dispatch(line) or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a chore under way, a status line or a refusal in plain words. Harvesting is scriptable through eb.economy.harvest. A node the rules leave is never clicked: the route leaves it and remembers it.

functions.name: harvest

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, status, near, route, left, tally, log, roam, cover, make, known, courtesy, plan, pause or resume. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: near / roam: their options (kind:<kinds> too; roam: patrol); route: the route's name; left: clear; tally: reset; log and courtesy: on or off; cover: sweep or a node's name, kind:<kinds>; make: the new route's name; known: clear; plan: list, clear <zone> or go <zone>.

functions.desc: Harvest: switch it on or off, show its status, take the nodes near you, or run a gather route. near takes options: once (one pull), reach:<m> (how far it looks), move:<m> (walks up to a node that far, on the mesh), count:<n> (how many pulls), until:<n>:<item> (until the bags hold that many; an underscore is a space), and a node's name. left says the nodes left a while and when each comes back (a refused pull, or another box on it: 90 seconds; a node the mesh could not reach: 5 minutes); left clear looks at them all again. tally says what this session gathered: pulls, rares, per minute, per kind (Ore, Gem, Wood, Root, Den, Shrub, Fish, Shiny); tally reset counts from zero. log on or off writes each step of a run (start, scan, pick, walk, pull, node, mark, end) to a file in logs, one a session; no word says where it is. roam lets the mesh pick where to look: look points in rings round you (a radius in metres) or inside an area you marked (mark:<name>: an area route of EB Gather, its corners, or a saved spot), each the mesh's own point, nearest first, round and round until you stop it, count:<n> or until:<n>:<item>. cover runs once over every node this box has seen in this zone (a node's name narrows it); cover sweep [radius] sweeps the whole zone in rings once. make <name> makes a gather route from the nodes seen here, nearest first from where you stand, without running it (eb gatherroute <name> runs it). known says how many nodes are known here, by kind; known clear forgets them. courtesy on or off: your own boxes, grouped or not, never go for one node - a node another box goes for is left to it - and each box harvesting in a zone takes its own part of a roam's look points and its own start on a route (on unless set off). kind:<kinds> (kind:ore,gem - ore, gem, wood, root, den, shrub, fish) on near, roam and cover takes only nodes of those kinds: a node of another kind is passed by, never clicked, and the next one looked at. roam <radius> patrol walks its look points ring by ring, round and round, instead of nearest first. pause holds the harvest under way where it stands (the walk stopped, nothing pulled); resume goes on from there. plan lists EB Gather's zone plans (how, the route or name, within, the kinds); plan clear <zone> clears one (its short name or its name); plan go <zone> travels there first - EB's own travel, this box only - and starts its plan there.
functions.notes: status also says how loot-as-you-go stands, the tally, the nodes left and a pause. A crew line (eb all harvest ...) never starts a harvest that moves on a box played by hand (paused, or EB stopped there): it is refused there, said. A node's tier comes from the harvest tiers' level bands (to the level cap and past it): a node above what your level gathers is left. A pull waits for the last one's cast. Script it with eco.harvest:wantNode, eco.harvest:runRoute and eco.harvest:watch (every step of a run). Also typed as: harv. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> harvest ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: shinies

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, status or track. Default: status.

functions.desc: Collect and track shinies: on, off, status, or track (watch for new ones and mark where they are).
functions.notes: Script it with eco.harvest:trackShiny. Also typed as: shiny. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> shinies ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: mats

params.name: cmd
params.desc: harvest (default), list, recipe, clear, go, stop or status. Default: harvest.

params.name: arg
params.desc: For recipe: the recipe's name (or its id), and how many: "name",3.

functions.desc: Gather the raw materials on a list. recipe <name> makes the list from that recipe's own components (how many times: "name",3), less what the bags hold; list says what is still missing; harvest gathers what is near you until every raw on the list is in the bags; clear empties the list. go harvests EB Gather's Materials list where it grows: each material in a zone of its tier (the one you stand in when it is of that tier, else EB's own travel there first), taking only the node kinds that give it (a mineral: ore and gem nodes) until its count is gathered over what the bags held on arrival, then Call to Guild Hall and the harvest into the hall's Harvesting Supply Depot; stop ends that run where it is; status says where it is, each material gathered of its count, and how each zone ended.
functions.notes: The list is the harvest.mats setting: each raw material and how many are wanted. A part no node gives (a refined part) stays missing and is said; the fuel is left out (it is bought). go's list is EB Gather's Materials tab (kept per character); a zone where none of its materials is gathered for 10 minutes (the bags full, or none grows there) is left for the next. A crew line never starts go on a box played by hand, and while this box is paused the run holds its harvest and goes on after. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> mats ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: gatherroute

params.name: name
params.desc: A route's name [kind:<kinds>]; or farm <route>, all, list, import [all | <file> | old [<zone>] [overwrite]], or stop.

functions.desc: Run a saved gather route (a route of another zone: this box travels there first, then it runs). list names the routes; import reads your own saved gather route files - all of them, or the one named - into EB's routes; import old reads the old bot's auto-hunt routes (each zone's route of named points and that zone's map) as gather routes walked in order and round again (one zone by its name; overwrite replaces a route already there); stop ends the run. farm <route> walks the route round and round taking every node on it (wide round each stop, its own node names set aside); all runs every route of the zone you stand in, one after another, then over again from the first (a route of another zone, or one with no zone, is never in it). kind:<kinds> anywhere among the words takes only nodes of those kinds.
functions.notes: An imported route keeps its name, its zone's short name, its stops, its node filters, its radius and whether it loops - nothing else from the file. An old auto-hunt route keeps its points in its own order and its zone; a point its map does not have is left out, and said. The files are only read, one a pulse step, a map in slices. The run walks up to each wanted node on the zone's mesh; an area route marked by its corners roams inside them (in all: swept once a round). A crew line never starts one on a box played by hand. Script it with eco.harvest:runRoute(stops, { filter, loop, walkToNode = true, kinds = { Ore = true } }). Also typed as: gather. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> gatherroute ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: packpony
functions.desc: Send the pack pony out to harvest: summon it, hail it and answer its questions. While an instance run or a quest line is going on this box it is held off - said - and goes out once the run is over.
functions.notes: For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> packpony ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.ic
modules.summary: The instance commands: run or loop an instance file, see the lockout timers, reset a zone, and the instance queue, creator and run-teams commands.
modules.description:
Type them in the console after the console word (eb ic run fixture_hollow), run them from a script with reg:dispatch("eb ic status"), or send them to the crew: eb all ic run fixture_hollow typed on the tank runs it on every box, with the box it was typed on as the lead and the others following it.

HOW TO RUN AN INSTANCE. 1. eb ic list shows the installed instance files. 2.
