On the tank: eb ic run <zone> [difficulty] [option=on|off] for one run, or eb ic loop <zone> [minutes] [difficulty] to keep at it (0 or nothing = until you stop it). 3. eb ic status says where it is. 4. eb ic stop ends it at once; nobody moves. 5. eb lockouts shows the zone timers; eb resetzone <zone> asks the game to reset one.

functions.name: ic

params.name: cmd
params.desc: What to do: run, loop, stop, status (the default), list or reload; and the run control words near, runnear, rundirect, goto, rerun, loopzone, looplist, ignorelock, checkitems, stats, rune, catchup, rezmember, gatherremains, acceptrez and entrance; the IC files' words options, option, files, load, save, export, addmonitor and addscript. Default: status.

params.name: zone
params.desc: The instance (its folder name), then for loop the minutes (0 = until stopped) and the difficulty ("[Heroic I]"); option=on|off words flip the instance's run options; laps=N (a loop stops after N laps), from=N (start at route step N), solo (this box alone) and loot=<method> (the group's loot method for this run: leader, ffa, lotto, nbg, roundrobin or keep - set by the lead as the run begins, before the instance's own loot method; keep sets nothing) and merc=on (the lead summons its mercenary as it starts when it runs alone: solo, or nobody else in its group - the Instance Runner's tick; eb set ic.mercSolo <words> makes it a swap to that one, and eb set ic.mercBack <words> swaps back when the run, or the instance queue it runs in, is over) are run options too; tse, repair or maintenance after the zone name the chores to run between laps and at a zone's end. For the control words: what each takes (below).

functions.desc: Run or loop an instance file, and control the run: run, loop, stop, status, list (the installed instance files) and reload (read the files again). The box the line is typed on leads; boxes that receive it from another box follow that box: they reach the hub on their own, are zoned in by the lead's door, and never walk the route. At the door the lead on a mount or swimming comes down for a few seconds first (the fly / swim-down key), then takes the door for the group: each member takes it from where it holds, never walked to it. A run's EVAC (my own class evac, then one member by class, then an evac item - each verified by the move) learns a zone whose evac the game refuses ("... isn't so easy to escape ..."): kept on this PC, never tried there again.
functions.notes:
eb ic run and loop start an EB task and answer at once; eb ic status reports on it. eb ic files lists the IC files EB can run: EB's own folders first, then the old bots' live folders with a count each - a host that has no folder listing says so on that line ("... cannot be listed here", "not listed"), never a missing line or a count of 0.

near <ic> [n] lists the n route steps nearest to where you stand (a path by its nearest spot, a camp spot), each with its step number and the fight it leads to. runnear <ic> [difficulty] runs the instance from the nearest step - only inside it: a path picked up mid-way walks on from its spot nearest to you, never back to its start. rundirect <ic> [difficulty] [step] runs it from a step. goto <step> makes the running run go on from that step: the wait in hand ends and the walk stops (on the lead's box, on the route only). rerun <ic> [difficulty] is one more run: out by the exit, the reset from outside once everyone is out, back in, the route. loopzone <ic> [difficulty] [minutes] is eb ic loop in that order (exp, a locked copy run again in place, is not in EB). looplist [runs] [minutes] runs the instance queue (eb iqueue) again and again: runs = passes of the whole list, minutes = a time cap, 0 or none = no cap. ignorelock on | off | status: with off (the default) the queue skips a zone this box is saved to (the zone it stands in never); on runs it anyway. checkitems ["item" ...] says what of the items this box lacks; with none named, the instance's own required_items (an instance that names them is checked on the lead before it starts, and every other box is asked to look in its own bags). stats [<ic>] is the run tracker: each run's time, nameds, deaths and revives, per instance the runs, the ones to the end and the best time (a new best is said when a run ends); stats csv writes its timing rows - one a run: the day, the zone, the difficulty, the seconds, the nameds, the deaths, how it ended and why - to eb-instance-timing.csv beside the install, a sheet to open. rune <name> puts that belt rune on every box (eb all beltadorn <name>). entrance <ic> walks this box to that instance's entrance (its file's entrance spot, else the end of the tank's approach) - only in its hub zone: eb hub <ic> gets it there, eb hubs destinations <hub> lists the instances entered from a hub. It never goes through the door: zoning in stays the tank's run. new [3boss | 5boss | raid] [name] lays an instance out from a template under your own instances, to walk in the Instance Builder (templates lists them). teststep <ic> <step> runs that ONE step now, on this box alone - no way in, no zone's end, not in the stats (the Instance Builder's Test this step); nextstep runs the step after the last tested.

THE WATCHDOG: a lead that is nowhere near the route (60 m off the step it is on and the next step with a place, not moving nor getting closer for 45 s, no fight on) goes on from the step nearest to where it stands, as eb ic goto does - twice a step and four times a run at most, then it says so and carries on.

THE GROUP'S MOVES IN TURN: with the crew's stagger on (eb stagger on; eb stagger leader auto = this group's tank), a member's walk to the lead's camp spot and its follow leave in turn, each box waiting its slot (the stagger's delay), the leader first - a newer order from the lead ends the wait. With the stagger off they leave at once.

A MEMBER DOWN: the lead's run holds between steps while a member of the group is down - the rez run is asked for (one rezzer runs to each body, Gather Remains when it reaches; asked again every minute), a fight is waited out, after 4 minutes the member releases to the revive point, and once it is up far off it walks back along the instance's own route; after 8 minutes the run goes on without them and says so. catchup [x y z] makes this member walk back to the lead along the route (the spots the file sends the group to on purpose, then the lead; with no spot, the lead's character in sight). rezmember <name> sends one rezzer to that member. gatherremains casts Gather Remains on this box. acceptrez, on a dead box, answers a rez offer on its screen yes (never a summon).

THE IC FILES. Besides EB's own instance files (eb ic list), eb ic run takes the IC files of the bots you ran before, where they live on this PC - the instance files (a wrapper over a shared base file, a file of templates too), your own zone files, the shipped and the test zone files - read live, never written: EB keeps its own copy (data\ebic\live) and reads the file again for each run. A script IC file is listed but never run. files [<folder> | <words>] lists them, each with the name to run it by (instances/<name>, custom/<name> ...). load <file> reads one now: what it is, what it becomes, and every step EB will not run of it, with the reason (a script, a raw key press, a test EB cannot read). An IF / a WHILE of the file is decided as the run reaches it; its console steps are done the EB way (the boxes each names; every box in this zone for the group). options [<ic>] lists an instance's own options (skip a named ...): ON or off for its next run and what each skips; option [<ic>] <id> on | off keeps one on this PC (every box of the PC reads it); an <id>=on|off word on the run line still wins for that run. save <ic> [<name>] (or export) writes your own copy into data\ebic\authored\instances: it opens in the Instance Builder under Mine and runs as eb ic run authored/<name>. addmonitor and addscript answer that EB runs no scripts: a fight rule goes in the Instance Builder. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> ic ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: lockouts

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), refresh (read them again now), check (is this box saved to the zone) or fleet (every box that is on answers for itself, on its own console, and every other character this PC keeps answers from its last read).

params.name: zone
params.desc: The zone to check (a part of its name is enough). check <zone> for <character> answers for that character; fleet with no zone lists what every character is saved to.

functions.desc: Show the zones this character is saved to, check one zone, or ask every character.
functions.notes: Every read of a box's own lockouts is kept on this PC, one record a character (with its class, level and the zone it stood in), so fleet and check answer for a character that is not logged in, "as of" that read. A lockout whose own timer ran out counts as free; a zone whose time left did not read stays saved as of its read. The read is held back until EB has proven it in the game: the answer says so (and names this PC's last record), nothing is written over the record, and eb resetzone <zone> still works by name. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> lockouts ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: zoneevent

params.name: event
params.desc: The event's name, for example Xygoz_ClickAdd (any case).

functions.desc: Do a zone's own event the EB way, on every box the line reaches: eb all zoneevent <event>. EB knows Xygoz_ClickAdd (The Fabled Veeshan's Peak, the fight with Xygoz): pressed when the crew stands next to its doppelgangers, each box double-clicks the NPC that bears its own character's name within 10 m, so every copy is taken by the character it copies.
functions.notes: A box with no copy of itself within 10 m clicks nothing and says so. An event EB has no version of is refused in words, with the events EB knows. The reads and the double-click are proven in the game: nothing waits for a live proof. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> zoneevent ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: resetzone

params.name: cmd
params.desc: one (the zone named next; with no zone, the zone of the run in hand), all (every zone this box is saved to - there is no second question), or force. Default: one.

functions.desc: Ask the game to reset a zone's lockout: one zone (the default), all of them, or forced.
functions.notes: A reset only takes from outside the zone; the instance loop resets from outside by itself. A reset is always this box's own: eb all resetzone <zone> makes each box reset itself. The reset is held back until EB has proven it in the game: the answer names the zone and says so. Also typed as: zonereset. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> resetzone ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: catalog

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, status (the default), scan (one look now, on or off), save, find, list or forget. Default: status.

params.name: what
params.desc: find: a name or part of one; list / forget: a zone (none = the zone you stand in).

functions.desc: The NPC and door catalogue: with it on, every few seconds the NPCs and the doors around this box are noted, zone by zone - where each was seen last, how many looks saw it, the day, named or not, its level. Never a player, a pet, a mercenary or you; no look in a fight or while zoning. Kept in eb-catalog.json beside the install.
functions.notes: find answers each place with its zone and spot, the most seen first; eb all catalog on notes on every box. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> catalog ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: iqueue

params.name: cmd
params.desc: add, start, stop, pause, resume, clear, remove, move, difficulty, save, load, presets, delete, takeover, tankdrives or status (the default). Default: status.

params.name: zone
params.desc: The zone to add; a row (start, remove); a row and where it goes (move 3 1); a row and its copy (difficulty 2 [Heroic II]; no copy = the instance's own); a preset's name (save, load, delete); on, off or status (tankdrives).

functions.desc: The instance queue: a list of zones run one after another - add zones, start, stop, pause, resume, clear, move a row, set a row's copy, keep the queue under a name and put it back, or hand the driving to the tank.
functions.notes:
eb iqueue status says "iqueue: stopped, 0 run(s)" when nothing is queued; with runs it names the one under way and the next ("on 1, next 2") and marks each run that ran to the end in this pass ("- done"; a new pass of eb ic looplist starts unmarked). The run under way is never moved, nor its copy changed. save <name> keeps the queue as it is (each run's copy, minutes, chores and options) in eb-icqueue-presets.json beside the install, presets lists them, load <name> puts them in the queue's place (never while it runs), delete <name> forgets one; names any case. Each character keeps its own queue (eb-icqueue-<character>.json beside the install: the boxes of a PC share the install); the old single eb-icqueue.json is read once into a character that has no file yet.

THE TANK DRIVES (eb iqueue tankdrives on | off | status; on unless you set it off, kept with the queue): eb iqueue start typed on a box whose character is no fighter, in a group with a fighter whose box runs EB (not one you play by hand), hands the whole queue to that fighter - its box takes every run (minutes, copy and chores kept), starts it and runs the way in alone, zoning the group in; this box says it follows. When the fighter's box is busy (its own queue, a run) or does not answer within 15 seconds, this box drives the queue after all and says why. eb iqueue takeover always drives from the box it is typed on. Also typed as: inst, instance. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> iqueue ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: creator

params.name: what
params.desc: ic (the default), quest or fight. Default: ic.

functions.desc: Open the point-and-click creator for an instance file, a quest pack or a fight.
functions.notes: It opens the window through the overlay: where the overlay cannot start, the answer says why. Also typed as: cr. This box only.

functions.name: teams

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), show, apply, set, team, name, unname, pin, pair, leader, clear, size, unpaired, on, off, formgroups, default, form, gather, leave, run, disband, runall, formall, disbandall, relay, waitdone, breakout, runlist, add, remove, new, duplicate, empty, class, unpin, unpair or unlead. Default: list.

params.name: arg
params.desc: What the word takes: a team (a name of several words in "quotes"), a content (solo, advanced_solo, heroic, group, quest, task), character names, classes, items.

functions.desc: Run teams: who runs with whom, and the crew at work in teams - forming a team's group, running its default run, sharing instances, quest lines or task lists out across the teams (breakouts), and running a task list with a regroup.
functions.notes:
list names each box with its team and its role, then the named teams and the rules.

THE TEAMS. The Teams window's teams are A to E (eb teams set <name> <A-E or -> [role]); eb teams name <team> <name> <name> ... makes a named team of any name (a letter puts those characters on that window team). One crew-wide file beside the install keeps them and the rules: pin <names> [leader <name>] keeps characters together; pair <class> <class> groups those classes; leader <character or class> says who leads first, leader <team> <character> a team's own; size <content> <n> (solo 1, advanced_solo 2, heroic 6, group 6, quest 6, task 6); unpaired solo | group | skip (each alone, join a team with room, or sit it out); on | off [<team>]; clear [pins | pairs | leaders | all]. show / apply [content] say the teams the rules make for a content: named teams first, then the pins, then the class pairs, every team split to the content's size, then the characters on no team; a team's leader is its own, else a fighter for heroic and group (the tank runs the way in), else the leader order, else its first. A box you play by hand (paused) is left out.

AT WORK. Typed on one box, these plan for every box and each box does only its own part: form <team> [content] (the members leave groups that are not theirs, the leader invites each one and says who did not come; EB accepts an invite from one of your own characters by itself), form <content> (the whole crew regrouped into the rules' teams), run <team> (formed, then its leader runs the team's default run - default <team> <ic | quest | tasklist> <what> [as <content>] [share] [disband]: several instances go through the leader's instance queue, share spreads them over the team's groups, disband breaks the group up once the run is over), disband <team> (each leaves a group it shares with another of the team), runall / formall [content] / disbandall (every team that is on), gather (this box leads; every crew character in no group asks to join, up to six), leave, relay <team or number> <command> (eb to its characters), waitdone [seconds] (until every team member is idle; who is still busy is named).

BREAKOUTS. breakout [size] splits the crew into the window's teams A to E, a tank and a healer first. breakout instances | quests | tasks <items, commas between> [content] shares them out in turn across the teams (solo, quest and task when no content is said), each team's leader running its share - formed first while formgroups is on; breakout queue shares this box's instance queue out the same way; save <name> <instances | quests | tasks> <items> [content], presets, show, delete and run <name> keep breakouts; breakout <name> team <team> add | remove | list | members | run | leader gives a team its own items.

RUN LISTS. runlist <list> [breakout] [regroup <zone>] [nowait] runs one of your task lists (the Tasks window's) on this box, or shares its instance steps out across the teams; regroup sends every box you are not playing by hand to that zone once it is over; nowait says nothing at the end. runlist lists | show | make | add <list> <instance | quest | command | wait> <what> | remove | move | delete | regroup <list> <zone | off> edit the lists. A list keeps its own way of running: runlist mode <list> sequential | breakout (what runlist <list> does when the line says neither), wait <list> on | off (its end said), limit <list> <minutes | off> (how long its end is waited for: a breakout's wait for every team before the regroup, 30 min unless set), team <list> <team> add <step | item> | remove <item> | clear | list (in a breakout that team runs exactly these items; the others share the rest in turn).

THE TEAMS WINDOW'S WORDS (each is one press there, and works the same typed). add <team> <name> ... puts them on a team (a new name makes it; a name of several words in "quotes"); put on a team that is on, a character leaves the other teams that are on, while a team that is off keeps its own list. remove [<team>] <name> ... takes them off that team, or off every team (a leader pick goes with it). new [<team>] makes an empty team (no name: the first free Team <n>); duplicate <team> [<new name>] makes a copy switched off; empty <team> takes everyone off it. class <name> <class | -> sets the class a character plays for building teams (the class its own box says always wins). unpin <name>, unpair <number | class class ...> and unlead <character | class> take a pin, a class group or one of the leader order off; list shows them all. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> teams ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.loot
modules.summary: Console commands for loot: auto-looting and the loot rules, the group's loot method, handing drops out, the loot window, and coin splitting.
modules.description: Type them as eb <command> in the console, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to <who> <command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a status line, a chore under way or a refusal in plain words. The Lua behind them is eb.economy.loot (the per-drop decision, the corpse sweep, the leader's hand-out), eb.economy.lootrules (the rules document), eb.economy.grouploot (method words) and eb.economy.auction.

functions.name: loot

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on | off (looting as you go), status, rules, method, now. Default: status. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: For rules: the rule to show or change; for method: the method (leader, ffa, lotto, need before greed, round robin) and optionally a rarity, or apply to send it again.

functions.desc: Loot control: turn looting as you go on or off, show the loot status, show or change the loot rules, set the group's loot method, or loot the nearest corpse or chest in reach now.
functions.notes: eb loot method sets EB's own looting and, on the group's leader, the game's own group loot method - again when the group changes. Looting never happens in a fight. A rules file that does not read means no looting by EB at all, and the status says why. From a script: eco.loot:classify / lootGrab / setMethod. Also typed as: lootrules. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> loot ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: lootdistro

params.name: cmd
params.desc: resolve (the Resolve auction), assign (the leader's hand-out), status - and the wish list: add, remove, skip, scan, look, sync. Default: status. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: add / remove / look: the item; skip: <item> <who>; scan: <item>|<item> to check too.

functions.desc: Loot distribution: hand gear to the member who gains the most Resolve, assign drops from the leader's window, and follow the quotas each member still wants.
functions.notes: THE WISH LIST: an item on it is wished for every member that misses it (unless taken off with skip). scan: this character checks itself - its bags (read now), its bank as EB last read it, what it wears; sync: every member's check on this PC opens a wish for a member missing it and closes one for a member that owns it now (and says where); a member never checked is said, never taken for missing. The open wishes go to the loot rules (a wished drop to a member still missing it), beside the user's own file's wishes. Every 2 minutes, out of a fight, each box checks itself and the group leader syncs. From a script: eco.auction:award and the leader path of eco.loot:lootGrab. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> lootdistro ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: lootwin

params.name: cmd
params.desc: open, claim, close. Default: open. Default: open.

functions.desc: Drive the loot window by hand: open the nearest corpse's window, claim what is in it, close it.
functions.notes: claim runs as a chore while the game answers "working". A lottery or need-before-greed window wants one answer for all of it: claim says so instead of taking. From a script: eco.loot:lootGrab. Also typed as: lw. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> lootwin ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: coinsplit

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off, toggle or status. Default: status.

functions.desc: The game's even coin split for the group: on or off sets it on the group leader's box, status says it.
functions.notes: EB remembers your choice (eb-economy.json loot.coinSplit). On the box that leads its group, on / off also sets the game's own split in its Group Options window: the window opened, the coin split box pressed when it reads the other way, Apply, the window opened again - done only when the box reads the wanted way then. A member's box only remembers it (the game takes the split from the leader). A Group Options window you already have open is left alone. EB for InnerSpace holds the window until its live proof; from a script: eb.economy.coinsplit, game.SetCoinSplit. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> coinsplit ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: langloot

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status, list, want or sync. Default: status. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: want: the quest or its language (want off [quest] = not any more).

functions.desc: Language quests in a group: every member needs its own items - the first one examined starts the quest and the rest finish it - so each box says which quest it wants and what it holds, and the group leader's loot rules hand each item to a member still short of it.
functions.notes: A box needs a quest's item when it wants that quest or holds its item or the studied item; left = the quest's count + 1, less what it holds. status says, per quest, how many are held and left; sync (on the leader, and every 2 minutes by itself) wishes each item for the group members still short of it, beside the Loot Distro's wishes. The journal's own done state is not read here: a finished quest comes off with want off. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> langloot ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: stoponnotrade

params.name: state
params.desc: on or off; nothing says how it is.

functions.desc: The instance queue's No-Trade guard: with it on, the next loot window that holds a No-Trade drop pauses the queue - the run under way goes on, the next one waits (eb iqueue resume goes on).
functions.notes: Off by default and kept in EB's economy settings. Said once per window; a drop whose No-Trade flag does not read on this box never pauses it. The guard looks at the window before the loot job takes anything from it. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> stoponnotrade ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: checkloot
functions.desc: The open loot window's drops, each No-Trade one marked; nothing is taken and nothing is paused.
functions.notes: A drop whose No-Trade flag does not read on this box is said as unknown, never as tradeable. This box only.

modules.name: commands.monitor
modules.summary: The combat monitor from the console: a fight's timeline and what went wrong, the crew's damage and healing meters, who the crew waits on, and the crew's status board.
modules.description: The meters count what each box's own combat lines show; a box sends the crew only a short summary per fight, never its raw lines. A script meters a fight with eb.ui.monitor.parser and eb.ui.monitor.parse_feed.

functions.name: anal

params.name: cmd
params.desc: show (default), timeline, why, fix, export, watch, mark, save or status. Default: show.

params.name: arg
params.desc: after watch: target, me, mouse, id <n> or a name (a part of one); after mark: a note; after timeline: list, days <n> or a boss's name (the game's chat log).

functions.desc: Fight analysis: the EB Anal window, and on the console what it opened on (the tab worth opening on, what to do to fill it, or why it did not open), then the summary of the last fight (the default), its timeline, why (what held each cast back, row by row), fix (the cast-stack rows EB will not cast) and export.
functions.notes: The window opens on the tab that has something: a fight on or the newest one (Fight), the fights read from the game's chat log (Encounters), a timeline (Timelines), what is watched (Watch), else what is around you (Actors) - asked softly: a tab you set to always open on stays yours. Before anything is recorded every tab says what to do to fill it (pull something with it open, Scan, eb anal watch target, Read the log), and a read the proof gate holds back on this box (an actor's effects, a player's guild, the mouse-over) is named, with how it gets out (eb proof evidence for a proof run). The console answer says the same in words, never only "opened". why reads the cast stack as it is now, so it works without a fight. watch puts that actor on EB Anal's Watch tab (EB Anal opens: it reads only while open; mouse reads the actor under the mouse 3 s later - hover it in the game), mark marks this fight (with a note), save writes this run, status says what is watched and the fights and marks so far. In the window: Name has and a kind narrow the Actors list, Scan reads it again, My target puts the target in the inspector, a click on a watched row shows its own changes, and every row has a Copy. eb anal watch id 4242; eb anal mark the adds came early. THE GAME'S CHAT LOG (logs\<server>\eq2log_<character>.txt in the game's folder, written while /log is on): timeline list reads it for the named fights in it, timeline days <n> sets how many days of it are read (0 = all of it, 30 at first), timeline <a boss> makes that boss's timeline from every pull of it (Copy for ACT / For the hub save it as for this run's). EB Anal opens for those two and reads the log a slice at a time while it is open, never in the press; the Timelines tab's Your chat log does the same, and the Encounters tab reads every fight in the log in full (its combatants and their abilities, the foes' hits that took several of you, who died and to what, what was said; Follow the newest fight reads on as the game writes). Nothing from the log goes into a file. eb anal timeline days 7; eb anal timeline Warden of the Fixture Vault. Also typed as: analysis, analyze, an. This box only.

functions.name: meters

params.name: cmd
params.desc: show (default), current or export. Default: show.

functions.desc: The crew's damage and healing meters: show opens the window; current says this fight's numbers.
functions.notes: show opens the window through the overlay; where the overlay cannot start, the answer says why. parser:current() gives the same numbers from a script. Also typed as: dps, acttab. This box only.

functions.name: announcements

params.name: cmd
params.desc: last (default), show, clear or status. Default: last.

params.name: arg
params.desc: after last: how many (10 when left out, at most 40); after show: on or off.

functions.desc: The game's on-screen announcements this box got - the big lines across the middle of the screen (a quest update, a fight's next phase): the last ones, newest first, with how long ago. show on says each one here as it comes.
functions.notes: EB keeps the last 40 of this session, as the screen shows them (a name for each link, no colour codes). show on is kept for this character (the setting announcements.show) and show off stops it. status says whether this box hears them at all: EB for InnerSpace hears the game's own announcements, EB Boxer none yet. A coordination rule answers one (its trigger: a line or an on-screen warning), and a script asks require("eb.onscreen.announcements").seen(words, since) - were these words on screen since then. eb announcements last 3; eb onscreen show on. Also typed as: onscreen. This box only.

functions.name: waiting
functions.desc: Who the crew is waiting on: each box and what it is doing, this box's brain and its instance run.
functions.notes: eb.relay.group's barrier says the same from a script. This box only.

functions.name: crew

params.name: cmd
params.desc: show (default), status or link. Default: show.

params.name: arg
params.desc: after link: on, off, status, hub <address:port>, host on | off, key [new | replace] or pc <name>.

functions.desc: The crew board: show opens the At a Glance window; status says one line per box - its zone, mode, health and power. link puts several PCs in one crew: off unless you turn it on.
functions.notes: show opens the window through the overlay; where the overlay cannot start, the answer says why. eb status crew says what this box hears of the others. THE CREW ACROSS PCs (eb crew link). Every box already hears the boxes of its own PC; with the link on it also joins the crew hub over the network, and the crew's lines and states cross PCs: eb all reaches every box of every PC, eb crew status lists another PC's boxes as <pc>/<box> (eb to <pc>/<box> reaches one of them; eb to is3 stays on this PC). Set it up once: eb crew link hub <address:port> on every PC (the network address of the PC that keeps the hub and a port for it), eb crew link host on on that PC only (a box there keeps the hub; when it goes, another box of that PC takes it over), the crew key on every PC, then eb crew link on (this PC's other boxes: eb relay all crew link on, or they join when they next start). status says how it stands: joined or dialing, who keeps the hub, whether the key is set, the name this PC goes by (the machine's own; eb crew link pc <name> when two PCs share one) and the boxes heard from other PCs. THE CREW KEY is a secret every PC proves to the hub (it never travels: the hub and each box prove they hold it). It is ONE line in a file of this PC's own, eb-crew.local.key in your own data folder (boot.json "data", the folder every EB of this PC shares): eb crew link key new makes one there (EB Boxer: from the system's random source), then copy that file to the same folder on each other PC; or write one of 16 characters or more yourself, the same on every PC. EB never shows it, logs it or puts it on a command line; eb crew link key says only whether it is set and where. A box you play by hand (paused, or EB stopped there) still never moves for a line from another PC. eb crew link hub <address:port>; eb crew link on; eb to pcb/is1 pause. Also typed as: fleet. This box only.

functions.name: sessionwatch

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (default), list, on, off, freeze or gone. Default: status.

params.name: value
params.desc: freeze / gone: whole seconds (freeze 10 to 600, 30 unless set; gone 30 to 3600, 180 unless set; gone always after the freeze).

functions.desc: Session watch: this PC's game sessions watched by their own crew. A session not heard for the freeze seconds froze, heard again it recovered, not heard for the gone seconds (or its EB stopped) it is gone; one box of the PC says each change on its console and raises SessionFrozen, SessionRecovered or SessionGone for your scripts.
functions.notes: Off until you turn it on, and saved for the whole PC (EB's settings file every box of the install shares): on, off, freeze and gone take effect on every box of the PC at once. It reads nothing from the game: every box already says who and where it is every 2 seconds, and a quiet one is what it watches. A zone load is not a freeze (a box that starts zoning says so first); a box of another PC (the crew link) is its own PC's to watch. The box that speaks is the lowest session number that is up, the changed one left out (is2 says that is1 froze, and that it came back). The events carry box, name, state, was, quietS, forS, why and reporter. Over IRC a nick you allow asks the same list with -List_Sessions. eb sessionwatch on; eb sessionwatch freeze 45; eb sessionwatch list. Also typed as: swatch. This box only.

functions.name: effects

params.name: cmd
params.desc: window (default), on, off, player, npc, merge or status. Default: window.

params.name: state
params.desc: after player / npc: on or off.

functions.desc: The Effect Tracker: what effects are called and what they say they do, zone by zone, for whoever writes the zone's fight files. With no word its window opens; on records the detriments that land on you (Player), npc on the effects on the mobs you fight (NPC), off both.
functions.notes: Both are off in every new session. Each effect is asked its words once, ever (one examine at a time, under the game layer's own budget), so a zone you ran before may show nothing new; both stand still while the Scanner records. The NPC capture leaves out a name on its ignore list (players' own casts: 74 as shipped, yours added or taken off in the window). Each character keeps its own record (data\ebeffects\<character>.json); merge puts every character's record of the zone you are in together (data\ebeffects\merged_<zone>.json, no character named in it). A right-click on a row in the window copies the lines a fight file takes for it. On EB for InnerSpace a mob's effects are read once that read passes its live proof. eb effects on; eb effects npc on; eb effects merge; eb effects status. Also typed as: effecttracker. This box only.

modules.name: commands.nav
modules.summary: The walking commands: walk to a spot, follow someone, walk to a named mark, keep routes out of a spot, hold a camp, go to a group member, record a path - the in-zone half of movement, typed or run from a script.
modules.description:
Every command here answers at once: a walk it starts runs on EB's frame pulse and the command says "issued", so a script can send it and carry on. A crew scope runs it on other boxes too: eb all follow Tankard, eb to is2 follow Tankard.

Movement is one thing: a walk along a route on the zone's .nav mesh, with the movement keys. Nothing here moves a character any other way - no straight run, no fallback walk, no swim across open water, no flying. A spot the mesh has no route to is not walked to: the command says why and the character stays where it is. A zone with no mesh refuses every walk, even a short step. Where the mesh joins two floors (a drop, a jump, a climb) the walk takes the link by itself: one tap of the jump key for a jump or a climb, none for a drop. A lift on record for the zone (the mesh fixes' lifts) is ridden: the walk stands on its board spot, clicks its lever or button once when it has one, stands still for the lift's wait and ride, then steps off at the exit.

Every command here is answered on EB for InnerSpace; check from a script with reg:unattached({ domain = "nav" }), which lists none of them.

How to walk the crew to a spot: 1. Save it once: eb marks set <name> where you stand. 2. Send everyone there: eb all marks go <name>. 3. Or have them follow you: eb others follow <your name>. 4. A walk or a follow ends when it arrives. To end one early: eb walk stop (the walk a command started), eb follow off (a follow), eb stop (everything EB is doing on the box) - or a script calls eb.nav.stop().

functions.name: walk

params.name: target
params.desc: x y z (or x,y,z), or the name of a route, a mark, something in sight or a map point; a route with ,<times> or ,loop after it; stop ends the walk.

params.name: how
params.desc: After a spot: fly asks for a flight (on a flying mount, when the zone lets you fly - EB decides the way and walks the rest), nofly keeps the trip on foot. eb walk 120 4 -88 fly. Every other nav word (precision, doors, nodoors) goes with eb nav to.

functions.desc: Walk to a spot in this zone over the zone's mesh, its drops, jumps and climbs on the way: x y z (or x,y,z), or the name of a route you recorded, a mark, something in sight by that name (the nearest whose name holds the words, within 80 m) or a map point. A spot the mesh has no way to is not walked to: the walk fails, says why, and nothing moves. Examples: eb walk 120,-4,388 / eb walk bank run / eb walk patrol,3 / eb walk patrol,loop. SOMETHING IN SIGHT BY ITS WORDS: an actor called exactly that first; else every word in a name, else in the title under it (eb walk broker, eb walk the nearest banker), else spread over the two (eb walk banker marcus) - an NPC before an object before a player, then the nearest; the, a, to, nearest are left out, and some words also mean others (vendor = merchant, repair = mender: data\eb\nav\actor_words.json). Nothing by those words: the walk is not made and the closest in sight are named. eb mm is the same word. eb walk stop ends the walk a command started. A route you recorded can be walked again and again: <route>,<times> walks it that many times (1 to 100), <route>,loop until eb walk stop (or another walk) ends it - the first time from the point nearest you, every time after from the route's first point.
functions.notes: Answers "issued" at once; the walk runs on the pulse. With no mesh for the zone it fails at once and says so - even for a short step. A spot sent by a crew line (eb all walk x,y,z) from a box standing in ANOTHER zone is not walked (those numbers belong to that zone): the box says "a spot in another zone"; a name is walked in this box's own zone. BOXES WALKING TOGETHER KEEP THEIR OWN SPOT: from eb all walk x,y,z the box that typed it walks to the point and every other box to its own spot 3 m round it (the crew's order, no two on one), stood on within 1 m - a spot the mesh does not reach in a straight line from the point is not used (that box walks to the point). Also typed as: mm. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> walk ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: follow

params.name: who
params.desc: A name (in quotes when it has several words), me, leader, target, an actor's number, or off; or a word for one: @PCTarget (the player you target), @NPCsTarget (the member the mob is on), @Tank, @Healer1-3, @DPS1-3, @Bard, @Enchanter, @Fighter1 / @Scout1 / @Mage1 / @Priest1 (the n-th of that kind in your group), or a cast stack alias (*MainHeal) - whoever it names right now; one that names nobody is said.

params.name: dist
params.desc: How close to stay, in metres.

functions.desc: Follow someone over the mesh by NAME: a crew member, or any player or NPC in range (the nearest of that name, an exact match first, case aside; when several share it, that is said once). A crew member is followed across zones: when it leaves the zone the follower walks to where it went, takes the zone line or the zone door and finds it again on the other side. Anyone else is found again by its name after a zone change, after the follower loses sight of it and after it despawns and comes back; a name not in range is looked for a short while, said once, then given up ("lost sight of <name>", never a guess). target follows the name of what this character has targeted at that moment; an actor's number follows that one actor only and ends with the zone (EB Map's Track sends it for one that has no name or shares it). me - or nothing, in a crew line - is the box that sent the line; off ends the follow, and eb follow alone says how it stands. It only walks: nothing is targeted, attacked or cast at. It never follows a character someone is playing by hand.
functions.notes: Answers "issued" at once; the follow runs on the pulse. A camp spot (eb leash) ends a follow, and so does eb stop; a follow of anyone outside the crew also ends when this character dies. Refused in words: your own name or number, nothing targeted, a dead one, a number nothing in this zone carries, and target in a crew line (the box that has it targeted sends eb others follow <name>). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> follow ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: marks

params.name: cmd
params.desc: set, list, go, del, cat, how or reload. Default: list.

params.name: name
params.desc: The place's name (with set, add x,y,z to mark that point instead of where you stand); go, cat and how take its number in the list too; list: words in a place's name, zone or category; cat: then the category (one word); how: then bell, spire, druid or any (every way again).

functions.desc: Your saved places, in every zone: set one where you stand (or at x,y,z), list them all numbered by category, go to one by its name or its number (a place in another zone: the trip there first, then the walk), del one; cat files a place under a category, how makes a trip to it ride one way only, reload reads the file again.
functions.notes: go answers "issued" and walks on the pulse; the rest answer at once. The places are this PC's own (eb-map-marks.json beside EB); a mark set by eb marks set is also a pin on the map ("a map mark" in the list). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> marks ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: blacklist

params.name: cmd
params.desc: add, remove, list or clear. Default: list.

params.name: what
params.desc: A radius in metres for the circle.

functions.desc: Keep every route out of the spot where you stand (blacklist), or allow it again (greenlight). Typed as eb bl or eb blacklist it blacklists; typed as eb gl, eb greenlight or eb prefer it greenlights: eb bl add 5 puts a 5 m circle where you stand, eb gl add lifts it.
functions.notes: The circles are this PC's own and take effect on the next walk. Also typed as: bl, gl, greenlight, prefer. This box only.

functions.name: nav

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status, path, where, why, door, info, load, unload, swimup, badlegs, to, plan, stop, end, panel, on, off, set or reset. Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: A zone, x,y,z for path or plan, x,y,z and the nav words for to, for swimup how long in ms and the height to come up to, clear for badlegs, on or off for panel, a setting and its value for set, a setting for reset.

functions.desc: The zone's mesh, the one mesh EB walks: status says whether it is loaded (or loading, or not in EB's mesh store); path <x,y,z> the length of the route to a spot over the mesh and in a straight line; where whether you stand on the mesh; why how the last walk ended; door the zone's door lines; info the mesh's own notes; load and unload a zone's mesh; swimup [ms] [height] swims straight up on the spot (5 s, at most 15 s) to get out of a hole under water - given a height, only when you are well under it; badlegs lists the legs walks wedged on in this zone - each is kept a day and told to the router before every walk here, so the same wall is not walked into again after a restart (a leg wedged on twice is routed round) - and badlegs clear forgets them. There is no other mesh or mover to pick between. THE TRIP: status also says this box's trip - its state (Idle, WaitingForMesh, Planning, Moving, Arrived, Stopped, Failed) and why, the waypoint it is on of how many and the metres to go, the mesh in use, a note when it is held, nav is switched off or EB is paused - and the nav settings changed from the shipped ones. to <x,y,z> walks there with the nav words after the spot: precision <m> (the spot counts as reached that close; under 2 m a spot to stand on), fly / nofly, doors / nodoors (the trip clicks no door). plan <x,y,z> plans the route and moves nothing: whole or partial, corners, metres, the work it took. stop (or end) ends the trip where it is. panel opens the Movement window; panel on makes it open by itself when a walk starts (and close when it ends), panel off stops that. off switches walking on the mesh off on this box - every walk is refused ("nav is switched off") - until on. set alone lists the nav settings changed; set <setting> <value> changes one, kept for this box and taken at once (the same as eb set nav.<setting>): arrive, finalarrive, arriveheight, lookmin, lookmax, lookangle, lookslew, looktime, pathwindow, heightbias, fellbelow, avoid, avoidlead, avoidside, avoidwant, avoidbias, stuckdistance, stuckstrikes, stuckreplans, retreatback, jumptries, blockms, doors, doortries, doorradius, mesh, panel, dumppath (each plan written to this PC's nav store as nav-lastplan.local.json), the flight's flyauto, autodetour, flyfar, sightahead, followfly, and the router's nearcost, stepcost, funnelclear, ledgeclear when the router takes them. reset puts one setting - or, alone, all of them - back to the shipped value.
functions.notes: Answers at once (to answers "issued": the walk runs on the pulse). A walk loads its zone's mesh by itself; load only starts it early. A walk waits up to 60 s for its zone's mesh while it loads or comes from the hub (state WaitingForMesh), then starts by itself; the wait is not part of its time. Also typed as: navigate. This box only.

functions.name: disperse

params.name: metres
params.desc: How far out the ring is: 3 to 60 metres (10 when left out).

functions.desc: Spread the group out evenly round you: typed on your box, every other box in your zone walks over the mesh to its own place on a ring of that many metres round you (no two share a place) and stops there. Nothing holds them there afterwards - a camp spot that holds a ring is eb others leash ring. Your own box does not move.
functions.notes: The others are sent eb others disperse <metres>; a box that is in another zone, or has not heard where you stand yet, does not move and says why. A new walk, eb walk stop or eb stop ends the walk to the ring. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> disperse ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: leash

params.name: cmd
params.desc: here, at, ring, rcs, drop, off, status, behind, front, right, left or angle. Default: here.

params.name: spot
params.desc: [x,y,z] [how many metres] [how far off it gives up]; rcs: tier <n> too; drop: the tier; behind / front / right / left: <npc> [metres from it] [how many metres it holds]; angle: <degrees> <npc> [metres].

functions.desc: Hold a camp: stay within some metres of a spot, walking back over the mesh whenever you are pulled or drift out. here holds where you stand; at x,y,z holds a point of this zone (the box walks there first); ring gives each box of a crew line its own place on a ring round the box that sent it; off lets go; status says where it holds. A second number is how far off it gives up: dragged farther than that, the box does not walk back (said once). In a fight the engine's own positioning stands, and the box walks back only well past the circle. A box its player walks out of the circle is never pulled back.
functions.notes: A leash ends a follow, and a zone change lets it go. CAMP SPOTS STACK IN TIERS and the top one is held: rcs puts one on top - where you stand, or at x,y,z; tier <n> names the tier, else the next one up (a raid mechanic's spot over the camp); drop lets the top tier go (or tier n) and the one below holds again; here / at / ring start a fresh camp (every tier above lets go); off lets every tier go; status lists them, the top first. The Camp Spots window (eb windows camp) shows the tiers and sets them by a press. BY AN NPC'S SIDE: behind, front, right or left <npc> [m] camps m metres (5 when left out) from a named NPC on that side of the way it faces - its front is where it looks, its right is its own right hand; angle <degrees> <npc> [m] takes any side, clockwise from its face (0 front, 90 right, 180 behind, 270 left). The box walks there and holds within 2 m (a third number changes that). The NPC by its exact name first, else the nearest whose name holds the words (in quotes when the name ends in a number); for a crew line (eb all leash behind <npc>) each box finds the NPC itself, and one that does not see it says so and stays. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> leash ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: gate

params.name: cmd
params.desc: scan, open or forget. Default: scan.

functions.desc: Doors and gates: scan lists the ones within 25 m (the zone's door lines and the live doors; a live door not on a line yet is learned on this PC), open clicks the nearest or the named one with its own verb, forget drops a door EB learned (a shipped line stays). Zone lines and teleporters are never clicked. eb door is the same command; a script opens a door with eb.nav.tryDoor.
functions.notes: The Zones window (eb windows zones) has a Door lines tab: a zone's door lines, the shipped ones and the ones this PC learned; in the zone you stand in Walk to one, Open it or Scan here by a press; for any zone give a door another verb in its box or forget a learned one - both kept on this PC beside the shipped lines, which never change. Also typed as: door. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> gate ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: navlink

params.name: cmd
params.desc: start, add, undo, cancel, save, del, jump, climb, ride, drop or list. Default: list.

functions.desc: Record a crossing the mesh cannot find, walked once by hand: eb navlink jump (or climb, or drop) marks the near side where you stand; cross it, then say the same word again where you land and the bridge is recorded, on this PC, and the router uses it from then on. list shows this zone's bridges. start, add, undo, cancel, save and del do the same step by step and remove one. A lift or a moving platform (ride) is refused: it is a lift entry, not a bridge. A walk takes the links by itself - no key press needed.
functions.notes: Also typed as: nl. This box only.

functions.name: record

params.name: cmd
params.desc: start, drop, stop, save, cancel or status. Default: status.

functions.desc: Record the path you walk as a route of waypoints (one every few metres, on a sharp turn and on a climb or a drop): start, drop a precise point where you stand, save it under a name (still recording), stop, cancel; status says how it stands. Routes are this PC's own, kept per zone. eb walk <name> walks one over the mesh, point by point.
functions.notes: Also typed as: rec. This box only.

functions.name: poi
functions.desc: Walk to a named point of this zone that holds every word you type: EB's own marks first, then the game's own map points (banks, mailboxes, bells, griffons, inns, zone doors). With no name it says what is known here, by kind.
functions.notes: For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> poi ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: gtgm
functions.desc: Go to a group member once, and stop within a few metres: in sight, or where the crew last heard it, or its zone first by the travel network. It runs on the box that types it only - never sent to the group by itself. eb follow does the same and keeps following.
functions.notes: Also typed as: gotomember, navtomember. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> gtgm ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: regroup

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (default), on, off or now. Default: status.

params.name: metres
params.desc: How far a member may be before it is called back (15 when left out).

functions.desc: Keep the group together, on the group's leader: a crew member more than 15 m away, with the group out of a fight for a minute, is called back and walks to the leader on the zone's mesh (the same walk as eb gtgm). on, off, now (call them back once), status.
functions.notes: Never in a fight, never during an instance run, never a member that follows someone already, and never a character played by hand: the member's own box says why it stayed. Off until you switch it on. This box only.

functions.name: face

params.name: how
params.desc: me, target, or a heading in degrees.

functions.desc: Turn this box, where it stands: eb others face me turns the others the way this box faces (each reads the sender's heading where it sees it); target turns to the target; a number turns to that heading, in the game's own degrees (as /loc shows them). Nothing says which way this box faces.
functions.notes: A turn only - nothing walks. A box that does not see the sender says so and stays as it is. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> face ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: movekeys

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), set or reset. Default: list.

params.name: what
params.desc: set: the role, then the key; reset: a role or all.

functions.desc: The game keys EB's walker holds and taps - your own binds in the game: list shows each role's key (forward, back, turn left / right, strafe left / right, jump, swim up / down, crouch, run / walk) and where it came from (yours, EB's default, set at start); set <role> <key> names one; reset [<role> | all] puts EB's default back.
functions.notes: A client whose A and D strafe names its turn keys here (or EB turns with the game's face command by itself and says so: eb set nav.steer face keeps that). A key is kept for the character (the setting keys.<role>, the same rows as EB Settings > Movement, folded) and taken at once and at every start; a name EB cannot press is refused in words. There is no auto-run key: EB moves by the mesh. Also typed as: movementkeys. This box only.

functions.name: camera
functions.desc: Put the game's camera back behind the character.
functions.notes: Held back until its live proof, and it says so. eb all camera reset does it on every box. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> camera ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: jump
functions.desc: Jump once, with this character's own jump key (eb movekeys says which).
functions.notes: eb all jump jumps every box; a box played by hand is left alone (a crew line says so). EB Boxer has no jump key yet, and says so. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> jump ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: crouch
functions.desc: Crouch, or stand up again: one tap of this character's crouch key (eb movekeys says which) - the same tap the fear walk makes.
functions.notes: No key set for it: it says how (eb movekeys set crouch <key>). A box played by hand is left alone. EB Boxer has no crouch yet, and says so. (The game's client has no crouch command of its own: the key is the way.) For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> crouch ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: runwalk
functions.desc: Run or walk: one tap of the game's own run / walk switch with your key for it (Shift+R unless you moved it: eb movekeys set run / walk <key>) - the same tap the fear walk makes. The game's own switch command goes instead once its live proof lets it out.
functions.notes: A pace switch, not a move: nothing moves by it. On EB Boxer it is the client's own switch, held back until its live proof, and it says so. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> runwalk ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: closer
functions.desc: Follow closer: a metre nearer to the one this box follows now, each time (2 m at the nearest).
functions.notes: Nothing followed here: it says so (a Follow button first). A follow a button's line gave steps from the distance it gave; one typed by hand from 4 m, EB's own start. eb all closer steps every box that follows. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> closer ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: farther
functions.desc: Follow farther back: a metre farther from the one this box follows now, each time (20 m at the farthest).
functions.notes: Nothing followed here: it says so. eb all farther steps every box that follows. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> farther ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.quest
modules.summary: The quest commands: the quest-line runner, power-level routes, the pack queue, the journal readers, languages, mission timers, single quest actions, NPC dialogs and the overseer.
modules.description:
Type them in the console after the console word, run them from a script with reg:dispatch or eb.dispatch, or send them to the crew with all / others / to. Each one answers: eb ql and eb pl say what is running (or that nothing is), eb queue the queue, eb dialog what an NPC shows. What EB cannot read yet it says in words: a journal read that is held back until it is proven in the game, a window whose elements are not captured, or a folder this host cannot list. A script can also drive quest packs and power-level routes through the Lua runners (eb.quest, eb.plroutes).

HOW TO RUN A QUEST PACK FROM A SCRIPT. 1. Bind the runner: local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps). 2. Load the pack and start it. 3. Call quests.step(run) once per tick from an EB task or a brain goal, handing travel, fights and loot to your nav, combat and loot. 4. Keep quests.pointer(run) after each step_done.

functions.name: ql

params.name: cmd
params.desc: load, start, resume, pause, cancel, skip, status (the default) or list. Default: status.

functions.desc: The quest-line runner: load a pack, start it, resume it, pause, cancel, skip a step, see its status, or list the packs.
functions.notes: With nothing running, eb ql status says so and shows the usage line. Also typed as: questline, q1. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> ql ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: pl

params.name: cmd
params.desc: start, stop, pause, resume, next, status (the default), list, route or map. Default: status.

params.name: route
params.desc: The route: its id, its name or its short code; after it, step <n> starts the route (or shows it on the map) at that step.

functions.desc: Run a power-level route and steer it while it runs: start it (from a step), pause and resume it, end the step in hand, stop it, see where it is, list the routes or a route's STEPS, or show a route on EB Map.
functions.notes: eb pl start <route> step 3 begins at step 3 (a step taken out of the plan: the next one in it). eb pl pause holds the route where it is - a fight goes on, and an instance run the route started runs to its end; eb pl resume goes on. With no route going, eb pl resume picks the last one up at the step it was on (kept per character). eb pl next ends the step in hand and goes on to the next one. eb pl list lists the routes; eb pl map [<route>] [step <n>] opens the Power Level window on the route with "Show on the map" on. eb pl alone, typed, opens the Power Level window. A LANGUAGE STEP: a hunt step that names a language makes every box want that language quest's items from the step's start (eb all langloot want <language> - the leader's loot rules hand each box its own); the step loots its kills even with its own loot off; the want is let go at the next step, at the route's end and when it stops. Also typed as: powerlevel. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> pl ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: queue

params.name: cmd
params.desc: add, start, stop, status (the default) or clear. Default: status.

functions.desc: A queue of quest packs run one after another: add, start, stop, status, clear.
functions.notes: Also typed as: que. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> queue ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: queststep
functions.desc: Show the active step of a quest, as the journal has it.
functions.notes: The journal is read from the game's quest updates: a quest the game has not said anything about this session answers that, in words. Also typed as: qstep. This box only.

functions.name: qsteps
functions.desc: List every step of a quest.
functions.notes: Also typed as: queststeps. This box only.

functions.name: questdone

params.name: cmd
params.desc: scan (the default), upload or resync. Default: scan.

functions.desc: Keep this character's list of completed quests: scan reads it from the journal, resync reads it again from the start.
functions.notes: Also typed as: questsdone. This box only.

functions.name: lang
functions.desc: Learn a language through its quests.
functions.notes: Also typed as: language. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> lang ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: linguist

params.name: what
params.desc: The language (and budget <coin>: the most the primer may cost); or where (which Linguist this box goes to, and why), list (the Linguists) or stop (end the trip).

functions.desc: Learn a language a Linguist sells - Halasian, Oggish, Ratongan, Stout or Ykeshan: the primer in the bags is used at once; else this box goes to its Linguist, walks up, buys the primer and uses it.
functions.notes: Which Linguist: the one of the zone this box stands in, else the one of its errand city (eb errands city, else its side's home city), else the first of its side. The trip is EB's own travel (bells, spires, rings, the hall - never the fast-travel map); the primer is bought with the purchase question answered and used from the bags. The buy is capped: budget <coin> (5g, 1p, 2p50g) names the most the primer may cost, 1 platinum when none is named; over it, or a price that does not read, nothing is bought and the trip says so. One trip at a time; eb all linguist <language> sends every box its own way; a box you play by hand is never sent. Also typed as: primer. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> linguist ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: taskfile

params.name: cmd
params.desc: run, or list (the default). Default: list.

params.name: name
params.desc: run: the task file, by its path under the task folder (Examples/Library_of_Erudin_Heroic) or its name in words (grab tso daily double); list: words the path holds.

functions.desc: The task files that came with EB (the Tasks window's "Task files" tab): list them by folder, or run one as a quest line of its own.
functions.notes: A word that names two task files is answered with both - nothing is guessed - and a path with .. or a drive is refused. A task file is the same table a quest is, so it runs on the quest runner (eb ql status shows it, eb ql cancel stops it) and starts from its first step every time: it keeps no place of its own. The manifest, the maintenance order and the mission tables are no tasks and are never listed or run. A task that needs a mission table (Grab TSO Daily Double: the instance run of the mission the NPC gives goes in the instance queue) reads it from the task folder. Also typed as: taskfiles. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> taskfile ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: missiontimer
functions.desc: Show the mission and collection reset timers.
functions.notes: The journal's Mission Timers tab is read only once EB has proven that read in the game: until then the answer says so. Also typed as: missions, missiontimers. This box only.

functions.name: action

params.name: name
params.desc: The verb and its arguments, as a pack step writes them.

functions.desc: Run one quest pack verb by name, on its own, outside a pack.
functions.notes: Also typed as: act. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> action ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: actor

params.name: name
params.desc: The actor (quote a name of several words).

params.name: verb
params.desc: The verb to use on it. A verb that cannot be sent by its name falls back to the double-click and says so.

functions.desc: Interact with a quest actor: hail it, click it, or use one of its verbs.
functions.notes: For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> actor ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: dialog

params.name: cmd
params.desc: reply (the default), choice, ok or close. Default: reply.

functions.desc: Answer an NPC conversation, a choice window or a reward window, picking the allowed path.
functions.notes: With no conversation open, eb dialog says so. Also typed as: dlg. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> dialog ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: questhelper

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off, toggle or status (nothing: status).

params.name: first
params.desc: first: with several replies, always pick the first.

functions.desc: A helper while you quest by hand on this box: a conversation that offers one reply gets it picked; with first, the first of several is always picked. Standing still with no conversation up, a quest giver within 10 m is targeted and hailed, and a quest object within 5 m is clicked - each at most once in 30 s. eb qh is the same command.
functions.notes: Never an object that would move you: a zone exit, a door, a portal, a bell, a spire, a flight or a banner is left alone. Nothing happens in a fight, while casting, moving or dead, in a guild hall, or while EB is stopped on this box. Whether an NPC offers a quest waits for its live proof: until then no giver is hailed, and status says so. Kept for this character. The MCP's QH 1 runs eb questhelper on first on every box. Also typed as: qh. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> questhelper ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: overseer

params.name: cmd
params.desc: run (the default), stop, status, window, go, buy, trip, missions, scrolls, agents, share, needs, set, options, who, auto, spares, side, starter, tutorial, brokerafter, broker, mark, agent, owned, lookup or help. Default: run.

params.name: arg
params.desc: What the word takes: go / buy season <1-7 or any> colour <any, blue, yellow, purple, green> num <1-50> copies <1-20> noscribe [off] destroy [off] gettogh [off] replenish price <copper> (buy stop / status too); agents list, add [destroy], scan or check <token> [bags]; share local, mygroup, irc or all [bags]; set <option> <value>; who local, mygroup, irc or all; on or off for auto, spares, brokerafter and starter (starter alone: the starter pack now); side home, good or evil; tutorial done or reset [character]; broker check, buy, list, cap <copper>, after on or off; agent <n>; lookup <agent or mission>.

functions.desc: EB Overseer, the game's Overseer missions in one command. run: one pass now - the finished missions turned in, the rewards taken, the boxes and scrolls in the bags added, new missions started with the agents whose traits suit them (run auto: the start the pass by itself makes, with its gates). stop: the pass, the missions job, a trip and a share on this box. status: what the pass does or did, the day's allowance, the next missions done, this box's driver. window: EB's Overseer window. go: Go buy missions (the trip to an Administrator Agent, a new character's first agents, the buy, the broker when that is on, then the pass); buy: the trip and the buy; trip: the trip alone. missions / scrolls: the bags' missions added now / listed. agents, share, needs: every box's agents, the spare cards shared, who still needs what. set / options: this character's options. who, auto, spares, side, starter, brokerafter, broker cap, mark, agent: this PC's preferences and the agent it buys from. tutorial, broker, owned, lookup, help.
functions.notes: The scope words go in front: eb all overseer run, eb relay mygroup overseer go, eb relay irc overseer agents scan - each box runs its own line, and a box played by hand turns a crew line down and says why. The pass runs as the brain's goal (eb.loops, eb.overseer.pass) with the character's options and the mission facts; a stop shuts a window EB opened before it ends. By itself it runs at most once an hour and when a mission it started is done (one timer per running mission in eb timer list) - never on a box played by hand, in a fight, while a task list or another run drives the box, outside a guild hall when Only in a guild hall is on, nor where the Overseer window cannot be read yet. A word whose part is not on this box yet (the trip, the share) says so. A game read or press that waits for its live proof answers held, in words. Never a Station Cash button, never a cancel, a card destroyed only on your word. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> overseer ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: sharequest

params.name: quest
params.desc: The quest's name as the journal has it, in quotes when it has several words, or all.

functions.desc: Offer quests of the journal to the group: one by its name (a mission is a quest here), or all of them, one a second. The game offers each to the members near and shares the ones it can.
functions.notes: Not in a group: nobody to share with, and it says so. all reads the journal's quest names, which wait for their live proof like the share itself; while either is held back it says so and sends nothing. Also typed as: sharemission. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> sharequest ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: hail

params.name: who
params.desc: An actor's id (a button's ${Target.ID}: what the box that pressed it has targeted), a name (within 30 m), or nothing: the nearest NPC to talk to within 15 m.

functions.desc: Hail an NPC: target it and say the game's own /hail, which only ever talks - never a double-click on something that can be fought.
functions.notes: The MCP's Hail target sends eb ${ForWho} hail ${Target.ID}: every box hails what the presser has targeted (an actor's id is the same on every box in the zone). A box played by hand is left alone. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> hail ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: special
functions.desc: Click the nearest special object within 30 m (the glowing thing a zone wants clicked).
functions.notes: Nothing special in reach: it says so. eb all special clicks on every box; a box played by hand is left alone. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> special ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.relay
modules.summary: Talk to the crew from the console: put a crew word in front of any command, announce a line, put every box on the same target, invite and disband.
modules.description:
The way to send any command to the crew is the crew word in front of it: eb all <command> (every box, this one too), eb others <command> (every box but this one), eb to <who> <command> (the boxes named). Lines reach the other boxes over the crew relay and run there once; a relayed line is never sent on.

How to drive the crew from a script: 1. eb.dispatch("eb all pause") - every box pauses, this one too. 2. eb.dispatch("eb to is2 follow is1") - one box follows another. 3. eb.dispatch("eb announce pulling now") - one line every box shows.

Every command of this page answers; reg:unattached({ domain = "relay" }) lists any that a build leaves out.

functions.name: relay

params.name: line
params.desc: The crew word and the command line, for example "all pause", "to is2 follow is1", "here walk 10,2,30", "awake tse saved", "stagger 3 gha go" or "mygroup rebuff".

functions.desc: The written-out form of a crew line: eb relay all pause is eb all pause. The line starts with the crew word (all, others, to <who>, or local for this box only), then the command. More words reach a set of boxes each box decides for itself: here = every box standing in this box's zone, never a paused one, this box too (eb relay here walk 10,2,30 walks them all to that spot; a box in another zone stays put); awake = every box that is not paused, so a box you play by hand is left alone (eb relay awake tse saved); stagger [seconds] = every box that is not paused, each in its turn - this box at once, then the others one after another, 2 seconds apart unless you say, at most 30 (eb relay stagger 3 gha go); mygroup = this character's group, this box too, and this box alone when it is in no group (eb relay mygroup rebuff).
functions.notes: It is the same as putting the crew word in front of the command; typed with the crew word in front it is the command you typed. The older crew words read the same way: irc / group / anywhere = all, other = others, zone / zoneall = here, to / fw / ircfw <name> = to <name>, stagger <seconds> = stagger. A here line carries this box's zone to the others; a box whose zone does not match, or that is paused, runs nothing and says nothing. A stagger's turns follow the crew's order (the box ids, the box that sent it first); each box waits its own turn and says what it did when it runs. A mygroup line names the members of this character's group as the game shows them. Also typed as: gr, grouprelay. This box only.

functions.name: marked

params.name: state
params.desc: on, off, toggle or status (the default). Default: status.

functions.desc: Mark this character so a crew line can pick it: eb to marked <command> runs on every box whose character is marked. on, off or toggle sets this character's mark; status (the default) says whether it is marked and which boxes of the crew are. eb to <name> marked on marks that character; eb all marked off takes every mark off.
functions.notes: The mark is kept per character (it outlives a reload) and rides the box's crew state, so any box knows who is marked. On a crew line (eb all marked) a marked box says so and an unmarked one says nothing. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> marked ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: ocdo

params.name: line
params.desc: A console line, for example !c -cfw igw:Leadbox -letsgo -Ofol auto Leadbox.

functions.desc: Do one line of the console command language your own MCP layout's buttons carry (!c -command who args ...) with EB's own systems: each -command whose who names this box (else the line's -cfw) runs EB's version - follow, letsgo, holdup, pause, resume, assist, jump, zone, zonedoor, special, evac, cast, cast on a player, use item, cancel maintained, accept reward and the reply buttons. A command EB has no version of is listed back, never guessed.
functions.notes: Answered on this build. eb all ocdo <line> hands it to the crew and each box decides for itself whether the line names it - this is what a button of your own MCP layout sends when you press it in EB's MCP. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> ocdo ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: oc
functions.desc: Hand one line to the other automation running beside EB in this session: stop, pause, resume, or zonedoor <door> - for this character's group only. It never moves a box for EB: a follow is eb follow and a camp spot is eb leash.
functions.notes: Typed on this box only. EB's own pause and stop are eb pause and eb stop. This box only.

functions.name: announce
functions.desc: Show one line on every box of the crew (and this one).
functions.notes: For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> announce ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: tgt

params.name: id
params.desc: An actor's id or name; me; none, off or clear.

functions.desc: Target an actor on this box or on the crew. eb tgt <id> targets that actor (a spawn id is the same on every box in the zone, so eb all tgt <id> puts the crew on one target); eb tgt <name> the nearest actor with exactly that name, else the nearest whose name holds the words; eb tgt me this character; eb tgt none, off or clear drops the target.
functions.notes: Answers false with why when the game did not take the target (out of reach, no such actor). From a script, game.TargetActor(id) on each box does the same. Also typed as: tar, settarget. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> tgt ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: grab

params.name: what
params.desc: loc (default), zone, target, npc or special. Default: loc.

functions.desc: Where you are, in a line to paste into a quest, a route or an instance run: your spot and heading, the zone, your target, the nearest NPC or the nearest special (an object you can use) within 30 m.
functions.notes: Said on this box's console; nothing is sent anywhere. Every read is proven in the game. eb g is the same. Also typed as: g, grabcursor, gc. This box only.

functions.name: invite

params.name: cmd
params.desc: invite (default), disband, raid or leave. Default: invite.

functions.desc: Group up. With no name this box invites every crew character that is not in its group yet, in the order set in Settings > Group, up to a full group (type it on the leader; a crew line asking for it is refused, six boxes inviting each other is no group); a name invites that character; raid <name> sends a raid invite; disband or leave takes this box out of its group, and eb all invite disband breaks the group up. It never invites a character someone plays by hand without EB.
functions.notes: The game layer decides: an invite EB has not proven in the game yet is held back, and the answer says so and claims nothing. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> invite ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: mentor

params.name: who
params.desc: The group member to mentor (me in a crew line is the box that sent it).

functions.desc: Mentor a group member: this character drops to that member's level until eb unmentor. The member must be in this character's group and, when the crew has said the levels, below this character's level. eb all mentor <name>: every box above that member's level mentors it; the member itself says no and sends nothing.
functions.notes: A verb you type or press only - never a step of a quest line. The game's own /mentor is held back until it is proven live, and the answer says so (nothing is sent meanwhile). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> mentor ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: unmentor
functions.desc: Stop mentoring: this character goes back to its own level. eb all unmentor stops it on every box.
functions.notes: The game's own /unmentor is held back until it is proven live, and the answer says so. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> unmentor ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: event

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (default), on, off or fire. Default: list.

params.name: name
params.desc: The event name, for example ChatLine.

functions.desc: Look at EB's events from the console: list the event names, switch a watch on or off, or fire one to test a helper.
functions.notes: on says each one on this box's console, at most 4 a second (the rest counted); off <name> or off all stops it; fire raises it once marked as a test. Events never go to the crew. From a script use eb.events (on, emit, eventNames). This box only.

functions.name: share
