params.name: what
params.desc: plan, nogo, travelactor, get, list, grant, revoke, delete or status (the default). Default: status.

params.name: arg
params.desc: plan: the plan's name; nogo: a zone or all; travelactor: one of your travel objects or all; get / delete: the code; grant / revoke: the code and the EB account; list: plan, nogo or travelactor.

functions.desc: Share through EB's hub, one thing at a time and only when you ask: plan <name> shares one of your power-level plans, nogo [zone | all] your keep-out spots, travelactor [<it> | all] your own travel objects (eb travelactor add); each gets a short code. get <code> fetches a share by its code (a plan joins your plans under a new name, keep-out spots join your walker's avoid list, travel objects join your own - never over one of yours); list shows your shares and the ones shared with you; grant / revoke <code> <EB account> lets another EB account read one, or not; delete <code>.
functions.notes: No character name is shared: a share is scrubbed by its kind (a plan's camp puller becomes "me"; a keep-out spot is a zone, a spot and a radius; a travel object is its facts only - its name in the game, never the label you gave it, how it is used, its places, its spot - one in a guild hall goes as any guild hall, never with the hall's zone, a place naming a guild hall is left out, and one whose words hold a name of your crew is left out whole and said) and then by the names of this box's character and its crew - and refused, nothing sent, when a name would still leave. A share is readable only by you and the accounts you grant (the hub has no public list). EB Setup on this PC carries each one to EB's hub for you; the answer comes on the console. Script: require("eb.share.install").handle(app, { what = "get", arg = "PL-XXXXXXX" }). This box only.

functions.name: emote

params.name: words
params.desc: An emote word, your own line, or list.

functions.desc: An emote: one of the game's own by its word (bow, wave, cheer ...), or your own emote line of two words or more (the game's /emote). list names the game's emotes.
functions.notes: For a rule's or a timer's line too: EB Coordination's "run one eb command" with eb emote cheer, or eb timer add cheer 5m eb emote cheer. On a box played by hand (EB paused on it - never just its window in front) only a line typed or pressed there goes; a crew line, a rule's or a timer's is refused and said. Held at the proof gate until its proof (the emote command is not proven yet). For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> emote ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: tell
functions.desc: A tell to a character.
functions.notes: For a rule's or a timer's line too; on a box played by hand only a line typed or pressed there goes. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> tell ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: say
functions.desc: A line said in group or raid chat - the game's own chat (EB's crew line is eb announce).
functions.notes: For a rule's or a timer's line too; on a box played by hand only a line typed or pressed there goes. Held at the proof gate until the group / raid chat command is proven. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> say ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: agent

params.name: id
params.desc: The agent's own word for its line (letters, digits, _ and -, at most 32), written back beside the answer.

params.name: line
params.desc: The EB line to run, as typed after eb. Nothing: answer here, run nothing.

functions.desc: A line from EB's agent server (the tool an agent program reads this box through), answered in one small file (EB for InnerSpace). The server hands it to the session through InnerSpace's relay - InnerSpace.exe relay is3 eb agent <id> <line> - and EB runs the line as a line from outside: never a Lua line, never sent on to the crew, never moving a box you play by hand (paused, or EB stopped there). The answer goes to agent\<session>.json in your EB data folder: the session, the agent's id, ok, the answer's words and the time - no character, no account. With no line it answers here and runs nothing (the agent server's list asks every session that way).
functions.notes: The answer is written by the files service a moment later, never in the middle of a frame - one file a session, its latest answer. The agent's reads run at once; a line that would change something is proposed instead (eb inbox add <line> -- <why>) and waits in the Ops Inbox for your Approve. No button: a press would answer into a file nobody reads. The agent server: tools\eb_mcp\server.py --token says how to register it. This box only.

functions.name: irc

params.name: cmd
params.desc: join (nothing), end, window, status, say, allow, disallow, disallowall, allowlist, allowifinraid, raidallow or raiddisallow. Default: join.

params.name: text
params.desc: say: the words; allow / disallow: a nick; allowifinraid: a nick and a character.

functions.desc: EB IRC: this box joins the IRC server set up in the EB IRC window (eb irc), leaves the channel and the server (eb irc end - also off or leave; eb end irc is the same line), opens EB IRC to set it up (eb irc window), says where it is and what it heard (eb irc status), or says a line in the channel (eb irc say <words>). With nothing set up yet, eb irc opens the window and says what is missing. eb all irc joins every box; eb relay all end irc takes every box off.
functions.notes: The setup is this PC's own (every box reads the same one) and is kept in eb-irc.local.json in your EB data folder - never shipped, synced or shown; its secret words (the server's, NickServ's, the channel key) never show in a log, a report or a line. A box with no nick set goes by a short tag of this PC and its number, never a character's name (unless you tick Use my character's name). A line heard there runs only from a nick you allow - your own EB boxes on other PCs sign theirs with your crew key - and only the way EB runs a crew line or your MCP's console line; a private message, a notice or a CTCP request never runs. EB for InnerSpace uses InnerSpace's IRC extension (loaded once with ext -require isxim; held at the proof gate until it is proven); EB Boxer and Linux use EB's own client, which looks a server's name up off the game's own thread, so the game never waits for it (an older EB Boxer takes the server's address in numbers). Join when EB starts joins each box once its character is in the world. eb relay irc here <command> (EB Map's Every PC walk) runs the command on this PC's boxes in this zone, as eb relay here does, and sends it over IRC so a box on your other PCs runs it only when it stands in this zone and is not paused. WHO MAY SEND COMMANDS: allow <nick> adds one, disallow <nick> takes one back, disallowall takes them all back, allowlist names them (the PC's own file: every box of the PC in the channel takes a change at once). allowifinraid <nick> <character> allows that nick when the character is in this box's raid; raidallow makes the PCs of your raid in the channel allow each other's nicks - each proves a character of its own is in the raid by a short hash, so no character's name goes over IRC - and raiddisallow takes back only the nicks a raid allowed. THE PC'S WORDS FROM THE CHANNEL: a nick you allow may ask this PC for its sessions (-List_Sessions: up, frozen or gone), its launch profiles (-List_AutoLoginProfiles [-details | -profile <name>]), a launch (-LaunchAutoLogin <profile>, -LoadCharacter <character>) and change who may send commands with the channel's own words. One box of the PC answers - the lowest session of this PC in the channel, or the box a line names by its nick - and no answer names a character or a box. -KillSession is always refused: EB never ends a game session. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> irc ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.travel
modules.summary: The travel commands: go to another zone over the game's own travel network, preview the hops first, ride a zone's pads - every hop walked to on the mesh, never fast travel.
modules.description:
A trip rides the bells, wizard spires, druid rings, the guild hall and the zones' own pads, walking to each portal on the mesh and re-planning from wherever each ride lands. City bells never cross between the good and the evil cities. Each command answers at once; a trip runs on EB's frame pulse and the command says "issued". A hop whose portal the mesh has no route to stops the trip and says why - nothing is walked straight at it.

Fast travel is no part of a trip. It exists in one place, eb ft, and only on your own press: it is refused while a quest line, a power-level route or an instance run is going, and from any line a pack or a run sent.

Every command here is answered on EB for InnerSpace except eb hotzone; check from a script with reg:unattached({ domain = "travel" }).

How to take the crew to another zone: 1. Preview it: eb route <zone>. 2. Go: eb all goto <zone> - each box makes its own trip; a box that is already there stays. 3. Watch each box's status line for the hop it is on. 4. eb travelcancel pauses, resumes or cancels a trip.

functions.name: goto

params.name: zone
params.desc: The destination: a zone's short name (fixture_port) or its name, or a mark's name; with bell, spire or druid before or after it (eb goto fixture_port spire / eb goto spire fixture_port) the trip rides that network only - no route that way is said, and the plain eb goto plans every way.

functions.desc: Travel to another zone (or to a saved mark) over the game's own travel network: plan the hops, walk to each portal on the mesh, ride it, and plan again from where it lands.
functions.notes: Answers "issued" at once; the trip runs on the pulse. The fast-travel map is never used. MOUNTED TRIPS: with eb set travel.automount on (off unless you turn it on; eb all set ... for every box) each box mounts itself before it sets off - never a box paused for its player, in a fight, or on a mount already. ONE LEG SHORT: a zone no bell, spire or ring reaches is gone to through a zone beside it - the network to that zone (or none, standing in it), then its zone line: the way to it walked, the door opened the way the zone data says (its verb, a click, the list's entry); a line from the game's own map is walked into, and only when nothing happens is the zone door at hand clicked. A one-way trip (bell / spire / druid) never adds a zone line. A zone line whose zone data says more than stand and open the door runs step by step: a griffon or city-bell ride on the way, a talk's option, a moving platform called and waited for, a travel-map object, a wait for the zone's name, a door by part of its name. A zone door's list is picked by the place's exact entry, with or without "The ", or the one entry holding it; a door's verb that did nothing in 3 s is tried once more in lower case. ON THE WAY: a walk of more than 400 m rides the zone's griffon / sokokar / flight pads when that saves 200 m or more, then walks on, and a walk that failed 300 m or more from its goal rides once to the pad nearest it and walks again (never after a stop). A box in the air on its flying mount comes down before Call to Guild Hall - only over ground on the zone's mesh within 40 m, never in a fight; otherwise it says why and the call is not cast in the air. A guild hall with no spire or ring of its own but its portal wizard or druid: the hireling is hailed and its portal ridden. A travel item this box holds (eb travelnet methods) is a way from anywhere, taken last while on its timer. A hop into a zone with several arrival points picks the one of its own way (a druid ring's, a spire's, the docks for a bell). A spire, ring or bell that opens no map: the next one of its kind within reach is clicked. BY THE GUILD HALL FIRST: on a TLE server (eb travelnet info) the trip calls to the guild hall first whenever the hall has a way on; on a live server when this zone's own way on stands 1200 m or more from you. Only with Call to Guild Hall ready, never from inside a hall, once a trip; eb route shows it. THE TRAVEL GRAPH: on a live server a trip plans by the travel graph EB ships first - any number of doors in a row (Gerion's Revelations of Malice door into the Fabled zones, its list's row picked), the guild hall's teleporters, the bells, spires and rings - and EB's own ways after; on a TLE server EB's own ways first, the graph only when they find none (eb travelnet info says which). A graph way that fails hands the trip to EB's own ways from where you stand. An instance whose file names its own way (druid, spire, bell) keeps the graph off its hub trip. A TLE server's bells come with what each was seen to offer: a bell is never rung for a place it lacks (the Thundering Steppes bell relays). Also typed as: t, travel. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> goto ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: route
functions.desc: Preview a trip without moving: the hops, the network each rides, and which side this character travels as.
functions.notes: The preview answers alone: use eb goto to make the trip. Also typed as: plan. This box only.

functions.name: ft
functions.desc: Fast travel to a place, on your own press only. Refused while a quest line, a pack step, a power-level route or an instance run is going, and from any line a pack or a run sent - each says why. Everything EB decides by itself travels in the world: bells, spires, rings, the guild hall and the zone's own pads.
functions.notes: eb fasttravel is the same word. It is the one command that opens the fast-travel map. Also typed as: fasttravel. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> ft ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: transit

params.name: dest
params.desc: The station to reach - or a word of the pad data's tools first: list, info [zone], path <pad> to <pad>, connections <pad>, addpad <name> [griffon | sokokar | teleporter | flight] [hail | click] [actor], connect <pad> to <pad>, reload.

functions.desc: The zone's own pads: with no destination, list this zone's pads and where each flies; with one, ride the pads to that station, walking to each pad on the mesh.
functions.notes: With a destination it answers "issued" and rides on the pulse. THE TOOLS: list = the zones with pads on record; info = each pad of a zone, how it opens (hail its tamer / click it), its actor, where it flies; path = the hops between two pads of this zone and their time; connections = where one pad flies. addpad puts a pad of your own where you stand and connect a flight of your own between two pads of this zone - kept on this PC (the shipped pad data is never written) and used by every ride and trip at once; reload reads the pad data again. A trip whose way is a pad flight into another zone walks to that pad, flies, and goes on from the zone it lands in. Also typed as: tr. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> transit ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: bell
functions.desc: Travel by this zone's bell (docks, city bell, a guild hall's bell) to a place on its map; with no place, say where the bell goes. The walk to the bell is on the mesh; eb goto <zone> rides bells for you.
functions.notes: For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> bell ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: travelmap
functions.desc: With no place, list the places of the travel window that is open (stand at a bell, spire or ring). With a place, pick it: when no window is open the nearest bell, spire or ring is used to open one first. Travel inside the world, never the fast-travel shortcut. A ride inside the zone it starts (a griffon, a city bell to the docks) is waited out until the box lands - 40 m from where it picked, then still for 3 s; given up after 5 minutes.
functions.notes: For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> travelmap ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: gha

params.name: cmd
params.desc: go, upkeep, exit, attune or porter. Default: go.

params.name: dest
params.desc: porter: the place as its list names it, or its number in the list.

functions.desc: The guild hall: go calls you to it and waits for the hall, exit leaves by its door, attune ties you to the hall's travel beacon (stand near it), porter [place] walks to the hall's Coldborne EverPorter over the mesh, clicks it and picks the place in the list it opens (by the name the list shows, or its number; with no place the list is left open for eb zonedoor). EB never pays the hall's upkeep: upkeep says so.
functions.notes: Also typed as: gh, guildhall. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> gha ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: zonedoor

params.name: entry
params.desc: A number, the place as the list names it, or last.

functions.desc: Pick in the zone-door list that is open on screen - an instance door, a porter, a zone's versions: its number, the place as the list names it (any case, with or without "The ", or the one entry holding the name - when two hold it nothing is picked and the entries are said), or last. It never clicks anything in the world; with no list open, or a list still showing its placeholders, it says so. eb all zonedoor 2 picks on every box that has the list open.
functions.notes: To open a door's list first: eb actor <door> <its verb>, or walk up and eb gate open <door>. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> zonedoor ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: hub

params.name: zone
params.desc: An instance, or the hub zone's short name.

functions.desc: Take this box to the hub zone of an instance - the zone with its entrance, where the crew gathers before a run - by the zone's own transit, on foot over the mesh. eb all hub <instance> sends every box there by its own way; nobody is led.
functions.notes: An instance you named with eb hubs add goes to the hub you gave it. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> hub ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: zoneroute

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), show, play, pause, resume, stop, status, record, add, undo, save, cancel, delete or reload. Default: list.

params.name: what
params.desc: show / play / delete: the route's name; record: <name> [to <place>]; add: here (a walk to where you stand - a goto first when the zone changed since the last step), an EB line (eb transit North Post, eb actor <door> use), or wait <minutes>.

functions.desc: Your stored zone routes: a way somewhere the planner does not find by itself, written down step by step and played back - each step an EB line (a goto, a walk, a door's verb, a pad ride, a bell) or a wait.
functions.notes: Recording: record, then add each step as you go, then save (cancel drops it; undo takes the last step out). Every line is checked as a task list's is - fast travel is never a step. play runs the route through EB's task runner: each line sent and waited out (its walk, its zone change), a refused line said and passed; pause holds it before the next step, resume goes on, stop ends it, status says where it is. The routes are kept on this PC for every character (eb-zone-routes.local.json); eb all zoneroute play <name> plays it on every box. Also typed as: zr, zoneroutes. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> zoneroute ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: traveltest

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (the default), start, stop, skip or report. Default: status.

params.name: mode
params.desc: start: all (the default), bell, druid, spire or hubs - bell / druid / spire: that network's places; hubs: the three; all: those and every zone on record (no instance copy). Default: all.

functions.desc: The travel test: this box travels the network zone by zone and writes down what happened - a pass when it lands in the zone, a fail with the reason when it does not.
functions.notes: Each box goes in its own order (shuffled by its character's name, so a crew does not pile into one zone): a zone it stands in already is a pass at 0 s; a trip has 3 minutes, then it is cancelled and failed; between zones it goes back to its guild hall (waiting for Call to Guild Hall when it is on its timer). skip cancels the zone under way (written down as skipped); stop ends the run. The results are kept per character on this PC (eb-traveltest.local.json): report says the last run - how many passed, and each fail with its reason. Never the fast-travel map. eb all traveltest start runs it on every box; a box you play by hand is never sent. Also typed as: tt. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> traveltest ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: portalwait

params.name: what
params.desc: druid or spire (none: either), then the place to pick on its map (none: the map is left open for eb travelmap <place>).

functions.desc: Through a group port: after a wizard's or a warlock's Translocate (Translocator Spires) or a fury's or a warden's Circle of Growth (a druid portal), this box waits for the portal, walks up to it, opens it and picks the place on its map, then zones.
functions.notes: The portal is looked for by its own name at once and by the other names it goes by after 5 s; a minute with no portal is said and nothing moves. eb all portalwait druid <place> sends every box through - the caster's box too; cast the port on the caster (its own button) when the boxes wait. A box you play by hand is never sent by a crew line; a server whose policy holds the group port back (eb travelnet info) refuses it. Also typed as: classport. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> portalwait ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: travelactor

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), destinations, use, add, edit, remove, reload or forget. Default: list.

params.name: what
params.desc: destinations / forget: the travel object (a part of its name will do); use: the object, then the place to pick in its list (a list object); add: [target | its name] [verb <its verb> | click | list | hail] [needs <feature>] [to <place> / <place> ...]; edit: one of yours, then what changes (verb <its verb>, click, list, hail, to <place> / ..., needs <feature> or needs none, name <new name>, spot); remove: one of yours.

functions.desc: Travel objects a guild hall (or a zone) holds that send you somewhere: the Tunneler of Thalumbra, the Pennant of Skyshrine Loyalty, the Yon Gorroth Teleporter, the Coldborne EverPorter, the guild hall teleporters EB's travel data names (a Draconic Teleporter's rows ...), and your own - each used with its own verb, a click, a pick in the list it opens, or a hail (a tamer, a guide: hailed, its travel reply answered, the place picked on its station list).
functions.notes: A trip takes one only when no bell, spire or druid ring goes there: Call to Guild Hall, then the object (eb route shows it as "travel object"), and never one into a zone this account lacks (eb features) or one that needs what it lacks. A hall's object stands there only when the guild placed it: a hall where one was not found is kept on this PC and not planned again there - list says so, forget <it> plans it in every hall again. use walks this box to it where it stands now (eb all travelactor use ... sends each box its own way). add reads the object you target (or the one of that name in sight): its name, this zone (in a guild hall: any hall), where it stands (a trip walks there first, from anywhere in its zone), how it is used (click unless you say verb or list; an open list - its travel map or its zone list - gives its places itself) and its places; a verb with spaces that holds "to" goes in quotes (verb "Travel to Thalumbra"). Yours are kept on this PC (eb-travel-actors-own.local.json beside EB) and used by every trip at once; a shipped one cannot be removed. A teleporter the travel data marks as a way through a zone is never a trip's last hop. eb share travelactor [<it> | all] shares yours through EB's hub with no character, guild or player name in them (eb share); a friend's eb share get <code> adds each one not there yet to their own. Also typed as: ta, travelactors. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> travelactor ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: hubs

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), destinations, add or remove. Default: list.

params.name: what
params.desc: destinations: the hub zone; add: <hub zone> <the instance's name> (the hub's short name, one word); remove: the instance's name.

functions.desc: The hub zones - where each instance is entered from, as the instance files say (each names its hub zone and its door), and your own additions.
functions.notes: list = the hub zones, the ones with most instances first, with their counts; destinations <hub> = the instances entered from it, their copies (heroic, solo ...) and the door with its verb (yours marked "this PC"). An instance the files do not name is added with its hub and kept on this PC; eb hub <it> then takes a box there. Only the way to the hub: the tank alone zones the group in. This box only.

functions.name: stagger

params.name: cmd
params.desc: on, off, reset, delay or leader. Default: on.

params.name: arg
params.desc: The delay, or the leader: a box, a character, or auto.

functions.desc: Space the crew's moves out so the boxes do not all move at once: on, off, reset, the delay in milliseconds, and who leads.
functions.notes: leader auto = this group's tank leads: the one declared with eb go tank when it is in the group, else a plate fighter (guardian, berserker, paladin, shadowknight) before a leather one (monk, bruiser), never a mercenary - read again at each move, so a new tank leads the next move; no fighter in the group: whoever sent the move leads. eb stagger shows the tank it reads. Every box answers the same, so the order is the same on every box. Into an instance nothing is staggered: every box gets to the hub on its own and the tank alone zones the group in. Also typed as: sg. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> stagger ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: itinerary
functions.desc: Say the hops still ahead at every zone change: on, off; status says them now. eb route <zone> shows the hops of a trip you have not started.
functions.notes: Also typed as: itin. This box only.

functions.name: travelnet

params.name: cmd
params.desc: scan, status, locs, merge, info, reload, allow, block, tle, methods, stats or save. Default: status.

params.name: what
params.desc: allow / block: a way - bell (city bells and docks), spire, druid, hall (Call to Guild Hall), hallbell (the hall's own bell) or port (a wizard's or a druid's group port); tle: on or off.

functions.desc: What EB knows of the travel network and of this server: scan the bells, spires and rings here (in a guild hall with none of its own: its portal wizard or druid), status, the places on record, merge; info = which ways this server has and what this box has; reload = read the server policy and the travel data again; allow / block <way> and tle on | off = your own choice for this server, kept on this PC; methods = which ways this box can leave its zone by right now, and why not; stats = what the travel data holds, what this PC learned and the trips this PC made; save = the trip counts written now and one copy of every learned travel file.
functions.notes:
THE SERVER POLICY. Each server's type (live or TLE) and the ways it has come with EB; a trip never plans a way its server does not have, and a trip that finds no way says which ways were held back. A server that is not on the list uses every way until you block one (eb travelnet block druid, eb travelnet tle on); your choices are kept on this PC and win over the list. A box that cannot read its server's name holds nothing back (info says so). On a TLE server eb ft is refused - there is no fast travel there. Info also says which planner goes first on this server: the travel graph (a live server) or EB's own ways (a TLE or unnamed one).

METHODS, one line a way: this zone's bell, wizard spire and druid ring (on its network or not; its spot on record, or found by its name when in sight), Call to Guild Hall (known, ready or on its timer, the hall learned), a group port (your own Translocate or Circle of Growth and its timer, or who in the group casts one), the transit pads here, the zone lines on record (eb zoneout list), the travel objects here, the travel items this box holds (a way from anywhere: examined and its reply picked, or used with its cast; on its timer it is taken last) and fast travel (your own press only). A way the server's policy holds back says so.

STATS AND SAVE. Every trip EB rides is counted on this PC (eb-travel-stats.local.json beside EB, never shipped): how many arrived, failed or were stopped, how long an arrived trip took over how many hops, each way's hops ridden and failed and the bells that lacked the place, what failed trips most, the last trips. Every learned travel file (the spots learned, the bell maps, your connections, zones, hubs, pads, zone routes, server choices) is kept the moment it changes; save keeps one copy of all of them in eb-travel-saved.local.json, to keep or carry to another PC. Also typed as: tnet. This box only.

functions.name: zoneout

params.name: what
params.desc: list [words], a number from the list, or words.

functions.desc: Leave this zone by its exit. The exits in sight and the ones the zone data knows are one list, best first: an exit by its own name (zone_to_, exit_to_, zone_exit, a guild hall's or a house's way out), then an object shown as an exit, the nearest first. eb zoneout takes the first; eb zoneout <n> the one of that number; eb zoneout <words> the first whose name or destination holds every word; list [words] shows them, numbered, saying where each comes from.
functions.notes: The box walks to within 3 m of the exit and uses it - a double-click; an exit only the zone data knows is used its own way (its door's verb or a hail, a line walked into) - answers the zone list with the data's entry (else the last copy, the same for every box) and waits for the zone to change, then says where it is. Never in a fight; a crew line never sends a box you play by hand. The pack step is ZoneOut [words] (eb action ZoneOut): the same exit, the same walk. Also typed as: exitzone. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> zoneout ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: connection

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), add or remove. Default: list.

params.name: what
params.desc: add: the zone, then line (the default), door <its name>, bell, spire or druid; remove: the zone (from the zone you stand in) or its number in the list; list: a zone (its ways in and out only).

functions.desc: Your own ways from one zone to another, kept on this PC and used by every trip at once. Stand at a zone line and eb connection add <zone it leads to>: where you stand is where the trip walks into it. door <its name> after the zone makes it a door clicked there; bell, spire or druid says this zone's bell, wizard spire or druid ring also goes there.
functions.notes: A zone no bell, spire or ring reaches is then gone to through yours: the network to this zone, then this way out (eb route shows it). One way of a kind between two zones: a new one replaces the old. A bell / spire / druid way that this server's policy holds back (eb travelnet info) stays held back. The shipped zone data is never written; list says how many zone lines it has out of the zone you stand in. Also typed as: conn, connections. This box only.

functions.name: travelcancel

params.name: state
params.desc: pause, resume or cancel. Default: cancel.

functions.desc: The trip under way: pause it, resume it, or cancel it. Typed as eb pausetravel, eb resumetravel or eb canceltravel it needs no argument. From a script, eb.nav.stop() ends the walk a trip is on.
functions.notes: Also typed as: pausetravel, resumetravel, canceltravel. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> travelcancel ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: zones

params.name: zone
params.desc: The zone to look at (a name of several words, quoted or not) - or a word first: list [words | mine] (mine = your own only), add <short name> [its name] (eb zones add exp99_fixture_vale Fixture Vale), remove <one of your own, by its name or its short name>, reload, import [status | forget].

functions.desc: The zones: where this box is (its portals on record, its guild hall, its lockouts), or one zone (its portals and the way there from here); browse the zones on record; teach every trip a zone the data does not name yet.
functions.notes: import reads the zone pieces your other bot keeps on this PC (its travel data, under each InnerSpace folder EB runs from; only read, never written) into your own file, one file a step, and says what came in: the bell, wizard spire and druid ring spots (each fills a gap - a spot EB's data or your own scan has stays), the zone doors (a way into a zone the network does not reach: the box walks to the door's spot, then uses the zone door at hand, picking the zone from its list when it asks) and the named points (eb poi finds them in their zone, after your own). A zone those files name that EB does not know is said - eb zones add teaches it, then import again. import status says what the last import holds; import forget drops it. Also typed as: zm, zonemanager. This box only.

functions.name: hotzone

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), count or refresh. Default: list.

functions.desc: Which zones carry bonus experience now: refresh reads the game's hot-zone rotation (the zone-reuse window's Hot Zones page), list says the last read - each entry, when it resets, its zones - and count how many.
functions.notes: The last read is kept on this PC, so list answers after a restart (it says when it was read). On EB for InnerSpace refresh opens the zone-reuse window, shows its Hot Zones page, reads the list and shuts the window again (a window you had open stays open); it takes a moment, and the answer is said when it comes. That read is held back until it is proven live: until then refresh says so. Also typed as: hz. This box only.

functions.name: zoneto

params.name: who
params.desc: The crew member (me in a crew line is the box that sent it).

functions.desc: Go to the zone a crew member is in, the best way (as eb goto); in its zone already, nothing to do. In another copy of the same zone, the game's own move to a group member's copy. eb all zoneto me brings every box to your zone.
functions.notes: The member's zone is what the crew last heard from it. Your own press only: refused while a quest line, a power-level route or an instance run is going. The move to another copy is held back until it is proven live; then it waits out a fight and tries up to three times. A crew line never moves a box you play by hand (paused). After a group trip the boxes land in one copy by themselves: the same row at the copy list, then a move into the tank's copy. Also typed as: changezoneto. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> zoneto ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: house
functions.desc: Leave the house you stand in: EB walks to its door (the actor named house) and uses its Exit. status says whether a house door is in sight.
functions.notes: With no door in sight nothing is sent. Also typed as: exithouse, leavehouse. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> house ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: heartstone

params.name: cmd
params.desc: rekindle (default), home or status. Default: rekindle.

functions.desc: In the guild hall, walk to its heartstone and use Rekindle Bond; home casts Call to Home; status says whether a heartstone is in sight.
functions.notes: Your own press only: refused while a quest line, a power-level route or an instance run is going. Also typed as: rekindle. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> heartstone ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: rallyflag

params.name: cmd
params.desc: status (default), use, go or get. Default: status.

functions.desc: The guild's rally flag, a Tactical Rally Banner in the bags: use it, go (rekindle the hall's heartstone, then use it: what a rally asks of each box), see whether you carry one (status), or get one from the guild hall's strategist.
functions.notes: get walks to the strategist, hails it and says its replies without picking any: which reply hands a banner is waiting for its live read. Your own press only. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> rallyflag ... (who after 'to').

functions.name: rally
functions.desc: Rally the crew to you: plant your Tactical Rally Banner where you stand; once it stands, every other box (in the guild hall, with a flag) rekindles its heartstone and uses its own flag.
functions.notes: Your own press only: refused while a quest line, a power-level route or an instance run is going. Also typed as: rallybanner. This box only.

functions.name: zoneclick
functions.desc: Click the zone door here: the zone's own door where EB knows it, else the nearest exit, zone line or door within 30 m, else the NPC who zones you. Never in a guild hall.
functions.notes: Then eb zonedoor picks in the list it opens (eb zonedoor 2, or last). eb all zoneclick clicks on every box; a box played by hand is left alone. To walk out of a zone by its exit from anywhere: eb zoneout. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> zoneclick ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: commands.ui
modules.summary: Open and arrange EB's windows from the console: the mini, EB Main, the map, the xp board, the tool windows, the radar, saved layouts, the theme and anon mode.
modules.description:
EB's windows open in EB's own window host, outside the game. Every window command answers on this build: each opens its window through the window bridge (eb windows lists every window with the line that opens it). Where the overlay host cannot start - no socket library, or it is not running - a command that opens a window says that and opens nothing. The mini, EB Console, EB Main and the MCP open by themselves only on the crew's lead box - the lowest session the crew relay hears, or a box alone - so a small box of a crew opens nothing until you open it there (eb mini, eb console open, eb ui, eb mcp); the setting ui.open_on_load says lead (the default), all or off, and ui.miniOnLogin = false keeps the mini shut.

A window can leave the game window and come back: eb windows <word> out puts it in a window of its own, eb windows <word> in puts it back, max and restore size it, and click off gives the mouse back to a window that is set to let clicks through. A window's lock and click-through are kept for each window; a window that is out of the game waits docked while its monitor is gone, and goes back out when it returns.

functions.name: mini

params.name: state
params.desc: toggle (default), open, close, show, hide, stop, go, group, skip or status. Default: toggle.

params.name: list
params.desc: after show: what the bar shows - name, class, doing (the line at the bottom), each switch (eb, pause, follow, move, camp, dps, combat, buffs, pet, loot), each button (main, mcp, cast, harvest, windows, stop, go, builder, zones, teams, adorn) and mine (your own HotBar buttons); or default, all or none. Words that all start with + or - change what it shows instead of replacing it. After group: on or off.

functions.desc: The mini, this box's own bar: open it, close it, pick what it shows, press its Stop group or Go on, or make its switches flip for the whole group.
functions.notes: Under its switches the mini keeps Main, MCP, Cast stack, Harvest (a dot on it while a harvest runs), Windows, Stop group and Go on; its cog ticks on the Instance Builder, Zones, Teams and Adornments buttons, each lit while its window is open, and your own HotBar buttons, which sit under the others. close and hide keep it closed on this character, also at the next login, as its X does, until eb mini or eb mini open. What it shows is the same on every box of the PC. eb mini show main stop zones; eb mini show +teams -pet; eb mini status. This box only.

functions.name: ui

params.name: panel
params.desc: crew, windows (the Windows view: every EB window by what it is for, and what EB runs on this box), dash (the Dash: the cards you pick) or a window's word, which opens that window; <word> toggle opens or shuts it.

functions.desc: Open EB Main: the crew at a glance and the way into every window.
functions.notes: The Dash's cards, each on or off and in your order (its Cards button): Overview (the group, the instance queue, how long EB has been up on this box and the run's time, this box's status), Live (in a fight or not, the mobs engaged, the target, where this box is), Quick Travel (a zone or a place, the best way / this zone's bell / its transport, for this box or everyone grouped with you - in the world, never fast travel; Show the way only says the hops), your own HotBar buttons (the ones the mini's cog ticked), the group in short rows, and the hirelings (Read; their window). EB Main's toolbar also has How do I..., which opens EB Help on the common jobs step by step. Also typed as: main. This box only.

functions.name: map

params.name: cmd
params.desc: show (default), marks, path, roam, search or level. Default: show.

params.name: words
params.desc: after search: a name or part of one (clear ends the search); after level: <min> [max] or <min>-<max> (clear: any level).

functions.desc: The map window: you, the group, the zone's exits, travel and marks, the path layer and the areas you drew.
functions.notes: marks, path and roam are views inside the window. search opens the map on its List showing only what matches; level shows only who is around at those levels (80 alone is 80 and up). Each is put in the map's own boxes once, as if typed there; one said more than two minutes before the map opens is left out. eb map search a placeholder fisher; eb map level 80 90; eb map level clear. This box only.

functions.name: inbox

params.name: cmd
params.desc: list (the default), add, approve, dismiss or clear. Default: list.

params.name: arg
params.desc: add: the EB line, then -- and why; approve / dismiss: the entry's number.

functions.desc: The ops inbox of the character you play: EB lines an agent or a script proposes, waiting for you. list shows them, who proposed each and why, then the last few that ran; approve <n> runs one on this box as if you typed it on EB Console; dismiss <n> drops it; clear drops them all; add <eb line> -- <why> puts one in. eb ops is the same command; the Ops Inbox window shows the same.
functions.notes: Nothing in the inbox ever runs by itself, and a line in it never works the inbox (approve, dismiss...). A line must be one EB command (no ';', no second line). A script or an agent outside EB can also drop one JSON object a file ({"line": "eb ...", "why": "...", "from": "..."}) in <EB>\data\ebinbox\<character>\drop\: it is picked up (and the file deleted) when the inbox is read - the open window looks every few seconds. An agent working through EB's agent server proposes every line that changes something this way: only its reads (eb status, eb waiting ...) run at once. For this box only. Also typed as: ops. This box only.

functions.name: site

params.name: page
params.desc: home (the default), account, download, docs or commands. Default: home.

functions.desc: EB's hub page in your web browser: the front page, your account page, the download, the docs or every EB command. eb web is the same command.
functions.notes: The page opens as if you had clicked a link: nothing is sent from the game and nothing is read back. For this box only (a crew line never opens six browsers). The MCP's hub button runs it. Also typed as: web. This box only.

functions.name: mcp

params.name: state
params.desc: show (default), hide, toggle or press. Default: show.

params.name: button
params.desc: after press: a button of your own grid, its label or key <the key kept on it>.

functions.desc: Open the Master Control Panel: a button for every EB command, for the whole crew or one box, and every EB window in its Windows tab.
functions.notes: This box only.

functions.name: forwho

params.name: pick
params.desc: all, group, others, me, fighter / priest / mage / scout, a box or a character (several with commas), or status; nothing opens the For Who window.

functions.desc: Who the MCP's buttons go to: all (every box), group (your group), others (every box but this one), me (this box only), or boxes and characters by name, several with commas. With no word the For Who window opens: one click flips the pick, and the MCP shows the same pick.
functions.notes: The pick is kept per character. On your own button grid a line takes the pick where it says ${ForWho} (eb ${ForWho} mount on; an imported console line's auto who too); a line without it runs where it is typed, and one that names its own boxes (eb all ..., eb relay mygroup ...) goes where it says; a window or a status read always runs on this box. eb forwho group; eb forwho is2,is3; eb forwho status. This box only.

functions.name: windows

params.name: name
params.desc: A window's word to open it (then toggle, show, hide, out, in, max, restore, or click on | off), or all: every window, with why one does not open here; or reset (this character's windows) / reset all (every character on this PC): every window back at its default place and size.

functions.desc: List every EB window by what it is for, with the line that opens each; a window's word opens it (eb windows glance). After the word: toggle, show or hide it; out, in, max or restore moves it out of the game window, back in, maximizes it or sizes it back; click off gives the mouse back to a click-through window (click on sets it); reset puts every window back at its default place and size. The same list as EB Main's Windows view and the MCP's Windows tab.
functions.notes: eb windows glance out puts At a Glance in a window of its own; eb windows glance in puts it back. A window that has been set click-through still answers eb windows <word> click off. eb windows reload closes every open EB window and opens it again, so each page loads its newest files (after an update, or a window that looks stuck); EB and the game keep running (eb reload restarts EB itself; EB Settings > Options has both as buttons). eb windows restart starts the window host itself again: a new copy takes over and opens the windows that were open (after an update of the window host, or when every window is stuck); EB and the game keep running. eb windows <word> through <group>,<page> lets one of the game's own windows through that EB window (MainHUD,Chat for the chat window): where it lies under the EB window it shows and takes the click; <group>,<page> off or through off takes one or all away. eb windows <word> mirror puts the same window in a browser on this PC (a second monitor, beside the game): its link comes to your clipboard - paste it into a browser here; it opens only on this PC and only while EB runs; mirror off ends it. eb windows reset puts every EB window back at its default place and size: the windows that are open close, forget where they were left and open again there (the one a button was pressed in too); the ones that are shut open at their default place next time. It applies to this character; eb windows reset all applies to every character on this PC - the other boxes of the crew each put their own windows back, and a character that is not running has its saved places cleared. The window host saves a window's place as it closes, so EB waits for each close before it clears a place; a window that has not closed in five seconds keeps its place and is named in the answer (eb windows reset tries again); a window that was mirrored in a browser loses its mirror (eb windows <word> mirror puts it back). Only where a window sits changes - never its look (eb uireset), its options or your saved looks. EB Main (right-click a window) and UI Options (Reset places) have it as a button. Also typed as: wins. This box only.

functions.name: front

params.name: name
params.desc: on or off (the opt-in, kept for this box: the setting ui.frontByName), or a character's name. Nothing: how it stands.

functions.desc: A game window to the front: eb front <name> brings that character's game window forward on this PC - a quick switch between your games. Off until you switch it on.
functions.notes: The window host does it: it finds the game by its character, never brings one forward on the main monitor and never guesses between two games of one name; when it cannot, the console says why. EB Settings > Options has the switch. This box only.

functions.name: boxes

params.name: what
params.desc: draw (the bare word: the Black Boxes window opens to draw them or change them), clear (every black box over this game window is removed and the window closes), off (taken off the game window, kept), on (put back) or status (how many, and whether they are over the game now). Default: draw.

functions.desc: Black boxes over this game window, which hide parts of it and let every click through: draw them, take them off, put them back or remove them, from the console line (or a HotBar button that runs the line).
functions.notes: The boxes are kept for each character. Over the game, holding Ctrl+Shift lets the boxes take the mouse: each box shows its x, the biggest one Change the boxes and Remove all. eb boxes clear always works, with or without the mouse. Also typed as: blackboxes. This box only.

functions.name: rotationboard
functions.desc: The Rotation Board: every box running a saved rotation (eb rotation), on one board - who casts what next, the part it plays, and when that ability is ready - with this box's saved rotations to start one from it.
functions.notes: The same as eb rotation board and eb windows rotationboard. The other boxes' lines come over the crew relay while the board is open; a box that runs no rotation is not on it. With none running, the board says how to save and start one. Also typed as: rotboard. This box only.

functions.name: xp

params.name: cmd
params.desc: show (default), combat, quest, board, reset, ignore, track, stop or start. Default: show.

params.name: name
params.desc: after ignore or track: a character's name.

functions.desc: Experience: the XP window (every box's level and how far into it, what each gained this session, its pace an hour and the time to its next level, and the XP potion each one has running) and a line a box on the console; board opens At a Glance on its XP column; reset starts the session numbers again from now; combat or quest flips the game's own combat or quest experience switch.
functions.notes: Gained, Per hour and To level come from what each box says on the crew relay (its level and how far into it), so they need no read of their own and keep counting while the window is shut; Per hour waits for two minutes of play, and a box that was away adds no time. reset (the window's Reset button) starts all of them again from now. ignore <name> takes that character off the XP window (as its x does), track <name> puts it back; stop / start makes every box stop or start reading its XP while its XP window is closed. In the window, a click on a column's head sorts by it (again: the other way; Box: name order, the default), and its gear picks what to track - Adventure, Tradeskill, AA, Ascension, XP potions and the session numbers (a potion is not read at all while it is off). A dash means that number is not read yet: the tradeskill and AA bars wait for a live proof. eb xp ignore a placeholder name. This box only.

functions.name: track

params.name: what
params.desc: track (default), cd or osa; after eb osa: pin, unpin, ignore, unignore, clear or map. Default: track.

params.name: key
params.desc: after pin / unpin / ignore / unignore: an effect's icon/backdrop (2341/33083); after clear: pins, ignores or all; after map: range <m> (10 to 500) or auto, big [on|off], names [on|off], hidden [on|off], shown, detach, who me|group|irc|all, or dets [on|off].

functions.desc: Open a fight window: track = Track (what is around you), cd = Group Cooldowns (every box's long cooldowns), osa = Target (your target and every mob in the fight), with the threat readout on the console. eb osa and eb cd open their own window.
functions.notes: eb osa pin <icon>/<backdrop> pins one of the target's effects to the front of the Target card, eb osa ignore hides it (unpin / unignore undo them; eb osa clear pins | ignores | all), kept for this character - the same as a click on the effect or the Target window's gear, which also picks the parts the card shows and big icons. eb osa map sets EB Raid's minimap for this session the way its own wheel and buttons do: range <m> (a member past it sits on the edge toward them; auto = every member), big, names on the dots, hidden / shown; a bare big or names flips it; detach opens EB Map; eb osa map alone says the view. eb osa map who me | group | irc | all picks whom a Ctrl+Shift+click on a map walks there (EB Raid's minimap and EB Map: just me, my group, every box in this zone on every PC over EB IRC, or every box online in this zone - never one played by hand), as EB Raid's gear does; eb osa map dets on | off shows the Detriments panel under EB Raid's rows (who has what, and what it does); both are kept for this PC. eb osa pin 2341/33083 Also typed as: osa, cd. This box only.

functions.name: look

params.name: cmd
params.desc: files (default), save, open or delete. Default: files.

params.name: name
params.desc: after save / open / delete: the look file's name (letters, digits, spaces, _ and -).

functions.desc: Your look as a file to share: the theme and your own colours written to <EB>/data/looks/<name>.eblook.json - a theme and colours only, nothing in it names anyone - and put on again by its name.
functions.notes: A friend's look file dropped into that folder opens the same way; a file that is not a look (not one EB wrote, another kind, another version, or no theme and no colour EB takes) is refused, in words. UI Options > Looks > Share has Save as a file and Open a look file. (The operating system's own file dialog is the window host's.) eb look save Night Blue This box only.

functions.name: title

params.name: tag

functions.desc: Your own scripts: Lua files in your scripts folder (and the shipped examples) whose header lines become real options in the Scripts window, with a panel, pages of their own and tests. eb script alone opens the Scripts window.
functions.notes:
WHERE THEY LIVE. Your scripts are the .lua files right in your scripts folder (scripts\ in your own EB data folder): pages and add-ins sit beside a script or in a folder below it, its values in options\<name>.json. EB's updates and EB Setup never write or delete there. The examples ship with EB and come back with every update: copy one first (eb script copy <Example>, never over a file of yours), and your copy takes its place in the list. The folders are read again every 8 s while the Scripts window is up, every minute otherwise, and at once on eb script reload.

THE HEADER. Comment lines that start -- ebscript and a word: name, about, author, version, icon (spell:<icon>/<back>, item:<icon> or ability:<name>), needs, section <title> [folded], option <key> <kind> ["Label"] [= default] [settings], button "Label" <eb line>, page "Title" file=<name>.html [settings], addin "Title" file=<name>.html in=<window> [at=top or bottom] and place "Name" <path>. The 15 kinds of option: check, number, slider, percent, text, list, choice, multi, location, zone, target, ability, item, file and folder. A line EB cannot read is listed (eb script info <Name>) with its line number and why.

RUNNING. A script runs a slice at a time on EB's own pulse: it runs until it waits (script.wait), then the game goes on. Stop asks nicely - its wait answers false and script.running() turns false - and a script that has not ended 8 s later is ended; a script that runs 50 ms without waiting is ended too. Who: me (this box), group (my group: eb relay mygroup), irc (every PC over EB IRC: the script must be in that PC's folder too) or all (every box online, never a box played by hand). A run reaching a box from another box is never started on a box played by hand.

WHAT A SCRIPT HAS. The object script: start, running, stopping, wait, opt / on / num / int / count / item / has / x / y / z, set / setMine, say, live / liveClear, panel, eb (an EB line on a Who), travel, moveTo, pick, page / pageClose, sound / soundStop, speak / speakStop, banner, fileName / folderOf / fileExists / readFile / listFolder / writeFile / appendLine (relative to your scripts folder, never above it), the test methods (testStart, check, expect, expectNum, expectValue, mayBeEmpty, skip, testDone), me / target / group (EB's own reads) and now / unix. Lua's string, table and math are there; files, other programs and EB's insides are not. Also typed as: userscripts, myscripts. For the crew: eb all|others|to <who> script ... (who after 'to').

modules.name: eb.combat
modules.summary: The combat engine: one decision per step from the cast stack - interrupts, heroic opportunities, dispels, mez, heals, rez, cures, power, upkeep, buffs, items, then the damage rotation - with guards never attacked and unwinnable fights given up.
modules.description:
The engine OWNS the fight. A script never casts the rotation by hand; it shapes what the engine does (switches, tags, presets, overrides, a target lock, an interrupt list) and lets the engine step. Each step reads the world once through the game layer's combat shim, picks the first category that has something to do, in a fixed order (engine.ORDER), and sends ONE cast - or holds and says why ("casting", "paused", "nothing to cast").

THE SEND GUARD. The engine watches what the game does with each cast. A cast is TAKEN when the cast bar runs or the ability goes on its recast; one the game does not take within a second is REFUSED. One send goes out at a time (the step holds "landing" until the last one is taken or judged), and at most one every half second: an instant art sent every step was a line the game could not take. A refused ability rests at that target for ten seconds, doubling for each refusal in a row up to a minute; refusals in a row at one actor rest the actor (a member is passed over by heals, cures and buffs, a mob by every target path); refusals at two targets mean the game takes nothing from this character (feigned, silenced, a state EB cannot read), so every send holds for a few seconds. A person's own order (eb rez now, eb cure now, eb cast) goes out past the rests and is judged like any send. A character that is stunned or mezzed casts nothing. eb anal why says what rests and for how long. THREE RULES NO SETTING CAN CHANGE. A guard is never selected as a target, and an AE is never fired with a guard in AE reach. A fight whose kill time stays past the limit after its grace period is given up and that mob is benched for the session. Readiness is always asked of the game, every time - an entry never carries its own recast timer.

In a running EB the engine is eb.app.combat.engine, stepped by the pulse 4 times a second; work on that one rather than building a second engine (two engines would both cast). A test or a tool builds its own with combat.new.

OVERRIDES are context-scoped changes the engine applies only while the context matches (a zone, an encounter, a mob, or a temporary manual one): turn AE, mez or heroic opportunities off, force tags, lock or assist, cap the give-up time, pause casting. With nothing matching, behaviour is exactly the default.

ON EB FOR INNERSPACE TODAY the engine's game reads cover the target, the group, hostiles, readiness, the cast bars, line of sight, your maintained spells, whether a mob is stunned or mezzed, and each member's distance. Some reads are not provided yet, and the parts that need them stay quiet (they never guess): the heroic-opportunity wheel (selectHO), "this mob has a buff to strip" (selectDispel; the on-cue engine:dispel works without it), your class's own resource reads (Savagery, Dissonance, a stacking effect at full) and the main assist's target (setAssist has no effect). A cast-stack row that needs one of them waits and says why. The engine's selection logic itself is the same on both targets.

A KNOWN LIMIT, SAID PLAINLY: the engine chooses the mob to fight (selectTarget never chooses a guard), but a damage cast goes to the game's current target. When your current target is not a fair fight - a guard you clicked, say - the engine picks another mob for its checks while its art still goes to what you have targeted. Target the mob the engine chose (game.TargetActor(engine:selectTarget(engine:snapshot()).id)) before you let it fight, and never leave a guard targeted.

How to script a fight with the engine: 1) take EB's engine (eb.app.combat.engine) - never build a second one in game; 2) shape it for the encounter: setContext / addOverride for the zone or the named, setInterruptList for the casts worth stopping, setMezList for the adds, lockTarget or the kill-first list for the order; 3) switch the cast stack's rows and tags for each phase (eb.app.combat.holder.setTagEnabled); 4) let EB's pulse step it - poll engine:activeOverride() and the decisions for your status line; 5) when the fight is over, clearOverride, clearLock and clear the lists you set.

functions.desc: The engine's small pure helpers, shared with scripts (see eb.combat.combat_util).

functions.name: DECISION
functions.signature: decision = { kind, ability, target, reason, entry, sent, sendWhy, at, position, mob, itemName }
functions.desc: What engine:step returns when it cast: kind = "interrupt" | "ho" | "dispel" | "mez" | "heal" | "rez" | "cure" | "power" | "upkeep" | "buff" | "item" | "dps" | "precast"; target = "Target" (the game's current target), "Me", an actor id or a role word; reason = a short why ("Member2 at 40%", "priority 97", "interrupt Fixture Blast"); sent / sendWhy = what the game answered; position = the positioning intent (eb.combat.combat_pos). A hold is { hold = true, reason, mob, position }.

functions.name: ENGINE_TAGS
functions.signature: entry.tags carries ";"-separated tags: AE, CA, DUMBFIRE, EMERGENCY, INTERRUPT, STUN, STIFLE, KNOCKDOWN, DISPEL, STRIP, MEZ, ROOT, CC, HO_STARTER, REZ, CURE, CURE_CURSE, POWER_HEAL ...

Any tag can be switched with engine:toggle.
functions.notes: A cast-stack row's own Type gives its first tag (eb.caststack.jsonstack.TYPES). A row's custom Tag is kept in a field of its own (the tag holder.setTagEnabled switches); only HO_STARTER also joins entry.tags - so an imported row cannot mark itself as the interrupt, dispel or mez art today. modules.name: eb.app.combat
modules.summary: The combat plane EB builds once per box: the character's cast stack (a live holder), the one engine, the pump the pulse runs, and the facade every part of EB asks - "is it winnable", "engage", "set the preset".
modules.description:
In a running EB this is eb.app.combat: combat.holder is the character's live cast stack (switch its rows and tags), combat.engine the engine, combat.facade the views over it. EB's pulse calls combat.pump 4 times a second, so the engine runs whether or not a fight is on you (heals, buffs, upkeep out of combat too).

THE FACADE has two views of the same engine. facade.brain is pollable - ask isWinnable before a pull, engage a target, poll clear until the fight is over, set the preset for what you are doing. facade.ic is what an instance script uses: find, count, pull, engage, clearArea and the waits, all bounded, plus cure, dispel and the overrides.

The cast stack is found by the character's name in the imported cast-stack profiles EB knows about; a box with none runs the engine on an empty stack and describe() says why.

modules.name: eb.combat.heals
modules.summary: The heal, rez, cure, power, upkeep, buff and damage categories of the engine - methods on an engine object.
modules.description:
These are methods of the engine (local engine = eb.app.combat.engine; engine:selectHeal(ctx)), never a file to require. Each selector looks at the loaded stack and one world read and returns a decision or nil; the step tries them in combat.ORDER. Call one yourself to preview what a category would cast: engine:loadStack(), local ctx = engine:snapshot(), ctx.mob = engine:selectTarget(ctx), then engine:selectHeal(ctx).

HEALS are weighted, not ordered: a heal's weight is its healWeight (default 20) plus how far its member has fallen, and an EMERGENCY-tagged heal adds 1000. A group heal (gates.groupHealTargetsBelowHP with groupHealMinTargets) fires only when that many recipients are under that health. A CURE fires only on a member who carries a detriment its type can remove (gates.cureTypes, or CURE_CURSE for curses; a cure with no types removes any); with no detriment read at all it fires rather than never cure. A REZ is for the dead; a POWER heal for whoever is under its power %.

WHO AN ENTRY'S TARGET NAMES: AllParty (or none) = every living member in the zone; Me = you; PartyTank = the tank; Healer1 / Healer2 = a priest; a role word (DPS1-3, Healer1-3, Bard, Enchanter - see eb.combat.roles); any other word = the player of that name. A rez looks among the dead instead.

functions.name: healChoice

returns.desc: { entry, target = the member, weight, low = their health % }, or nil when nobody it covers is under its threshold (gates.useBelowTargetHP, default 100) or a group heal's count is not met.

modules.name: eb.combat.overrides
modules.summary: How the engine reads the override layer: what matches, what wins, and the effective value of each switch.
modules.description:
Methods on an engine object. A step resolves the directives once (engine.ov = engine:resolveOverride(ctx)); every switch is then read through these, which answer the override's value when one is set and the engine's own value otherwise - so no override at all and an empty one behave the same.

THE OVERRIDE (engine:addOverride): { name, priority, match = { zone, encounter, mob, manual }, directives }. match keys are ANDed; zone and encounter take a name or a list (any case), mob is part of the target's name, an empty match never applies. A higher priority wins a conflicting key; the manual override (setOverride) sits above all. THE DIRECTIVES: disableAE / disableMez / disableHO, tags = { TAG = false | true }, forceAssist = name, lockTarget = id, ttkMax / ttkGrace = ms, losGate, positioning = "behind" | "range" | "stack" | "melee" (or { mode, range, on }), autoTarget = { enabled, oocScan, list, scanRadius }, interruptAll, interruptList, cureScope = "group" | "single", pause, trashFirst, stack = a cast-stack name. None of them can make the engine fight a guard or keep an unwinnable fight.

modules.description: Methods on an engine object. An ALLOW entry (entry.allowTag) casts only while its tag is raised (unless entry.allowTrigger); an EMBARGO entry (entry.embargoTag) is blocked while its tag is raised. engine:raiseTag and engine:tagFor raise a tag for some seconds; the engine's own timer puts it back. modules.description: Methods on an engine object. Nothing moves the box for it: EB does not move in a fight yet, and the engine says so once in the console for each mode asked. An entry with a positional need (entry.positional = "behind" | "front" | "flank") waits for the angle; an unknown angle never blocks. The line-of-sight gate holds a cast only when the game says the line is blocked.

modules.name: eb.combat.hunt
modules.summary: Auto Hunt's rules, with no game in them: the saved hunt list read into one shape, which mob is pulled next, and where to look when nothing is in reach.
modules.description:
A hunt list is a window's own file (<EB folder>\data\huntlists\<name>.json): names to hunt, names to avoid, the cons and levels it keeps to, named / heroic / epic, how far to scan, where to hunt (around the start, a camp spot, the whole zone, along waypoints in order, or inside an area), the kills or minutes it stops at, the health and power to rest at. With no names it hunts any mob the group can kill.

WHO IS PULLED: the nearest mob that passes - a mob_order name first. An NPC (never a player, a pet, a corpse or a door), alive, on the list's names (none = any), not on its avoid list; NEVER A GUARD, whatever the list says; never one the kill-time watch gave up on, one resting after a cast the game did not take, or one another player is fighting; its level against yours inside the list's band; a named only while the list allows named; inside the hunt's bounds. A mob row with its con is judged by the list's cons (none ticked = every con but red); where the con is not read and the list has no level band, the hunt keeps to mobs at most two levels above you.

WHERE: around = within the roam of where the hunt started; camp = within the scan of the spot; zone = the whole zone; patrol = within the scan of the waypoint path; area = inside the outline. WHERE NEXT: patrol walks the waypoints in order, round and round; area and around search a grid of spots, the one looked at longest ago first; camp goes back to the spot. The live loop that walks, orders the kill and waits is eb.combat.hunt_run.

modules.name: eb.registry
modules.summary: The one table of eb commands: run a line as if it was typed, send it to the crew with all / others / to, answer a declared command with your own handler, and read the help and tab-completion.
modules.description:
Every eb command is declared ONCE, in EB's command schema (data/eb/commands.json). The console's tab-completion, the button windows, the help window, the crew relay and the brain all read this one registry, so a line a script runs with reg:dispatch behaves exactly like the same line typed in the console.

A COMMAND ROW (what reg:command and reg:view return) is a plain table: { id = "<domain>.<verb>", domain, verb, aliases = { words }, desc, args = { { name, type, required, default, values, help } }, scopes = { "local", "all", "others", "to" }, module, ship }. A command answers only the scopes its row lists.

A HANDLER is function(args, ctx, parsed) -> ok, text. args holds the typed arguments by name, already read as their types (whole numbers, numbers, on/off and choices in their canonical spelling). It must return at once: start long work as a task or a goal and answer "issued". ok may be true, "issued" (accepted, the work goes on) or false.

A CREW LINE: "eb all <cmd>", "eb others <cmd>" and "eb to <who> <cmd>" are handed to ctx.relay. The line that travels carries no scope word, so it runs where it lands and is never relayed again. who may be a box id (is2), a character, a class, an archetype (priest) or @archetype, or several of them joined by commas.

modules.name: eb.coord.rules
modules.summary: Coordination in plain rules: "when the tank casts X, the healers cast Y", "when this line is said, hold that ability for 20 seconds", "a moment after this, if that follows, do this" - for one box, the group or the raid.
modules.description:
A RULE is a trigger, an optional delay, an optional follow-up gate, an action and a scope. The trigger is something seen on this box: an ability cast (by me, a role, a class, a character - or a mob, by the cast's name), a chat, text or emote line, a zone change, an eb.events event, a detriment on me, or a named TAG another rule fired. The action is a cast (or use, interrupt, assist, cure, joust, move, stop) for EB's combat and walker to carry out, firing a tag, raising or lifting an EMBARGO (a hold on an ability), or one crew command line. A rule with a typo is kept and shown with what is wrong, and never runs: coord:add answers its problems.

Rules compose: a rule's action can fire a tag that is another rule's trigger. A rule whose scope reaches the group or the raid sends ONE message over the crew relay (through eb.coord.relaylink); every box that hears it runs its own matching rules locally and never sends it on, so a rule reaches the crew in exactly one hop. Every box on the uplink hears every line, so a group-wide line carries a token made from the group's members (hashed: no name travels) and a box of another group - or in no raid, or in another raid - drops it; a rule that names a character reaches that character wherever it is.

The engine reads no game: facts come in through coord:feed (or coord:bindEvents, which feeds it from eb.events), actions go out through the coord:onIntent handler, and EB's combat asks coord:holdsCast before it casts.

Give each box the rules for its OWN abilities, and give a rule that reacts to a tag the scope "self": every box that owns the ability then acts for itself, exactly once. (A tag-reaction rule with a group or role scope that sits on every box acts twice on the boxes it reaches.)

How to coordinate the crew with a rule: 1. Make one engine per box: Coord.new{ me = { box, name, role }, link = relaylink, clock = P.now }. 2. Add rules with coord:add (the rule format below), the same list on every box. 3. Hand intents to your caster with coord:onIntent(fn) and the state its casts must respect (a tag is up, a hold starts or ends) with coord:onSignal(fn), and feed facts (coord:bindEvents(events) for chat, text and zoning; coord:feed for casts you see). 4. Run coord:tick(now) from a pulse job: it fires delayed rules, closes gates and expires embargoes and tags.

functions.name: rule
functions.signature: rule = { id, name, enabled, trigger = { ... }, delayMs, gate = { ... }, action = { ... }, scope }
functions.desc: The rule format. trigger.kind is "cast" (with who and ability, or mob: a mob's cast by its name or number), "chat", "text" or "emote" (with match, optional chan; a chat rule also hears text lines and the other way round; emote is a mob's line or an on-screen warning), "zone" (with event "ZoningStarted" or "ZoningFinished"; none = either), "tag" (with tag), "event" (with event, an eb.events name), "det" (a detriment lands on me; type is any, arcane, noxious, elemental, trauma or cursed) or "bind" (no trigger: a standing rule that holds a row while a hold is up). trigger.who is "" or "anyone" (any actor), "self" (this box), "@npc" (a mob), a role ("tank", "healer", "mez", "@priest" = healer, "@fighter" = tank), a class or a character's name; trigger.ability may list several separated by ";", or be "*" for any. delayMs waits that long after the trigger (at most 10 minutes); everyMs is how soon the rule may act again (default 1 s). gate = { kind, match | event | tag, withinMs (default 3000), mode = "require" (act only if it happens within the window) | "block" (act only if it does NOT) }. action.kind is "cast" or "use" (a row of this character's cast stack, by its ability's name, with an optional target), "interrupt", "assist", "cure" (what = group, single or any: one priest casts it, by claim), "joust" (dir = out, in or outback, backMs, metres), "move" (walk to x, y, z on the mesh, and back after backMs), "stop" (what = dps or all, durationMs: nothing leaves this box for a while, at most two minutes), "firetag" (with tag), "embargo" (with ability or tag, and durationMs, default 20000; or with bindAbility and tag: hold that ability while the tag's embargo is up), "lift" (with ability or tag; "liftembargo" is the same word) or "crew" (with line, one eb command line). scope names who acts: "self" (this box), "group", "raid", a role, a class, or a character or box name.

functions.name: fact
functions.desc: The fact format coord:feed takes. cast: { kind = "cast", actor, name, role, subclass, ability, isMe, isNPC, castId } (a mob's cast carries its number). chat and text: { kind, text, chan, speaker }. announce: { kind = "announce", text }. zone: { kind = "zone", event = "ZoningStarted" | "ZoningFinished" }. event: { kind = "event", event = "<name>", payload }. det: { kind = "det", type }. tag: { kind = "tag", tag, from, scope, relayed }.

functions.name: intent
functions.signature: intent = { kind, ability, target, scope, rule, name, relayed, at, line }
functions.desc: The intent format onIntent hands over: kind is "cast", "use", "interrupt", "assist", "cure", "joust", "move", "stop" or "crew"; ability and target say what to cast on whom; line is the crew command for a "crew" intent; the rest of the rule's action (dir, metres, x, y, z, what, durationMs ...) comes along; rule is the rule's id, name its name and relayed is true when another box's rule set it off. Only intents meant for this box (in the rule's scope) are handed over.

modules.name: eb.coord.arbiter
modules.summary: "Only one of us does this": before a box group-cures, cures or rezzes a member, it claims the action over the crew relay; exactly one box acts, and if it fails, the next one takes over.
modules.description:
Each box wanting the same action (the same cure on the same member) lays down a bid and waits a short claim window (150 ms) to hear the others. The winner is decided the same way on every box - the lowest role rank, then the lowest box id - so it never depends on who was fastest. The winner acts and says so; if it never reports the cure landed within the failover time (2.5 s: it died, or the cast never went out), the others drop it and the next box acts. A box that cannot cast at all hands the claim over at once.

How to claim an action: 1. Make one arbiter per box: Arb.new{ box, role, link = relaylink, clock = P.now }. A link has ONE arbiter: asking again hands back the one that exists. 2. Each tick, ask arb:request(req). "go": cast now, then arb:acted(req, now, ttlMs). "wait": the window is open - ask again next tick. "standdown": another box has it. 3. When it landed, arb:done(req, true, now, restMs); when it did not, arb:done(req, false) (the next box takes over); when you cannot cast at all, arb:fail(req); when the need went away, arb:release(req); when this box cannot act at all (dead, zoning, held), arb:standDown() gives up everything it holds or bid for. 4. Run arb:poll(now) every tick.

modules.name: eb.economy.craft
modules.summary: Craft at a station: select the recipe, make sure the fuel is there, run each combine with the right reaction art, and craft a whole list of orders.
modules.description:
The craft pillar of the economy (eco.craft). Every call is pollable: call it every tick with the same order and it answers "working" until the order is "done", or "blocked" with a plain reason. It never walks: stand at a station first (the brain or your script walks there). While a combine runs it casts one reaction art a tick, rescuing durability first, then quality, else pushing progress.

The pillars run on a drive table: the game windows each pillar reads and pokes (eb.economy.drive names every one). On this build a running EB does not build the economy for scripts yet and the craft commands answer "not wired yet"; a script builds its own economy with require("eb.economy").new{ drive = ... }.

How to craft from a script: 1) build or get the economy (eco); 2) stand at a station that serves the recipe (craft.serves tells you); 3) call eco.craft:craftOne({ recipe = name, qty = n }, { station = device }) every tick until it is not "working"; 4) for several recipes call eco.craft:queue(orders) the same way.
