modules.name: eb.economy.harvest
modules.summary: Harvest: decide which nodes to take, run a gather route, send the pack pony out, and track shinies.
modules.description:
The harvest pillar (eco.harvest). wantNode is the node rule; runRoute walks a route's stops on the mesh and harvests the wanted nodes in reach at each; packPony and trackShiny are the pony and shiny helpers. Every run is pollable ("working" / "done" / "blocked", why). The route walk needs a mesh walker in the economy (eco built with nav = ...); without one runRoute is blocked.

Config (cfg.harvest): blacklist = { [resource name or colour] = true }, categories = { [category] = true } (empty = every category), routes = { [name] = { { x, y, z }, ... } }. The tier band: one harvest tier per ten levels (level 1-10 = tier 1 ... 91-100 = tier 10); a node above your band is left.

How to gather: 1) put your route in cfg.harvest.routes (or pass the stops); 2) build the economy with a walker; 3) call eco.harvest:runRoute("<name>", { loop = true }) every tick.

functions.desc: A harvest node as the drive reports it (drive["harvest.nodeNear"](filter)).

modules.name: eb.economy.writs
modules.summary: Work orders (rush orders and the Work Order Clipboard): take an order, work out which recipe each step wants, craft it, hand the order in - again for as many orders as you ask.
modules.description:
The writs pillar (eco.writs). The clever part is which recipe a step asks for: its text loses its leading verb and its progress, then EB tries, in order, a learned answer, a known spelling fix, the exact recipe book name, a partial spelling fix, the name without its article, and last a LOOSE match - only when exactly one recipe in the book fits. A loose or unverified pick is crafted once and the step read again: it moved, the pick is learned (cfg.writs.learned) and exact next time; it did not, the next candidate is tried; none left, the run stops and names the step and every recipe it tried. It never logs a character out when done.

How to run work orders: 1) stand at the clipboard (or a rush-order giver) with a station in reach; 2) call eco.writs:run({ count = 3, kind = "clipboard" }) every tick until it is not "working".

Nothing fits: "ambiguous" (with the candidates) or "unknown".

modules.name: eb.economy.skills
modules.summary: Read a crafting skill (Tinkering, Adorning, Transmuting) as cur / max, without a temporary bonus, with the cap your levels allow - and say plainly when it cannot be read.
modules.description:
The skill reader the levelling runs stand on. The rule: an unknown read is UNKNOWN (ok = false and the reason), never a 0, and no levelling run starts on one. The reader asks an object for the read - the game layer is one (it has Skill, SkillText, SkillAbsent and TSLevel); eb.economy.new builds one for you as eco.env.skills over the shim you give it. The pure helpers turn the game's text into numbers and name the state.

How to read a skill: local r = require("eb.economy.skills").new({ shim = game, me = function() return { level = game.Me().level } end }):read("tinkering"); use r.cur and r.max only when r.ok.

modules.name: eb.economy.skilllevel
modules.summary: Level a crafting skill by its bands (Tinkering, Adorning) and a new crafter's tradeskill level, always from the live read.
modules.description:
The levelling pillar (eco.skilllevel). Every round starts from a live read of the skill, so a stopped run carries on where the skill is, and an unknown read never starts or continues a run. A secondary skill is levelled band by band from EB's levelling data: each band names the books to scribe and the recipe rows a round crafts. A round that gains nothing twice, or three broker trips with no gain, ends the run with the reason. Nothing is bought unless you ask (opts.broker = true, each book under the band's price cap), and what a round made is destroyed only when you opt in (cfg.skilllevel.destroyMade = true), each item through the safety rules.

How to level Tinkering: 1) stand at a work bench with the band's materials; 2) call eco.skilllevel:level("tinkering") every tick until it is not "working"; 3) read eco.skilllevel:status("tinkering") any time to see the band and the books ahead.

modules.name: eb.economy.transmute
modules.summary: Bulk transmute, salvage, extract or destroy a pick of bag items through the safety rules, and level the Transmuting skill on a stone merchant.
modules.description:
The transmute pillar (eco.transmute). A bulk run takes only what a PICK selects, and every item still passes the safety rules: a protected item, a Master or better spell scroll, a bound item (heirloom, attuned, no trade) you did not opt in by name, and an item whose details never read are always kept. A pick that does not say what goes - any tier, no bag, no kind, no flag, no resolve, the whole level range - is refused before a single item is touched. dry = true only previews, and a destroy only previews until you add go = true.

How to clear old gear: 1) preview: eco.transmute:preview({ action = "salvage", tiers = { TREASURED = true }, maxLevel = 50 }); 2) when the list is right, call eco.transmute:tse(the same pick) every tick until it is not "working".

functions.desc: Does an item fit the pick?

returns.desc: The items a run would take, the items it keeps ({ { item, why } }), and the opt-ins it used.

functions.desc: What a run would take and keep, and why - touching nothing.

params.name: opts
params.desc: The pick, plus action ("transmute" default, "salvage", "extract", "destroy"), dry = true (preview only), go = true (a destroy really destroys).

returns.desc: "blocked", "refuse: say what goes" for an empty pick; "done", { preview = true, taken, skipped } for a preview; else "working" until "done".

A pick must name at least one of tiers, bags, kind, a flag, resolve or a real level range.

modules.name: eb.economy.adornments
modules.summary: Adornment profiles: what each slot should carry, what is still missing, apply a profile or your class set, strip old gear, keep temporary adornments up.
modules.description:
The adornments pillar (eco.adornments). A PROFILE is { <slot> = <adornment name> }. Applying one gets each missing adornment from the bags, else the adornment depot in reach, else (only when you allow it) the broker under a price cap, and applies it to the slot's worn piece; a slot with nothing worn is skipped and said. Class sets live in the config (cfg.adorn.classSets) keyed by subclass, class or archetype.

How to adorn a character: 1) write the profile; 2) eco.adornments:audit(profile) shows what is missing and where it is; 3) call eco.adornments:applyProfile(profile, { broker = true, maxCopper = 50000 }) every tick until it is not "working".

modules.name: eb.economy.gearup
modules.summary: Score gear the way EB does, wear the best pieces in the bags, fill empty slots from the broker, and plan which spare piece goes to whom in the group.
modules.description:
The gear-up pillar (eco.gearup). The score ranks Resolve first, then Fervor, then Potency, then the role's main stat (fighter stamina, priest wisdom, mage intelligence, scout agility), then the weights you set in cfg.gear[role], with item level only breaking a tie (eb.economy.gearscore: the stat lines under one key set whatever the game calls them; a piece whose stats did not read is never judged). An upgrade that is worn takes the old piece's adornments over (the gear job, eb.economy.gearswap).

How to gear up: 1) eco.gearup:aup() every tick until "done" wears the best of the bags; 2) eco.gearup:fillFromBroker { maxCopper = ... } fills empty slots; 3) for a group, gather each box's export and read eco.gearup:groupMatch(exports, { planOnly = true }).

modules.name: eb.economy.grandmasters
modules.summary: Turn the "(Master)" spell scrolls in the bags or the Scroll Depot into "(Grandmaster)" crafts.

modules.name: eb.economy.collections
modules.summary: Collections: read the journal's collections, work out the missing pieces, add the ones you have (bags, then the Collectible Depot), and plan or buy the rest.
modules.description:
The collections pillar (eco.collections). A SCOPE word picks the incomplete collections to work on: an exact category wins, else every collection whose name contains the word; "all", "missing" or nothing means every incomplete one. Adding a piece CONSUMES it, so only a piece the journal still misses, not already collected and not protected is ever added. Buying has three models: "confirm" (the default) counts and stops, "queue" hands back the buy list, "auto" buys on the broker - and auto refuses without a per-piece price cap. A piece already in the bags is never bought.

How to finish a category: 1) eco.collections:missing("<category>") lists what is needed; 2) eco.collections:fill ("<category>", { depot = true }) every tick adds what you have; 3) eco.collections:buy("<category>", { model = "auto", maxCopper = 1000 }) buys the rest.

modules.name: eb.relay
modules.summary: Send scoped lines between boxes (all, others, to <who>), hear every box's short state, and run what the crew sends this box exactly once.
modules.description:
Each box makes one relay and joins it; nothing is sent or heard before join(). R.send(line) reads the line's one leading scope word: "all" reaches every box (this one acts at once, never twice), "others" every box but this one, "to <who>" the boxes the list names, and a line with no scope word runs only here. A line a box receives runs through onLocal and is never relayed again, so a crew line can never loop round the crew.

Every line carries a message id ("<box>#<n>"); a box acts on an id once however many times the line arrives. Boxes find each other by what they hear: every EB broadcasts its short state every two seconds (box id, character, zone, mode, health, power, a fight on), and R.boxes() is the roster built from it.

In a running EB the app's relay is eb.app.relay and its crew plane eb.app.crew; a helper normally sends through eb.dispatch("eb all ...") or events.crew(). Make your own relay when you build a tool or a test.

modules.name: eb.economy.lootrules
modules.summary: The loot rules: which rule names a dropped item, what each box does with a loot window (need, greed, pass, leave, assign to a member or a role), and the guard on destroying or transmuting after looting.
modules.description:
Pure Lua - it reads no game and no file, so a helper or a test can ask it anything. You hand it the rules (a decoded loot-rules table), the items a loot window shows and the window's type; it answers a verb per item and the one act for the window.

A RULE is { id, on, match = "exact" | "contains", item = "<name or text, * is a wildcard>", act, to, tier, notrade, lore, note }. act is need, greed, pass, leave, assign (to = a member, or @fighter / @priest / @scout / @mage / a class), or an after-looting act: destroy, transmute, salvage. The most specific rule wins: an exact name beats a contains text, a longer text a shorter one, a rule with conditions one without, then list order. A condition the window did not tell (tier, No-Trade, Lore) counts as not met.

Fail-safe throughout: an item no rule names follows the fallback (leave by default), and a destroy only ever acts on an item's exact name.

modules.name: eb.economy
modules.summary: The economy as one object: bags, selling, repair, restock, depots, bank, mail, broker, loot, crafting and the ledger, every part built over one table of window actions (the drive), plus the nine calls EB's brain makes between goals.
modules.description:
economy.new{ drive = ... } builds every part over ONE drive table - the window actions for bags, worn gear, merchants and the mender, depots, the bank, the mailbox, the broker, the loot window, trades and crafting stations (eb.economy.drive lists them all). The parts are fields of the economy: eco.inventory, eco.vendor, eco.depot, eco.bank, eco.mail, eco.broker, eco.loot, eco.auction, eco.commissions, eco.ledger, eco.craft, eco.harvest, eco.gearup, eco.transmute, eco.adornments, eco.writs, eco.grandmasters, eco.collections, eco.skilllevel and eco.tse.

EVERY ACTION IS A POLLED JOB: call it once a tick with the same arguments; it starts the work the first time, advances it a bite each call after, and answers at once with "working", "done" or "blocked" plus a plain reason. Calling with the same arguments resumes the same job; a finished job is replaced by a fresh one on the next call. Nothing waits, loops to completion or touches a file on the game thread.

FAIL-SAFE: nothing is sold, destroyed, transmuted, deposited or mailed unless a rule you configured picks it, and every pick still passes the safety gate (eb.economy.rules): protected items, items whose details were never read and bound items you did not opt in are always kept. Every buy answers the game's purchase question Yes only when it names the exact item being bought.

IN THIS BUILD the economy does not run inside EB yet: EB does not build it at start, so the item and loot commands answer "not wired yet", and the drive over the game's windows is not complete. A script can build its own economy over a drive it provides (the docs' examples run on an offline drive), and every planning call - what would be sold, kept, deposited, mailed or listed, and at what price - works on any drive.

How to run an economy job from a script: 1. Build the drive: a table of the window actions you can do (missing ones refuse with "blocked"). 2. local eco = require("eb.economy").new{ drive = drive, cfg = settings, me = snapshot, relay = crew } 3. Call the job once a tick (eco.vendor:sell(), eco.depot:topUp(rows) ...) until it answers "done" or "blocked". 4. Read what happened: eco.ledger:status(), or the job's reason when it was blocked.

functions.desc: The economy settings document (every key optional; economy.new and rules.load fill the safe defaults): bags = { fullThreshold = 3 } (that many free slots or fewer counts as full); protect = { names = { ["lowercase name"] = true } } (never sold, destroyed, transmuted or deposited); depot = { keep = { ["name"] = true } (never deposited), depositRule = a filter spec (eb.economy.filter) }; vendor = { sellList = { exact names }, sellJunk = false, sellTiers = { Rarity = true }, junkTiers = { Rarity = true } (with "novalue" for worthless items), repairBelowPct = 40, restockPresets = { name = { restock rows } }, fuelMaxCopper = 1000000 (the most one fuel buy may cost: eb restock craftmats' fuel and the craft bot's fuel step) }; loot = { method = "leader", space = 2 (free slots kept), rules = { ["name"] = need | greed | pass | leave | take | transmute | salvage | destroy | "to:<member>" }, autoTake = { names }, quotas = { ["item"] = { member = count } }, owned = { member = { ["item"] = count } }, confirmNoTrade = true, autoTakeNoTrade, keepValueCopper, rulesDoc = a loot-rules document (eb.economy.lootrules), aliases, wishers, resolveAuction = false, auction = { minResolve }, passLore, exports }; broker = { undercut = 1, beatAll = false, friendsFloorCopper = 0, priceDefaults = { ["name"] = copper, ["tier:type"] = copper, ["*"] = copper } }; bank = { depositRule, allowValuables = false, keepFree = 1 }; mail = { keepFree = 1 }; craft = { commissions = { enabled = false, allow = "fleet", names = { names } } }.
functions.notes: Names in the lookup tables are lower case. A settings file holds this table as JSON or a Lua data file (ebkit.jsontable or ebkit.lua_fmt).

The pure modules ride along on the economy table too: economy.rules, economy.drive, economy.confirm, economy.merchantread, economy.skills, economy.filter, economy.ledger (the ledger model), economy.lootrules, economy.grouploot and economy.commands.

modules.name: eb.economy.drive
modules.summary: The window actions the economy works through (the drive): the full list, a check of a drive against it, and honest stubs for the actions a drive does not have yet.
modules.description:
A DRIVE is a plain table, one function per window action, keyed "group.name": eco = economy.new{ drive = d }. A READ answers a plain value at once (a table, a boolean, nil, numbers) and keeps to the per-frame read budget; an ACTION starts the game's action and answers "working" (call the job again next tick), "done" or "blocked" plus a reason. No action waits, and none ever confirms a purchase by itself.

Write your own drive for a window EB does not drive yet, or a test: every action you leave out becomes a stub that refuses with "blocked" (an empty answer for a read), and the economy's job says so instead of failing. A drive may carry d.__drive = { name, proven = { [action] = true }, need = { [action] = "what it still needs" } }: the stubs and report() use those words.

How to wire a window of your own: 1. Write the actions you can do, for example d["bags.items"] and d["merchant.sell"]. 2. Check it: drive.validate(d) lists what is missing; drive.report(d) what is present and proven. 3. Hand it over: economy.new{ drive = d } - the missing actions refuse plainly until you add them.

modules.name: eb.economy.brokerexamine
modules.summary: One broker listing examined, whatever results page it sits on, in the three calls a job polls: send it, read what its examine window says, shut the window.
modules.description:
Built over the drive's broker.examine: the results page turned to the listing's, any examine window left up shut first, the row's own examine sent, the window's name and description read once the window names that listing, then the page turned back to the one shown before - one step each time you call. The send takes the first step and says a refusal at once, in the drive's words; each read takes the next step and answers nothing while the page turns; then the words come as { name, lines }. An examine that ended unread (the window never named it, its description did not read, the listing left its page) is never handed on as words - a decision made on missing words would be a wrong one. A drive without broker.examine of its own examines through the game layer's one-row examine instead (the listing must sit on the results page shown).

How to examine the listings of a search: 1. local ex = brokerexamine.new{ drive = eco.env.drive, game = game, has = eco.env.driveHas } 2. ex.row(listing), then each tick ex.window() until it answers words (or your own wait runs out), then ex.close().

params.desc: { drive = the drive (its broker.examine), game = the game layer (its examine window's close; optional), has = fn(action) -> true when the drive really has that action (the economy's env.driveHas; optional) }

returns.desc: ex: row(listing) sends the examine of a listing of the last search ({ name, row, serial, page }), window() reads it - nil while it still turns or waits, nil and why once it ended unread - and close() shuts the window and lets the examine go; ex.last = { why } of the last examine refused or unread.

functions.desc: The three calls a job polls to examine one broker listing on any results page.

modules.summary: Your bags: what is in them, the protect list, the one gate every sell, transmute, salvage, extract, destroy and deposit goes through, junk clearing, item search and handing items to a player.
modules.description:
eco.inventory reads the bags through the drive (bags.items never includes worn gear) and owns applyAction - the single door every destructive or selling action passes. It asks the safety gate first (eb.economy.rules.canTake, or the keep list for a deposit), so no path can take a protected, unread or bound item, and it writes the ledger line for a finished sell, deposit or transmute.

How to clear junk safely: 1. Say what junk is: cfg.vendor.junkTiers = { Junk = true } (add novalue = true for worthless items). 2. Call eco:contract().junk() once a tick until it answers "done" - it sells at an open merchant, destroys otherwise. 3. Put anything you must keep on the protect list first: eco.inventory:protect(name).

modules.description:
A RESTOCK ROW is { name, qty = how many to KEEP in the bags, who = the subclass, class or archetype it is for (nothing: everyone), depot = the depot kind (else from the item: ammo, fuel, food, harvest) }. One list works for the whole group: each box takes only its own rows; rows for the same item under one "who" add up, and across different "who"s the larger target stands. Depot kinds include harvest, ammo, fuel, food, adorn, collectible and scroll. A deposit moves nothing without a rule, and the keep list (cfg.depot.keep) and protected items always stay.

How to restock a group from one list: 1. Write the rows once: { { name = "Bread", qty = 20 }, { name = "Arrows", qty = 200, who = "ranger" } }. 2. On every box, call eco:contract().restock(rows) (or eco.depot:topUp(rows)) once a tick until "done".

modules.name: eb.economy.loot
modules.summary: Loot: what this box does with each drop, the corpse and chest sweep behind the brain's lootGrab, the leader's hand-out (quotas, the Resolve auction, Lore passing) and the group's loot method.
modules.description:
Each drop of a loot window gets one decision: take, assign, pass or leave. The loot-rules document (cfg.loot.rulesDoc with on = true, eb.economy.lootrules) comes first: a wish of someone in the group, then the rule that names the drop (need, greed, pass, leave, assign, or an after-looting action). A drop no rule names gets EB's own default: the per-name rule (cfg.loot.rules: need, greed, pass, leave, take, transmute, salvage, destroy or "to:<member>"), the always-take list, a quota a member still wants (cfg.loot.quotas against cfg.loot.owned), the leader's Resolve auction, then the group's method - leader only, keep and free for all TAKE the drop (the leader hands out what is assigned and loots the rest itself; a free-for-all window is taken whole), a lottery, need-before-greed or round robin answers Greed. A leader window this box does not lead is never touched. Leave is never a decline: the drop stays where it is. A lottery or need-before-greed window takes ONE answer for the whole window (Request All, Need or Greed when anything is wanted, Decline only when every drop is passed); with nothing decided it is left for you and never closed over its drops.

Never in a fight: lootGrab answers "working" and touches nothing while this box fights. A rules file that does not read means no looting by EB at all (cfg.loot.rulesProblem says why). A drop is only taken while cfg.loot.space slots stay free (an upgrade or an assigned drop always is), a No-Trade or Heirloom question is answered only when cfg.loot.confirmNoTrade, and nothing is destroyed or transmuted unless a rule says so (the after-looting action runs on the bag item once its facts are read, through the safety rules). Every drop taken is a ledger line.

How to loot by rule after each fight: 1. cfg.loot.rules = { ["fixture gem"] = "need", ["fixture rag"] = "leave" }. 2. When eco:contract().lootPending() is true, call lootGrab() once a tick until it answers "done" or "empty".

modules.name: eb.events
modules.summary: Subscribe to game events (chat, zoning, dialogs, loot, quest offers and updates, level and group changes) and react to them.
modules.description:
eb.events is one registry of event handlers. A handler you add with on() runs once per event, from EB's frame pulse - never inside the game's own event callback - so it may read the game, but it should stay short: record what happened or queue the work, and let a task do anything that waits.

Events fire on the box whose game client produced them and are never sent to the other boxes by themselves. When the crew should act on an event, the handler sends one deliberate line with events.crew().

A handler that raises is counted (events.stats.totalHandlerFailures) and stays subscribed, so one bad handler never takes the others down. The same line seen twice inside 1.5 seconds (the game often repeats a line once per chat window) is delivered once. At most events.MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK events are delivered in one frame; a flood past that is counted and dropped, never delivered late.

EB for InnerSpace's boot attaches the game's events and ticks this registry every frame before your script runs; your script only subscribes.

modules.name: eb.fly
modules.summary: A walk flies when flying is better - on a flying mount only, over the zone's flight field - and walks the rest.
modules.description:
A walk (eb.nav goPoint, every movement verb and quest step) asks eb.fly once, with its first ground route. On a flying mount, with flight on (the setting nav.flyauto, on by default), it flies when the ground has no route, only part of one, the destination is farther than nav.flyfar (100 m) in a straight line, or the ground route is longer than nav.autodetour (2.5) times the straight line; a trip that is short both ways (25 m) is always walked. A flight takes off where there is open sky (from under a tree or a roof it first walks out to open ground), flies the route the planner found over the zone's flight field (<zone>.hf: what stands in each 8 m cell and the open air under ledges and canopies; <zone>.fbound.json: the flight wall; <zone>.nofly.json: the game's no-fly regions), lands, and walks the rest. A destination under cover - a cave, a house, under a hill - is never flown into: the flight lands on the nearest open ground a walk joins to it and the walk goes in. A zone that will not let the mount fly is walked in instead, and walked in unasked for ten minutes after.

THE SETTINGS (eb set nav.<key> <value>, this box's own): nav.flyauto (on), nav.autodetour (2.5), nav.flyfar (100), nav.sightahead (200: a far end is decided again in flight), nav.followfly (on: a follower takes off, flies and lands with the member it follows).

THE GATE: the flight keys (fly-up, fly-down, steering in the air) and the flying-mount read are held until they are proven live in a game; a held one makes the walk walk and say why once a zone.

Every flight line in the walk's trace starts with [fly]. A walk can ask for a flight (opts.fly = true) or forbid one (opts.noFly = true).

A zone's flight ceiling (less 8 m) caps every height. No flight crosses the wall or enters a no-fly region.

modules.name: game
modules.summary: The game layer: your character, your target, actors near you, abilities, effects, items and the game's windows - read in batches and acted on. Get it with local game = require("eb.platform").game().
modules.description:
Every game read and action a script needs goes through this one object; it is the same on both EB targets. Reads are batched and kept for the rest of the frame: Me() answers name, level, health, power, zone, target and state from ONE read, and asking again in the same frame costs nothing. An action (target, cast, use) forgets what it changes, so the next read is fresh. EB's frame pulse starts a new frame with BeginTick(); a read is also refreshed on its own after 100 ms.

It only sends the game members EB has verified to work. A member that is not verified yet is never sent: the field it would fill keeps an honest default (nil where 0 would mislead), and an action that needs it answers false. Where a function below is held back that way, its notes say so.

Waits (WaitTarget, WaitCasting, Wait, LoadAbilities) only work inside an EB task; everything else answers at once and may be called from a handler or a frame job. Keep to about 8 game reads a frame: the reads here are batched so that a whole combat frame stays inside that.

functions.notes: inCombat is "a fight is on me" (the game's hate flag), not the game's lingering in-combat flag, so it drops the moment the fight is over. powerPct is nil (unknown) rather than 0 when power cannot be read. Perf: one read a frame, shared with Target(), InGame() and the cast bars.

modules.name: eb.ic
modules.summary: The instance runner: load an instance file (its hub, door, route steps and encounter scripts) and run it once or in a loop - the tank zones the group in, walks the route, fights each encounter, loots and leaves by the exit door.
modules.description:
An instance is a FOLDER: instance.lua (the zone, the hub, the door and the ordered route STEPS) plus encounters/<name>.lua, one fight or mechanic each, called from the route by name. Both files are pure data that only return a table. runner:load(folder) reads and checks them; runner:run(inst) runs one lap; runner:loop(inst) runs it again and again.

THE GROUP RULE. Every box reaches the hub zone by its own travel and holds there. Only the TANK walks the hub route to the door, and its one use of the door zones the whole group in. Inside, the tank walks the route alone: the group camps on the tank's camp spots and follows on the mesh only where a path step says group = "follow". The group never walks the route together, and a hub step that would move it is refused at load. A member's runner holds, waits to be zoned in and waits to be taken out; it never opens the door or takes the exit itself.

MOVEMENT. The runner moves characters only by walking the mesh (and the zone's own doors). After a death it waits for the revive and walks back from the nearest positioned step; when a box is wedged it uses the class evac chain.

FAIL CLOSED. A step the runner cannot honour stops the run with the reason (the next step assumes the last one happened). The only step that never stops a run is a chest that is not there.

THE INTERFACES. The runner does not pathfind, pick spells or read the fight itself: it calls the five interfaces it is given (nav, combat, brain, loot, upkeep - see the "env" entry). In a running EB, `eb ic` builds them from EB's own nav, combat engine and crew (eb.app.ic); a test or a dry run hands it its own. Every wait inside the runner uses the env's sleep and checks brain.aborting(), so a stop ends any wait at once, and a pause holds the run and moves nobody.

HOW TO SCRIPT AN INSTANCE. 1. Make a folder named after the zone's short name with an instance.lua: schema, zone, short, the hub (the hub zone, the door, where the tank stands to use it, its approach) and the route STEPS in order. 2. Write one encounters/<name>.lua per fight or mechanic: a when gate, phases of actions, a done test. 3. Load it with runner:load(folder) and read the reason when it is refused. 4. Run it once with opts.dry = true: every step says what it would do and nothing moves. 5. Run it for real - runner:run(inst), or eb ic run <zone> on the tank - and loop it with runner:loop or eb ic loop <zone> [minutes]. 6. Read report.verdicts (and the log lines) to see what each step came to, and fix the step that stopped the run.

functions.name: new

params.name: env
params.desc: The interfaces and host pieces: { nav, combat, brain, loot, upkeep, events, now = fn() -> ms, sleep = fn(ms), log = fn(line), limits = { overrides of eb.ic.ic_base LIMITS }, loadInstance = fn(dir) -> table, loadEncounter = fn(dir, name) -> table }. A missing interface is looked up among EB's own modules.

returns.desc: A runner: every function below is a method on it (runner:load, runner:run, runner:loop ...).

functions.desc: Make an instance runner over its interfaces.
functions.notes: loadInstance / loadEncounter default to reading <dir>/instance.lua and <dir>/encounters/<name>.lua; set them to hand the runner tables you built in code. now and sleep are the run's clock: every wait goes through them.

functions.name: load

params.name: dir
params.desc: The instance folder (or any key your env.loadInstance understands).

returns.desc: The instance table, its encounters attached (inst._enc[name]).
Why the file was refused.

functions.desc: Read and check an instance: the schema must be "eb.ic/1"; no hub step may move the group; every option must skip real route steps; every encounter a route step calls must load.
functions.notes: Errors: never raises; a broken file is refused with its reason (nothing of it runs).

functions.name: run

params.name: opts
params.desc: { dry = true (report, send nothing), from = route step index to start at, isTank = false (this box is a member), solo = true (no group waits), difficulty = the copy to ask the door for (else hub.difficulty), options = { <option id> = true | false } }

returns.desc: ok, "run complete" or the reason it stopped, and { verdicts = { [step id] = verdict }, checkpoint = the last step id started }.

functions.desc: One lap: zone in by role, then the route steps in order, then the result.
functions.notes: Errors: a step that fails stops the run with "step <n> '<id>': <why>". Perf: runs inside an EB task; every wait sleeps through env.sleep, so it never holds a frame.

functions.name: loop

params.name: opts
params.desc: Every run option, plus { minutes = the loop window (0 = until stopped, the default), laps = stop after this many, rerunFirst = override loop.rerun_first, between = { tse, repair, maintenance } (the chores at each run's end, all off by default) }

returns.desc: ok, why it ended ("stopped", "laps done", "loop time is up", or a failure), and { laps, chores = { per lap }, verdicts, checkpoint }.

functions.desc: Run one instance again and again. Looping ONE zone, the tank waits out the reuse timer INSIDE the cleared copy where the run ended, then leaves by the exit door, resets the copy from outside and goes back in. The first lap is a rerun of the copy you stand in unless the file's loop.rerun_first is false. A lap that finds every named already gone ran a copy whose reset did not take: the loop ends and says so rather than cycle a cleared copy.
functions.notes: A stop is how an until-stopped loop ends, so it answers ok. Members follow: they wait inside to be taken out and zoned in again. A LIST of zones (leave at once for the next zone) is not this loop.

functions.name: newCtx

returns.desc: The run state every step reads: { inst, opts, w (the world facade), verdicts, isTank, solo, difficulty, options, aborting = fn, paused = fn, ... }.

functions.desc: The state of one run. Use it to call a single part yourself (runner:zoneIn(ctx), runner:runEncounter(enc, ctx)).

functions.name: runOnce

returns.desc: ok, or the reason the lap stopped.

functions.desc: Zone in, then walk the route from ctx.opts.from (default the first step): the body of run without its header and report.

functions.name: runStep

returns.desc: ok, what happened, and "died" when the step ended in a death.

functions.desc: Run one route step by its act (see "route"), logging one line for it.

functions.name: zoneIn

returns.desc: ok, or why the group did not get in.

functions.desc: The whole entry, by role. Already inside: run from here. Otherwise this box travels to the hub on its own; a member then holds until the tank's door takes it in; the tank waits for the whole group in the hub, re-sends any member still elsewhere its OWN travel (three rounds, then it goes on and says so), walks the hub route alone, checks the group is in its copy and uses the door once for everyone.

functions.name: reachHub

returns.desc: ok once this box stands in the hub zone.

functions.desc: This box gets itself to the hub zone by its own travel (nav.travelTo); nobody is carried.

functions.name: awaitGroupIn
functions.signature: runner:awaitGroupIn(ctx, short, display, roundMs) -> ok, partial

params.name: display
params.desc: The zone's display name (either name counts).

returns.desc: true (and "partial" when someone never came), or false, "stopped".

functions.desc: Wait until every member is in the zone; a member still missing after a round is re-sent its own travel. Members are named by role or box id in the log, never by character.

functions.name: awaitZoneIn

returns.desc: ok once inside, or "never got zoned in" / "stopped".

functions.desc: A member holds in the hub until the tank's door takes it in. A loop waits as long as it takes.

functions.name: walkHubRoute

returns.desc: ok, or the hub step that failed.

functions.desc: The tank's own walk to the door: hub.route's steps (path, campspot who = "me", wait, interact; a wait_group step is skipped and said), else hub.approach's waypoints.

functions.name: useDoor

returns.desc: ok once this box is inside.

functions.desc: Stand within hub.entrance.tolerance of the entrance, then use hub.door (its actor and verb) for the whole group (who = "group"; "me" on a solo run), picking ctx.difficulty's copy.

functions.name: leaveInstance

params.name: solo
params.desc: true: leave with this box only.

returns.desc: ok and where we are now, or why we are still inside after three tries.

functions.desc: Leave by the exit door (leaveByExit), tried up to three times while still inside.

functions.name: leaveByExit

returns.desc: ok and "now in <zone>", or why not.

functions.desc: One try at the exit: find the nearest zone exit within 80 m, camp the group 3 m short of it when it is further than 4 m (an exit only takes from within about 4 m, measured flat), use the exit, answer the copy picker with its last row so every box lands in the same copy, and wait up to 90 s for the zone change (using the exit again after 20 s). No exit in range: use the zone command where we stand.

functions.name: awaitOut

returns.desc: ok once out of the instance.

functions.desc: A member waits for the tank's exit to take it out.

functions.name: nearestExit

returns.desc: nil | { name, x, y, z } of the nearest zone exit within 80 m, or nil.

functions.name: campShort
functions.signature: ic.campShort(mx, mz, door, short) -> x, z

returns.desc: The point that far short of the door on the line from me (the group's exit camp spot).

functions.desc: Where the group camps before an exit: never ON the door, where everyone would push into it.

functions.name: runEncounter

returns.desc: "killed", "cleared" (a trash encounter), "skipped:gate", "FAILED:<why>" or "DIED:<why>".

functions.desc: Run one encounter: its when gate, its combat override for the fight, its phases in order with the reactive ones checked between phases and on every fight tick, then its done test.
functions.notes: A failed gate is a skip, not a failure: a bonus named that did not spawn is skipped. Each pull restarts the fight clock and re-arms the once-only reactive phases.

functions.name: sweepReactive

params.name: ctx
params.desc: A run state inside an encounter.

functions.desc: Fire every reactive phase whose condition holds now (the engage action calls this on each fight tick).

functions.name: runAction

returns.desc: ok and what happened; nil, "unknown action" for a table with no known key.

functions.desc: Do one action: one key names one call to the interfaces.

functions.name: lootOp

params.name: key
params.desc: The verdict key to record the result under (default "<encounter id>.<op>").

returns.desc: Always true (a chest that is not there is a success), and what was looted.

functions.desc: Take loot through the loot interface and record what came. In a running EB a chest step takes every chest within 75 m, nearest first - a far one (the chest a named left out of reach, a double drop) is summoned once (game.SummonChest, /summon, when the command gate lets it out), else walked to - and the tank walks back to where it stood; a chest that will not open is said and left. A LORE drop that stays in the window because the tank holds one is asked of the group (every other EB box checks itself: eb others lootdistro scan <item>): the leader's own window hands it to the first member who lacks it (the window's own hand-out, held until it is proven live), any other window leaves it for them to take, and a chest whose lore everyone holds is skipped for the rest of the visit; the window is closed.

functions.name: watchRoute
functions.desc: The run watchdog: a lead nowhere near the route - more than OFF_M (60) from the spots of the step it is on and of the next step with a place, neither moving nor getting closer for OFF_SECS (45) - goes on from the step nearest to where it stands (a path from its nearest spot): it sets ctx.jump, and the wait in hand ends, as with eb ic goto. Every wait polls it through ctx.aborting, at most once a second.
functions.notes: Never while a fight is on, while zoning or dead, while a chest is walked to, while a member-down hold has the run, on a step with no place (an evac, the way out, a wait), on a dry run or a member's box. At most STEP_TRIES (2) a step and RUN_RESTARTS (4) a run, then it says so once and carries on.

functions.name: lootWatch

params.name: s
params.desc: The route step about to run.

returns.desc: nil | What the look took ("none" when nothing), or nil when it does not look (not a walk, a member, a dry run, no loot.watch).

functions.desc: Chests as they appear: before the tank walks on (a path step) every chest that appeared since - a trash named's, an event's - is taken (loot.watch, within 75 m), so none is left behind on the way. Said only when there was one. runOnce calls it before each step.

functions.name: lootSweep

returns.desc: nil | What the sweep took, or nil (a member, a dry run, no loot.sweep).

functions.desc: The sweep before the way out: at the zone's end every chest within 100 m is taken (loot.sweep), before the members' hand-over and the T.S.E, so what the chests held is traded and transmuted too. zoneEnd calls it.

functions.name: announce

params.name: msg
params.desc: The text; {{verdict.<step id>}} is filled with that step's result.

functions.desc: Say a line (the log, and brain.report for the windows), with the run's results filled in.

returns.desc: { actorPresent(name), actorDead(name), actorCount(query), myHealth(), mobHealth(name), inCombat(), distanceTo(spot), timerElapsed(name), resetTimer(name), detrimentPresent(q), chatSeen(q), hasItem(item), actorType(name), markFight() }

functions.desc: The one object every condition reads through, built over the combat, nav and events interfaces. A sensor that cannot be read answers false, never a made-up true.

functions.name: evalCond

functions.desc: Evaluate one condition.

params.name: list
params.desc: A when / done list: every entry must hold (nil holds).

functions.desc: Evaluate a when or done list.

functions.name: recoverDeath

params.name: enc
params.desc: Its encounter: an on_death list there runs first.

returns.desc: The step to run again (the one we died on).

functions.desc: After a death: run the encounter's own on_death actions, wait for the group to be revived, then walk back from the nearest positioned step at or before the death (skipping loot and skipped steps). Nothing is moved any other way.

functions.name: recoverStuck

returns.desc: What the evac chain answered.

functions.desc: When this box is wedged: the evac chain (nav.evac). Never any other move.

functions.name: betweenRuns

params.name: ctx
params.desc: A run state; ctx.between = { tse, repair, maintenance } says which chores run.

returns.desc: { tse = note, repair = note, maintenance = note } for the chores that ran ("done", "repaired", "not needed", "nothing ran", "cap reached", "unwired", "stopped" ...).

functions.desc: The chores at the end of a run, in order: every box's saved T.S.E pass (this box waits for its own, 10 minutes at most), a repair trip to the guild hall mender when this box's gear is under 90%, then the maintenance cycle (20 minutes at most). A chore that cannot be done is said and skipped; it never stops a loop.

params.name: text

The usage line when no file is named.

functions.notes: Where this box cannot read the zone's reuse timer nobody is walked out on a guess: a loop of one zone ends inside and says what to do (leave, reset the zone, start the loop again).

A missing id, an id twice, or a skip step the route does not have.

The hub step that would move the group, and why.

functions.name: saveRun

params.name: opts

returns.desc: A plain record (schema "eb.icsave/1") with the live reuse timer copied in (reuse = { [zone] = seconds }, savedAt = seconds).

functions.desc: Snapshot a configured run to keep. The record is plain data: store it off the game thread, read it back later.

functions.notes: Errors: a record that does not validate answers false, "bad saved run: <why>".

functions.name: stepIndexById

returns.desc: nil | That step's index in the route.

functions.desc: A route step id to the index run's opts.from takes.

functions.name: waitCombatClear

params.name: capMs
params.desc: The longest wait in ms (nil or 0: no cap).

returns.desc: true and "clear" or "stuck", or false and "stopped" / "timeout".

functions.desc: The instance combat wait: it holds while the group is in a fight or a straggler nobody fights is near (handed to the combat engine's own target list), and lets go on a clear or a combat flag with nothing behind it for 5 seconds. A lone in-combat flag never holds a run forever.
functions.notes: Perf: the nearby-NPC look happens at most once a second, and only in combat with nobody hated.

functions.name: anyHated

returns.desc: Me or the group in a fight (combat.anyHated, else my own hate flag, else the in-combat flag).

functions.desc: The fight read the combat wait uses.

functions.name: holdLook

functions.desc: One step of the combat wait.

functions.name: applyOverride

params.name: enc
params.desc: An encounter with a combat_override block.

functions.desc: Turn an encounter's combat override on for its fight (the runner does this on entry, and clearOverride on every way out).

functions.name: clearOverride
functions.desc: Turn its combat override off again.

functions.name: swimSet

returns.desc: ok and what happened. No swim hold wired is not a failure.

functions.desc: Hold or release swim-up for a water fight. The tank holds it for the group; a member's runner holds.

functions.name: swimRelease
functions.desc: Let a held swim-up go. The end of every run calls it, whatever ended the run.

functions.name: instance.lua
functions.signature: instance.lua -> { schema = "eb.ic/1", zone, short, hub, route, encounters, rules, options, loop, variants, loot_method }
functions.desc: The instance file. schema "eb.ic/1" (required); zone = its display name; short = its short name (what nav.zone() answers inside); hub = how to get in (see "hub"); route = the ordered STEPS the tank runs (see "route"); encounters = the ordered list of encounter file names (for checks and progress); rules = the rotation to arm before the first pull ("default" = the character's own cast stack); options = run options (see "options"); loop = { reset = "self", rerun_first = true, max_minutes = 0 }; variants = the difficulties the file covers; loot_method = { method = "leader" | "ffa" | "lotto" | "nbg" | "roundrobin" | "keep", rarity = "all" | "treasured" | "legendary" | "fabled" } = the group's loot method the lead sets as a run begins (see "startLootMethod"). The file only returns this table: nothing may run when it loads.

functions.name: hub
functions.signature: inst.hub -> { zone, name, difficulty, approach, route, entrance, door }
functions.desc: Getting in. zone = the hub zone every box travels to first, each on its own; name = its display name (optional); difficulty = the copy the door is asked for ("[Heroic I]"; eb ic run ... [difficulty] wins); approach = the tank's sparse waypoints to the door ({ {x,y,z}, ... }, the mesh fills the gaps); route = the tank's own hub steps (wins over approach): path, campspot (who = "me"), wait, interact, wait_group (skipped); entrance = { loc = {x,y,z}, tolerance = 8 }: where the tank must stand to use the door; door = { actor = "<door name>", verb = "<its verb>" }.

functions.name: route
functions.desc: Every step has an id (a stable label: verdicts, announces, resume pointers and options name it) and an act: path { spots = { {x,y,z}, ... }, group = "hold" (default: the tank walks alone, the group stays camped) | "follow" (the group follows on the mesh, for bringing it into a boss room) }; campspot { name, spot = {x,y,z}, who = "group" (camp on the tank) | "me" | a role list (split part of the group) }; encounter { name = "<encounter file>" }; loot { op = "chest" | "shinies" } (a missing chest is a success); announce { message } with {{verdict.<id>}} filled in; zoneout { via = "exit" } (the tank takes the group out by the exit door; a member waits); wait { seconds }; wait_actor_dead { name, seconds }; interact { actor, verb } (the tank clicks); swim { dir = "up" | "stop", who }; evac (the end-of-run evac to the entrance, inside the copy); lootmethod { method, rarity } (the lead sets the group's loot method from here on - the same words as loot_method). Any step may carry when = { <condition>, ... }: it runs only when every condition holds (else it is skipped and said).
functions.notes: Route parts are steps. A member's runner holds on path, campspot and interact steps (the tank's camp spots move it) and never walks the route itself.

functions.name: encounter.lua
functions.signature: encounters/<name>.lua -> { schema, name, aka, kind, spot, search, when, phases, done, on_death, kill_order, extra_targets, no_autotarget, combat_override, override_priority }
functions.desc: One fight or mechanic as conditions -> actions. name = the actor the fight is about; aka = other names it goes by; kind = "named" | "boss" | "trash" | "mechanic"; spot = where the tank fights it from; when = a gate (all must hold, else the verdict is "skipped:gate"); phases = the ordered phases (see "phases"); done = a success test after the phases (false = "FAILED:done-test"); on_death = actions run on a wipe here, before the walk back (they may not move the group); kill_order = a kill-first list (extra_targets go after it); no_autotarget = true keeps this fight's names off the engine's kill-first list (neither its own step nor the walk toward it sets one); combat_override = a combat override block applied for exactly this fight.

functions.name: phases
functions.signature: enc.phases[n] -> { id, when, repeat_, once, do_ }
functions.desc: A phase is { id, do_ = { <action>, ... } }. No when: it runs once, in order. when without repeat_: a one-shot gate that waits (up to 2 minutes) for its condition, then runs. when with repeat_ = true: a REACTIVE phase, checked between the ordered phases and on every fight tick, that runs whenever its condition holds - adds surfacing, a cure, a position swap. once = true makes a reactive phase fire one time per pull (an enrage, a scripted event).

functions.name: conditions
functions.signature: { actor_present = name } | { actor_dead = name } | { actor_count = { query, cmp, value } } | ...
functions.desc: The conditions a when or done list may hold (a list means every one must hold): actor_present / actor_dead = "<name>"; actor_count = { query = "<name>", cmp = ">=" | "<=" | ">" | "<" | "==", value }; health_below / health_above = <my health %>; mob_health_below = { name, pct }; in_combat = true | false; near_spot = { spot = {x,y,z}, within = metres }; timer_expired = { seconds, name } (since the pull, or since a reset_timer); detriment_present = { who = "group", type = "noxious", name } (true = any curable one); chat_seen = { match = "<text>", since = seconds } (a chat or emote line this fight); mob_casting = { mob = "<part of its name>", ability = "<part of the cast's name>" | <its number>, since = seconds } (that mob is casting it now - its cast bar, else the game's own "<mob> begins casting <ability>" line - it opens with the mob's name; a player who quotes it never counts - in the last since seconds, 5 by default, never before the pull: a reactive phase answers each cast); has_item = "<item>" (in my bags); actor_type = { name, type }; the combinators all = { ... }, any = { ... }, not_ = <condition>; or a function(w) for anything else. An unknown condition is FALSE: a misspelled gate never pulls a boss.

functions.name: actions
functions.signature: { engage = name } | { pull = name } | { clear_area = name | true, radius } | ...
functions.desc: One key per action, each one call: cast = "<ability>", who (only that role casts); target = { names } (a kill-first list); campspot = { name, spot, who }; pull = "<name>"; engage = "<name>", opts = { radius, reach, hpFloor, leash, chase, absentIsDead, timeoutMs } (fight it to death; reactive phases fire on its ticks); clear_area = "<name>" | true, radius (clear a pack; true = everything attackable); cure = { who, type, name } | true; dispel = { mob, name } | true (strip a mob's buff); reset_timer = "<timer>"; move_to = {x,y,z}; interact = { actor, verb }; wait = seconds; wait_combat = seconds (the combat-hold wait); wait_actor_dead = "<name>", seconds; use_item = "<item>", on, who, until_ = { conditions }, tries, seconds, every; swim = "up" | "stop"; ability_tag = { tag, seconds, mode = "allow" | "embargo" }; announce = "<text>"; loot = "chest" | "shinies"; wait_ready = { ability, who = "group" | "me" | <a member>, seconds, fallback } (wait until that box has the ability ready - it casts it the moment it is, eb readycast - else the fallback goes to every box that has it ready); anchor = "<label>" | true (keep where the tank stands - the yo-yo's out) and to_anchor = "<label>" | true, who = "group" | "me", within = metres (walk back to it: the group camps there too; it is used up, a later walk back needs a fresh keep; none kept is said, never a failed fight) - a joust out and back, a run-out that returns to the very spot; fn = function(ctx) ... end (anything else; ctx has w, verdicts and opts).
functions.notes: cure and dispel defer to the combat engine (only the box that wins the claim acts); with no such path wired they are a success, because the engine's own rotation may handle them. So does wait_ready: no wait-ready path wired is a success, and an ability that is not ready in time is never a failed fight (the fallback went; the fight tells).

functions.name: options
functions.desc: A run option: { id = "skip_bonus", label = "...", default = true | false, skip_steps = { "<route step id>", ... } }. An option that is ON skips its steps. A run flips one with opts.options = { skip_bonus = false } or by typing skip_bonus=off after eb ic run / loop. A skipped step is said, never run, never walked back to.

functions.name: blocks
functions.signature: inst.blocks[<id>] -> { kind = "if" | "while" | "repeat", test, until, max, seconds }
functions.desc: The gates a converted zone file puts on its steps (another bot's zone file read by EB, and the shipped copies made from such files): a step carries blocks = { "<id>:then" | "<id>:else", ... } and runs only inside its branch; a while or repeat runs its steps again until its until test holds (max times). A test is one of the conditions above, or the run's own: difficulty = "heroic2"; zone = { is | is_not | contains | starts | ends = "<text>" }; group_has_class = { "<class>", ... }; var = { name, op = "=" | "~=" | "set" | "unset", value } (a run variable a setvar step wrote); me_coord = { axis = "x" | "y" | "z", cmp, value } (where I stand); actor_near = { name, within | beyond }; engaged = { name, within = 50 } (that named is in its fight: up within the reach while I am in a fight; no name = I am in a fight); actor_at = { name, axis, cmp, value } (a living one of that name stands on that side of the line; a box whose actor rows carry no place says so and reads false); dead = true; option = { id, on }; always / never; unread = "<what the file said>" (false, said once). An unknown test is refused at load.
functions.notes: The zone-file steps beside the route's own: do { actions }, wait_until { test, seconds, on_timeout = "proceed" | "fail" }, command { line, who }, setvar { name, value, op = "set" | "add" (a number added, 1 when no value) | "unset" | "unset_prefix" (every variable whose name starts so) }, setup { kind }. Run variables last the run.

functions.name: env
functions.signature: env -> { nav, combat, brain, loot, upkeep, events, now, sleep, log }
functions.desc: What the runner calls. A call may block and answer ok[, why] or be pollable and answer a status ("working" = call again). nav: zone(), here(), distance(x,y,z) (flat), pathTo(spots, opts), goTo(x,y,z, opts), toActor(name, opts), interact(name, verb), campSpot(name, x,y,z, who), releaseCamp(who), travelTo(zone, opts) (this box, by its own allowed travel), zoneDoor(actor, difficulty, opts), exits(radius), zoneExit(who), copyPicker(), answerCopyPicker(who, choice), reuseSeconds(zone), resetZone(which), stuck(), evac(opts). combat: find(name, opts), count(query), myHealth(), mobHealth(name), inCombat(), amDead(), setRules(name), autoTarget(list), cast(ability, who), pull(name, opts), engage(name, opts), clearArea(name, radius, opts), waitActorDead(name, ms, opts); optional: cure, dispel, detriment, anyHated, npcsNear, addTarget, dropTarget, setContext, addOverride, removeOverride, useItem, hasItem, actorType, abilityTag. brain: isTank(), role(), group() -> { { isMe, id, role, zone } }, sendToZone(id, zone), sameCopyAsGroup(), gatherToMyCopy(), paused(), aborting(), revived(), afk(on), report(ev). loot: chest(opts), shinies(opts). upkeep (the chores): tse(scope), tseBusy(), gear(), inHall(), callToHall(scope), mender(), repair(scope), maintenance(opts), maintenanceBusy(). events: chatSeen(match, sinceMs) (optional).

functions.name: verdicts
functions.desc: What each step came to: an encounter step's verdict ("killed", "cleared", "skipped:gate", "FAILED:<why>", "DIED:<why>"), a loot step's drop (or "none"). announce messages read them as {{verdict.<step id>}}.

functions.name: begin
functions.desc: The start of a run: one header line (the zone, the copy, this box's role, DRY RUN when it is one), the rotation armed (combat.setRules with the file's rules, "default" = the character's own cast stack), the damage source said, one line per run option, and the group's loot method (startLootMethod). run and loop call it; call it yourself before runOnce when you drive a run by hand.

functions.name: STEP
functions.signature: runner.STEP -> { [act] = function(runner, s, ctx) -> ok, note, tag }
functions.desc: The route step handlers, by act: path, campspot, encounter, loot, announce, zoneout, wait, wait_actor_dead, interact, evac, swim, lootmethod. runStep looks the step's act up here, so a new act is one entry: STEP.ring_gong = function(runner, s, ctx) ... return true, "rang it" end, and a route step { id = "gong", act = "ring_gong" } runs it. An act with no handler is said and skipped.
functions.notes: The table is shared by every runner in the session: add an act once, at start. A handler returns ok (false stops the run with note as the reason), a note for the log, and "died" as its third value when the step ended in a death (the runner then recovers and runs the step again).

functions.name: stepPath

params.name: s
params.desc: A path step: { id, act = "path", spots = { {x,y,z}, ... }, group = "hold" | "follow" }.

returns.desc: ok and what happened ("walked 2 waypoint(s)"), or false and why the walk failed.

functions.desc: The tank walks the spots on the mesh (nav.pathTo, stopping when the run stops). A member's runner holds at the tank's camp, or follows on the mesh when the step says group = "follow" (the tank first lets go of the group's camp then). A dry run only says what it would walk.

functions.name: stepCampspot

params.name: s
params.desc: A campspot step: { id, act = "campspot", name, spot = {x,y,z}, who = "group" | "me" | roles }.

returns.desc: ok and "camp '<name>' set (who=<who>)".

functions.desc: The tank sets a camp spot (nav.campSpot): who = "group" camps every member on it, "me" only the tank, a role list splits part of the group off. A member's runner holds: the tank's camp spots move it. A swim-up hold that was on is put back after the camp walk.

functions.name: stepEncounter

params.name: s
params.desc: An encounter step: { id, act = "encounter", name = "<encounter file>" }.

returns.desc: ok and "verdict <v>"; false and the verdict when it FAILED; false, the verdict and "died" when the fight ended in a death.

functions.desc: Run the named encounter (runEncounter) and record its verdict under the step's id.
functions.notes: Errors: an encounter the file did not load answers false, "encounter '<name>' not loaded".

functions.name: stepLoot

params.name: s
params.desc: A loot step: { id, act = "loot", op = "chest" | "shinies" }.

returns.desc: Always true (a missing chest is not a failure), and what was looted.

functions.desc: Take the loot through the loot interface (lootOp) and record the drop under the step's id.

functions.name: stepAnnounce

params.name: s
params.desc: An announce step: { id, act = "announce", message = "<text with {{verdict.<id>}}>" }.

returns.desc: Always true.

functions.desc: Say the step's message with the run's verdicts filled in (announce).

functions.name: stepZoneout

params.name: s
params.desc: A zoneout step: { id, act = "zoneout", via = "exit" }.

returns.desc: ok and "left by the exit door (now in <zone>)" for the tank, "out with the group" for a member; false and why not.

functions.desc: The tank takes the group out by the exit door (leaveInstance); a member waits to be taken out (awaitOut).

functions.name: stepWait

params.name: s
params.desc: A wait step: { id, act = "wait", seconds = 1 }.

returns.desc: Always true, and "waited <n>s".

functions.desc: Wait a number of seconds (a stop ends the wait at once; a dry run does not wait).

functions.name: stepWaitActorDead

params.name: s
params.desc: { id, act = "wait_actor_dead", name = "<actor>", seconds = the longest wait }.

returns.desc: What the wait_actor_dead action answered.

functions.desc: Wait until an actor is dead (an event mob, a pet the boss leaves behind).

functions.name: stepInteract

returns.desc: ok and what the click did; a member's runner holds and answers true.

functions.desc: The tank clicks an actor (a lever, a portal, a chest that needs opening) through nav.interact.

functions.name: stepSwim

returns.desc: What swimSet answered; a member's runner holds and answers true.

functions.desc: The route act swim: the tank holds swim-up (for itself or the group) through a water fight, and lets it go.

functions.name: stepEvac

params.name: ctx
params.desc: A run state. (The step itself carries nothing but its id and act = "evac".)

returns.desc: ok and "evacuated: <n> m to the entrance, inside the copy", or false and why not.

functions.desc: The end-of-run evac, inside the copy: wait for the fight to clear (a while at most), let the last loot settle, let go of any swim hold and of the group's camp, then nav.evac takes this box or the group to the entrance. A member's runner holds; the tank's evac takes it along.
functions.notes: Errors: with no evac wired the step fails and says the group is still at the last fight - nothing moves the group any other way. Perf: one fight-clear wait and one settle, no extra reads.

functions.name: preArm

params.name: i
params.desc: The route step about to run.

returns.desc: nil | The names put first, or nil (not a walk, no fight after it, or nothing to put first).

functions.desc: The next named first from its section's start: when step i is a walk (a path step) toward an encounter - the next encounter step on the route - that encounter's names go on the engine's kill-first list once (preArmNames), so a fight the walk runs into takes the named first, not only once its own step is reached. runOnce calls it before each step; each lap puts it first again. The list orders a fight that is on: it opens none.
functions.notes: Not for an encounter whose phases set their own list (a target action), nor a dry run (it only says it). Never in the middle of a fight: while the group is hated it is held (ctx.armPending) and armWhenClear puts it first once the group is clear - the adds beating on the group come first.

functions.name: meetFight
functions.desc: A file's fight met in a fight: while the tank walks the route and the group fights, a mob of one of the next MEET_AHEAD (2) fights - its name, alive in reach - brings that fight's rules on for this fight: its combat override and its kill-first names, said once. They go off when the fight is over, or stay with the fight's own step once the route reaches it; meetEnd takes them off when a run or a lap ends. The waits look at it (ctx.aborting), at most once a second. The fight's phases stay with its own step.
functions.notes: Never a mechanic, a fight already done, a dry run or a member's box.

functions.name: meetEnd
functions.desc: A met fight's rules still on when a run or a lap ends go off (run and loop call it).

functions.name: armWhenClear
functions.desc: A section's named held off while the group fought (preArm) goes on the kill-first list once the group is clear; dropped when its own fight's step is reached (that fight sets its own list). The waits look at it (ctx.aborting), at most once a second, and runOnce before each step.

functions.name: preArmNames

returns.desc: Its kill_order then its extra_targets; with neither, its own name when it is a named or a boss; nothing for a trash pack, a mechanic or no_autotarget.

functions.desc: What a section puts first before its fight.

functions.name: stepLootMethod

returns.desc: Always true (a loot method that could not be set is said, and the run goes on), and what happened.

functions.desc: The route act lootmethod: the lead sets the group's loot method from this step on (setLootMethod); a member's runner leaves it to the lead.

functions.name: startLootMethod

returns.desc: nil | The line it said, or nil when neither the run nor the file names a loot method.

functions.desc: As a run begins (begin calls it): the run's own pick (opts.loot, from loot=<method> on the eb ic line) before the file's loot_method, and "keep" (either one) sets nothing. The lead sets it; a member's runner says the lead does.

functions.name: setLootMethod
functions.signature: runner:setLootMethod(ctx, method, rarity, why) -> true, note

params.name: why
params.desc: What asked for it, for the log ("a route step").

returns.desc: Always true - a loot method that could not be set never stops a run - and what happened.

functions.desc: Set the group's loot method on the lead's box: upkeep.lootMethod sends EB's own eb loot method <method> <rarity> (EB's own looting follows it, and the group's leader sets it on the game's group). A member's runner, a dry run and a box with no such line each say so and send nothing; ctx.lootMethod keeps what was set.

functions.name: checkLootMethod

returns.desc: nil, string | true, or nil and why: a method or a tier the runner does not know.

functions.desc: The loader's check of an instance's loot_method and of a lootmethod route step: a file the runner could not honour is refused at load.

functions.name: swimReassert
functions.desc: Put a held swim-up back on the boxes that had it (a camp walk lets the key go); campspot calls it.

functions.name: engage.abort
functions.desc: What the engage and clear_area actions hand the combat interface as opts.abort: a function that answers true once the run is stopping. A combat interface that fights over many waits checks it and gives up at once.
functions.notes: For writers of a combat interface (the env's combat table); EB's own engine already honours it.

functions.name: engage.onTick
functions.desc: What the engage action hands the combat interface as opts.onTick: call it on each fight tick and the encounter's reactive phases (adds surfacing, a cure, a position swap) are checked and run mid-fight.

functions.name: w.markFight
functions.desc: Restart the fight clock (the engine does this at each pull): every named timer starts over, and chat_seen counts lines from now.

functions.name: w.resetTimer
functions.desc: Start a named timer now (the reset_timer action does this): timer_expired { name = ... } counts from here.

modules.name: eb.app.ic
modules.summary: eb ic on a running box: start an instance run or loop as an EB task, see its status, stop it.
modules.description:
This is what the eb ic command runs: eb ic run <zone> [difficulty] [option=on|off] [loot=<method>], eb ic loop <zone> [minutes] [difficulty], eb ic stop, eb ic status, eb ic list, eb ic reload. The run is an EB task over the live environment (EB's nav, combat engine and crew), shown to the brain as its goal, and ended by eb ic stop, eb stop or eb pause.

WHO LEADS. The box the line is TYPED on leads: its runner is the tank. A box that receives the run from another box (eb all ic run <zone> typed on the tank) follows that box: it holds in the hub, is zoned in, moves only on the lead's camp spots, assists the lead's character, and refuses a run from a box whose character is not in its group.

A script reaches it as eb.app.ic and calls the same functions the command does.

HOW TO RUN AN INSTANCE FROM THE CONSOLE. 1. Put the instance folder where eb ic list shows it. 2. Bring every box to the hub zone, or let the run send each one there by its own travel. 3. On the tank, type eb ic run <zone> [difficulty] (or eb all ic run <zone> on the tank: the others follow it). 4. eb ic status says where it is; eb ic stop ends it and nobody moves. 5. To keep at it, eb ic loop <zone> [minutes] - 0 or nothing loops until you stop it.

modules.name: eb.loops
modules.summary: The self-sustaining chore loops as brain goals: overseer, errands, trainer, mercenary and collections. Build one, hand it the activities provider it acts through, and set it on the brain.
modules.description:
Each loop is a brain GOAL: { name, kind, params, ctx, advance(self, brain, snapshot) }. The brain calls advance once per tick between its own interrupts (death, fights, full bags), so a loop never waits: each call does one bite and answers "working", "done" or "blocked" with a reason. ctx is the loop's resume point; an interrupt freezes it and the loop carries on from the same phase.

THE PROVIDER. params.act is the activities provider (eb.loops.interface): the window drivers the loop acts through (overseer, trainer, mercenary, city writs) and the economy's writs and collections. A loop with no provider for its domain answers blocked once and says so.

SAFE BY DEFAULT. Every loop checks params.stop first, on every tick. Spending coin (buying mission scrolls, hiring a mercenary) and using items up (unlocking mercenaries from the bags) run only behind an explicit flag. The trainer spends points only on abilities your trainList names - it never picks one itself. No loop dismisses anything, and none ever logs a character out.

LOOPING ZONES. Looping an instance is eb ic loop (eb.ic, runner:loop): looping ONE zone, the tank waits inside the cleared copy until its timer is up, then goes out, resets it from outside and goes back in, with the chores (T.S.E first) at the END of each run, inside where it ended. A LIST of zones - call the crew out and move on to the next - is the instance queue (eb iqueue), which has no runner yet.

WHAT EB CALLS A TASK. Several kinds of repeating work, each with its own home in these docs: (1) a pulse JOB - a function EB calls every frame or every N ms, which must never wait - and a pulse TASK - work in its own coroutine that may wait with eb.delay (eb.platform: pulse.every, pulse.spawn); (2) a brain GOAL - one pollable step per brain tick, with the brain's death, fight and full-bag interrupts around it (eb.brain, and the chore loops on this page: overseer, errands, trainer, mercenary, collections); (3) an instance LOOP - one zone again and again, waiting inside until its timer is up (eb.ic runner:loop); (4) a power-level ROUTE - STEPS from one level band to the next (eb.plroutes); (5) an economy JOB - an ordered list of step functions with a cursor, advanced one bite per call, that every economy action stands on (eb.economy.job); and (6) the T.S.E hand-over - at the zone's END, inside, each member gives its T.S.E pick to the leader and every box runs its saved T.S.E pass (eb.economy.tse, and the instance runner's chores).

HOW TO RUN A CHORE LOOP. 1. Build a provider for its domain (eb.loops.providers.build fills the verbs you do not have with stubs that say so). 2. Make the goal: loops.new{ kind = "overseer", params = { act = provider, dest = { zone, x, y, z }, stop = fn } }. 3. Hand it to the brain (brain:setGoal / pushGoal), or call goal:advance(brain, snapshot) yourself once per tick. 4. It answers "working" until its pass is done; "blocked" names what is missing.

modules.name: eb.loops.overseer
modules.summary: The overseer loop: one whole Overseer pass - turn the finished missions in, add the mission scrolls, start missions with the agents the game's own rules pick, answer the reward windows - and buy scrolls only when you allow it.
modules.description: A single-pass goal: it answers "done" after one pass, so a schedule can queue the next. The pass is eb.overseer.pass: open the window (only what EB opened is shut again), read the day's allowance and the mission list, open the Overseer Quests boxes, add the mission scrolls under each mission's 10-charge cap, turn the finished missions in (never another character's), read the agent list, start missions - rescues, the tutorial, plain ones in list order, then charged ones by name - with the agents whose traits each mission likes (eb.overseer.rules), answer the reward windows, use the research material after a turn-in, shut the window. params: act (act.overseer is the driver, eb.loops.interface), options (the character's eb.overseer.options), facts (eb.overseer.facts), first (missions to try first), lift (a trip's own pass: "Do not touch the Overseer" lifted for it), hold, report, dest, stop, and the older scribe = false / research = false / buy / buyOpts. ctx.result holds the counters (eb.overseer.words renders them).

modules.name: eb.plroutes
modules.summary: Power-level routes: a plan of STEPS (travel, hunt, instance, actions) the route runner drives a tick at a time, with breaks, goals and pull rules. Load one from the shipped catalog or write your own.
modules.description:
A route is a plain table (see "route"). Bind the runner to the brain-shaped adapters, load a route, start it, and call runner:step(run) once per tick; like the quest runner it answers "working", "step_done", "complete", "blocked" (with why), "need_combat", "need_loot" or "need_travel" (with a zone), and the caller does those.

THE RULES IT KEEPS. Travel and walks are mounted, on the mesh, never fast travel. Pulls are closest first. The route runs at the group's own level: a route never mentors down and never uses a chrono (the format has no such field). The runner asks the combat engine for a pull; it never drives a fight.

Each step runs while the group's level is in its band and ends at its goal (a level, a number of kills or runs, minutes, AA points) or when the group outlevels it; the next step that fits the group's level comes next.

modules.name: eb.economy.job
modules.summary: The pollable job every economy action stands on: an ordered list of steps, advanced one bite per call, that never waits, never loops to the end and never touches a file on the game thread.
modules.description:
A Job is long work cut into steps: job:tick(ctx) runs the current step once and answers "working", "done" or "blocked" with a reason, so the brain (or your helper) calls it once per tick until it ends. A step is function(job, ctx) -> verb[, info], where verb is "stay" (still on this step), "next" (this step is done), "done" (the whole job finished early) or "blocked" (it cannot go on; info says why). job.mem is the current step's scratch table; it is cleared when the job moves to the next step.

ONE JOB PER REQUEST. Job.gate(holder, key, build) keeps one live job per key on any table you own, so calling the same action every tick resumes the same job instead of starting it over, and a different key is a separate job. A stop flag on holder.env.stop ends a gated job at once.

HOW TO WRITE A JOB. 1. Write each step as a function(job, ctx) that does one bite and returns "stay", "next", "done" or "blocked". 2. Keep a step's progress in job.mem. 3. Build it with Job.new(name, steps). 4. Call job:tick(ctx) once per tick (inside an EB pulse job is fine: a tick never waits) until it is not "working". 5. To make an action idempotent, wrap it: return Job.gate(self, "sell", function() return Job.new("sell", steps) end):tick(ctx).

modules.name: eb.economy.tse
modules.summary: The T.S.E hand-over: a member gives its T.S.E pick to the leader before the leader's pass, and the pick can be sold at a merchant instead.
modules.description:
The T.S.E is the pass that breaks a chosen pick of unwanted items down - transmute, salvage, extract or destroy, by rule (eb tse). This module adds its two other ends. SELL takes each pick item's adornments off (kept), opens the merchant in reach (the guild hall's Guild Commodities Exporter, else any merchant) and sells the pick item by item, each through the economy's rules-gated item action and recorded in the ledger. GIVE is the hand-over: a member trades its pick to the leader, twelve items to a trade, within trade range, leaving out what cannot change hands (No-Trade, Heirloom, Attuned, Lore) and anything it wished for in a loot roll; a member that cannot give answers "failed" at once, so the leader never waits on it.

WHERE IT HAPPENS. At the zone's END, inside, once the run is known to be complete: members hand over, then every box runs its saved T.S.E pass (the instance runner's first chore does this after each run).

FAIL-SAFE. Nothing is sold or given without a pick (a names list and/or a set of tiers in the T.S.E config, or the items you hand in); a protected item is never unadorned; a trade only goes to the leader the trade rules allow (with no trade rules set, a group member).

THE ENV. tse.new(env) takes the economy's env: { cfg = { tse = { names, tiers }, trade = { whitelist } }, pillars = { inventory = { scan(), applyAction(item, "sell", ctx) } }, rules = { isProtected(item, cfg) }, drive = the window actions ("merchant.isOpen", "merchant.near", "merchant.open", "merchant.close", "adorn.remove", "trade.near", "trade.open", "trade.add", "trade.accept"), ledger = { add(row) }, relay = { groupState() }, tradePolicy, now, log }. Every action is a pollable Job: call it every tick until it is not "working".

modules.name: eb.ui.monitor.parser
modules.summary: A combat meter for scripts: feed it combat records and read damage, healing and damage taken per fight, per character and per ability, with fights split by a quiet gap.
modules.description:
The parser moves only when you hand it a record (parser:ingest); it never reads the game. A fight starts with the first hit, heal or ward and ends after 7 seconds without one (or when you call breakEncounter, which EB does on a zone change); the last 25 fights are kept so two runs can be compared.

FRIEND OR FOE: the parser has no faction read. Your own name and every name you hand it (setFriends, addFriend) are friends; a name with a space or a leading "a", "an" or "the" is a mob; a single word is taken for a player. Whoever heals or wards someone becomes a friend, and so does the one healed. Outgoing damage is a friend hitting a foe; incoming (damage taken) is a foe hitting a friend.

How to meter a fight from a script: 1. local parser = Parser.new{ me = "<your character>", friends = { the crew's names } }. 2. Turn each combat line into a record with eb.ui.monitor.combatlog.parse and hand it to parser:ingest - or let eb.ui.monitor.parse_feed.attach do both from eb.events. 3. Read parser:current() for the fight going on, parser:snapshot() for it and the recent fights, parser:export() for a flat record to save or compare.
