modules.name: eb.nav
modules.summary: Walk the zone's mesh: to a point, to a saved spot, after an actor, to another zone by its own transit - and stop cleanly. EB's one mover.
modules.description:
eb.nav is the only way EB moves a character, and it moves one way: along a route on the zone's own .nav mesh, with the movement keys (eb.move). A walk plans ONE route over EB's mesh for the zone, then steers along it a frame at a time, re-planning only when it has to: stuck, a door to open, a hazard to back away from. A point within nav.SHORT_HOP metres whose straight line the mesh itself proves clear is walked without a route; a line the mesh cannot prove is planned like any other walk. There is no other mode to choose and nothing else to configure.

NO ROUTE, NO WALK: a goal the mesh has no route to - a spot past its edge, or any goal in a zone with no mesh at all, even six metres away - is not walked at. There is no straight run at it, no fallback walk and no swim across open water: goPoint answers false and says why in plain words ("no mesh: ...", "no route on the .nav: ... - the mesh has no way to this spot", "the spot is in open water the mesh does not reach (...)"), the character stays where it is, and whatever started the walk decides what to do next. A goal a few metres past the mesh's edge (within the router's 4 m snap) is walked to the mesh's nearest point.

LINKS: where the mesh joins two floors - a drop, a jump, a climb, a door - the walk goes to the take-off, faces the landing, taps the jump key ONCE for a jump or a climb, and goes on from the landing (nav.linkAction); a lift (kind 5: a mesh fixes lift, eb.nav_fixes.liftBridges / liftAt) is boarded, its actor clicked once (nav.liftClick), its wait and ride stood out, then it is stepped off at the exit.

CAVES AND RIMS: the progress along the route counts height twice over (a cave under a hill is never "near" the hill), a descent's aim is pushed out so the walk walks off a rim, arrival waits until the character is at rest (and walks back at most twice if it slid past), a partial route's end is no arrival ("the route ended N m short"), a walk knocked off the route's floor plans again from where it fell, and a wedged walk tries a door, hops a step the route goes on over, backs up and re-plans. nav.state says where a trip stands: Idle, WaitingForMesh, Planning, Moving, Arrived, Stopped (ended on purpose) or Failed; nav.last.state keeps how the last one ended.

IN THE WAY: a circle that comes up on the route ahead after the walk planned - a live blocker standing up, a circle added on the way - makes the walk plan again round it ("<name> stands on the route ahead"). No route while a live blocker stands up, but one with it down: the walk is held where it stands, keys up, until the blocker goes down ("held (live blockers): <name> is up - waiting for it to go down"), at most a minute, and the time held is not the walk's time budget. A solid prop is a circle only while its object stands there and is in the way (the mesh does not already wall it off, a walk does not go over it), at its radius + 0.8 m. Each "stands on the route ahead" re-plan is counted on its own (nav.AHEAD_REPLANS, 30 a walk) and never spends the stuck re-plans (stuckreplans). The route goes ROUND a circle - it keeps the object's radius + 0.8 m and takes a short way round its edge - instead of closing the ground it touches; only an object with no way round closes the polygons it covers ("no way round N avoid circle(s) (...) - routed round the ground they cover"). A circle holding the route's start or goal shrinks so that point sits 0.1 m outside it; the start's and the goal's own polygons are never closed.

A walk WAITS for the game a frame at a time, so it runs inside an EB pulse task (require("eb.platform").pulse() .spawn) or through a command (eb walk / eb follow / eb goto), never in an event handler or a frame job. Inside a task the default wait is eb.delay(0); pass opts.yield to wait your own way.

Safety is built in: a goal that stands in lava becomes its shore; twice a second a walk checks for lethal liquid and for health lost out of combat, backs away the way it came and plans round the spot. Cross-zone trips use the game's own travel network only (bells, wizard spires, druid rings, the zone's pads) - never the fast-travel map.

A walk ends with every movement key released and its outcome kept in nav.last. nav.active is the walk running now (its goal and corners, for a window) or nil.

How to walk somewhere: 1. Run your code as an EB task (require("eb.platform").pulse().spawn(name, fn)), or type a command (eb walk, eb follow, eb goto). 2. Call nav.goPoint(x, y, z) and read its ok, why. 3. Leave a walk early with nav.stop() - from anywhere, a handler included. 4. For a saved spot call nav.gotoNamed(name); for another zone nav.gotoZone(name). 5. Read how it ended in nav.last.

functions.name: goPoint
functions.signature: nav.goPoint(x, y, z, opts) -> ok, why

params.name: y
params.desc: The point's Y (height). A point is reached from its own floor, not one above or below.

params.name: opts
params.desc: { arrive = metres (a wider arrival circle than the default nav.FINAL, 2 m), exact = true (a spot to STAND ON: the circle is nav.EXACT, 0.5 m, or a smaller arrive), budgetMs = the walk's time budget (it grows to fit the first route), yield = fn() (how to wait a frame; default eb.delay(0)), onStatus = fn(text) (one line per step of the journey), watch = fn() (asked every step: nil goes on, a text ends the walk there with that reason, a { x, y, z } re-aims the walk to a new goal with the keys kept - how a follower tracks a moving actor), noHazard = true (skip the hazard watch for this walk), allowLethal = true (a quest step that has to go into lethal liquid) }

returns.desc: Arrived.

Why not: "stopped" (nav.stop), "no mesh: ..." (the zone has no mesh, or it is still loading), "no route on the .nav: ... - the mesh has no way to this spot", "the spot is in open water the mesh does not reach (...)", "... no ground way on the .nav (needs a transit)" for a far goal, a hazard limit, or "timed out N m short".

functions.desc: Walk to a point in this zone over the mesh. The walk is a route on the zone's .nav and nothing else: a goal the mesh has no route to fails and says why, and nothing is walked straight at it - the character stays where it stands.
functions.notes: Errors: never raises for a bad walk; the reason comes back. Only inside a task (it waits). Perf: one route for the whole walk on a clear floor, then one position read a frame; never plan routes from a frame job.

functions.name: plan
functions.signature: nav.plan(x, y, z, yield, popts) -> plan | nil, why, noWay

params.name: yield
params.desc: Called to wait a frame (inside a task): while the zone's mesh is still loading or on its way from the hub (up to 60 s), and between the slices of a long plan. Without it a loading mesh answers nil, "no mesh yet: this zone's .nav is still loading", and the route is planned at once.

params.name: popts
params.desc: The walk's own: { trip (its state - after a wedge trip.stepsAsGround plans step ground as plain ground), hold = { heldMs } (the time waited for the mesh is added there, so it is not the walk's), say = fn(text) (the waiting line) }. A plain preview leaves it out.

returns.desc: { waypoints = { { x, y, z, link, kind, steep, sharp } }, goal = { x, y, z }, goalY, mesh = ".nav", note, partial, start = { x, y, z } } - the corridor from where you stand; sharp marks a corner the walk turns at at once.
No route, and why; the third value is true when the mesh has no ground way to a far goal (that needs transit, not a walk).

functions.desc: Plan the route to a point without walking it: preview a walk, measure it, or check that a spot is reachable.
functions.notes: Perf: one route request. Do it once, not every frame.

functions.name: pathLength
functions.signature: nav.pathLength(ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz) -> metres | nil, why

returns.desc: The length of the route over this zone's mesh from A to B, in metres: the planner a walk uses.
Why not: "the mesh is still loading", "no mesh: ...", or "no route on the .nav: ...".

functions.desc: How far a walk would be: the length of the mesh route between two points, not the straight distance. For ordering spots by the way there.
functions.notes: Perf: one route request.

params.name: ax
params.desc: The start's X (or the start itself: { x, y, z } or { x =, y =, z = }).

params.name: ay
params.desc: The start's Y (or the end itself, when the start was given as one).

returns.desc: The walker's way from A to B over this zone's mesh: every corner of the route up to B, each { x, y, z } (A itself is not repeated).
Why not: "the mesh is still loading", "no mesh: ...", "no route on the .nav: ...", or "two spots: x, y, z each".

functions.desc: The way a walk would take between two spots, as points to draw: the planner a walk uses. The instance builder's Map view draws it, leg by leg.
functions.notes: Perf: one route request.

functions.name: follow

params.name: opts
params.desc: { once = true (return as soon as you are within the range), range = metres (stay this close; default nav.FOLLOW_RANGE), startAt = metres (a box standing in reach sets off again only beyond this), locOf = fn(name) -> x, y, z (where the actor is; default eb.actor.locOf), yield, onStatus }. A crew's follow wires more reads in; they are listed under eb.nav_follow.

returns.desc: Caught up (once), or the follow was stopped with nav.stop.
Only with once: "lost <who>" when the actor is not in sight, or why the last walk failed.

functions.desc: Follow a moving actor over the mesh, re-aiming the walk as it moves. Without once it keeps following until nav.stop(): when the actor leaves the zone the follower walks to where it went (on the mesh), tries the ways across in turn - the zone door, a step farther along its way - and finds it again on the other side. A zone line past the mesh's edge is said so ("the zone line is past the mesh's edge here - the mesh has no way across") and the door is tried instead; nothing walks off the mesh.
functions.notes: Only inside a task. Never follow a character someone is playing by hand.

params.name: why

returns.desc: true when a walk was running.

functions.desc: End the walk or follow that is running and release every movement key. Safe to call any time, from anywhere (a handler, a command, a frame job): the walk notices on its next step and returns false, "stopped".

params.name: on
params.desc: true pauses every walk on this box; false lets them go.

returns.desc: true.

functions.desc: Pause the walks without ending them: keys up at once, the walk waits where it stands (the time held is not counted against its time budget), and when it is let go it plans again from where it is. nav.stop() ends a walk; nav.hold keeps it.

functions.name: drop

params.name: co
params.desc: The coroutine a walk runs on, which its caller will never resume again.

returns.desc: true when it was the walk running now.

functions.desc: End the one walk that runs on a coroutine - keys up - without raising the stop request every other walk reads. For code that runs its own walk task; nav.stop() ends them all.

params.name: name

returns.desc: Arrived.
Why not.

params.name: zoneName
params.desc: The zone's display or short name.

returns.desc: In the zone.

params.desc: The walk options (goPoint's) for goto and follow.

functions.desc: Under this many metres, a line the zone's own mesh proves clear (its raycast, on this zone's loaded mesh) is walked without asking for a route. A mesh that cannot answer, or is still loading, is no proof: the hop is planned like any walk, and with no mesh at all it fails. The other tuning values beside it: nav.FINAL (2 m, the arrival circle), nav.ARRIVE (3 m), nav.FOLLOW_RANGE (4 m), nav.STUCK_MS (2 s stuck sample), nav.REPLANS (4).

functions.name: EXACT
functions.desc: The arrival circle for a spot to stand on (goPoint's opts.exact): half a metre instead of nav.FINAL's two. Used where a two metre circle would stop short - the mesh's own point just past a zone line.

params.desc: The walk's step state ({ i = the index of the corner the walk is at }).

functions.desc: Walk one of the mesh's links. A take-off is reached exactly (within nav.LINK_TAKEOFF across); for a jump or a climb the walk then faces the landing, holds forward and taps the jump key ONCE; a drop is walked off its edge and passed once you stand on the floor below; a landing is passed on its own floor. functions.desc: Set it to be told each time the jump key goes out for a link: kind is "jump" or "climb", landing the corner it leads to ({ x, y, z, kind }). Nothing is told for a drop, which takes no key.

params.name: range
params.desc: How far across to look for a known door, in metres.

params.name: trip
params.desc: The walk's own record (a table you keep for the walk): it remembers which doors were clicked, so one door is clicked at most twice a walk and never twice within 8 seconds.

returns.desc: A door was clicked, and which ("known door 'a fixture gate' -> apply_verb 'open'").

functions.desc: Open the known door nearest a spot - what a walk that is stuck in front of a door does by itself. The click goes out through nav.doorDeps.click (EB wires the game's own door clicker at start). See eb.nav_doors for the door data.

functions.desc: The door clicker a walk uses. door is a door record (eb.nav_doors.forZone), verb the verb it takes ("open", "use"), attempt 1 for the first try (the door's own verb) and 2 for the second (a double-click). Set it to your own table to test a door offline; nil means no door can be clicked and the walk says so.

modules.name: eb.move
modules.summary: The low-level mover the walker steers with: where you stand and face, turn to a point, hold and release the movement keys.
modules.description:
require("eb.move") answers the platform's movement service - EB for InnerSpace's mover below, or EB Boxer's with the same walking set (pos, heading, headingTo, face, stop, forwardOn and the turn keys). Prefer eb.nav for walking anywhere; use eb.move to face something, nudge, or read your position cheaply.

HEADINGS: EB counts headings its own way - 0 faces +Z, 90 faces +X - and converts to the game's once, inside. KEYS are your own game binds (setKeys); a key command goes out only when its state changes, and every held key is let go by stop(), by the end of a walk and when EB stops.

COST: pos(), heading() and swimming() share ONE game read a frame.

NO AUTO-RUN, NO FLIGHT: there is no auto-run key and no fly key. A character moves along a route on the mesh (eb.nav) or by a key you hold yourself for a step (forwardOn), and a walk lets every key go when it ends.

How to turn and step by hand: 1. move.face(x, z) to turn to a point (or move.faceActor(id)). 2. move.forwardOn(true) to walk, move.forwardOn(false) to stop - or move.tap("forward") for one short step. 3. Always end with move.stop(), which lets go of every key. 4. If your movement binds are not the defaults, call move.setKeys once at start.

modules.name: eb.navd
modules.summary: The mesh router under the walker: is this zone's mesh ready, one route, the nearest mesh point, the floor height, a straight line's clearance, lava and water under a point.
modules.description:
require("eb.navd") answers the platform's nav service: EB's own mesh router over EB's own mesh files, one per zone (the EBNav extension on EB for InnerSpace). eb.nav uses it for every walk; call it yourself to ask the mesh a question without moving.

A zone's mesh LOADS IN THE BACKGROUND: ready(zone) answers false, "loading" until it is in, and a zone with no mesh file says so plainly ("no .nav for <zone> in EB's mesh store").

COST: every call here is one request to the router. A route is a whole walk's worth of work: plan it once, never every frame.

How to ask the mesh a question: 1. navd.ready(eb.zone.shortName()) - on the first ask it starts the load and answers false, "loading"; ask again on a later frame until it answers true. 2. Ask: path / pathChained for a route, nearest to snap a point onto the mesh, clear for a straight line, height / floorAt / floorsAt for floors, waterAbove and polyAt for liquid and lava. 3. Keep the answer: the mesh does not change while you stay in the zone.

functions.name: ready

params.name: zone
params.desc: The short zone name (eb.zone.shortName()); a new zone starts loading its mesh.

returns.desc: The mesh is in and routes can be asked.
"loading", or why there is no mesh for it.

returns.desc: true when the zone's mesh is loaded or loading; false when there is none.

functions.desc: Start loading a zone's mesh ahead of time (before you zone in, or on arrival).

returns.desc: { { x, y, z, offmesh, kind, steep }, ..., partial = bool, why } - the corners after the start. kind marks a link corner (1 drop, 2 jump, 3 door, 4 climb).
No route, and why.

functions.notes: Perf: one request; a long route is one request too.

returns.desc: The route, as path() returns it.
No route, or a partial one that ends too far short ("partial route ends N m short").

modules.name: eb.nav_travel
modules.summary: Cross-zone trips over the game's own travel network: bells, wizard spires, druid rings, the guild hall and the zones' pads, planned as hops and ridden one at a time. Never fast travel.
modules.description:
A trip is a list of HOPS. Inside one network (the bells, say) every zone it lists is one ride from any other, so a plan is the fewest hops from here to there; each hop walks to that zone's portal on the mesh, opens it and picks the destination, and the trip re-plans from wherever the ride really landed.

City bells cannot cross between the good and the evil cities: a ride to the other side's city does not exist, and a trip whose destination is the other side's city stops and says why. An unknown side filters nothing.

The network comes from EB's own travel data (new(deps) swaps it for your own, as the examples do). The destination pick in the travel window is the step that depends on the game's window: when it cannot be made, to() stops there and says so.

How to go to another zone: 1. Preview the trip: travel.preview(name) (or eb route <zone>). 2. From a task, call nav.gotoZone(name) - or type eb goto <zone>. 3. Read ok, why: a refusal names the hop that could not be taken. 4. To see the hops yourself, travel.plan(deps, from, to) answers them without moving.

modules.name: eb.nav_hazard
modules.summary: The walker's safety rules as calls you can make: is a point lava, where is the shore of a pool, which zones' liquid kills - and the hazard watch every walk runs.
modules.description:
THE HAZARD WATCH. Twice a second (hazard.SAMPLE_MS) a walk puts one sample on its track: where you stand, your health, swimming or not, in a fight or not, on lava or not. A HAZARD is (a) lethal liquid - swimming in a zone whose liquid kills, or standing on the mesh's lava, unless the walk allows it - or (b) health lost out of combat: hazard.LOST_HP points or more within hazard.WINDOW_MS. Out of combat is strict: the window ends at the last sample taken in a fight and at any gap in the track, and a fresh stretch gets hazard.SETTLE_MS for a damage-over-time still ticking.

On a hazard the walk lets go of every key, circles the spot (hazard.CIRCLE_R metres) so routes go round it, walks back the way it came to the last safe spot (dry, health no lower than before, hazard.BACK metres or more back) and plans again. At most one abort every hazard.COOLDOWN_MS and hazard.MAX a walk. A walk that STARTED in the hazard has no safe spot behind it: it keeps walking, because its route is the way out.

How to run the same watch over your own mover: 1. mon = hazard.new(). 2. Every half second call hazard.sample(mon, { t, x, y, z, hp, swim, combat, lava }). 3. hz = hazard.check(mon, now, { lethalZone, allowLethal }); a table back is a hazard. 4. hazard.abort(mon, now), then walk hazard.wayBack(mon, k) to the spot hazard.safeSpot(mon, hz.x, hz.z, hz.was) found.

modules.name: eb.nav_doors
modules.summary: The zone's known doors and gates: what opens each one, which a walk may click, and how a stuck walk opens the door in front of it.
modules.description:
A DOOR LINE is one door: where it stands, the verb that opens it and its name. The router bridges every door line, so a route goes through a closed door; when the walk then wedges against it, it clicks the door - the live actor found at that spot - at most twice a walk. A name that is a zone line or a teleporter is never clicked by a walk (that would zone the box). A door's height must be the mesh's floor within 3 m.

TWO LAYERS: the door lines that ship with EB's mesh store, and this PC's own corrections (a door line at the same spot replaces the shipped one). A door whose menu says Close or Shut is already open.

How to add a door a route keeps wedging on: 1. Stand at it and note its verb. 2. doors.saveLocal(zone, { x, y, z, verb, name }) writes it to this PC's layer. 3. The next walk through that spot clicks it.

modules.name: eb.nav_fixes
modules.summary: The mesh corrections layer: bridges that join two pieces of the mesh, circles no route crosses, links switched off or added, and zones whose "lava" is floor.
modules.description:
EB's mesh is baked from the game's own geometry, and a bake can miss a join or add a false link. The corrections file lists, per zone, what to change: a BRIDGE joins two separate pieces of the mesh (and only that - a bridge with both ends on one piece does nothing, checkBridges says so); an AVOID circle keeps every route out; drop_links / drop_tris switch a false link or a triangle off; add_links adds a link the bake missed; lava_is_floor marks a zone whose lava floors are walkable ground (the lava rule is off there).

TWO LAYERS, like the doors: the corrections that ship with EB's mesh store, and what was installed on this PC (never shipped, so an update cannot drop it). The router is fed both merged.

How to check a zone's corrections: 1. fixes.describe(zone) for one line. 2. fixes.checkBridges(zone, navd.pieceAt) to see which bridges really join two pieces. 3. fixes.avoidCircles(zone) for the circles in force.

modules.name: eb.nav_bellmaps
modules.summary: What each bell's travel map was seen to offer, per side: the memory a trip asks before it picks a bell.
modules.description:
The travel network on file is one list, but a real bell may offer fewer destinations, and a city bell offers its reader's own side only. So every ring is remembered: which buttons the bell's map showed, per zone and bell, kept for the SIDE that read it (a map read by a good character says nothing for an evil one). A whole map (two reads that agree) that lacks a destination says "lacks"; a partial read never does, and a button that could be the destination is left for the ring to try. A memory older than 14 days counts for nothing.

The memory is this PC's own (beside the EB install, never shipped). EB writes it on a ring - rare, never per frame.

How to read a ring: 1. m = bellmaps.look(now) when the map opens. 2. bellmaps.addRead(m, labels, now) for each read of its buttons. 3. bellmaps.judge(m, dest, now) answers offered, miss or wait.

modules.name: eb.nav_swim
modules.summary: Swimming on EB's walker: the swim keys, the in-the-water read, the depth rule a walk follows in the water, no dive during a fight, and the group's swim-up hold.
modules.description:
THE DEPTH RULE: in the water every step holds swim-up while the corner it swims to is above you and swim-down while it is below, neither otherwise. A corner straight above or below is risen or sunk to on the spot. A goal under water that the mesh reaches is walked to as close as the bottom lets you; a goal under water the mesh has no route to is not swum to at all (the walk fails and says so - see eb.nav_swimout). IN THE WATER is the game's own swimming flag, else the mesh's liquid surface over you.

NO DIVE IN A FIGHT: a step that would go down while a fight is on holds where it is and asks again every second; after two minutes it dives anyway. A hold is never counted as stuck.

THE GROUP HOLD: before a fight in deep water every box latches swim-up (nav.swimHold(true)) until it is released. Flight stays off: this is swimming, not flying. Every read here can be swapped through nav.swimDeps for a test.

modules.name: eb.nav_follow
modules.summary: Follow a member across zones: step toward it over the mesh, wait at the zone line it left by, cross the line or click the zone door, and find it again on the other side.
modules.description:
nav.follow(who, opts) calls this. A follow has phases, and nav_follow.describe() says which: follow (in sight: one step toward it, re-aimed as it moves), far (out of sight in this zone, but the crew has newer word of it: a step to where the crew heard it), line (gone from the zone: walk to where it was last seen, and a little on along its way), wait (at the line: the zone door near here is tried, and a step farther along its way), zoned (this box changed zones: nothing is read or walked until it stands somewhere again) and hold (it is dead, this box is, or something else drives this box).

ON THE MESH: every spot past a zone line is aimed at the mesh's own point there - the nearest mesh point within nav_follow.SNAP_XZ across and nav_follow.SNAP_Y up or down (opts.nearest) - so a walk-through line the mesh reaches is crossed on the mesh. A step farther along its way that the mesh does not reach (no mesh point, or none farther along than the last by nav_follow.PUSH_GAIN) is spent and said plainly: "the zone line is past the mesh's edge here - the mesh has no way across"; the zone door is tried instead. Nothing walks off the mesh.

A follow never ends by itself: eb follow off, a stop or a new walk ends it. With opts.once it means one approach: false when the member is not in sight.

ACTOR MODE (opts.actor, eb follow <name> / target / <actor id> for anyone who is not crew): the same walk, distance and stop rules, with the one followed found by eb.nav_seek - by its name again after a lost sight, a despawn or a zone change; an id alone is that one actor and ends with the zone. A name nobody in range answers to is looked for a short while, then given up; a dead one is held for, never run to; this character's death ends it.

modules.name: eb.nav_zoneword
modules.summary: Pick the right zone from a short or ambiguous typed word: "ts" for a zone's initials, the start of a name, a word inside it - and say so plainly when the word is ambiguous.
modules.description:
A resolver, not a guesser: a word that scores below the floor answers nil (never a wrong zone), and an ambiguous word reports its rivals so a script can ask instead of picking blind. The rules, strongest first: the exact name, a whole word of the name, the start of a word, the name with its spaces taken out, the initials, then a part of the name. A one or two letter word only matches exactly, a whole word or the initials.

How to turn a typed word into a zone: 1. Build the candidates { { short, display } } (eb.nav_travel_live.candidates() gives EB's own). 2. zoneword.resolve(word, candidates) answers the short name, or nil and the ranking. 3. zoneword.explain(word, candidates) gives the line to show.

modules.name: eb.platform
modules.summary: One script, both EB targets: which target this is, the one clock, the frame pulse (jobs and tasks), files, settings and the log - every service a script needs, taken from one place.
modules.description:
EB runs the same Lua on EB for InnerSpace and on EB Boxer. A script never reaches for the target's own machinery; it asks eb.platform for a service and calls that service's methods, which are the same on both targets: local P = require("eb.platform"), then P.game(), P.pulse(), P.files() and so on.

TIME is P.now(): milliseconds that only go forward. Never use os.time in a script (it is not monotonic, and it has failed inside the game's Lua host); use P.now() for intervals and clock.wall() for a date stamp.

THE FRAME. Everything EB does runs on the game's own frame, about 100 times a second. A pulse JOB is one short call per run and must return at once; a pulse TASK is a coroutine that may wait with eb.delay(ms) without holding up the frame. Waiting anywhere else (a job, an event handler, a command handler, a window verb) raises a named error.

THE 100-FPS RULE: about 8 game reads a frame (the game layer batches them for you), no file work inside a frame (queue saves with files.writeLater), and examine-style reads (item, ability or effect details) are requests to the game's servers: read them once and keep the answer.

How to run work on EB's frame: 1. Something short and regular (watch a value, refresh a window): P.pulse().every("my.job", 250, fn). 2. Something that waits (a walk, a click then a pause, a sequence): P.pulse().spawn("my.task", fn), and inside it eb.delay(ms) or P.pulse().waitUntil(pred, timeoutMs). 3. Clean up when EB stops: P.pulse().onStop("my.helper", fn). 4. Save from game code with P.files().writeLater(path, text) - never a write inside a frame.

modules.name: eb.quest
modules.summary: The quest-pack runner: load a quest pack, start or resume it, and advance it one step per tick - it hands travel, fights and loot back to its caller and moves on when the journal's own text says a stage is done.
modules.description:
A quest PACK is a data file: the quest's name, its gates and an ordered list of steps, each one command line ("HailActor Warden Fixturo,1,1", "MM 12,0,30", 'CheckQuestStep "Collect three fixture lanterns"'). The runner is a tick machine: quests.step(run) does one bounded bite of the current step and returns a status at once - it never waits. Long work (a walk, a lift ride, a wait for the journal) spans many ticks.

THE STATUSES. "working" (call again next tick); "step_done" (a step finished: keep quests.pointer(run) now); "complete" (the quest is done, or deliberately skipped); "blocked", why (it cannot go on: an unknown or refused verb, a gate it fails, a wait that ran out); "need_travel", zone (get there by the zone's own transit, then call again); "need_combat", target (pull and fight it, then call again); "need_loot" (loot, then call again). EB's brain drives a pack this way, with its own death, stuck and fight interrupts around every step.

STAGES. A pack moves on when the JOURNAL says so: a step's completed line, CheckQuestStep, WaitForQuestStep and SkipIfJournal all read the quest tracker's own objective text (open, done, or gone when the stage has moved on). The journal is never read while a zone is loading.

OPTIONAL STEPS. A step with "optional": true may fail: it gets ONE try (unless it names max_retries) and, when it cannot be done, the run goes on without it - said once in the run's log, never a failed run, a trip back or an ended route. A zone change it asks for (a bell that is not on this ring) is driven by the runner itself on the nav's own answer, so a refusal passes the step by instead of ending the line.

NO FAST TRAVEL. A pack reaches every zone the ground way: its own zone routes, then the zone's allowed transit (bells, spires, druid rings, docks, doors). FastTravel is refused inside a pack. EB never flies, in a pack or out of one: a flight-only step (FlyUp, FlyDown) stops with that reason, FlyTo walks the zone's mesh to where its chain ends, and FlyDownInto reaches its zone on the ground. A spot the mesh has no route to is a failed step, said in words.

IN AN INSTANCE. Every box reaches the hub on its own; a group member's pack waits in the hub for the tank to zone the group in, and never walks the instance's route.

THE ADAPTERS. bind(deps) ties the runner to what it reads and drives (see "deps"). A missing adapter or method turns the step that needs it into a clear "blocked", never an error.

HOW TO WRITE A QUEST PACK. 1. Write a Lua file that returns one table: schema "eb-quest/1", quest_name exactly as the journal shows it, and steps = { { type = "command", command = "<verb> <args>" }, ... } in order. 2. Give each step that does repeatable work (kills, clicks, gathers) its completed = "<the journal line>" so it repeats until the journal says it is done. 3. Add the pack's own ways into its zones under zone_routes, and gates (level_required, faction_required ...) where they apply - never a fast travel. 4. Load it (quests.load), start it (quests.start), and call quests.step(run) once per tick, routing need_travel / need_combat / need_loot to your nav, combat and loot. 5. Keep quests.pointer(run) after every step_done so a stop resumes there (quests.resume).

returns.desc: { load, start, resume, step, pointer, stepTarget }: the runner bound to your adapters.

functions.desc: Bind the runner. Every function below is on the table this returns.

The file does not load, does not return a table, or has no steps.

functions.desc: Read a pack file. It is loaded as pure data: it may only return a table.
functions.notes: A pack built in code is used the same way: { quest = pack, name = pack.quest_name }.

params.name: opts

returns.desc: A run, to pass to step / pointer / stepTarget.

returns.desc: A run that starts at that step.

functions.desc: Resume a pack where it was.

functions.name: step

functions.desc: Advance the current step by one bite and say where it is. Call it once per tick.
functions.notes: Errors: never raises; a verb that raises becomes blocked with the message. Perf: a step's condition reads are capped at 8 a tick; a long run of skipped steps finishes next tick.

functions.name: pointer
functions.signature: quests.pointer(run) -> { step, zone, x, y, z }

returns.desc: The resume point: the next step and where the character last stood.

functions.desc: What to keep after each step_done so the pack can resume there. Write it off the game thread.

functions.name: stepTarget
functions.signature: quests.stepTarget(run) -> x, y, z, zone | { actor, zone } | nil

returns.desc: A move step's first point and zone; nil, nil, nil, zone for a travel step.
{ actor, zone } for a step about an NPC (a hail, a follow).

functions.desc: Where the current step wants the character, without running it - for a map, or to plan ahead.

functions.name: supported

returns.desc: true when a pack may use it (ported and not refused).

functions.desc: Can a pack say this?

functions.name: ported

returns.desc: Every verb a pack may use, sorted, with one line about it and its group (move, npc, act, travel, fight, quest, wait, gather, economy, relay, other).

functions.desc: The full verb list.

functions.name: refused

returns.desc: The verbs EB refuses on purpose, each with the reason a run stops there.

functions.desc: What a pack may not say, and why (grouping is the crew's job, an instance run belongs in its own file, ...).

functions.name: pack
functions.signature: <pack>.lua -> { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name, steps, zone_routes, fallback_travel, step_validation, ... }
functions.desc: The pack file. quest_name = the quest's name as the journal shows it; steps = the ordered steps (see "steps[n]"); zone_routes = { ["<zone>"] = { { why, from = { zones } | "@guildhall", side, bind, steps = { ... } }, ... } }: this pack's own ways into a zone, tried closest first, a failed way moving on to the next; fallback_travel = steps that reach the quest's start zone; step_validation = { check_quest_steps = { { text, step } } } (where to start when the journal already shows a line). Gates: level_required, ts_level_required, faction_required = { faction, min, max }, skip_if_holding = { sibling quests }, optional, continues_later (ending with the quest still held is not a failure), repeatable. Flags: no_smart_travel (default true: no fast travel), no_flight (kept for old packs: EB never flies whatever it says), stay_mounted.

functions.name: steps[n]
functions.signature: steps[n] -> { type = "command", command, completed, condition, skip_if_condition_false, max_retries, zone }
functions.desc: One step. command = one line: a verb and its arguments; completed = the journal line that says this step's work is done (kills, clicks and gathers repeat until it is); condition = an expression read before the step starts (${Me.Level} >= 120, ${Zone.ShortName}); skip_if_condition_false = skip the step when it reads false (a condition EB cannot read runs the step); max_retries = how often a retry may start the step over (3); zone = the zone the step belongs to. { type = "comment", description = ... } is a note the runner skips. ${...} in a command's arguments is filled from the world before the verb runs.

functions.name: deps
functions.signature: deps -> { world, nav, combat, economy, events, relay, journal, act, me, shouldStop, log }
functions.desc: The adapters a run reads and drives. world.snapshot() -> { now, inGame, zone, x, y, z, level, hated, zoning, group = { count } }; nav: walkTo(x, y, z, opts), travelTo(zone, opts), stop(), progress(), position(), ensure(); combat: engage, isWinnable, clear, active, fightIsOn, setPreset; economy: lootPending(snap), lootGrab(opts) (+ merchantBuy, brokerBuy, harvest, haveItem, depotDeposit, depotWithdraw for those verbs); events: poll, answer, peek, text(sinceMs) (game text lines for the chat waits); relay: send, barrier(name), amDriver(), evac; journal: trackerRows() -> { { name, parts = { { text, progress = { current, total, complete } } } } }, questActive(name), questCompleted(name); act: the in-world seam the verbs call - hail(npc, picks, flags), reply(n), choice(n), acceptReward(n), acceptQuest(), click(spec), useItem(...), transit({ post, tamer }), zoneOut(words), actorLoc(name, range), actorFind(spec), face(x, y, z) ...; me: alignment(), bind(), deity(), tsLevel(), faction(name); shouldStop() -> true ends the run on its next tick; log(line).
functions.notes: A verb whose adapter method is missing answers blocked, "no act seam for <verb> (wire act.<method>)".

functions.name: verbs.move
functions.signature: MM x,y,z | MoveToActor <name> | FaceLoc x,z | FollowActor <name> | Mount | Dismount | StopMovement | RideLift
functions.desc: Moving. MM walks the mesh to a point (x,y,z, or several joined by |); MoveToActor / FollowActor walk to an actor; FaceLoc / FaceActor turn; Mount / Dismount (LandMount is the same step: on foot); StopMovement / HoldUp stop; JumpToward jumps a gap; RideLift, UseLift and ClimbWall ride a lift or climb, a tick at a time. stay_mounted remounts before a move.

functions.name: verbs.npc
functions.signature: HailActor <npc>,<pick>,<pick>... | HailThrough <npc>[,rounds] | ReplyDialog <reply>[,<reply>...] | ChoiceWindow n | AcceptReward [n]
functions.desc:
Talking. HailActor hails an NPC and clicks its dialog by the picks given ("1", "3", or "1.1.1" for three clicks); HailThrough clicks the whole talk through; ReplyDialog / ReplyNow answer the open conversation, ReplyClose closes it; ChoiceWindow n answers a yes/no popup; AcceptReward [n] / AcceptNoChoiceReward / AcceptQuest / OK. A popup that asks the character to forsake its faith is never answered for you.

REPLIES. ReplyDialog / ReplyNow take a list, answered one after another a second apart (wait=<deciseconds> sets the gap): a number (1.1.1 is three clicks), LAST_ENTRY (the last reply) or the WORDS a reply holds, in any case ("ReplyNow Zephyl", "ReplyDialog mission"): the reply that IS the words first, else the first that holds them. Words that no reply holds block the step and list the replies - never a click on a guess. A conversation that is not up yet is waited for (2.5 s a reply). A reply window whose replies cannot be read as words is answered by number only.

THE OBJECTIVE AUDIT. Before a hail the runner reads the quest's journal: a still-open WORK objective (never a go-and-see line such as "return to <giver>") that an EARLIER step's "!journal key" of 8 letters or more owns sends the run back to that step - to its zone check first when the box stands elsewhere - instead of handing in unfinished. Twice a quest at most, then it hails anyway; said in the run's log. Never inside an authored route, for a hail run alone, or for a quest that is not in the journal.

functions.name: verbs.act
functions.signature: ClickActor <name> | DoubleClickActor <name> | ...UntilUpdate | InteractNearby | ApplyVerb | UseItem | Examine
functions.desc: Acting on the world. ClickActor / DoubleClickActor click an actor (by name, and/or at x,y,z); ClickActorUntilUpdate / DoubleClickActorUntilUpdate keep clicking until the step's completed line is done (20 s at most); InteractNearby, ApplyVerb, UseItem, UseAbility, Examine, Equip, Target, Press, ReadBook, Escort, DoorOption. Special [Auto] clicks the nearest special object (a glowing thing a zone wants clicked; the command is eb special) with the box standing, sees what it did and waits a zone load out; nothing in reach is tried again, then fails in words.

functions.name: verbs.fight
functions.signature: KillMobs "<mob>","",<radius>,<pulls> | KillQuestMobs ... | Pull <name> | LootAll | Leash | AvoidArea
functions.desc: Fighting, handed back to the caller. KillMobs / KillQuestMobs / Pull answer need_combat with the target until the step's completed line (or the objective) is done; LootAll answers need_loot until nothing is pending. Leash and AvoidArea put fences on every pull of the run. The combat engine owns the fight: it judges what is winnable and never attacks guards.

functions.name: verbs.travel
functions.signature: CheckZone "<zone>" | TravelBell | TravelSpire | TravelDruid | Transit "<post> | <tamer>" | ZoneDoor | ZoneOut
functions.desc: Changing zones, always the ground way. CheckZone runs the pack's own zone routes, then hands the zone back as need_travel; TravelBell / TravelSpire / TravelDruid / NavigateToZone name the zone's transit; Transit rides an in-zone transport to a post; ZoneDoor uses a door; ZoneOut leaves by the zone's exit; WaitForZone / WaitForZoning wait out a load; CallGH recalls to the guild hall; Evac. SmartTravelTo and TravelTo reach their zone on the ground. FastTravelFirst "<zone>",<place>,<n>: with n = 0 (or none) a ground trip to the place; with n above 0 it is done at once, because the n steps written below it are the pack's own way in the world - never a jump on the map. FastTravel is refused in a pack; FlyUp / FlyDown stop (EB never flies); FlyTo walks the mesh to where its chain ends and FlyDownInto reaches its zone on the ground.

functions.name: verbs.quest
functions.desc: Reading the journal. CheckQuestStep is a gate: the line must be in the quest's journal (open or done); WaitForQuestStep waits (working, never blocking) until the line shows or moves on, blocked at its time limit (or goes on with -continue); WaitForJournalStep waits for a step to complete and never fails; SkipIfJournal skips the next N steps when the line is done; SkipIf / SkipIfQuestActive / SkipIfHaveItems / SkipIfActorWithin and the other SkipIf forms skip on other facts; RepeatUntilJournal / RepeatUntilQuest go back N steps until the journal moves; CheckCompletedQuest skips a quest that is already done; QuestComplete checks the quest left the journal (the hand-in worked); MakeCurrentQuest sets which quest the journal checks read.

functions.name: verbs.wait
functions.desc: Waiting, a tick at a time: Wait, WaitFor (a condition), WaitForCombat, WaitForActorNear, WaitForActorSpawn, WaitForActorDeath, EventWaitForChat / EventWaitForEmote (a line of game text), EventWaitForZoneChange, CheckActorExists. No wait is longer than an hour, whatever a pack says.

functions.name: verbs.more
functions.signature: MerchantBuy | BrokerBuyItem | CraftItem | ScribeRecipe | HarvestQuestItem | OpenMail | TakeTurn | EndTurn
functions.desc:
The rest, by group: economy (MerchantBuy, BuyFromMerchant, BrokerBuyItem, CraftItem, ScribeRecipe, DumpAllToDepots, RemoveFromDepot, StartResearch, OpenMail, GetMailAttachment), gather (HarvestQuestItem, GatherMultipleUntilComplete), and the crew (TakeTurn / EndTurn: one box at a time at a world event). quest.ported() lists every verb; quest.refused() lists the ones EB refuses with the reason.

QueueMissionIC <table>[,mark][,run][,wait=<seconds>] puts the instance run of the mission an NPC just gave in the instance queue: with mark, before the hail, it notes which missions of the table (the _missions folder of the task folder, <table>.lua: the NPC's missions and the run of each) the journal already holds; without it, after the hail, it waits (20 s) for ONE mission that was not held, takes the offer if one is still up, and queues its run (eb iqueue add); run starts the queue. No mission in time, two at once, a mission with no run in EB or a refusing queue: the step fails and says why.

Linguist <language> (Halasian, Oggish, Ratongan, Stout or Ykeshan) learns a language the in-world way: it sends eb linguist <language> once - this character's Linguist, the primer bought (never over its budget) and used - and waits while the trip goes (30 minutes at most, then it stops the trip). It passes with the words of the trip, and fails, saying why, when the trip is refused (a language no Linguist sells, no Linguist to reach, a trip already going) or ends without the language. A quest that is stopped, cancelled or skipped past while its trip goes stops the trip.

modules.name: eb.quest.verbs
modules.summary: The pack verb registry: add your own verb, and the small parsers every verb's arguments go through.
modules.description:
Every verb a pack can say is registered here once. register(keys, fn, about, group) adds one; its handler gets the step's context (ctx) and answers with one of the statuses through ctx:done, ctx:work, ctx:travel, ctx:combat, ctx:loot, ctx:complete, ctx:block or ctx:stop. A handler is called again every tick while it answers working, so it must return at once and keep its progress in ctx.state (that step's own scratch table).

THE CONTEXT. ctx.cmd = { verb, key (lower case), rest (the arguments), line }; ctx.step = the step table; ctx.state = this step's scratch; ctx.snap = this tick's world snapshot; ctx.dep = the adapters; ctx.jrnl = the journal reader (eb.quest.journal); ctx.questName; ctx:zone(), ctx:pos(), ctx:loading(), ctx:groupCount(), ctx:amDriver(), ctx:deadline(ms), ctx:since(key), ctx:retry(why), ctx:skip(n), ctx:jump(i).

A verb nobody registered stops the run with a clear reason - a pack is never guessed at.

A window is two things. Its STATE: build(win) returns a plain, JSON-able table of everything the page shows; state() returns the SAME table until something changes, so a quiet window costs nothing (the bridge only sends a new table). Call win:touch() when something it shows changed. Its VERBS: the allow-list of what a click may do; a page can run nothing else. modules.name: ebkit.push_budget
modules.summary: Keep windows from costing frames: cap how often each window's state goes out, and spread a big game scan over several frames with a read budget.
modules.description:
A window's class sets its pace: hud 100 ms (an always-on gauge), bar 250 ms, panel 200 ms, request 50 ms (it changes only on a press). A change that comes sooner than its class allows is HELD and the newest one goes out when the window is due - never a queue of old ones. A shared bucket (24 a second, bursts of 5) keeps a whole pass of windows from going out at once.

The READ BUDGET is for code that reads the game in a loop: count the reads, stop at about 8, and carry on next frame instead of costing the game its frame rate.

Every caller in the same frame gets the SAME table, so ten readers cost one read. A window builds its state from the snapshot, never with game reads of its own.

THE SNAPSHOT: { now, inGame, name, class, archetype ("fighter" | "priest" | "mage" | "scout"), level, zone, hpPct, powerPct, dead, hated (a fight is on you), moving, x, y, z, bagsFreeSlots, group = { count, members = { { name, zone, dead, distance, subclass, role } } }, reads, partial }. When inGame is false (character select, a zone loading) nothing else in it is to be trusted. A group member in another zone has no zone (nil), never a guess.

modules.name: eb.brain.contracts
modules.summary: What every subsystem gives the brain - nav, combat, quests, economy, events, relay, the world - and the statuses a goal reads back. Check your own subsystem against it.
modules.description:
THE ONE CONVENTION: every action a subsystem gives the brain is NON-BLOCKING, POLLABLE and IDEMPOTENT. A goal calls it once per tick with the same arguments; the first call starts the work and every later call reports progress, and it returns at once with a short status: "working" (still going, call me again), "done" (finished; movement says "arrived"), "blocked" (cannot go on now, with a reason as the second value). Movement adds "stuck"; combat answers "engaged" / "refused" and "fighting" / "clear"; a quest step answers "working", "step_done", "complete", "blocked", "need_travel", "need_combat" or "need_loot".

So a goal never waits: it asks nav.walkTo(...) each tick until it says "arrived", combat.clear() each tick until it says "clear", and so on. Long work lives in the subsystem; recovery (death, stuck, a fight, full bags) lives in the brain's interrupts, which freeze the goal and give it back where it was.

modules.name: eb.brain
modules.summary: The autonomy brain: one goal at a time, advanced one bite per tick (about 4 a second), with interrupts that take over for death, a zone reset, a fight, being stuck, a member down, full bags and low health or power.
modules.description:
brain:pulse(now) is called every frame and ticks at most every tickMs (250 ms). A tick takes ONE world snapshot (inside the read budget) and does ONE bite of work: the highest interrupt that fires (death 100, zone reset 80, combat 70, stuck 60, group down 50, full bags 40, low health or power 30), else the active goal's advance(). While an interrupt runs the goal is frozen, untouched, and resumes from the same phase when it clears.

A GOAL is a table { name, ctx = { phase = ... }, advance = fn(self, b, snap) -> status, describe = fn(self) -> text }. advance returns "working" (call again), "done" (finished: it leaves the stack) or "blocked" (with a reason). It never waits: it calls the subsystems (b.sub.nav, b.sub.combat, b.sub.relay ...), which answer at once with their status. The built-in kinds are grind, vendor, travel, questline, harvest, craft and follow ({ kind = "grind", params = { camp = { x, y, z, radius }, maxKills } }).

The brain answers what it can by itself (rez offers, group invites, popups) and never stops to ask. A running EB keeps its brain as eb.app.brain; eb pause and eb resume pause it.

modules.name: eb.brain.goals
modules.summary: The goals the brain can pursue: grind a camp, vendor, travel, run a quest line, harvest, craft and follow - each a small phase machine advanced one bite per tick.
modules.description: Every goal follows the same loop: select, travel, act, loot, continue. advance(self, b, snap) returns "working", "done" or "blocked" (with a reason) and never waits: it calls a subsystem and asks again next tick. The goal's ctx is its resume point - an interrupt never touches it, so the goal carries on where it was.

functions.name: new

params.name: spec
params.desc: { kind = "grind" | "vendor" | "travel" | "questline" | "harvest" | "craft" | "follow", params = { ... } } - or a goal table of your own (one with advance), which is returned as it is.

returns.desc: { name, kind, params, ctx = { phase, kills }, preset, advance, describe }

functions.desc: Build a goal. Each kind starts in its own first phase and sets a combat preset (grind, questline and harvest: openworld; vendor, travel and craft: afk; follow: instance).
functions.notes: Errors: raises on an unknown kind.

functions.name: describe

returns.desc: "<name>[<phase>]", for example "grind[travel]".

functions.desc: A goal and where it is, in one word.

functions.name: KINDS
functions.desc: The goal kinds. grind params: { camp = { x, y, z, radius }, maxKills (nil = forever), preset }. A goal of your own needs only name, ctx = { phase }, advance(self, b, snap) and describe(self).

modules.name: eb.brain.interrupts
modules.summary: The seven things that take over from the goal, highest first: death, a zone reset, a fight, being stuck, a member down, full bags, and low health or power.
modules.description: Each interrupt is a small recovery routine: poll(b, snap) says whether it fires this tick (cheap), enter(b, snap) runs once when it takes over, handle(b, snap) does one bite ("working", "cleared" or "failed") and reset() forgets its state. A higher one firing takes over from a lower one (death over stuck). Death waits for the revive and goes back; a fight is left to the combat engine (the brain only waits); stuck tries the crew's catch-up first and the evac chain second - never anything but walking; full bags junk and then vendor; low health or power rests only when nothing else needs doing.

functions.name: new

params.name: cfg
params.desc: Not used: each interrupt reads its thresholds from the brain's cfg every tick (stuckMs, bagMinSlots, restHpPct, restPowerPct ...).

returns.desc: The interrupts, highest priority first: death 100, zone_reset 80, combat 70, stuck 60, group_down 50, full_bags 40, low_hp_power 30.

functions.desc: Build the interrupt set (brain.new does).

examples.title: Ask the platform for a service
examples.summary: One script runs on both EB targets: ask eb.platform which target it is on and take each service from it.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
print("target " .. P.name())                       -- "isx" on EB for InnerSpace, "boxer" on EB Boxer

local clock = P.clock()                            -- the same as P.get("clock")
local pulse, files, log = P.pulse(), P.files(), P.log()
log.info("docs", "services ready: clock %s, pulse %s, files %s", tostring(clock ~= nil), tostring(pulse ~= nil),
    files.kind)

-- every service of this target against its contract: nothing missing, nothing unavailable
local missing = {}
for service, r in pairs(P.check()) do
    if r.unavailable or #(r.missing or {}) > 0 then missing[#missing + 1] = service end
end

-- check
DOCS.eq(P.name(), "isx", "the target")
DOCS.check(P.get("clock") == clock, "P.clock() is P.get('clock')")
DOCS.eq(#missing, 0, "every service meets its contract")
DOCS.check(w.said("services ready"), "the log line reached the console")
examples.expect: Names the target, gets the clock, pulse, files and log services, and checks every service meets its contract.

examples.title: Time something with the platform clock
examples.summary: P.now() is milliseconds that only go forward: measure how long something took without os.time.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local started = P.now()                 -- ms; eb.now() is the same clock on the eb global
w.frame(30)                             -- (offline: 30 frames of 16 ms pass; in game, time just passes)
local elapsed = P.now() - started
print(("elapsed %d ms (%.2f s)"):format(elapsed, P.seconds() - started / 1000))

-- check
DOCS.eq(elapsed, 480, "30 frames of 16 ms")
DOCS.eq(eb.now(), P.now(), "eb.now() is the platform clock")
DOCS.check(P.now() >= started, "the clock never steps back")
examples.expect: Measures the time across 30 frames (480 ms on the offline world) with P.now(), eb.now() and P.seconds().

examples.title: Run a job on a timer
examples.summary: A pulse job runs fn(now) on its interval, inside the frame. Cancel it by name.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local pulse = require("eb.platform").pulse()
local runs = 0
pulse.every("docs.heartbeat", 500, function(now)
    runs = runs + 1                      -- a job is ONE short call per run: read, decide, queue - never wait here
end)

w.runFor(2000)                           -- (offline: 2 seconds of frames)
print(("heartbeat ran %d times"):format(runs))
local before = runs
pulse.cancel("docs.heartbeat")
w.runFor(2000)

-- check
DOCS.eq(before, 4, "every 500 ms over 2 s: four runs")
DOCS.eq(runs, before, "a cancelled job runs no more")
examples.expect: A 500 ms job runs 4 times in 2 seconds of frames, then stops once cancelled.

examples.title: Wait inside a task
examples.summary: Work that waits runs as a pulse task: eb.delay(ms) pauses the task, never the game's frame.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local pulse = P.pulse()
local marks, started = {}, P.now()
pulse.spawn("docs.slow-errand", function(task)
    marks[#marks + 1] = "start"
    eb.delay(500)                        -- yields this task; the frame (and every other job) keeps running
    marks[#marks + 1] = "half"
    eb.delay(500)
    marks[#marks + 1] = "end"
end)

local framesWhileWaiting = 0
pulse.every("docs.count-frames", 0, function() framesWhileWaiting = framesWhileWaiting + 1 end)
w.runUntil(function() return #marks == 3 end, 5000)
print(("task done after %.1f s"):format((P.now() - started) / 1000))

-- check
DOCS.eq(table.concat(marks, ","), "start,half,end", "the steps ran in order")
DOCS.check(P.now() - started >= 1000, "the two waits took their time")
DOCS.check(framesWhileWaiting > 50, "frames kept coming while the task waited")
DOCS.check(not pulse.running("docs.slow-errand"), "the task is finished")
examples.expect: The task waits 1 second in two steps while the frames go on; it records three marks in order.

examples.title: Never wait in a job or a handler
examples.summary: A job, an event handler or a command handler must return at once: waiting there raises. Let a task wait.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local pulse = require("eb.platform").pulse()
local refused, finished = nil, false
pulse.every("docs.impatient", 100, function()
    pulse.cancel("docs.impatient")
    local ok, err = pcall(eb.delay, 200)             -- WRONG: a job cannot wait
    if not ok then refused = tostring(err) end
    -- RIGHT: hand the waiting part to a task
    pulse.spawn("docs.patient", function()
        eb.delay(200)
        finished = true
    end)
end)
w.runFor(1000)
print("refused: " .. tostring(refused):match("eb%.delay called outside an EB task"))

-- check
DOCS.has(refused, "outside an EB task", "the wait in a job was refused with its reason")
DOCS.check(finished, "the task did the waiting")
examples.expect: eb.delay inside a job raises (caught here); the same work handed to a task waits and finishes.

examples.title: Wait for a condition, with a timeout
examples.summary: Inside a task, pulse.waitUntil(pred, timeoutMs) checks pred every frame and gives up after the timeout.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.addActor({ id = 201, name = "a cave bat", distance = 12 })
w.host:run("docs.offline-player", function()      -- offline: someone targets the bat 600 ms from now
    wait(0.6)
    w.self.targetId = 201
end)

-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local pulse, game = P.pulse(), P.game()
local first, second, why = nil, nil, nil
local result = w.task(function()
    first = pulse.waitUntil(function() return game.Me().targetId == 201 end, 3000)
    second, why = pulse.waitUntil(function() return game.Me().isDead end, 500)
    return first and "targeted after a wait" or "no target"
end)
print(("%s; second wait: %s"):format(result, tostring(why)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(first, true, "the target appeared before the timeout")
DOCS.eq(second, false, "the second wait gave up")
DOCS.eq(why, "timeout", "and said why")
examples.expect: The first wait sees the target appear; the second one times out and says so.

examples.title: Clean up when EB stops
examples.summary: pulse.onStop(name, fn) runs your cleanup when EB stops: release what you hold, save what you queued.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local pulse = require("eb.platform").pulse()
local ticks, cleaned = 0, {}
pulse.every("docs.watcher", 250, function() ticks = ticks + 1 end)
pulse.onStop("docs.watcher", function(why)
    pulse.cancel("docs.watcher")
    cleaned[#cleaned + 1] = why
    print("cleanup: " .. tostring(why))
end)
w.runFor(1000)
w.stop()                                   -- (offline: EB stops; in game: eb stop, or the session ends)

-- check
DOCS.eq(#cleaned, 1, "the cleanup ran once")
DOCS.has(cleaned[1], "the example ended", "with the reason EB stopped")
DOCS.check(ticks >= 4, "the job ran while EB was up")
examples.expect: The cleanup runs once, with the reason EB stopped, and the job it cancels never runs again.

examples.title: Write a log line
examples.summary: P.log() writes tagged lines at four levels; a bad format string is printed as it is, never raised.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local log = require("eb.platform").log()
log.info("buffwatch", "%d buffs up, %s missing", 7, "none")
log.warn("buffwatch", "power at %d%%", 12)
log.error("buffwatch", "%d of %d", "seven")      -- a wrong argument: the raw format is written, nothing raises
local n = 0
for _ in w.echoed():gmatch("buffwatch") do n = n + 1 end
print(("%d log lines"):format(n))

-- check
DOCS.check(w.said("[info] buffwatch 7 buffs up, none missing"), "info line formatted")
DOCS.check(w.said("[warn] buffwatch power at 12%"), "warn line formatted")
DOCS.check(w.said("[error] buffwatch %d of %d"), "a bad format prints the raw text")
DOCS.eq(n, 3, "three lines")
examples.expect: Three lines reach the console, the last one carrying its unformatted text.

examples.title: Stay inside the read budget
examples.summary: About 8 game reads a frame: Me, Target and Group come in a few batched reads; asking again is free.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world({ pulse = false })
for i = 1, 5 do
    w.addMember({ name = "Mate" .. i, id = 10 + i, class = "templar", healthPct = 80, inZone = true })
    w.addActor({ id = 10 + i, name = "Mate" .. i, type = "PC", isNPC = false, distance = 6 })
end
w.addActor({ id = 200, name = "a moss crawler", distance = 9 })
w.self.targetId = 200

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
game.BeginTick()                                 -- EB's pulse does this at the start of every frame
local r0 = game.GameDataReads()
local me, target, group = game.Me(), game.Target(), game.Group()
local firstRound = game.GameDataReads() - r0
local again = game.GameDataReads()
game.Me(); game.Target(); game.Group()           -- the same frame: answered from the frame's memo
local secondRound = game.GameDataReads() - again
print(("first round: %d reads, second round: %d reads"):format(firstRound, secondRound))

-- check
DOCS.check(firstRound >= 1 and firstRound <= 8, "the first round fits the budget")
DOCS.eq(secondRound, 0, "the same frame reads nothing twice")
DOCS.eq(#group, 5, "the whole group came from one batch")
DOCS.eq(target.name, "a moss crawler", "and the target from the self batch")
examples.expect: One frame reading Me, Target and Group twice stays at or under 8 reads; the second round costs 0.

examples.title: Test a script with a fake service
examples.summary: P.install(target, service, adapter) hands the platform a stand-in: test a script against a clock you step.
examples.code:
-- your script: a tiny cooldown helper that reads the platform clock
local P = require("eb.platform")
local function cooldown(ms)
    local readyAt = P.now() + ms
    return function() return P.now() >= readyAt end
end

-- the test: pin the target, hand in a fake clock, step it
P.reset()
P.use("isx")
local fake = { t = 1000 }
P.install("isx", "clock", { now = function() return fake.t end, seconds = function() return fake.t / 1000 end,
                            wall = function() return nil end })
local ready = cooldown(2000)
local early = ready()
fake.t = 3000
print(("cooldown ready at %d ms"):format(P.now()))

-- check
DOCS.eq(early, false, "not ready before its time")
DOCS.eq(ready(), true, "ready once the clock reaches it")
P.reset()                                        -- forget the fake: the next script gets the real services
DOCS.check(P.get("clock") ~= nil, "the platform answers again after a reset")
examples.expect: A hand-stepped clock replaces the real one; the script under test sees exactly the times it is given.

examples.title: Drive the clock in a test
examples.summary: clock.use hands EB's clock a source you step; the clock never runs backwards - when its source steps back it holds - and seconds() is the same clock.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script: a clock you step by hand
local P = require("eb.platform")
local clock = P.clock()
local t = 1000
clock.use(function() return t end)
local a = clock.now()
t = 500                                     -- the source jumps back (a clock was set)
local b = clock.now()                       -- EB's clock holds
t = 2500
local c = clock.now()                       -- and moves on from where it held
print(("now %d -> %d (source stepped back) -> %d"):format(a, b, c))

-- check
DOCS.eq(b, a, "never backwards")
DOCS.eq(c, 3000, "it carries on by the source's own steps")
DOCS.eq(P.now(), c, "P.now() is the same clock")
DOCS.eq(clock.seconds(), 3, "seconds() is now() / 1000")
local stamp = clock.wall()
DOCS.check(stamp == nil or type(stamp) == "number", "wall() is a number of seconds, or nil")
examples.expect: 1000, then 1000 again when the source steps back, then 3000; P.now() reads the same clock.

examples.title: Drive EB's frames yourself
examples.summary: With no frame loop running, pulse.frame(now) runs one frame at a time: jobs on their interval, a task's wait, the stop flag and the cleanups - the way to test a helper offline, exactly.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: a world with NO frame loop of its own (pulse = false), so this script drives every frame
local w = DOCS.world({ pulse = false })

-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local pulse = P.pulse()
local said = {}
pulse.setLog(function(line) said[#said + 1] = line end)     -- the pulse's own messages, captured
pulse.bindEb(eb)                                             -- eb.delay waits on this pulse

local runs, doneAt, cleaned = 0, nil, nil
pulse.every("count", 100, function(now) runs = runs + 1 end)
pulse.spawn("wait-a-bit", function()
    eb.delay(250)                                            -- a wait is fine inside a task
    doneAt = P.now()
end)
pulse.onStop("my.helper", function(why) cleaned = why end)

local t = 0
P.clock().use(function() return t end)
for i = 1, 10 do t = i * 50; pulse.frame(t) end
pulse.stop("test over")
local stopping, why = pulse.stopping()
pulse.cleanup()
print(("job ran %d times, task done at %d ms, stopping: %s (%s)"):format(runs, doneAt, tostring(stopping), why))

-- check
DOCS.eq(runs, 5, "a 100 ms job over 500 ms of frames")
DOCS.eq(doneAt, 300, "the task woke on the first frame after its wait")
DOCS.eq(cleaned, "test over", "cleanup ran the onStop handler with the reason")
DOCS.eq(pulse.otherRunning(t), false, "after cleanup no EB counts as running here")
DOCS.eq(#said, 0, "no job raised and no task ran slow")
examples.expect: Over 10 frames of 50 ms the 100 ms job runs 5 times and the task wakes after its 250 ms wait; stop then cleanup runs the onStop handler.

examples.title: Read the settings catalog
examples.summary: The settings window's catalog as data: a setting's label and range, its default, what one + press gives, how it prints, and what "Apply to All" shows when the characters differ.

-- your script
local S = require("eb.ui.settings.settings")
local it = S.item("followDistance")
local def = S.defaultOf(it)
local nextOne = S.step(it, 6, 1)
local values = { Tankard = { followDistance = 6 }, Mendwell = { followDistance = 8 } }
local chars = { "Tankard", "Mendwell" }
local all = S.valueFor(values, "All", "followDistance", chars)
local preset = S.preset("instance")
print(("%s = %s; 6 -> %d; All reads %s; instance preset %d"):format(it.label, S.format(it, def), nextOne,
    S.format(it, all), preset.settings.followDistance))

-- check
DOCS.eq(it.unit, "m", "a distance in metres")
DOCS.eq(S.snap(it, 6.4), 6, "snap keeps a number on its step (and whole)")
DOCS.eq(S.snap(it, 99), 40, "and inside its range")
DOCS.eq(all, S.MIXED, "the two characters differ")
DOCS.eq(S.baseValue(values, "All", "followDistance", chars), 6, "a press starts from the first character's value")
DOCS.eq(#S.targets(it, "Tankard", chars), 1, "Apply to one character reaches only that one")
DOCS.eq(S.step(S.item("autoLoot"), true, 1), false, "a switch flips")
DOCS.eq(S.defaults().autoLoot, false, "a switch defaults to off")

examples.title: Test a helper's saves without a disk
examples.summary: ebkit.files.memory is a files host over a table: give it to a helper's save function in a test and read back exactly what it wrote - including a failed write.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script: a helper's save, written against any files host
local function save(fs, state)
    return fs.write("notes/helper.json", ('{"kills":%d}'):format(state.kills))
end

local F = require("ebkit.files")
local disk = {}
local mem = F.memory(disk)                 -- in game: require("eb.platform").files()
save(mem, { kills = 3 })
local names = mem.list("notes", "*.json")
mem.copy("notes/helper.json", "notes/helper.json.old")
mem.failNext = "disk full"
local ok, why = save(mem, { kills = 4 })
print(("saved %d file: notes/%s; backup made; a failed save says: %s"):format(#names, names[1], why))

-- check
DOCS.eq(disk["notes/helper.json"], '{"kills":3}', "the first save is on the table")
DOCS.check(mem.exists("notes/helper.json.old"), "copy made the backup")
DOCS.eq(ok, false, "the forced failure is reported")
DOCS.eq(mem.writes, 1, "only the good save counted")
local fs = require("eb.platform").files()
DOCS.check(fs.isDir("notes") ~= true, "the real host has no such folder offline")
DOCS.eq(type(fs.probeNative()), "boolean", "probeNative answers true or false")

examples.title: A tour of the platform services
examples.summary: The target and the install folder, the eb global, the crew transport's box id, the frame loop's own status line, folders and queued saves, and the window bridge's helpers - each in one line.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real), its files on a table
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { name = "Fixturae" } })
local disk = require("data.lib.memdisk").install()

-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local target = P.detect()                                   -- what the environment looks like
local folder = P.root()                                     -- "." offline; the EB folder in game
local g = P.installGlobal()                                 -- fills only what is missing (EB's start made it)
local box = P.relay().session()                             -- this box's id on the crew relay
local fs = P.files()
local made = fs.mkdirs("eb-docs-notes")                    -- a folder for a helper's files
local who = P.ui().me()                                     -- nil until EB's start names the character
fs.writeLater("eb-docs-example.txt", "one queued save")    -- no disk work now
local written = fs.flushAll()                               -- a cleanup or a task writes the queue
local landed = disk["eb-docs-example.txt"]
local status = P.pulse().status()                           -- the frame loop in one line
local empty = P.ui().emptyList()
print(("%s | box %s | %d save written | %s"):format(target, box, written, status:match("^frames") or status))

-- check
DOCS.eq(target, "isx", "EB for InnerSpace")
DOCS.eq(type(folder), "string", "root is a folder name")
DOCS.eq(g.now, eb.now, "the eb global is the one installGlobal returns")
DOCS.eq(box, "is1", "the session name is the box id")
DOCS.eq(written, 1, "flushAll wrote the queued save")
DOCS.eq(landed, "one queued save", "the whole text, once")
DOCS.check(made ~= nil, "mkdirs answers")
DOCS.check(who == nil or type(who) == "string", "ui.me is a name or nil")
DOCS.eq(fs.pending(), 0, "nothing left in the queue")
DOCS.eq(next(empty), nil, "an empty list for a window state")
DOCS.eq(require("eb.platform.isx.services.files_isx").parent("notes/helper.json"), "notes", "the folder part of a path")
examples.expect: The target is isx, eb.now is the platform clock, the transport names this box, a queued save is written by flushAll, and the window bridge gives an empty list that is sent as [].

examples.title: Ask about many abilities for the price of one read
examples.summary: Every ability you asked about recently is read in ONE batch at the first ask of a frame; the rest of the frame answers from that batch. ReadyStats() shows it.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.addAbility({ id = 5001, name = "Fixture Strike", ready = true })
w.addAbility({ id = 5002, name = "Fixture Ward", ready = false, secondsUntilReady = 9 })
w.addAbility({ id = 5003, name = "Fixture Mend", ready = true })
local names = { "Fixture Strike", "Fixture Ward", "Fixture Mend" }

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
for _, n in ipairs(names) do game.AbilityReady(n) end      -- the first frame learns which names you use
game.BeginTick()                                             -- the next frame (EB's pulse does this every frame)
local before = game.GameDataReads()
local ready = {}
for _, n in ipairs(names) do ready[n] = game.AbilityReady(n) end
local reads = game.GameDataReads() - before
print(("%d asks, %d read"):format(#names, reads))

-- check
DOCS.eq(reads, 1, "one batched read for the whole set")
DOCS.eq(ready["Fixture Ward"], false, "the one on its timer")
local r, shared = game.ReadyStats()
DOCS.eq(r .. "/" .. shared, "1/2", "one read, two answers shared from it")
examples.expect: Three readiness asks in a warm frame cost one game read; ReadyStats reports one read and two shared answers.

examples.title: Read what you and your target are casting, and cancel

DOCS.eq(id, 4242, "the target's cast id")
DOCS.eq(w.world.commands[#w.world.commands], "/cancel_spellcast", "the cancel went out")
DOCS.eq(game.CastingName(), "", "after the cancel your cast bar is empty")

examples.title: Check a buff without flooding the server
examples.summary: An effect's name lives in its effect info, which the game asks the SERVER for. HasEffect(name) resolves each effect's name once and keeps it, so asking every frame costs no more server requests.

examples.title: Hold a helper while a zone loads
examples.summary: Zoning() is true while a zone loads (and at character select); InGame() is false then. A helper that acts in the world checks them first and waits.

w.world.zoning, w.world.inGame = true, false

examples.title: Call out in group chat and send a tell
examples.summary: Say("group" | "raid", text) speaks in group or raid chat once EB has proven that call in the game - until then it sends nothing and answers false with the reason; Tell(name, text) whispers one player. Text is sent as plain words, never evaluated.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.addMember({ name = "Mendfixture", id = 12, class = "templar", healthPct = 30, powerPct = 70, inZone = true })

-- your script

local groupHeld
for _, m in ipairs(game.Group()) do
    if m.healthPct < 40 then
        -- group and raid chat are held back until EB has proven them in the game: Say answers false, and why
        local sent, why = game.Say("group", m.name .. " is low!")
        if not sent then groupHeld = why end
        game.Tell(m.name, "drink a potion, ${not code}")       -- a "${" in text is defused, never run
    end
end
print(("sent %d chat line; group chat: %s"):format(#w.world.chatOut, groupHeld and "held back" or "sent"))

-- check
DOCS.check(groupHeld ~= nil, "Say answered false: group chat is held back for now")
DOCS.has(groupHeld, "proven", "and said why")
DOCS.eq(#w.world.chatOut, 1, "so only the tell went out")
DOCS.eq(w.world.chatOut[1].to, "Mendfixture", "a tell to the member")
DOCS.eq(w.world.chatOut[1].text, "drink a potion, $ {not code}", "the words as written, the ${ defused")

examples.title: Record chat lines from the game's own chat event
examples.summary: OnChat(fn) gives your function every chat line the moment the game raises it. That runs inside the game's event, so the function only records; the frame code acts on what it recorded.

-- your script (eb.events' ChatLine is the easier choice: its handlers run in EB's frame, where they may act)

w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 8, speaker = "Someonefixture", message = "hello" })

for _, ev in ipairs(inbox) do if ev.speaker == "Questfixture" then n = n + 1 end end
print(("%d line from Questfixture"):format(n))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#inbox, 2, "both lines recorded")
DOCS.eq(inbox[1].message, "Bring me three fixture pelts.", "the text")
DOCS.eq(n, 1, "one from the speaker we care about")
