    isStunned = true })
w.addMember({ name = "Mendfixture", id = 12, class = "templar", healthPct = 90, powerPct = 70, inZone = true })
w.addActor({ id = 11, name = "Tankfixture", type = "PC", isNPC = false, distance = 4, isStunned = true })
w.addActor({ id = 12, name = "Mendfixture", type = "PC", isNPC = false, distance = 6 })

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
for _, m in ipairs(game.Group()) do
    local n = game.ControlCount(m.id)
    if n > 0 then print(("cure %s: %d control effect"):format(m.name, n)) end
end

-- check
DOCS.eq(game.ControlCount(11), 1, "the tank is stunned")
DOCS.eq(game.ControlCount(12), 0, "the healer is free")
DOCS.eq(game.ControlCount(0), 0, "an id of 0 is no one")
examples.expect: Finds the stunned member and reads zero for the free one.

examples.title: Where an actor stands, and whether it is gone
examples.summary: ActorPos(id) answers an actor's position, heading and distance; ActorDead(id) is true when it is dead or no longer in the zone; ActorHeading(id) is its facing in degrees, or nil when it is gone.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.addActor({ id = 220, name = "a fixture boar", x = 12, y = 0, z = -8.5, heading = 90, distance = 14 })

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local p = game.ActorPos(220)
if p then print(("%s at %.1f, %.1f, %.1f facing %d"):format(p.name, p.x, p.y, p.z, game.ActorHeading(220))) end
local aliveBefore = not game.ActorDead(220)
w.world.actors[220] = nil                           -- the boar despawns
game.BeginTick()                                    -- a new frame (EB's pulse does this every frame)

-- check
DOCS.eq(aliveBefore, true, "alive before")
DOCS.eq(game.ActorDead(220), true, "gone from the zone counts as dead")
DOCS.eq(game.ActorPos(220), nil, "and has no position")
DOCS.eq(game.ActorHeading(220), nil, "nor a heading")
examples.expect: Reads the mob's position, then calls it dead once it has despawned.

examples.title: Repair at a mender and close the window
examples.summary: Double-click the mender with ClickActor(id), then RepairAll() repairs everything; CloseMerchantWindow() closes the window it opened.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)

    game.CloseMerchantWindow()

end

-- check
DOCS.eq(mender.id, 300, "the mender was found")
DOCS.eq(w.world.commands[#w.world.commands], "/mender_repair_all", "repair all went out")
DOCS.eq(w.world.windows.merchant, nil, "the window is closed")
examples.expect: The mender is clicked, the repair goes out, and the merchant window is closed.

examples.title: Hail an NPC
examples.summary: Target the NPC with TargetActor(id), then send the game's own hail with Execute("eq2execute hail"). Execute sends one console line as written: use it only for commands EB knows to work.
examples.code:

w.addActor({ id = 310, name = "Questfixture", type = "NPC", distance = 5 })

-- your script

    game.Execute("eq2execute hail")

DOCS.eq(w.self.targetId, 310, "targeted first")
DOCS.eq(w.world.commands[#w.world.commands], "/hail", "then hailed")
examples.expect: The quest giver is targeted and the hail goes out to the game.

examples.title: Wait for something without freezing the game
examples.summary: Wait(seconds, cond) waits inside an EB task until cond() is true or the time runs out; the game keeps running every frame meanwhile. WaitCasting(seconds) waits for your cast bar.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local frames = 0
w.world.onFrame = function(host)
    frames = frames + 1
    if frames == 2 then host.world.self.isCasting = true end          -- a cast starts two frames from now
end

-- your script: every wait lives inside a task (in game: require("eb.platform").pulse().spawn(name, fn))
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local started = w.task(function()
    return game.WaitCasting(1.0)                   -- true as soon as the cast bar shows, false after 1 s
end)
print(("casting seen after %d frames"):format(frames))

-- check
DOCS.eq(started, true, "the cast was seen")
DOCS.check(frames >= 2 and frames < 10, "it waited a couple of frames, not the whole second")
examples.expect: The task waits until the cast starts (the frame after the world begins it), then reports it.

examples.title: Read several Me members in ONE read
examples.summary: A data sequence with several ${} in it is ONE game read, however many members it names. Batch the members you need into one IS.Parse instead of one read each.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { healthPct = 64, powerPct = 80 } })

-- your script (EB for InnerSpace: IS is ISXLUA's bridge; the game layer's Me() already batches these for you)
local before = w.host.stats.parse
local raw = IS.Parse("${Me.Health}|${Me.Power}|${Me.Level}|${Me.SubClass}")
local hp, power, level, sub = raw:match("^([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)$")
hp, power, level = tonumber(hp), tonumber(power), tonumber(level)      -- every answer is text
print(("hp %d power %d level %d %s in %d read"):format(hp, power, level, sub, w.host.stats.parse - before))

-- check
DOCS.eq(w.host.stats.parse - before, 1, "four members, one read")
DOCS.eq(hp, 64, "Health is a percent")
DOCS.eq(sub, "warden", "SubClass")
DOCS.eq(level, require("eb.platform").game().Me().level, "the same answer the game layer gives")
examples.expect: One read answers four members; the values arrive as text and are converted with tonumber.

examples.title: Read one member the game layer does not return
examples.summary: game.GetVar(expr, default) reads any member EB has verified, typed (a number comes back as a number), and counted in the per-frame read budget.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.world.bagsFree = 12
w.self.isGroupLeader = true

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local free = game.GetVar("Me.InventorySlotsFree", 0)            -- the default answers when it cannot be read
local leader = game.GetVar("Me.IsGroupLeader", false)
print(("%d bag slots free, group leader: %s"):format(free, tostring(leader)))
if free <= 3 then print("bags nearly full") end

-- check
DOCS.eq(free, 12, "a number, not text")
DOCS.eq(leader, true, "a boolean")
examples.expect: Reads the free bag slots as a number and the group-leader flag as a boolean.

examples.title: What GetVar does with a member that is not verified yet
examples.summary: EB only sends members verified to work. GetVar on a member that is not verified yet sends nothing and answers your default; GateSkipped() lists what was held back.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local before = w.host.stats.getvar
local arch = game.GetVar("Me.Archetype", "unknown")              -- not verified yet: held back
print(("archetype: %s (held back, %d reads)"):format(arch, w.host.stats.getvar - before))
local held = table.concat(game.GateSkipped(), ", ")

-- check
DOCS.eq(arch, "unknown", "your default, never a guess")
DOCS.eq(w.host.stats.getvar - before, 0, "nothing reached the game")
DOCS.has(held, "Me.Archetype", "GateSkipped lists it")
DOCS.eq(game.Me().subclass, "warden", "the game layer's own reads still answer")
examples.expect: The not-yet-verified member answers the default, nothing is sent to the game, and GateSkipped names it.

examples.title: Target members, and what NULL looks like
examples.summary: ${Target.Name} and friends read your target. With no target the whole chain reads NULL - no error - which the game layer turns into nil.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.addActor({ id = 220, name = "a fixture boar", healthPct = 77, distance = 5 })
w.self.targetId = 220

-- your script
local raw = IS.Parse("${Target.Name}|${Target.Health}|${Target.Distance}|${Target.Type}")
local name, hp, dist, kind = raw:match("^([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)$")
print(("%s %s%% %s %s"):format(name, hp, dist, kind))
w.self.targetId = 0                                -- no target
local none = IS.Parse("${Target.ID}")

-- check
DOCS.eq(name, "a fixture boar", "the name")
DOCS.eq(tonumber(dist), 5, "a distance is text with decimals")
DOCS.eq(none, "NULL", "no target reads NULL, not an error")
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
game.BeginTick()
DOCS.eq(game.Target(), nil, "the game layer answers nil for NULL")
examples.expect: Reads the target's members in one read; with no target the same read answers NULL and Target() is nil.

examples.title: Read an actor by its id
examples.summary: Actor[id,N] is the fast, exact way to read one actor; the game layer reads it through ActorPos / ActorDead / ActorTarget, once per frame however often you ask.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.addActor({ id = 220, name = "a fixture boar", level = 98, distance = 7.5, targetId = 1 })

-- your script
local raw = IS.Parse("${Actor[id,220].Name}|${Actor[id,220].Level}|${Actor[id,220].Distance}|${Actor[id,220].Target.ID}")
local name, lvl, dist, tid = raw:match("^([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)$")
print(("%s lvl %s, %s m, targeting id %s"):format(name, lvl, dist, tid))
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
game.BeginTick()
local p = game.ActorPos(220)
local reads = game.GameDataReads()
game.ActorPos(220); game.ActorDead(220)            -- the same frame: answered from the first read

-- check
DOCS.eq(p.name, name, "the game layer reads the same actor")
DOCS.eq(game.GameDataReads(), reads, "no extra read in the same frame")
DOCS.eq(tonumber(tid), 1, "its target is me")
examples.expect: Reads the mob by id directly and through the game layer; both agree, and asking again in the same frame reads nothing more.

examples.title: Search actors with a query
examples.summary: ActorsNear(query, radius) runs one game actor query; its terms are actor members (Type, Level, Health, InCombatMode ...), and EB refuses a query that names a member it has not verified.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.addActor({ id = 320, name = "a fixture elder", level = 99, distance = 12 })
w.addActor({ id = 321, name = "a fixture whelp", level = 20, distance = 8 })
w.addActor({ id = 322, name = "a fixture elder", level = 97, distance = 25 })

-- your script: query terms are combined with && || ! and compared with == != < > <= >=
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local big = game.ActorsNear('Type == "NPC" && Level >= 95 && Health > 0', 30)
print(("%d NPCs of level 95+ within 30 m"):format(#big))
local refused = game.ActorsNear('Type == "NPC" && IsNamed', 30)   -- IsNamed is not verified yet: refused

-- check
DOCS.eq(#big, 2, "the two elders")
DOCS.eq(big[1].id, 320, "nearest first")
DOCS.eq(#refused, 0, "a query with a member that is not verified yet sends nothing")
examples.expect: Lists the two high-level NPCs; a query naming a member that is not verified yet answers an empty list.

examples.title: Read a group slot: Me.Group[n]
examples.summary: Me.Group[0] is you and 1 to 5 are the others. A member in another zone reads ID 0 and has no distance, so check InZone before acting on one.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.addMember({ name = "Tankfixture", id = 11, class = "guardian", healthPct = 72, powerPct = 60, inZone = true })
w.addMember({ name = "Farfixture", id = 13, class = "wizard", healthPct = 100, powerPct = 90, inZone = false })
w.addActor({ id = 11, name = "Tankfixture", type = "PC", isNPC = false, distance = 6 })

-- your script (the game layer's Group() reads all five slots like this, in one batch)
local raw = IS.Parse("${Me.GroupCount}|${Me.Group[1].Name}|${Me.Group[1].InZone}|${Me.Group[1].HitPoints}|" ..
    "${Me.Group[1].MaxHitPoints}|${Me.Group[2].Name}|${Me.Group[2].InZone}|${Me.Group[2].ID}")
local f = {}
for v in (raw .. "|"):gmatch("([^|]*)|") do f[#f + 1] = v end
print(("%s in zone %s/%s; %s %s"):format(f[2], f[4], f[5], f[6], f[7] == "TRUE" and "here" or "away"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(tonumber(f[1]), 3, "GroupCount counts you too")
DOCS.eq(f[3], "TRUE", "the tank is in the zone")
DOCS.eq(f[8], "0", "a member in another zone reads ID 0")
examples.expect: Reads both slots in one read and tells the member in the zone from the one away.

examples.title: Read the raid outside your group
examples.summary: game.Raid(myGroup, refreshSec) reads Me.Raid[n] for the raid members who are not in your own group, at most once every refreshSec (default half a second).
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.world.raid = {
    { name = "Tankfixture", id = 11, class = "guardian", healthPct = 80, inZone = true, raidGroupNum = 1 },
    { name = "Raidfixture", id = 21, class = "templar", healthPct = 95, inZone = true, raidGroupNum = 2 },
    { name = "Raiderfixture", id = 22, class = "ranger", healthPct = 40, inZone = true, raidGroupNum = 2 },
}
for _, m in ipairs(w.world.raid) do w.addActor({ id = m.id, name = m.name, type = "PC", isNPC = false, distance = 10 }) end

-- your script: pass your own group's names (lower case) so the raid list holds only the others
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local rows = game.Raid({ tankfixture = true }, 0)
local parts = {}
for _, r in ipairs(rows) do parts[#parts + 1] = ("%s (%d%%)"):format(r.name, r.healthPct) end
print("raid: " .. table.concat(parts, ", "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#rows, 2, "your own group is left out")
DOCS.eq(rows[2].healthPct, 40, "health in percent")
DOCS.eq(game.GetVar("Me.RaidCount", 0), 3, "Me.RaidCount counts the whole raid")
examples.expect: Lists the two raid members outside your group and leaves your own group member out.

examples.title: Zone.Name changes at the START of a zone load
examples.summary: ${Zone.Name} names the NEW zone as soon as the load begins, while the zone is not playable yet. Wait for EQ2.Zoning to read 0 (game.Zoning() false) before you act on the new zone.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.self.zone = "a test hall"
w.world.zoning, w.world.zoneName = true, "a fixture vale"          -- the load has just started

-- your script
local raw = IS.Parse("${Zone.Name}|${EQ2.Zoning}")
local zone, zoning = raw:match("^([^|]*)|([^|]*)$")
if tonumber(zoning) ~= 0 then print(("loading %s (Zoning %s): wait"):format(zone, zoning)) end
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local actedEarly = not game.Zoning()
w.world.zoning = false                                              -- the load ends
game.BeginTick()

-- check
DOCS.eq(zone, "a fixture vale", "the name is already the new zone")
DOCS.eq(actedEarly, false, "game.Zoning() held the helper during the load")
DOCS.eq(game.Zoning(), false, "and lets it go once the load is over")
DOCS.eq(IS.Parse("${Zone.ShortName}"), "afixturevale", "ShortName is the zone's short key")
examples.expect: During the load the zone name is already new but Zoning is not 0; the helper acts only after the load ends.

examples.title: Read the cast bars through GetGameData
examples.summary: Me.GetGameData[key].Label reads a value the game's own interface shows. Spells.Casting is your cast bar; ImpliedTarget.Casting is the spell your (implied) target is casting.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.self.castingName = "Fixture Mend"
w.addActor({ id = 290, name = "a fixture shaman", distance = 14, castId = 4242, castName = "Fixture Blast" })
w.self.targetId = 290

local mine, theirs = raw:match("^([^|]*)|([^|]*)$")
print(("me: %s / target: %s"):format(mine, theirs))

-- check
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
DOCS.eq(game.CastingName(), mine, "the game layer's own cast bar read")
DOCS.eq((game.TargetCasting()), theirs, "and the target's")
examples.expect: Both labels read in one batch; the game layer's CastingName() and TargetCasting() answer the same.

examples.title: Check that the game extension is ready
examples.summary: ${ISXEQ2.IsReady} is TRUE once ISXEQ2 can answer game reads; Extension[ISXEQ2](exists) only says it is loaded. game.IsExtensionReady() checks both, and is the first thing a stand-alone script should wait for.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.world.isxeq2Ready = false

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local early = game.IsExtensionReady()
w.world.isxeq2Ready = true                         -- a moment later
game.BeginTick()
if game.IsExtensionReady() then
    print("ISXEQ2 ready, in the world: " .. IS.Parse("${Me.InGameWorld}"))
end

-- check
DOCS.eq(early, false, "not ready while it starts")
DOCS.eq(game.IsExtensionReady(), true, "ready")
DOCS.eq(IS.Parse("${Extension[ISXEQ2](exists)}"), "TRUE", "the extension is loaded")

examples.title: TRUE or NULL, and numbers as text
examples.summary: X(exists) answers TRUE or NULL - never FALSE - so test for "TRUE". Every answer is text: numbers come back as "100" or "7.500000", booleans as TRUE / FALSE.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local none = IS.Parse("${ChoiceWindow(exists)}")
w.setWindow("choice", { text = "Join the fixture group?", choice1 = "Accept", choice2 = "Decline" })
local up = IS.Parse("${ChoiceWindow(exists)}")
local level, dead = IS.Parse("${Me.Level}"), IS.Parse("${Me.IsDead}")
print(('no popup: %s; popup: %s; level "%s"; dead "%s"'):format(none, up, level, dead))
local isUp = (up == "TRUE")                         -- the only safe test: anything else means "not there"

-- check
DOCS.eq(none, "NULL", "absent reads NULL, never FALSE")
DOCS.eq(isUp, true, "present reads TRUE")
DOCS.eq(type(level), "string", "numbers are text")
DOCS.eq(tonumber(level), 100, "convert with tonumber")
DOCS.eq(dead, "FALSE", "booleans are TRUE / FALSE text")

examples.title: Effect names are server requests - never poll them
examples.summary: Me.Effect[n].ToEffectInfo.Name asks the SERVER whenever it is read. Reading it for every effect every frame floods the server; read the plain fields (ID, Type) per frame and look a name up once per new effect id.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.world.effects = {
    { id = 9001, name = "Fixture Ward", type = "Beneficial", icon = 11 },
    { id = 9002, name = "Fixture Haste", type = "Beneficial", icon = 12 },
}

-- the WRONG way, shown once: 10 frames x 2 effects of name reads
w.world.stats.examine = 0
for _ = 1, 10 do IS.Parse("${Me.Effect[1].ToEffectInfo.Name}|${Me.Effect[2].ToEffectInfo.Name}") end
local polled = w.world.stats.examine

-- the right way: per frame only the plain id; a name is asked once per id never seen before
w.world.stats.examine = 0
local names = {}
for _ = 1, 10 do
    local n = tonumber(IS.Parse("${Me.CountEffects}")) or 0
    for i = 1, n do
        local id = IS.Parse("${Me.Effect[" .. i .. "].ID}")
        if names[id] == nil then names[id] = IS.Parse("${Me.Effect[" .. i .. "].ToEffectInfo.Name}") end
    end
end
print(("polling names: %d server requests; cached by id: %d"):format(polled, w.world.stats.examine))

-- check (in a real script use game.HasEffect / game.MyEffectNames: they already work this way, in one read a frame)
DOCS.eq(polled, 20, "a request per effect per frame")
DOCS.eq(w.world.stats.examine, 2, "one per effect, once")
DOCS.eq(names["9001"], "Fixture Ward", "the cache maps id to name")
examples.expect: Polling names directly costs a server request per effect per frame; the cached way costs one per effect, once.

examples.title: Read the items in an open loot window
examples.summary: LootWindow.NumItems and LootWindow.Item[n].Name read an OPEN loot window. Read them only after the game's loot event (or game.LootWindow()) says one is up: asking with none open is slow.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
game.LootWindow()                                  -- (EB's own watch is listening for the loot event)
w.setWindow("loot", { type = "Lotto", items = { { name = "a fixture pelt" }, { name = "a fixture fang" } } })
w.host:fire("EQ2_onLootWindowAppeared", "1001")

-- your script
game.BeginTick()
local lw = game.LootWindow()                       -- nil while no loot window is up: no read is made
local names = {}
if lw and lw.items and lw.items > 0 then
    local seqParts = {}
    for i = 1, lw.items do seqParts[i] = "${LootWindow.Item[" .. i .. "].Name}" end
    for v in (IS.Parse(table.concat(seqParts, "|")) .. "|"):gmatch("([^|]*)|") do names[#names + 1] = v end
end
print(("%s: %s"):format(lw.type, table.concat(names, ", ")))

-- check
DOCS.eq(lw.type, "Lotto", "the window type")
DOCS.eq(#names, 2, "both names in one read")
examples.expect: Waits for game.LootWindow() to report the window, then reads both item names in one read.

examples.title: What a merchant pays for a bag item
examples.summary: With a merchant window open, MerchantWindow.MyInventory["name"].PriceString is what it pays for one of your items, and .Quantity how many you hold.

w.world.items = { ["Fixture Ore"] = { where = "bag", quantity = 5, id = 71, priceString = "0p,1g,20s,0c" } }

    '${MerchantWindow.MyInventory["Fixture Ore"].PriceString}')
local visible, qty, price = raw:match("^([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)$")
if visible == "TRUE" then print(("Fixture Ore x%s: %s each"):format(qty, price)) end
w.setWindow("merchant", nil)                       -- the window closes

-- check

DOCS.eq(tonumber(qty), 5, "how many you hold")
DOCS.eq(IS.Parse("${MerchantWindow.IsVisible}"), "FALSE", "closed")
examples.expect: Reads the offer for the ore while the window is open; with the window closed it reads FALSE for IsVisible.

examples.title: Read an interface element by its full name
examples.summary: EQ2UIPage[window,page].Child[type,full.element.name].GetProperty[prop] reads one element of the game's interface by NAME. Always name the element; never walk a window's children by number.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.setWindow("ho", { visible = true, name = "Fixture Wrath", wheel = { { slot = 1, icon = 4, open = true } } })

-- your script
local v = IS.Parse("${EQ2UIPage[_HUD,heroic].Child[page,_HUD.heroic].GetProperty[visible]}")
print("heroic window visible: " .. tostring(v))

-- check
DOCS.eq(v, "TRUE", "read by its full name")
DOCS.eq(require("eb.platform").game().HOState().visible, true, "the game layer reads it the same way")
examples.expect: Reads the heroic window's visible flag by the element's full name; the game layer's HOState() agrees.

examples.title: Check EB's nav extension before you route
examples.summary: EB's mesh router answers through its own EBNav TLO. Scripts never read EBNav directly: eb.navd checks that the extension is loaded first (an unknown TLO prints an error in game) and says plainly why it cannot route.

-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()                              -- the offline world has no nav extension loaded

-- your script
local navd = require("eb.navd")
local ok, why = navd.lib()

-- check

examples.title: The classic conversation window

examples.title: InnerSpace's own reads: session, extensions, the window, the folder
examples.summary: ${Session} names this InnerSpace session, Extension[name](exists) says whether an extension is loaded, Display.Foreground whether this window has the focus, and LavishScript.HomeDirectory where InnerSpace runs from - build paths from it, never hard-code one.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local raw = IS.Parse("${Extension[ISXEQ2](exists)}|${Extension[ISXNoSuchThing](exists)}|${Display.Foreground}")
local loaded, missing, front = raw:match("^([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)$")
print(("session %s, ISXEQ2 %s, missing %s, front %s"):format(game.SessionName(), loaded, missing, front))
local home = IS.Parse("${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}")
local myFile = home and (home .. "/Scripts/my_helper_notes.txt")     -- a path built from it, not typed in

-- check

DOCS.eq(missing, "NULL", "an extension that is not loaded reads NULL, never FALSE")
DOCS.check(type(home) == "string" and #home > 0, "the folder is known")
DOCS.check(myFile:sub(1, #home) == home, "and paths are built from it")

examples.title: React to a chat line
examples.summary: Subscribe to ChatLine, let the game deliver a tell, and handle it on EB's next frame.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local events = w.events()        -- in game EB's boot has already attached the game's events and ticks them

-- your script
local heard = {}
events.on("ChatLine", function(ev)
    -- runs from EB's frame pulse, never inside the game's own event callback: reading the game here is fine
    heard[#heard + 1] = ev
    print(("heard %s: %s"):format(ev.speaker, ev.message))
end)

-- the game delivers a tell (offline: the fake host fires ISXEQ2's chat event)
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 28, speaker = "Friendo", message = "are you ready?" })
w.frame(2)

-- check
DOCS.eq(#heard, 1, "one line delivered")
DOCS.eq(heard[1].speaker, "Friendo", "the speaker")
DOCS.eq(heard[1].category, 28, "the chat category number")
examples.expect: The handler sees the tell's speaker and text once, after the frame that delivered it.

examples.title: React to a zone change
examples.summary: Subscribe to ZoningStarted and ZoningFinished, and read the new zone only after the load has finished.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { zone = "a test hall" } })
local events = w.events()

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local log = {}
events.on("ZoningStarted", function()
    log[#log + 1] = "started"           -- the zone's name may already read the NEW zone here: never trust it yet
end)
events.on("ZoningFinished", function(ev)
    local zone = game.Me().zone         -- read after the end of the load: the new zone
    log[#log + 1] = "finished"
    print(("now in %s (the load took %s s)"):format(zone, tostring(ev.seconds)))
end)

-- the game loads a zone (offline: the fake host fires the game's own zoning events)
w.host:fire("EQ2_StartedZoning")
w.world.self.zone = "a fixture vault"
w.frame(2)
w.host:fire("EQ2_FinishedZoning", "3.5")
w.frame(2)

-- check
DOCS.eq(log[1], "started", "the start of the load")
DOCS.eq(log[2], "finished", "then its end")
DOCS.eq(game.Me().zone, "a fixture vault", "the zone read after the end")
examples.expect: The handlers see the start and the end of the load, and the zone read after the end is the new zone.

examples.title: A one-time handler, and unsubscribing
examples.summary: Use { once = true } for a handler that should run only for the next event, and off() to stop one.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local events = w.events()

-- your script
local first, every = {}, {}
events.on("IncomingText", function(ev) first[#first + 1] = ev.text end, { once = true })
local id = events.on("IncomingText", function(ev) every[#every + 1] = ev.text end)

w.host:emitText("You have been hit by a fixture brute.")
w.frame(2)
w.host:emitText("You feel refreshed.")
w.frame(2)
events.off("IncomingText", id)          -- stop listening
w.host:emitText("You feel tired.")
w.frame(2)

-- check
DOCS.eq(#first, 1, "the once-handler ran one time")
DOCS.eq(first[1], "You have been hit by a fixture brute.", "for the first line")
DOCS.eq(#every, 2, "the other handler heard two lines before off()")
examples.expect: The once-handler runs for the first line only; after off() the other handler hears nothing more.

examples.title: Turn an event into one command for the crew
examples.summary: Events never travel to the other boxes by themselves: a handler that wants the crew to act sends ONE deliberate eb line with events.crew().
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local events = w.events()
local sent = {}
-- in game EB sets the sender to its crew relay at start; offline we record what would be sent
events.setRelay(function(targets, line) sent[#sent + 1] = targets .. " " .. line end)

-- your script
events.on("Announcement", function(ev)
    if ev.text:find("Overseer of Fixtures", 1, true) then
        events.crew("all", "eb pause")       -- one line, on purpose; every box runs it once
    end
end)

w.host:fire("EQ2_onAnnouncement", "The Overseer of Fixtures stirs!", "alert", "5")
w.frame(2)
w.host:fire("EQ2_onAnnouncement", "A fixture brute wanders off.", "", "0")
w.frame(2)

-- check
DOCS.eq(#sent, 1, "one crew line")
DOCS.eq(sent[1], "all eb pause", "to every box")
examples.expect: The announcement of a named makes the handler send exactly one "eb pause" line to every box.

examples.title: A handler that fails never stops the others
examples.summary: Every handler runs protected: one that raises is counted, keeps its place, and the other handlers of the same event still run.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local events = w.events()

-- your script
local seen = 0
events.on("IncomingText", function() error("this handler has a bug") end)
events.on("IncomingText", function() seen = seen + 1 end)
local before = events.stats.totalHandlerFailures

w.host:emitText("Line one.")
w.frame(2)
w.host:emitText("Line two.")
w.frame(2)

-- check
DOCS.eq(seen, 2, "the healthy handler heard both lines")
DOCS.eq(events.stats.totalHandlerFailures - before, 2, "the failing one was counted each time")
examples.expect: The failing handler is counted once per event and the healthy handler still sees every line.

examples.title: The same line twice is delivered once
examples.summary: The game often repeats a chat line once per chat window; eb.events delivers a repeat inside 1.5 seconds only once, and counts it.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local events = w.events()

-- your script
local heard = {}
events.on("ChatLine", function(ev) heard[#heard + 1] = ev.message end)
local before = events.stats.totalDeduped

w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 28, speaker = "Friendo", message = "pull when ready" })
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 28, speaker = "Friendo", message = "pull when ready" })   -- the same line again
w.frame(2)
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 28, speaker = "Friendo", message = "go" })
w.frame(2)

-- check
DOCS.eq(#heard, 2, "two distinct lines delivered")
DOCS.eq(heard[1], "pull when ready", "the first")
DOCS.eq(heard[2], "go", "then the next one")
DOCS.eq(events.stats.totalDeduped - before, 1, "the repeat was counted as a duplicate")
examples.expect: Two identical tells in a row reach the handler once; a different line is delivered.

examples.title: Follow a quest's progress
examples.summary: QuestOffered and QuestUpdated deliver the quest's name and the game's own update text, the text a quest pack's stages advance on.

local events = w.events()

-- your script
local seen = {}
events.on("QuestOffered", function(ev) seen[#seen + 1] = "offered " .. ev.name end)

    "1/3 lanterns lit")

examples.title: Type an eb command
examples.summary: Boot EB for InnerSpace offline and run console lines through the one command registry.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game you type in the console)
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script: lines exactly as you type them in the InnerSpace console
local said = a.console("eb status crew")
print(said)
local refused = a.console("eb dance")

-- check
DOCS.has(said, "crew: box is1", "eb status crew names this box")
DOCS.has(refused, "refused", "a word that is not a command is refused")
a.stop()
DOCS.check(a.said("EB stopped"), "eb stop ends EB")
examples.expect: eb status crew answers with this box's crew line; a word that is not a command is refused plainly.

examples.title: Run a command from a script in a running EB
examples.summary: The running EB is eb.app; eb.dispatch(line) runs a line through the same registry a typed one uses.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game it is already running)
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script
local ok, text = eb.dispatch("eb status")
print(text:match("eb%-app 1 on isx"))
local lines = eb.app.status()                    -- { lines }: version, what is up, what is not and why
eb.dispatch("eb pause")
local paused = eb.app.brain.paused
eb.dispatch("eb resume")

-- check
DOCS.check(ok, "eb status ran")
DOCS.has(lines[1], "eb-app 1 on isx", "the first status line")
DOCS.eq(eb.app.stages.registry, "up", "the registry stage came up")
DOCS.eq(paused, true, "eb pause paused the brain")
DOCS.check(not eb.app.brain.paused, "eb resume let it go")
a.stop()
examples.expect: eb.dispatch answers eb status; app.status() says what came up; pause and resume flip the brain.

examples.title: Answer an eb command with your own handler
examples.summary: Attach a handler to a command the schema declares, then run lines through the registry like typed ones.
examples.code:
-- your script
local R = require("eb.registry")
local reg = assert(R.default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))      -- data/eb/commands.json, the customer schema

local seen = {}
local ok, why = reg:attach("core.afk", function(args, ctx, parsed)
    seen[#seen + 1] = args.state                                  -- the schema's [state:onoff] argument, canonical
    return true, "afk " .. tostring(args.state) .. ": handled by my_helper"
end, { owner = "my_helper" })

local done, text = reg:dispatch("eb afk on")
print(text)
local _, text2 = reg:dispatch("afk yes")                          -- the "eb" head is optional; yes reads as on
local again, whyAgain = reg:attach("core.afk", function() return true end, { owner = "someone_else" })
local replaced = reg:attach("core.afk", function() return true, "new owner" end, { owner = "someone_else", replace = true })

-- check
DOCS.check(ok, "attached: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.check(done, "the line ran")
DOCS.eq(seen[1], "on", "the parsed argument")
DOCS.eq(seen[2], "on", "yes is read as on")
DOCS.eq(again, false, "a second owner is refused")
DOCS.has(whyAgain, "already wired by my_helper", "and told who owns it")
DOCS.check(replaced, "replace = true takes it over on purpose")
DOCS.eq(select(2, reg:dispatch("eb afk off")), "new owner", "the new handler answers")
examples.expect: The handler gets the parsed state argument; a second owner is refused unless it asks to replace.

examples.title: Send a command to the crew
examples.summary: A leading all / others / to <who> hands the line to the crew relay; the registry decides where it also runs.
examples.code:
-- your script
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))
local ranHere = 0
reg:attach("core.pause", function() ranHere = ranHere + 1; return true, "paused" end, { owner = "my_helper" })

-- ctx.relay carries a crew line (EB sets it to the crew relay; here it just records what would go out)
local sent = {}
local ctx = {
    relay = function(scope, who, line) sent[#sent + 1] = { scope = scope, who = who, line = line }; return true end,
    isMe = function(who) for _, w in ipairs(who or {}) do if w == "is1" then return true end end return false end,
}

reg:dispatch("eb all pause", ctx)              -- goes out AND runs here
print(("sent %s: %s"):format(sent[1].scope, sent[1].line))
reg:dispatch("eb others pause", ctx)           -- goes out, never runs here
reg:dispatch("eb to is2 pause", ctx)           -- goes out; is2 is not this box
reg:dispatch("eb to is1,is3 pause", ctx)       -- goes out; is1 IS this box, so it runs here too
local ok, why = reg:dispatch("eb all help")    -- help runs on one box only

-- check
DOCS.eq(#sent, 4, "four crew lines went out")
DOCS.eq(sent[1].line, "eb pause", "the relayed line carries no scope word (it runs on arrival, never relays again)")
DOCS.eq(sent[3].who[1], "is2", "to names who")
DOCS.eq(ranHere, 2, "all and to is1,is3 ran here; others and to is2 did not")
DOCS.eq(ok, false, "a command that runs on this box only refuses a crew scope")
DOCS.has(why, "runs on this box only", "and says so")
examples.expect: all runs here and goes out; others only goes out; to is2 runs here only when this box is is2.

examples.title: A crew line leaves this box
examples.summary: Typed with a crew scope, a line runs here and goes out on the crew relay for every other box.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game: type it in the console)
local a = DOCS.app()
local function crewLines()                 -- offline: count what left this box on the relay
    local n = 0
    for _, item in ipairs(a.host.log.relay) do if item.kind == "event" and item.name:match("Cmd$") then n = n + 1 end end
    return n
end

-- your script
local before = crewLines()
a.console("eb all pause")
local out = crewLines() - before
print("crew lines out: " .. out)
local pausedHere = a.app.brain.paused
a.console("eb resume")

-- check
DOCS.eq(out, 1, "one crew line went out")
DOCS.eq(pausedHere, true, "and the line ran here too")
DOCS.eq(crewLines() - before, 1, "eb resume (no scope) did not go out")
DOCS.check(not a.app.brain.paused, "resumed here")
a.stop()
examples.expect: eb all pause pauses this box and puts one crew line on the relay; eb resume (no scope) stays here.

examples.title: Read the built-in help
examples.summary: reg:help() lists the domains, reg:help(domain) its commands, reg:help(verb) one command's card.
examples.code:
-- your script
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))
local top = reg:help()                         -- { lines }: the domains and how many commands each has
local nav = reg:help("nav")                    -- one domain's commands
local card = reg:help("follow")                -- one command: usage, what it does, its args, aliases, crew scopes
print(card[1])
local usage = reg:usage("follow")
local unknown = reg:help("juggle")

-- check
DOCS.has(top[1], "eb <command>", "the first line says how to type a command")
DOCS.has(table.concat(nav, "\n"), "follow", "the nav domain lists follow")
DOCS.eq(usage, "eb follow [who] [dist]", "the usage line")
DOCS.has(card[#card], "for the crew: eb all|others|to follow", "the card says it can go to the crew")
DOCS.has(unknown[1], "no eb command or domain", "an unknown topic is answered, never an error")
examples.expect: The help lists the domains, the nav domain lists follow, and follow's card shows its usage and crew scopes.

examples.title: Tab-complete a command line
examples.summary: reg:complete(line, opts) returns the words that could come next and the line advanced to them.
examples.code:
-- your script
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))
local cands, line = reg:complete("eb pau")               -- one candidate: the line gets the word and a space
print(line)
local boxes = reg:complete("eb to ", { who = { "is1", "is2", "is3" } })
local onoff = reg:complete("eb cures ")                  -- cures takes [state:onoff]
local verbs = reg:complete("eb all fo")                  -- after a scope word: verbs only

-- check
DOCS.eq(cands[1], "pause", "pau -> pause")
DOCS.eq(line, "eb pause ", "the line advanced with a trailing space")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(boxes, ","), "is1,is2,is3", "after 'to' the box ids you passed")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(onoff, ","), "off,on", "an onoff argument offers off and on")
DOCS.check(#verbs >= 1 and verbs[1]:sub(1, 2) == "fo", "verbs starting fo")
examples.expect: pau completes to pause; after "to" it offers box ids; an onoff argument offers on and off.

examples.title: Build a button row from the registry
examples.summary: reg:view(filter) lists the shipped commands of a domain in schema order: an allow-list for a window.
examples.code:
-- your script
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))
local buttons = {}
for _, row in ipairs(reg:view({ domain = "nav" })) do
    buttons[#buttons + 1] = { label = row.verb, line = "eb " .. row.verb, help = row.desc }
end
local row = reg:command("ah")                     -- a verb, an alias or a "<domain>.<verb>" id, any case
print(("ah -> %s"):format(row.id))
local byId = reg:command("NAV.FOLLOW")
local notWired = reg:unattached({ domain = "nav" })   -- a fresh registry: no handler attached yet

-- check
local labels = {}
for _, b in ipairs(buttons) do labels[b.label] = true end
DOCS.check(labels.follow and labels.walk, "the nav row has follow and walk")
DOCS.eq(row.verb, "autohunt", "the alias found the command")
DOCS.eq(byId.verb, "follow", "an id finds it too, any case")
DOCS.eq(#notWired, #buttons, "nothing is wired in a fresh registry")
examples.expect: The nav view lists follow; an alias finds its command; a fresh registry reports what is not wired yet.

examples.title: Read a command line without running it
examples.summary: eb.registry.parse splits a line into its scope, who, command and typed arguments, or says what is wrong.
examples.code:
-- your script
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))
local Parse = require("eb.registry.parse")
local p = assert(Parse.parse(reg, 'eb to is2,is3 follow Tankard 4'))
print(("%s %s: %s"):format(p.scope, table.concat(p.who, ","), Parse.canonical(p)))
local bad, why = Parse.parse(reg, "eb follow Tankard close")       -- dist is a float
local quoted = Parse.parse(reg, 'eb announce "pull in five"')     -- the last string argument takes the rest

-- check
DOCS.eq(p.id, "nav.follow", "the command id")
DOCS.eq(p.args.who, "Tankard", "the who argument")
DOCS.eq(p.args.dist, 4, "dist read as a number")
DOCS.eq(bad, nil, "a word where a number belongs is refused")
DOCS.has(why, "wants a number", "with the reason")
DOCS.eq(quoted.args.text, "pull in five", "a quoted argument stays one")
examples.expect: The line reads as scope to, two boxes, follow with who and dist; a bad number is refused with the reason.

examples.title: What a refused line tells you
examples.summary: reg:dispatch never raises: every refusal is ok == false plus a plain reason a script can show or log.
examples.code:
-- your script
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))
local function try(line)
    local ok, text = reg:dispatch(line)
    if not ok then print("refused: " .. text) end
    return ok, text
end
local _, unknown = try("eb juggle home")
local _, badArg = try("eb pause maybe")             -- pause takes pause | resume | toggle | status
local _, missing = try("eb end")                    -- end needs <system>
local _, notWired = try("eb follow")                -- a real command with no handler attached in this registry
local raised = reg:attach("core.reload", function() error("boom") end, { owner = "my_helper" }) and
    select(2, reg:dispatch("eb reload"))

-- check
DOCS.has(unknown, "is not an eb command", "an unknown word")
DOCS.has(badArg, "is one of pause|resume|toggle|status", "a bad value names the choices")
DOCS.has(missing, "needs system", "a missing required argument is named")
DOCS.has(notWired, "does not answer on this box yet", "a command nothing answers yet")
DOCS.has(raised, "raised: ", "a handler that raises is caught and reported")
examples.expect: An unknown word, a bad argument, a missing argument and a command nothing answers yet are each refused.

examples.title: Export the command list
examples.summary: reg:customerSchema() is every shipped command as a plain table; reg:customerJson() is the same as JSON.
examples.code:
-- your script
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))
local J = require("ebkit.jsontable")
local doc = reg:customerSchema()
print(("%d commands in %d domains"):format(doc.counts.commands, doc.counts.domains))
local back = assert(J.decode(reg:customerJson()))
local allShipped = true
for _, c in ipairs(doc.commands) do if c.ship ~= "shipped" then allShipped = false end end

-- check
DOCS.eq(doc.schema, "eb.command-schema/1", "the schema name")
DOCS.eq(doc.counts.commands, #doc.commands, "the count matches the list")
DOCS.check(doc.counts.commands > 100, "a full command list")
DOCS.check(allShipped, "only shipped rows")
DOCS.eq(#back.commands, #doc.commands, "the JSON decodes back to the same rows")
examples.expect: The schema's counts match its lists, every row is shipped, and the JSON decodes back to the same count.

examples.title: Pause, resume, status and the kill switch
examples.summary: The core commands every box answers, typed in the console and run from a script with eb.dispatch: help's usage line, pause and resume, status goal, and eb stopall halting the brain.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game you type in the console)
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script: lines as typed, then the same from code
local usage = a.console("eb help pause"):match("eb pause[^\n]*")
local paused = a.console("eb pause")
local wasPaused = a.app.brain.paused
local okR, resumed = eb.dispatch("eb resume")              -- a script runs a line exactly as if typed
local goal = a.console("eb status goal")
local halted = a.console("eb stopall")
print(("%s | %s | %s | %s"):format(usage, paused:match("EB paused"), resumed, halted:match("the brain is halted")))

-- check
DOCS.check(wasPaused == true, "eb pause froze the brain")
DOCS.check(okR and a.app.brain.paused == false, "eb.dispatch ran eb resume")
DOCS.has(goal, "brain:", "eb status goal names the brain's state")
DOCS.check(a.app.brain.halted == true, "eb stopall halted the brain")
a.stop()
DOCS.check(a.said("EB stopped"), "typed eb stop ends EB on this box")
examples.expect: pause freezes the brain and resume frees it; a script's eb.dispatch takes the same path; stopall halts the brain while EB stays loaded.

examples.title: Which commands this box answers
examples.summary: reg:unattached lists the declared commands nothing on this box answers yet (each part of EB attaches its commands as it starts; a part that did not start leaves its commands there, and eb status says which). Such a command - here a script's own, declared before it has a handler, in a registry built from EB's command list - is refused in plain words when typed, never run (EB Help marks such a row "this box does not answer it yet").
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script
local reg = a.app.reg
local waiting = reg:unattached()                    -- EB's own declared commands nothing answers on this box
local answered = #reg:view({ domain = "core" }) - #reg:unattached({ domain = "core" })

-- a command of your own, declared before its handler: a registry built from EB's command list, plus one row
local R = require("eb.registry")
local mine = R.new()
assert(mine:load(assert(R.readFile("data/eb/commands.json"))))  -- the shipped list (in game: under the EB folder)
assert(mine:load({ schema = R.SCHEMA, domains = { { id = "myscript", label = "My script", desc = "my own commands" } },
    commands = { { id = "myscript.myreport", domain = "myscript", verb = "myreport", name = "eb myreport",
                   desc = "my own report", module = "my.script", ship = "shipped", scopes = { "local" }, args = {} } } }))
local listed = mine:unattached({ domain = "myscript" })
local okBefore, before = mine:dispatch("eb myreport")
mine:attach("myscript.myreport", function() return true, "my report: all quiet" end, { owner = "my.script" })
local okAfter, after = mine:dispatch("eb myreport")
print(("myreport: %s | EB's own commands waiting on this box: %d"):format(
    tostring(before):match("does not answer on this box yet") or tostring(before), #waiting))

-- check
DOCS.check(answered >= 5, "the core commands are answered (help, status, stop, pause, resume)")
DOCS.eq(#reg:unattached({ domain = "core" }), 0, "no core command waits on a booted box")
DOCS.eq(listed[1], "myscript.myreport", "unattached lists the declared command nothing answers yet")
DOCS.check(okBefore == false and tostring(before):find("does not answer on this box yet", 1, true) ~= nil,
    "typed, it is refused in plain words - never run")
DOCS.check(okAfter == true and after == "my report: all quiet", "once a handler is attached, it answers")
a.stop()
examples.expect: the core commands are answered on the booted box; the script's own command, declared without a handler, is listed by unattached and refused plainly (it does not answer on this box yet) until a handler is attached.

examples.title: A console word of your own
examples.summary: eb.console is the console window's model: register a word it answers itself, run lines, and read what a window draws - the newest row, the word list and this box's own row.
examples.code:
-- your script
local Console = require("eb.console")
local C = Console.new({ box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", clock = function() return 0 end,
    dispatch = function(line) return true, "ran " .. line end })      -- in game: eb.dispatch
local rev0 = C.vocabRev()
C.register("roll", function(args) return true, "rolled " .. tostring(args[1]) end, "roll a die")
local _, rolled = C.run("roll 20")
local _, ran = C.run("eb status")
C.setSelfState({ zone = "fixture_hollow", mode = "idle", hp = 100, pw = 90 })
local words = {}
for _, v in ipairs(C.vocabData()) do words[#words + 1] = v.verb end
print(("%s | %s | words: %s"):format(rolled, ran, table.concat(words, ", ")))

-- check
DOCS.check(C.vocabRev() > rev0, "registering a word moved the word list's revision")
DOCS.eq(words[#words], "roll", "your word comes last, after the built-in ones")
DOCS.check(C.newest() >= 2, "the output holds the rows the two lines made")
DOCS.eq(C.boxes()[1].state.zone, "fixture_hollow", "this box's own row (first in the box list)")
DOCS.eq(C.state().boxes[1].zone, "fixture_hollow", "and in the state a window draws")
examples.expect: The new word is answered by the console; any other line goes to the dispatch; the word list grew once.

examples.title: A registry of your own, and wrapping a handler
examples.summary: Load EB's command list into a registry of your own (a tool or a test), answer a command, then wrap its handler to add a step - and take the wrapper off again.
examples.code:
-- your script
local R = require("eb.registry")
local reg = R.new()
local doc = assert(R.readFile("data/eb/commands.json"))    -- the shipped list (in game: under the EB folder)
assert(reg:load(doc))
reg:attach("util.timer", function(args) return true, "resting 30" end, { owner = "my.helper" })

local original = reg:handler("util.timer")
reg:attach("util.timer", function(args, ctx, parsed)
    local ok, text = original(args, ctx, parsed)
    return ok, "[checked] " .. tostring(text)
end, { owner = "my.helper", replace = true })              -- replace = true: take it over on purpose
local _, wrapped = reg:dispatch("eb timer add rest 30")
reg:detach("util.timer")
local okAfter, after = reg:dispatch("eb timer list")
print(("wrapped: %s | after detach: %s"):format(wrapped, after:match("does not answer on this box yet")))

-- check
DOCS.check(#reg:view({}) > 100, "the copy holds every shipped command")
DOCS.eq(wrapped, "[checked] resting 30", "the wrapper ran the original handler")
DOCS.eq(okAfter, false, "detached: the command is no longer answered")
local second, why = reg:attach("util.timer", function() return true end, { owner = "my.helper" })
local third, why2 = reg:attach("util.timer", function() return true end, { owner = "another.helper" })
DOCS.check(second and not third, "one owner per command")
DOCS.has(why2, "already wired", "a second owner is told who has it")
examples.expect: The copy loads every shipped command; the wrapper runs before the original; detach leaves the command unanswered again.

examples.title: The window and monitor commands in this release
examples.summary: Types each window and monitor command on a booted EB and reads its answer: each opens its window through the window bridge (eb ui, eb mini, eb map, eb xp, eb track, eb radar, eb meters, eb crew, eb anal, eb mybutton), lists the kept workspaces (eb battlestation) or prints its readout (eb waiting, eb crew status); eb windows lists every window with the line that opens it. (eb uireset, eb anon and eb streamer answer too; they change the user's own files, so a doc example does not press them.)
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script: the lines as a player types them
local lines = { "eb mini show", "eb ui", "eb map", "eb xp", "eb track cd", "eb radar on", "eb mybutton",
                "eb battlestation", "eb anal", "eb meters", "eb waiting", "eb crew", "eb crew status" }
local answered = 0
for _, line in ipairs(lines) do
    local ok, text = eb.dispatch(line)
    if not tostring(text):find("not wired yet", 1, true) then answered = answered + 1 end
end
local okList, list = eb.dispatch("eb windows")
local _, waiting = eb.dispatch("eb waiting")
local card = a.console("eb help meters")
print(("%d window and monitor commands typed, %d answered"):format(#lines, answered))

-- check
DOCS.eq(answered, #lines, "every window and monitor command is answered")
DOCS.check(okList, "eb windows answers")
DOCS.has(list, "eb mcp", "with the line that opens the MCP")
DOCS.has(waiting, "what the crew is waiting on", "eb waiting prints the crew's waits")
DOCS.has(card, "eb meters", "a help card still prints")

examples.expect: every window and monitor command is answered; eb windows lists every window with the line that opens it.

examples.title: The utility commands in this release
examples.summary: Types the utility commands on a booted EB: settings by command (eb set reads a value; eb preset and eb alias list theirs), seeing what EB does (eb debug, eb fps, eb uiscan, eb tlocheck), the timers, the keep-alive and the voice (eb tts) answer at once - eb tts says why when the overlay that speaks is not there - and a script can always use the settings store.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script
local store = require("eb.platform").settings()             -- the settings store a script uses directly
store.set("myhelper.enabled", true)
local okSet, readBack = eb.dispatch("eb set myhelper.enabled")
local answered = { "eb preset", "eb alias", "eb debug", "eb fps", "eb afk status", "eb timer list", "eb tts", "eb uiscan",
                   "eb tlocheck" }
local okCount = 0
for _, line in ipairs(answered) do
    local ok, text = eb.dispatch(line)
    if not tostring(text):find("does not answer on this box yet", 1, true) then okCount = okCount + 1 end
end
print("eb set myhelper.enabled -> " .. tostring(readBack))

-- check
DOCS.check(okSet, "eb set answers")
DOCS.has(readBack, "myhelper.enabled = on", "and reads what the store holds")
DOCS.eq(okCount, #answered, "every utility command typed answers")
DOCS.eq(store.get("myhelper.enabled"), true, "the store holds the value for this session")
a.stop()
examples.expect: eb set reads what the store holds; every utility command typed answers - none says "does not answer on this box yet". (eb set <key> <value>, eb export, eb dumplog and eb debugreport answer too, but they write the user's own files, and eb grabloc puts down the house item on your cursor in the game, so a doc example does not press them.)

examples.title: Two boxes, one crew
examples.summary: eb.relay carries scoped lines between boxes: all reaches everyone once, others skips the sender, to names who.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an offline relay bus between two boxes (in game each box's relay rides InnerSpace's own)
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()

-- your script: one relay per box; onLocal is what a box does with a line meant for it
local Relay = require("eb.relay")
local function box(id, name, subclass)
    local ran = {}
    local R = Relay.new({ box = id, name = name, subclass = subclass, transport = bus.box(id) })
    R.onLocal(function(line, env) ran[#ran + 1] = line end)
    R.join()                                   -- opt in: nothing is sent or heard before join()
    return R, ran
end
local tank, tankRan = box("is1", "Tankard", "guardian")
local heal, healRan = box("is2", "Mendwell", "templar")

tank.send("all pause")                         -- everyone, the sender included (it acts at once)
tank.send("others stop")                       -- everyone but the sender
tank.send("to is2 follow is1")                 -- only box is2
print(("is1 ran: %s | is2 ran: %s"):format(table.concat(tankRan, ", "), table.concat(healRan, ", ")))

-- check
DOCS.eq(table.concat(tankRan, ","), "pause", "the sender ran all once and nothing else")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(healRan, ","), "pause,stop,follow is1", "the other box ran each line meant for it, once")
local dec = tank.send("to is2 all pause")
DOCS.eq(dec.ok, false, "a line may carry only one scope word")
examples.expect: all runs once on each box, others only on the other one, to is2 only on is2.

examples.title: Address boxes by box, name, class or archetype
examples.summary: A to <who> list may name a box id, a character, a class or an archetype; wire.shouldHandle decides who acts.
examples.code:
-- your script
local wire = require("eb.relay.wire")
local boxes = {
    { box = "is1", name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian" },
    { box = "is2", name = "Mendwell", subclass = "templar" },
    { box = "is3", name = "Sparkwick", subclass = "wizard" },
}
local function who(scope, list, from)
    local out = {}
    for _, me in ipairs(boxes) do
        if wire.shouldHandle({ scope = scope, who = list, from = from or "is1" }, me) then out[#out + 1] = me.box end
    end
    return table.concat(out, ",")
end
print("priest -> " .. who("to", "priest"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(who("to", "priest"), "is2", "an archetype")
DOCS.eq(who("to", "@fighter"), "is1", "@archetype")
DOCS.eq(who("to", "templar,is3"), "is2,is3", "a class and a box id together")
DOCS.eq(who("to", "sparkwick"), "is3", "a character name, any case")
DOCS.eq(who("others", ""), "is2,is3", "others never reaches the sender")
DOCS.eq(who("all", ""), "is1,is2,is3", "all reaches everyone")
DOCS.eq(wire.archetype("dirge"), "scout", "the archetype of a class")
examples.expect: to priest reaches the templar, to @fighter the guardian, to is3 only is3, and others never the sender.

examples.title: Split a typed line into scope and command
examples.summary: wire.parseScope reads the one leading scope word of a line: local, all, others or to <who>.
examples.code:
-- your script
local wire = require("eb.relay.wire")
local scope, who, rest = wire.parseScope("to is2,is3 follow Tankard")
print(("%s | %s | %s"):format(scope, who, rest))
local s2, _, r2 = wire.parseScope("others pause")
local s3, _, r3 = wire.parseScope("pause")
local s4, w4, r4 = wire.parseScope("to")                  -- "to" with nobody after it is NOT a broadcast

-- check
DOCS.eq(scope, "to", "the scope")
DOCS.eq(who, "is2,is3", "who")
DOCS.eq(rest, "follow Tankard", "the command left over")
DOCS.eq(s2 .. ":" .. r2, "others:pause", "others")
DOCS.eq(s3 .. ":" .. r3, "local:pause", "no scope word means this box")
DOCS.eq(s4 .. ":" .. w4 .. ":" .. r4, "local::to", "a lone to stays local")
DOCS.check(wire.isScopeWord("ALL") and not wire.isScopeWord("pause"), "scope words, any case")
examples.expect: Each line splits into its scope, who and the command left over; a bare line is local.

examples.title: Hear what the other boxes are doing
examples.summary: Each box broadcasts a small state (zone, mode, health, power, a fight on); every box keeps a roster of it.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an offline relay bus between two boxes
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()

-- your script
local Relay = require("eb.relay")
local tank = Relay.new({ box = "is1", name = "Tankard", transport = bus.box("is1") })
local heal = Relay.new({ box = "is2", name = "Mendwell", transport = bus.box("is2") })
tank.join(); heal.join()
local heard = {}
heal.onState(function(boxId, st) heard[#heard + 1] = boxId end)

tank.broadcastState({ name = "Tankard", zone = "a_test_hall", mode = "ic-lead", hp = 64, pw = 90, combat = true })
for _, p in ipairs(heal.boxes()) do
    local st = p.state
    print(("%s: %s hp %d%s"):format(p.box, st.zone, st.hp, st.combat and " FIGHTING" or ""))
end

-- check
DOCS.eq(heard[1], "is1", "is2 heard is1's state")
local st = heal.boxes()[1].state
DOCS.eq(st.hp, 64, "health travels as a number")
DOCS.eq(st.combat, true, "the fight flag")
DOCS.eq(st.mode, "ic-lead", "and the mode")
examples.expect: is2 hears is1's state: its zone, health and that it is fighting.

examples.title: A line heard twice runs once
examples.summary: Every crew line carries a message id; a box acts on an id once, however many times the line arrives.
examples.code:
-- your script
local wire = require("eb.relay.wire")
local seen = wire.seenSet(64)              -- a bounded set: it forgets the oldest ids past 64
local first = seen.add("is1#41")
local again = seen.add("is1#41")
local next = seen.add("is1#42")
print(("first %s, again %s, next %s"):format(tostring(first), tostring(again), tostring(next)))

-- a whole command line on the wire: encode, decode, and the id it carries
local fields = wire.encodeCmd({ from = "is1", seq = 43, scope = "to", who = "is2", line = "eb follow is1" })
local env = wire.decodeCmd(fields)

-- check
DOCS.eq(first, true, "a new id")
DOCS.eq(again, false, "the same id again is dropped")
DOCS.eq(next, true, "the next id is new")
DOCS.eq(env.mid, "is1#43", "the id is <box>#<sequence>")
DOCS.eq(env.line, "eb follow is1", "the line survives the trip, spaces and all")
DOCS.eq(seen.count(), 2, "two ids remembered")
examples.expect: The same message id is new the first time and a duplicate after; a different id is new again.

examples.title: Wait for the group at a mark
examples.summary: group.barrier(name) is non-blocking: call it each tick until every member here has reached the same mark.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the group as the world snapshot reports it, and a clock you step
local t = { now = 0 }
local world = { snapshot = function()
    return { name = "Tankard", class = "guardian", group = { count = 2, members = {
        { name = "Mendwell", zone = "a_test_hall", subclass = "templar" },
        { name = "Sparkwick", zone = "a_test_hall", subclass = "wizard" } } } }
end }
local peerMarks = {}

-- your script
local Group = require("eb.relay.group")
local G = Group.new({ world = world, me = { box = "is1", name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian" },
    clock = function() return t.now end,
    broadcastMark = function(name) end,                       -- (offline: EB puts the mark on the crew relay)
    peerMarks = function() return peerMarks end })
local seen = {}
seen[#seen + 1] = G.barrier("door", { timeoutMs = 15000 })   -- nobody else has reached it yet
peerMarks.mendwell = "door"
seen[#seen + 1] = G.barrier("door", { timeoutMs = 15000 })   -- one of two
peerMarks.sparkwick = "door"
seen[#seen + 1] = G.barrier("door", { timeoutMs = 15000 })   -- everyone here
print("barrier: " .. table.concat(seen, ", "))

G.resetBarrier()                                              -- the next objective starts fresh
peerMarks = {}
G.barrier("boss", { timeoutMs = 5000 })
t.now = 6000
local late = G.barrier("boss", { timeoutMs = 5000 })

-- check
DOCS.eq(table.concat(seen, ","), "waiting,waiting,ready", "waits until every member has the mark")
DOCS.eq(late, "timeout", "never a silent hang: it times out and the caller decides")
examples.expect: The barrier waits while one member is missing, is ready once both marks are in, and times out on its own.

examples.title: Who drives the group
examples.summary: The tank runs the route and zones the group in; group.role() and group.amDriver() say who that is.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an offline relay bus and the world snapshot of each box
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()
local function worldOf(class, others)
    return { snapshot = function() return { name = "Me", class = class, group = { count = #others, members = others } } end }
end
local party = {
    { name = "Tankard", zone = "a_test_hall", subclass = "guardian" },
    { name = "Mendwell", zone = "a_test_hall", subclass = "templar" },
}

-- your script
local Relay, Group = require("eb.relay"), require("eb.relay.group")
local tankRelay = Relay.new({ box = "is1", name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian", transport = bus.box("is1") })
local healRelay = Relay.new({ box = "is2", name = "Mendwell", subclass = "templar", transport = bus.box("is2") })
local drives = {}
tankRelay.onLocal(function(line) drives[#drives + 1] = line end)
tankRelay.join(); healRelay.join()
local tank = Group.new({ relay = tankRelay, world = worldOf("guardian", { party[2] }) })
local heal = Group.new({ relay = healRelay, world = worldOf("templar", { party[1] }) })
print(("guardian: %s driver=%s | templar: %s driver=%s"):format(tank.role(), tostring(tank.amDriver()),
    heal.role(), tostring(heal.amDriver())))
local handed = heal.handoffToTank("a_test_hall")       -- the healer asks the tank to drive

-- check
DOCS.eq(tank.role(), "tank", "a fighter is the tank")
DOCS.eq(heal.role(), "healer", "a priest is the healer")
DOCS.check(tank.amDriver() and not heal.amDriver(), "only the tank drives")
DOCS.eq(handed, "ok", "the drive was handed over")
DOCS.has(drives[1], "a_test_hall", "the tank's box got the hand-over line")
DOCS.eq(Group.roleOf("wizard"), "member", "everyone else is a member")
examples.expect: The guardian is the tank and the driver; the templar is the healer and hands the drive to the tank.

examples.title: Give the followers an order
examples.summary: The lead sends an order with crew.order, a follower answers it with crew.onOrder; boxes hear each other.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an offline relay bus between two boxes and a clock you step
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()
local t = { now = 0 }

-- your script
local Relay, Crew = require("eb.relay"), require("eb.app.crew")
local function box(id, name)
    local R = Relay.new({ box = id, name = name, transport = bus.box(id), clock = function() return t.now end })
    local crew = Crew.new({ relay = R, now = function() return t.now end,
        me = function() return { name = name, zone = "a_test_hall", mode = "idle", hp = 100, pw = 100 } end })
    R.join()
    return crew
end
local lead, follower = box("is1", "Tankard"), box("is2", "Mendwell")
local got
follower.onOrder("camp", function(args, env) got = { args = args, from = env.from } end)

lead.tick(t.now); follower.tick(t.now)                     -- EB runs tick() as a pulse job: each box says who it is
lead.order("to is2", "camp", { "12.5", "0", "-40" })      -- travels as a crew line, never as an eb command
print(("is2 got camp %s from %s"):format(got and got.args or "?", got and got.from or "?"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(got.args, "12.5 0 -40", "the order's arguments")
DOCS.eq(got.from, "is1", "and who sent it")
DOCS.eq(#lead.peers(), 1, "the lead hears one other box")
DOCS.eq(follower.nameOf("is1"), "Tankard", "a box learns the others' characters from their state")
DOCS.check(follower.isMe("is2") and not follower.isMe("is3"), "isMe answers for this box only")
examples.expect: The follower gets the lead's camp order with its arguments and the sender's box id; each box hears the other. A crew line from a box that has not said who it is waits for that box's state, so each box ticks first.

examples.title: Drive the console from a script
examples.summary: eb.console is the console window's model: scoped lines through the relay, history, search and completion.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an offline relay bus between two boxes
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()

-- your script
local Relay, Console = require("eb.relay"), require("eb.console")
local function box(id, name)
    local ran = {}
    local R = Relay.new({ box = id, name = name, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local C = Console.new({ relay = R, box = id, name = name,
        dispatch = function(line) ran[#ran + 1] = line; return true, "ran " .. line end })
    R.join()
    return C, ran
end
local c1, ran1 = box("is1", "Tankard")
local _, ran2 = box("is2", "Mendwell")
local _, answer = c1.run("others pause")
print(answer)
c1.run("boxes")                                   -- a console verb, answered right here
local hits = c1.search("pause")
local comp = c1.complete("to ")

-- check
DOCS.eq(#ran2, 1, "the other box ran it")
DOCS.eq(#ran1, 0, "others never runs on the sender")
DOCS.eq(c1.historyList()[1], "others pause", "the typed line is in the history")
DOCS.check(#hits >= 1, "search finds it in the output")
DOCS.check(#comp.candidates >= 2, "after 'to' the console offers box ids and archetypes")
examples.expect: A scoped line goes to the crew and the other box's dispatcher runs it; history and search see it.

examples.title: Turn one box's event into a crew command
examples.summary: Events never travel by themselves: a handler sends ONE deliberate line with events.crew(targets, line).
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an offline relay bus between two boxes
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()

-- your script
local events, Relay = require("eb.events"), require("eb.relay")
local me = Relay.new({ box = "is1", name = "Tankard", transport = bus.box("is1") })
local mate = Relay.new({ box = "is2", name = "Mendwell", transport = bus.box("is2") })
local mateRan = {}
mate.onLocal(function(line) mateRan[#mateRan + 1] = line end)
me.join(); mate.join()

events.setRelay(function(targets, line) return me.send(targets .. " " .. line) end)
events.on("IncomingText", function(ev)

examples.title: Call the group back, evacuate, read the group
examples.summary: eb.relay.group's calls over a real relay: send a line, read the group from the world snapshot, record a member's mark, call stuck members back (catchup) and evacuate (evac); then leave the relay.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an in-memory relay between two boxes, and the group as the world snapshot reports it
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()
local world = { snapshot = function()
    return { name = "Tankard", zone = "a_test_hall", group = { count = 2, members = {
        { name = "Mendwell", zone = "a_test_hall", subclass = "templar" } } } }
end }

-- your script
local Relay = require("eb.relay")
local Group = require("eb.relay.group")
local tank = Relay.new({ box = "is1", name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian", transport = bus.box("is1") })
local healer = Relay.new({ box = "is2", name = "Mendwell", subclass = "templar", transport = bus.box("is2") })
local heard, notes = {}, {}
healer.onLocal(function(line) heard[#heard + 1] = line end)
tank.note(function(text) notes[#notes + 1] = text end)        -- lines the console shows but does not act on
tank.join(); healer.join()

local G = Group.new({ relay = tank, world = world, me = { box = "is1", name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian" },
    clock = function() return 0 end })
G.send("others", "eb pause")
local back = G.catchup("is2")                 -- the first answer to a member who fell behind
local out = G.evac()                          -- the evacuation chain, then a totem - only ever by spell
local gs = G.groupState()
G.recordMark("Mendwell", "door")
print(("heard: %s; %s is the %s"):format(table.concat(heard, " | "), gs.members[1].name, gs.members[1].role))

tank.leave()                                  -- in game: the transport leaves the relay group join() joined

-- check
DOCS.eq(back, "working", "the catch-up order went out")
DOCS.eq(out, "working", "the evacuation order went out")
DOCS.eq(gs.leader, "Tankard", "the leader is this box's character")
DOCS.eq(gs.members[1].role, "healer", "a templar is the healer")
DOCS.eq(tank.joined, false, "leave marks the relay as no longer joined")
DOCS.eq(#notes, 0, "nothing needed a console note")

examples.title: Read the world snapshot
examples.summary: eb.world builds ONE plain table per frame from the game layer: you, your state and your group.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world({ pulse = false, me = { healthPct = 72, powerPct = 55, inCombat = true } })
w.addMember({ name = "Mendwell", id = 11, class = "templar", healthPct = 90, inZone = true })
w.addActor({ id = 11, name = "Mendwell", type = "PC", isNPC = false, distance = 7 })

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local world = require("eb.world").new({ game = game })
local snap = world.snapshot()
w.self.healthPct = 40                     -- the game moves on ...
local same = world.snapshot()             -- ... but inside one frame the snapshot is the same table
world.invalidate()                        -- rebuild the table (the game layer still answers this frame's reads)
local rebuilt = world.snapshot()
world.beginTick()                         -- a new frame: the game layer reads again, the snapshot is rebuilt
local fresh = world.snapshot()
print(("%s %s (%s) hp %d power %d fighting=%s group %d"):format(snap.name, snap.class, snap.archetype,
    snap.hpPct, snap.powerPct, tostring(snap.hated), snap.group.count))

-- check
DOCS.eq(snap.inGame, true, "in the world")
DOCS.eq(same, snap, "one snapshot per frame")
DOCS.check(rebuilt ~= snap and rebuilt.hpPct == 72, "invalidate builds a new table from this frame's reads")
DOCS.eq(fresh.hpPct, 40, "beginTick: the next snapshot reads the game again")
DOCS.eq(snap.archetype, "priest", "the archetype from the class")
DOCS.eq(snap.hated, true, "a fight is on (the hate flag, not the lingering in-combat flag)")
DOCS.eq(snap.group.members[1].name, "Mendwell", "the group member")
DOCS.eq(snap.group.members[1].role, "priest", "with the member's archetype")
DOCS.check(snap.reads <= 8 and not snap.partial, "inside the read budget")

examples.title: Give the brain your own goal
examples.summary: A goal is a phase machine the brain advances one bite per tick: return working, done or blocked; never wait.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: a world the brain can snapshot (in game EB builds the brain over eb.world itself)
local world = { snapshot = function() return { inGame = true, name = "Tankard", class = "guardian", zone = "a_test_hall",
    hpPct = 100, powerPct = 100, x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, group = { count = 0, members = {} } } end }

-- your script
local Brain = require("eb.brain")
local brain = Brain.new({ world = world }, { log = function() end })      -- missing subsystems get safe stubs
local goal = {
    name = "count-to-three", ctx = { phase = "count", n = 0 },
    advance = function(self, b, snap)
        local c = self.ctx
        if c.phase == "count" then
            c.n = c.n + 1
            if c.n >= 3 then c.phase = "report" end
            return "working"
        end
        return "done"
    end,
    describe = function(self) return "count[" .. self.ctx.phase .. "]" end,
}
brain:pushGoal(goal)
local t, ticks = 0, 0
while brain:activeGoal() and ticks < 20 do
    t = t + 50                                   -- the host calls pulse every frame; the brain ticks every 250 ms
    if brain:pulse(t) then ticks = ticks + 1 end
end
print(("goal done after %d ticks"):format(ticks))

-- check
DOCS.eq(ticks, 4, "three counts and one report")
DOCS.eq(brain:activeGoal(), nil, "the finished goal left the stack")
DOCS.eq(brain:pulse(t + 250), "idle", "the brain is idle")
examples.expect: The goal steps through count -> report -> done over four brain ticks, then the brain is idle.

-- your script

brain:pushGoal({ name = "watch", ctx = { phase = "watch" }, advance = function() return "working" end,
    describe = function() return "watch[watch]" end })
brain:pause()
print("paused -> " .. tostring(brain:pulse(1000)))
local ticksWhilePaused = brain.ticks
brain:pause(false)
local after = brain:pulse(2000)

-- check

DOCS.eq(after, "goal:watch/working", "resumed, it ticks the goal")

examples.title: Goals, interrupts and one tick
examples.summary: The brain's seven interrupts in priority order, a built-in goal's phase, and ticks stepped by hand: a fight takes the tick while it is on, then the goal resumes where it was.
examples.code:
-- your script
local Brain = require("eb.brain")
local Goals = require("eb.brain.goals")
local Irq = require("eb.brain.interrupts")
local C = require("eb.brain.contracts")

local order = Irq.new()                                    -- highest priority first
local grind = Goals.new({ kind = "grind", params = { camp = { x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, radius = 40 }, maxKills = 1 } })

-- a brain over stand-in subsystems (in game EB's start gives it the real ones) and a world you control
local fightOn = true
local deps = C.stubs()
deps.world = { snapshot = function()
    return { inGame = true, hated = fightOn, x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, zone = "fixture_hollow", hpPct = 100,
             powerPct = 100, bagsFreeSlots = 20, group = { count = 1, members = {} } }
end }
local b = Brain.new(deps, { log = function() end })
b:pushGoal({ name = "watch", ctx = { phase = "look" },
             advance = function(self, brain, snap) return "working" end,
             describe = function(self) return "watch[look]" end })
local during = b:tick(0, 250)                              -- a fight is on: the combat interrupt has the tick
fightOn = false
local after = b:tick(250, 250)                             -- the fight is over: the goal goes on
print(("first: %s (%d) | %s | %s then %s"):format(order[1].name, order[1].priority, grind:describe(), during, after))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#order, 7, "seven interrupts")
DOCS.eq(order[#order].name, "low_hp_power", "resting comes last")
DOCS.eq(grind.preset, "openworld", "a grind goal sets the openworld preset")
DOCS.eq(during, "irq:combat/cleared", "the fight took the tick")
DOCS.eq(after, "goal:watch/working", "the goal resumed")
DOCS.has(b:status(), "watch[look]", "status names the goal and its phase")
