examples.title: Step a brain by hand
examples.summary: Every part of a brain tick on its own: the snapshot, the events it answers, the stuck watch, choosing and driving an interrupt, the goal stack, the resume point and the log - over stand-in subsystems you control.
examples.code:
-- your script: stand-in subsystems (C.stubs) with the few calls this example drives replaced
local Brain = require("eb.brain")
local C = require("eb.brain.contracts")
local deps = C.stubs()
local answered, saved = {}, {}
deps.events = { poll = function() return { { kind = "rez_offer", from = "Mendwell" } } end,
                answer = function(ev, choice) answered[#answered + 1] = ev.kind .. ":" .. choice end }
deps.world = { snapshot = function()
    return { inGame = true, hated = true, x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, zone = "fixture_hollow", hpPct = 90, powerPct = 80,
             bagsFreeSlots = 10, group = { count = 1, members = {} } }
end }
local report, allOk = C.check(deps)
local lines = {}
local b = Brain.new(deps, { log = function(l) lines[#lines + 1] = l end, persist = function(p) saved[#saved + 1] = p end,
    persistThrottleMs = 0 })

local snap = b:snapshot(0)
b:consumeEvents(snap)                              -- answers the rez offer itself, never asks
b:trackProgress(snap, 250)
local irq = b:selectInterrupt(snap)                -- a fight is on: the combat interrupt
local drove = b:driveInterrupt(irq, snap)
b:setGoal({ name = "camp", ctx = { phase = "select" }, advance = function() return "working" end,
            describe = function() return "camp[select]" end })
b:markPointer()
b:persistMaybe(1000)
local pointer = b:goalPointer()
b:popGoal()
b:log("stepped %d parts by hand", 8)
b:stop()
print(("rez %s | %s | goal after pop: %s | saved %s@%s"):format(answered[1]:match("accept") and "accepted" or "?",
    drove, b:activeGoal() and "some" or "none", saved[1].goal, saved[1].phase))

-- check
DOCS.check(allOk, "the stand-ins have every contract function")
DOCS.eq(#C.SPECS.nav, 6, "the nav contract names six calls")
DOCS.eq(answered[1], "rez_offer:accept", "the rez offer was accepted")
DOCS.eq(irq.name, "combat", "the fight interrupt was chosen")
DOCS.eq(pointer.goal, "camp", "the resume point names the goal")
DOCS.check(b.halted, "stop halts the brain for the session")
DOCS.has(lines[#lines], "stepped 8 parts", "b:log writes the brain's log")
DOCS.eq(require("eb.world").archetypeOf("templar"), "priest", "the world knows a subclass's archetype")
examples.expect: The stand-ins pass the contract check; the rez offer is accepted; the fight interrupt is chosen and clears; setGoal / popGoal move the stack; the resume point is handed to persist once.

examples.title: A walk the mesh has no route for fails and says why
examples.summary: EB moves a character only by walking a route on the zone's .nav mesh. A goal the mesh has no route to is not walked to - no straight line, no fallback, no swim across open water: nav.goPoint answers false with the reason in plain words, the character stays where it is, and whatever started the walk decides what to do next. The same for a zone with no mesh at all - even a six metre step.
examples.code:

local mesh = require("nav.lib.navworld").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow", reach = 20 })

-- your script

local function walk(x, y, z) return w.task(function() return nav.goPoint(x, y, z) end) end

local okFar, whyFar = walk(0, 0, 60)                          -- 60 m out, the mesh ends 20 m out: no route
print("no route: " .. tostring(whyFar))
local x, y, z = move.pos()                                    -- still where it was: nothing was walked

local reached, whyNot = walk(10, 0, 10)                       -- 14 m: the mesh reaches it

mesh.ready = function() return false, "no .nav for fixture_hollow in EB's mesh store" end

print("no mesh: " .. tostring(whyNone))

-- check
DOCS.eq(okFar, false, "a spot the mesh has no route to is not walked to")
DOCS.has(whyFar, "no route on the .nav", "and the answer says why")
DOCS.has(whyFar, "the mesh has no way to this spot", "in plain words")
DOCS.check(math.abs(x) < 1 and math.abs(z) < 1, "the character did not move: no straight run at a spot with no route")
DOCS.eq(reached, true, "a spot the mesh reaches is walked to (" .. tostring(whyNot) .. ")")
DOCS.eq(okNone, false, "with no mesh for the zone every walk fails, a 6 m step too")
DOCS.has(whyNone, "no mesh", "and says so")

DOCS.check(not move.held("forward"), "no key is held after a failed walk")

examples.title: Where the mesh joins two floors: one jump tap
examples.summary: Some routes cross a gap the mesh itself bridges with a link: a take-off corner, then the landing. The walk goes to the take-off, faces the landing, taps the jump key ONCE and walks on from the landing - the same goPoint, no other mover. A drop needs no key at all. EB never flies: a link is a jump, a climb, a drop or a door, never a flight.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the mesh is real): a mesh whose way east crosses
-- a gap at x 20..22 by a jump link - the take-off at x 19.5, the landing at x 25
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, heading = 90 } })
local mesh = require("nav.lib.navworld").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow" })
mesh.pathChained = function(fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz)
    local route
    if fx < 22 then
        route = { { x = 19.5, y = 0, z = 0, offmesh = true },       -- the take-off: a corner navd flags as a link
                  { x = 25, y = 0, z = 0, kind = 2 },               -- the landing; kind 1 drop, 2 jump, 3 door, 4 climb
                  { x = tx, y = ty, z = tz } }
    else
        route = { { x = tx, y = ty, z = tz } }
    end
    route.why, route.partial = "", false
    return route
end

-- your script
local nav, move = require("eb.nav"), require("eb.move")
local told, where = {}, nil
nav.onLink = function(kind, landing)                      -- told each time a jump or a climb key goes out
    told[#told + 1] = kind
    local x = move.pos()
    where = { x = x, off = math.abs(move.turnDelta(move.heading(), move.headingTo(landing.x, landing.z))) }
end
local ok, why = w.task(function() return nav.goPoint(40, 0, 0) end)

local taps = 0
for _, line in ipairs(w.host.log.exec) do if line == "press space" then taps = taps + 1 end end
print("jump key taps: " .. taps)
print("nav.onLink told: " .. table.concat(told, ", "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "the walk over the link arrives (" .. tostring(why) .. ")")
DOCS.near(w.self.x, 40, 2.5, "and ends on the goal")
DOCS.eq(taps, 1, "ONE tap of the jump key for the whole link")
DOCS.eq(told[1], "jump", "nav.onLink says what kind of link it was")
DOCS.check(where and where.x >= 18 and where.x <= 22, "the key went out at the take-off, not before it")
DOCS.check(where and where.off <= nav.FACE_TOL, "facing the landing")
DOCS.eq(nav.LINK_TAKEOFF, 1.5, "a take-off counts as reached within this many metres across")
DOCS.eq(nav.FLY, nil, "there is no flight mode to switch on: EB never flies")
examples.expect: The walk over a jump link arrives; the jump key was pressed exactly once, near the take-off and facing the landing; nav.onLink was told it was a jump.

examples.title: Face a point and hold a key
examples.summary: eb.move is the low-level mover the walker uses: read where you stand and face, turn to a point, hold forward, stop.

DOCS.check(not move.held("forward"), "forward is released")
DOCS.near(move.turnDelta(350, 10), 20, 1e-6, "turnDelta: the shortest signed turn")

examples.title: Ask the mesh directly
examples.summary: eb.navd is the mesh router under the walker: is this zone's mesh ready, one route, the nearest point on the mesh, the floor height, a straight line's clearance.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)

require("nav.lib.navworld").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow", loadFrames = 2, walls = { { 10, -2, 12, 2 } } })

-- your script

local ok, why = navd.ready(zone)                  -- a zone's mesh loads in the background: "loading" first

while not navd.ready(zone) do w.frame(1) end      -- in a task you would wait with eb.delay(100) instead
print("ready after loading: true")

local route = navd.path(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 24)        -- ONE route: { {x,y,z,kind}, ..., why, partial }
local nx, ny, nz = navd.nearest(5, 3, 5)          -- the closest point on the mesh
local floor = navd.height(5, 0, 5)                -- the floor under a point
local clear = navd.clear(0, 0, 0, 20, 0, 0)       -- can the straight line be walked?
print(("route %d corners; nearest %.0f,%.0f,%.0f; floor %.0f; clear to 20,0,0: %s"):format(
    #route, nx, ny, nz, floor, tostring(clear)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, false, "not ready while loading")
DOCS.eq(why, "loading", "says it is loading")
DOCS.eq(#route, 3, "a corner every 8 m")
DOCS.eq(route.partial, false, "a whole route")
DOCS.eq(ny, 0, "the nearest point is on the floor")
DOCS.eq(floor, 0, "the floor height")
DOCS.eq(clear, false, "the wall at x 10..12 blocks the straight line")
DOCS.eq(navd.meshWord(), ".nav", "EB's own mesh files")
examples.expect: The mesh reports ready after it loads, a 24 m route has 3 corners, the nearest mesh point and the floor read 0, and a wall blocks the straight line.

examples.title: Ask the mesh service directly
examples.summary: Load a zone's mesh in the background with eb.navd.ready, then ask it for one route, the nearest mesh point, a straight line's clearance and the floor height - each one request.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game: EB's own mesh extension answering over a toy flat floor (in game: the zone's mesh)
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 } })
local fake = require("nav.lib.ebnav").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow", loadFrames = 2 })

-- your script
local navd = require("eb.navd")
local frames = 0
local ok, why = navd.ready("fixture_hollow")             -- the first ask starts the load and answers at once
while not ok and frames < 20 do                            -- in a task you would eb.delay(0) between asks
    w.frame(1); frames = frames + 1
    ok, why = navd.ready("fixture_hollow")
end
print(("mesh ready after %d frames (%s)"):format(frames, tostring(navd.source())))

local route = navd.pathChained(0, 0, 0, 30, 0, 40, 1.0)   -- ONE request for the whole walk
local last = route[#route]
local mx, my, mz, off = navd.nearest(12, 5, 12)           -- snap a point onto the mesh
local clear = navd.clear(0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 0)               -- can the straight line be walked?
local floor = navd.height(3, 2, 3)
print(("route: %d corners to %.0f,%.0f; nearest floor y %.1f; straight line clear: %s"):format(
    #route, last.x, last.z, my, tostring(clear)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "the mesh came in (" .. tostring(why) .. ")")
DOCS.check(frames >= 1, "it loaded in the background, not in the first ask")
DOCS.near(last.x, 30, 0.05, "the route ends at the goal x"); DOCS.near(last.z, 40, 0.05, "and z")
DOCS.eq(route.partial, false, "a whole route")

examples.title: Open the door a route goes through
examples.summary: The zone's door lines say where its doors are and the verb each takes; nav.tryDoor clicks the known door in reach through nav.doorDeps, never a teleporter, and never the same door twice in a few seconds.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game and its mesh, with EB's nav data kept in memory (in game: EB's mesh store)
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { x = 8, y = 0, z = 5 } })
require("nav.lib.navworld").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow" })
local store = require("eb.nav_store")
store.writeText(store.storePath(store.join(store.DOORS, "fixture_hollow.txt")),
    "# fixture_hollow doors -- x y z verb name\n" ..
    "10.00\t0.00\t5.00\topen\ta fixture gate\n" ..
    "40.00\t0.00\t5.00\t\ta fixture portal\n")
store.writeText(store.storePath(store.GATES), "T\ta fixture portal\n")    -- a teleporter: never clicked by a walk

-- your script
local nav, doors = require("eb.nav"), require("eb.nav_doors")
local clicks = {}
nav.doorDeps = { click = function(door, verb, attempt)                    -- in game EB wires the game's own clicker
    clicks[#clicks + 1] = door.name .. " / " .. verb .. " / try " .. attempt
    return true
end }
for _, d in ipairs(doors.forZone("fixture_hollow")) do
    print(("door '%s' at %.0f,%.0f: verb %s (%s)"):format(d.name, d.x, d.z, tostring(d.clickVerb), d.src))
end
local trip = {}                                           -- one walk's record of the doors it tried
local ok, what = nav.tryDoor(8, 0, 5, 6, trip)
print(what)
local again, why = nav.tryDoor(8, 0, 5, 6, trip)          -- the same door moments later
print("again: " .. tostring(why))

-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "the gate was clicked")
DOCS.eq(clicks[1], "a fixture gate / open / try 1", "with its own verb, first try")
DOCS.eq(again, false, "a door clicked moments ago is not clicked again")
DOCS.has(why, "moments ago", "and the walk says why")
DOCS.eq(doors.gateKind("a fixture portal"), "T", "the portal is listed as a teleporter")
DOCS.eq(doors.vetoed("a fixture portal"), true, "so a walk never clicks it")
DOCS.eq(#clicks, 1, "one click in all")
examples.expect: The gate 2 m away is clicked with its own verb; a second try at once is refused; the teleporter is vetoed.

examples.title: Fix a door's verb on this PC
examples.summary: A door line is "x y z verb name", tab separated. Write one with eb.nav_doors.line, merge a correction into a door file's text, and keep a live fix on this PC's own layer with saveLocal - the shipped file is never touched.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: EB's nav data kept in memory (in game: the mesh store and this PC's own nav folder)
local w = DOCS.world()
require("nav.lib.navworld").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow" })

-- your script
local doors = require("eb.nav_doors")
local line = doors.line(12.5, 3, -4, "open", "a fixture hatch")
local parsed = doors.parse("# a comment\n" .. line .. "\nnot a door line\n")
local text, result = doors.merge(line .. "\n", "fixture_hollow", { x = 12.8, y = 3, z = -4, verb = "pull", name = "x" }, true)

local hatch = { x = 20, y = 0, z = 9, verb = "open", name = "a fixture hatch" }
local r1 = doors.saveLocal("fixture_hollow", hatch)                     -- a new door on this PC's layer
local r2 = doors.saveLocal("fixture_hollow", hatch)                     -- the same door again: nothing written
local r3 = doors.saveLocal("fixture_hollow", { x = 20.5, y = 0, z = 9, verb = "pull", name = "a fixture hatch" }, true)
print(("saveLocal: %s, %s, %s"):format(r1, r2, r3))
local now = doors.forZone("fixture_hollow")

-- check
DOCS.eq(line, "12.50\t3.00\t-4.00\topen\ta fixture hatch", "a door line is tab separated")
DOCS.eq(#parsed, 1, "comments and bad lines are skipped")
DOCS.eq(result, "fixed", "merging at the same spot with a new verb fixes it")
DOCS.has(text, "\tpull\t", "the merged text carries the new verb")
DOCS.eq(r1, "added", "added"); DOCS.eq(r2, "listed", "listed"); DOCS.eq(r3, "fixed", "fixed")
DOCS.eq(#now, 1, "one door for the zone")
DOCS.eq(now[1].verb, "pull", "with the corrected verb")
DOCS.eq(now[1].src, "local", "from this PC's own layer")
examples.expect: The first save adds the door, a second save at the same spot is already listed, a new verb is "fixed".

examples.title: Hold, tap and release the movement keys
examples.summary: eb.move holds a key by its role and sends a key command only when its state changes; tap presses once; the group's swim-up hold survives every stop until it is released; headings convert between EB's and the game's.

-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the keys reach the game client)

local move = require("eb.move")

local second = move.hold("forward", true)       -- already held: nothing is sent

DOCS.eq(afterStop, false, "stop() let forward go")

DOCS.eq(move.swimHeld(), false, "until it was released")

DOCS.eq(move.fromGameHeading(game90), 90, "and back")

examples.title: Plan a multi-zone trip by bell and spire, by your side
examples.summary: A trip of several hops over the game's own networks: a bell to the steppe, then a wizard spire to the isle. City bells never cross sides, so a good character's trip to an evil city is left out and the planner says why.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the travel network and the cities' sides as data (in game: EB's own travel data)
local w = DOCS.world()
require("nav.lib.navworld").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow" })
local SHORT = { ["Fixture Hollow"] = "fixture_hollow", ["Fixture Keep"] = "fixture_keep",
    ["Fixture Gloom"] = "fixture_gloom", ["Fixture Steppe"] = "fixture_steppe", ["Fixture Isle"] = "fixture_isle" }
require("eb.nav_side").load({ zones = { ["Fixture Keep"] = "good", ["Fixture Gloom"] = "evil" } }, true)

-- your script
local travel = require("eb.nav_travel")
local deps = {
    connections = function()
        return {
            bell_travel = { connects_to = { { zone_name = "Fixture Hollow" }, { zone_name = "Fixture Keep" },
                                            { zone_name = "Fixture Gloom" }, { zone_name = "Fixture Steppe" } } },
            wizard_spires_travel = { connects_to = { { zone_name = "Fixture Steppe" }, { zone_name = "Fixture Isle" } } },
        }
    end,
    displayToShort = function(name) return SHORT[name] end,
    bind = function() return "Fixture Keep" end,          -- where this character is bound: a good city
}
local mySide, from = travel.side(deps)
local hops = travel.plan(deps, "fixture_hollow", "fixture_isle")
for i, h in ipairs(hops) do print(("hop %d: %s -> %s"):format(i, travel.LABEL[h.network], h.display)) end

print("to the evil city: " .. tostring(why))

-- check
DOCS.eq(mySide, "good", "the side comes from the bind city (" .. tostring(from) .. ")")
DOCS.eq(#hops, 2, "two hops")
DOCS.eq(hops[1].network, "bell_travel", "a bell to the steppe first")
DOCS.eq(hops[2].network, "wizard_spires_travel", "then a wizard spire")
DOCS.eq(travel.shortOf(deps, "Fixture Isle"), "fixture_isle", "display names resolve to short names")
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "no route into the other side's city")
DOCS.has(why, "left out for this character's side", "and the planner says which hops it left out")

examples.title: Read a zone's pads and plan a pad trip

NW.attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow" })

    { name = "Fixture Landing", loc = { 0, 0, 0 }, network = "griffon", method = "hail", actor = "a fixture tamer",
      dest = { { to = "Fixture Ridge", land = { 300, 20, 0 }, cost = 30 } } },
    { name = "Fixture Ridge", loc = { 300, 20, 0 }, network = "griffon", method = "hail", actor = "a fixture tamer",

    { name = "Fixture Tower", loc = { 600, 40, 0 }, network = "griffon", method = "hail", actor = "a fixture tamer",

} }, fixture_vale = { zone = "fixture_vale", name = "Fixture Vale", pads = {
    { name = "Fixture Gate", loc = { 10, 0, 10 }, network = "griffon", method = "hail", dest = {} },
} } })

examples.title: Catch health lost out of combat and back out
examples.summary: Run the walker's hazard watch over your own samples: health falls 15 points in three seconds with no fight on, the watch calls it a hazard, and the way back to the last safe spot is the track walked in reverse.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game a walk samples you twice a second)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local hazard = require("eb.nav_hazard")
local mon = hazard.new()
local hp = { 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 98, 94, 90, 85 }          -- health, one sample every 500 ms while walking east
local hz
for i, h in ipairs(hp) do
    local t = 10000 + i * 500
    hazard.sample(mon, { t = t, x = i * 2, y = 0, z = 0, hp = h, swim = false, combat = false, lava = false })
    hz = hz or hazard.check(mon, t, { lethalZone = false })
end
print("hazard: " .. tostring(hz and hz.what))
local losing, was = hazard.losing(mon.track, 10000 + #hp * 500, hp[#hp])
local safe, k = hazard.safeSpot(mon, hz.x, hz.z, hz.was)
local back = hazard.wayBack(mon, k)
print(("back out to %.0f,%.0f over %d points"):format(safe.x, safe.z, #back))

-- check
DOCS.check(hz ~= nil, "the watch called a hazard")
DOCS.eq(losing, true, "the losing rule on its own agrees")
DOCS.eq(was, 100, "the most health this stretch held")
DOCS.check(hz.x - safe.x >= hazard.BACK, "the safe spot is at least 6 m back")
DOCS.check(safe.hp >= hz.was - 2, "and you were unhurt there")
DOCS.eq(back[#back].x, safe.x, "the way back ends at the safe spot")
examples.expect: The losing rule fires; the safe spot is the last dry, unhurt sample at least 6 m back; the way back leads to it.

examples.title: Never swim where the liquid kills
examples.summary: The zones whose liquid kills are a list you can set; swimming in one is a hazard at once, unless the walk says it has to go in (a quest step) with allowLethal.

-- your script
local hazard = require("eb.nav_hazard")
hazard.setLethalZones("fixture_magma, fixture_cinders")

end

examples.title: Where EB's nav data lives
examples.summary: Two roots: the mesh store that ships with EB (read-only at run time) and this PC's own nav data. Point both at a files host of your own - here one kept in memory - and read and write nav data through the one door.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS); the files host here keeps everything in memory
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local store = require("eb.nav_store")
store.configure({ root = "store", localRoot = "local", fs = require("ebkit.files").memory({}) })

local doc = store.readJson(store.localPath(store.PLACES))
local missing, why = store.readJson(store.storePath(store.SIDES))

-- check
DOCS.eq(fixesFile, "store\\fixes\\mesh_fixes.json", "a shipped file sits under the mesh store")
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "the JSON was written")
DOCS.eq(doc.blacklist[1].zone, "fixture_hollow", "and reads back as plain tables")
DOCS.eq(missing, nil, "a file that is not there answers nil")
DOCS.check(why ~= nil, "with a reason")

examples.title: Remember what a bell's map offers
examples.summary: A bell's travel map may offer less than the network on file, and a city bell offers its reader's own side only. Keep each ring in a bell map memory per side, ask it before ringing, and judge an open map read by read.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game EB keeps this memory in its own file)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local bellmaps = require("eb.nav_bellmaps")
local s = bellmaps.new()
bellmaps.recordSide(s, "Fixture Server", "Fixturae", "good", 1000)    -- the side her guild hall globe showed her
bellmaps.record(s, { server = "Fixture Server", zone = "fixture_port", bell = "bell", bind = "side:good",
    labels = { "Fixture Hollow", "Fixture Steppe" }, complete = true, asked = "Fixture Isle", now = 1000 })
local ctx = { server = "Fixture Server", zone = "fixture_port", me = "Fixturae", now = 5000 }

-- an open map, read twice (two reads that agree make a whole map)

bellmaps.mapShown(m, 100)
bellmaps.addRead(m, { "Fixture Hollow", "Fixture Steppe" }, 900)
bellmaps.addRead(m, { "Fixture Hollow", "Fixture Steppe" }, 1700)

-- check

DOCS.eq(isle, "lacks", "a whole map without the isle lacks it")
DOCS.eq(stranger, "unknown", "a character of no known side gets no verdict: ring and read")
DOCS.eq(bellmaps.judge(m, "Fixture Steppe", 4000), "offered", "the open map offers the steppe")
DOCS.eq(bellmaps.judge(m, "Fixture Isle", 4000), "miss", "and is a miss for the isle")

examples.title: Swim corners, the water's surface and no dive in a fight
examples.summary: The swim corner decision is pure: climb toward a higher corner, dive toward a lower one - but never dive while a fight is on. The mesh's liquid surface says whether you are under water. A goal under the surface that the mesh has no route to is NOT swum to: the walk fails, saying the spot is in open water the mesh does not reach.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: EB's mesh extension over a toy lake whose surface stands 1 m over the floor east of x = 60
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { x = 70, y = -2, z = 0 } })
require("nav.lib.ebnav").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow", lavaAt = 1e9 })
local navd = require("eb.navd")
navd.ready("fixture_hollow"); w.frame(1); navd.ready("fixture_hollow")

-- your script
local swim, swimout, nav = require("eb.nav_swim"), require("eb.nav_swimout"), require("eb.nav")
local corner = { px = 70, py = -2, pz = 0, wx = 80, wy = -12, wz = 0, surfaceY = 1 }
local calm = swim.want(corner)                                   -- no fight: dive toward the lower corner
corner.inCombat = true
local fight = swim.want(corner)                                  -- a fight on: hold at the surface
print("dive in a fight: " .. tostring(fight.reason))
nav.swimDeps = { surfaceY = function() return 1 end, swimming = true }    -- the reads, swapped for this example
local surface = swim.surfaceY(nav, 70, -2, 0)
local inWater = swim.swimming(nav, 70, -2, 0)
local openWater = swimout.inOpenWater(nav, 70, -2, 0, 78, -6, 4)     -- words only: it moves nothing
nav.swimDeps = nil

-- check
DOCS.eq(calm.dive, true, "a corner 10 m below is a dive")
DOCS.eq(calm.forward, true, "and the walk swims on toward it")
DOCS.eq(fight.hold, true, "the same dive holds while a fight is on")
DOCS.eq(surface, 1, "the water's surface is 1 m up")
DOCS.eq(inWater, true, "you are in the water")
DOCS.eq(openWater, true, "a goal under the water the mesh does not reach is said as such - never swum to straight")
examples.expect: A corner below is a dive; the same dive in a fight holds; you are under the surface; a goal under the water is said to be in open water the mesh does not reach - and never swum to straight.

examples.title: One engine step, one decision
examples.summary: Build the combat engine over the game layer's combat shim and a small cast stack, and step it: each step casts the highest-priority entry that is ready.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Cleave", "Fixture Strike", "Fixture Smash" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 10)
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute" })
FW.target(w, 200)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local Combat = require("eb.combat")
local stack = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = {      -- the entry shape the engine runs
    { name = "Fixture Cleave", ability = "Fixture Cleave", group = "dps", tags = "AE", priority = 99, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 97, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Smash",  ability = "Fixture Smash",  group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 95, gates = {} },
} })
local engine = Combat.new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = stack })

local picks = {}
for i = 1, 3 do
    local d = engine:step()                   -- ONE decision: a cast it sent, or a hold with a reason
    print(("step %d: %s %s (%s)"):format(i, tostring(d.kind), tostring(d.ability), tostring(d.reason)))
    picks[i] = d.ability
    w.runFor(500)                              -- EB steps the engine 4 times a second; a quick art goes out at most every half second
end

-- check
DOCS.eq(picks[1], "Fixture Cleave", "highest priority first")
DOCS.eq(picks[2], "Fixture Strike", "the next once the first is on recast")
DOCS.eq(picks[3], "Fixture Smash", "and the one after")
DOCS.eq(#FW.casts(w), 3, "each decision was sent to the game")
examples.expect: Step 1 casts the AE (priority 99); with it on recast step 2 casts the next art (97), step 3 the one after (95).

examples.title: Guards are never pulled or splashed
examples.summary: Ask the combat plane whether a target is winnable before you pull: a guard is refused. With a guard standing in AE reach of your fight, the engine skips its AE and casts a single-target art instead.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Cleave", "Fixture Strike" })
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute", distance = 6 })
w.addActor({ id = 210, name = "a fixture guard", type = "NPC", distance = 12 })   -- standing near, not in the fight
FW.target(w, 200)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local P = require("eb.platform")
local combat = require("eb.app.combat").new({ game = game, clock = P.now })   -- what EB's start builds once per box
combat.holder.rebind({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Cleave", ability = "Fixture Cleave", group = "dps", tags = "AE", priority = 99, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 97, gates = {} } } })

for _, name in ipairs({ "a fixture guard", "a fixture brute" }) do
    local ok, why = combat.facade.brain.isWinnable(name)      -- ask before any pull
    print(("%s: %s %s"):format(name, tostring(ok), tostring(why)))
end
local d = combat.engine:step()
print(("cast %s at %s"):format(tostring(d.ability), tostring(d.target)))

-- check

DOCS.eq(okG, false, "a guard is never winnable")
DOCS.eq(whyG, "guard", "and the reason says so")
DOCS.eq((combat.facade.brain.isWinnable("a fixture brute")), true, "a plain mob is fine")
DOCS.eq(d.ability, "Fixture Strike", "the AE is vetoed with a guard in reach")
DOCS.eq(#w.world.casts, 1, "one cast went out")
DOCS.eq(w.world.casts[1].target, 200, "...at the brute")

examples.title: Change combat for one zone
examples.summary: Register an override for a zone (no AE in the vault); it applies only while the context matches, and needs no change to the cast stack.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Cleave", "Fixture Strike" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 10)                              -- the game shows each cast as taken: the ability goes on its reuse
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute" })
FW.target(w, 200)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = { entries = function() return {
    { name = "Fixture Cleave", ability = "Fixture Cleave", group = "dps", tags = "AE", priority = 99, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 97, gates = {} },
} end } })
engine:addOverride({ name = "vault - no AE", priority = 10, match = { zone = "fixture_vault" },
                     directives = { disableAE = true } })

engine:setContext({ zone = "fixture_vault" })       -- an instance script sets this when it zones in
local inside = engine:step()                        -- the AE is ready, and the override still leaves it out
local ov = engine:activeOverride()
w.runFor(500)                                       -- a quick art goes out at most every half second
engine:setContext({ zone = "" })                    -- and again when it zones out
local outside = engine:step()
print(("outside: %s; in the vault: %s (override: %s)"):format(outside.ability, inside.ability, ov and ov.name))

-- check
DOCS.eq(outside.ability, "Fixture Cleave", "no override outside the vault")
DOCS.eq(inside.ability, "Fixture Strike", "the AE is skipped in the vault")
DOCS.eq(ov and ov.name, "vault - no AE", "the override in force")
DOCS.eq(engine:resolveOverride({}).disableAE, nil, "out of the vault again: back to the defaults")

examples.title: Readiness costs one read a frame
examples.summary: The abilities you ask about are remembered as a hot set: on the next frame one batched read answers all of them, and asking again in the same frame is free.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
local names = { "Fixture Art 1", "Fixture Art 2", "Fixture Art 3", "Fixture Art 4", "Fixture Art 5" }
FW.book(w, names)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
for _, n in ipairs(names) do game.AbilityReady(n) end    -- the first frame learns which abilities you care about
w.frame(1)
game.BeginTick()                                          -- a new frame (EB's pulse opens one every frame)
for _, n in ipairs(names) do game.AbilityReady(n) end
local reads, shared = game.ReadyStats()
print(("%d asks: %d read, %d from the frame's cache"):format(#names, reads, shared))

-- check
DOCS.eq(reads, 1, "one batched read for the whole hot set")
DOCS.eq(shared, 4, "the rest answer from this frame's cache")

examples.title: Why does the engine not cast that?
examples.summary: Ask the engine which gate holds each entry of your stack right now - on recast, below its power line, its tag switched off, its target-health window not reached - then send a cast of your own through the engine's one send.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { powerPct = 30 } })
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Finisher", "Fixture Smash", "Fixture Nuke", "Fixture Cleave", "Fixture Strike" })
FW.recast(w, "Fixture Smash", 10)                         -- offline: it is on recast in the game
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute", healthPct = 80 })
FW.target(w, 200)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local Combat = require("eb.combat")
local stack = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Finisher", ability = "Fixture Finisher", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 99,
      gates = { useBelowTargetHP = 20 } },                               -- only under 20% target health
    { name = "Fixture Smash",  ability = "Fixture Smash",  group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 98, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Nuke",   ability = "Fixture Nuke",   group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 97,
      gates = { useAbovePower = 50 } },                                  -- only above 50% of your power
    { name = "Fixture Cleave", ability = "Fixture Cleave", group = "dps", tags = "AE", priority = 96, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 90, gates = {} },
} })
local engine = Combat.new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = stack })
engine:toggle("AE", false)                                 -- AE switched off for this pull

-- what a step does before its categories: the stack, one world read, the mob it would fight
engine:loadStack()
local ctx = engine:snapshot()
ctx.mob = engine:selectTarget(ctx)
local held = {}
for _, e in ipairs(stack.entries()) do
    local why = engine:passesGate(e, ctx, ctx.mob)         -- nil = it would cast now
    held[e.name] = why or "would cast"
    print(("%s held by %s"):format(e.name, why or "nothing: would cast"))
end

-- a cast of your own through the engine's one send (the same path its own decisions take)
local mine = Combat.U.decision("dps", stack.get("Fixture Strike"), "Target", "by hand")
local sent = engine:cast(mine)

-- check
DOCS.eq(held["Fixture Finisher"], "TargetHPBelow", "the target is not low enough yet")
DOCS.eq(held["Fixture Smash"], "Ready", "on recast: the game says it is not ready")
DOCS.eq(held["Fixture Nuke"], "PowerAbove", "you are under its power line")
DOCS.eq(held["Fixture Cleave"], "Toggled", "its AE tag is switched off")
DOCS.eq(held["Fixture Strike"], "would cast", "the one that passes every gate")
DOCS.eq(sent, true, "the hand-made decision was sent")
DOCS.eq(FW.casts(w)[1], "Fixture Strike", "and reached the game")
examples.expect: Each entry names the gate that holds it (TargetHPBelow, Ready, PowerAbove, Toggled) or "would cast"; the hand-made decision is sent to the game.

examples.title: Give up a fight that cannot be won
examples.summary: The engine measures each fight's kill time from two health readings; past the grace window, a mob it picked itself whose kill time stays over the limit is benched for the session. What the tank or you fight (and an ordered kill) is never given up - a training dummy is there to be hit. An override caps both for a hard zone.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture colossus", healthPct = 100 })                    -- on you; nobody targeted it
FW.mob(w, { id = 201, name = "a fixture training dummy", healthPct = 100, distance = 4 })
FW.target(w, 201)                                                                       -- you have the dummy targeted

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local Combat = require("eb.combat")
local engine = Combat.new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = { entries = function() return {} end } })
engine:setOverride({ ttkGrace = 1000, ttkMax = 2000 })    -- a hard zone: judge after 1 s, give up past 2 s

local function mobIn(ctx, id) for _, m in ipairs(ctx.hostiles) do if m.id == id then return m end end end
local ctx = engine:snapshot()
engine.ov = engine:resolveOverride(ctx)                    -- what a step does first
local grace, cap = engine:ttkGrace(), engine:ttkMax()
local first = engine:winnable(ctx, mobIn(ctx, 200))        -- the first reading only starts the measure

w.runFor(1500)                                             -- the fights go on; no health moves
ctx = engine:snapshot()
local ok, why = engine:winnable(ctx, mobIn(ctx, 200))
print("gave up: " .. tostring(why))
local benched = engine:isTooStrong("a fixture colossus")
local dummy = engine:winnable(ctx, ctx.target)             -- your own target: never given up
engine:forgetStrong()                                      -- after a gear upgrade, say

local eta = Combat.killEta(100, 60, 20000)                 -- lost 40% in 20 s: 60% left = 30 s more

-- check
DOCS.eq(grace, 1000, "the override's grace window")
DOCS.eq(cap, 2000, "the override's give-up limit")
DOCS.eq(first, true, "the first reading keeps fighting")
DOCS.eq(ok, false, "no progress past the grace window: given up")
DOCS.eq(why, "tooStrong", "with the reason")
DOCS.eq(benched, true, "and benched for the session")
DOCS.eq(dummy, true, "the dummy you targeted is still fought")
DOCS.eq(engine:isTooStrong("a fixture colossus"), false, "until forgetStrong()")
DOCS.eq(eta, 30000, "the kill time two readings imply")
examples.expect: With a 1-second grace and a 2-second cap, a mob EB picked whose health never moves is given up ("tooStrong") and benched until forgetStrong(); the dummy you targeted is still fought; the kill time of a mob that does lose health is measured.

examples.title: Timed tags and a pre-cast
examples.summary: An allow row casts only while its tag is raised, an embargo row is held while its tag is raised, and a pre-cast goes out right before the ability it belongs to - all on the engine's own clock.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Burn", "Fixture Slow", "Fixture Strike", "Fixture Focus" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 10)                                      -- the game shows each cast as taken: the ability goes on its reuse
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute" })
FW.target(w, 200)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local stack = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Burn", ability = "Fixture Burn", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 99, gates = {},
      allowTag = "BURN" },                                   -- casts only while BURN is raised
    { name = "Fixture Slow", ability = "Fixture Slow", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 98, gates = {},
      embargoTag = "SLOW" },                                 -- held while SLOW is raised
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 90, gates = {},
      precast = "Fixture Focus" },                           -- cast Fixture Focus right before it
} })
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = stack })
local burn, slow = stack.get("Fixture Burn"), stack.get("Fixture Slow")

local before = engine:timedTagFail(burn)                   -- "ATagOff": BURN is not raised
engine:raiseTag("SLOW", 5)                                 -- another box asked everyone to hold the slow
local slowHeld = engine:timedTagFail(slow)
engine:tagFor("BURN", 2, "Allow")                          -- open the burn rows for 2 seconds
local d1 = engine:step()                                   -- the burn goes out
w.runFor(2100)
local d2 = engine:step()                                   -- BURN has ended (the engine's timer); Strike's pre-cast first
w.runFor(500)                                              -- a quick art goes out at most every half second
local d3 = engine:step()                                   -- then Strike itself
local after = engine:timedTagFail(burn)
local pre = engine:precastFor("Fixture Strike", stack.get("Fixture Strike"))
print("casts: " .. table.concat(FW.casts(w), ", "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(before, "ATagOff", "an allow row waits for its tag")
DOCS.eq(slowHeld, "Embargoed", "an embargo row is held while its tag is raised")
DOCS.eq(d1.ability, "Fixture Burn", "the allow row casts while its tag is raised")
DOCS.eq(d2.kind, "precast", "the pre-cast goes first")
DOCS.eq(d2.ability, "Fixture Focus", "it is the ability the entry names")
DOCS.eq(d3.ability, "Fixture Strike", "then the main ability")
DOCS.eq(after, "ATagOff", "the burn waits again once its window ended")
DOCS.eq(engine:tagLive("SLOW"), true, "SLOW is still raised (5 seconds)")
DOCS.eq(pre, "Fixture Focus", "the pre-cast the engine looks up")
examples.expect: The burn row waits for its tag, casts while it is raised for 2 seconds, and waits again after; the slow row stays held while SLOW is raised; Fixture Focus goes out right before Fixture Strike.

examples.title: Strip a named's buff
examples.summary: engine:dispel strips a mob's beneficial buff on cue with the stack's dispel art. The automatic dispel category also needs the game's "has a buff to strip" read; a script supplies it here, and setDispelOn(false) stops it.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Purge", "Fixture Strike" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 2)                                       -- the game shows each cast as taken: the ability goes on its reuse
FW.mob(w, { id = 300, name = "Overseer of Fixtures", type = "NamedNPC" })
FW.target(w, 300)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local Combat = require("eb.combat")
local rows = { entries = function() return {
    { name = "Fixture Purge",  ability = "Fixture Purge",  group = "dps", tags = "DISPEL", priority = 10, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA",     priority = 90, gates = {} },
} end }
local engine = Combat.new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = rows })

local status = engine:dispel({ mob = "Overseer" })         -- on cue: strip it now
print("dispel: " .. tostring(status))
local noArt = Combat.new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = { entries = function() return {} end } }):dispel()

-- the automatic category: it needs the game to say the mob has something to strip
local shim = game.combatShim()
shim.dispellable = function(id) return id == 300 end      -- offline: that read (EB for InnerSpace has none yet)
local auto = Combat.new({ shim = shim, stacks = rows })
auto:loadStack()
w.runFor(2500)                                             -- the first dispel's recast has run out
local art = auto:dispelArt()
local d = auto:step()
auto:setDispelOn(false)
w.runFor(500)                                              -- a quick art goes out at most every half second
local d2 = auto:step()

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "ok", "the on-cue dispel was sent")
DOCS.eq(FW.casts(w)[1], "Fixture Purge", "with the dispel art")
DOCS.eq(noArt, "no-dispel-art", "a stack without one says so and casts nothing")
DOCS.eq(art.ability, "Fixture Purge", "the art tagged DISPEL")
DOCS.eq(d.kind, "dispel", "the automatic dispel goes ahead of the rotation")
DOCS.eq(d2.ability, "Fixture Strike", "switched off: the rotation runs")
examples.expect: The on-cue dispel goes out at the named; without a dispel art it says so; the automatic category casts the dispel ahead of the rotation, until it is switched off.

examples.title: The kill-first list, rules and stragglers
examples.summary: Give the engine a kill-first list with a health rule, see how it ranks and filters the mobs in the fight, hold it for a moment, hand it a straggler, and ask for the trash first.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.mob(w, { id = 201, name = "a fixture scout", healthPct = 30, distance = 8 })
FW.mob(w, { id = 202, name = "a fixture brute", healthPct = 90, distance = 6 })
FW.mob(w, { id = 203, name = "Overseer of Fixtures", type = "NamedNPC", distance = 3 })
FW.mob(w, { id = 204, name = "a fixture straggler", distance = 12 })

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = { entries = function() return {} end } })
engine:setAutoTarget({ { name = "a fixture scout", hp = 50 }, "a fixture brute" })   -- order = priority

local ctx = engine:snapshot()
local scout = engine:findHostile("scout")
local rule, rank = engine:killListMatch(scout)                    -- its row on the list, and its place
local scoutOk = engine:eligibleMob(ctx, scout, rule)              -- under its 50% rule: not now
local pick = engine:scanAutoTarget(ctx)
print("kill list picks: " .. tostring(pick and pick.name))

engine:suppressAutoTarget("waiting for the tank")                 -- hold the list for a reason of your own
local held = engine:autoTargetSuppressed()
local fallback = engine:selectTarget(ctx)                         -- held: the nearest hostile in the fight
engine:releaseAutoTarget("waiting for the tank")

engine:addTarget(204, "a fixture straggler")                      -- a mob nobody is fighting: take it
local straggler = engine:pickStraggler(ctx)
local has = engine:hasStragglers()
engine:clearStragglers()

local trash = engine:pickTrashFirst(ctx)                          -- what an override's trashFirst prefers
local rows = engine:normalizeKillList({ "A Fixture Brute" })
local eff = engine:effAutoTarget()

-- check
DOCS.eq(rank, 1, "the scout is first on the list")
DOCS.eq(scoutOk, false, "but its 50% rule keeps it out at 30% health")
DOCS.eq(pick.name, "a fixture brute", "so the list picks the brute")
DOCS.eq(held, true, "the list can be held")
DOCS.eq(fallback.name, "Overseer of Fixtures", "and selection falls back to the nearest hostile")
DOCS.eq(engine:autoTargetSuppressed(), false, "released again")
DOCS.eq(straggler and straggler.id, 204, "a handed-over straggler is engaged")
DOCS.eq(has, true, "while it is held")
DOCS.eq(engine:hasStragglers(), false, "until cleared")
DOCS.eq(trash.name, "a fixture brute", "trash first: the nearest eligible non-named")
DOCS.eq(rows[1].name, "a fixture brute", "list rows are read lower case")
DOCS.eq(eff.enabled, true, "a non-empty list switched auto-target on")
examples.expect: The scout is first on the list but skipped while under 50% health, so the brute is picked; a held list falls back to the nearest hostile; a straggler is engaged when handed over; trash-first prefers a non-named.

examples.title: The engine's small helpers
examples.summary: require("eb.combat").U holds the pure helpers the engine uses - tag lists, kill time, valid mobs, AE entries, the encounter count, decisions, the lowest member, word matches, ability-line keys and safe optional calls.
examples.code:
-- your script (pure Lua: no game needed)
local U = require("eb.combat").U

local tags = U.splitTags(" ae; Dumbfire ;")
local eta = U.killEta(100, 75, 10000)                       -- lost 25% in 10 s: 75% left = 30 s
local stalled = U.killEta(80, 80, 10000)                    -- nothing came off: math.huge
local live = U.validMob({ id = 7, isNPC = true, healthPct = 50 })
local corpse = U.validMob({ id = 7, isNPC = true, healthPct = 0 })
local ae = U.isAE({ tags = "CA;AE" })
local splash = U.isAE({ tags = "CA", gates = { minEncounterSize = 3 } })
local count = U.mobCount({ engagedCount = 4 }, { encounterSize = 2 })
local d = U.decision("dps", { ability = "Fixture Strike" }, "Target", "by hand")
local who, low = U.lowestOf({ { name = "Member1", healthPct = 70 }, { name = "Member2", healthPct = 35 } })
local guardish = U.anyWord("Captain of the Gate Watchman", { "watchman", "sentry" })
local key = U.lineKey("Fixture Blast III")
local present = U.fn({ ping = function() return "pong" end }, "ping")
local answer = U.call({ ping = function(x) return x * 2 end }, "ping", 21)
local absent = U.call({}, "missing")
print("helpers ok")

-- check
DOCS.eq(table.concat(tags, ","), "AE,DUMBFIRE", "tags trimmed and upper case")
DOCS.eq(eta, 30000, "the kill time from two readings")
DOCS.eq(stalled, math.huge, "no progress: never")
DOCS.eq(live, true, "a living NPC with an id")
DOCS.eq(corpse, false, "not a corpse")
DOCS.eq(ae, true, "an AE-tagged entry")
DOCS.eq(splash, true, "an encounter-size gate over 1 counts as AE")
DOCS.eq(count, 4, "the encounter as the # gate counts it")
DOCS.eq(d.ability, "Fixture Strike", "a decision carries its entry's ability")
DOCS.eq(who.name, "Member2", "the member who needs a heal most")
DOCS.eq(low, 35, "and their health")
DOCS.eq(guardish, true, "a word match on part of the text")
DOCS.eq(key, "fixture blast", "the rank numeral dropped")
DOCS.check(type(present) == "function", "an optional function that is there")
DOCS.eq(answer, 42, "called safely")
DOCS.eq(absent, nil, "and nil for one that is not")

examples.title: The combat plane, its facade and the follower view
examples.summary: Build the combat plane the way EB does, see its one step throttle, record an encounter's damage rules on the facade, and run an instance's pull / clear / engage through the follower-aware view.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Strike" })
local brute = FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute" })
FW.target(w, 200)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local AppCombat = require("eb.app.combat")
local plane = AppCombat.new({ game = game, clock = w.P.now, sleep = function(ms) eb.delay(ms) end })
plane.holder.rebind({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 90, gates = {} } } })

local a = plane.engine:step()
local b = plane.engine:step()                               -- the same moment: the same decision, no second cast

local facade = require("eb.wiring.combat_facade").new({ engine = plane.engine, game = game })
local rulesBefore = facade.ic.damageSource()
facade.ic.setRules("burst")
local rulesNow = facade.ic.damageSource()

local follower = plane.icView({ lead = function() return false end })   -- this box is not the one that pulls
local okP, pulled = follower.pull("a fixture brute")
local okC, cleared = follower.clearArea()
local t0 = w.now()                                          -- offline: the lead kills the brute a second from now
w.world.onFrame = function() if w.now() - t0 > 1000 then brute.healthPct, brute.isDead = 0, true end end
local engaged = w.task(function()                           -- a follower's engage waits: inside a task
    local ok, note = follower.engage("a fixture brute", { ms = 10000 })
    return note
end, 20000)
print("follower: " .. pulled .. " | " .. tostring(engaged))

local none, why = AppCombat.findStack({ files = { read = function() return nil end, list = function() return {} end },
                                       dirs = {}, char = "Fixturae" })

-- check
DOCS.check(a == b, "two steps in one moment answer one decision")
DOCS.eq(#FW.casts(w), 1, "and only one cast went out")
DOCS.eq(rulesBefore, "default", "the facade's damage rules start as default")
DOCS.eq(rulesNow, "burst", "and record what the encounter set")
DOCS.eq(pulled, "the lead pulls a fixture brute", "a follower never pulls")
DOCS.eq(cleared, "the lead clears the area", "nor clears an area on its own")
DOCS.eq(engaged, "assisting on a fixture brute: down", "its engage waited for the lead's kill")
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "no profile folder known: no stack")
DOCS.check(type(why) == "string" and #why > 0, "and a plain reason")

examples.title: Heal whoever fell furthest
examples.summary: The engine weighs every heal entry by how far its member has fallen; an EMERGENCY heal jumps the queue. One step heals the lowest member with the heaviest choice.

end

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local stack = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Mend", ability = "Fixture Mend", group = "heal", target = "AllParty", priority = 50,
      gates = { useBelowTargetHP = 80 } },                          -- anyone under 80%
    { name = "Fixture Rescue", ability = "Fixture Rescue", group = "heal", target = "AllParty", priority = 40,
      tags = "EMERGENCY", gates = { useBelowTargetHP = 50 } },      -- anyone under 50%, ahead of every other heal
} })

engine:loadStack()
local ctx = engine:snapshot()

-- check
DOCS.eq(plain.target.name, "Member2", "the plain heal would go to the lowest member")
DOCS.eq(plain.weight, 80, "weight 20 + 60 fallen")
DOCS.eq(urgent.weight, 1080, "the emergency heal adds 1000")
DOCS.eq(d.kind, "heal", "a heal decision")
DOCS.eq(d.ability, "Fixture Rescue", "the heaviest choice wins")
DOCS.eq(d.reason, "Member2 at 40%", "on the member who fell furthest")
DOCS.eq(FW.casts(w)[1], "Fixture Rescue", "sent to the game")

examples.title: A group heal waits for enough hurt members
examples.summary: A group heal entry gated on "2 members under 70%" stays quiet for one scratch and fires once two members are under the line - on the lowest of them.
examples.code:

local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")

examples.summary: A rez entry looks among the dead; once everyone is up, a power heal goes to the member under its power line, lowest first. On EB for InnerSpace the engine's group rows carry no power reading yet, so the script adds it.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)

local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Revive", "Fixture Channel" })

local m2 = w.addMember({ name = "Member2", id = 12, class = "wizard", healthPct = 0, powerPct = 0, inZone = true,
                         isDead = true })

    w.addActor({ id = id, name = name, type = "PC", isNPC = false, distance = 5 })
end

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local shim = game.combatShim()
local groupRows = shim.group
function shim.group()                         -- add each member's power from game.Group() (read in the same frame)
    local rows, power = groupRows(), {}
    for _, m in ipairs(game.Group()) do power[m.id] = m.powerPct end
    for _, r in ipairs(rows) do r.powerPct = r.powerPct or power[r.id] end
    return rows
end
local revive = { name = "Fixture Revive", ability = "Fixture Revive", group = "cure", tags = "REZ",
                 target = "AllParty", priority = 60, gates = {} }
local channel = { name = "Fixture Channel", ability = "Fixture Channel", group = "cure", tags = "POWER_HEAL",
                  target = "AllParty", priority = 50, gates = { belowPower = 50 } }
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = shim,
    stacks = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = { revive, channel } }) })

local d1 = engine:step()                                          -- the rez category comes before the power heals
m2.healthPct, m2.isDead, m2.powerPct = 40, false, 20              -- offline: Member2 accepts the rez
w.runFor(500)                                                     -- a quick art goes out at most every half second
local low = engine:needPower(engine:snapshot().group, channel)    -- who is under the power line, lowest first
local d2 = engine:step()
print("rez then power: " .. tostring(d1.ability) .. ", " .. tostring(d2.ability))

-- check
DOCS.eq(d1.kind, "rez", "a dead member is rezzed first")
DOCS.eq(d1.target, 12, "Member2")
DOCS.eq(low[1].name, "Member2", "after the rez Member2 is the lowest on power (20%)")
DOCS.eq(low[2].name, "Member1", "then Member1 (30%)")
DOCS.eq(#low, 2, "Member3 at 85% is not under the line")
DOCS.eq(d2.kind, "power", "then the power heal")
DOCS.eq(d2.target, 12, "on the lowest")

examples.title: Mez the adds, renew before it breaks
examples.summary: With a mez art in the stack the engine mezzes the adds in the mez list's order - never the mob being killed, never a guard, never an epic - and renews a mez that has 10 seconds or less left.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Mesmerize", "Fixture Strike" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 1)                                                       -- the game shows each cast as taken: the art goes on a second's reuse
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute", distance = 4 })            -- the mob being killed
FW.mob(w, { id = 201, name = "a fixture imp", distance = 9 })
FW.mob(w, { id = 202, name = "a fixture hound", distance = 5 })
FW.mob(w, { id = 203, name = "a fixture sentry", distance = 7 })           -- a guard: never touched
FW.mob(w, { id = 204, name = "a fixture behemoth", isEpic = true, distance = 6 })
FW.target(w, 200)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local stack = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Mesmerize", ability = "Fixture Mesmerize", group = "dps", tags = "MEZ", priority = 50, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 90, gates = {} },
} })
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = stack })
engine:setMezList({ "imp" })                                                -- the imp first, whatever is nearer

-- a mez is cast at the add by its id, which leaves the add targeted: point the target back at the kill mob after it
local function stepKeepingTarget(killId)
    local d = engine:step()
    if d.kind == "mez" then game.TargetActor(killId) end
    return d
end

-- EB steps the engine 4 times a second: the next step sees that the game took the cast. The same art goes at the next
-- add only once its reuse is over (a second here), so the clock runs on before the step after that.
local function afterCast()
    w.runFor(250); engine:step()
    w.runFor(1000)
end

local log = {}
local d1 = stepKeepingTarget(200); log[1] = d1.reason
w.addMaintained({ name = "Fixture Mesmerize", targetId = 201, duration = 30 })   -- offline: the imp is mezzed
afterCast()
local d2 = stepKeepingTarget(200); log[2] = d2.reason
w.addMaintained({ name = "Fixture Mesmerize", targetId = 202, duration = 30 })
w.world.maintained[1].duration = 6                                          -- the imp's mez runs low
afterCast()
local d3 = stepKeepingTarget(200); log[3] = d3.reason
print("mez order: " .. table.concat(log, " | "))

engine:loadStack()
local arts = engine:mezEntries()
local rankImp, rankHound = engine:mezRank({ name = "a fixture imp" }), engine:mezRank({ name = "a fixture hound" })
local epic = engine:mezImmune({ id = 204, isEpic = true })

-- check
DOCS.eq(d1.kind, "mez", "an add needs a mez before the rotation")
DOCS.eq(d1.target, 201, "the imp first: it is first on the mez list")
DOCS.eq(d2.target, 202, "then the hound")
DOCS.eq(d3.reason, "renew mez a fixture imp", "a mez with 6 seconds left is renewed")
DOCS.eq(#arts, 1, "the mez arts in the stack")
DOCS.eq(rankImp, 1, "the imp's place on the list")
DOCS.eq(rankHound, 2, "an add not on the list comes after it")
DOCS.eq(epic, true, "an epic is treated as immune")
DOCS.check(d1.target ~= 203 and d2.target ~= 203 and d3.target ~= 203, "the guard was never mezzed")
examples.expect: The imp is mezzed first (first on the mez list), then the hound; the imp's mez is renewed once it runs low.

examples.title: Open and advance a heroic opportunity
examples.summary: With no wheel up the engine opens a heroic opportunity with the stack's opener; with your wheel up it casts the art whose icon the wheel needs, holds rotation arts that would disturb it, and never uses an excluded ability.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Chance", "Fixture Smash", "Fixture Strike" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 10)                         -- the game shows each cast as taken: the ability goes on its reuse
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute" })
FW.target(w, 200)
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local shim = game.combatShim()
local wheel = { visible = false }
shim.hoState = function() return wheel end    -- offline: the wheel read (EB for InnerSpace does not provide it yet)

-- your script
local stack = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Chance", ability = "Fixture Chance", group = "dps", tags = "HO_STARTER", priority = 10, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Smash",  ability = "Fixture Smash",  group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 95, gates = {}, hoIcon = 9 },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 90, gates = {}, hoIcon = 7 },
} })
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = shim, stacks = stack })

local d1 = engine:step()                                  -- no wheel: open one
wheel = { visible = true, started = true, mine = true, needIcon = 9 }    -- offline: your wheel is up and needs icon 9
w.runFor(500)                                         -- a quick art goes out at most every half second
local d2 = engine:step()                                  -- advance it with the matching art
print("heroic: " .. d1.reason .. ", " .. d2.reason)

local strikeHeld = engine:hoDisturbs(stack.get("Fixture Strike"))   -- icon 7 would disturb the running wheel
local smashOk = engine:hoDisturbs(stack.get("Fixture Smash"))       -- the needed icon may pass
engine:setHOExcludes({ "Fixture Smash" })
local excluded = engine:hoExcluded("fixture smash")
local advancer = engine:hoAdvancer(engine:snapshot(), 9)            -- the only icon-9 art is excluded now
local opener = engine:hoStarterEntry()
engine:toggle("ho", false)
w.runFor(500)
local d3 = engine:step()

-- check
DOCS.eq(d1.kind, "ho", "a heroic decision")
DOCS.eq(d1.ability, "Fixture Chance", "the opener first")
DOCS.eq(d2.ability, "Fixture Smash", "the art with the needed icon advances it")
DOCS.eq(strikeHeld, true, "a rotation art with another icon is held while the wheel runs")
DOCS.eq(smashOk, false, "the needed icon is not held")
DOCS.eq(excluded, true, "an excluded ability")
DOCS.eq(advancer, nil, "is never used to advance a wheel")
DOCS.eq(opener.ability, "Fixture Chance", "the stack's opener")
DOCS.eq(engine:entryHOIcon(stack.get("Fixture Strike")), 7, "an entry's icon")
DOCS.check(d3.kind ~= "ho", "switched off: nothing heroic")

examples.title: Overrides per zone, per mob, and a timed pause
examples.summary: Register a zone override and a stronger one for one mob, see which wins and what each switch reads while it applies, then pause every cast for one second with a temporary manual override.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Strike" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 1)                                       -- the game shows each cast as taken: the art goes on a second's reuse
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute" })
FW.target(w, 200)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = { entries = function() return {
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 90, gates = {} } } end } })

local zone = { name = "hall rules", priority = 1, match = { zone = "a test hall" }, directives = { interruptAll = true } }
engine:addOverride(zone)
engine:addOverride({ name = "brute rules", priority = 5, match = { mob = "brute" }, directives = {
    tags = { BURN = false }, disableMez = true, positioning = "behind", interruptList = { "Fixture Blast" },
    stack = "brute stack" } })

local d = engine:step()                                    -- a step resolves the overrides first
print("active override: " .. engine:activeOverride().name)
local matched = engine:overrideMatches(zone, engine:snapshot())
local read = { mez = engine:moduleOn("mez"), burn = engine:tagForcedOff("BURN"), all = engine:effInterruptAll(),
               list = engine:effInterruptList()["fixture blast"], pos = engine:effPosition().mode,
               stack = engine:activeStackName(), raw = engine:ovGet("disableMez") }

engine:setOverride({ pause = true }, { ttlMs = 1000, name = "hold a second" })
w.runFor(250)
local held = engine:step()
local paused = engine:isPaused()
w.runFor(1100)
local after = engine:step()

-- check
DOCS.eq(d.ability, "Fixture Strike", "the rotation runs under the overrides")
DOCS.eq(matched, true, "the zone override applies too")
DOCS.eq(read.mez, false, "mez off on the brute")
DOCS.eq(read.burn, true, "the burn tag forced off")
DOCS.eq(read.all, true, "interrupt-all from the zone override")
DOCS.eq(read.list, true, "and the brute's listed cast")
DOCS.eq(read.pos, "behind", "stand behind it")
DOCS.eq(read.stack, "brute stack", "the stack this context asks for")
DOCS.eq(read.raw, true, "one resolved directive")
DOCS.eq(held.reason, "paused", "the manual override holds every cast")
DOCS.eq(paused, true, "while it lasts")
DOCS.eq(after.ability, "Fixture Strike", "and lets go after its second")

examples.title: Where to stand, and line of sight
examples.summary: Ask the engine to position behind the mob: every decision then carries where it would stand - EB does not move in a fight for it yet (moves = false, said once in the console). A positional entry waits for its angle when the angle can be read, and the line-of-sight gate holds casts through a wall.

-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Strike" })

                 gates = {} }

engine:setPosition("behind", 3)

local d = engine:step()
print(("position: %s %d m"):format(d.position.mode, d.position.range))
local ctx = engine:snapshot()
ctx.mob = engine:selectTarget(ctx)
local plan = engine:planPosition(ctx)
local angle = engine:relativeAngle(ctx, ctx.mob)                 -- no facing on the mob rows: unknown
local open = engine:positionalFail("behind", ctx.mob)            -- unknown never blocks

local shim = game.combatShim()                                   -- offline: an angle read, to show the gate working
shim.behindTarget = function() return false end
shim.inFrontTarget = function() return true end
local angled = Combat.new({ shim = shim, stacks = { entries = function() return { strike } end } })
local front = angled:relativeAngle(ctx, ctx.mob)
local waits = angled:positionalFail("behind", ctx.mob)

local hold = engine:step()

DOCS.eq(d.position.targetId, 200, "relative to the mob being fought")
DOCS.eq(plan.range, 3, "at 3 metres")
DOCS.eq(angle, nil, "the angle cannot be read here")
DOCS.eq(open, nil, "so a positional art is never held for it")
DOCS.eq(front, "front", "with an angle read: in front of it")
DOCS.eq(waits, "Positional[behind]", "a behind-only art waits for the angle")
DOCS.eq(engine:losActive(), true, "the line-of-sight gate is on")
DOCS.eq(blocked, true, "the line to the brute is blocked")
DOCS.eq(hold.hold, true, "so nothing is cast through the wall")

end
local mezByEB = engine:moduleOn("mez")

-- your script: take eb mez over (replace = true), counting what it was asked
local asked = 0
local ok = reg:attach("combat.mez", function(args)
    asked = asked + 1
    engine:toggle("mez", args.state ~= "off")
    return true, "mez " .. tostring(args.state) .. " (my script)"
end, { owner = "my-combat-helper", replace = true })
if ok then print("the script answers eb mez") end
local said = a.console("eb mez on")
local again = reg:attach("combat.mez", function() return true end, { owner = "someone-else" })   -- one owner per command

-- check
local function has(list, id) for _, v in ipairs(list) do if v == id then return true end end return false end
DOCS.check(not has(unwired, "combat.mez") and not has(unwired, "combat.embargo"), "EB answers the combat commands itself")
DOCS.eq(mezByEB, false, "eb mez off (EB's own handler)")
DOCS.eq(engine:isPaused(), true, "eb combat off")
DOCS.eq(engine:switchOn("cures"), false, "eb cures off")
DOCS.eq(engine:switchOn("interrupts"), true, "eb interrupts on")
DOCS.eq(engine:tagLive("BURN"), true, "eb embargo tag BURN 15")
DOCS.eq(engine:moduleOn("ho"), false, "eb ho off")
DOCS.eq(asked, 1, "after the take-over, eb mez runs the script's handler")
DOCS.eq(engine:moduleOn("mez"), true, "eb mez on (through the script)")
DOCS.check(said:find("my script", 1, true) ~= nil, "the console shows the script's answer")
DOCS.eq(again, false, "a second owner is refused without replace = true")
a.stop()
examples.expect: Each typed line changes the engine: mez off, casting paused, cures off, interrupt-all on, the BURN tag held for 15 seconds, the heroic part off. After the script takes eb mez over, eb mez off runs the script's handler.

examples.title: Build a cast stack from its rows
examples.summary: eb.caststack.jsonstack turns a cast-stack profile's rows into the entries the combat engine runs: slot order becomes priority, a row's Type becomes its group and tag.
examples.code:
-- your script: a profile as the stack's rows (EB reads them from the character's imported profile file)
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local profile = { castStack = {
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA",     disabled = false, cond = {} },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Burn",   ability = "Fixture Burn",   type = "CA",     disabled = false, cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Hex",    ability = "Fixture Hex",    type = "Debuff", disabled = false, cond = {} },
    { slot = 4, name = "Fixture Flare",  ability = "Fixture Flare",  type = "CA",     disabled = false, cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
} }
local result = assert(JS.build(profile, { class = "warden" }))
print(JS.summary(result))
for _, e in ipairs(result.entries) do
    print(("  %-22s %-14s %-4s priority %d tags %s"):format(e.name, e.ability, e.group, e.priority, tostring(e.tags)))
end

-- check
DOCS.eq(#result.entries, 4, "one entry per row")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[1].priority, 99, "slot 1 = priority 99")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[4].priority, 96, "slot 4 = priority 96")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[3].tags, "DEBUFF", "a Debuff row is tagged DEBUFF")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[1].group, "dps", "a combat art runs in the dps group")
DOCS.has(JS.summary(result), "4 entries", "the summary counts")

examples.title: Switch one cast-stack row off and on
examples.summary: The holder is the live cast stack the engine reads every step; setEntryEnabled switches a row by its name or ability, and the engine stops casting it at once.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Strike", "Fixture Smash" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 10)                         -- the game shows each cast as taken: the ability goes on its reuse
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute" })
FW.target(w, 200)

-- your script
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local holder = JS.holder({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 99, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Smash",  ability = "Fixture Smash",  group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 97, gates = {} },
} })
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = require("eb.platform").game().combatShim(), stacks = holder })

local ok, said = holder.setEntryEnabled("Fixture Strike", false)     -- on = true | false | nil (toggle)
print(said)
local off = engine:step()
w.runFor(500)                                                         -- a quick art goes out at most every half second
holder.setEntryEnabled("fixture strike", true)                        -- any case
local on = engine:step()

-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "the row was found")
DOCS.eq(off.ability, "Fixture Smash", "switched off: the next row casts")
DOCS.eq(on.ability, "Fixture Strike", "switched on again: back to the top row")
DOCS.eq((holder.setEntryEnabled("Fixture Nothing", false)), false, "a name that is no row is refused")
examples.expect: With Fixture Strike switched off the engine casts Fixture Smash instead; switched back on, Fixture Strike again.

examples.title: Switch every row with a tag
examples.summary: A row's custom Tag groups rows a fight switches together: setTagEnabled turns every row carrying it off or on in one call.
examples.code:
-- your script
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local result = JS.build({ castStack = {
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = {} },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Burn",   ability = "Fixture Burn",   type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Flare",  ability = "Fixture Flare",  type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
} }, { class = "warden" })
local holder = JS.holder(result)

local ok, said = holder.setTagEnabled("burn", false)    -- case-insensitive; a third argument true matches part of a tag
print(said)
local function state()
    local t = {}
    for _, e in ipairs(holder.entries()) do t[e.ability] = e.disabled and "off" or "on" end
    return t
end
local during = state()
holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", true)
local after = state()

-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "rows carry the tag")
DOCS.eq(during["Fixture Burn"], "off", "tagged row 1 off")
DOCS.eq(during["Fixture Flare"], "off", "tagged row 2 off")
DOCS.eq(during["Fixture Strike"], "on", "the untagged row is untouched")
DOCS.eq(after["Fixture Burn"], "on", "back on together")
DOCS.eq((holder.setTagEnabled("NOPE", false)), false, "a tag no row carries is refused")
examples.expect: Both BURN rows go off together and come back together; the untagged row is never touched.

examples.title: A reload keeps your switches
examples.summary: rebind swaps a freshly built stack into the same holder and carries every row's on/off state across by name, so a profile reload never undoes what a fight script switched.
examples.code:
-- your script
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local function build()                                  -- the profile as read again from its file
    return JS.build({ castStack = {
        { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = {} },
        { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Burn",   ability = "Fixture Burn",   type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = {} },
    } }, { class = "warden" })
end
local holder = JS.holder(build())
holder.setEntryEnabled("Fixture Burn", false)           -- a fight script switched it off
local same = holder.rebind(build())                     -- EB reloads the profile when its file changes
local burn
for _, e in ipairs(holder.entries()) do if e.ability == "Fixture Burn" then burn = e end end
print("after the reload: Fixture Burn " .. (burn.disabled and "off" or "on"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(burn.disabled, true, "the switch survived the reload")
DOCS.eq(same, holder, "rebind returns the same holder: never build a new one per tick")
DOCS.eq(#holder.entries(), 2, "the fresh entries are served")
examples.expect: The row switched off before the reload is still off after it, and the holder is the same object the engine holds.

examples.title: Class facts fill in what a heal row leaves out
examples.summary: A row says when and on whom; it does not say whether a heal is a single or a group spell. With no class facts EB builds the row from its own Target, % and # (a single-target heal at the default weight); with the class's facts the same row builds as the group heal it is.
examples.code:
-- your script
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local CF = require("eb.caststack.classfacts")
local function profile()
    return { castStack = { { slot = 1, name = "Word of Redemption", ability = "Word of Redemption", type = "Heal",
                             target = "@Group", disabled = false, cond = {} } } }
end
local bare = JS.build(profile(), { class = "templar" })
local facts = assert(CF.forClass("templar"))           -- cached: the same table every call
local full = JS.build(profile(), { class = "templar", facts = facts })
print(("without facts: %s; with facts: %s"):format(bare.entries[1].def.type, full.entries[1].def.type))
print("with facts: held " .. #full.held .. ", type " .. tostring(full.entries[1].def.type))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#bare.held, 0, "no facts: the row is built from its own words, not held")
DOCS.eq(bare.entries[1].def.type, "SINGLE_BASIC", "as a single-target heal: the row alone cannot say it is a group spell")
DOCS.eq(#full.held, 0, "with facts it builds")
DOCS.eq(full.entries[1].def.type, "GROUP_HEAL", "as a group heal")
DOCS.check(#CF.classes() > 20, "EB ships facts for every class")
DOCS.eq(CF.forClass("no such class"), nil, "an unknown class has none")
examples.expect: Without facts the heal row builds from the row alone, as a single-target heal; with the templar's facts it builds as a group heal. Nothing is held either way.

examples.title: Switch a tag from the engine
examples.summary: engine:toggle switches a whole category (ae, mez, ho, dumbfires) or any custom tag; a custom tag also switches the holder's tagged rows.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Cleave", "Fixture Burn", "Fixture Strike" })
FW.mob(w, { id = 200, name = "a fixture brute" })
