examples.title: Find a character's cast stack by name
examples.summary: eb.caststack.loader finds the character's imported profile by its name, builds it with the class facts and serves it from a live holder; a character with no profile gets a plain reason.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the profiles folder, in a files host of your own (in game: EB's files service and your profiles)
local disk = {
    ["stacks/Main/Fixture Server_Fixturae.json"] = [[{"_v": 1, "default": "Main", "profiles": {"Main": {"sections":
        {"CastStack": [{"Type": "CA", "name": "Fixture Strike"}, {"Type": "CA", "name": "Fixture Burn", "Tag": "BURN"}]}}}}]],
}
local files = {                                            -- a files host: the loader needs read and list
    read = function(path) return disk[(path:gsub("[\\/]", "/"))] end,
    list = function(dir, glob)
        local pat, out = "^" .. glob:gsub("[%.%-]", "%%%0"):gsub("%*", ".*") .. "$", {}
        for path in pairs(disk) do
            local d, name = path:match("^(.*)/([^/]+)$")
            if d == dir:gsub("[\\/]", "/") and name:match(pat) then out[#out + 1] = name end
        end
        return out
    end,
}
local where = function() return "stacks" end              -- offline: which folder holds the profiles

-- your script
local loader = require("eb.caststack.loader")
local ld = loader.new({ files = files, getenv = where, me = function() return "Fixturae", "warden" end })
local ok = ld.load()                                       -- in game EB has done this already for eb.app.combat
print(ld.describe())
local none, why = loader.find({ files = files, getenv = where, char = "Nobodyhere" })
print("another character: " .. tostring(why))

-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "the profile was found and built")
DOCS.eq(#ld.holder.entries(), 2, "both rows")
DOCS.eq(ld.result.server, "Fixture Server", "the server comes from the file's name")
DOCS.has(ld.describe(), "class facts: warden", "the class facts were added")
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "no profile for another name")
DOCS.check(type(why) == "string" and #why > 0, "and a plain reason")
DOCS.eq(loader.pinKey("Fixturae"), "caststack.server.fixturae", "the setting that pins a server for a name")
examples.expect: The loader finds Fixturae's profile and builds its two rows with the warden's facts; a name with no profile is refused with why.

examples.title: Write cast-stack rows by hand
examples.summary: Build a stack from hand-written rows of several Types and conditions, and read what came of each row: its kind, tags and priority, the rows held with a reason, an unknown Type, an empty row skipped.
examples.code:
-- your script (pure Lua: no game needed)
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local rows = {                                                    -- priority order: slot 1 first
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA", cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Blast", ability = "Fixture Blast", type = "NamedCA", cond = { ["#"] = 2 } },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Mend", ability = "Fixture Mend", type = "Heal", target = "@Group", cond = { ["%"] = 70 } },
    { slot = 4, name = "Fixture Cleanse", ability = "Fixture Cleanse", type = "Cure", target = "@Group", cond = {} },
    { slot = 5, name = "Fixture Revive", ability = "Fixture Revive", type = "Res", target = "@Group", cond = {} },
    { slot = 6, name = "Fixture Ward", ability = "Fixture Ward", type = "Buff", target = "@Me", cond = {} },
    { slot = 7, name = "Fixture Quick", ability = "Fixture Quick", type = "CA", cond = { ["Aggro>"] = 80, ATag = "OPEN" } },
    { slot = 8, name = "Fixture Odd", ability = "Fixture Odd", type = "Buff", cond = { ["HP<"] = 50 } },
    { slot = 9, name = "", type = "CA", cond = {} },
    { slot = 10, name = "Fixture Mystery", ability = "Fixture Mystery", type = "Wobble", cond = {} },
    { slot = 11, name = "Fixture Regrowth", ability = "Fixture Regrowth", type = "Combat", target = "@Tank", cond = { ["RW<"] = 5 } },
    { slot = 12, name = "Fixture Shield", ability = "Fixture Shield", type = "Buff", target = "*offtank", cond = {} },
}
local result = JS.build({ castStack = rows }, { class = "warden" })
print(JS.summary(result))
local byAbility = {}
for _, e in ipairs(result.entries) do byAbility[e.ability] = e end
local heldWhy = {}
for _, h in ipairs(result.held) do heldWhy[h.name] = h.why end

-- check
DOCS.eq(#result.entries, 10, "ten rows became entries")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Strike"].group, "dps", "a CA row is a damage entry")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Strike"].priority, 99, "slot 1 = priority 99")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Blast"].tags, "NAMED_CA", "a NamedCA row is tagged NAMED_CA")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Ward"].group, "buff", "a Buff row")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Regrowth"].target, "PartyTank", "@Tank becomes PartyTank")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Quick"].disabled, true, "an allow-tag row is built off until its tag is raised")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Quick"].allowTag, "OPEN", "carrying its allow tag")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Mend"].group, "heal", "a heal row builds from its own Target, % and # when no class fact says more")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Mend"].target, "AllParty", "aimed at the group")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Cleanse"].tags, "CURE", "so does a cure row")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Revive"].tags, "REZ", "and a Res row, tagged REZ")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Odd"].def.useBelowMyHP, 50, "a buff's HP< is a gate on my own health")
DOCS.check(heldWhy["Fixture Mend"] == nil and heldWhy["Fixture Cleanse"] == nil and heldWhy["Fixture Odd"] == nil,
    "none of them is held")
DOCS.eq(heldWhy["Fixture Shield"], JS.ALIAS_UNDEFINED, "a * alias the profile's Aliases do not define is held: it names nobody")
DOCS.eq(result.unknown[1].name, "Fixture Mystery", "a Type EB does not run")
DOCS.eq(result.skipped[1].slot, 9, "an empty row is skipped")
DOCS.eq(JS.target("@Tank"), "PartyTank", "a row's target read the way build reads it")
DOCS.eq(JS.target("@Nowhere"), nil, "an @ word with no meaning cannot be aimed")
DOCS.eq(JS.bound(0), nil, "0 is an unset bound, never a gate at zero")
DOCS.eq(JS.bound("5"), 5, "a number is a bound")
DOCS.eq(JS.isToken("PartyTank"), true, "one of the engine's target words")
DOCS.eq(JS.isToken("Member1"), false, "a name is not")
DOCS.eq(JS.typeOf("namedca").group, "dps", "a Type, any case")
DOCS.check(#result.notes > 0, "notes say what is worth knowing")

examples.title: A class module of your own
examples.summary: Record a small class module - a heal template, a heal, a cure with its types, a rez, a stealth opener - into class facts, then build heal and cure rows that would otherwise be held.
examples.code:
-- your script (pure Lua: no game needed)
local F = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack_facts")
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local H = { New = function(Mx, prefix, o) return Mx end }          -- a class helper of your own: its New names the prefix
local unknown
local facts = F.record(function(M)                                  -- the class module: entries on four managers
    H.New(M, "FIXTURE", { forceNamedCA = false })
    M.Heals.DefineAbility({ name = "T_FixtureSingle", type = "SINGLE_BASIC", healWeight = 30 })   -- a heal template
    M.Heals.DefineAbility({ name = "FIXTURE_Mend", ability = "Fixture Mend", baseAbility = "T_FixtureSingle",
                            targets = "AllParty" })
    M.Heals.Enable("FIXTURE_Mend", { priority = 10 })
    M.Cures.DefineAbility({ name = "FIXTURE_Cleanse", ability = "Fixture Cleanse", type = "GROUP", tags = "CURE",
                            cureTypes = "noxious;arcane", targets = "AllParty" })
    M.Cures.Enable("FIXTURE_Cleanse")
    M.Cures.DefineAbility({ name = "FIXTURE_Revive", ability = "Fixture Revive", type = "GROUP_REZ", tags = "REZ",
                            targets = "AllParty" })
    M.Cures.Enable("FIXTURE_Revive")
    M.Dps.DefineAbility({ name = "FIXTURE_Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", tags = "CA" })
    M.Dps.Disable("FIXTURE_Strike")
    M.Dps.SetStealthOpeners({ "Fixture Ambush" }, { "Fixture Sneak" })
    unknown = M.Dps.Enable("FIXTURE_Nothing")                       -- no such entry: false
end, { H = H })
print(("facts: prefix %s, %d entries, %d template"):format(facts.prefix, #facts.list, (function()
    local n = 0; for _ in pairs(facts.templates) do n = n + 1 end; return n end)()))

local mend = facts.byName.FIXTURE_Mend
local merged = F.effective(facts, mend)                             -- the fact with its template under it
local result = JS.build({ castStack = {
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Mend", ability = "Fixture Mend", type = "Heal", target = "@Group", cond = { ["%"] = 70 } },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Cleanse", ability = "Fixture Cleanse", type = "Cure", target = "@Group", cond = {} },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Revive", ability = "Fixture Revive", type = "Res", target = "@Group", cond = {} },
} }, { facts = facts })

-- check
DOCS.eq(facts.prefix, "FIXTURE", "the prefix the class helper's New was given")
DOCS.eq(facts.classOpts.forceNamedCA, false, "and its options")
DOCS.check(facts.templates.T_FixtureSingle ~= nil, "a T_ name with no ability is a template")
DOCS.eq(merged.healWeight, 30, "the heal inherits its template's weight")
DOCS.eq(F.group(facts, mend), "heal", "a Heals entry that is not kept up is a heal")
DOCS.eq(F.lineKey("Fixture Mend II"), "fixture mend", "facts and rows meet on the ability line")
DOCS.eq(facts.index.heal["fixture mend"][1], mend, "indexed by kind and line")
DOCS.eq(F.index(facts), facts, "index can be rebuilt after a change by hand")
DOCS.eq(facts.byName.FIXTURE_Strike.enabled, false, "Disable leaves an entry off")
DOCS.eq(facts.stealth.openers[1], "Fixture Ambush", "the stealth openers")
DOCS.eq(unknown, false, "Enable of a name never defined answers false")
DOCS.eq(#result.held, 0, "with the facts no row is held")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[1].group, "heal", "the heal row runs")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[2].gates.cureTypes, "noxious;arcane", "the cure took its types from the class")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[3].tags, "REZ", "the rez row runs")
examples.expect: The facts hold the template, the entries and the stealth openers; with them the heal, cure and rez rows build and run, and the class's own prefix names every entry.

examples.title: Hand a built stack to category managers
examples.summary: jsonstack.apply defines every built entry on a set of category managers - damage, heals, cures, buffs - and item rows on an item manager, enabling all but the ones switched off.
examples.code:
-- your script (pure Lua: no game needed)
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local result = JS.build({ castStack = {
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA", cond = {} },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Ward", ability = "Fixture Ward", type = "Buff", target = "@Me", cond = {} },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Slow", ability = "Fixture Slow", type = "CA", disabled = true, cond = {} },
    { slot = 4, name = "Fixture Charm", ability = "Fixture Charm", type = "Buff", isItem = true, target = "@Me", cond = {} },
} }, { class = "warden" })

local log = { Dps = {}, Buffs = {}, Heals = {}, Cures = {}, items = {}, enabled = {} }
local function manager(kind)                                     -- a category manager: define, then enable
    return { DefineAbility = function(def, disabled) log[kind][#log[kind] + 1] = def.name end,
             Enable = function(name, o) log.enabled[name] = o.priority end }
end
local managers = { Dps = manager("Dps"), Heals = manager("Heals"), Cures = manager("Cures"), Buffs = manager("Buffs") }
local itemclick = { ClearDefined = function() end, Define = function(item) log.items[#log.items + 1] = item end }
local n = JS.apply(result, managers, itemclick)
print(("defined %d: Dps %d, Buffs %d, items %d"):format(n, #log.Dps, #log.Buffs, #log.items))

-- check
DOCS.eq(n, 4, "four entries defined")
DOCS.eq(log.enabled.WARDEN_FixtureStrike, 99, "the art enabled with its priority")
DOCS.check(log.enabled.WARDEN_FixtureWard ~= nil, "the buff enabled")
DOCS.eq(log.enabled.WARDEN_FixtureSlow, nil, "the row that is off in the profile is not enabled")
DOCS.eq(log.items[1].item, "Fixture Charm", "the item row went to the item manager")
DOCS.eq(log.items[1].target, "self", "kept up on you")
examples.expect: Four entries are defined: the art and the buff enabled with their priorities, the row that is off in the profile defined but not enabled, and the item kept up on you.

examples.title: Reload a cast stack when its file changes
examples.summary: Join a loader to the combat plane, pin the server for a name, and let a changed profile file reload the stack - through refresh (a stamp check) or the plane's own reload - with the loader telling you each time.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the profiles folder, in a files host of your own (in game: EB's files service and your profiles)
local w = DOCS.world()
local function profile(names)
    local rows = {}
    for _, n in ipairs(names) do rows[#rows + 1] = ('{"Type": "CA", "name": "%s"}'):format(n) end
    return '{"_v": 1, "default": "Main", "profiles": {"Main": {"sections": {"CastStack": [' .. table.concat(rows, ", ") .. ']}}}}'
end
local disk = { ["stacks/Main/Fixture Server_Fixturae.json"] = profile({ "Fixture Strike" }),
               ["stacks/Main/Second Server_Fixturae.json"] = profile({ "Fixture Other" }) }
local files = {
    read = function(path) return disk[(path:gsub("[\\/]", "/"))] end,
    list = function(dir, glob)
        local pat, out = "^" .. glob:gsub("[%.%-]", "%%%0"):gsub("%*", ".*") .. "$", {}
        for path in pairs(disk) do
            local d, name = path:match("^(.*)/([^/]+)$")
            if d == dir:gsub("[\\/]", "/") and name:match(pat) then out[#out + 1] = name end
        end
        table.sort(out)
        return out
    end,
}
local where = function() return "stacks" end
local stamp = 1

-- your script
local loader = require("eb.caststack.loader")
local store = { ["caststack.server.fixturae"] = "Fixture Server" }       -- this name has profiles on two servers
local settings = { get = function(key) return store[key] end }
local pinned = loader.pinnedServer(settings, "Fixturae")

local plane = require("eb.app.combat").new({ game = w.game })           -- in game: eb.app.combat
local ld = loader.new({ files = files, getenv = where, settings = settings, stat = function() return stamp end,
                        me = function() return "Fixturae", "warden" end })
loader.attach(ld, plane)                                                 -- the plane now casts from the loader
local heard, joined = 0, ld.onChange
ld.onChange = function(l) heard = heard + 1; joined(l) end
ld.load()
local first = #plane.holder.entries()

disk["stacks/Main/Fixture Server_Fixturae.json"] = profile({ "Fixture Strike", "Fixture Burn" })   -- the file changed
stamp = 2
local ok = ld.refresh()
local unchanged, why = ld.refresh()                                      -- the stamp did not move again
local again = plane.reload()                                             -- the plane's reload goes through the loader
print(plane.describe())
local stat = loader.lfsStat()                                            -- nil here; a stamp reader inside ISXLUA

-- check
DOCS.eq(pinned, "Fixture Server", "the server pinned for this name")
DOCS.eq(first, 1, "the pinned server's profile was loaded")
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "a changed stamp reloads")
DOCS.eq(#plane.holder.entries(), 2, "the plane casts from the new rows")
DOCS.eq(unchanged, false, "an unchanged stamp does nothing")
DOCS.eq(why, "unchanged", "and says so")
DOCS.eq(again, true, "the plane's reload works through the loader")
DOCS.check(heard >= 3, "the change callback heard every load and reload")
DOCS.has(plane.describe(), "2 entries", "the plane's status line follows the loader")
DOCS.eq(stat, nil, "no file-time reader in a plain Lua")
examples.expect: The pinned server picks the profile; the plane casts from the loader's stack; after the file changes, refresh reloads it (two rows now) and the change callback hears it; an unchanged stamp does nothing.

examples.title: Recipe: script a named fight
examples.summary: A complete named-fight script: the boss's emote sends you to a safe spot and back, half health switches the burn rows on, a detriment on a member is cured on cue, and the boss's big cast is interrupted on cue.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real) -----------------------
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 } })
require("nav.lib.navworld").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_lair" })
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Strike", "Fixture Burn", "Fixture Stun", "Fixture Cure" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 2)                                           -- the game shows each cast as taken: the ability goes on its reuse
local boss = FW.mob(w, { id = 300, name = "the Ashen Overseer", type = "NamedNPC", distance = 5 })
FW.target(w, 300)
local member = w.addMember({ name = "Member1", id = 11, class = "templar", healthPct = 90, powerPct = 80, inZone = true,
                             afflict = { noxious = 0 } })
w.addActor({ id = 11, name = "Member1", type = "PC", isNPC = false, distance = 4 })
w.events()                                                     -- EB's boot attaches the game's events and ticks them
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local app = require("eb.app.combat").new({ game = w.game, clock = w.P.now })   -- EB builds this once per box ...
app.holder.rebind(JS.build({ castStack = {                     -- ... with the character's own cast stack
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Burn",   ability = "Fixture Burn",   type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = {} },
} }, { class = "warden" }))                                    -- (the stun is not in the rotation: the script casts it on cue)
w.pulse.every("eb.combat", 0, function(t) app.pump(t) end)    -- ... and steps it 4 times a second
eb.app = { combat = app }                                      -- in game: eb.app.combat

-- your script: the fight ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
local P = require("eb.platform")
local game, pulse = P.game(), P.pulse()
local events, nav = require("eb.events"), require("eb.nav")
local combat = eb.app.combat                                   -- EB's own combat plane: never build a second engine

local FIGHT = { boss = "the Ashen Overseer", emote = "draws in the flames", stopCast = "Ashen Wail", stun = "Fixture Stun",
                cure = "Fixture Cure", home = { x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 }, safe = { x = -20, y = 0, z = 0 }, log = {} }
combat.holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", false)                     -- phase 1: hold the burn

local cues = {}                                                -- handlers only record; the fight task acts
events.on("IncomingText", function(ev)
    if ev.text:find(FIGHT.emote, 1, true) then cues[#cues + 1] = "flames" end
end)

pulse.spawn("fight: " .. FIGHT.boss, function()
    local phase = 1
    while true do
        local b = game.Target()
        if not b or b.isDead or (b.healthPct or 0) <= 0 then break end
        if phase == 1 and b.healthPct <= 50 then               -- phase 2 at half health: burn on
            phase = 2
            combat.holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", true)
            FIGHT.log[#FIGHT.log + 1] = "phase 2"
        end
        if cues[1] == "flames" then                            -- the emote: out of the fire, then back in
            table.remove(cues, 1)
            combat.holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", false)
            local s, h = FIGHT.safe, FIGHT.home
            if nav.goPoint(s.x, s.y, s.z) then
                eb.delay(3000)
                if nav.goPoint(h.x, h.y, h.z) then FIGHT.log[#FIGHT.log + 1] = "out and back" end
            end
            if phase == 2 then combat.holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", true) end
        end
        if game.TargetCasting() == FIGHT.stopCast and game.AbilityReady(FIGHT.stun) then   -- the big cast: stop it
            game.Cast(FIGHT.stun)
            FIGHT.log[#FIGHT.log + 1] = "stunned " .. FIGHT.stopCast
        end
        for _, m in ipairs(game.Group()) do                    -- the cure on cue: a noxious detriment on anyone
            if (m.noxious or 0) > 0 and game.AbilityReady(FIGHT.cure) then
                game.Cast(FIGHT.cure, { name = m.name })
                FIGHT.log[#FIGHT.log + 1] = "cured " .. m.name
            end
        end
        eb.delay(250)
    end
    FIGHT.over = true
end)

-- offline: the fight plays out ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
local function casted(name) for _, c in ipairs(w.world.casts) do if c.ability == name then return true end end end
local function burnOn()
    for _, e in ipairs(combat.holder.entries()) do if e.ability == "Fixture Burn" then return not e.disabled end end
end
local burnAway, onFrame = nil, w.world.onFrame
w.world.onFrame = function(h) onFrame(h); if w.self.x <= -18 then burnAway = burnOn() end end   -- watch the safe spot
w.runFor(500)
w.host:emitText("The Ashen Overseer draws in the flames!", 0)
w.runUntil(function() return FIGHT.log[1] == "out and back" end, 30000)
boss.healthPct = 45
w.runUntil(function() return FIGHT.log[2] == "phase 2" end, 3000)
member.afflict.noxious = 1
w.runUntil(function() return casted(FIGHT.cure) end, 3000)
member.afflict.noxious = 0
boss.castId, boss.castName = 77, FIGHT.stopCast
w.runUntil(function() return casted(FIGHT.stun) end, 3000)
boss.castId = 0
boss.healthPct, boss.isDead = 0, true
w.runUntil(function() return FIGHT.over end, 3000)
print("fight over: " .. table.concat(FIGHT.log, " | "))

-- check -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DOCS.eq(FIGHT.log[1], "out and back", "the emote sent us to the safe spot and back")
DOCS.check(math.sqrt(w.self.x ^ 2 + w.self.z ^ 2) <= 3, "home again after it")
DOCS.eq(FIGHT.log[2], "phase 2", "half health started phase 2")
DOCS.eq(FIGHT.log[3], "cured Member1", "the detriment was cured on cue")
DOCS.eq(FIGHT.log[4], "stunned Ashen Wail", "the boss's cast was interrupted on cue")
DOCS.eq(burnAway, false, "the burn was held while we stood at the safe spot")
DOCS.eq(burnOn(), true, "and ends switched on (phase 2)")
DOCS.eq(FIGHT.over, true, "the script ended with the boss")
examples.expect: The emote moves you out of the fire and back home with the burn held meanwhile; phase 2 turns the burn on; Member1's detriment is cured; Ashen Wail is stunned; the script ends when the boss dies.

examples.title: React to a boss emote
examples.summary: The pattern every fight script uses: an event handler only records the cue; a pulse task acts on it, because acting may wait and a handler must not.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.events()                                    -- EB's boot attaches the game's events and ticks them every frame

-- your script
local events = require("eb.events")
local pulse = require("eb.platform").pulse()
local CUES = { ["calls for its kin"] = "kill the adds", ["shudders violently"] = "spread out" }
local cues, done = {}, {}

events.on("IncomingText", function(ev)        -- runs inside the frame: record, never wait
    for text, what in pairs(CUES) do
        if ev.text:find(text, 1, true) then cues[#cues + 1] = what end
    end
end)
pulse.spawn("cue worker", function()           -- a task: free to wait (eb.delay) while it acts
    while #done < 1 do
        local what = table.remove(cues, 1)
        if what then print("acting on: " .. what); done[#done + 1] = what end
        eb.delay(100)
    end
end)

w.host:emitText("A fixture wolf howls.", 0)                          -- nothing to do with the fight
w.host:emitText("The Ashen Overseer shudders violently!", 0)         -- the cue
w.runFor(500)

-- check
DOCS.eq(#done, 1, "one cue acted on")
DOCS.eq(done[1], "spread out", "the right one")
DOCS.eq(#cues, 0, "nothing left waiting")
examples.expect: The emote is recorded by the handler and acted on by the task one pulse later; other text is ignored.

examples.title: Time a mechanic from an announcement

events.on("Announcement", function(ev)
    if ev.text:find("Ashen Storm", 1, true) and ev.timer then

    end
end)

    if due and now >= due then moved, due = now, nil end
end)

examples.summary: On a cue, walk to the fight's safe spot over the mesh, wait out the mechanic, and walk back to where you fought.

examples.title: Shape combat for one encounter
examples.summary: Name the encounter you are in, register an override that applies only to it - no AE near the boss, its big cast on the interrupt list - and clear it when the fight is over so the next pull is back to normal.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local FW = require("combat.lib.fightworld")
FW.book(w, { "Fixture Cleave", "Fixture Strike", "Fixture Stun" })
FW.recastOnUse(w, 10)                                       -- the game shows each cast as taken: the ability goes on its reuse
local boss = FW.mob(w, { id = 300, name = "the Ashen Overseer", type = "NamedNPC" })
FW.target(w, 300)

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local stack = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Cleave", ability = "Fixture Cleave", group = "dps", tags = "AE", priority = 99, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 90, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Stun", ability = "Fixture Stun", group = "dps", tags = "STUN", priority = 10, gates = {} },
} })
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = stack })   -- in game: eb.app.combat.engine

engine:setEncounter("the Ashen Overseer")                   -- where you are and what you fight
engine:addOverride({ name = "overseer", priority = 10, match = { encounter = "the Ashen Overseer" },
                     directives = { disableAE = true, interruptList = { "Ashen Wail" } } })
local d1 = engine:step()
local why = engine:passesGate(stack.get("Fixture Cleave"), engine:snapshot(), engine:snapshot().target)
boss.castId, boss.castName = 88, "Ashen Wail"               -- offline: the boss starts its big cast
w.runFor(500)                                               -- a quick art goes out at most every half second
local d2 = engine:step()
boss.castId = 0

engine:setEncounter(nil)                                    -- the fight is over: back to normal
engine:removeOverride("overseer")
w.runFor(500)
local d3 = engine:step()
print(("encounter: %s, then %s"):format(d2.reason, d3.ability == "Fixture Cleave" and "the AE again" or "?"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(d1.ability, "Fixture Strike", "no AE during the encounter")
DOCS.eq(why, "Toggled", "the override switched the AE tag off")
DOCS.eq(d2.kind, "interrupt", "the listed cast is interrupted")
DOCS.eq(d2.ability, "Fixture Stun", "with the stun")
DOCS.eq(d3.ability, "Fixture Cleave", "after the encounter the AE casts again")
examples.expect: During the encounter the AE is held (disableAE switches the AE tag off) and the boss's Ashen Wail is interrupted; after the encounter is cleared the AE casts again.

        approach = { { 10, 0, 10 }, { 20, 0, 25 } },
        entrance = { loc = { 20, 0, 25 }, tolerance = 8 },
        door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" },
    },
    rules = "default",                                      -- arm the character's own cast stack
    encounters = { "captain_fixturo", "hollow_skitters" },
    route = {                                               -- the STEPS the tank runs, in order
        { id = "camp.entry", act = "campspot", name = "entry", spot = { 0, 0, -30 }, who = "group" },
        { id = "n1.walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, 10 }, { 15, 0, 40 } } },
        { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" },
        { id = "n1.loot", act = "loot", op = "chest" },
        { id = "trash", act = "encounter", name = "hollow_skitters" },
        { id = "said", act = "announce",
          message = "Fixture Hollow: {{verdict.n1}} / {{verdict.trash}} (chest {{verdict.n1.loot}})" },
        { id = "exit.walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, -38 } } },
        { id = "exit", act = "zoneout", via = "exit" },
    },
}

-- the encounter files: what encounters/<name>.lua return (conditions -> actions)
local ENCOUNTERS = {
    captain_fixturo = {
        schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named", spot = { 15, 0, 42 },
        phases = { { id = "pull", do_ = { { target = { "Captain Fixturo" } }, { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } },
        done = { { actor_dead = "Captain Fixturo" } },
    },
    hollow_skitters = {
        schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "a hollow skitter", kind = "trash",
        when = { { actor_count = { query = "a hollow skitter", cmp = ">=", value = 1 } } },   -- no pack = skipped
        phases = { { id = "clear", do_ = { { clear_area = "a hollow skitter", radius = 30 } } } },
    },
}

-- offline stand-in for the game (in game EB hands the runner its live nav, combat engine and crew)
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({
    alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 }, packs = { ["a hollow skitter"] = 4 }, drops = { "a fixture chest" } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end                    -- the file above, instead of a folder on disk
env.loadEncounter = function(_, name) return ENCOUNTERS[name] end

-- your script
local IC = require("eb.ic")
local runner = IC.new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ok, why, report = runner:run(inst)
print(why)
for _, line in ipairs(world.lines) do
    local said = line:match("ANNOUNCE: (.*)$")
    if said then print(said) end
end

-- check
DOCS.check(ok, "the run completes: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.n1, "killed", "the named")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.trash, "cleared", "the trash pack")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts["n1.loot"], "a fixture chest", "the chest")
DOCS.eq(world.did("door"), 1, "the door was used once, by the tank")
DOCS.eq(world.did("camp"), 1, "one camp spot for the group")
DOCS.eq(world.zone, "fixture_docks", "out by the exit door, back in the hub")
examples.expect: The run completes: the named is killed, the trash cleared, the chest looted, the door used once and the exit taken back to the hub.

examples.title: What runner:load refuses
examples.summary: The loader checks an instance file before anything runs: its schema, a hub route that would move the group, an option that skips a step the route does not have, and an encounter file that will not load. Each refusal says why.
examples.code:
local IC = require("eb.ic")
local env = require("instances.lib.icworld").make()           -- offline interfaces (the loader needs none of them)

local function try(inst, encounters)
    env.loadInstance = function() return inst end
    env.loadEncounter = function(_, name)
        local e = encounters and encounters[name]
        if not e then error("encounters/" .. name .. ".lua is missing") end
        return e
    end
    return IC.new(env):load("fixture_hollow")
end

local base = function()
    return { schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
             hub = { zone = "fixture_docks", door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" } },
             route = { { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" } } }
end
local ENC = { captain_fixturo = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named", phases = {} } }

-- 1. not an eb.ic/1 file
local bad1 = base(); bad1.schema = "something/else"
local _, why1 = try(bad1, ENC)
-- 2. a hub route step that walks the group along (the tank walks the hub route ALONE)
local bad2 = base()
bad2.hub.route = { { id = "h1", act = "path", spots = { { 1, 0, 1 } } },
                   { id = "h2", act = "path", spots = { { 9, 0, 9 } }, group = "follow" } }
local _, why2 = try(bad2, ENC)
print("refused: " .. why2)
-- 3. an option that skips a step id the route does not have
local bad3 = base(); bad3.options = { { id = "skip_bonus", default = true, skip_steps = { "bonus" } } }
local _, why3 = try(bad3, ENC)
-- 4. a route step that calls an encounter with no file
local _, why4 = try(base(), {})

local inst = try(base(), ENC)

DOCS.has(why1, "unknown schema", "the schema is checked")
DOCS.has(why2, "the tank walks the hub route alone", "a hub step may not move the group")
DOCS.has(why3, "which is not a route step", "an option must name real route steps")
DOCS.has(why4, "will not load", "a missing encounter refuses the load")
DOCS.eq(inst and inst._enc.captain_fixturo.name, "Captain Fixturo", "the good file loads with its encounter")
examples.expect: Four broken files are refused with their reasons; the fixed file loads with its encounter attached.

examples.title: The tank zones the group in

examples.title: A mechanic mid-fight: a reactive phase
examples.summary: An encounter whose boss calls in adds: a phase with when + repeat_ is checked on every fight tick and between phases, and clears the adds whenever they are up, while the main phase fights the boss.
examples.code:
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    route = { { id = "boss", act = "encounter", name = "mire_queen" } },
}
local MIRE_QUEEN = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Mire Queen Fixtura", kind = "boss",
    phases = {
        { id = "burn", do_ = { { engage = "Mire Queen Fixtura" } } },
        -- REACTIVE: when + repeat_ = checked on every fight tick; it fires whenever its condition holds
        { id = "adds", repeat_ = true,
          when = { { actor_count = { query = "a mire spawn", cmp = ">=", value = 1 } } },
          do_ = { { clear_area = "a mire spawn", radius = 25 } } },
    },
    done = { { actor_dead = "Mire Queen Fixtura" } },
}

-- offline stand-in: engaging the queen surfaces three adds
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy",
    alive = { ["Mire Queen Fixtura"] = 100 }, adds = { on = "Mire Queen Fixtura", name = "a mire spawn", count = 3 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function() return MIRE_QUEEN end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ok, _, report = runner:run(inst)
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("reactive", 1, true) then print(l) end end

DOCS.check(ok, "the run completes")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.boss, "killed", "the boss")
DOCS.eq(world.did("clear"), 1, "the adds were cleared once, when they surfaced")
DOCS.eq(env.combat.count("a mire spawn"), 0, "no add left up")
examples.expect: The reactive phase fires once the adds surface, clears them, and the boss is killed.

examples.title: Encounter conditions, and how they fail closed
examples.summary: Evaluate when / done conditions against the runner's world facade: actor_present, actor_dead, actor_count, health_below, the all / any / not_ combinators, and a function. A condition the runner does not know is always false.
examples.code:
local env = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy",
    alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 }, packs = { ["a hollow skitter"] = 2 } })
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local w = runner:worldFacade()                 -- what an encounter's conditions read through

local function holds(cond) return runner.evalCond(cond, w) end

DOCS.check(holds({ actor_present = "Captain Fixturo" }), "the named is up")
DOCS.check(not holds({ actor_dead = "Captain Fixturo" }), "so it is not dead")
DOCS.check(holds({ actor_count = { query = "a hollow skitter", cmp = ">=", value = 2 } }), "two skitters")
DOCS.check(not holds({ health_below = 40 }), "my health is not under 40%")
DOCS.check(holds({ any = { { health_below = 40 }, { actor_present = "Captain Fixturo" } } }), "any = one of them")
DOCS.check(not holds({ all = { { health_below = 40 }, { actor_present = "Captain Fixturo" } } }), "all = every one")
DOCS.check(holds({ not_ = { actor_present = "a missing mob" } }), "not_ flips one condition")
DOCS.check(holds(function(facade) return facade.actorCount("a hollow skitter") == 2 end), "a function reads the facade")
-- a `when` list means AND: every entry must hold
DOCS.check(runner.evalWhen({ { actor_present = "Captain Fixturo" }, { health_above = 50 } }, w), "a when list")

local misspelled = holds({ actor_presnet = "Captain Fixturo" })
print("unknown condition -> " .. tostring(misspelled))
DOCS.eq(misspelled, false, "an unknown condition is false: a typo never pulls a boss")
examples.expect: Each condition reads the fake world as expected; the misspelled one is false, never a silent true.

examples.code:
local INSTANCE = {

    route = {
        { id = "camp", act = "campspot", name = "entry", spot = { 0, 0, -30 }, who = "group" },
        { id = "walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, 10 }, { 15, 0, 40 } } },
        { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" },
    },
}
local CAPTAIN = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named",
                  phases = { { id = "pull", do_ = { { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } } }

-- offline stand-in: the first pull of the captain kills the tank
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy",
    alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 }, dieOnFirst = "Captain Fixturo" })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function() return CAPTAIN end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ok, _, report = runner:run(inst)
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("RECOVERY", 1, true) then print(l) end end

DOCS.check(ok, "the run completes after the recovery")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.n1, "killed", "the second pull kills the named")
DOCS.eq(world.attempts["Captain Fixturo"], 2, "two pulls: the wipe, then the kill")

examples.title: Instance options and step gates
examples.summary: An instance declares an option that skips its bonus named by default; a run flips it with skip_bonus=off. A route step with its own when gate runs only when the gate holds. A skipped step is said and never run.
examples.code:
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    options = { { id = "skip_bonus", label = "skip the bonus named", default = true, skip_steps = { "bonus" } } },
    route = {
        { id = "bonus", act = "encounter", name = "bonus_named" },
        -- a step gate: loot the chest only when the bonus named is dead
        { id = "bonus.loot", act = "loot", op = "chest", when = { { actor_dead = "Old Fixturo" } } },
    },
}
local BONUS = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Old Fixturo", kind = "named",
                phases = { { id = "pull", do_ = { { engage = "Old Fixturo" } } } } }

local function runWith(flags)
    local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy", alive = { ["Old Fixturo"] = 100 },
        drops = { "an old chest" } })
    env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
    env.loadEncounter = function() return BONUS end
    local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
    local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
    local options = runner.parseOptionFlags(flags)       -- "skip_bonus=off" -> { skip_bonus = false }
    local ok, _, report = runner:run(inst, { options = options })
    return ok, report, world
end

local ok1, rep1, w1 = runWith("")
for _, l in ipairs(w1.lines) do if l:find("option skip_bonus", 1, true) then print(l) end end
local ok2, rep2, w2 = runWith("skip_bonus=off")

DOCS.check(ok1 and ok2, "both runs complete")
DOCS.eq(rep1.verdicts.bonus, nil, "default: the bonus named is skipped (no verdict)")
DOCS.eq(w1.did("chest"), 0, "default: its gate does not hold, so no chest step")
DOCS.eq(rep2.verdicts.bonus, "killed", "skip_bonus=off: the bonus named is fought")
DOCS.eq(rep2.verdicts["bonus.loot"], "an old chest", "and its gated chest is looted")
local flags, rest = require("eb.ic").parseOptionFlags("fixture_hollow 30 skip_bonus=off")
DOCS.eq(flags.skip_bonus, false, "parseOptionFlags takes the option words out")
DOCS.eq(rest, "fixture_hollow 30", "and hands back the rest of the line")
examples.expect: The default run skips the bonus named and the gated chest; the run with skip_bonus=off fights it.

examples.title: Save a run and resume it at a step
examples.summary: runner:saveRun snapshots a configured run (file, difficulty, loop window, chores, a resume pointer = a route step id, and the reuse timer) as a plain record. Store it however you like; runner:resumeRun restores it and starts at the pointer.
examples.code:
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    route = {
        { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "first" },
        { id = "n2", act = "encounter", name = "second" },
    },
}
local ENC = {
    first = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named", phases = { { do_ = { { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } } },
    second = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Mire Queen Fixtura", kind = "boss", phases = { { do_ = { { engage = "Mire Queen Fixtura" } } } } },
}

local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy", reuseNow = 900,
    alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100, ["Mire Queen Fixtura"] = 100 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function(_, name) return ENC[name] end
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))

-- save: a single run (loop = false) to resume at route step "n2"
local record = runner:saveRun({ inst = inst, name = "evening run", loop = false, pointer = "n2",
                                between = { tse = true } })
-- the record is plain data: write it off the game thread, read it back later
local SAVED = require("eb.ic.ic_saved").SAVED
local back = assert(SAVED.decode(record))

local ok, _, report = runner:resumeRun(inst, back)
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("saved run", 1, true) then print(l) end end

DOCS.eq(record.schema, "eb.icsave/1", "the record's schema")
DOCS.eq(record.reuse.fixture_hollow, 900, "the reuse timer at save")
DOCS.eq(SAVED.reuseRemaining(record, "fixture_hollow", 600), 300, "10 minutes after a save at 0 s, 5 are left")
DOCS.check(ok, "the resumed run completes")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.n1, nil, "step n1 was before the pointer")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.n2, "killed", "the run resumed at n2")
DOCS.eq(world.attempts["Captain Fixturo"], nil, "the first named was never pulled")
examples.expect: The record round-trips through decode, and the resumed run starts at step n2: the first named is never fought again.

examples.title: When does a combat wait end?
examples.summary: The instance runner's combat wait decides with a small pure rule: a fight on the group or a straggler nobody fights HOLDS the wait; a clear, or a combat flag with nothing behind it for 5 seconds, lets it go. A lone in-combat flag never holds a run forever.
examples.code:
local HOLD = require("eb.ic.ic_hold").HOLD

-- decide(inCombat, anyHated, nearby NPCs, ms the bare flag has held)
local fight = HOLD.decide(true, true, {}, 0)
local straggler = HOLD.decide(true, false, { { id = 41, name = "a hollow skitter", dist = 12, combatMode = true } }, 0)
local clear = HOLD.decide(false, false, {}, 0)
local stuck = HOLD.decide(true, false, {}, 6000)
local early = HOLD.decide(true, false, {}, 2000)          -- not 5 s yet: a pull may still be landing

print(("in combat, nobody hated, nothing near, 6 s -> %s"):format(stuck.hold))

DOCS.eq(fight.hold, "fight", "someone in the group is hated")
DOCS.eq(straggler.hold, "straggler", "an NPC in combat mode nobody fights")
DOCS.eq(straggler.straggler.name, "a hollow skitter", "the straggler handed to the combat engine")
DOCS.eq(clear.hold, "clear", "out of combat")
DOCS.eq(stuck.hold, "stuck", "a bare combat flag for 5 s or more")
DOCS.eq(early.hold, "fight", "under 5 s it still counts as a fight")
DOCS.check(HOLD.holds(fight.hold) and HOLD.holds(straggler.hold), "fight and straggler hold the wait")
DOCS.check(not HOLD.holds(clear.hold) and not HOLD.holds(stuck.hold), "clear and stuck let it go")
examples.expect: The four cases decide fight, straggler, clear and stuck; only the first two hold the wait.

examples.title: eb ic from the console and from a script
examples.summary: On a running box, eb ic run / loop / stop / status drive the instance runner as an EB task. Type the line, or call the same launcher from a script through eb.app.ic: status says what runs, a file name that is not installed is refused with the reason.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game you type in the console)
local a = DOCS.app()

-- the console line
local status = a.console("eb ic status")
print(status)
-- the same launcher from a script: the app's `eb ic` object
local IC = a.app.ic
local ok, why = IC.launch({ cmd = "run", zone = "fixture_nowhere" })
local where, notFound = IC.find("fixture_nowhere")

DOCS.has(status, "ic: idle", "nothing is running")
DOCS.eq(ok, false, "an IC that is not installed is refused")
DOCS.has(why, "no IC called 'fixture_nowhere'", "with the reason")
DOCS.eq(where, nil, "find answers nil for it")
DOCS.has(notFound, "eb ic list", "and points at the list")
DOCS.eq(IC.run, nil, "no run was started")
a.stop()
examples.expect: eb ic status answers idle; an unknown IC name is refused and nothing starts.

examples.title: A hub route the tank walks alone
examples.summary: hub.route lists the tank's own steps from the hub to the door: a walk, its own camp spot (who = "me"), a click on a lever. A wait_group step loads but is skipped: the group holds in the hub and the door takes it in.
examples.code:
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    hub = {
        zone = "fixture_docks", difficulty = "[Heroic I]",
        route = {                                             -- wins over hub.approach when both are given
            { id = "h1", act = "path", spots = { { 5, 0, 5 }, { 12, 0, 18 } } },
            { id = "h2", act = "campspot", name = "dock", spot = { 12, 0, 18 }, who = "me" },
            { id = "h3", act = "interact", actor = "a rusted fixture lever", verb = "pull" },
            { id = "h4", act = "wait_group" },
        },
        entrance = { loc = { 12, 0, 18 }, tolerance = 8 },
        door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" },
    },
    route = { { id = "inside", act = "wait", seconds = 1 } },
}

local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ group = { { id = "is2", role = "healer" } } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ctx = runner:newCtx(inst, {})
local ok, why = runner:zoneIn(ctx)
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("no wait for the group", 1, true) then print(l) end end

DOCS.check(ok, "in: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 2, "the tank walked the hub route's two waypoints")
local _, camp = world.first("camp")
DOCS.eq(camp[3], "me", "the hub camp spot is the tank's own")
local _, lever = world.first("interact")
DOCS.eq(lever[2], "a rusted fixture lever", "the click on the way")
DOCS.eq(world.did("door"), 1, "then the door, once, for everyone")
examples.expect: The tank walks, camps itself, pulls the lever and uses the door; the wait_group step is skipped and said.

examples.title: One route step of each kind
examples.summary: A route mixes camp spots, walks, clicks, waits, a wait for an actor's death, loot, an announce and the exit. Run one of each as the tank, then hand the same steps to a member's runner: it holds on every step that would move it, because only the tank walks the route and the tank's camp spots move the group.
examples.code:
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    hub = { zone = "fixture_docks", entrance = { loc = { 0, 0, 0 }, tolerance = 8 },
            door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" } },
    route = {
        { id = "camp",     act = "campspot", name = "entry", spot = { 0, 0, -30 }, who = "group" },
        { id = "walk",     act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, 10 }, { 12, 0, 20 } } },
        { id = "lever",    act = "interact", actor = "a rusty fixture lever", verb = "pull" },
        { id = "pause",    act = "wait", seconds = 2 },
        { id = "warden",   act = "wait_actor_dead", name = "a fixture warden", seconds = 30 },
        { id = "chest",    act = "loot", op = "chest" },
        { id = "said",     act = "announce", message = "chest: {{verdict.chest}}" },
        { id = "out.walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, -38 } } },
        { id = "out",      act = "zoneout", via = "exit" },
    },
}

-- offline stand-in for the game (in game EB hands the runner its live nav, combat engine and crew)
local ICW = require("instances.lib.icworld")
local env, world = ICW.make({ alive = { ["a fixture warden"] = 100 }, drops = { "a fixture chest" } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end

-- your script: the tank runs the lap
local IC = require("eb.ic")
local runner = IC.new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ok, why, report = runner:run(inst)
print("lap: " .. tostring(why))

-- a member's runner gets the same steps and holds (the step handlers can be called one at a time)
local menv = ICW.make({ tank = false, start = "copy" })
local member = IC.new(menv)
local mctx = member:newCtx(inst)
local _, onPath = member:stepPath(inst.route[2], mctx)
local _, onCamp = member:stepCampspot(inst.route[1], mctx)
local _, onClick = member:stepInteract(inst.route[3], mctx)
print("member on path: " .. onPath)

-- check
DOCS.check(ok, "the lap completes: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.chest, "a fixture chest", "the loot step recorded its drop")
DOCS.eq(world.did("camp"), 1, "the camp spot was set for the group")
DOCS.eq(world.did("interact"), 1, "the tank pulled the lever")
DOCS.eq(world.zone, "fixture_docks", "out by the exit door")
DOCS.has(onCamp, "holding", "a member holds on a campspot step")
DOCS.has(onClick, "holding", "and on an interact step: the tank does the click")
DOCS.eq(menv.nav.zone(), "fixture_hollow", "the member's runner moved nobody")
examples.expect: The tank's lap runs every step in order and leaves by the exit; the member holds on path, campspot and interact.

examples.title: Add your own route step kind
examples.summary: runner.STEP holds the route step handlers by act and runner.ROUTE_ACTS the acts a route file may carry (a step with an act in neither is refused when the file loads). Add one entry to each and a route step with that act loads and runs: here a "ring_gong" step that clicks a gong and waits for the room's door to open. A handler returns ok, a note for the log, and false stops the run with the note as the reason.
examples.code:
local IC = require("eb.ic")

-- your script: one entry in each table adds the act (they are shared by every runner: add it once, at start)
IC.ROUTE_ACTS.ring_gong = true                               -- the loader lets a route step with this act in ...
IC.STEP.ring_gong = function(runner, s, ctx)                  -- ... and this is what the runner does for it
    if not runner.combat.find(s.gong, { alive = true }) then return false, "no gong called " .. s.gong .. " here" end
    if ctx.opts.dry then return true, "would ring " .. s.gong end
    runner.nav.interact(s.gong, "ring")
    runner.sleep(1500)                                        -- every wait goes through the env's sleep
    return true, "rang " .. s.gong .. ", the door opened"
end

local function instance(gong)
    return {
        schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
        hub = { zone = "fixture_docks", entrance = { loc = { 0, 0, 0 }, tolerance = 8 },
                door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" } },
        route = {
            { id = "gong", act = "ring_gong", gong = gong },
            { id = "walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, 12 } } },
        },
    }
end

-- offline stand-in for the game
local ICW = require("instances.lib.icworld")
local env, world = ICW.make({ start = "copy", alive = { ["a fixture gong"] = 100 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return instance("a fixture gong") end
local runner = IC.new(env)
local ok, why = runner:run(assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow")))
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("ring_gong", 1, true) then print((l:gsub("^%[ic%] ", ""))) end end

local env2 = ICW.make({ start = "copy" })
env2.loadInstance = function() return instance("a missing gong") end
local runner2 = IC.new(env2)
local ok2, why2 = runner2:run(assert(runner2:load("fixture_hollow")))
print("stopped: " .. tostring(why2))

-- check
DOCS.check(ok, "the lap with the custom step completes: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(world.did("interact"), 1, "the gong was rung once")
DOCS.eq(ok2, false, "a handler's false stops the run")
DOCS.has(why2, "no gong called a missing gong here", "with the handler's own reason")
IC.STEP.ring_gong = nil
IC.ROUTE_ACTS.ring_gong = nil
examples.expect: The custom step runs between the built-in ones and the lap completes; a gong that is not there stops the run with the handler's reason.

examples.title: Read a fight's sensors through the world facade
examples.summary: Every condition in an encounter reads through runner:worldFacade(): fight timers, a curable detriment, a chat or emote line since the pull, an item in the bags, an actor's type. Here each sensor is wired to a small fake and read directly, the way a custom fn = function(ctx) action reads ctx.w.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game: the combat and events interfaces the sensors read through
local ICW = require("instances.lib.icworld")
local env, world = ICW.make({ start = "copy", alive = { ["Overseer of Fixtures"] = 80 } })
env.combat.detriment = function(q) return q.type == "noxious" end                 -- a noxious curse is up
env.combat.hasItem = function(name) return name == "a fixture tonic" end
env.combat.find = function(name) return name == "Overseer of Fixtures" and { name = name, type = "NamedNPC" } or nil end
local heard = { { at = 0, text = "The Overseer of Fixtures roars: the floor will burn!" } }
env.events = { chatSeen = function(match, sinceMs)
    for _, l in ipairs(heard) do if l.at >= sinceMs and l.text:find(match, 1, true) then return true end end
    return false
end }

-- your script
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local w = runner:worldFacade()
w.markFight()                                    -- the pull: the fight clock starts
world.clock = world.clock + 3000
w.resetTimer("adds")                             -- what the reset_timer action does
world.clock = world.clock + 12000
print(("adds timer: %d ms since reset_timer"):format(w.timerElapsed("adds")))

-- check
DOCS.eq(w.timerElapsed("adds"), 12000, "a named timer counts from its reset")
DOCS.eq(w.timerElapsed(), 15000, "the default timer counts from the pull")
DOCS.check(w.detrimentPresent({ who = "group", type = "noxious" }), "a noxious detriment is on the group")
DOCS.check(not w.detrimentPresent({ type = "elemental" }), "no elemental one")
DOCS.check(w.chatSeen({ match = "the floor will burn" }), "the emote arrived since the pull")
DOCS.check(not w.chatSeen({ match = "the walls close in" }), "a line that never came")
DOCS.check(w.hasItem("a fixture tonic"), "the tonic is in the bags")
DOCS.eq(w.actorType("Overseer of Fixtures"), "NamedNPC", "the actor's type")
examples.expect: The timer counts from its reset, the detriment, emote and item sensors answer what the fakes hold, and the actor's type comes from the combat interface's row.

examples.title: Who is still elsewhere, and one copy for the door
examples.summary: Before the door the tank waits for the group in the hub. runner:stragglers names every member still in another zone (by role or box id, never by character), and runner:sameCopy asks the brain to bring a group split across copies of the hub into the tank's copy - nobody walks for it.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game: the tank in the hub, a healer still travelling, the group split across two copies
local ICW = require("instances.lib.icworld")
local env, world = ICW.make({ group = { { id = "is2", role = "healer", zone = "fixture_vale" },
                                        { id = "is3", role = "dps", zone = "fixture_docks" } } })
local sameCopy, gathered = false, 0
env.brain.sameCopyAsGroup = function() return sameCopy end
env.brain.gatherToMyCopy = function() gathered = gathered + 1; sameCopy = true; return true end

-- your script
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = { zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow", hub = { zone = "fixture_docks" }, route = {} }
local ctx = runner:newCtx(inst)
local missing = runner:stragglers(ctx, "fixture_docks", "Fixture Docks")
for _, m in ipairs(missing) do print(("still elsewhere: %s (in %s)"):format(m.label, m.zone)) end
local goOn = runner:sameCopy(ctx)

-- check
DOCS.eq(#missing, 1, "one member is not in the hub")
DOCS.eq(missing[1].id, "is2", "the healer's box")
DOCS.eq(goOn, true, "the door goes ahead")
DOCS.eq(gathered, 1, "the brain was asked once to bring the group into the tank's copy")
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 0, "nobody walked for it")
examples.expect: One member is still on its way; after the brain gathers the group into one copy the door can go ahead.

examples.title: The T.S.E at the zone's end, inside
examples.summary: Looping one zone, the chores run once at the END of each run, inside the copy where the run ended: every box runs its saved T.S.E pass first, then a repair trip if gear is low. Only then does the tank wait out the timer, leave by the exit and reset. Here the T.S.E call records the zone it ran in.
examples.code:
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    hub = { zone = "fixture_docks", entrance = { loc = { 0, 0, 0 }, tolerance = 8 },
            door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" } },
    route = { { id = "walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, 10 } } } },    -- the run ends inside: no zoneout step
    loop = { rerun_first = false },
}

-- offline stand-in for the game: the upkeep interface's T.S.E records where it was asked
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy", upkeep = { gear = 100 },
    group = { { id = "is2", role = "healer" } } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
local tseZone, tseScope
local tse = env.upkeep.tse
env.upkeep.tse = function(scope) tseZone, tseScope = env.nav.zone(), scope; return tse(scope) end

-- your script: one lap, the T.S.E and repair chores ticked
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ok, why, report = runner:loop(inst, { laps = 1, between = { tse = true, repair = true } })
print(("T.S.E ran in %s for %s"):format(tostring(tseZone), tostring(tseScope)))

-- check
DOCS.check(ok, "the loop ends cleanly: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(world.did("tse"), 1, "one T.S.E pass")
DOCS.eq(tseZone, "fixture_hollow", "inside the copy where the run ended")
DOCS.eq(tseScope, "all", "every box runs its own")
DOCS.eq(report.chores[1].tse, "done", "the chore report says it ran and ended")
DOCS.eq(report.chores[1].repair, "not needed", "gear at 100%: no repair trip")
examples.expect: The T.S.E runs once, for every box, while the tank is still inside the cleared copy; the loop then ends after its one lap.

examples.title: Spot a reset that did not take
examples.summary: After each lap the loop checks the nameds it reached: when every one was already gone ("skipped:gate"), the lap ran a copy that was still cleared, so its reset did not take. ic.clearedCopy says why and the loop ends instead of cycling an empty copy.
examples.code:
local IC = require("eb.ic")

-- an instance with one named encounter (only the parts clearedCopy reads)
local inst = {
    zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    route = { { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain" }, { id = "t1", act = "encounter", name = "skitters" } },
    _enc = { captain = { kind = "named" }, skitters = { kind = "trash" } },
}

-- your script: the check the loop makes after each lap
local fresh = IC.clearedCopy({ inst = inst, verdicts = { n1 = "killed", t1 = "cleared" } })
local stale = IC.clearedCopy({ inst = inst, verdicts = { n1 = "skipped:gate", t1 = "skipped:gate" } })
print(stale)

-- check
DOCS.eq(fresh, nil, "a lap that killed its named is fine")
DOCS.has(stale, "its reset did not take", "an all-gone lap is reported")
examples.expect: A lap where the named was killed passes; a lap where it was already gone is reported.

examples.title: The runner's small helpers in a custom action
examples.summary: eb.ic.ic_base carries what every part of the runner uses: a log line in the runner's own voice, the flat distance doors and exits are measured with, the short countdown text and how often a long wait reports. Use them in an fn = function(ctx) action so your step reads like the runner's own.
examples.code:
local base = require("eb.ic.ic_base")

-- offline stand-in for the game
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy" })
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)

-- your script: a custom action, the kind an encounter's phase can hold as { fn = function(ctx) ... end }
local function leverCheck(ctx)
    local x, _, z = runner.nav.here()
    local d = base.flat(x, z, 3, 4)                          -- the lever stands at x = 3, z = 4
    local left = 5400                                        -- seconds a reuse timer has left
    base.say(runner, "lever is %.1f m away (flat); reset in %s, said every %d s", d, base.short(left), base.every(left))
    return true
end
leverCheck(runner:newCtx({ zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow", route = {} }))
print(world.lines[#world.lines])

-- check
DOCS.near(base.flat(0, 0, 3, 4), 5, 1e-9, "flat distance ignores height")
DOCS.eq(base.short(45), "45s", "under a minute")
DOCS.eq(base.short(1620), "27m", "minutes")
DOCS.eq(base.every(300), 120, "a short wait reports every 2 minutes")
DOCS.has(world.lines[#world.lines], "[ic] lever is 5.0 m away", "the line went to the runner's log")
examples.expect: The custom action logs one runner line with the distance to the lever and the countdown text.

examples.title: Tell a stuck combat flag from a real fight
examples.summary: The game's in-combat flag can stay lit with nobody fighting. The combat hold's flag watch times that bare flag: HOLD.observe counts how long it has held, and after HOLD.STUCK_MS it is called stuck so a run never waits on it forever. A real fight between looks (HOLD.hated) starts the count over.
examples.code:
local HOLD = require("eb.ic.ic_hold").HOLD

-- your script: one look a second at "in combat, nobody hated, nobody near"
local f = HOLD.newFlag()
local held = 0
for t = 0, 5000, 1000 do held = HOLD.observe(f, t, true) end
print(HOLD.stuckLine(held))

local st = HOLD.newState()
HOLD.observe(st.flag, 0, true)
HOLD.observe(st.flag, 4000, true)
HOLD.hated(st)                                        -- the group was seen in a real fight between looks
local after = HOLD.observe(st.flag, 5000, true)

-- check
DOCS.eq(held, 5000, "the bare flag held five seconds")
DOCS.check(f.stuck, "and is called stuck")
DOCS.eq(after, 0, "a real fight in between starts the count over")
DOCS.eq(HOLD.observe(HOLD.newFlag(), 9000, false), 0, "a look that is not a bare flag counts nothing")
examples.expect: The bare flag is stuck after five seconds; a real fight in between resets the count.

examples.title: The instance commands from the console
examples.summary: Boot EB offline and type the instance commands the way you would in game: eb ic status, eb lockouts and eb resetzone. Each answers at once; a run itself is an EB task that eb ic status reports on. Resetting a zone (and reading which zones you are saved to) is held back until EB has proven that call in the game: the answer names the zone and says so.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script: lines exactly as you type them
local status = a.console("eb ic status")
local locks = a.console("eb lockouts")
local reset = a.console("eb resetzone one fixture_hollow")
print(status)
print(reset)

-- check
DOCS.has(status, "ic: idle", "no run is going")
DOCS.has(locks, "lockouts:", "eb lockouts answers")
DOCS.has(reset, "the reset of fixture_hollow", "eb resetzone names the zone it was asked for")
DOCS.has(reset, "held back until it is proven live", "and says the reset is held back for now")
DOCS.has(a.console("eb resetzone"), "which zone?", "with no zone it asks which")
a.stop()

examples.title: Recipe: a quest pack with stages, hails and clicks
examples.summary: Write a quest pack, bind the quest runner, and drive it to completion the way EB's brain does: travel by the zone's own transit, walk, hail the giver through its dialog, click the quest objects until the journal updates, kill and loot, then hand in. Each stage advances on the journal's own text.
examples.code:
-- the pack: what a quest file returns (pure data; each step is one command line)
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1",
    quest_name = "The Fixture Errand",
    no_smart_travel = true,                  -- a pack never fast travels (this is also the default)
    steps = {
        { type = "comment", description = "Stage 1: take the errand from the warden" },
        { type = "command", command = 'CheckZone "Fixture Vale"' },           -- the zone's own transit, never fast travel
        { type = "command", command = "MM 12,0,30" },                         -- walk the mesh to the warden
        { type = "command", command = "HailActor Warden Fixturo,1,1" },       -- hail, then dialog picks 1 and 1
        { type = "command", command = 'CheckQuestStep "Collect three fixture lanterns"' },
        { type = "comment", description = "Stage 2: the lanterns and the thief" },
        { type = "command", command = 'DoubleClickActorUntilUpdate "a fixture lantern"',
          completed = "Collect three fixture lanterns" },                     -- click until the journal ticks it
        { type = "command", command = 'KillMobs "a lantern thief","",30,5', completed = "Defeat the lantern thief" },
        { type = "command", command = "LootAll" },
        { type = "comment", description = "Stage 3: back to the warden" },
        { type = "command", command = 'CheckQuestStep "Return to Warden Fixturo"' },
        { type = "command", command = "HailActor Warden Fixturo,1" },         -- the hand-in
        { type = "command", command = "QuestComplete" },                      -- verified: the quest left the journal
    },
}

-- offline stand-in: a scripted world (in game the journal, the NPCs and the fights are real)
local QUEST = PACK.quest_name
local lanterns = 0
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({
    onHail = function(npc, picks, w)
        if not w.quests[QUEST] and not w.completed[QUEST] then
            w.journal.give(QUEST, { "Collect three fixture lanterns", "Defeat the lantern thief" })
        elseif w.quests[QUEST] then w.journal.complete(QUEST) end            -- the hand-in
    end,
    onClick = function(spec, w)
        lanterns = lanterns + 1
        if lanterns >= 3 then w.journal.check(QUEST, "Collect three fixture lanterns") end
    end,
    onKill = function(target, w) w.journal.check(QUEST, "Defeat the lantern thief"); w.lootPending = true end,
    onLoot = function(w) w.journal.stage(QUEST, { "Return to Warden Fixturo" }) end,   -- stage 3 shows up
})

-- your script: bind the runner to its adapters, start the pack, and drive it one step per tick
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = QUEST }, {})
local trace, status, info = {}, nil, nil
for _ = 1, 100 do
    status, info = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = status
    if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end
    -- the brain's part: the runner hands travel, fights and loot back, and the brain does them
    if status == "need_travel" then deps.nav.travelTo(info, { pack = true })
    elseif status == "need_combat" then deps.combat.engage(info); world.hated = false
    elseif status == "need_loot" then deps.economy.lootGrab({}) end
    world.tick(5000)
end
print(status .. ": " .. tostring(info))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "the pack ran to its end")
DOCS.check(world.completed[QUEST], "the quest left the journal at the hand-in")
DOCS.eq(world.did("travel"), 1, "one trip, by the zone's own transit")
DOCS.eq(world.did("hail"), 2, "two hails: the giver and the hand-in")
DOCS.eq(lanterns, 3, "clicked until the journal ticked the lanterns")
DOCS.eq(world.did("engage"), 1, "one pull for the thief")
DOCS.eq(world.did("loot"), 1, "one loot pass")
local seen = table.concat(trace, " ")
DOCS.has(seen, "need_travel", "travel was handed to the brain")
DOCS.has(seen, "need_combat", "the fight was handed to the brain")
DOCS.has(seen, "need_loot", "the loot was handed to the brain")
examples.expect: The pack runs to complete; the journal shows each stage in turn and the quest leaves the journal at the hand-in.

examples.title: What quests.step answers, and what to do with it
examples.summary: quests.step(run) does one bounded bite and returns at once with a status: working, step_done, need_travel (a zone), need_combat (a target), need_loot, complete or blocked (a reason). The runner never waits; the caller acts on the need_* statuses and calls again.
examples.code:
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Basics",
    steps = {
        { type = "command", command = 'CheckZone "Fixture Vale"' },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 4,0,9" },
        { type = "command", command = 'Pull "a fixture beetle"' },
        { type = "command", command = "LootAll" },
    },
}
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ onKill = function(_, w) w.lootPending = true end })
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})

local trace = {}
for _ = 1, 40 do
    local status, info = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = status
    if status == "need_travel" then print("need_travel " .. info); deps.nav.travelTo(info, { pack = true })
    elseif status == "need_combat" then deps.combat.engage(info)
    elseif status == "need_loot" then deps.economy.lootGrab({})
    elseif status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end
    world.tick(5000)
end

DOCS.eq(trace[1], "need_travel", "CheckZone hands the zone change back")
DOCS.eq(trace[#trace], "complete", "the last status")
DOCS.has(table.concat(trace, " "), "need_combat", "a pull is handed back as need_combat")
DOCS.has(table.concat(trace, " "), "need_loot", "a loot pass is handed back as need_loot")
DOCS.has(table.concat(trace, " "), "step_done", "a finished step says step_done")
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 1, "the MM step walked")
examples.expect: The trace shows each status once in order; the walk, the trip, the fight and the loot each happened once.

examples.title: Load a quest pack from its file
examples.summary: quests.load(path) reads a pack file as pure data (it may not run code) and hands back a handle to start. A file that is a quest line index, not a quest, still loads, but its run is blocked with what it is.
examples.code:
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)

local handle = assert(quests.load("tests/eb/docs_examples/quests/lib/packs/fixture_lanterns.lua"))
print(("loaded %s: %d steps"):format(handle.name, #handle.quest.steps))
local run = quests.start(handle, {})
local status
for _ = 1, 30 do
    status = quests.step(run)
    if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end
    world.tick(1000)
end

-- a quest LINE index (the order of a line's quests) is data too, but it is not a quest
local index = { quest = { schema = "eb-questline/1", name = "Fixture Line" }, name = "Fixture Line",
                notRunnable = "an eb-questline/1 index (the order of a quest line), not a quest: run the line's quests" }
local st, why = quests.step(quests.start(index, {}))

DOCS.eq(handle.quest.quest_name, "The Fixture Lanterns", "the handle carries the pack")
DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "the pack ran to its end")
DOCS.eq(world.did("click"), 2, "both lanterns were clicked")
DOCS.eq(st, "blocked", "an index file is not run")
DOCS.has(why, "not a quest", "and says what it is")
examples.expect: The pack loads with its name and five steps and runs to complete; the line index loads as not runnable.

examples.title: Save where a quest is, and resume there
examples.summary: After a step finishes, quests.pointer(run) is the resume point to keep: { step, zone, x, y, z }. quests.resume(handle, pointer) starts a fresh run at that step, so a restart never repeats the steps already done.
examples.code:
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Rounds",
    steps = {
        { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1" },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 2,0,2" },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 3,0,3" },
    },
}
local handle = { quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }

local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start(handle, {})
quests.step(run); quests.step(run)                -- two steps done
local pointer = quests.pointer(run)               -- keep this (write it OFF the game thread)
print("resume at step " .. pointer.step)

-- later (a reload, a new session): a fresh world and a fresh runner
local deps2, world2 = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests2 = require("eb.quest").bind(deps2)
local resumed = quests2.resume(handle, pointer)
local status
repeat status = quests2.step(resumed) until status == "complete" or status == "blocked"

DOCS.eq(pointer.step, 3, "the next step to run")
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 2, "the first run walked two waypoints")
DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "the resumed run finishes")
DOCS.eq(world2.did("walk"), 1, "and walks only the step that was left")
examples.expect: The pointer after two steps is step 3; the resumed run walks only the last waypoint.

examples.title: Where does the current step want the character?
examples.summary: quests.stepTarget(run) reads the step about to run: x, y, z (and its zone) for a move, the zone for a travel step, { actor, zone } for a step about an NPC. A map window or the brain can show or pre-plan it without running the step.
examples.code:
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Targets",
    steps = {
        { type = "command", command = "MM 10,2,30" },
        { type = "command", command = 'CheckZone "Fixture Vale"' },
        { type = "command", command = "HailActor Warden Fixturo,1" },
    },
}
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ zone = "Fixture Vale" })
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})

local x, y, z = quests.stepTarget(run)                -- step 1: the move
quests.step(run)
local _, _, _, zone = quests.stepTarget(run)          -- step 2: the travel
quests.step(run)
local who = quests.stepTarget(run)                    -- step 3: the hail
print("hail target: " .. who.actor)

DOCS.eq(x, 10, "x"); DOCS.eq(y, 2, "y"); DOCS.eq(z, 30, "z")
DOCS.eq(zone, "Fixture Vale", "a travel step answers its zone")
DOCS.eq(who.actor, "Warden Fixturo", "an NPC step answers { actor }")
examples.expect: The move step answers its point, the travel step its zone, and the hail step its actor.

examples.title: Skip a step on a condition or on the journal
examples.summary: A step's condition is read before it starts: false plus skip_if_condition_false skips it. SkipIfJournal "<line>",N skips the next N steps when the journal already shows that line done, so a pack resumed mid-quest does not redo work.
examples.code:
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Conditions",
    continues_later = true,              -- the quest is still in the journal when these steps end, on purpose
    steps = {
        { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1", condition = "${Me.Level} >= 120", skip_if_condition_false = true },
        { type = "command", command = 'SkipIfJournal "Gather the fixture reeds",2' },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 2,0,2" },
        { type = "command", command = 'ClickActor "a fixture reed"' },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 3,0,3" },
    },
}
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ level = 100 })
world.journal.give("Fixture Conditions", { "Gather the fixture reeds" })
world.journal.check("Fixture Conditions", "Gather the fixture reeds")      -- that part is already done

local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do status = quests.step(run); if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end end
print("walks: " .. world.did("walk"))

DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "the pack finishes")
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 1, "only the last walk ran")
DOCS.eq(world.did("click"), 0, "the skipped click never happened")
examples.expect: The level-gated walk is skipped at level 100, and the two steps behind SkipIfJournal are skipped because the line is done.

examples.title: Wait for the journal to move on
examples.summary: WaitForQuestStep "<quest>","<line>",<seconds> holds the pack (status working, never a blocking wait) until the journal shows that line, or ticks it. At the time limit the step is blocked, or with -continue it says so and goes on.
examples.code:
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Escort", continues_later = true,
    steps = {
        { type = "command", command = 'WaitForQuestStep "Fixture Escort","Speak to the ferryman",60' },
        { type = "command", command = "HailActor a fixture ferryman" },
    },
}
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
world.journal.give("Fixture Escort", { "Escort the ferryman to the pier" })

local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local waited, status = 0, nil
for _ = 1, 30 do
    status = quests.step(run)
    if status ~= "working" then break end
    waited = waited + 1
    world.tick(5000)
    if world.now >= 15000 then world.journal.add("Fixture Escort", "Speak to the ferryman") end   -- the escort arrives
end
repeat status = quests.step(run) until status == "complete" or status == "blocked"
print(("waited %d tick(s) for the journal"):format(waited))

-- a wait whose line never comes: blocked at its limit (10 s here)
local deps2, world2 = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
world2.journal.give("Fixture Escort", { "Escort the ferryman to the pier" })
local q2 = require("eb.quest").bind(deps2)
