local run2 = q2.start({ quest = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Escort", steps = {
    { type = "command", command = 'WaitForQuestStep "Fixture Escort","Speak to the ferryman",10' } } },
    name = "Fixture Escort" }, {})
local st2, why2
for _ = 1, 10 do st2, why2 = q2.step(run2); if st2 ~= "working" then break end; world2.tick(5000) end

DOCS.eq(waited, 3, "working while the line was missing (0 s, 5 s, 10 s)")
DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "then the pack went on")
DOCS.eq(world.did("hail"), 1, "and hailed the ferryman")
DOCS.eq(st2, "blocked", "no line in time: blocked")
DOCS.has(why2, "after 10s", "with the limit in the reason")
examples.expect: The wait reports working until the escort NPC's line shows up 15 s in, then the pack goes on; a wait that never sees its line is blocked at its limit.

examples.title: Packs never fast travel
examples.summary: Inside a pack the destination is always reached the ground way: SmartTravelTo hands the zone back as need_travel (the zone's own transit), FastTravel is refused with the reason, and a flight-only step (FlyUp) stops because EB never flies: it walks the zone's mesh and nothing else.
examples.code:
local function once(line)
    local deps = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ zone = "Fixture Docks" })
    local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
    local run = quests.start({ quest = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Travel",
        steps = { { type = "command", command = line } } }, name = "Fixture Travel" }, {})
    return quests.step(run)
end

local s1, info1 = once('SmartTravelTo "Fixture Vale"')
local s2, info2 = once('FastTravel "Fixture Vale"')
local s3, info3 = once("FlyUp")
print("FastTravel -> " .. s2)

DOCS.eq(s1, "need_travel", "SmartTravelTo takes the ground way")
DOCS.eq(info1, "Fixture Vale", "to the zone the step names")
DOCS.eq(s2, "blocked", "FastTravel is refused in a pack")
DOCS.has(info2, "packs never fast travel", "with the reason")
DOCS.eq(s3, "blocked", "a flight-only step stops")
DOCS.has(info3, "EB never flies", "EB never flies: it walks the mesh only")
examples.expect: SmartTravelTo answers need_travel; FastTravel and FlyUp are blocked with their reasons (EB never flies).

examples.title: What a pack can say: the verb list
examples.summary: eb.quest knows every verb a pack may use. supported(verb) answers yes or no, ported() lists each verb with what it does and its group, refused() lists the verbs EB refuses on purpose with the reason. A line with a verb nobody handles stops the run with a clear reason; it is never guessed or skipped.
examples.code:
local Q = require("eb.quest")
local ported, refused = Q.ported(), Q.refused()
local groups = {}
for _, v in ipairs(ported) do groups[v.group] = (groups[v.group] or 0) + 1 end

local deps = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests = Q.bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Verbs",
    steps = { { type = "command", command = 'FrobnicateLever "a fixture lever"' } } }, name = "Fixture Verbs" }, {})
local st, why = quests.step(run)
print("FrobnicateLever -> " .. st)

DOCS.check(Q.supported("HailActor"), "HailActor is a pack verb")
DOCS.check(Q.supported("mm"), "verbs match in any case")
DOCS.check(not Q.supported("FrobnicateLever"), "a made-up verb is not")
DOCS.check(#ported > 200, "hundreds of verbs are ported")
DOCS.check(groups.npc and groups.travel and groups.quest, "grouped by concern: npc, travel, quest ...")
DOCS.check(#refused > 5, "the refused ones are listed with their reason")
DOCS.eq(st, "blocked", "an unknown verb stops the run")
DOCS.has(why, "not handled", "and says why")
examples.expect: HailActor is supported, a made-up verb is not, and running it stops the pack with "not handled".

examples.title: A pack's own way into a zone
examples.summary: zone_routes names how this pack gets into a zone: each way is a list of steps run as a sub-sequence when CheckZone needs that zone. A way that fails moves on to the next; only when every written way is spent does CheckZone hand the zone to the zone's allowed transit.
examples.code:
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Crossing",
    zone_routes = {
        ["Fixture Vale"] = {
            { why = "via the ferry", steps = { { type = "command", command = 'Transit "Vale Landing | a fixture ferryman"' } } },
            { why = "via the pier bell", steps = {
                { type = "command", command = "MM 30,0,5" },
                { type = "command", command = 'TravelBell "Fixture Vale"' } } },
        },
    },
    steps = { { type = "command", command = 'CheckZone "Fixture Vale"' } },
}
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ zone = "Fixture Docks" })
deps.act.transit = function() return "blocked", "the ferry is not running" end    -- the first way fails
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})

local trace, status, info = {}, nil, nil
for _ = 1, 40 do
    status, info = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = status
    if status == "working" and tostring(info):find("running route", 1, true) then print(info) end
    if status == "need_travel" then deps.nav.travelTo(info, { pack = true }) end   -- the bell's ride
    if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end
    world.tick(5000)
end

DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "in the zone")
DOCS.eq(world.zone, "Fixture Vale", "arrived")
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 1, "walked to the bell (the second way's first step)")
examples.expect: The first way's ride fails, the second way (walk to the bell, ring it) is taken, and the pack arrives without a need_travel.

examples.title: A quest that goes into an instance, in a group
examples.summary: When a pack's CheckZone names an instance and the box is a group member (not the driver), it waits in the hub at a barrier for the tank to zone the group in. It never walks the instance's route itself. The driver goes on.
examples.code:
local PACK = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Depths",
               steps = { { type = "command", command = 'CheckZone "Fixture Hollow: Heroic"' } } }

local function firstStatus(amDriver)
    local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ zone = "Fixture Docks", groupCount = 3,
        amDriver = amDriver })
    local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
    local st, info = quests.step(quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {}))
    return st, info, world
end

local stM, infoM, wM = firstStatus(false)
print(infoM)
local stD = firstStatus(true)

DOCS.eq(stM, "working", "the member waits")
DOCS.has(infoM, "waiting for the tank", "for the tank to zone the group in")
DOCS.eq(wM.did("barrier"), 1, "at a crew barrier in the hub")
DOCS.eq(wM.did("walk") + wM.did("travel"), 0, "and moves nowhere on its own")
DOCS.check(stD == "need_travel" or stD == "working", "the driver goes on")
examples.expect: The member answers working and waits at the hub barrier; the driver's same step goes on.

examples.title: Read a quest's journal lines
examples.summary: eb.quest.journal reads the quest tracker the way packs need it: lineState(text, quest) answers open, done, gone (the quest is up but its stage moved on) or nil (not on the tracker). A line matches its text inside the objective, else word by word with small typos forgiven.
examples.code:
local Journal = require("eb.quest.journal")

-- a reader: the game's quest tracker rows (EB's game layer supplies these in game)
local reader = {
    trackerRows = function()
        return { { name = "The Fixture Reeds", parts = {
            { text = "Gather three fixture reeds", progress = { current = 1, total = 3 } },
            { text = "Speak to Warden Fixturo", progress = { complete = true } } } } }
    end,
}
local J = Journal.new(reader)

local open = J:lineState("Gather three fixture reeds", "The Fixture Reeds")
print("Gather three fixture reeds -> " .. open)

DOCS.eq(open, "open", "1 of 3: still open")
DOCS.eq(J:lineState("Speak to Warden Fixturo", "The Fixture Reeds"), "done", "a checked line")
DOCS.eq(J:lineState("Return to the docks", "The Fixture Reeds"), "gone", "the quest is up but no part holds it")
DOCS.eq(J:lineState("Gather thre fixture reed", "The Fixture Reeds"), "open", "small typos are forgiven")
DOCS.eq(J:lineState("Anything", "Another Quest"), nil, "a quest the tracker does not show")
DOCS.check(J:questActive("The Fixture Reeds"), "the quest is on the tracker")
DOCS.eq(#J:openLines("The Fixture Reeds"), 1, "one unfinished objective")
DOCS.check(Journal.lineHolds("Collect 3 fixture reeds (1/3)", "fixture reeds"), "lineHolds: text inside an objective")
examples.expect: The open, done and gone lines read as such; a slightly misspelled line still matches; an untracked quest reads nil.

examples.title: A pack's gates: level, a held sibling, a zone's wing
examples.summary: Before the first step the runner checks the pack's gates: level_required stops a character that is too low (with the reason), skip_if_holding skips the quest while a sibling from the same giver is held. Zone names compare the hub-aware way: a hub is never its own instance wing.
examples.code:
local function firstStep(pack, opts, held)
    local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make(opts)
    if held then world.journal.give(held, { "a line" }) end
    local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
    return quests.step(quests.start({ quest = pack, name = pack.quest_name }, {}))
end

local st1, why1 = firstStep({ schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Trial", level_required = 60,
    steps = { { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1" } } }, { level = 20 })
print(why1)
local st2, why2 = firstStep({ schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Chore B", optional = true,
    skip_if_holding = { "Fixture Chore A" }, steps = { { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1" } } }, {}, "Fixture Chore A")

local G = require("eb.quest.gates")
DOCS.eq(st1, "blocked", "too low: the run stops")
DOCS.has(why1, "level 60 required", "and says so")
DOCS.eq(st2, "complete", "a held sibling: this one is skipped for now")
DOCS.has(why2, "sibling", "with the reason")
DOCS.check(G.zoneEqual("Fixture Hollow", "Fixture Hollow"), "a zone equals itself")
DOCS.check(not G.zoneEqual("Fixture Hollow", "Fixture Hollow: Heroic"), "a hub is not its wing")
DOCS.check(G.isInstanceZone("Fixture Hollow: Heroic"), "a ':' tag names an instance")
DOCS.check(G.flags({}).pack, "every quest is a pack (no fast travel) unless it says no_smart_travel = false")
examples.expect: The level gate blocks at level 20, the sibling gate completes as skipped, and the zone compares answer as the game names zones.

examples.title: Add your own pack verb
examples.summary: eb.quest.verbs.register(keys, fn, about, group) adds a verb every pack can use. The handler gets the step's context: ctx.cmd (the parsed line), ctx:zone(), ctx.state (this step's own scratch table) and answers with ctx:done, ctx:work, ctx:travel, ctx:combat, ctx:loot, ctx:block or ctx:stop. It must return at once and never wait.
examples.code:
local verbs = require("eb.quest.verbs")
verbs.register({ "ringgong", "gong" }, function(ctx)
    local times = tonumber(verbs.csv(ctx.cmd.rest)[1]) or 1
    ctx.state.rung = (ctx.state.rung or 0) + 1                 -- per-step scratch, kept across ticks
    if ctx.state.rung < times then return ctx:work("ringing (" .. ctx.state.rung .. "/" .. times .. ")") end
    return ctx:done(("rang the fixture gong %d times in %s"):format(times, tostring(ctx:zone())))
end, "ring the fixture gong N times (a docs example verb)", "act")

local PACK = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Gong", steps = {
    { type = "command", command = "RingGong 3" },
    { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1" } } }
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local trace, msg = {}, nil
for _ = 1, 10 do
    local st, info = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = st
    if st == "step_done" and tostring(info):find("gong", 1, true) then msg = info end
    if st == "complete" or st == "blocked" then break end
end
print(msg)

DOCS.check(require("eb.quest").supported("ringgong"), "the new verb is supported")
DOCS.eq(trace[1], "working", "tick 1: still ringing")
DOCS.eq(trace[3], "step_done", "tick 3: rung three times")
DOCS.eq(trace[#trace], "complete", "the pack goes on and completes")
examples.expect: The custom verb waits two ticks while it rings, then the pack goes on and completes.

examples.title: Stop a quest run at once
examples.summary: deps.shouldStop is asked first on every step: when it answers true the step returns blocked, "stopped by request", before touching anything. Because the runner never waits, a stop takes effect on the very next tick.
examples.code:
local stop = false
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
deps.shouldStop = function() return stop end              -- e.g. your own "eb stop" handling
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Patrol", steps = {
    { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1" }, { type = "command", command = "MM 2,0,2" } } },
    name = "Fixture Patrol" }, {})

local first = quests.step(run)
stop = true
local st, why = quests.step(run)
print(why)

DOCS.eq(first, "step_done", "the first step ran")
DOCS.eq(st, "blocked", "the stop is honoured on the next tick")
DOCS.eq(why, "stopped by request", "with that reason")
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 1, "nothing moved after the stop")
examples.expect: The first tick walks; after the stop flag goes up the next tick is blocked and nothing else moves.

examples.title: The quest commands from the console
examples.summary: Boot EB offline and type the quest commands the way you would in game. eb ql starts a quest line (or one quest) by its name and runs it as EB's goal; eb pl runs a power-level route; eb queue lines them up; eb dialog reads and answers what an NPC shows; eb timer leaves a reminder or runs a line later. With nothing running yet, each one answers at once and says what it would do.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script: lines exactly as you type them
local ql = a.console("eb ql status")
local pl = a.console("eb pl status")
local queue = a.console("eb queue")
local dialog = a.console("eb dialog")
local timer = a.console("eb timer add tea 5m the tea is ready")
local help = a.console("eb help quest")
print(ql)
print(queue)

-- check
DOCS.has(ql, "ql: no quest line - eb ql start <line or quest>", "eb ql answers: no line is running yet")
DOCS.has(pl, "pl: no route running", "eb pl answers: no route is running")
DOCS.has(queue, "queue: stopped, 0 waiting", "the quest queue is empty")
DOCS.has(dialog, "dialog: no conversation is open", "eb dialog reads what an NPC shows: nothing now")
DOCS.has(timer, "timer #1 tea", "eb timer leaves a reminder")
DOCS.has(help, "ql", "eb help quest lists the quest commands")
a.stop()
examples.expect: eb ql status says no line is running, eb pl status no route, the queue is empty, no conversation is open, and eb help quest lists the domain.

examples.title: EB Overseer from the console
examples.summary: eb overseer is the Overseer's one command: run a pass, stop it, read where it stands, set this character's options (a season or a colour is ONE choice), keep the PC's preferences (who a click is for, after each run), and buy missions with words a crew line carries to every box (eb all overseer buy season 3 colour blue ...). A word whose part is not on this box yet says so; a game read that waits for its live proof answers held, in words.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script: lines exactly as you type them
local set = a.console("eb overseer set neutral on")
local opts = a.console("eb overseer options")
local who = a.console("eb overseer who mygroup")
local status = a.console("eb overseer status")
local stop = a.console("eb overseer stop")
print((tostring(set):gsub(" %(.*$", "")))

-- the buy's words: what EB's Overseer window sends to every box of its Who (the dash flags read as EB's own words)
local OV = require("eb.mcpverbs.overseer")
local buy = require("eb.overseer.trip.args").parse("-season 3 -colour blue -num 12 -amount 10 -noscribe",
    require("eb.overseer.options").defaults())

-- check
DOCS.has(set, "overseer set: neutral on", "an option is set and read back")
DOCS.has(opts, "neutral", "the character's options list it as on")
DOCS.has(who, "who: My group", "who a click is for is kept for the PC")
DOCS.has(status, "Overseer: idle", "no pass has run yet")
DOCS.has(stop, "nothing of the Overseer runs on this box", "stop finds nothing running")
DOCS.eq(OV.buyWords(buy.opts), "season 3 colour blue num 12 copies 10 noscribe destroy off gettogh off", "the flags read as EB's buy words")
a.stop()
examples.expect: set neutral on reads back and options lists it; who mygroup is kept for every box of the PC; the buy's dash flags read as EB's words; status says the pass is idle; stop finds nothing running.

examples.title: A pack verb that reads the journal and the world
examples.summary: A verb's handler gets the step's context. Besides the statuses it can answer, the context reads for it: ctx:completedDone() (the step's completed line is done in the journal), ctx:truth(condition), ctx:zoneEqual, ctx:groupCount() and ctx:inGuildHall(); ctx:log writes a line to the run's log.
examples.code:
local verbs = require("eb.quest.verbs")
verbs.register("lightlantern", function(ctx)
    if ctx:completedDone() then return ctx:done("the journal says the lantern is lit") end
    if ctx:truth("${Me.Level} >= 20") ~= true then return ctx:stop("too low for the lantern") end
    if not ctx:zoneEqual(ctx:zone(), "Fixture Docks") then return ctx:travel("Fixture Docks") end
    if not ctx.state.clicked then
        ctx.state.clicked = true
        ctx.dep.act.click({ name = "a fixture lantern", double = true })
        ctx:log("lit the lantern in %s (level gate passed, %s)", ctx:zone(), ctx:groupCount() == 1 and "solo" or "grouped")
    end
    return ctx:work("waiting for the journal")
end, "light the fixture lantern (a docs example verb)", "act")

local PACK = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Lanterns", continues_later = true, steps = {
    { type = "command", command = "LightLantern", completed = "Light the fixture lantern" } } }

-- offline stand-in for the game: the journal holds the line; clicking the lantern ticks it on the next tick
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({
    onClick = function(spec, w) w.journal.check("Fixture Lanterns", "Light the fixture lantern") end })
world.journal.give("Fixture Lanterns", { "Light the fixture lantern" })

-- your script
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local trace = {}
for _ = 1, 6 do
    local st = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = st
    if st == "complete" or st == "blocked" then break end
    world.tick(1000)
end
print(world.lines[1])

-- check
DOCS.eq(world.did("click"), 1, "the lantern was clicked once")
DOCS.eq(trace[1], "working", "then the step waited for the journal")
DOCS.eq(trace[#trace], "complete", "and the pack completed once the journal said so")
DOCS.has(world.lines[1], "Fixture Docks", "ctx:log wrote to the run's log")
examples.expect: The verb lights the lantern once, waits for the journal, and its step is done when the journal says so.

examples.title: The verb registry's parsers and its refusals
examples.summary: The helpers every verb's arguments go through: flags takes the -flag words out of a hail, splitFields keeps a ${...} condition whole, isComment spots a note line. dispatch runs one parsed line through its verb and turns a refused verb, or one nobody registered, into a final "blocked" with the reason - a pack is never guessed at.
examples.code:
require("eb.quest")                                   -- loads every verb family into the registry
local verbs = require("eb.quest.verbs")

-- your script
local rest, found = verbs.flags("-peaceful,Warden Fixturo,1")
print(("hail args: %s (%s)"):format(rest, found.peaceful and "peaceful" or "-"))
local fields = verbs.splitFields('${If[${Me.X} < 400,TRUE,FALSE]},60')
local unknown, uwhy = verbs.dispatch({ cmd = verbs.parse("DanceWithFixtures 3") })
local refusedRow = verbs.refusedList()[1]
local ctx = { cmd = verbs.parse(refusedRow.verb .. " Fixture Vale") }
local refused, rwhy = verbs.dispatch(ctx)

-- check
DOCS.eq(rest, "Warden Fixturo,1", "the flag word is taken out")
DOCS.check(found.peaceful, "and reported")
DOCS.eq(#fields, 2, "the condition is one field, the seconds another")
DOCS.check(verbs.isComment("# a note in the pack"), "a # line is a comment")
DOCS.eq(unknown, "blocked", "a verb nobody registered stops the pack")
DOCS.has(uwhy, "not handled", "and says so")
DOCS.eq(refused, "blocked", "a refused verb stops the pack")
DOCS.check(ctx.final == true, "for good, not as a block to recover from")
DOCS.has(rwhy, refusedRow.why, "with the reason it is refused")
examples.expect: The hail's -peaceful flag is found, the wait's condition stays one field, and both an unknown and a refused verb stop with a reason.

examples.title: Is a quest on the tracker?
examples.summary: A journal view reads the quest tracker through any reader with trackerRows(). J:rows() gives every tracked quest and its objectives; J:questHeld(name) says whether a quest is tracked - and answers nil, not false, when the tracker reads empty and it cannot tell.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game: the quest tracker
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
world.journal.give("Fixture Lanterns", { "Light the fixture lantern" })

-- your script
local Journal = require("eb.quest.journal")
local J = Journal.new(deps.journal)
for _, row in ipairs(J:rows()) do print(("tracked: %s (%d line)"):format(row.name, #row.parts)) end

-- check
DOCS.eq(J:questHeld("Fixture Lanterns"), true, "the quest is tracked")
DOCS.eq(J:questHeld("Fixture Bells"), false, "another one is not")
world.journal.complete("Fixture Lanterns")
DOCS.eq(J:questHeld("Fixture Bells"), nil, "an empty tracker cannot tell")
DOCS.eq(Journal.new(nil):questHeld("Fixture Lanterns"), nil, "nor can a view with no reader")
examples.expect: The tracked quest is held, another is not, and an empty tracker cannot tell.

examples.title: Run a pack on the runner's core, with only your own verbs
examples.summary: eb.quest.quests is the runner without the verb families loaded: register the verbs you want, bind the core to your adapters, and step a pack. Here a two-step pack of one custom verb runs to completion, and stepTarget reads a move step's point without running it.
examples.code:
local Q = require("eb.quest.quests")
local verbs = require("eb.quest.verbs")
local chimes = 0
verbs.register("chime", function(ctx) chimes = chimes + 1; return ctx:done("chimed") end, "chime once", "act")

local PACK = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Chimes", steps = {
    { type = "command", command = "Chime" }, { type = "command", command = "Chime" } } }

-- offline stand-in for the game's adapters
local deps = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()

-- your script
local api = Q.bind(deps)
local run = api.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local status
for _ = 1, 6 do status = Q.step(run); if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end end
print(("chimed %d times, then: %s"):format(chimes, status))

local moveRun = api.start({ quest = { quest_name = "Fixture Walk", steps = { { command = "MM 4,0,5", zone = "Fixture Docks" } } } }, {})
local x, y, z, zone = Q.stepTarget(moveRun)

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "the pack completed")
DOCS.eq(chimes, 2, "each chime step ran once")
DOCS.eq(x, 4, "stepTarget reads the move step's x")
DOCS.eq(z, 5, "and z")
DOCS.eq(zone, "Fixture Docks", "and its zone, without running it")
examples.expect: Both chime steps finish, the pack completes, and stepTarget names the move step's point.

examples.title: Read a pack's condition text yourself
examples.summary: eb.quest.cond reads the ${...} conditions packs carry, over a world snapshot: expand fills the terms, truth decides true, false or unknown, conditionExpr normalizes a bare condition first. A term EB cannot read is UNKNOWN - never a guess - and show() makes it readable (question marks).
examples.code:
local cond = require("eb.quest.cond")

-- a world snapshot, as the runner hands one to every step
local snap = { level = 100, zone = "fixture_docks", x = 10, y = 0, z = 20 }
local env = { snap = snap }

-- your script
print(cond.expand("level ${Me.Level} in ${Zone.ShortName}", env))
local ok = cond.truth("${Me.Level} >= 20", env)
local wrapped = cond.conditionExpr("${Me.Level} >= 20")
local unknown = cond.truth("${Me.GetGameData[Self.Fixture].Label} == 3", env)
local kept = cond.expandKnown("go to ${Me.GetGameData[Self.Fixture].Label}", env)

-- the same reader a run uses, built over its journal and adapters
local deps = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local run = require("eb.quest.quests").bind(deps).start({ quest = { quest_name = "Fixture Walk", steps = {} } }, {})
local renv = require("eb.quest.quests").condEnv(run, snap)

-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "the comparison holds")
DOCS.has(wrapped, "If[", "a comparison is wrapped before it is read")
DOCS.eq(unknown, nil, "an unreadable term is unknown, not false")
DOCS.eq(kept, nil, "expandKnown refuses a text with an unknown in it")
DOCS.check(not cond.show("a " .. cond.UNKNOWN .. " b"):find("\1", 1, true), "show() leaves no marker in the text")
DOCS.eq(cond.truth("${Me.Level} >= 20", renv), true, "the run's own reader answers the same")
examples.expect: The level and zone terms fill in, the comparison is true, and an unreadable term comes back unknown.

examples.title: Pick a letter for OpenMail
examples.summary: The mail verbs pick a letter by its subject (and, when given, by the sender's whole name) at the nearest mailbox. The rules are pure: parseArgs reads the verb's arguments, shown takes the game's hidden key off a field, and pick finds the first letter that fits and counts how many do.
examples.code:
local mail = require("eb.quest.verbs.mail").mail       -- loading it registers the verbs; .mail holds the rules

-- the inbox rows, in the order the mailbox lists them (offline: invented letters)
local rows = { { subject = "Fixture Fair results" }, { subject = ":47541fd6e0da31d6:Your fixture lantern" },
               { subject = "Fixture Fair tickets" } }

-- your script: OpenMail "fixture lantern",take
local a = mail.parseArgs('"fixture lantern",take', false)
local index, fits = mail.pick(a, rows)
print(("letter %d of %d that fit"):format(index, fits))

-- check
DOCS.eq(a.subject, "fixture lantern", "the subject")
DOCS.eq(a.take, true, "the take word")
DOCS.eq(index, 2, "the letter that fits")
DOCS.eq(mail.shown(rows[2].subject), "Your fixture lantern", "the game's hidden key is taken off")
DOCS.eq(mail.pick(mail.parseArgs('""', false), rows), nil, "no subject and no sender picks nothing")
examples.expect: The second letter fits the subject; the take word is read; the hidden key is taken off.

examples.title: Loop one instance: wait inside until it can be reset
examples.summary: runner:loop runs one instance again and again (until stopped by default; laps caps it here). Looping ONE zone, the tank waits out the reuse timer INSIDE the cleared copy where the run ended, then leaves by the exit door, resets the copy from outside and goes back in. The first lap is a rerun of the copy we stand in.
examples.code:
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    hub = { zone = "fixture_docks", entrance = { loc = { 0, 0, 0 }, tolerance = 8 },
            door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" } },
    route = {
        { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" },
        { id = "exit.walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, -38 } } },
        { id = "exit", act = "zoneout", via = "exit" },
    },
    loop = { reset = "self", rerun_first = true },      -- the defaults: until stopped, first lap a rerun
}
local CAPTAIN = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named",
                  phases = { { do_ = { { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } } }

-- offline stand-in: we stand inside a copy we just cleared; it can be reset in 5 minutes, and 0 after each lap
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy", reuseNow = 300, reuse = { 0, 0, 0 },
    alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function() return CAPTAIN end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local ok, why, report = runner:loop(assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow")), { laps = 2 })
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("waiting INSIDE", 1, true) then print(l) end end

DOCS.check(ok, "the loop ended cleanly: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(why, "laps done", "after the two laps asked for")
DOCS.eq(report.laps, 2, "two laps")
DOCS.check(world.said("waiting INSIDE the cleared copy"), "the timer was waited out inside")
for _, c in ipairs(world.calls) do
    if c[1] == "reset" then DOCS.eq(c[3], "fixture_docks", "every reset is done from outside the copy") end
end
DOCS.check(world.did("reset") >= 2, "a reset before each lap")
examples.expect: Two laps run; the 5-minute wait happens inside the copy, every reset is done from outside, and the loop ends with "laps done".

examples.title: Loop windows and the reset decision
examples.summary: eb ic loop <file> [minutes] [difficulty]: no minutes (or 0) loops until stopped. parseLoopArgs splits the line, loopMinutes picks the window (the command line over the file's loop.max_minutes), and decide says what the tank does between laps: reset now, wait the timer out, or end because the wait outlasts the window.
examples.code:
local IC = require("eb.ic")
local a = assert(IC.parseLoopArgs("fixture_hollow 480 [Heroic I]"))
print(("%s for %d min at %s"):format(a.file, a.minutes, a.difficulty))
local forever = assert(IC.parseLoopArgs("fixture_hollow"))

DOCS.eq(a.minutes, 480, "minutes")
DOCS.eq(a.difficulty, "[Heroic I]", "the rest of the line is the difficulty")
DOCS.eq(forever.minutes, 0, "no minutes = 0 = until stopped")
DOCS.eq(select(2, IC.parseLoopArgs("")), IC.LOOP_USAGE, "an empty line answers the usage")
DOCS.eq(IC.loopMinutes({ loop = { max_minutes = 90 } }, {}), 90, "the file's window when the line names none")
DOCS.eq(IC.loopMinutes({ loop = { max_minutes = 90 } }, { minutes = 30 }), 30, "the line wins")
-- decide(seconds until the copy can be reset, minutes left in the loop; -1 = uncapped)
DOCS.eq(IC.decide(0, 60), "reset", "the timer is up: reset now")
DOCS.eq(IC.decide(600, -1), "wait", "an uncapped loop waits out any timer")
DOCS.eq(IC.decide(7200, 30), "end", "a 2 h wait past a 30 min window ends the loop")
examples.expect: The line splits into file, minutes and difficulty; the three decisions come out reset, wait and end.

examples.title: Chores at the end of each run
examples.summary: A loop's between option turns chores on (all off by default): each box's saved T.S.E first, then a repair trip when this box's gear is under 90%, then the maintenance cycle. They run once at the END of each run, inside where it ended, and a chore that cannot be done is said and skipped - it never stops the loop.
examples.code:
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    route = { { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" } },
    loop = { rerun_first = false },                   -- the first lap runs where we stand
}
local CAPTAIN = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named",
                  phases = { { do_ = { { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } } }

local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy", alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 },
    upkeep = { gear = 62 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function() return CAPTAIN end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local ok, _, report = runner:loop(assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow")),
    { laps = 1, between = { tse = true, repair = true, maintenance = true } })
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("gear at", 1, true) then print(l) end end

local chores = report.chores[1]
DOCS.check(ok, "the loop ends after its lap")
DOCS.eq(chores.tse, "done", "the saved T.S.E ran on every box")
DOCS.eq(chores.repair, "repaired", "gear under 90%: the repair trip")
DOCS.eq(chores.maintenance, "unwired", "no maintenance runner here: skipped, said, the loop goes on")
DOCS.eq(world.did("hall"), 1, "called to the guild hall once")
examples.expect: After lap 1 the T.S.E ran and the gear at 62% was repaired; maintenance is unwired here, so it is skipped and said.

examples.title: Hand the brain a chore loop
examples.summary: eb.loops builds a chore loop as a brain goal: overseer, errands, trainer, mercenary or collections. Give it an activities provider (the window driver it acts through) and set it on the running brain; the brain advances it one bite per tick between its own interrupts. A trainer only ever spends points on abilities YOUR list names.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: EB booted on the offline world; the provider below stands in for the trainer window driver
local a = DOCS.app()
local points, trained, claimed = 2, {}, false
local provider = {
    near = function() return nil end,                          -- nil: no trainer NPC needed for these upgrades
    points = function() return { training = points, aa = 0 } end,
    trainable = function() return { { id = "t1", name = "Fixture Ward", kind = "training" },
                                    { id = "t2", name = "Fixture Bloom", kind = "training" } } end,
    train = function(id) trained[#trained + 1] = id; points = points - 1; return "done" end,
    researchClaim = function() claimed = true; return "done" end,
    researchStart = function() return "done" end,
    researchNext = function() return nil end,
}

-- your script
local Loops = require("eb.loops")
local brain = a.app.brain
brain:setGoal(Loops.new({ kind = "trainer", params = { act = { trainer = provider }, trainList = { "Fixture Ward" } } }))
a.w.runFor(5000)                                   -- the brain ticks about 4 times a second
for _, l in ipairs(a.app.brainLog) do if l:find("done", 1, true) then print(l:match("goal .*")) end end

DOCS.eq(#trained, 2, "both points were spent")
DOCS.eq(trained[1], "t1", "on the listed ability")
DOCS.eq(trained[2], "t1", "and only on it")
DOCS.check(claimed, "finished research was claimed (free, safe)")
DOCS.eq(brain:activeGoal(), nil, "the goal finished and left the brain idle")
a.stop()
examples.expect: The brain runs the trainer pass on the booted box: it trains the listed ability with both points, claims finished research, and leaves the unlisted one alone.

examples.title: The loops' own decisions: an upgrade and a hire
examples.summary: The chore loops keep their choices in small pure functions you can call yourself: the trainer's next upgrade comes from YOUR priority list (exact name first, then a part of a name, and it never guesses), and the mercenary pick takes the cheapest offer of the role you ask for.
examples.code:
local Trainer = require("eb.loops.trainer")
local Mercenary = require("eb.loops.mercenary")

local trainable = { { id = "t1", name = "Fixture Ward", kind = "training" },
                    { id = "t2", name = "Fixture Bloom", kind = "aa" } }
local pick = Trainer.pickNext(trainable, { "Fixture Bloom", "Fixture Ward" }, false)   -- AA spends not allowed
local withAA = Trainer.pickNext(trainable, { "Fixture Bloom", "Fixture Ward" }, true)
local none, why = Trainer.pickNext(trainable, {}, true)
print("next upgrade: " .. pick.name)

local offers = { { id = "k1", name = "a fixture guard", role = "tank", cost = 500 },
                 { id = "k2", name = "a fixture medic", role = "healer", cost = 400 },
                 { id = "k3", name = "a fixture nurse", role = "healer", cost = 350 } }
local hire = Mercenary.pickOffer(offers, "healer")
local wrong, whyRole = Mercenary.pickOffer(offers, "utility")

DOCS.eq(pick.id, "t1", "AA off: the first listed TRAINING upgrade")
DOCS.eq(withAA.id, "t2", "AA on: the list's own order decides")
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "no list: nothing is picked")
DOCS.has(why, "no train list", "the trainer never guesses an upgrade")
DOCS.eq(hire.id, "k3", "the cheapest healer")
DOCS.eq(wrong, nil, "never a wrong-role hire")
DOCS.has(whyRole, "utility", "it says which role was missing")
examples.expect: The trainer picks the first listed upgrade it may spend on, refuses to pick with no list, and the healer pick is the cheapest healer.

examples.title: Build a loop's provider and see what is missing
examples.summary: A chore loop acts through an activities provider: overseer, trainer, mercenary and city-writ drivers plus the economy's writs and collections. eb.loops.providers.build fills every verb you do not supply with a stub that says "needs a live window" the first time it is hit, so a loop runs end to end while you bring a driver up; gaps lists what is still missing.
examples.code:
local Providers = require("eb.loops.providers")
local Interface = require("eb.loops.interface")

-- a trainer driver that can only read points so far
local partial = { points = function() return { training = 2, aa = 0 } end }
local notes = {}
local provider = Providers.build({ trainer = partial, note = function(m) notes[#notes + 1] = m end })

local ok, missing = Interface.validate("trainer", partial)
local gaps = Providers.gaps({ trainer = partial })
local st, why = provider.trainer.train("t1")                    -- a stub: blocked, and it says so once
provider.trainer.train("t1")
print(notes[1])

DOCS.eq(ok, false, "the partial driver is not complete")
DOCS.check(#missing >= 5, "validate lists every missing verb")
DOCS.check(table.concat(gaps, " "):find("trainer.train", 1, true) ~= nil, "gaps names trainer.train")
DOCS.eq(provider.trainer.points().training, 2, "the real verb is kept")
DOCS.eq(st, "blocked", "a stubbed action reports blocked")
DOCS.has(why, "no trainer window", "with the reason")
DOCS.eq(#notes, 1, "and notes the gap once, not every tick")
examples.expect: The partial trainer driver validates as incomplete, the gaps list names its missing verbs, and a stubbed verb reports itself once.

examples.title: A chore loop's stop flag and coin gate
examples.summary: Every chore loop checks its stop predicate first, on every tick: when it answers true the goal ends at once, before any action. Coin-spending steps (the overseer's buy, a mercenary hire) run only behind an explicit flag. Drive a goal yourself by calling goal:advance(brain, snapshot) once per tick.
examples.code:
local Loops = require("eb.loops")

-- a minimal brain for driving a goal by hand: b.sub.* adapters, b:log, b:markPointer
local function brainStub()
    local b = { sub = { nav = { travelTo = function() return "arrived" end, walkTo = function() return "arrived" end } },
                logs = {}, cfg = {} }
    function b:log(fmt, ...) self.logs[#self.logs + 1] = select("#", ...) > 0 and fmt:format(...) or fmt end
    function b:markPointer() end
    return b
end
local snap = { zone = "Fixture Docks", x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 }

local touched = false
local stopped = Loops.new({ kind = "mercenary", params = { stop = function() return true end,
    act = { mercenary = { active = function() touched = true; return "none" end } } } })
local first = stopped:advance(brainStub(), snap)

local state, hired = "suspended", false
local merc = { active = function() return state end, contactNear = function() return true end,
               offers = function() return { { id = "k1", role = "healer", cost = 400 } } end,
               hire = function() hired = true; return "done" end,
               unsuspend = function() state = "active"; return "done" end, addFromBags = function() return "done" end }
local goal = Loops.new({ kind = "mercenary", params = { act = { mercenary = merc }, role = "healer" } })
local b, status = brainStub(), nil
for _ = 1, 10 do status = goal:advance(b, snap); if status ~= "working" then break end end
print("mercenary: " .. state .. " (unsuspended)")

DOCS.eq(first, "done", "a stop ends the goal on its first tick")
DOCS.eq(touched, false, "nothing was read or done")
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the mercenary pass finishes")
DOCS.eq(state, "active", "the suspended merc was brought back (free, safe)")
DOCS.eq(hired, false, "no hire without params.allowHire")
DOCS.check(Loops.describeAll().overseer ~= nil, "describeAll explains every kind and its params")
examples.expect: The stopped goal ends on its first tick with nothing done; the mercenary goal unsuspends a suspended merc and never hires without allowHire.

examples.title: Run a power-level route, step by step
examples.summary: A power-level route is a list of STEPS: travel, hunt, actions and instance. Bind the route runner to its adapters, load a route table, and call runner:step(run) once per tick; like the quest runner it answers working, step_done, need_combat, need_loot, need_travel, complete or blocked. Travel and walks are mounted on the mesh, pulls are closest first, and a route never mentors down.
examples.code:
local ROUTE = {
    schema = "eb-plroute/1", name = "Fixture warm-up", level_of = "lowest",
    breaks = { hp = 50, power = 30, resume = 90, dead = true },
    steps = {
        { kind = "travel", name = "To the vale", zone = "Fixture Vale" },
        { kind = "actions", name = "Check in", actions = {
            { kind = "go", at = { x = 10, y = 0, z = 12 } },
            { kind = "click", actor = "a fixture camp master", how = "hail" },
            { kind = "wait", secs = 5 } } },
        { kind = "hunt", name = "Hunt to 12", zone = "Fixture Vale", levels = { 10, 20 },
          goal = { kind = "level", value = 12 }, pull = { mode = "single", target_order = "closest" } },
    },
}

local PL = require("loops.lib.plworld")
local deps, world = PL.make({ zone = "Fixture Docks", level = 10 })

local routes = require("eb.plroutes")
local runner = routes.bind(deps)
-- a hand-written route is normalized first: every option gets its default, every step its full shape
local handle = assert(runner:load(require("eb.plroutes.route").normalize(ROUTE)))
local run = runner:start(handle, {})
local status = PL.drive(runner, run, deps, world, 100)       -- the brain's part (need_combat -> the fight, ...)
print(("route %s at level %d"):format(status, world.level))

DOCS.eq(handle.check, "", "the route needs nothing filled in")
DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "the route ran to its end")
DOCS.eq(world.level, 12, "the hunt's goal: level 12")
local travel
for _, c in ipairs(world.calls) do if c[1] == "travel" then travel = c end end
DOCS.eq(travel[3], true, "travel is mounted")
for _, c in ipairs(world.calls) do if c[1] == "engage" then DOCS.eq(c[2], "closest", "pulls are closest first") end end
DOCS.eq(world.did("hail"), 1, "the actions step hailed the camp master")
examples.expect: The route travels mounted, hails the camp master, then hunts with closest-first pulls until level 12 and completes.

examples.title: The power-level routes EB ships, and their short codes
examples.summary: eb.plroutes.catalog() loads the shipped routes (a template to copy plus examples); list() summarizes them, resolve() finds one by id, name or its PL- short code. The template's zones and spots are blank on purpose: its check says what to fill in before it can run.
examples.code:
-- the shipped routes live in data/eb/plroutes beside EB's lua folder; a script started elsewhere names the folder
require("eb.plroutes.catalog").DATA_DIR = "data/eb/plroutes"
local routes = require("eb.plroutes")
local cat = assert(routes.catalog())
local list = routes.list()
print("first route: " .. list[1].name)

local byId = routes.resolve(cat, "template")
local byName = routes.resolve(cat, "General plan")
local byCode = routes.resolve(cat, byId.code)
local missing, why = routes.resolve(cat, "no such route")

DOCS.check(#list >= 2, "the template and the examples")
DOCS.eq(list[1].ready, false, "the template needs filling in")
DOCS.check(byId.check ~= "", "its check says what is missing")
DOCS.eq(byName, byId, "by name")
DOCS.eq(byCode, byId, "by short code")
DOCS.check(require("eb.plroutes.share").isShortCode(byId.code), "codes look like PL-XXXXXXX")
DOCS.eq(missing, nil, "an unknown route")
DOCS.has(why, "no route", "is refused with the reason")
examples.expect: The catalog lists the template first; it resolves the same entry by id, by name and by short code; the template is marked fill-me-in.

examples.title: Share a route: the scrub and the short code
examples.summary: eb.plroutes.share makes a route safe to hand to a friend: scrubForShare replaces a camp puller's character name with "me" (roles stay) and says what it removed; shortCode gives the same PL- code for the same plan every time, so two copies of a plan can be told apart from two different plans.
examples.code:
local Share = require("eb.plroutes.share")
local Route = require("eb.plroutes.route")

local route = {
    schema = "eb-plroute/1", name = "Fixture camp",
    steps = { { kind = "hunt", zone = "Fixture Vale", where = "camp", at = { x = 1, y = 0, z = 2 },
                goal = { kind = "level", value = 30 },
                pull = { mode = "camp", puller = "Fixturo", target_order = "closest" } } },
}
local clean, removed = Share.scrubForShare(route)
print("scrubbed: " .. removed[1])

local code1, code2 = Share.shortCode(route), Share.shortCode(route)
local other = Route.normalize(route)
other.steps[1].goal.value = 40
local code3 = Share.shortCode(other)

DOCS.eq(clean.steps[1].pull.puller, "me", "a character name never leaves in a share")
DOCS.eq(code1, code2, "the same plan, the same code")
DOCS.check(code1 ~= code3, "a different plan, a different code")
DOCS.check(Share.isShortCode(code1), "PL-XXXXXXX")
DOCS.eq(Route.check(Route.normalize(route)), "", "a complete camp step passes the route check")
examples.expect: The puller's name is scrubbed to me, the code is stable, and changing one step changes the code.

examples.title: The pull and break rules behind a route
examples.summary: eb.plroutes.plan holds a route's decisions as pure functions: resolveCap turns "aggro by group" into a mob count, packDecide says whether a pack pull keeps walking or turns to fight, needBreak says when to rest or wait for a member, and goalMet says when a step is done.
examples.code:
local Plan = require("eb.plroutes.plan")

local cap = Plan.resolveCap("group", 1, 3)                              -- aggro_by group, 1 per member, 3 members
local keepWalking = Plan.packDecide(1, cap, 2, 25, false, false)        -- 1 mob on us, under the cap
local turn = Plan.packDecide(3, cap, 2, 25, false, false)               -- at the cap

local breaks = { hp = 50, power = 30, resume = 90, dead = true, range = 60, zone = true }
local members = { { name = "me", hp = 100, power = 100, dead = false, in_zone = true, dist = 0 },
                  { name = "Member1", hp = 40, power = 90, dead = false, in_zone = true, dist = 10 } }
local brk = Plan.needBreak(breaks, members, false)
print(brk.text)

local stepGoal = require("eb.plroutes.route").normalize({ steps = { { kind = "hunt", zone = "Fixture Vale",
    goal = { kind = "level", value = 30 } } } }).steps[1]

DOCS.eq(cap, 3, "one mob per group member")
DOCS.check(keepWalking ~= turn, "under the cap the pull goes on; at the cap it turns")
DOCS.eq(brk.kind, "rest", "a member under 50% health: rest")
DOCS.check(Plan.goalMet(stepGoal, { group_level = 30, my_level = 30, minutes = 0, kills = 0, runs = 0, aa = -1 }),
    "a level goal is met at its value")
DOCS.check(not Plan.goalMet(stepGoal, { group_level = 29, my_level = 29, minutes = 0, kills = 0, runs = 0, aa = -1 }),
    "and not before")
examples.expect: A 3-box group caps a pack at 3, the pack turns at the cap, a member under 50% health calls a rest, and a level goal is met at its value.

examples.title: The overseer's daily pass, and how it picks agents
examples.summary: eb.overseer.plan picks by the game's own rules: the order (rescues, the tutorial, plain missions in list order, then charged ones by name), the skips (the day's allowance, the player's switches) and each party - an agent whose traits the mission likes first, an agent with a trait it dislikes never unless the player's option says so. The overseer goal (eb.loops) runs ONE whole pass a bite per tick over the window driver: open the window, read both lists, turn in what is done, start the plan, shut the window it opened. Buying spends coin: only with params.buy.
examples.code:
local Mo = require("eb.overseer.model")
local Plan = require("eb.overseer.plan")
local Op = require("eb.overseer.options")
local Loops = require("eb.loops")

-- the window's reads as a driver hands them (offline: invented missions and agents)
local missionRows = {
    { name = "Fixture Survey [Season II: Charged]", charges = 3, state = "available", slots = 1, positive = { "Lantern Lore" }, negative = {} },
    { name = "Sample Patrol", state = "available", slots = 1, positive = { "Fixturecraft" }, negative = { "Clumsy" } },
    { name = "Example Ruins", state = "complete" },
}
local agentRows = {
    { name = "Fixture Archer", status = "idle", traits = { "Fixturecraft" } },
    { name = "Fixture Sage", status = "idle", traits = { "Lantern Lore" } },
    { name = "Fixture Tinker", status = "idle", traits = { "Clumsy" } },
}

-- your script: the plan on its own (the rows made into EB's shapes first)
local missions, agents = {}, {}
for _, r in ipairs(missionRows) do missions[#missions + 1] = Mo.mission(r, 0) end
for _, a in ipairs(agentRows) do agents[#agents + 1] = Mo.agent(a) end
local plan = Plan.make(missions, agents, Op.defaults(), { plainLeft = 10 })
print(("plan: %d start(s), %d agent(s) left"):format(#plan.starts, plan.left))

-- and the whole pass as the goal, driven by hand (in game the brain calls goal:advance once per tick) over a driver
-- that has the base verbs only: the turn-in and the start go through its composites (collect, assign)
local started, turnedIn, bought = {}, 0, false
local ov = {
    near = function() return true end, open = function() return "done" end,
    state = function() return { finished = 1, openSlots = 2, idleAgents = 3, scrolls = 0 } end,
    missions = function() return missionRows, { at = 0, complete = true } end,
    agents = function() return agentRows, { at = 0, complete = true } end,
    collect = function() turnedIn = turnedIn + 1; return "done" end,
    addScrolls = function() return "done" end, research = function() return "done" end,
    assign = function(key, agentKeys) started[#started + 1] = key .. ": " .. table.concat(agentKeys, ", "); return "done" end,
    buy = function() bought = true; return "done" end,
}
local b = { sub = {}, logs = {}, cfg = {} }
function b:log(fmt, ...) self.logs[#self.logs + 1] = select("#", ...) > 0 and fmt:format(...) or fmt end
function b:markPointer() end
local goal = Loops.new({ kind = "overseer", params = { act = { overseer = ov }, options = Op.defaults() } })
local status
for _ = 1, 40 do status = goal:advance(b, { zone = "Fixture Docks", now = 0 }); if status ~= "working" then break end end

-- check
DOCS.eq(plan.starts[1].m.name, "Sample Patrol", "the plain mission is tried first")
DOCS.eq(plan.starts[1].party[1].name, "Fixture Archer", "with the agent whose trait it likes")
DOCS.eq(plan.starts[2].party[1].name, "Fixture Sage", "then the charged one, with its own")
DOCS.eq(plan.left, 1, "the agent with the disliked trait stays home")
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the pass ends")
DOCS.eq(turnedIn, 1, "the finished mission was turned in")
DOCS.eq(#started, 2, "both missions were started")
DOCS.eq(bought, false, "no scrolls bought without params.buy")
examples.expect: The plain mission goes first with the agent it likes, then the charged one with its own; the agent with the disliked trait stays home; the pass turns the finished mission in, starts both, buys nothing and ends "done".

examples.title: Writs and collections as chore loops
examples.summary: The errand loop runs tradeskill writs through the economy's writs pillar (walking to the station first when one is configured); the collections loop scribes every piece it already has, from the bags and the depot. Both are brain goals: each tick does one bite, and they end "done".
examples.code:
local Loops = require("eb.loops")

-- a brain to drive goals by hand (in game EB's brain calls goal:advance once per tick)
local b = { sub = { nav = { travelTo = function() return "arrived" end, walkTo = function() return "arrived" end } },
            logs = {}, cfg = {} }
function b:log(fmt, ...) self.logs[#self.logs + 1] = select("#", ...) > 0 and fmt:format(...) or fmt end
function b:markPointer() end
local snap = { zone = "Fixture Docks", x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 }
local function drive(goal)
    local st
    for _ = 1, 20 do st = goal:advance(b, snap); if st ~= "working" then break end end
    return st
end

-- the providers (offline: the economy's two pillars, as recorders)
local writCalls = 0
local writs = { run = function(self, opts) writCalls = writCalls + 1; return writCalls < 3 and "working" or "done" end }
local filled = {}
local collections = { fill = function(self, scope, opts) filled[#filled + 1] = scope; return "done", { added = 4 } end }

-- your script
local errands = Loops.new({ kind = "errands", params = { act = { writs = writs }, mode = "tradeskill", count = 2 } })
local e = drive(errands)
local col = Loops.new({ kind = "collections", params = { act = { collections = collections }, scope = "fixture" } })
local c = drive(col)
print(b.logs[1])

-- check
DOCS.eq(e, "done", "the writ run finished")
DOCS.eq(writCalls, 3, "polled until the pillar said done")
DOCS.eq(c, "done", "the collections pass finished")
DOCS.eq(filled[1], "fixture", "for the scope asked")
DOCS.has(table.concat(b.logs, "\n"), "scribed 4 piece(s)", "and said how many pieces it scribed")
examples.expect: The writ run polls until the pillar says done; the collections pass scribes the pieces once and ends.

examples.title: Look a route up in the catalog
examples.summary: eb.plroutes.catalog.load builds the shipped route catalog; resolve finds an entry by id, name or short code, and list gives one row per route with whether it is ready to run and what it still needs.
examples.code:
local C = require("eb.plroutes.catalog")
C.DATA_DIR = "data/eb/plroutes"                   -- a script started outside EB's own folder names it

-- your script
local cat = assert(C.load())
local entry = assert(C.resolve(cat, "template"))
local rows = C.list(cat)
print("template ready: " .. tostring(rows[1].ready))
local none, why = C.resolve(cat, "no such route")

-- check
DOCS.eq(entry.id, "template", "found by id")
DOCS.eq(rows[1].id, "template", "the template lists first")
DOCS.check(rows[1].note ~= "", "with what it still needs")
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "an unknown key")
DOCS.has(why, "no route", "says so")
examples.expect: The template resolves by its id, its list row says it needs filling in, and an unknown key says so.

examples.title: A route's plan helpers: skipped steps, repeats, stalls, rates
examples.summary: The route planner is pure: firstOnFrom skips the steps a route switched off, repeatsAt says whether a back-and-forth step goes round again at this level, stallCheck notices a run that stopped making progress, and perHour turns a count into an hourly rate.
examples.code:
local plan = require("eb.plroutes.plan")

-- a route's steps, as normalize leaves them (offline: invented steps)
local route = { steps = {
    { name = "warm-up", off = true, levels = { 1, 10 } },
    { name = "fixture vale", levels = { 10, 20 }, again = 1, again_to = 18 },
    { name = "fixture hollow", levels = { 20, 30 } },
} }

-- your script
local first = plan.firstOnFrom(route, 1)
local again15 = plan.repeatsAt(route.steps[2], 15)
local again19 = plan.repeatsAt(route.steps[2], 19)
local clock, stalled = { seen = {} }, nil
plan.stallCheck(clock, 0, { kills = 12, xp = 40, zone = "Fixture Vale" }, 5)          -- the first look sets the clock
stalled = plan.stallCheck(clock, 301, { kills = 12, xp = 40, zone = "Fixture Vale" }, 5)
print(("30 kills in 20 minutes = %d per hour"):format(plan.perHour(30, 20)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(first, 2, "the switched-off warm-up is skipped")
DOCS.eq(again15, true, "the step repeats below level 18")
DOCS.eq(again19, false, "and not at 19")
DOCS.eq(stalled, true, "five quiet minutes is a stall")
DOCS.eq(plan.perHour(5, 0.5), 0, "under a minute gives no rate")
examples.expect: Step 2 is the first one on; the repeat holds below its target level; a quiet run stalls after its limit.

examples.title: A route's actions, one bite at a time
examples.summary: An actions step is a list of single actions; eb.plroutes.actions runs one per call and says where it is. A go in another zone hands the zone back as need_travel; a wait counts on the snapshot's clock; a click goes to the act adapter. resolveTarget and actionTarget say what a step or an action is about without running it.
examples.code:
local A = require("eb.plroutes.actions")
local runner = require("eb.plroutes.runner")

-- the adapters an actions step uses (offline: recorders)
local clicked, queued = nil, nil
local deps = {
    nav = { walkTo = function() return "arrived" end },
    act = { click = function(name) clicked = name; return true end },
    ic = { queue = function(ic) queued = ic end, state = function() return "idle" end },
}
local snap = { now = 0, zone = "Fixture Docks" }

-- your script
local go = { kind = "go", zone = "Fixture Vale", at = { x = 4, y = 0, z = 9 } }
local s1, z1 = A.runAction(go, snap, deps, {})
print("go: " .. s1 .. " " .. z1)
local wait, ws = { kind = "wait", secs = 3 }, {}
local w1 = A.runAction(wait, snap, deps, ws)
snap.now = 3000
local w2 = A.runAction(wait, snap, deps, ws)
local c = A.runAction({ kind = "click", actor = "Warden Fixturo", how = "doubleclick" }, snap, deps, {})
local target = runner.resolveTarget({ kind = "actions", actions = { go } }, 1)
local inst = A.instance({ route = { recovery = {} } }, snap, { kind = "instance", ic = "fixture_hollow" }, deps)

-- check
DOCS.eq(s1, "need_travel", "a go in another zone asks for travel first")
DOCS.eq(w1, "working", "the wait is still counting")
DOCS.eq(w2, "done", "and done after its seconds")
DOCS.eq(c, "done", "the click went to the act adapter")
DOCS.eq(clicked, "Warden Fixturo", "on the named actor")
DOCS.eq(A.actStatus("refused"), "blocked", "an adapter's refusal reads as blocked")
DOCS.eq(target.kind, "go", "resolveTarget names the step's first action")
DOCS.eq(A.actionTarget(go).zone, "Fixture Vale", "actionTarget names its zone")
DOCS.eq(inst, "working", "an instance step starts a run")
DOCS.eq(queued, "fixture_hollow", "through the instance adapter")
examples.expect: The go asks for travel first, the wait finishes after its seconds, the click is done, and an instance step queues one run through the instance adapter.

examples.title: Write long work as a pollable job
examples.summary: An economy Job cuts long work into steps and runs one bite per call: a step answers "stay" (still on it), "next" (move on), "done" (finish early) or "blocked" with a reason, and keeps its progress in job.mem. Call job:tick once per tick - from a pulse job is fine, a tick never waits - until it is no longer "working".
examples.code:
local Job = require("eb.economy.job")

-- your script: walk to the vendor, sell three items one per tick, close the window
local sold = 0
local job = Job.new("fixture-sell", {
    function(j, ctx) return ctx.atVendor and "next" or "stay" end,
    function(j, ctx)
        j.mem.i = (j.mem.i or 0) + 1                         -- this step's own scratch
        sold = sold + 1
        if j.mem.i < #ctx.items then return "stay" end
        return "next"
    end,
    function() return "done" end,
})
local ctx = { atVendor = false, items = { "a fixture cup", "a fixture plate", "a fixture fork" } }
local trace = {}
for t = 1, 10 do
    if t == 2 then ctx.atVendor = true end                  -- the walk arrives on the second tick
    local st = job:tick(ctx)
    trace[#trace + 1] = st
    if job:finished() then break end
end
print(("sold %d of %d, then: %s"):format(sold, #ctx.items, trace[#trace]))

local broken = Job.new("broken", { function() error("the vendor window closed") end })
local bst, bwhy = broken:tick({})

-- check
DOCS.eq(trace[1], "working", "the first tick waits for the walk")
DOCS.eq(trace[#trace], "done", "the job ends done")
DOCS.eq(sold, 3, "one sale per tick")
DOCS.eq(job:tick(ctx), "done", "an extra tick after the end does not restart it")
DOCS.eq(bst, "blocked", "a step that raises ends the job")
DOCS.has(bwhy, "the vendor window closed", "with the error as its reason")
DOCS.eq(job:reset().i, 1, "reset starts it over at the first step")
examples.expect: The three-step job reports working for each bite, then done; a step that raises ends the job as blocked instead of breaking the frame.

examples.title: One job per request: call it every tick, it resumes
examples.summary: Job.gate keeps one live job per key on a table you own, so an action called every tick with the same request resumes its job instead of starting over, and a different key is a separate job. Job.live finds a running one without building, Job.clear drops them, and a stop flag on holder.env.stop ends a gated job at once.
examples.code:
local Job = require("eb.economy.job")

-- your script: an action that is safe to call every tick
local stop = false
local pillar = { env = { stop = function() return stop end } }
local function restock()
    return Job.gate(pillar, "restock:food", function()
        return Job.new("restock", { function() return "next" end, function() return "next" end, function() return "done" end })
    end):tick()
end
local a, b, c = restock(), restock(), restock()
print(("restock: %s, %s, %s"):format(a, b, c))

local sweep = Job.gate(pillar, "sweep", function() return Job.new("sweep", { function() return "stay" end }) end)
sweep:tick()
local running = Job.live(pillar, "sweep")
stop = true
local st, why = sweep:tick()
Job.clear(pillar)

-- check
DOCS.eq(c, "done", "the same job ran through its three steps")
DOCS.eq(running, sweep, "Job.live finds the running job")
DOCS.eq(st, "blocked", "the stop flag ends a gated job at once")
DOCS.eq(why, "stop requested", "and says why")
DOCS.eq(Job.live(pillar, "sweep"), nil, "clear dropped every job")
examples.expect: Three calls advance the same job; a stop ends a second one as blocked; clear forgets them.

examples.title: The T.S.E hand-over: a member gives its pick to the leader
examples.summary: At the zone's end, inside, each member hands its T.S.E pick to the leader before the leader's pass: twelve items to a trade, leaving out what cannot change hands and anything wished for in a loot roll. The give is a pollable job; when it ends the member's answer tells the leader it is finished.
examples.code:
local TSE = require("eb.economy.tse")                        -- its plan helpers; the pillar itself comes from the economy

-- offline stand-in for the game's side of the economy: the bags, the trade window, the group (every name invented)
local bags = {
    { id = 1, name = "a fixture bracer", qty = 1 }, { id = 2, name = "a fixture ring", qty = 2 },
    { id = 3, name = "a fixture heirloom", qty = 1, heirloom = true }, { id = 4, name = "a wished-for mantle", qty = 1 },
}
local added = {}
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({                      -- EB builds this once per box; the T.S.E is eco.tse
    cfg = {}, now = function() return 1000 end, log = function() end,
    relay = { groupState = function() return { members = { { name = "Leaderio" }, { name = "Memberino" } } } end },
    drive = {
        ["bags.items"] = function() return bags end,
        ["trade.near"] = function(to) return to == "Leaderio" end,
        ["trade.open"] = function() return "done" end,
        ["trade.add"] = function(id, qty) added[#added + 1] = id .. "x" .. qty end,
        ["trade.accept"] = function() return "done" end,
        ["trade.state"] = function() return { theyAccepted = true } end,   -- the leader accepted (a gone trade is never counted)
    },
})

-- your script: the member's side (call give every tick until it is not "working")
local tse = eco.tse
local wished = { ["a wished-for mantle"] = true }
local status
for _ = 1, 5 do
    status = tse:give({ to = "Leaderio", items = bags, wished = wished })
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
local answer = tse:answer()
print(("gave %d line(s) to Leaderio: %s"):format(answer.given, answer.state))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the hand-over finished")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(added, ","), "1x1,2x2", "the bracer and both rings went over; the heirloom and the mantle stayed")
DOCS.check(select(1, tse:mayGive("Leaderio")), "a group member may receive the pick")
DOCS.eq(#TSE.plan.packs(TSE.plan.merge({ { name = "a fixture shard", qty = 1 } }), 12), 1, "a small pick is one trade")
DOCS.eq(#tse:givePick(bags, wished), 2, "givePick leaves out what cannot or should not change hands")
DOCS.check(TSE.plan.allAnswered({ "Memberino" }, { Memberino = answer.at }, 500), "the leader sees every member answered")
examples.expect: The heirloom and the wished-for mantle stay; the two tradeable lines go in one trade; the member answers done.

examples.title: Sell the T.S.E pick at the merchant instead
examples.summary: tse:sell (the T.S.E of the economy EB builds for the box) resolves the pick from the bags by the T.S.E config (a names list and/or a set of tiers), takes each pick item's adornments off and keeps them, opens the merchant in reach, sells the pick item by item through the rules-gated item action, and closes the window. With no pick configured it sells nothing. Items the game has not told the type of are never in a pick.
examples.code:
local Model = require("eb.economy.ledgermodel")

-- offline stand-in for the game's side of the economy (every name invented)
local bags = {
    { id = 1, name = "a fixture bracer", type = "armor", qty = 1, value = 50 },
    { id = 2, name = "a fixture ring", type = "jewelry", qty = 1, value = 20 },
    { id = 3, name = "a keepsake fixture", type = "armor", qty = 1, value = 5 },
}
local adorns, sold, open = { [1] = { { slot = 1 } } }, {}, false     -- the bracer wears one adornment
local function nameOf(id) for _, b in ipairs(bags) do if b.id == id then return b.name end end end
local function game() return {
    ["bags.items"] = function() return bags end,
    ["adorn.on"] = function(id) return adorns[id] or {} end,
    ["adorn.remove"] = function(id) adorns[id] = nil; return "done" end,
    ["merchant.isOpen"] = function() return open end,
    ["merchant.near"] = function() return { name = "a Guild Commodities Exporter" } end,
    ["merchant.open"] = function() open = true; return "done" end,
    ["merchant.sell"] = function(id) sold[#sold + 1] = nameOf(id); return "done" end,
    ["merchant.close"] = function() open = false end,
} end

-- your script: EB builds the economy once per box; the T.S.E is eco.tse
local Economy = require("eb.economy")
local eco = Economy.new({ me = { name = "Sellbox" }, log = function() end, drive = game(),
    cfg = { tse = { names = { "a fixture bracer", "a fixture ring" }, unadorn = true } } })
local tse = eco.tse
local pick = tse:resolvePick({})
local status
for _ = 1, 8 do status = tse:sell({}); if status ~= "working" then break end end
print("sold: " .. table.concat(sold, ", "))
local none, why = Economy.new({ me = { name = "Sellbox" }, log = function() end, cfg = {},
    drive = { ["bags.items"] = function() return bags end } }).tse:sell({})
local kinds = {}
for _, row in ipairs(eco.ledger:rows()) do kinds[#kinds + 1] = Model.kinds[row.kind] end

-- check
DOCS.eq(#pick, 2, "the names list picks two items from the bags")
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the sale finished")
DOCS.eq(#sold, 2, "both picked items were sold, the keepsake was not")
DOCS.eq(adorns[1], nil, "the bracer's adornment was reclaimed first")
DOCS.eq(kinds[1], "unadorn", "and recorded in the ledger")
DOCS.eq(open, false, "the merchant window was closed again")
DOCS.eq(none, "blocked", "no pick configured: nothing is sold")
DOCS.has(why, "no T.S.E pick", "and it says so")
examples.expect: The two picked items are sold after one adornment is reclaimed; an empty config refuses to sell anything.

examples.title: Which loot rule names an item
examples.summary: lootrules.parse(doc) reads a loot-rules table; bestRule(rules, name, facts) picks the rule that decides an item. The most specific rule wins: an exact name beats a "contains" text, a longer text a shorter one.
examples.code:
-- your script: the rules a box keeps in its own loot-rules file, decoded to a Lua table
local LR = require("eb.economy.lootrules")
local d = LR.parse({
    fallback = "leave",
    rules = {
        { id = "r1", match = "contains", item = "shard", act = "greed" },
        { id = "r2", match = "exact", item = "Fixture Rune Shard", act = "need" },
    },
})
local out = {}
for _, name in ipairs({ "Fixture Rune Shard", "a cracked fixture shard", "a fixture pelt" }) do
    local rule = LR.bestRule(d.rules, name, {})
    out[#out + 1] = name .. " -> " .. (rule and rule.act or "(no rule)")
end
print(table.concat(out, "; "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(LR.bestRule(d.rules, "fixture rune shard", {}).id, "r2", "names compare without case")
DOCS.eq(LR.bestRule(d.rules, "a cracked fixture shard", {}).act, "greed", "the contains rule")
DOCS.eq(LR.bestRule(d.rules, "a fixture pelt", {}), nil, "no rule names it")
DOCS.eq(d.opts.fallback, "leave", "what happens to an item no rule names")
examples.expect: The exact-name rule wins for the rune; the "contains" rule takes the other shards; an unnamed item has no rule.

examples.title: Decide what to do with a whole loot window
examples.summary: decideWindow(rules, opts, items, windowType, ctx) gives each item a verb (need, greed, pass, leave ...) and the one act for the window: loot everything, loot the wanted items, or nothing.
examples.code:
-- your script
local LR = require("eb.economy.lootrules")
local d = LR.parse({ fallback = "leave", rules = {
    { match = "contains", item = "fixture", act = "greed" },
} })
local ctx = { me = "Botfixture", sub = "warden", group = {} }
local allWanted = LR.decideWindow(d.rules, d.opts,
    { { name = "a fixture pelt" }, { name = "a fixture fang" } }, LR.parseWin("Free For All"), ctx)
local oneNot = LR.decideWindow(d.rules, d.opts,
    { { name = "a fixture pelt" }, { name = "a rusty nail" } }, LR.parseWin("Free For All"), ctx)
print(("all wanted: %s; one unwanted: %s"):format(LR.actText(allWanted.act), LR.actText(oneNot.act)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(allWanted.act, "lootall", "take the lot")
DOCS.eq(oneNot.act, "lootitems", "take only the wanted ones")
DOCS.eq(oneNot.items[2].verb, "leave", "the item no rule names follows the fallback")
DOCS.eq(oneNot.lootIdx[1], 1, "the index of the wanted item")
examples.expect: A free-for-all window where every item is wanted becomes "Loot All"; with one unwanted item only the wanted ones are taken.

examples.title: Give a drop to a role: @priest, @fighter ...
examples.summary: An "assign" rule's "to" may name a role with @ (fighter, priest, scout, mage, a class or a subclass). On a need-or-greed window each box rolls need when it fits the role and passes when it does not.
examples.code:
-- your script
local LR = require("eb.economy.lootrules")
local d = LR.parse({ rules = { { match = "exact", item = "Fixture Censer", act = "assign", to = "@priest" } } })
local item = { { name = "Fixture Censer" } }
local healer = LR.decideWindow(d.rules, d.opts, item, "nbg", { me = "Healfixture", sub = "templar" })
local tank = LR.decideWindow(d.rules, d.opts, item, "nbg", { me = "Tankfixture", sub = "guardian" })
print(("templar: %s, guardian: %s"):format(healer.items[1].verb, tank.items[1].verb))

-- check
DOCS.eq(healer.act, "need", "the priest rolls need")
DOCS.eq(tank.items[1].verb, "pass", "the fighter passes")
DOCS.eq(LR.roleFits("priest", "templar"), true, "templar is a priest")
DOCS.eq(LR.roleFits("mage", "templar"), false, "and not a mage")
examples.expect: The templar box needs the priest item and the guardian box passes on it.

examples.title: A loot helper: read the window, apply the rules, take the lot
examples.summary: When the game reports a loot window, read its type and item names, let the loot rules decide, and take everything only when every item is wanted.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local events = w.events()               -- in game EB's boot has already attached the game's events and ticks them

-- your script
local LR = require("eb.economy.lootrules")
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local rules = LR.parse({ fallback = "leave", rules = { { match = "contains", item = "fixture", act = "greed" } } })
local said
events.on("LootOpened", function()
    game.NoteLoot()                                       -- tell the game layer's loot watch a window is up
    local lw = game.LootWindow()
    if not (lw and (lw.items or 0) > 0) then return end
    local items = {}
    for i = 1, lw.items do items[i] = { name = game.GetVar("LootWindow.Item[" .. i .. "].Name", "") } end
    local d = LR.decideWindow(rules.rules, rules.opts, items, LR.parseWin(lw.type), { me = game.Me().name })
    if d.act == "lootall" then
        game.Execute("LootWindow:LootAll")
        said = ("looted %d items (%s)"):format(#items, LR.actText(d.act))
        print(said)
    end
end)

-- a corpse is opened: the window appears and the game raises its loot event
w.setWindow("loot", { type = "Free For All", items = { { name = "a fixture pelt" }, { name = "a fixture fang" } } })
w.host:fire("EQ2_onLootWindowAppeared", "1001")
w.frame(2)

-- check
DOCS.check(said ~= nil, "the helper ran")
local last = w.world.actions[#w.world.actions]
DOCS.eq(last and last.kind, "lootall", "Loot All went out")
examples.expect: The LootOpened event arrives, both items are wanted, and the helper sends Loot All.

examples.title: The after-looting guard: destroy only by exact name
examples.summary: An after-looting rule (destroy, transmute, salvage) acts on an item once it is in your bags. afterBlock(rule, item) says why it would be left alone: a destroy needs the item's exact name, and No-Trade, Heirloom, Lore or attuned items are never destroyed.
examples.code:
-- your script
local LR = require("eb.economy.lootrules")
local d = LR.parse({ rules = {
    { id = "a", match = "exact", item = "a fixture rag", act = "destroy" },
    { id = "b", match = "contains", item = "fixture scrap", act = "destroy" },
} })
local rag = { name = "a fixture rag", type = "Item", tier = "COMMON" }
local scrap = { name = "a fixture scrap", type = "Item", tier = "COMMON" }
local boundRag = { name = "a fixture rag", type = "Item", tier = "COMMON", noTrade = true }
local function verdict(it)
    local rule = LR.afterRule(d.rules, it.name)
    local why = rule and LR.afterBlock(rule, it, false, false) or "no rule"
    return why == "" and "go" or why
end
print(("exact: %s; contains: %s; no-trade: %s"):format(verdict(rag), verdict(scrap), verdict(boundRag)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(verdict(rag), "go", "an exact-name destroy may go")
DOCS.eq(LR.destroyOk(LR.afterRule(d.rules, "a fixture scrap")), false, "a contains text never destroys")
DOCS.eq(verdict(boundRag), "it is No-Trade", "No-Trade is never destroyed")
examples.expect: The exact-name destroy may go; the "contains" destroy and the No-Trade item are left alone with their reasons.

examples.title: Pick items from a list with a filter
examples.summary: filter.pick(list, spec) keeps the items that match every criterion you set (tiers, flags, a level band, a class, a name), and tells you why each other item was skipped. An exclude list is never matched.
examples.code:
-- your script: a bag list in EB's item shape (name, tier, level, flags ...)
local F = require("eb.economy.filter")
local bags = {
    { name = "Fixture Gauntlets", tier = "FABLED", level = 75 },
    { name = "Fixture Greaves", tier = "fabled", level = 78 },
    { name = "Fixture Mount Training Scroll", tier = "FABLED", level = 76 },
    { name = "Fixture Bracer", tier = "TREASURED", level = 76 },
    { name = "Fixture Helm", tier = "FABLED", level = 60 },
}
local spec = { tiers = { "fabled" }, minLevel = 70, maxLevel = 80, exclude = { "mount training" } }
local picked, skipped = F.pick(bags, spec)
local names = {}
for _, it in ipairs(picked) do names[#names + 1] = it.name end
print(("picked: %s; skipped %d"):format(table.concat(names, ", "), #skipped))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#picked, 2, "fabled, level 70 to 80")
DOCS.eq(skipped[1].why, "a valuable (never matched)", "the exclude list protects it")
DOCS.eq((F.saysWhat({})), false, "an empty filter names nothing and is refused")
examples.expect: Picks the two fabled items in the level band, never the excluded one, and says why the rest were skipped.

examples.title: Ask the safety gate before destroying or selling
examples.summary: rules.canTake(action, item, ctx) is the one gate every destroy, transmute, salvage and sell goes through. It fails safe: an item whose details were not read, a protected item, or a no-trade item you did not opt in is refused, with the reason.
examples.expect: The plain junk item may go; the unread, the protected and the no-trade items are refused with their reasons.

examples.title: Economy settings and their safe defaults
examples.summary: rules.load(userCfg) lays your settings over safe defaults: nothing is sold or destroyed until you turn it on. rules.whoApplies(who, me) reads a row's "for" word (everyone, a class, an archetype).
examples.code:
-- your script
local R = require("eb.economy.rules")
local cfg = R.load({ bags = { fullThreshold = 5 } })
print(("bags full at %d free; sell junk: %s; repair below %d%%"):format(cfg.bags.fullThreshold,
    tostring(cfg.vendor.sellJunk), cfg.vendor.repairBelowPct))

-- check
DOCS.eq(cfg.bags.fullThreshold, 5, "your setting")
DOCS.eq(cfg.vendor.sellJunk, false, "selling junk stays off until you turn it on")
DOCS.eq(R.whoApplies("priest", { subclass = "templar" }), true, "a templar is a priest")
DOCS.eq(R.whoApplies("fighter", { subclass = "templar" }), false, "and not a fighter")
DOCS.eq(R.archetypeOf("Shadow Knight"), "fighter", "any spelling of a subclass")
examples.expect: Your threshold replaces the default while everything you did not set keeps its safe default.

examples.title: Coin in words and a day's sums
examples.summary: ledgermodel.coin(copper) writes coin the way the game says it ("1p 23g 4s 5c", leading zero units left out); newSums / addRow / countsText add up a day of ledger rows (sells, deposits, loot).
examples.code:
-- your script
local L = require("eb.economy.ledgermodel")
local sums = L.newSums()
for _, row in ipairs({
    { kind = L.kindOf("sell"), qty = 1, cp = 75000, item = "a fixture blade" },
    { kind = L.kindOf("sell"), qty = 1, cp = 50000, item = "a fixture vest" },
