    { kind = L.kindOf("loot"), qty = 1, cp = 0, item = "a fixture pelt" },
}) do L.addRow(sums, row) end
print(("earned %s; %s"):format(L.coin(sums.cp), L.countsText(sums)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(L.coin(12345), "1g 23s 45c", "leading zero units are left out")
DOCS.eq(L.coin(0), "0c", "none at all")
DOCS.eq(sums.cp, 125000, "the copper of both sells")
examples.expect: Two sells and a loot line add up to the right copper and the right counts.

examples.title: Understand a group loot method however it is typed
examples.summary: grouploot.findMethod(words) and findRarity(words) accept every spelling a person types ("lol", "Leader Only", "need before greed", "fabled and above"); said(method, rarity) gives the game's own words.
examples.code:
-- your script
local GL = require("eb.economy.grouploot")
local m1, m2 = GL.findMethod("lol"), GL.findMethod("Leader Only")
local fabled = GL.findRarity("fabled and above")
print(GL.said(m1, fabled))
local ok, method, rarity = GL.parseWords({ "need", "before", "greed", "treasured" })

-- check
DOCS.eq(m1.word, m2.word, "two spellings, one method")
DOCS.eq(GL.findMethod("pizza"), nil, "not a method")
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "a method and a rarity in one line")
DOCS.eq(method.label .. " / " .. rarity.label, "Need Before Greed / treasured items and above", "the game's words")
examples.expect: Two spellings name the same method, and the method plus a rarity reads back in the game's words.

examples.title: Answer a purchase question only for your own item
examples.summary: The game asks "Are you sure you want to purchase X?" on some buys. confirm.asksFor(question, item) is true only when the question names exactly the item you are buying - the rule for pressing Yes; anything else is answered No or left alone.
examples.code:
-- your script
local C = require("eb.economy.confirm")
local q = "Are you sure you want to purchase Fixture Stone?  This cannot be undone."
print(("ours: %s, someone else's: %s"):format(tostring(C.asksFor(q, "Fixture Stone")),
    tostring(C.asksFor(q, "Fixture Gem"))))

-- check
DOCS.eq(C.asksFor(q, "fixture stone"), true, "case does not matter")
DOCS.eq(C.asksFor("Join the fixture group?", "Fixture Stone"), false, "not a purchase question")
DOCS.eq(C.seconds(2), 20, "a wait under 5 s falls back to the default")
examples.expect: The question about our own item matches; a question about another item does not.

examples.title: Read a merchant's price and the game's buy lines
examples.summary: merchantread.parsePriceLabel(label) reads the price under a selected merchant row (a currency amount, or coin); boughtCount(line, item) and refused(line) read the game's own "You buy ..." and refusal lines.
examples.code:
-- your script
local MR = require("eb.economy.merchantread")
local link = string.char(92) .. "aITEM 123 456:[Fixture Mark]" .. string.char(92) .. "/a"      -- the game's item link
local price = MR.parsePriceLabel("Fixture Stone\n25 " .. link)
local n = MR.boughtCount("You buy 3 Fixture Stone from a fixture merchant.", "Fixture Stone")
local why = MR.refused("You need 25 Fixture Mark to purchase Fixture Stone.")
print(("price: %d %s; bought %d; refused: %s"):format(price.amount, price.currency, n, why))

-- check
DOCS.eq(price.amount, 25, "the amount")
DOCS.eq(price.coin, false, "a currency price, not coin")
DOCS.eq(MR.parsePriceLabel("Fixture Stone"), nil, "a name alone has no price")
DOCS.eq(MR.refused("You buy 1 Fixture Stone."), "none", "not a refusal")
examples.expect: Reads a price of 25 marks, counts a purchase of 3, and recognises a "not enough" refusal.

examples.title: The economy's bags-full check
examples.summary: economy.new{ drive = ... }:contract() is the table EB's brain calls between goals. bagsFull(snap) compares the free slots with your threshold (3 by default); with a world snapshot it reads no game at all.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.world.bagsFree = 2

-- your script: a tiny drive that answers the free slots from the game (EB's own drive does this in game)
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local drive = { ["bags.slots"] = function() return game.GetVar("Me.InventorySlotsFree", 0), 40 end }
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = drive })
local c = eco:contract()
local full, free = c.bagsFull()
local fullTen = c.bagsFull({ bagsFreeSlots = 10 })              -- a world snapshot answers without a read
print(("%d free: %s; 10 free: %s"):format(free, full and "full" or "not full", fullTen and "full" or "not full"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(full, true, "2 free slots is full (threshold 3)")
DOCS.eq(fullTen, false, "10 free is not")
DOCS.eq((eco:validateContract()), true, "every function the brain calls is there")
examples.expect: Two free slots is full, ten is not; the free-slot count comes from the game.

examples.title: Write the economy settings
examples.summary: One settings table drives every economy part; whatever you leave out takes a safe default (nothing sold, destroyed or deposited until a rule says so). eco:configure(patch) changes it while EB runs, merging a table one level deep. This is the document a settings file holds.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world()

-- your script: the settings (every key optional)
local settings = {
    bags    = { fullThreshold = 4 },                                    -- 4 or fewer free slots = full
    protect = { names = { ["fixture charm"] = true } },                 -- never sold / destroyed / deposited
    depot   = { keep = { ["fixture arrow"] = true } },                  -- never deposited
    vendor  = { sellList = { "Fixture Pelt" }, junkTiers = { Junk = true }, repairBelowPct = 40,
                restockPresets = { food = { { name = "Fixture Bread", qty = 20 } } } },
    loot    = { method = "nbg", space = 2, rules = { ["fixture gem"] = "need" } },
    broker  = { undercut = 5, friendsFloorCopper = 1000, priceDefaults = { ["fixture ore"] = 1200 } },
    bank    = { keepFree = 2 },
    mail    = { keepFree = 1 },
    craft   = { commissions = { enabled = false } },
}
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, cfg = settings })
local cfg = eco.env.cfg
DOCS.eq(cfg.bags.fullThreshold, 4, "yours")
DOCS.eq(cfg.vendor.sellJunk, false, "a default kept: junk selling stays off")
DOCS.eq(cfg.broker.beatAll, false, "a default kept")

eco:configure({ vendor = { repairBelowPct = 25 } })                     -- a live change
print("repair below " .. cfg.vendor.repairBelowPct .. "%")

-- check
DOCS.eq(cfg.vendor.repairBelowPct, 25, "changed")
DOCS.eq(cfg.vendor.sellList[1], "Fixture Pelt", "the rest of the vendor block is untouched")
DOCS.eq(eco:contract().bagsFull({ bagsFreeSlots = 4 }), true, "4 free is full at this threshold")
examples.expect: The defaults fill the gaps; a live change of the repair threshold takes effect at once.

examples.title: Sell a list of items at a merchant
examples.summary: eco.vendor:sell() opens the merchant in reach, sells every bag item your sell list names, skips anything protected, closes the window and writes a ledger line per sale. Call it once a tick until it stops answering "working".
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (only the docs runner has it; in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ bags = {
    { name = "Fixture Pelt", qty = 3, value = 20 },
    { name = "Fixture Charm", qty = 1, value = 500 },
    { name = "Fixture Lantern", qty = 1, value = 90 },
} })

-- your script
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({
    drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, wallNow = function() return 1763000000 end,
    cfg = {
        vendor = { sellList = { "Fixture Pelt", "Fixture Charm" } },       -- exact names this sweep may sell
        protect = { names = { ["fixture charm"] = true } },               -- never sold, whatever a list says
    },
})
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do                       -- the brain calls it once a tick with the same arguments
    status = eco.vendor:sell()
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
print("sell: " .. status)
print(eco.ledger:status().text)

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the sweep finished")
DOCS.eq(W.merchant.coin, 60, "three pelts at 20 copper")
local charm = false
for _, it in ipairs(W.bags) do if it.name == "Fixture Charm" then charm = true end end
DOCS.check(charm, "the protected charm was not sold")
DOCS.has(eco.ledger:status().text, "3 sold", "the sale is in the ledger (counted in items)")
DOCS.check(not W.merchant.open, "the merchant window was closed")
examples.expect: The three pelts are sold (60 copper), the protected charm stays in the bags, and the ledger counts them.

examples.title: Protect an item from every bulk action
examples.summary: eco.inventory:protect(name) puts a name on the protect list; applyAction - the one door every sell, transmute, salvage, extract, destroy and deposit goes through - then refuses it with the reason. unprotect takes it off again (and remembers you did, so a default never comes back by itself).
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ bags = { { name = "Fixture Charm", qty = 1 } } })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })

-- your script
local inv = eco.inventory
local charm = inv:scan()[1]
inv:protect("Fixture Charm")
local s1, why = inv:applyAction(charm, "destroy")
print("refused: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.check(inv:isProtected(charm), "on the protect list")

inv:unprotect("Fixture Charm")
local s2 = inv:applyAction(charm, "destroy")
print("after unprotect: " .. s2)

-- check
DOCS.eq(s1, "blocked", "a protected item is never destroyed")
DOCS.eq(s2, "done", "unprotected, the destroy went through")
DOCS.eq(W.log[#W.log], "destroy Fixture Charm x1", "what the game was asked for")
DOCS.eq(inv:freeSlots(), 40, "the bags are empty again")
examples.expect: The destroy is refused while the charm is protected and goes through after unprotect.

examples.title: Clear junk without a vendor trip
examples.summary: The brain's junk() frees bag slots by rule: an item whose tier is in cfg.vendor.junkTiers is sold when a merchant window is open, destroyed otherwise. With no junk rule it does nothing at all and says "done". An item whose type or tier the game has not told is never junked.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local function bags()
    return { { name = "Fixture Rag", type = "Loot", tier = "Junk" }, { name = "Fixture Bone", type = "Loot", qty = 4, tier = "Junk" },
             { name = "Fixture Ore", type = "Resource", qty = 30, tier = "Treasured" } }
end

-- your script, part 1: no rule configured - fail-safe, nothing is touched
local W1 = Fake.world({ bags = bags() })
local eco1 = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W1), me = W1.me })
local first = eco1:contract().junk()
DOCS.eq(first, "done", "no junk rule: done at once")
DOCS.eq(#W1.log, 0, "and nothing was sent to the game")

-- part 2: the Junk tier is junk
local W2 = Fake.world({ bags = bags() })
local eco2 = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W2), me = W2.me,
    cfg = { vendor = { junkTiers = { Junk = true } } } })
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco2:contract().junk()
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
print("junk destroyed: " .. #W2.log)

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the junk pass finished")
DOCS.eq(#W2.bags, 1, "only the ore is left")
DOCS.eq(W2.bags[1].name, "Fixture Ore", "the good item stayed")
examples.expect: Without a rule nothing moves; with the Junk tier listed the two junk stacks are destroyed and the good item stays.

examples.title: Repair only when the gear needs it
examples.summary: eco.vendor:repair() reads the worst condition of your worn gear and walks the mender's window only when it is at or under cfg.vendor.repairBelowPct (40 by default); { force = true } repairs anyway. The same call the brain makes after a run or a death.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ worn = { chest = { name = "Fixture Vest", condition = 90 },
                                legs = { name = "Fixture Leggings", condition = 95 } } })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })

-- your script
local function repairNow()
    local s
    for _ = 1, 20 do
        s = eco.vendor:repair()
        if s ~= "working" then return s end
    end
    return s
end

DOCS.eq(eco.vendor:worstCondition(), 90, "the worst piece is at 90%")
DOCS.eq(repairNow(), "done", "above the threshold: done without a trip")
DOCS.eq(#W.log, 0, "no window was opened")

W.worn.legs.condition = 30                     -- a hard fight later
DOCS.eq(repairNow(), "done", "under the threshold: repaired")
print("repaired: " .. W.worn.legs.condition)

-- check
DOCS.eq(W.worn.legs.condition, 100, "the legs are mended")
DOCS.eq(W.log[#W.log], "repair all", "the mender's repair-all ran")
examples.expect: At 90% nothing opens; at 30% the mender repairs everything back to 100%.

examples.title: Buy from a merchant and answer the purchase question
examples.summary: eco.vendor:buyFromMerchant(name, qty) buys the row by its exact name and answers the game's "Are you sure you want to purchase X?" with Yes ONLY when X is the item you are buying - a question naming anything else is answered No and the buy stops. A name that several rows share at different prices is refused before any click.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ offers = {
    { name = "Fixture Lantern Kit", asks = true },                        -- a currency row: the game asks first
    { name = "Fixture Exchange", price = { amount = 1, currency = "Fixture Crest" } },
    { name = "Fixture Exchange", price = { amount = 5, currency = "Fixture Crown" } },
} })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })

local function buy(name, qty)
    local s, why
    for _ = 1, 20 do
        s, why = eco.vendor:buyFromMerchant(name, qty)
        if s ~= "working" then return s, why end
    end
    return s, why
end

-- your script, part 1: the question names our item -> Yes
local s1 = buy("Fixture Lantern Kit", 1)
for _, line in ipairs(W.log) do if line:find("^yes") then print(line) end end
DOCS.eq(s1, "done", "bought")

-- part 2: the question names something else -> No, and the buy stops
W.askOther = "Fixture Gold Crown"
local s2, why2 = buy("Fixture Lantern Kit", 1)
W.askOther = nil
DOCS.eq(s2, "blocked", "a question about another item is never answered Yes")
DOCS.has(why2, "different item", "and the reason says so")

-- part 3: two rows share a name at different prices -> refused before any click
local s3, why3 = buy("Fixture Exchange", 1)

-- check
DOCS.eq(s3, "blocked", "a shared-name row is not bought by name")
DOCS.has(why3, "several rows", "the reason")
DOCS.has(W.log[#W.log] or "", "no:", "the last answer to the game was No")
examples.expect: The lantern kit is bought on a Yes; a question naming another item is answered No; a shared-name row is refused.

examples.title: Answer the purchase question in your own buy helper
examples.summary: When your own helper buys something, answer the game's purchase question the way EB does: confirm.new(env) over a drive that can read the question (choice.purchasePrompt) and answer it (choice.answer), expect(item) before the buy, then resolve(item) - Yes only for the exact item, No for anything else, "none" while no question is up.
examples.code:
-- your script: the two drive actions the answerer needs (in game EB's drive has them)
local question = nil
local answers = {}
local env = {
    drive = {
        ["choice.purchasePrompt"] = function() return question and { text = question } or nil end,
        ["choice.answer"] = function(n) answers[#answers + 1] = n; question = nil; return "done" end,
    },
    log = function() end,
    now = function() return 0 end,
}
local Confirm = require("eb.economy.confirm")
local c = Confirm.new(env)

c:expect("Fixture Tonic", 30)                                 -- about to buy: keep expecting it for 30 s
DOCS.eq(c:resolve("Fixture Tonic"), "none", "no question up yet")

question = "Are you sure you want to purchase Fixture Tonic?  This cannot be undone."
DOCS.eq(c:resolve("Fixture Tonic"), "confirmed", "our item: Yes")

question = "Are you sure you want to purchase Fixture Crown?  This cannot be undone."
DOCS.eq(c:resolve("Fixture Tonic"), "declined", "another item: No")
print("answered: " .. table.concat(answers, ", "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(answers[1], 1, "1 = Yes")
DOCS.eq(answers[2], 2, "2 = No")
DOCS.eq(Confirm.seconds(2), 20, "a wait under 5 s falls back to 20")
DOCS.eq(c.expected.item, "Fixture Tonic", "what it expects")
examples.expect: "none" with no question up, "confirmed" for our item, "declined" for another one.

examples.title: Read a stone merchant's rows
examples.summary: merchantread turns the rows of a merchant that sells transmuter's stones for a currency into a table: the currency the stones cost, the stones cheapest first, and the exchange rows that turn another currency into it. pickStone chooses one, usableExchanges says which exchanges you can pay for, and stopReason says why a run should stop. All pure: they read what the window driver handed back, never the game.
examples.code:
-- the merchant's rows, as a window driver reads them
local rows = {
    { index = 1, name = "Greater Transmuter's Stone", price = { amount = 12, currency = "Fixture Crest" } },
    { index = 2, name = "Lesser Transmuter's Stone", price = { amount = 5, currency = "Fixture Crest" } },
    { index = 3, name = "Fixture Crest (25)", price = { amount = 1, currency = "Fixture Crown" } },
}

-- your script
local MR = require("eb.economy.merchantread")
local t = MR.buildStoneTable(rows)
local list = {}
for _, s in ipairs(t.stones) do list[#list + 1] = s.name .. " " .. s.price end
print("stones in " .. t.currency .. ": " .. table.concat(list, ", "))

DOCS.eq(MR.exchangeGives("Fixture Crest (25)", "Fixture Crest"), 25, "an exchange row gives 25")
DOCS.eq(MR.pickStone(t, "greater"), 2, "asked by part of its name")
DOCS.eq(MR.pickStone(t, "", 1), 2, "the cheapest, one price step up")
local usable = MR.usableExchanges(t, { ["Fixture Crown"] = 3 })
DOCS.eq(#usable, 1, "the crowns pay for the exchange")

-- check
DOCS.eq(t.currency, "Fixture Crest", "the stones' currency")
DOCS.eq(t.stones[1].price, 5, "cheapest first")
DOCS.has(MR.stopReason(100, 100, 20, 4, true, 0, 5), "at its max", "a maxed skill stops")
DOCS.has(MR.stopReason(10, 100, 3, 4, true, 0, 5), "bag slots", "full bags stop")
DOCS.eq(MR.stopReason(10, 100, 20, 4, true, 0, 5), "", "otherwise go on")
examples.expect: The stones cost Fixture Crests; the 25-crest exchange is usable with crowns; a maxed skill stops the run.

examples.title: Restock from the depot with one list for the whole group
examples.summary: A restock row says how many to KEEP in the bags and who it is for; each box takes only its own rows and pulls just the shortfall from the right depot (food, ammo, fuel, harvest). eco.depot:planLines shows the plan, and the brain's restock(list) (or eco.depot:topUp) runs it. It never buys anything.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ bags = { { name = "Fixture Bread", qty = 5 } },
                       depots = { food = { ["Fixture Bread"] = 50 }, ammo = { ["Fixture Arrow"] = 900 } } })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })   -- me: a warden

-- your script: one list, shared by every box of the group
local rows = {
    { name = "Fixture Arrow", qty = 200, who = "ranger" },    -- only a ranger takes this row
    { name = "Fixture Bread", qty = 20 },                      -- everyone keeps 20
}
local lines, notMine = eco.depot:planLines(rows)
DOCS.eq(#lines, 1, "one line for this box")
DOCS.eq(notMine, 1, "the ranger's row is not mine")
DOCS.eq(lines[1].kind, "food", "bread comes from the food depot")

local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco:contract().restock(rows)
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
local bread = 0
for _, it in ipairs(W.bags) do if it.name == "Fixture Bread" then bread = it.qty end end
print("bread: " .. bread)

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the restock finished")
DOCS.eq(bread, 20, "topped up to the target")
DOCS.eq(W.depots.food.contents["Fixture Bread"], 35, "15 came out of the depot")
DOCS.eq(W.depots.ammo.contents["Fixture Arrow"], 900, "the arrows were left for the ranger")
examples.expect: The warden skips the ranger's arrows and pulls 15 bread to reach 20.

examples.title: Deposit by a rule, keep the keep list
examples.summary: eco.depot:deposit() moves NOTHING without a rule - a list, an opts.only predicate, a filter in cfg.depot.depositRule, or all = true. Whatever the rule picks, the keep list (cfg.depot.keep) and every protected item stay in the bags; each item goes to its own depot kind.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({
    bags = { { name = "Fixture Ore", qty = 30 }, { name = "Fixture Arrow", qty = 200 }, { name = "Fixture Charm" } },
    depots = { harvest = {}, ammo = {} },
})
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me,
    cfg = { depot = { keep = { ["fixture arrow"] = true } }, protect = { names = { ["fixture charm"] = true } } } })

-- your script, part 1: no rule -> refused, nothing deposited
local s0, why0 = eco.depot:deposit()
DOCS.eq(s0, "blocked", "no rule, no deposit")
DOCS.has(why0, "no deposit rule", "the reason")

-- part 2: a rule - everything with "Ore" or "Arrow" in its name (the arrows are on the keep list anyway)
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.depot:deposit(nil, { only = function(it) return it.name:find("Ore") or it.name:find("Arrow") end })
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
for _, line in ipairs(W.log) do print(line) end

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the deposit finished")
DOCS.eq(W.depots.harvest.contents["Fixture Ore"], 30, "the ore is in the harvest depot")
DOCS.eq(W.depots.ammo.contents["Fixture Arrow"], nil, "the kept arrows were not deposited")
DOCS.eq(#W.bags, 2, "arrows and the protected charm stay in the bags")
examples.expect: With no rule it refuses; with a rule for ore the ore goes to the harvest depot and the kept arrows stay.

examples.title: Top up your ammo from the ammo depot
examples.summary: Count the ammo you hold, work out the shortfall, and pull it with eco.depot:withdraw(name, qty, "ammo"), which opens the ammo depot in reach, withdraws and closes it. eco.inventory:quiver{ ammo, target } answers "blocked" with the reason when no ammo depot is open; in this build its pull step loses the count, so a script withdraws the shortfall itself as shown.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ bags = { { name = "Fixture Arrow", qty = 50 } }, depots = { ammo = { ["Fixture Arrow"] = 900 } } })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })

-- your script
local s1, why1
for _ = 1, 5 do
    s1, why1 = eco.inventory:quiver({ ammo = "Fixture Arrow", target = 200 })
    if s1 ~= "working" then break end
end
DOCS.eq(s1, "blocked", "no ammo depot open")
DOCS.has(why1, "ammo depot not open", "the reason")

local target, held = 200, 0
for _, it in ipairs(eco.inventory:scan()) do if it.name == "Fixture Arrow" then held = held + it.qty end end
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.depot:withdraw("Fixture Arrow", target - held, "ammo")
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
print("arrows: " .. W.bags[1].qty)

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "withdrawn")
DOCS.eq(W.bags[1].qty, 200, "the target")
DOCS.eq(W.depots.ammo.contents["Fixture Arrow"], 750, "150 came from the depot")
DOCS.check(W.depotOpen == nil, "the depot was closed again")
examples.expect: quiver refuses with no depot open; the withdraw pulls the 150 arrows that make 200.

examples.title: Find an item and hand some to a player
examples.summary: eco.inventory:search(words, index) finds every bag stack whose name contains the words, plus rows of an index you pass (another box's bags, a depot's contents). eco.inventory:distribute(item, qty, who) trades that many to a player in trade range; a bound item cannot be traded.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ bags = { { name = "Fixture Ore", qty = 30 }, { name = "Fixture Bound Ring", noTrade = true } },
                       trade = { friendo = true } })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })
local inv = eco.inventory

-- your script
local hits = inv:search("ore", { { where = "a harvest depot", name = "Rough Fixture Ore", qty = 200 } })
DOCS.eq(#hits, 2, "the bags and the index")
DOCS.eq(hits[2].where, "a harvest depot", "the index row says where")

local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = inv:distribute("Fixture Ore", 5, "Friendo")
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
for _, line in ipairs(W.log) do print(line) end
local bound, why
for _ = 1, 20 do
    bound, why = inv:distribute("Fixture Bound Ring", 1, "Friendo")
    if bound ~= "working" then break end
end

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "traded")
DOCS.eq(W.bags[1].qty, 25, "five ore left the bags")
DOCS.eq(bound, "blocked", "a bound item is never traded")
DOCS.has(why, "bound", "the reason")
examples.expect: Two hits for "ore"; five ore are traded to Friendo; the bound ring is refused.

examples.title: Plan a bank deposit before you make it
examples.summary: eco.bank:deposit{ which, filter | items | bags | all, page, dry } puts bag items in the personal, shared or guild bank. dry = true answers the plan without moving anything: what would go and what stays, with the reason (a bag, a protected item, an account valuable, info not loaded). A guild deposit needs a page, 1 to 4.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ bags = {
    { name = "Fixture Ore", qty = 30 }, { name = "Fixture Satchel", container = true },
    { name = "Fixture Charm" }, { name = "Lesser Mount Training Writ" },
} })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me,
    cfg = { protect = { names = { ["fixture charm"] = true } } } })

-- your script: the plan first
local s, plan = eco.bank:deposit({ which = "shared", all = true, dry = true })
for _, k in ipairs(plan.kept) do print("kept: " .. k.item.name .. " (" .. k.why .. ")") end
DOCS.eq(s, "done", "a dry run answers at once")
DOCS.eq(#plan.picked, 1, "only the ore would go")
DOCS.eq(#plan.kept, 3, "the bag, the protected item and the valuable stay")

-- a guild deposit without a page is refused
local g, gwhy = eco.bank:deposit({ which = "guild", filter = { names = { "Fixture Ore" } } })
DOCS.eq(g, "blocked", "the guild bank needs a page")
DOCS.has(gwhy, "page", "the reason")

-- the real deposit: the ore, by name, into the shared bank
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.bank:deposit({ which = "shared", filter = { names = { "Fixture Ore" } } })
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "deposited")
DOCS.eq(W.bank.rows.shared[1].name, "Fixture Ore", "the ore is in the shared bank")
DOCS.eq(#W.bags, 3, "the rest stayed in the bags")
examples.expect: The dry run keeps the bag, the protected charm and the training writ; the real deposit moves the ore.

examples.title: Keep a set amount of coin on you
examples.summary: eco.bank:coin{ keepCopper = N } opens the bank and deposits what you carry over N, or withdraws the shortfall when you carry less. Coin is counted in copper: 100 copper = 1 silver, 100 silver = 1 gold, 100 gold = 1 platinum. ledgermodel.coin turns copper into the game's words ("4p 0g 0s 0c").
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ coin = { bank = 0, carried = 5000000 } })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })
local coin = require("eb.economy.ledgermodel").coin

-- your script
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.bank:coin({ keepCopper = 1000000 })
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
print(("banked %s, carrying %s"):format(coin(W.bank.coin.bank), coin(W.bank.coin.carried)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the purse is set")
DOCS.eq(W.bank.coin.carried, 1000000, "1 platinum carried")
DOCS.eq(W.bank.coin.bank, 4000000, "4 platinum banked")
examples.expect: 5 platinum carried, 1 kept: 4 platinum go to the bank.

examples.title: Mail items and coin to another character
examples.summary: eco.mail:send(to, { names | filter, count, copper }) needs a recipient (one character name) and an explicit pick - it never mails "everything". Bound items cannot be mailed and protected items stay unless named exactly and allowed. One item per letter; the coin rides on the first letter.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ bags = { { name = "Fixture Ore", qty = 30 }, { name = "Fixture Bound Ring", noTrade = true } } })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })

-- your script: what a send refuses
local p1, why1 = eco.mail:sendPlan("Friendo Fixwell", { names = { "Fixture Ore" } })
DOCS.check(p1 == nil and why1:find("one character name"), "a recipient is one name")
local p2, why2 = eco.mail:sendPlan("Friendo", {})
DOCS.check(p2 == nil and why2:find("name the items"), "a send names what it mails")
local picked, kept = eco.mail:sendPlan("Friendo", { names = { "Fixture Ore", "Fixture Bound Ring" } })
DOCS.eq(#picked, 1, "the ore can go")
DOCS.eq(kept[1].why, "bound (cannot be mailed)", "the bound ring cannot")

-- the send itself: called once a tick until it is done
local status
for _ = 1, 30 do
    status = eco.mail:send("Friendo", { names = { "Fixture Ore" }, copper = 500 })
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
for _, line in ipairs(W.log) do print(line) end

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "mailed")
local letter = W.mail.sent[1]
DOCS.eq(letter.to, "Friendo", "to the recipient")
DOCS.eq(letter.items[1].name, "Fixture Ore", "the ore attached")
DOCS.eq(letter.coin, 500, "with the coin")
examples.expect: A two-word recipient and an empty pick are refused; the ore and 500 copper go out in one letter.

examples.title: Open one letter by its subject and take what it carries
examples.summary: A letter is picked by a part of its subject, by its sender's WHOLE name, or both - a part of a name never matches. The game may put a key in front of a subject (":<key>:"); it is never part of it. mail.pick is the pure rule; eco.mail:open(subject, sender, take) opens the first letter that fits and, with take, takes its attachments. A quest letter opened this way starts its quest.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ inbox = {
    { id = 1, from = "Fixwell", subject = "A note", attachments = {} },
    { id = 2, from = "Lamplighter Fixto", subject = ":0123abcd:The Fixture Lantern",
      attachments = { { name = "Fixture Lantern Oil", qty = 1 } } },
} })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })
local Mail = require("eb.economy.mail")

-- your script: the pure rules first
DOCS.eq(Mail.shown(":0123abcd:The Fixture Lantern"), "The Fixture Lantern", "the key is not part of the subject")
DOCS.eq((Mail.pick("lantern", nil, W.mail.inbox)), 2, "a part of the subject matches")
DOCS.eq((Mail.pick(nil, "Fix", W.mail.inbox)), nil, "a part of a name never matches")
DOCS.eq((Mail.pick(nil, "fixwell", W.mail.inbox)), 1, "the whole name, any case, does")

-- open it and take the attachment
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.mail:open("lantern", nil, true)
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
print("opened: " .. Mail.shown(W.mail.inbox[2].subject))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "opened and taken")
DOCS.check(W.mail.inbox[2].read, "the letter was read")
local oil = false
for _, it in ipairs(W.bags) do if it.name == "Fixture Lantern Oil" then oil = true end end
DOCS.check(oil, "the attachment is in the bags")
examples.expect: The keyed subject is matched, "Fix" does not match the sender "Fixwell", and the lantern oil reaches the bags.

examples.title: Reprice your broker listings
examples.summary: eco.broker:targetPrice says what one listing should cost: the cheapest other seller's price minus cfg.broker.undercut copper (or equal to it with beatAll), never under the friends floor or the item's own price default. eco.broker:reprice() walks every listing of yours and sets each price, accepting it only when the window reads it back.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({
    mine = { { id = 501, name = "Fixture Ore", priceCopper = 2000 } },
    listings = { { name = "Fixture Ore", priceCopper = 1500, seller = "Seller Fixmore" } },
})
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me,
    cfg = { broker = { undercut = 5, friendsFloorCopper = 1000, priceDefaults = { ["fixture ore"] = 1200 } } } })

-- your script: the price rule
local ore = { name = "Fixture Ore" }
DOCS.eq(eco.broker:priceFloor(ore), 1200, "the item's own price default")
DOCS.eq(eco.broker:targetPrice(ore, 2000, 1500), 1495, "undercut by 5")
DOCS.eq(eco.broker:targetPrice(ore, 2000, 1100), 1200, "never under the floor")
DOCS.eq(eco.broker:targetPrice(ore, 2000, nil), 2000, "no other seller: the price stays")

-- reprice every listing of mine
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.broker:reprice()
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
for _, line in ipairs(W.log) do print(line) end

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "repriced")
DOCS.eq(W.broker.mine[1].priceCopper, 1495, "the listing undercuts by 5")
examples.expect: 1500 from another seller becomes 1495; a market at 1100 stops at the 1200 floor; the listing is repriced.

examples.title: Buy what you are short of, under a price cap
examples.summary: eco.broker:buy(name, { count, maxCopper, optional }) counts what the bags already hold, buys only the shortfall from the cheapest listing under the cap, and answers the purchase question for that exact item. With optional = true a missing item is skipped instead of stopping the run.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({
    bags = { { name = "Fixture Lantern Oil", qty = 1 } },
    listings = { { name = "Fixture Lantern Oil", priceCopper = 900, seller = "Seller A", asks = true },
                 { name = "Fixture Lantern Oil", priceCopper = 400, seller = "Seller B", asks = true } },
})
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me })

-- your script
local function buy(name, opts)
    local s, why
    for _ = 1, 20 do
        s, why = eco.broker:buy(name, opts)
        if s ~= "working" then return s, why end
    end
    return s, why
end
local status = buy("Fixture Lantern Oil", { count = 3, maxCopper = 500 })
for _, line in ipairs(W.log) do if line:find("^yes") then print(line) end end

-- an item nobody sells under the cap: optional moves on, otherwise the run stops
local skip = buy("Fixture Rare Gem", { count = 1, maxCopper = 10, optional = true })
local stop, why = buy("Fixture Rare Gem", { count = 1, maxCopper = 10 })

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "bought")
DOCS.eq(W.bags[1].qty, 3, "three in the bags now")
DOCS.eq(skip, "done", "optional: skipped")
DOCS.eq(stop, "blocked", "not optional: the run stops")
DOCS.has(why, "under cap", "and says why")
examples.expect: One oil is held, three wanted: two are bought from the 400-copper listing (the 900 one is over the cap).

examples.title: Put bag items up on the broker
examples.summary: eco.broker:listFromBags() lists what CAN go up, each with a suggested price (its price default, else its merchant value); bound, protected, worthless and not-yet-read items are left out. Nothing goes up until you call eco.broker:addFromInventory(id, copper).
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ bags = {
    { name = "Fixture Ore", qty = 30, value = 30 },

    { name = "Fixture Charm", value = 400 },
    { name = "Fixture Pebble", value = 0 },
    { name = "Fixture Mystery Box", value = 50, type = "Unknown" },
} })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me,
    cfg = { protect = { names = { ["fixture charm"] = true } } } })

-- your script

DOCS.eq(#offer, 1, "one item can go up")
DOCS.eq(offer[1].name, "Fixture Ore", "the ore")
DOCS.eq(offer[1].priceCopper, 30, "suggested at its merchant value")

local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.broker:addFromInventory(offer[1].id, 2500)
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
print(("listed: %s @ %d"):format(W.broker.mine[1].name, W.broker.mine[1].priceCopper))

examples.title: What this box does with each drop
examples.summary: eco.loot:classify(item) is the simple per-drop rule: a rule for the item's name first (cfg.loot.rules), then the always-take list (cfg.loot.autoTake), then a quota a group member still wants (cfg.loot.quotas, counted against cfg.loot.owned), then the group's loot method. A full loot-rules document (cfg.loot.rulesDoc, see eb.economy.lootrules) replaces this path when it is on.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows and the crew (in game EB passes its own)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world()
local relay = { groupState = function() return { leader = "Tankard",
    members = { { name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian" }, { name = "Fixturae", subclass = "warden" } } } end,
    role = function() return "member" end, send = function() end }

-- your script
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, relay = relay, cfg = { loot = {
    rules = { ["fixture gem"] = "need" },
    autoTake = { "Fixture Coin Pouch" },
    quotas = { ["fixture shard"] = { tankard = 2 } },        -- the tank wants two shards ...
    owned = { Tankard = { ["fixture shard"] = 1 } },         -- ... and holds one
    method = "nbg",
} } })
local loot = eco.loot
print("shard: " .. loot:classify({ name = "Fixture Shard" }))

-- check
DOCS.eq(loot:classify({ name = "Fixture Gem" }), "need", "a name rule first")
DOCS.eq(loot:classify({ name = "Fixture Coin Pouch" }), "take", "the always-take list")
DOCS.eq(loot:classify({ name = "Fixture Shard" }), "to:Tankard", "a member's quota")
DOCS.eq(loot:classify({ name = "Fixture Rag" }), "greed", "need before greed: greed by default")
DOCS.eq(#loot:roster(), 2, "the roster comes from the crew's group state")
DOCS.check(not loot:amLeader(), "this box is not the group's leader")
examples.expect: need for the gem, take for the pouch, to:Tankard for the shard, greed for the rest (need before greed).

examples.title: Loot a corpse by rule
examples.summary: The brain's lootGrab() opens the nearest corpse or chest, applies the rule to every drop, closes the window and answers "done", or "empty" when there is nothing to loot. lootPending() says whether there is something to loot. Each drop taken is a ledger line.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ corpse = { id = 77, name = "a fixture brute's corpse" },
    window = { mode = "ffa", items = { { id = 1, name = "Fixture Gem" }, { id = 2, name = "Fixture Rag" } } } })
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, wallNow = function() return 1763000000 end,
    cfg = { loot = { rules = { ["fixture gem"] = "need", ["fixture rag"] = "leave" } } } })

-- your script
local brain = eco:contract()                  -- the same table EB's brain calls between goals
DOCS.check(brain.lootPending(), "a corpse in reach")
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = brain.lootGrab()
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
for _, it in ipairs(W.bags) do print("took: " .. it.name) end

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "looted")
DOCS.eq(#W.bags, 1, "only the gem was taken")
DOCS.check(not brain.lootPending(), "nothing left in reach")
DOCS.eq(brain.lootGrab(), "empty", "the next call: nothing to loot")
DOCS.has(eco.ledger:status().text, "1 looted", "the take is in the ledger")

examples.title: Hand drops out from the leader's loot window
examples.summary: On a leader window the leading box hands each drop to the member whose quota still wants it and tells that member over the crew relay; what nobody claims follows the rule or the method. eco.loot:setMethod(method) sets the group's method and, on the leader, tells the crew.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows and the crew (in game EB passes its own)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ corpse = { id = 78, name = "a fixture chest" },
    window = { mode = "leader", assignable = true, items = { { id = 1, name = "Fixture Shard" } } } })
local said = {}
local relay = {
    groupState = function() return { leader = "Fixturae",
        members = { { name = "Fixturae", subclass = "warden" }, { name = "Healwell", subclass = "templar" } } } end,
    role = function() return "tank" end,
    send = function(to, line) said[#said + 1] = to .. ": " .. line end,
}
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, relay = relay,
    cfg = { loot = { quotas = { ["fixture shard"] = { healwell = 1 } } } } })

-- your script
DOCS.check(eco.loot:amLeader(), "this box leads the group")
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.loot:lootGrab()
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
for _, line in ipairs(W.log) do print(line) end
eco.loot:setMethod("lotto")

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the window was handled")
DOCS.eq(said[1], "to Healwell: loot incoming: Fixture Shard", "the member is told")
DOCS.eq(said[2], "all: loot method lotto", "the new method went to the crew")
DOCS.eq(eco.env.cfg.loot.method, "lotto", "and is the setting now")
examples.expect: The shard is assigned to Healwell, the crew is told, and the method change reaches everyone.

examples.title: Give a gear drop to the member who gains the most
examples.summary: The Resolve auction (opt-in: cfg.loot.resolveAuction = true): an equipment drop in a leader's loot window goes to the member who gains the most Resolve over what they wear in that slot. Each member's bid comes from the group's gear exports. auction.bid / auction.winner are the pure rule; eco.auction:award(item, roster) picks the winner from the exports.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive and reads the group's exports)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world()
local exports = {   -- what each member's box publishes: worn gear, class and level
    Tankard = { class = "guardian", level = 100, worn = { chest = { name = "Old Vest", stats = { resolve = 10 } } } },
    Healwell = { class = "templar", level = 100, worn = { chest = { name = "Good Robe", stats = { resolve = 40 } } } },
}
local drop = { name = "Fixture Breastplate", slot = "chest", stats = { resolve = 50 } }

-- your script: the pure rule
local A = require("eb.economy.auction")
DOCS.eq((A.bid(drop, exports.Tankard)), 40, "the tank gains 40")
DOCS.eq((A.bid(drop, exports.Healwell)), 10, "the healer gains 10")
DOCS.check(A.qualifies(drop, {}), "equipment with Resolve goes to auction")

-- the live call the leader's loot window makes
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me,
    cfg = { loot = { resolveAuction = true, exports = exports } } })
local who = eco.auction:award(drop, { "Tankard", "Healwell" })
print(("%s -> %s (+%d)"):format(drop.name, who, A.bid(drop, exports[who])))

-- check
DOCS.eq(who, "Tankard", "the biggest gain wins")
local off = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, cfg = { loot = { exports = exports } } })
local none, why = off.auction:award(drop, { "Tankard", "Healwell" })
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "the auction is off unless you turn it on")
DOCS.eq(why, "auction off", "and says so")
examples.expect: The tank gains 40 Resolve, the healer 10: the breastplate goes to the tank. With the auction off, nobody.

examples.title: Record and read the money and item ledger
examples.summary: Every sell, deposit, transmute and loot EB does is one ledger line (eco.ledger:add), kept on the PC that wrote it. day(key) sums one day, last12() the last 12 hours, status() is this box's today in one line, and command(words) answers the same words eb ledger takes (status, day <YYYY-MM-DD>, last12, clear <day> | all).
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: no files host, so the ledger keeps this session's lines itself
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world()
local NOW = 1763000000                                         -- a fixed wall-clock time, in seconds
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, wallNow = function() return NOW end })
local Model = require("eb.economy.ledgermodel")

-- your script
local ledger = eco.ledger
ledger:add({ kind = "sell", item = "Fixture Pelt", qty = 3, cp = 60, where = "Merchant Fixtel" })
ledger:add({ kind = "sell", item = "Fixture Gem", qty = 1, cp = 10000, where = "Merchant Fixtel" })
ledger:note("depot", "Fixture Ore", { qty = 30, where = "a harvest depot" })
DOCS.check(not ledger:add({ kind = "gift", item = "Fixture Pelt" }), "a kind the ledger does not know is not written")

local today = Model.localDay(NOW)
local day = ledger:day(today)
print(Model.countsText(day.sums) .. " (" .. Model.coin(day.sums.cp) .. ")")
DOCS.eq(day.sums.cp, 10060, "the day's coin, in copper")
DOCS.eq(#day.rows, 3, "three lines")
DOCS.has(ledger:status().text, "4 sold", "this box's today (counted in items)")
local ok, text = ledger:command({ "day", today })
DOCS.check(ok and text:find("4 sold", 1, true), "the eb ledger words answer the same")
DOCS.eq(#ledger:last12(NOW).rows, 3, "all three are in the last 12 hours")

-- check: clear the day
local n = ledger:clear(today)
DOCS.eq(n, 1, "one day file removed")
DOCS.eq(#ledger:rows(), 0, "the ledger is empty")
examples.expect: Two sales (4 items) and a deposit (30 ore) are summed for the day; clearing the day removes its file.

examples.title: Accept crafting commissions only from your own people
examples.summary: eco.commissions:watch() handles a crafting commission another character opened with this box: off by default (left for the player); on (cfg.craft.commissions.enabled) it serves only an allowed requester - your group, as the crew relay reports it, plus cfg names - and declines anyone else, which costs nothing.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows and the crew (in game EB passes its own)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world({ commission = { from = "Stranger Fixmo", recipe = "Fixture Stew", qty = 1 } })
local relay = { groupState = function() return { members = { { name = "Fixturae" }, { name = "Healwell" } } } end }
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, relay = relay,
    cfg = { craft = { commissions = { enabled = true, allow = "fleet", names = { "Friendo" } } } } })

-- your script
local c = eco.commissions
DOCS.check(c:allowed("Healwell"), "a group member is allowed")
DOCS.check(c:allowed("friendo"), "a listed name is allowed (any case)")
DOCS.check(not c:allowed("Stranger Fixmo"), "anyone else is not")

local s1, what = c:watch()
DOCS.eq(what, "declined", "the stranger's commission is declined")

W.commission = { from = "Healwell", recipe = "Fixture Stew", qty = 1 }
c:watch()                                    -- accepts, then hands the recipe to the craft pillar
for _, line in ipairs(W.log) do print(line) end

-- check
DOCS.eq(s1, "done", "declining is done at once")
DOCS.has(table.concat(W.log, "\n"), "accept commission from Healwell", "the member's commission was accepted")
examples.expect: A stranger's commission is declined; a group member's is accepted.

examples.title: See which window actions a drive provides
examples.summary: The economy works through a DRIVE: one table of window actions (bags.items, merchant.sell, depot.withdraw, ...). eb.economy.drive lists every action, checks a drive against the list, and fills the gaps with honest stubs: a missing read answers empty, a missing action answers "blocked" with what it still needs. eco:driveGaps() and eco:driveReport() say the same for a built economy.
examples.code:
-- your script: a drive of your own that only knows the bags
local Drive = require("eb.economy.drive")
local mine = {
    ["bags.slots"] = function() return 12, 40 end,
    ["bags.items"] = function() return {} end,
    __drive = { name = "my bag reader", proven = { ["bags.slots"] = true },
                need = { ["merchant.buy"] = "the merchant window's Buy button" } },
}
print(Drive.signature("broker.setPrice"))
DOCS.eq(Drive.kind("bags.items"), "read", "a read")
DOCS.eq(Drive.kind("merchant.sell"), "action", "an action")

local ok, missing = Drive.validate(mine)
DOCS.check(not ok and #missing == #Drive.SPEC - 2, "everything but the two is missing")

local full = Drive.withFallback(mine)
local s, why = full["merchant.buy"]("Fixture Tonic", 1)
DOCS.eq(s, "blocked", "a missing action refuses")
DOCS.has(why, "the merchant window's Buy button", "with what it still needs")
DOCS.eq(#full["merchant.offers"](), 0, "a missing read answers empty")

local report = Drive.report(mine)
DOCS.eq(report.present, 2, "two present")
DOCS.eq(report.proven, 1, "one of them proven")

-- check: the same from a built economy
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = mine })
DOCS.eq(#eco:driveGaps(), #Drive.SPEC - 2, "driveGaps")
DOCS.eq(eco:driveReport().missing, #Drive.SPEC - 2, "driveReport")
examples.expect: A two-action drive is reported with the rest missing; a stubbed buy answers blocked with its reason.

examples.title: The item and loot commands in this build
examples.summary: The loot, depot and broker commands are declared in EB's command schema, so eb help lists them and the console completes them, and EB runs the economy behind them: eb bank status, eb loot status and eb broker status each say how things stand. eb roster list names your characters from EB's own sources (never a login detail). reg:unattached shows which commands a domain still waits for.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game you type in the console)
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script: lines exactly as you type them
local help = a.console("eb help depot")
local bank = a.console("eb bank status")
print(bank)
local loot, broker = a.console("eb loot status"), a.console("eb broker status")
local roster = a.console("eb roster list")
local waiting = a.app.reg:unattached({ domain = "depot" })

-- check
DOCS.has(help, "bank", "eb help depot lists the bank command")
DOCS.has(bank, "bank (personal)", "eb bank status says how the bank stands")
DOCS.has(loot, "loot as we go", "eb loot status says whether looting runs")
DOCS.has(broker, "broker: idle", "eb broker status says what the broker is doing")
DOCS.has(roster, "character(s)", "eb roster list names the characters EB knows")
DOCS.eq(#waiting, 0, "no depot command waits for the economy")

examples.title: Build a window's state
examples.summary: An ebkit window builds its WHOLE state as a plain table, and returns the SAME table until something changes.
examples.code:
-- your script
local W = require("ebkit.window")
local kills, builds = 0, 0
local win = W.new({
    id = "killcounter", title = "Kill Counter", about = "kills this session",
    build = function(self)                       -- called only after a change: build from your data, never the game
        builds = builds + 1
        return { kills = kills, label = kills == 1 and "1 kill" or (kills .. " kills") }
    end,
})
local a, b = win:state(), win:state()
local first = builds
kills = 3
win:touch()                                       -- "something it shows changed"
local c = win:state()
print(("builds: %d, then %d after touch"):format(first, builds))

-- check
DOCS.check(a == b, "the same table while nothing changed: the window bridge sends nothing")
DOCS.eq(first, 1, "one build")
DOCS.eq(c.label, "3 kills", "a fresh state after touch")
DOCS.check(c ~= a, "a new table, so the bridge sends it")
examples.expect: Two state() calls give the same table and one build; touch() makes the next state() build a new one.

examples.title: Answer a click with a verb
examples.summary: A window's verbs are its allow-list: a click runs one by name, answers at once, and nothing else can run.
examples.code:
-- your script
local W = require("ebkit.window")
local kills = 7
local win = W.new({
    id = "killcounter", title = "Kill Counter",
    build = function() return { kills = kills } end,
    verbs = {
        reset = function(args, self) kills = 0; return true, "cleared" end,
        add = function(args, self)
            local n = W.int(args.n, 1, 100)          -- what a page sent, made safe: a whole number in 1..100, or nil
            if not n then return false, "add takes n = 1..100" end
            kills = kills + n
            return true, "added " .. n
        end,
        broken = function() error("oops") end,
    },
})
local ok, text = win:verb("reset", {})
print(("reset -> %s %s"):format(tostring(ok), text))
local okAdd = win:verb("add", { n = "4" })
local okBad, badText = win:verb("add", { n = 500 })
local okUnknown, unknownText = win:verb("unknown_verb", {})
local okRaised, raisedText = win:verb("broken", {})

-- check
DOCS.eq(win:state().kills, 4, "the verbs changed the data and the window rebuilt")
DOCS.check(okAdd and not okBad, "a bad argument is refused by the verb itself")
DOCS.has(badText, "1..100", "with its reason")
DOCS.eq(okUnknown, false, "an unknown verb never runs")
DOCS.has(unknownText, "add, broken, reset", "and the answer lists the verbs there are")
DOCS.eq(okRaised, false, "a verb that raises answers false")
DOCS.has(raisedText, "raised", "and says so")
examples.expect: reset answers "cleared", an unknown verb is refused with the list, and one that raises answers false.

examples.title: Refresh a window from data that moves on its own
examples.summary: A live() signature is read at most every liveSec; a new signature rebuilds the state, an equal one costs nothing.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world({ pulse = false, me = { healthPct = 90 } })

-- your script: a window that shows your health, built from the ONE world snapshot (never its own game reads)
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local world = require("eb.world").new({ game = game })
local W = require("ebkit.window")
local builds = 0
local win = W.new({
    id = "myhealth", title = "My Health",
    build = function() builds = builds + 1; return { hp = world.snapshot().hpPct } end,
    live = function() return world.snapshot().hpPct end,     -- cheap: the snapshot is already built this frame
    liveSec = 1,
})
local first = win:state()
w.frame(70); world.beginTick()                                -- over a second later, nothing changed
local same = win:state()
w.self.healthPct = 55
w.frame(70); world.beginTick()
local changed = win:state()
print(("hp %d after the change"):format(changed.hp))

-- check
DOCS.check(first == same, "an equal signature: no rebuild")
DOCS.eq(changed.hp, 55, "a new signature: rebuilt")
DOCS.eq(builds, 2, "two builds in all")
examples.expect: The window rebuilds when the snapshot's health changes and not while it stays the same.

examples.title: Cap how often a window's state goes out
examples.summary: ebkit.push_budget gates a window: a change too soon after the last one is held and the newest goes out next.
examples.code:
-- your script
local W = require("ebkit.window")
local budget = require("ebkit.push_budget")
budget.reset()
local t, n = 0, 0
local win = W.new({ id = "busypanel", build = function() return { n = n } end })
local gate = budget.gate(win, { class = "panel", clock = function() return t end, phase = 0 })

for step = 1, 20 do                       -- the data changes every 50 ms for one second
    n = step
    win:touch()
    gate.state()                          -- what the window bridge calls instead of win:state()
    t = t + 50
end
local st = gate.stats()
print(("emits %d, held %d"):format(st.emits, st.held))

-- check
DOCS.eq(st.class, "panel", "a panel's cadence")
DOCS.eq(st.ms, 200, "is 200 ms")
DOCS.eq(st.emits, 5, "one emit per 200 ms")
DOCS.eq(st.emits + st.held, 20, "every change was either sent or held")
examples.expect: A panel changing every 50 ms for a second emits at 0, 200, 400, 600 and 800 ms; the rest are held.

examples.title: Spread a big scan over several frames
examples.summary: A scan that reads the game counts its reads and stops at the budget, then carries on next frame.
examples.code:
-- your script
local budget = require("ebkit.push_budget")
local rows, nextRow, frames, peak = {}, 1, 0, 0
local function readRow(i) return { id = i } end           -- stands for one game read

while nextRow <= 20 do                                   -- each pass of this loop is one frame
    frames = frames + 1
    local rb = budget.readBudget(8)
    while rb:ok() and nextRow <= 20 do
        rb:take(1)
        rows[#rows + 1] = readRow(nextRow)
        nextRow = nextRow + 1
    end
    if rb:used() > peak then peak = rb:used() end
end
print(("%d rows in %d frames, at most %d a frame"):format(#rows, frames, peak))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#rows, 20, "every row read")
DOCS.eq(frames, 3, "8 + 8 + 4")
DOCS.eq(peak, 8, "never over the budget")
examples.expect: 20 rows are read 8 per frame: the scan takes 3 frames and no frame goes over 8 reads.

examples.title: Register a window with EB's window bridge
examples.summary: P.ui().register(win) adds your window to the bridge at run time; P.ui().adapter(win) is what the bridge sees.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()

-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local W = require("ebkit.window")
local kills = 0
local win = W.new({ id = "killcounter", title = "Kill Counter", about = "kills this session",
    build = function() return { kills = kills } end,
    verbs = { reset = function() kills = 0; return true, "cleared" end } })
local ok, why = P.ui().register(win)
print(("registered %s: %s"):format(win.id, tostring(ok)))
local adapter = P.ui().adapter(win)
local opened, whyNot = P.ui().open(win)       -- in game the window shows; offline there is no window host
kills = 2
win:touch()

-- check
DOCS.check(ok, "registered: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(adapter.state().kills, 2, "the bridge reads the window's state")
DOCS.eq(adapter.about, "kills this session", "and what it is about")
DOCS.check(adapter.verbs.reset ~= nil and adapter.verbs.unknown_verb == nil, "only the window's own verbs")
DOCS.eq(select(2, adapter.verbs.reset({})), "cleared", "a verb through the adapter")
DOCS.check(opened or type(whyNot) == "string", "open answers whether the window showed, and why not")
DOCS.eq(type(win.clock), "function", "registering gave the window EB's clock (its spec brought none)")
examples.expect: The window registers, and its adapter answers state() and exposes exactly the window's verbs.

examples.title: Check a UI read before you send it
examples.summary: Read the game's window elements by name. eb.uiguard checks a UI path first and refuses the unsafe kinds.
examples.code:
-- your script
local G = require("eb.uiguard")
local byName = 'EQ2UIPage[Inventory,Merchant].Child[TabbedPane,Tabs].Child[Page,Buy]'
local byPosition = 'EQ2UIPage[Inventory,Merchant].Child[TabbedPane,Tabs].Child[2]'
local okName = G.checkExpr(byName)
local okPos, why = G.checkExpr(byPosition)
print(("by name: %s | by position under tabs: %s"):format(okName and "allowed" or "refused",
    okPos and "allowed" or "refused"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(okName, true, "a read by name is always allowed")
DOCS.eq(okPos, false, "by position under a tabbed window is refused")
DOCS.has(why, "read its child by name", "and the reason says what to do instead")
DOCS.check(G.isTabbed("TabbedPane") and not G.isTabbed("Page"), "isTabbed names the window type that needs care")
DOCS.eq(G.allowChildRead("Page", "index"), true, "by position is fine under an ordinary page")
examples.expect: A by-name read is allowed; a read by position under a tabbed window is refused with the reason.

examples.title: Press EB Main's buttons from a script
examples.summary: eb.control is what EB Main and the mini press through: summary and toggles for what they show, act for a press - each press becomes a command line through the one registry.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot
local a = DOCS.app()

-- your script
local before = eb.control.summary()
local ok = eb.control.act("pause", { on = true })
local tg = eb.control.toggles()
local okNo, why = eb.control.act("loot")
eb.control.act("start")                                  -- start = eb resume (a pause-off press does not resume yet)
print(("running %s, paused %s -> pause on: %s"):format(tostring(before.running), tostring(before.paused),
    tostring(tg.pause)))

-- check
DOCS.check(ok, "the pause press went through the registry")
DOCS.eq(tg.pause, true, "the toggle shows the pause")
DOCS.eq(okNo, false, "a verb with no action is refused")
DOCS.has(why, "not wired yet", "and says why")
DOCS.eq(a.app.brain.paused, false, "the start press resumed")
a.stop()
examples.expect: The pause press pauses the brain and the toggle shows it; the start press resumes; a verb with no action says not wired yet.

examples.title: Put icons on a window's rows
examples.summary: eb.ui.icons resolves an ability, item or class name to an icon a page draws (or nil, and the page keeps its glyph); iconmap gives the sheet math. Static tables, no game reads.
examples.code:
-- your script: in a window, make the resolver once and use it while you build the state
local Icons = require("eb.ui.icons.icons")
local map = require("eb.ui.icons.iconmap")
local icons = Icons.new({                         -- small tables of your own here; Icons.new({ require = require }) loads EB's
    ability = { icons = { ["fixture strike"] = 1153 }, backs = { ["fixture strike"] = 315 } },
    item = { icons = { ["fixture tonic"] = 40 } },
    class = { classes = { warden = "Warden" } },
})
local row = { name = "Fixture Strike" }
row.icon = icons:forAbility(row.name)
local sp = icons:sprite(row.icon, 18)
local tonic = icons:forItem("Fixture Tonic")
local cls = icons:forClass("warden")
print(("%s -> %s at %d,%d | tonic item %d | warden %s"):format(row.name, sp.file, sp.bgX, sp.bgY, tonic.id, cls.file))

-- check
DOCS.eq(row.icon.back, 315, "the ability's backdrop tile")
DOCS.eq(icons:forAbility("Nothing Like It"), nil, "an unknown name has no icon")
DOCS.eq(map.norm("  Fixture   STRIKE "), "fixture strike", "names are looked up by a plain key")
DOCS.eq(map.backTile(65535), -1, "an empty backdrop reads -1")
DOCS.eq(map.locate(1153, true).atlas, 33, "id 1153 sits on sheet 33")
local own = Icons.new({ require = require })      -- EB's own tables
DOCS.check(own:counts().abilities > 1000, "EB ships thousands of ability icons")
