examples.title: A window's verbs, its open and close, and the push budget
examples.summary: An ebkit window lists its verbs, hears when its page opens and closes, cleans what a page sends (str, args), and the push budget's classes and report say how often each window may send.
examples.code:
-- your script
local Window = require("ebkit.window")
local Budget = require("ebkit.push_budget")
local seen = { open = 0, close = 0 }
local win = Window.new({ id = "fixture-board", title = "Fixture board",
    build = function(w) return { greeting = w.data.greeting or "" } end,
    verbs = {                                     -- a verb gets (args, win) and answers at once
        greet = function(a, w)
            local name = Window.str(a.name, 12)          -- trimmed text, or nil when not text or too long
            if not name then return false, "a name of 1 to 12 letters" end
            w.data.greeting = "hello " .. name
            return true, "ok"
        end,
        clear = function(a, w) w.data.greeting = nil; return true, "cleared" end,
    },
    open = function() seen.open = seen.open + 1 end, close = function() seen.close = seen.close + 1 end,
    clock = function() return 0 end })
win.data = {}
local names = win:verbNames()
win:opened()
local tooLong = { win:verb("greet", Window.args({ name = "Fixturae Fixturae" })) }
win:verb("greet", Window.args({ name = "  Fixturae " }))
win:closed()
local g = Budget.gate(win, { class = "panel", clock = Budget.defaultClock() })
local rep = Budget.report()
print(("verbs: %s | opened %d, closed %d | panel every %d ms"):format(table.concat(names, ", "), seen.open, seen.close,
    Budget.CLASSES.panel.ms))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#names, 2, "two verbs")
DOCS.eq(tooLong[1], false, "a name over 12 characters is refused")
DOCS.eq(win:state().greeting, "hello Fixturae", "str trimmed the spaces")
DOCS.eq(type(Window.args("not a table")), "table", "args always hands a verb a table")
DOCS.check(type(rep.windows) == "table", "the report lists the gated windows")
DOCS.check(g ~= nil, "a gate for the window")
examples.expect: The window lists its two verbs, counts one open and one close, refuses a name that is too long, and the budget report counts its windows.

examples.title: Turn a table into JSON and back
examples.summary: ebkit.jsontable encodes any plain table (object keys sorted, so the same table is always the same text).
examples.code:
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.jsontable")
local text = J.encode({ name = "Tankard", hp = 64, pos = { 12.5, 0, -40 } })
print(text)
local back = J.decode(text)
local bad, why = J.decode('{"hp": 64,')

-- check
DOCS.eq(text, '{"hp":64,"name":"Tankard","pos":[12.5,0,-40]}', "sorted keys; 0 and -40 written as integers")
DOCS.eq(back.pos[1], 12.5, "decoded back")
DOCS.eq(back.name, "Tankard", "strings come back as strings")
DOCS.eq(bad, nil, "malformed JSON is refused")
DOCS.check(type(why) == "string" and #why > 0, "with a reason, never an error")
DOCS.eq(J.encode({ 1, 2, 3 }), "[1,2,3]", "a 1..n table is an array")
examples.expect: The table encodes with sorted keys, decodes back equal, and bad input answers nil and a reason.

examples.title: Write an empty list as []
examples.summary: An empty Lua table encodes as {}; give an empty LIST the __tojson marker and it writes [] instead.
examples.code:
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.jsontable")
local EMPTY_LIST = { __tojson = function() return "[]" end }
local function emptyList() return setmetatable({}, EMPTY_LIST) end    -- the marker always writes []: empty lists only

local state = { name = "Tankard", buffs = emptyList() }
print(J.encode(state))

-- check
DOCS.eq(J.encode({}), "{}", "a plain empty table is an object")
DOCS.eq(J.encode(state), '{"buffs":[],"name":"Tankard"}', "the marked one is a list")
DOCS.eq(J.encode({ buffs = { "Shield", "Haste" } }), '{"buffs":["Shield","Haste"]}', "a list with items needs no marker")
examples.expect: A plain empty table writes {}; one with the __tojson marker writes [], inside a bigger state too.

examples.title: Keep a null in a JSON document
examples.summary: decode turns null into J.null (a key with no value stays a key); J.val(v) turns it back into nil.
examples.code:
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.jsontable")
local doc = J.decode('{"target":null,"zone":"a_test_hall"}')
print("target: " .. tostring(J.val(doc.target)))

-- check
DOCS.check(doc.target == J.null, "null decodes to the J.null marker, so the key is kept")
DOCS.eq(J.val(doc.target), nil, "J.val reads it as nil")
DOCS.eq(J.val(doc.zone), "a_test_hall", "and passes every other value through")
DOCS.eq(J.encode(doc), '{"target":null,"zone":"a_test_hall"}', "it encodes back as null")
examples.expect: The null keeps its key, reads as nil through J.val, and encodes back as null.

examples.title: Change one field in a JSON file another program owns
examples.summary: ebkit.json reads losslessly: change one value, write it back, and the rest stays exactly as it was spelled.
examples.code:
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.json")
local file = '{\n  "scale": 1.50,\n  "theme": "bw",\n  "volume": 0.5\n}'
local doc = assert(J.read(file))
J.set(doc, "volume", J.num(0.8))                 -- numbers are kept as their text: J.num makes a new one
local out = J.write(doc)
print(out:match('"volume": [%d.]+'))

-- check
DOCS.has(out, '"scale": 1.50', "an untouched number keeps its spelling")
DOCS.has(out, '"theme": "bw"', "an untouched string too")
DOCS.eq(J.tonum(J.get(doc, "volume")), 0.8, "the edited value")
DOCS.eq(J.write(assert(J.read(file))), file, "read and written with no edit, the file comes back byte for byte")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(J.keys(doc), ","), "scale,theme,volume", "the keys in file order")
examples.expect: Only the edited value changes; a number spelled 1.50 and a key the script never touched come back the same.

examples.title: Write a Lua data file
examples.summary: ebkit.lua_fmt writes a table as a stable "return { ... }" file that load() reads back with no environment.
examples.code:
-- your script
local LF = require("ebkit.lua_fmt")
local route = { name = "a test hall", steps = { { kind = "walk", at = { 12.5, 0, -40 } }, { kind = "camp", at = { 30, 0, -12 } } } }
local text = LF.document(route, { order = function(t) return { "name", "kind" } end })   -- these keys first
print(text:match("^return {"))
local back = assert(load(text, "route", "t", {}))()        -- a data file needs no globals at all

-- check
DOCS.has(text, 'name = "a test hall"', "a bare key where Lua allows one")
DOCS.has(text, "at = {12.5, 0, -40}", "a short number list stays on one line")
DOCS.eq(back.steps[2].kind, "camp", "it loads back")
DOCS.eq(LF.document(route, { order = function() return { "name", "kind" } end }), text, "the same table writes the same text")
DOCS.eq(LF.num(150.0), "150", "numbers are minimal: never 150.0")
examples.expect: The document starts with return, keeps the chosen key order, and loads back to the same values.

examples.title: Read, write, copy and list your helper's files
examples.summary: Every files host has the same calls: read, write, exists, copy and list, each answering a reason on failure.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the platform's files service over a disk in a table (in game: the real EB folder)
local w = DOCS.world()
local disk = require("data.lib.memdisk").install()

-- your script (a tool or a task: these calls touch the disk now - game code saves with writeLater instead)
local files = require("eb.platform").files()
files.write("helper/notes.txt", "first line\n")
files.copy("helper/notes.txt", "helper/notes.txt.bak")      -- one backup per file, overwritten each time
local names = files.list("helper", "notes*")
print(table.concat(names, ", "))
local missing, why = files.read("helper/none.txt")

-- check
DOCS.eq(files.read("helper/notes.txt"), "first line\n", "read back, byte for byte")
DOCS.check(files.exists("helper/notes.txt.bak"), "the copy exists")
DOCS.eq(#names, 2, "list matches the pattern")
DOCS.eq(missing, nil, "a missing file reads nil")
DOCS.has(why, "no such file", "and says why")
DOCS.eq(disk["helper/notes.txt"], "first line\n", "(offline: it landed on the table disk)")
examples.expect: A write, a one-per-file backup copy and a pattern list all work; a missing file reads nil with the reason.

examples.title: Save from game code without touching the disk in the frame
examples.summary: files.writeLater(path, text) only queues; a pulse job writes one file per slot, newest text wins.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the platform's files service over a disk in a table, and the flush job EB's boot runs for you
local w = DOCS.world()
local disk = require("data.lib.memdisk").install()
local P = require("eb.platform")
P.pulse().every("files", 250, function() P.files().flush(1) end, { prio = 90 })

-- your script
local files = P.files()
for i = 1, 10 do
    files.writeLater("helper/kills.json", '{"kills":' .. i .. '}')     -- from a job or a handler: just a queue
end
local pendingBefore = files.pending()
w.runFor(600)                                                          -- a couple of flush slots go by
print(("%d write for %d saves"):format(files.stats.writes, 10))

-- check
DOCS.eq(pendingBefore, 1, "one queued file, not ten")
DOCS.eq(files.stats.coalesced, 9, "nine saves folded into the first")
DOCS.eq(files.stats.writes, 1, "one write")
DOCS.eq(disk["helper/kills.json"], '{"kills":10}', "the newest text won")
examples.expect: Ten quick saves of the same file coalesce into one write that lands on the next flush, with the last text.

examples.title: Keep a helper's own config in a JSON file
examples.summary: Read your helper's file once at start, keep it in a table, and queue a save when it changes.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the platform's files service over a disk in a table, and the flush job EB's boot runs for you
local w = DOCS.world()
local disk = require("data.lib.memdisk").install({ ["helper/lowhp.json"] = '{"threshold":40}' })
local P = require("eb.platform")
P.pulse().every("files", 250, function() P.files().flush(1) end, { prio = 90 })

-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.jsontable")
local PATH = "helper/lowhp.json"
local DEFAULTS = { threshold = 50, announce = true }
local function load()
    local cfg = {}
    local text = P.files().read(PATH)                  -- once, at start: never on every frame
    local doc = text and J.decode(text) or {}
    for k, v in pairs(DEFAULTS) do cfg[k] = (doc[k] ~= nil) and doc[k] or v end
    return cfg
end
local function save(cfg) P.files().writeLater(PATH, assert(J.encode(cfg))) end

local cfg = load()
cfg.threshold = 35
save(cfg)
w.runFor(300)
print(("threshold %d, saved %s"):format(cfg.threshold, disk[PATH]))

-- check
DOCS.eq(load().threshold, 35, "the saved value reads back")
DOCS.eq(load().announce, true, "a key missing from the file takes its default")
DOCS.eq(disk[PATH], '{"announce":true,"threshold":35}', "the file on disk")
examples.expect: The config loads with defaults for missing keys; a change is saved by the next flush, not in the frame.

examples.title: Read and change an EB setting
examples.summary: P.settings() is EB's settings store: get with a default, set for the session, save once off the hot path.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: no EB folder is known here, so the store cannot be saved (in game save() writes eb-settings.json)
local w = DOCS.world()
eb.root = ""

-- your script
local settings = require("eb.platform").settings()
local before = settings.get("ui.miniOnLogin", true)
settings.set("ui.miniOnLogin", false)
print("ui.miniOnLogin = " .. tostring(settings.get("ui.miniOnLogin", true)))
local saved, why = settings.save()                   -- once, from a task or on stop: never every frame

-- check
DOCS.eq(before, true, "an unset key answers the default")
DOCS.eq(settings.get("ui.miniOnLogin", true), false, "set changed it")
DOCS.eq(settings.dirty(), true, "the store knows it has unsaved changes")
DOCS.eq(saved, false, "offline there is nowhere to save")
DOCS.has(why, "no settings path", "and save() says why instead of raising")
examples.expect: get answers the default for an unset key; set changes it and marks the store dirty; save says why it cannot.

examples.title: Print numbers the same way everywhere
examples.summary: eb.compat.numstr prints 3 and 3.0 both as "3"; format and sortedkeys keep output stable on every target.
examples.code:
-- your script
local compat = require("eb.compat")
print(("%s | %s | %s"):format(compat.numstr(3.0), compat.numstr(2.5), compat.format("hp %d", 64.0)))
local keys = compat.sortedkeys({ zone = 1, [2] = "b", name = 2, [1] = "a" })

-- check
DOCS.eq(compat.numstr(3.0), "3", "an integral float prints as an integer")
DOCS.eq(compat.format("%d", 3.7), "3", "%d truncates instead of raising")
DOCS.eq(compat.toint(-3.7), -3, "toint truncates toward zero")
DOCS.check(compat.isint(3.0) and not compat.isint(3.5), "isint")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(compat.sortedkeys({ b = 1, a = 2 }), ","), "a,b", "strings in order")
DOCS.eq(keys[1], 1, "numbers first, then strings")
DOCS.eq(keys[4], "zone", "the last key")
examples.expect: Whole numbers print without .0, %d takes a fractional number, and keys come out in one stable order.

examples.title: One JSON string, and the key order files use
examples.summary: ebkit.json.quote writes one string exactly as the codec does; ebkit.json.less is the key order every EB file is written in, so a file reads the same on every computer.
examples.code:
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.json")
local q = J.quote('say "hi"\n')
local keys = { "b", "a", "B" }
table.sort(keys, J.less)
print(("%s | %s"):format(q, table.concat(keys, " ")))

-- check
DOCS.eq(q, '"say \\"hi\\"\\n"', "the escaped string")
DOCS.eq(keys[1], "B", "a capital sorts first")
DOCS.check(not J.less("a", "a"), "a key is not before itself")
examples.expect: Quotes, backslashes and newlines are escaped; keys sort by their bytes (capitals first).

examples.title: A JSON null, and Lua values as text
examples.summary: ebkit.jsontable.null keeps a JSON null through a round trip; ebkit.lua_fmt.encode writes any value as a Lua literal, and ident says whether a key can be written bare.
examples.code:
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.jsontable")
local F = require("ebkit.lua_fmt")
local text = J.encode({ gone = J.null })
local back = J.decode(text)
local lua = F.encode({ one = 1, ["two words"] = 2 })
print(("%s | %s"):format(text, (lua:gsub("%s+", " "))))

-- check
DOCS.eq(back.gone, J.null, "decode gives the same null back")
DOCS.check(F.ident("one"), "a plain name is written bare")
DOCS.check(not F.ident("two words"), "a key with a space needs brackets")
DOCS.has(lua, '["two words"] = 2', "the bracketed key")
DOCS.eq(load("return " .. lua)().one, 1, "the text loads back as the same table")
examples.expect: The null survives encode and decode; a table becomes a Lua literal with bare and bracketed keys.

examples.title: Does this station serve the recipe?
examples.summary: eb.economy.craft.serves(actorName, device) answers from EB's station data whether a crafting station in reach can make a recipe's device - and never mistakes a look-alike name for the real station.
examples.code:
-- your script (pure: no game reads)
local Craft = require("eb.economy.craft")
local checks = {
    { "Forge", "Forge" },                               -- the station itself
    { "Sootfoot Forge", "Forge" },                      -- an NPC whose name only holds "forge"
    { "A Festive Work Bench", "Work Bench" },           -- a decoration, not a bench
    { "Rickety Crafting Table", "Chemistry Table" },    -- serves every device
    { "Forge", "a device nobody has heard of" },
}
for _, c in ipairs(checks) do print(("%s -> %s"):format(c[1], tostring(Craft.serves(c[1], c[2])))) end

-- check
DOCS.eq(Craft.serves("Forge", "Forge"), true, "the forge serves forge recipes")
DOCS.eq(Craft.serves("Sootfoot Forge", "Forge"), false, "a name that only holds 'forge' is no forge")
DOCS.eq(Craft.serves("A Festive Work Bench", "Work Bench"), false, "the festive bench is not a work bench")
DOCS.eq(Craft.serves("Rickety Crafting Table", "Chemistry Table"), true, "an any-device station serves it")
DOCS.eq(Craft.serves("Forge", "a device nobody has heard of"), nil, "an unknown device cannot be judged")
examples.expect: A forge serves a Forge recipe, a look-alike forge name and a festive bench do not, a station that serves every device always does, and an unknown device answers nil (cannot judge).

examples.title: Pick the reaction art for this moment of a combine
examples.summary: craft:pickArt(state, arts) is the decision EB makes every tick of a combine: rescue durability first, then quality, else push progress - and only with an art that is ready.
examples.code:
-- offline: the economy facade with no game behind it (pickArt reads nothing)
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = {} })

-- your script
local arts = {
    { name = "Fixture Focus", boosts = "progress", ready = true },
    { name = "Fixture Steady", boosts = "durability", ready = true },
    { name = "Fixture Finesse", boosts = "quality", ready = true },
}
local low = eco.craft:pickArt({ durability = 40, quality = 90 }, arts)
local plain = eco.craft:pickArt({ durability = 95, quality = 50 }, arts)
local healthy = eco.craft:pickArt({ durability = 95, quality = 95 }, arts)
print("durability 40 -> " .. tostring(low))
print("quality 50 -> " .. tostring(plain))
print("all fine -> " .. tostring(healthy))
for _, a in ipairs(arts) do a.ready = false end
local none = eco.craft:pickArt({ durability = 30 }, arts)

-- check
DOCS.eq(low, "Fixture Steady", "durability is rescued first")
DOCS.eq(plain, "Fixture Finesse", "then quality")
DOCS.eq(healthy, "Fixture Focus", "a healthy combine pushes progress")
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "no art ready, no art cast")
examples.expect: Low durability picks the durability art, low quality the quality art, a healthy combine the progress art, and nothing ready picks nothing.

examples.title: Craft one order at the station in reach
examples.summary: eco.craft:craftOne(order) selects the recipe, checks fuel, runs each combine with reaction arts and closes the station. It is pollable: call it every tick with the same order until it answers "done".
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: a work bench in reach and a recipe book (the game's windows, faked)
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ station = { name = "Work Bench" },
    recipes = { { name = "Fixture Lantern", level = 20, device = "Work Bench" } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script: the same call every tick until it is done (EB's tick model: never wait inside a call)
local order = { recipe = "Fixture Lantern", qty = 2 }
local status, why
repeat status, why = eco.craft:craftOne(order, { station = "Work Bench" }) until status ~= "working"
print(("craftOne -> %s (%d made)"):format(status, #world.made))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the order finished")
DOCS.eq(#world.made, 2, "two combines")
DOCS.check(#world.artsUsed > 0, "reaction arts were cast while the combines ran")
DOCS.eq(world.craft.open, false, "the station was closed")
examples.expect: Two Fixture Lanterns are made at the work bench, reaction arts were cast during the combines, and the station window is closed at the end.

examples.title: Craft a list of orders
examples.summary: eco.craft:queue(orders) crafts each order in turn and answers "done" when the last one is finished, or "blocked" with the order it stalled on.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: a work bench and a two-recipe book
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ station = { name = "Work Bench" }, recipes = {
    { name = "Fixture Lantern", level = 20, device = "Work Bench" },
    { name = "Fixture Spoon", level = 10, device = "Work Bench" } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local orders = { { recipe = "Fixture Lantern", qty = 2 }, { recipe = "Fixture Spoon", qty = 1 } }
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.craft:queue(orders) end)
print("queue -> " .. status .. ": " .. table.concat(world.made, ", "))

local stuck, why = CW.poll(function() return eco.craft:queue({ { recipe = "Fixture Anvil", qty = 1 } }) end)
print("queue -> " .. stuck .. ": " .. tostring(why))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the queue finished")
DOCS.eq(#world.made, 3, "three items")
DOCS.eq(world.made[3], "Fixture Spoon", "in order")
DOCS.eq(stuck, "blocked", "an unknown recipe stops the queue")
DOCS.has(why, "Fixture Anvil", "and says which order")
examples.expect: Two orders (three items) are crafted in order; a queue naming a recipe the book lacks stops on it.

examples.title: Refuse a station that does not serve the recipe
examples.summary: Pass the recipe's device as opts.station and craftOne checks the station in reach first: a station that does not serve it is refused with its name, before anything is selected.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the only station in reach is a decoration
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ station = { name = "A Festive Work Bench" },
    recipes = { { name = "Fixture Lantern", level = 20, device = "Work Bench" } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local status, why = CW.poll(function() return eco.craft:craftOne("Fixture Lantern", { station = "Work Bench" }) end)
print(status .. ": " .. tostring(why))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "blocked", "refused")
DOCS.has(why, "does not serve", "with the reason")
DOCS.eq(#world.made, 0, "nothing was crafted")
examples.expect: With only a festive work bench in reach, a Work Bench recipe is refused and nothing is crafted.

examples.title: Fetch missing fuel from the fuel depot before a combine
examples.summary: When the station says the recipe is short of fuel, craftOne pulls the missing fuel from a fuel depot in reach, then crafts. Still short after the pull, it stops and says so.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the recipe needs 3 coal the bags do not have; the fuel depot in reach has 20
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ station = { name = "Work Bench" }, fuelOk = false,
    fuelNeed = { { name = "Fixture Coal", qty = 3 } },
    depots = { fuel = { { name = "Fixture Coal", qty = 20 } } },
    recipes = { { name = "Fixture Lantern", level = 20, device = "Work Bench" } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.craft:craftOne("Fixture Lantern") end)
local coal = 0
for _, it in ipairs(world.bags) do if it.name == "Fixture Coal" then coal = it.qty end end
print(("fuel pulled: %d Fixture Coal, craft %s"):format(coal, status))

-- the same order with the fuel depot empty
local dry = CW.world({ station = { name = "Work Bench" }, fuelOk = false,
    fuelNeed = { { name = "Fixture Coal", qty = 3 } }, depots = { fuel = {} },
    recipes = { { name = "Fixture Lantern", level = 20, device = "Work Bench" } } })
local ecoDry = CW.economy(dry)
local stuck, why = CW.poll(function() return ecoDry.craft:craftOne("Fixture Lantern") end)
print(stuck .. ": " .. tostring(why))

-- check
DOCS.eq(coal, 3, "the missing fuel came from the depot")
DOCS.eq(world.depots.fuel[1].qty, 17, "and left the depot")
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "then the lantern was made")
DOCS.eq(stuck, "blocked", "no fuel anywhere stops the order")
examples.expect: The coal comes out of the fuel depot into the bags and the lantern is made; with an empty fuel depot the order stops with "out of fuel".

examples.title: Work out which recipe a work-order step asks for
examples.summary: eb.economy.writs.stripVerb drops the step's leading verb and its progress; resolve() then finds the recipe: a learned answer, a known spelling fix, the exact book name, a partial fix, the name without its article, and last a loose match only when exactly one recipe fits.
examples.code:
-- your script (pure: give it the step text and the recipe book rows)
local Writs = require("eb.economy.writs")
local book = {
    { name = "Fixture Lantern" }, { name = "Fixture Spoon" }, { name = "Fixture Longbow" },
    { name = "Fixture Ladle" },
}
local function show(text, learned)
    local recipe, how = Writs.resolve(text, book, learned)
    print(("%-38s -> %s (%s)"):format(text, tostring(recipe), how))
    return recipe, how
end
print(Writs.stripVerb("I need to create Fixture Lantern (0/6)"))
local r1, h1 = show("Create Fixture Lantern (0/6)")
local r2, h2 = show("Craft Fixture Long Bow")               -- a partial spelling fix: Long Bow -> Longbow
local r3, h3 = show("I need to create a Fixture Spoon")     -- the article comes off
local r4, h4 = show("Make Lantern")                         -- a loose match: exactly one recipe fits
local r5, h5 = show("Make Fixture L")                       -- two fit (Lantern, Ladle): none is picked
local r6, h6 = show("Make the odd thing", { ["the odd thing"] = "Fixture Ladle" })   -- learned last time
local r7, h7 = Writs.resolve("Create Fixture Bowl", nil)     -- the book did not read

-- check
DOCS.eq(r1 .. "/" .. h1, "Fixture Lantern/exact", "exact")
DOCS.eq(r2 .. "/" .. h2, "Fixture Longbow/partial", "partial fix")
DOCS.eq(r3 .. "/" .. h3, "Fixture Spoon/trimmed", "article trimmed")
DOCS.eq(r4 .. "/" .. h4, "Fixture Lantern/loose", "one loose fit")
DOCS.eq(r5, nil, "two loose fits pick nothing")
DOCS.eq(h5, "ambiguous", "and say why")
DOCS.eq(r6 .. "/" .. h6, "Fixture Ladle/learned", "a learned answer wins")
DOCS.eq(r7 .. "/" .. h7, "Fixture Bowl/unverified", "no book: try the text once")
examples.expect: Each kind of step text resolves the way the rules say; two loose fits pick nothing; with no book read the text itself is tried once ("unverified").

examples.title: Take a work order, craft every step, hand it in
examples.summary: eco.writs:run{ count, kind } asks the Work Order Clipboard (or the rush-order giver) for an order, crafts what each step asks for, verifies a guessed recipe by watching the step move, and hands the order in.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: a clipboard, a work bench, and the order it hands out
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ station = { name = "Work Bench" }, writGiver = { name = "Work Order Clipboard" },
    recipes = { { name = "Fixture Lantern", device = "Work Bench" }, { name = "Fixture Spoon", device = "Work Bench" } },
    nextWrit = { name = "a fixture work order", steps = {
        { text = "Create Fixture Lantern (0/2)", have = 0, need = 2, makes = "Fixture Lantern" },
        { text = "I need to create a Fixture Spoon", have = 0, need = 1, makes = "Fixture Spoon" } } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local status, why = CW.poll(function() return eco.writs:run({ count = 1, kind = "clipboard" }) end)
local learned = eco.env.cfg.writs.learned["a Fixture Spoon"]
print(("writs -> %s, %d handed in, learned: %s"):format(status, world.writsDone, tostring(learned)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the run finished")
DOCS.eq(world.writsDone, 1, "one order handed in")
DOCS.eq(#world.made, 3, "two lanterns and a spoon")
DOCS.eq(learned, "Fixture Spoon", "the guess was verified and learned")

examples.title: Decide which harvest nodes to take
examples.summary: eco.harvest:wantNode(node) is the node rule: never a blacklisted resource, never a tier above your level band (one tier per ten levels), and only the preferred categories when you set any.
examples.code:
-- offline: the economy facade with a harvest config (wantNode reads only the config and your level)
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = {}, me = { level = 45 },
    cfg = { harvest = { blacklist = { ["a fixture weed"] = true }, categories = { ore = true, wood = true } } } })

-- your script
local nodes = {
    { name = "a fixture vein", tier = 5, category = "ore" },
    { name = "a deep fixture vein", tier = 6, category = "ore" },
    { name = "a fixture weed", tier = 1, category = "root" },
    { name = "a fixture shrub", tier = 2, category = "root" },
}
local verdict = {}
for i, n in ipairs(nodes) do
    local want, why = eco.harvest:wantNode(n)
    verdict[i] = want
    print(("tier %d -> %s%s"):format(n.tier, tostring(want), why and (" (" .. why .. ")") or ""))
end

-- check
DOCS.eq(verdict[1], true, "tier 5 is inside the level-45 band")
DOCS.eq(verdict[2], false, "tier 6 is above it")
DOCS.eq(verdict[3], false, "a blacklisted resource is never taken")
DOCS.eq(verdict[4], false, "a category you did not choose is left")
examples.expect: At level 45 a tier-5 node is taken and a tier-6 one left; a blacklisted node and a node outside the preferred categories are left with their reasons.

examples.title: Run a gather route
examples.summary: eco.harvest:runRoute(route) walks to each stop on the mesh, harvests every wanted node in reach, leaves the rest (it never clicks a node it leaves, and remembers it), and moves on. A named route comes from your config (cfg.harvest.routes).
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: two route stops with nodes at each, and a walker that arrives on the next call
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ nodes = {
    { id = 1, name = "a fixture vein", tier = 2, category = "ore", near = "10,0,10" },
    { id = 2, name = "a fixture weed", tier = 1, category = "root", near = "10,0,10" },
    { id = 3, name = "a fixture log", tier = 2, category = "wood", near = "40,0,-5" } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world, { me = { level = 30 }, nav = CW.nav(world),
    cfg = { harvest = { blacklist = { ["a fixture weed"] = true },
        routes = { ["fixture loop"] = { { x = 10, y = 0, z = 10 }, { x = 40, y = 0, z = -5 } } } } } })

-- your script: a saved route by name, polled to the end
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.harvest:runRoute("fixture loop") end)
local gathered, left = 0, 0
for _, node in ipairs(world.nodes) do
    if world.harvested[node.id] == "gathered" then gathered = gathered + 1 else left = left + 1 end
end
print(("route %s: %d gathered, %d left"):format(status, gathered, left))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the route finished")
DOCS.eq(gathered, 2, "ore and wood")
DOCS.eq(world.harvested[2], nil, "the weed was never clicked: the route leaves it and remembers it")
DOCS.eq(world.walked, 2, "one walk per stop")
examples.expect: Two stops: the ore and the wood are gathered, the blacklisted weed is never clicked and never looped on, and the route answers done.

examples.title: Track shinies and send the pack pony out
examples.summary: eco.harvest:trackShiny{ color } reports each NEW shiny once (with its spot, and one line to the crew); eco.harvest:packPony{ answers } summons the pack pony, hails it and answers its questions.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: one silver shiny nearby, and a crew relay that only records
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ nodes = { { id = 7, name = "a fixture glint", color = "silver", shiny = true,
    x = 12, y = 3, z = -40 } } })
local heard = {}
local eco = CW.economy(world, { relay = { send = function(scope, line) heard[#heard + 1] = scope .. ": " .. line end } })

-- your script: poll the tracker each tick; only new finds come back
local first = eco.harvest:trackShiny({ color = "silver" })
local again = eco.harvest:trackShiny({ color = "silver" })
for _, n in ipairs(first) do print(("new shiny: %s at %d,%d,%d"):format(n.name, n.x, n.y, n.z)) end

local pony = CW.poll(function() return eco.harvest:packPony({ answers = { 2, 1, 3 } }) end)
print("pack pony -> " .. pony)

-- check
DOCS.eq(#first, 1, "the shiny is reported")
DOCS.eq(#again, 0, "once")
DOCS.eq(#heard, 1, "the crew heard one line")
DOCS.eq(pony, "done", "the pony went out")
DOCS.eq(#world.answers, 3, "three questions answered")
DOCS.eq(world.answers[3].option, 3, "with the chosen options")

examples.title: Read a skill value the way EB does
examples.summary: eb.economy.skills turns the game's skill text into cur / max, takes a temporary bonus off, works out the cap your levels allow, and names the state: notlearned, unreadable, level or done. Unknown is never 0.
examples.code:
-- your script (pure)
local Skills = require("eb.economy.skills")
local a = Skills.parse("\\#FFFFFF354/400")          -- the game's text: a colour code, then cur/max
local b = Skills.parse("\\#22FF2218/560")           -- 18/560, not 2218/560
local junk = Skills.parse("NULL")
print(("%d/%d and %d/%d"):format(a.cur, a.max, b.cur, b.max))

local boosted = Skills.withoutBonus({ ok = true, cur = 57, max = 425 }, 400)   -- a +25 buff raised both numbers
local cap = Skills.capFromLevels(80, 90)                                       -- 5 x the higher level
local states = {
    Skills.stateOf(false, { ok = true, cur = 0, max = 400 }),     -- reads 0 and nobody said it is learned
    Skills.stateOf(true, { ok = false }),                         -- learned, but the read failed
    Skills.stateOf(false, { ok = true, cur = 12, max = 400 }),
    Skills.stateOf(false, { ok = true, cur = 400, max = 400 }),
}
print("states: " .. table.concat(states, ", "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(a.cur + a.max, 754, "354/400")
DOCS.eq(b.cur, 18, "the colour code came off first")
DOCS.eq(junk.ok, false, "junk does not parse")
DOCS.eq(boosted.cur .. "/" .. boosted.max, "32/400", "the bonus came off both numbers")
DOCS.eq(cap, 450, "the cap from levels")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(states, ","), "notlearned,unreadable,level,done", "the four states")
examples.expect: The colour code is stripped (354/400, 18/560), junk does not parse, a +25 bonus comes off 57/425, the cap from levels 80 and 90 is 450, and each state comes out as the rules say.

examples.title: Read a crafting skill through the game layer
examples.summary: The skill reader takes any object with Skill / SkillText / SkillAbsent / TSLevel - the game layer is one. A skill EB cannot read yet answers ok = false with the reason: unknown, never a made-up 0.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.self.tsLevel = 90
w.world.skills = { tinkering = { 354, 400 } }

-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local Skills = require("eb.economy.skills")
local reader = Skills.new({ shim = game, me = function() return { level = game.Me().level } end })
local t = reader:read("tinkering")
print(("tinkering %d/%d (cap %d)"):format(t.cur, t.max, t.cap))
local other = reader:read("transmuting")
print("transmuting: " .. (other.ok and "read" or ("unknown - " .. other.why)))

-- check
DOCS.eq(t.ok, true, "tinkering read")
DOCS.eq(t.cur, 354, "its value")
DOCS.eq(t.cap, 500, "5 x the higher of the adventure (100) and tradeskill (90) level")
DOCS.eq(other.ok, false, "a skill that does not read is unknown")
DOCS.eq(other.cur, nil, "never a made-up 0")
examples.expect: Tinkering reads 354 of 400 with the cap the levels give; a skill that does not read answers unknown.

examples.title: Where a secondary skill stands, and the books a trip would buy
examples.summary: eco.skilllevel:status(id) reads the skill live and answers its state, the levelling band it is in (the books and the recipe rows of that band) and the books a book trip would buy ahead.
examples.code:
-- offline: the skill seam answers 25 of 100 (in game the game layer answers it)
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = {}, me = { level = 20 },
    shim = { Skill = function(id) if id == "tinkering" then return 25, 100 end end, TSLevel = function() return 20 end } })

-- your script
local st = eco.skilllevel:status("tinkering")
print(("tinkering %d/%d: %s, band tier %d, %d books ahead"):format(st.read.cur, st.read.max, st.state, st.band.tier,
    #st.books))
print("first book: " .. st.books[1] .. "; the round crafts " .. st.band.queue[1].count .. " of a recipe")
local unknown = eco.skilllevel:status("juggling")

-- check
DOCS.eq(st.state, "level", "still levelling")
DOCS.eq(st.band.tier, 2, "the band from 20")
DOCS.eq(#st.books, 8, "this band's book and the next seven below the cap")
DOCS.eq(unknown.state, "unknown", "a skill with no levelling data")
examples.expect: Tinkering at 25 of 100 is in the tier-2 band; a trip buys that band's book and the next ones that start below the cap (8 books).

examples.title: The levelling decisions, step by step
examples.summary: eb.economy.skilllevel's pure rules: decide() says where a run starts (learn, unreadable, done, book or level); afterRound() says what a finished round comes to (done, again, buy, book or giveup); for Adorning, mostStockedTier() and roundFromStock() plan a round from what is on hand.
examples.code:
-- your script (pure)
local L = require("eb.economy.skilllevel")
local r = function(cur, max) return { ok = true, cur = cur, max = max } end
local starts = {
    L.decide({ learned = false, read = { ok = false } }),                     -- never learned
    L.decide({ learned = true, read = { ok = false } }),                      -- learned, does not read
    L.decide({ learned = true, read = r(100, 100) }),                         -- capped
    L.decide({ learned = true, read = r(10, 100), bandBooksInBags = true }),  -- scribe the band's books first
    L.decide({ learned = true, read = r(50, 100), bookDone = true }),         -- craft the band's rows
}
print("starts: " .. table.concat(starts, ", "))
local again = L.afterRound({ before = r(10, 100), after = r(14, 100) })
local done = L.afterRound({ before = r(97, 100), after = r(100, 100) })
local short = L.afterRound({ before = r(10, 100), after = r(10, 100), missing = true, tripsNoGain = 3 })
local stuck = L.afterRound({ before = r(10, 100), after = r(10, 100), noGain = 1, secs = 300, tierTried = true })
print(("after a gain -> %s; capped -> %s; short -> %s; stuck -> %s"):format(again, done, short, stuck))

local tier = L.mostStockedTier({ { tier = 1, powders = 2, fragments = 30 }, { tier = 2, powders = 5, fragments = 10 } })
local plan = L.roundFromStock(5, 10, 6)

-- check
DOCS.eq(table.concat(starts, ","), "learn,unreadable,done,book,level", "where a run starts")
DOCS.eq(again, "again", "a gain goes again")
DOCS.eq(done, "done", "capped is done")
DOCS.eq(short, "giveup", "short of materials after 3 trips with no gain gives up")
DOCS.eq(stuck, "giveup", "two rounds with no gain give up")
DOCS.eq(tier, 2, "the tier with the most worth on hand")
DOCS.eq(plan.dilute .. "/" .. plan.distil, "5/4", "dilute 5 powders, distil 4")
examples.expect: Each case answers as the rules say; the best-stocked Adorning tier is 2 and a round dilutes 5 and distils 4.

examples.title: Level Tinkering to its cap
examples.summary: eco.skilllevel:level("tinkering") reads the skill live before every round, crafts the band's rows, reads again, and stops when the skill caps - or blocks with the reason when a round gains nothing.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: a work bench, and a skill that rises by one for each item made (the game does that)
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ station = { name = "Work Bench" }, anyRecipe = true })
world.tinker = { cur = 18, max = 20 }

local eco = CW.economy(world, { me = { level = 20 },
    shim = { Skill = function(id) if id == "tinkering" then return world.tinker.cur, world.tinker.max end end } })

-- your script: poll it until it answers
local status, why = CW.poll(function() return eco.skilllevel:level("tinkering") end, 2000)
print(("tinkering 18 -> %d: %s"):format(world.tinker.cur, status))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the run finished")
DOCS.eq(world.tinker.cur, 20, "at the cap")
DOCS.check(#world.made >= 2, "the band's recipe was crafted")
examples.expect: Tinkering goes from 18 to its cap of 20 in one round of the band's recipe and the run answers done.

examples.title: Level a new crafter's tradeskill

DOCS.eq(world.made[3], "Fixture Hinge", "the recipe moved up with the level")

local world = CW.world({ bags = {

examples.title: Run a bulk salvage - and the guards that refuse a careless one
examples.summary: eco.transmute:tse(pick) transmutes, salvages, extracts or destroys the items a pick selects, each through the safety rules. A pick that does not say what goes is refused before anything is touched; dry = true only previews; a destroy without go = true only previews too.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: three treasured bag items
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ bags = {
    { id = 1, name = "Fixture Ring", rarity = "TREASURED", tier = "TREASURED", type = "Ring", ilvl = 40 },
    { id = 2, name = "Fixture Gloves", rarity = "TREASURED", tier = "TREASURED", type = "Gloves", ilvl = 42 },
    { id = 3, name = "Fixture Cape", rarity = "TREASURED", tier = "TREASURED", type = "Cape", ilvl = 45, heirloom = true } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local refused, why = eco.transmute:tse({})                                     -- "everything": refused
local dry, preview = eco.transmute:tse({ action = "destroy", tiers = { TREASURED = true } })   -- no go: a preview
print("empty pick -> " .. refused .. " (" .. why .. "); destroy without go -> " .. dry .. ", would take " .. #preview.taken)

local pick = { action = "salvage", tiers = { TREASURED = true }, maxLevel = 50 }
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.transmute:tse(pick) end)
print(("salvage -> %s, %d item left in the bags"):format(status, #world.bags))

-- check
DOCS.eq(refused, "blocked", "a pick that names nothing is refused")
DOCS.eq(preview.preview, true, "a destroy without go only previews")
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the salvage ran")
DOCS.eq(#world.bags, 1, "two salvaged")
DOCS.eq(world.bags[1].name, "Fixture Cape", "the heirloom stayed")
examples.expect: An empty pick is refused, a destroy without go only previews, and the salvage of treasured items up to level 50 takes the two that may go and keeps the heirloom.

examples.title: Level the Transmuting skill on a stone merchant
examples.summary: eco.transmute:levelTransmute(opts) opens the stone merchant, picks the cheapest stone in the currency most stones cost, buys one (answering the purchase question only when it names that stone), transmutes it, and goes again until the skill caps, the bags fill or the currency runs out.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: a stone merchant in reach, 50 marks, and a skill that rises with each transmute
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ merchant = { name = "a fixture stone merchant" }, currency = { ["fixture marks"] = 50 },
    offers = { { name = "Transmuter's Stone (Fixture)", price = { amount = 5, currency = "fixture marks" } } } })
world.tm = { cur = 30, max = 40 }
world.onTransmute = function(w) w.tm.cur = w.tm.cur + 1 end
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script: opts.skill reads the skill (in game EB reads it from the game layer); oneRound stops after one
local status = CW.poll(function()
    return eco.transmute:levelTransmute({ oneRound = true, skill = function() return world.tm.cur, world.tm.max end })
end)
print(("one round: Transmuting %d/%d, %d marks left"):format(world.tm.cur, world.tm.max, world.currency["fixture marks"]))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the round finished")
DOCS.eq(world.tm.cur, 31, "one transmute, one skill point")
DOCS.eq(world.answers[1].choice, 1, "the purchase question was answered Yes")
DOCS.has(world.answers[1].prompt, "Transmuter's Stone (Fixture)", "because it named the stone being bought")
DOCS.eq(world.merchantOpen, false, "the merchant window was closed")
examples.expect: One round buys the stone, confirms the purchase for that exact stone, transmutes it and raises the skill from 30 to 31.

examples.title: What an adornment profile still needs
examples.summary: An adornment PROFILE is { <slot> = <adornment name> }. eco.adornments:audit(profile) answers which slots already wear theirs and which still need it - and whether the missing adornment is in your bags.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: worn gear (one piece already adorned) and one adornment in the bags
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({
    worn = { chest = { id = 50, name = "Fixture Vest", adorns = { { slot = "white", name = "Fixture Rune" } } },
             legs = { id = 51, name = "Fixture Greaves" } },
    bags = { { id = 9, name = "Fixture Glyph" } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local profile = { chest = "Fixture Rune", legs = "Fixture Glyph", feet = "Fixture Sigil" }
local missing, present = eco.adornments:audit(profile)
local lines = {}
for _, p in ipairs(present) do lines[#lines + 1] = p.slot .. ": present" end
for _, m in ipairs(missing) do lines[#lines + 1] = ("%s: missing (%s)"):format(m.slot, m.where) end
table.sort(lines)
print(table.concat(lines, "; "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#present, 1, "the chest is done")
DOCS.eq(#missing, 2, "legs and feet still need theirs")
DOCS.eq(eco.adornments:hasAdorn(world.worn.chest, "Fixture Rune"), true, "hasAdorn reads the worn piece")
DOCS.eq(eco.adornments:adornInBags("Fixture Glyph").id, 9, "adornInBags finds the bag item")
examples.expect: The chest already wears its rune; the legs' glyph is missing but in the bags; the feet's sigil is missing and nowhere to be had.

examples.title: Apply an adornment profile
examples.summary: eco.adornments:applyProfile(profile, opts) gets each missing adornment - from the bags, else the adornment depot in reach, else (opts.broker = true) the broker under opts.maxCopper - and applies it to the slot's worn piece. A slot with nothing worn is skipped.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: two worn pieces, one adornment in the bags, one in the adornment depot
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({
    worn = { chest = { id = 50, name = "Fixture Vest" }, legs = { id = 51, name = "Fixture Greaves" } },
    bags = { { id = 9, name = "Fixture Rune" } },
    depots = { adorn = { { name = "Fixture Glyph", qty = 2 } } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local profile = { chest = "Fixture Rune", legs = "Fixture Glyph", feet = "Fixture Sigil" }
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.adornments:applyProfile(profile, { name = "raid set" }) end)
local on = {}
for _, slot in ipairs({ "chest", "legs" }) do
    for _, ad in ipairs(world.worn[slot].adorns or {}) do on[#on + 1] = slot .. " " .. ad.name end
end
print("applied: " .. table.concat(on, ", "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the profile run finished")
DOCS.eq(#on, 2, "two adornments applied")
DOCS.eq(world.depots.adorn[1].qty, 1, "the glyph came out of the adornment depot")
DOCS.check(CW.logged(world, "nothing worn in feet"), "the feet were skipped and said so")
examples.expect: The rune comes from the bags, the glyph from the adornment depot, both are applied; the feet are skipped because nothing is worn there.

examples.title: A class set of adornments, picked for each character
examples.summary: Put class sets in the config (cfg.adorn.classSets, keyed by subclass, class or archetype). eco.adornments:classSetFor(me) picks the one for a character; applyClassSet() applies it.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: a templar with a vest on and the set's rune in the bags
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ worn = { chest = { id = 50, name = "Fixture Vest" } }, bags = { { id = 9, name = "Fixture Rune" } } })
local cfg = { adorn = { classSets = {
    templar = { chest = "Fixture Rune" },          -- a subclass's own set
    priest = { chest = "Fixture Ward" },           -- every other priest
} } }
local eco = CW.economy(world, { me = { name = "Fixturae", subclass = "templar" }, cfg = cfg })

-- your script
local mine = eco.adornments:classSetFor()                                  -- this character (the snapshot)
local warden = eco.adornments:classSetFor({ subclass = "warden" })         -- anyone else
print(("templar -> chest %s; warden -> chest %s"):format(mine.chest, warden.chest))
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.adornments:applyClassSet() end)

-- check
DOCS.eq(mine.chest, "Fixture Rune", "the templar's own set")
DOCS.eq(warden.chest, "Fixture Ward", "the archetype's set for a warden")
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the class set was applied")
DOCS.eq(world.worn.chest.adorns[1].name, "Fixture Rune", "on the chest")
examples.expect: The templar gets its own set, a warden falls back to the priest set, and applying the templar's set puts its rune on the chest.

examples.title: Strip old gear's adornments, keep temporary adornments up
examples.summary: eco.adornments:unadorn{ tiers } takes the adornments off bag items of those tiers (a protected item is never touched); tempAdorns(profile, { active = fn(slot) }) re-applies only the slots whose temporary adornment is no longer on.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: two adorned bag items, worn gear for the temp profile and its adornments in the bags
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({
    bags = { { id = 20, name = "Fixture Old Vest", rarity = "FABLED", adorns = { { slot = "white", name = "Fixture Rune" } } },
             { id = 21, name = "a personal treasure of fixtures", rarity = "FABLED", adorns = { { slot = "white", name = "Fixture Gem" } } },
             { id = 30, name = "Fixture Spark" } },
    worn = { chest = { id = 50, name = "Fixture Vest" }, legs = { id = 51, name = "Fixture Greaves" } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local stripped = CW.poll(function() return eco.adornments:unadorn({ tiers = { FABLED = true } }) end)
local temp = { chest = "Fixture Flare", legs = "Fixture Spark" }
local still = CW.poll(function()
    return eco.adornments:tempAdorns(temp, { active = function(slot) return slot == "chest" end })
end)
local allOn = eco.adornments:tempAdorns(temp, { active = function() return true end })
print(("unadorn -> %s; temp -> %s"):format(stripped, world.worn.legs.adorns and "legs only" or "none"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#world.bags[1].adorns, 0, "the old vest was stripped")
DOCS.check(eco.adornments:adornInBags("Fixture Rune") ~= nil, "its rune is back in the bags")
DOCS.eq(#world.bags[2].adorns, 1, "the protected treasure was not touched")
DOCS.eq(still, "done", "the temp run finished")
DOCS.eq(world.worn.chest.adorns, nil, "the still-active chest was left alone")
DOCS.eq(allOn, "done", "every slot still on: nothing to do")
examples.expect: The old vest's rune comes back into the bags and the protected treasure keeps its adornment; with the chest's temporary adornment still on, only the legs are applied; with every slot on, nothing is done.

examples.title: How EB scores a piece of gear
examples.summary: eco.gearup:score(item, role) ranks Resolve first, then Fervor, then Potency, then the role's main stat (fighter stamina, priest wisdom, mage intelligence, scout agility), then any weights you set in cfg.gear, with item level only breaking a tie. roleOf(me) is the character's archetype.
examples.code:
-- offline: the economy facade for a templar, with an extra weight for the "haste" stat
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = {}, me = { subclass = "templar" }, cfg = { gear = { priest = { haste = 2 } } } })

-- your script
local role = eco.gearup:roleOf()
local s = function(stats, ilvl) return eco.gearup:score({ stats = stats, ilvl = ilvl or 0 }, role) end
local resolve, fervor, potency = s({ resolve = 1 }), s({ fervor = 999 }), s({ potency = 999 })
local wisdom, stamina = s({ wisdom = 50 }), s({ stamina = 50 })
print(("role %s: resolve > fervor > potency > wisdom"):format(role))

-- check
DOCS.eq(role, "priest", "a templar is a priest")
DOCS.check(resolve > fervor and fervor > potency and potency > wisdom, "the strict order")
DOCS.check(wisdom > stamina, "a priest's main stat is wisdom")
DOCS.check(s({ haste = 10 }) > s({}), "a configured weight counts")
DOCS.check(s({ wisdom = 50 }, 90) > s({ wisdom = 50 }, 80), "item level breaks a tie")
examples.expect: One point of Resolve outweighs any Fervor, Fervor outweighs Potency, a priest prefers wisdom, and a configured weight counts too.

examples.title: Wear the best gear in the bags (auto-upgrade)
examples.summary: eco.gearup:aup(opts) compares every bag piece with what is worn in its slot, equips each upgrade, carries the old piece's adornments over, and repeats (up to 5 passes) until a pass changes nothing.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: worn gear (the old vest is adorned) and two bag pieces
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({
    worn = { chest = { id = 60, name = "Fixture Plain Vest", slot = "chest", stats = { wisdom = 10 },
                       adorns = { { slot = "white", name = "Fixture Rune" } } },
             head = { id = 63, name = "Fixture Good Hat", slot = "head", stats = { wisdom = 5 } } },
    bags = { { id = 61, name = "Fixture Fine Vest", slot = "chest", stats = { wisdom = 30 } },
             { id = 62, name = "Fixture Junk Hat", slot = "head", stats = {} } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world, { me = { subclass = "templar" } })

-- your script
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.gearup:aup() end)
local chest = world.worn.chest
print(("chest: %s (%s), head: %s"):format(chest.name, (chest.adorns and #chest.adorns > 0) and "rune kept" or "bare",
    world.worn.head.name))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the passes ended")
DOCS.eq(chest.name, "Fixture Fine Vest", "the upgrade is worn")
DOCS.eq(chest.adorns[1].name, "Fixture Rune", "with the old piece's adornment")
DOCS.eq(world.worn.head.name, "Fixture Good Hat", "a worse piece is not worn")
examples.expect: The better vest is worn and keeps the old vest's rune; the worse hat stays in the bags.

examples.title: Fill an empty slot from the broker
examples.summary: eco.gearup:fillFromBroker{ slots, maxCopper } buys the best-scoring listing for each empty slot (the purchase question answered only when it names that listing), then an auto-upgrade pass wears it.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: nothing on the legs, two broker listings for that slot
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ listings = {
    { id = 1, name = "Fixture Leggings", slot = "legs", priceCopper = 500, stats = { wisdom = 20 } },
    { id = 2, name = "Fixture Cheap Pants", slot = "legs", priceCopper = 50, stats = { wisdom = 5 } } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world, { me = { subclass = "templar" } })

-- your script
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.gearup:fillFromBroker({ slots = { "legs" }, maxCopper = 1000 }) end)
print("legs now: " .. (world.worn.legs and world.worn.legs.name or "nothing"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "bought and worn")
DOCS.eq(world.worn.legs.name, "Fixture Leggings", "the best-scoring listing")
DOCS.has(world.answers[1].prompt, "Fixture Leggings", "the purchase question named it")
DOCS.eq(world.answers[1].choice, 1, "and was answered Yes")
examples.expect: The legs slot is empty; the better of two listings is bought, the purchase is confirmed for that item, and the leggings end up worn.

examples.title: Plan who in the group should get which spare piece
examples.summary: eco.gearup:planGroupTrades(exports) reads every box's worn gear and spare bag pieces and plans each trade to whoever it upgrades most (never a no-trade or heirloom piece). groupMatch(exports, opts) carries the plan out; with opts.planOnly it only answers the plan.
examples.code:
-- offline: three boxes' exports (in game each box sends its own over the crew relay)
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = {}, me = { name = "Fixturae", subclass = "templar" } })
local exports = {
    Tankard = { role = "fighter", worn = { chest = { stats = { stamina = 10 } } },
                bags = { { name = "Fixture Plate", slot = "chest", stats = { stamina = 50 } } } },
    Fixturae = { role = "priest", worn = { chest = { stats = { wisdom = 40 } } },
                 bags = { { name = "Fixture Robe", slot = "chest", stats = { wisdom = 20 } },
                          { name = "Fixture Heirloom Robe", slot = "chest", stats = { wisdom = 99 }, heirloom = true } } },
    Healio = { role = "priest", worn = { chest = { stats = { wisdom = 5 } } }, bags = {} },
}

-- your script
local plan = eco.gearup:groupMatch(exports, { planOnly = true })
for _, p in ipairs(plan) do print(("%s: %s -> %s (gain %.0f)"):format(p.item.name, p.from, p.to, p.gain)) end

-- check
DOCS.eq(#plan, 1, "one trade planned")
DOCS.eq(plan[1].to, "Healio", "the robe goes where it upgrades most")
DOCS.eq(plan[1].from, "Fixturae", "from the box that holds it")
examples.expect: The priest's spare robe goes to the other priest it upgrades; the tank's spare plate is best on the tank itself, so it is not traded; the heirloom is never planned.

examples.title: Turn Master scrolls into Grandmaster crafts
examples.summary: eco.grandmasters:plan(opts) lists each "(Master)" scroll in the bags (and, with depot = true, in the Scroll Depot) whose "(Grandmaster)" recipe is in your book; run(opts) only previews until you pass go = true, because every craft consumes a scroll.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: two scrolls in the bags, one in the Scroll Depot, the recipe book and a station
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ station = { name = "Engraved Desk" },
    bags = { { id = 1, name = "Fixture Heal IX (Master)", level = 131 }, { id = 2, name = "Fixture Smite X (Master)", level = 132 },
             { id = 3, name = "Fixture Oddity II (Master)", level = 131 } },
    depots = { scroll = { { name = "Fixture Ward XI (Master)", qty = 1 } } },
    recipes = { { name = "Fixture Heal IX (Grandmaster)" }, { name = "Fixture Smite X (Grandmaster)" },
                { name = "Fixture Ward XI (Grandmaster)" } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local Grandmasters = require("eb.economy.grandmasters")
local base, gm = Grandmasters.gmOf("Fixture Heal IX (Master)")
local plan = eco.grandmasters:plan({ depot = true })
local _, preview = eco.grandmasters:run({ depot = true })            -- no go: a preview, nothing consumed
local before = #world.made
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.grandmasters:run({ depot = true, go = true }) end)
print(("plan: %d crafts, %d skipped; preview made %d; go made %d"):format(#plan.crafts, #plan.skipped, before, #world.made))

-- check
DOCS.eq(gm, "Fixture Heal IX (Grandmaster)", "gmOf names the Grandmaster recipe")
DOCS.eq(base, "Fixture Heal IX", "and the ability")
DOCS.eq(#plan.crafts, 3, "three scrolls can be crafted up")
DOCS.eq(plan.skipped[1].why, "no (Grandmaster) recipe in the book", "the odd one is skipped with the reason")
DOCS.eq(preview.preview, true, "without go it only previews")
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "with go the run finished")
DOCS.eq(#world.made, 3, "three Grandmaster crafts")
DOCS.eq(Grandmasters.crafterFits("sage", "templar"), true, "a sage crafts priest upgrades")
DOCS.eq(Grandmasters.crafterFits("jeweler", "templar"), false, "a jeweler does not")
examples.expect: Three scrolls can become Grandmaster crafts (one from the Scroll Depot), one is skipped with no recipe; without go nothing is made; with go all three are crafted.

examples.title: Which collection pieces you still miss
examples.summary: eco.collections:journal() reads the journal's collections; scope(rows, word) picks the incomplete ones a word names (an exact category wins, else a name that contains the word; "all" = every incomplete one); missing(word) answers the piece names still needed and the ones that cannot be acted on.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the journal's collections page
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({ journal = {
    { name = "Fixture Shells", category = "Fixture Isle", level = 10, have = { "a pink shell" }, missing = { "a blue shell", "[12345]" } },
    { name = "Fixture Bones", category = "Fixture Isle", level = 12, missing = { "a fixture rib" } },
    { name = "Fixture Coins", category = "Fixture Mainland", level = 20, missing = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Feathers", category = "Fixture Mainland", level = 20, missing = { "a gray feather (Shiny)", "?" } } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local Collections = require("eb.economy.collections")
local rows = eco.collections:journal()
local isle, how = Collections.scope(rows, "fixture isle")
local feathers, how2 = Collections.scope(rows, "feathers")
local all = Collections.scope(rows, "all")
local names, unresolved = eco.collections:missing("all")
print("missing: " .. table.concat(names, ", "))
for _, u in ipairs(unresolved) do print(("set aside: %s (%s)"):format(u.name, u.why)) end

-- check
DOCS.eq(#isle .. " " .. how, "2 category", "a category")
DOCS.eq(#feathers .. " " .. how2, "1 collection", "a name")
DOCS.eq(#all, 3, "every incomplete collection (the complete one is never picked)")
DOCS.eq(#names, 3, "three pieces to find")
DOCS.eq(#unresolved, 2, "a placeholder and an unknown row are set aside")
DOCS.eq(Collections.clean("a gray feather (Shiny)"), "a gray feather", "clean drops the trailing tag")
DOCS.eq(Collections.usable("[12345]"), false, "a placeholder is not usable")
examples.expect: "fixture isle" is a category (two collections), "feathers" matches a name, "all" gives the three incomplete ones; the missing pieces are cleaned of their "(...)" tag and the placeholder rows are set aside.

examples.title: Add the collection pieces you already have
examples.summary: eco.collections:fill(word, { depot = true }) adds every missing piece that is in the bags, then takes the rest from the Collectible Depot in reach and adds those. Adding consumes the piece, so only a piece the journal still misses, not already collected and not protected, is ever added.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: the journal, three bag items and the Collectible Depot
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({
    journal = { { name = "Fixture Shells", category = "Fixture Isle", missing = { "a blue shell" } },
                { name = "Fixture Bones", category = "Fixture Isle", missing = { "a fixture rib" } },
                { name = "Fixture Feathers", category = "Fixture Mainland", missing = { "a gray feather" } } },
    bags = { { id = 1, name = "a blue shell", collectible = true },
             { id = 2, name = "a fixture rib", collectible = true, alreadyCollected = true },
             { id = 3, name = "a gray feather" } },                       -- its details never read: kept
    depots = { collectible = { { name = "a fixture rib", qty = 1, item = { collectible = true } } } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.collections:fill("all", { depot = true }) end)
local still = eco.collections:missing("all")
print("fill -> " .. status .. "; still missing: " .. table.concat(still, ", "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the fill finished")
DOCS.eq(#still, 1, "only the feather is still missing")
DOCS.eq(world.depots.collectible[1].qty, 0, "the rib came from the Collectible Depot")
DOCS.eq(#world.bags, 2, "the collected rib and the unread feather stayed")
DOCS.eq(eco.collections:needs("a gray feather (Shiny)"), true, "needs() answers for a shiny you just found")
examples.expect: The blue shell is added from the bags, the rib comes from the Collectible Depot and is added, the already-collected rib and the unread feather stay in the bags.

examples.title: Buy the missing collection pieces - the three models
examples.summary: eco.collections:buy(word, opts) plans by default ("confirm": counts and stops), hands back the buy list ("queue"), or buys on the broker ("auto") - and auto refuses without a per-piece price cap. A piece already in the bags is never bought.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: two missing pieces, both on the broker, one too dear
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local world = CW.world({
    journal = { { name = "Fixture Shells", category = "Fixture Isle", missing = { "a blue shell", "a fixture rib" } } },
    listings = { { id = 1, name = "a blue shell", priceCopper = 40 }, { id = 2, name = "a fixture rib", priceCopper = 400 } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)

-- your script
local _, confirm = eco.collections:buy("shells")                                   -- the default model
local _, queued = eco.collections:buy("shells", { model = "queue" })
local refused, why = eco.collections:buy("shells", { model = "auto" })
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.collections:buy("shells", { model = "auto", maxCopper = 100 }) end)
local bought = {}
for _, it in ipairs(world.bags) do bought[#bought + 1] = it.name end
print(("auto -> %s: bought %s; the rib was over the cap"):format(status, table.concat(bought, ", ")))

-- check
DOCS.eq(confirm.model .. " " .. #confirm.plan, "confirm 2", "confirm plans two and stops")
DOCS.eq(#queued.plan, 2, "queue hands back the list")
DOCS.eq(refused, "blocked", "auto with no cap is refused")
DOCS.has(why, "price cap", "and says why")
DOCS.eq(#bought, 1, "only the piece under the cap")
DOCS.eq(world.answers[1].choice, 1, "its purchase question was answered Yes")
examples.expect: confirm and queue spend nothing, auto without a cap is refused, auto with a 100 copper cap buys the shell (the purchase question answered for it) and passes the rib that costs more.

examples.title: Answer the economy's commands from your own economy
examples.summary: eb.economy.commands attaches the economy's command handlers to a registry for an economy you built: rows() are the command rows it needs, handlers(eco) the handler table, attach(reg, eco) declares any row the registry lacks and attaches every handler.
examples.code:
-- offline: an economy over the offline stand-in, and a fresh command registry
local CW = require("crafting.lib.craftworld")
local eco = CW.economy(CW.world())
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))

-- your script
local Commands = require("eb.economy.commands")
local ids = {}
for _, row in ipairs(Commands.rows()) do ids[#ids + 1] = row.id end
local ok, why = Commands.attach(reg, eco)
local okT, text = reg:dispatch("eb tse")
print(("eb tse -> %s: %s"):format(tostring(okT), text))
local okG, textG = reg:dispatch("eb tse give")

-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "attached (" .. tostring(why) .. ")")
local have = {}
for _, id in ipairs(ids) do have[id] = true end
DOCS.check(have["depot.ledger"] and have["depot.tse"] and have["gear.gearset"] and have["gear.unadorn"],
    "the rows it carries: the ledger, the T.S.E and the gear sets among them")
DOCS.check(type(Commands.handlers(eco)["depot.tse"]) == "function", "the handler table")
DOCS.eq(okT, false, "the bulk transmute refused an empty pick")
DOCS.has(text, "no saved T.S.E", "and says why: nothing is set up to take")
DOCS.eq(okG, false, "give needs the leader's name")
DOCS.has(textG, "needs the leader's name", "and says so")

examples.title: Which crafting, harvest and gear commands are live on this box
examples.summary: reg:unattached{ domain } lists the declared commands nobody answers yet on this box. On a box with the economy installed (EB for InnerSpace's boot does that) the crafting, harvest and gear commands are all attached: each typed line answers - a chore under way, a refusal in words, or a status line.

-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game you type in the console)
