examples.title: When the tank shouts, the healer reacts
examples.summary: Two boxes, two rules: the tank's cast fires a tag to the group, the healer's own rule turns the tag into a cast intent - one relay message, one reaction.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an in-memory relay between two boxes (in game each box's link rides the crew relay)
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()
local now = 0

-- your script: one coordination engine per box, each with the rules for its own abilities
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local Link = require("eb.coord.relaylink")
local function box(id, name, role)
    local link = Link.new({ box = id, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = id, name = name, role = role }, link = link, clock = function() return now end })
    link.join()                                   -- nothing is heard before join()
    local intents = {}
    coord:onIntent(function(it) intents[#intents + 1] = it end)   -- in game: hand it to the caster
    return coord, intents
end
local tank, tankIntents = box("is1", "Tankard", "tank")
local healer, healIntents = box("is2", "Mendwell", "healer")

tank:add({ id = "burn-on-shout", trigger = { kind = "cast", who = "tank", ability = "Rallying Shout" },
           action = { kind = "firetag", tag = "Burn" }, scope = "group" })
healer:add({ id = "heal-on-burn", trigger = { kind = "tag", tag = "Burn" },
             action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Mend", target = "PartyTank" }, scope = "self" })

-- the tank's box sees its own cast (in game EB's combat feeds this)
tank:feed({ kind = "cast", actor = "Tankard", name = "Tankard", role = "tank", ability = "Rallying Shout", isMe = true })
local it = healIntents[1]
print(("healer casts %s on %s (rule %s)"):format(it.ability, it.target, it.rule))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#healIntents, 1, "the healer reacts once")
DOCS.eq(#tankIntents, 0, "the tank has no reaction rule, so no intent")
DOCS.eq(it.kind, "cast", "a cast intent")
examples.expect: The tank sends one tag; the healer's box gets exactly one cast intent and the tank's gets none.

examples.title: Hold an ability for a while
examples.summary: An embargo rule puts an ability on hold for 20 seconds when a line is said; the cast stack asks holdsCast before casting, and the hold ends on its own.
examples.code:
-- your script
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local now = 0
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "mage" }, clock = function() return now end })
coord:add({ id = "no-blast", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "reflects all spells" },
            action = { kind = "embargo", ability = "Fixture Blast", durationMs = 20000 }, scope = "self" })
coord:add({ id = "blast-again", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "shield shatters" },
            action = { kind = "liftembargo", ability = "Fixture Blast" }, scope = "self" })

coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The Overseer of Fixtures reflects all spells!" })
local a = coord:holdsCast("Fixture Blast")
now = 19000; coord:tick(); local b = coord:holdsCast("Fixture Blast")
now = 21000; coord:tick(); local c = coord:holdsCast("Fixture Blast")
print(("held: %s at 0 s, %s at 19 s, %s at 21 s"):format(tostring(a), tostring(b), tostring(c)))

-- a second warning, then the lift line ends it early
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "It reflects all spells again" })
local up = #coord:activeEmbargoes()
coord:feed({ kind = "text", text = "Its shield shatters." })

-- check
DOCS.check(a and b and not c, "held for its 20 seconds, then free")
DOCS.eq(up, 1, "one embargo up after the second warning")
DOCS.eq(coord:holdsCast("Fixture Blast"), false, "the lift line ended it at once")
DOCS.eq(coord:holdsCast("Fixture Strike"), false, "other abilities are never held")
examples.expect: Fixture Blast is held after the warning line, still held at 19 s, free again at 21 s; a lift ends a hold early.

examples.title: A moment after this, if that follows
examples.summary: A rule with a delay and a follow-up gate: act only when a second line comes within the window ("require"), or only when it does NOT ("block").
examples.code:
-- your script
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local now = 0
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "healer" }, clock = function() return now end })
local did = {}
coord:onIntent(function(it) did[#did + 1] = it.ability end)

-- 1. "Beware", then 500 ms later, if "flames" is said within 3 s: ward the group
coord:add({ id = "ward", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "Beware" }, delayMs = 500,
            gate = { kind = "chat", match = "flames", withinMs = 3000, mode = "require" },
            action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Ward" }, scope = "self" })
-- 2. "rumbles": stand still if "calms" follows within 2 s, dodge if it does not
coord:add({ id = "stand", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "rumbles" },
            gate = { kind = "chat", match = "calms", withinMs = 2000, mode = "require" },
            action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Stand" }, scope = "self" })
coord:add({ id = "dodge", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "rumbles" },
            gate = { kind = "chat", match = "calms", withinMs = 2000, mode = "block" },
            action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Dodge" }, scope = "self" })

coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "Beware the fixture!" })
now = 600; coord:tick()                                   -- the delay is up: the gate opens
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "Fixture flames rise" })
local afterWard = #did

coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The floor rumbles" })    -- this time the calm line follows
now = 1200; coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The floor calms" })
now = 4000; coord:tick()
local afterCalm = #did

coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The floor rumbles" })    -- and this time it does not
now = 7000; coord:tick()                                  -- the 2 s window passed quietly
print("casts in order: " .. table.concat(did, ", "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(afterWard, 1, "the ward went up when its follow-up line came")
DOCS.eq(afterCalm, 2, "the calm line let stand act and held dodge back")
DOCS.eq(did[3], "Fixture Dodge", "with no calm line, dodge acted when its window closed")
DOCS.eq(#did, 3, "nothing else acted")
examples.expect: The require rules act when their follow-up line arrives; the block rule acts only when its window passes quietly.

examples.title: A rule that listens to the game
examples.summary: bindEvents feeds a rules engine from eb.events: a tell or an emote line triggers a crew rule, and the intent becomes one eb command line.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local events = w.events()

-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "tank" }, clock = P.now })
local lines = {}
coord:onIntent(function(it) if it.kind == "crew" then lines[#lines + 1] = it.line end end)
coord:add({ id = "pause-on-roar", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "lets out a deafening roar" },
            action = { kind = "crew", line = "eb all pause" }, scope = "self" })
coord:bindEvents(events)
P.pulse().every("coord.tick", 100, function(now) coord:tick(now) end)   -- delays, gates and embargo expiry

-- the game delivers the emote (offline: the fake host fires ISXEQ2's chat event)
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 15, speaker = "Overseer of Fixtures", speakerIsNPC = true,
                  message = "The Overseer of Fixtures lets out a deafening roar!" })
w.frame(3)
print("crew line: " .. tostring(lines[1]))

-- check
DOCS.eq(#lines, 1, "one crew intent")
DOCS.eq(lines[1], "eb all pause", "the rule's command line")
examples.expect: The emote line in chat triggers the rule; its crew intent carries "eb all pause".

examples.title: Exactly one box cures
examples.summary: Two healers want the same cure: each lays a bid, the claim window closes, the same winner is picked on both boxes, the winner casts and reports it landed.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an in-memory relay between two boxes
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()
local now = 0

-- your script: one arbiter per box, on a relay link
local Arb = require("eb.coord.arbiter")
local Link = require("eb.coord.relaylink")
local function box(id, rank)
    local link = Link.new({ box = id, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local arb = Arb.new({ box = id, role = rank, link = link, clock = function() return now end })
    link.join()
    return arb
end
local a, b = box("is1", 10), box("is2", 20)
local cure = { action = "cure", target = "1234", scope = "group" }    -- the member being cured

local first = { a:request(cure), b:request(cure) }       -- both bid; is2 hears is1's better bid at once
now = 200                                                 -- the 150 ms window has passed
local ra, rb = a:request(cure), b:request(cure)
print(("is1 %s, is2 %s"):format(ra, rb))
if ra == "go" then a:acted(cure) end                      -- the winner casts and says so
local whileActing = b:statusOf("cure", "1234")
a:done(cure, true)                                        -- the cure landed: everyone clears it

-- check
DOCS.eq(first[1], "wait", "is1 waits while the window is open")
DOCS.eq(first[2], "standdown", "is2 already knows a better box wants it")
DOCS.eq(ra, "go", "the lower rank wins")
DOCS.eq(rb, "standdown", "the other box stands down")
DOCS.eq(whileActing, "standdown", "while is1 casts, is2 keeps standing down")
DOCS.eq(a:statusOf("cure", "1234"), "idle", "done cleared the claim")
examples.expect: is1 waits out the claim window; is2 has already heard the better bid and stands down; then is1 gets go.

examples.title: When the winner never finishes
examples.summary: The box that won a rez casts it but never reports it landed; after the failover time the next box takes the rez, so a member is never left lying.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an in-memory relay between two boxes
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()
local now = 0

-- your script
local Arb = require("eb.coord.arbiter")
local Link = require("eb.coord.relaylink")
local function box(id, rank)
    local link = Link.new({ box = id, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local arb = Arb.new({ box = id, role = rank, link = link, clock = function() return now end })
    link.join()
    return arb
end
local a, b = box("is1", 10), box("is2", 20)
local rez = { action = "rez", target = "5678", scope = "group" }

a:request(rez); b:request(rez)
now = 200
local won = a:request(rez)
b:request(rez)
a:acted(rez)                                  -- is1 starts the rez ... and its box dies before it lands
now = 1000; b:poll()
local early = b:request(rez)
now = 3000; b:poll()                          -- past the 2.5 s with no word from is1: the rez is open again
b:request(rez)                                -- is2 bids anew (a new round: its bid has a short window of its own)
now = 3200
local late = b:request(rez)
print("is2 takes over: " .. late)

-- check
DOCS.eq(won, "go", "is1 won the rez")
DOCS.eq(early, "standdown", "inside the failover time is2 still stands down")
DOCS.eq(late, "go", "after it, is2 takes the rez")
examples.expect: is1 wins and acts, then goes silent; 2.5 s later the rez is open again, is2 bids anew and, once its bid's short window has passed, its request answers go.

examples.title: Claim before a group cure
examples.summary: needsClaim says which combat casts need a claim; attach wraps an engine's cast so a group cure is claimed first and stands down when another box has it.
examples.code:
-- your script
local gate = require("eb.coord.combat_gate")
local Arb = require("eb.coord.arbiter")
local now = 0
local arb = Arb.new({ box = "is1", role = 10, clock = function() return now end })   -- no link: a solo box

local cureAll = { kind = "cure", target = "group", entry = { target = "AllParty", gates = { type = "GROUP" } } }   -- a group cure says so
local nuke = { kind = "dps", target = 200, entry = { target = "Target" } }
local key = gate.needsClaim(cureAll)
local none = gate.needsClaim(nuke)

-- an engine of your own with a cast(dec) method: attach claims before every cast that needs it
local engine = { sent = 0 }
function engine:cast(dec) self.sent = self.sent + 1; return true end
local detach = gate.attach(engine, arb, { now = function() return now end })
local first = engine:cast(cureAll)                         -- the claim window is still open
now = 200
local second = engine:cast(cureAll)                        -- this box won: the cast goes out
detach()
print(("%s|%s|%s: %s, then %s"):format(key.action, key.target, key.scope, first and "go" or "wait",
    second and "go" or "wait"))

-- check
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "a damage art needs no claim")
DOCS.eq(first, false, "the first cast waited for the claim window")
DOCS.eq(second, true, "the second cast went out")
DOCS.eq(engine.sent, 1, "the engine's own cast ran exactly once")
DOCS.eq(cureAll.sendWhy, "wait for the arbitration (collecting bids)", "the decision says why it held")
examples.expect: A group cure needs the "groupcure" claim, a damage art none; the wrapped cast waits, then casts once it wins.

examples.title: Read a cast stack's tags as rules
examples.summary: An imported cast stack's ability tag and embargo tag become plain rules; imported into an engine, the tag fires and the hold works.
examples.code:
-- your script
local Import = require("eb.coord.tagimport")
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local rows = {
    { name = "Fixture Shout", ATag = "Burn", AType = "Trigger Only" },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ATag = "Burn", AType = "Listen Only", Target = "@Group" },
    { name = "Fixture Blast", ETag = "Calm", EType = "Listen Only" },
    { name = "Fixture Jab" },                                              -- no tags: not coordination
}
local res = Import.importRows(rows)
local names = {}
for _, r in ipairs(res.rules) do names[#names + 1] = r.name end
print(("%d rules: %s"):format(#res.rules, table.concat(names, " | ")))

local now = 0
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "" }, clock = function() return now end })
local cast = {}
coord:onIntent(function(it) cast[#cast + 1] = it.ability end)
Import.importInto(coord, rows)
coord:feed({ kind = "cast", actor = "Fixturae", name = "Fixturae", ability = "Fixture Shout", isMe = true })
coord:add({ id = "calm-on", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "calms" }, action = { kind = "embargo", tag = "Calm" } })
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The room calms" })

-- check
DOCS.eq(#res.rules, 3, "three rules from the tagged rows")
DOCS.eq(res.count.atag, 2, "two rows carried an ability tag")
DOCS.eq(cast[1], "Fixture Strike", "the tag made the listener cast")
DOCS.eq(coord:holdsCast("Fixture Blast"), true, "the embargo holds the bound ability")
examples.expect: Two rows with tags give three rules; casting the trigger ability fires the tag, which casts the listener; the embargo trigger holds the bound ability.

examples.title: The coordination messages and the tie-break
examples.summary: A tag and a claim as relay fields and back, the one claim key, and the tie-break every box computes the same way.
examples.code:
-- your script
local W = require("eb.coord.cowire")
local tag = W.decodeTag(W.encodeTag({ from = "is1", seq = 7, scope = "group", phase = "raise", tag = "Hold Fire",
    data = "20000" }))
local claim = W.decodeClaim(W.encodeClaim({ from = "is2", seq = 3, role = 5, scope = "raid", action = "Cure",
    target = "1234", phase = "bid" }))

local bids = { { from = "is1", role = 10 }, { from = "is2", role = 5 }, { from = "is3", role = 10 } }
local best = W.winner(bids)
local tie = W.winner({ { from = "is3", role = 10 }, { from = "is1", role = 10 } })
local key = W.claimKey("Cure", "1234", "raid")
print(("winner %s (rank %d) | tie goes to %s | key %s"):format(best.from, best.role, tie.from, key))

-- check
DOCS.eq(tag.tag, "HoldFire", "a tag travels without spaces")
DOCS.eq(tag.phase, "raise", "an embargo raise")
DOCS.eq(tag.data, "20000", "the free-text field comes back whole")
DOCS.eq(tag.mid, "is1#7", "every message carries <box>#<seq>")
DOCS.eq(claim.role, 5, "the rank comes back as a number")
DOCS.eq(claim.action, "cure", "actions are lower case on the wire")
DOCS.check(W.outranks({ from = "is9", role = 1 }, { from = "is1", role = 2 }), "a lower rank beats a smaller box id")
examples.expect: Both messages survive the round trip; the lower rank wins, a tie goes to the smaller box id.

examples.title: Keep a set of rules
examples.summary: Add a saved set of rules at once, look one up, switch it off and on, remove it, and list what is left - what a rules window does.
examples.code:
-- your script
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "healer" }, clock = function() return 0 end })
local acted = 0
coord:onIntent(function() acted = acted + 1 end)
local ids = coord:addAll({
    { id = "ward-on-flames", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "flames" },
      action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Ward" }, scope = "self" },
    { id = "hold-on-root", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "roots you" },
      action = { kind = "embargo", ability = "Fixture Leap", durationMs = 5000 }, scope = "self" },
    { id = "crew-on-wipe", trigger = { kind = "event", event = "GroupChanged" },
      action = { kind = "crew", line = "eb all pause" }, scope = "self" },
})

coord:enable("ward-on-flames", false)
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "Fixture flames rise" })
local whileOff = acted
coord:enable("ward-on-flames", true)
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "Fixture flames rise" })
local afterOn = acted
local rule = coord:get("ward-on-flames")
coord:remove("ward-on-flames")
local left = {}
for _, r in ipairs(coord:all()) do left[#left + 1] = r.id end
print(("loaded %d, acted while off: %d, after on: %d, left: %s"):format(#ids, whileOff, afterOn, table.concat(left, ", ")))

-- check
DOCS.eq(rule.trigger.kind, "chat", "get answers the stored rule")
DOCS.eq(rule.action.kind, "cast", "with its action")
DOCS.eq(#left, 2, "two rules left")
DOCS.eq(coord:get("ward-on-flames"), nil, "the removed rule is gone")
examples.expect: Three rules load; a switched-off rule does not act; the removed one is gone from the list.

examples.title: Hand a claim over at once
examples.summary: A box that cannot cast at all calls fail() and the next box takes the cure straight away; a box whose need went away calls release(); claims can also be carried over your own transport with onClaim.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in: an in-memory relay between two boxes
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()
local now = 0

-- your script
local Arb = require("eb.coord.arbiter")
local Link = require("eb.coord.relaylink")
local W = require("eb.coord.cowire")
local function box(id, rank)
    local link = Link.new({ box = id, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local arb = Arb.new({ box = id, role = rank, link = link, clock = function() return now end })
    link.join()
    return arb
end
local a, b = box("is1", 10), box("is2", 20)
local cure = { action = "cure", target = "1234", scope = "group" }
a:request(cure); b:request(cure)
now = 200
a:request(cure)
a:fail(cure)                                    -- out of power: give the claim up now
local next = b:request(cure)
b:release(cure)                                 -- the member was cured by something else
local cleared = b:statusOf("cure", "1234")

-- a third arbiter with no link: carry a claim to it yourself (your own transport decoded it)
local c = Arb.new({ box = "is3", role = 30, clock = function() return now end })
c:onClaim(W.decodeClaim(W.encodeClaim({ from = "is9", seq = 1, role = 1, scope = "group", action = "rez",
    target = "77", phase = "bid" })))
local hand = c:request({ action = "rez", target = "77", scope = "group" })
print(("is1 failed -> is2 %s | released -> %s | hand-fed bid -> %s"):format(next, cleared, hand))

-- check
DOCS.eq(next, "go", "the next box takes over at once")
DOCS.eq(cleared, "idle", "release cleared this box's claim")
DOCS.eq(hand, "standdown", "a better bid carried by hand makes this box stand down")
examples.expect: After is1 fails, is2's next request is go; release clears the key; a claim fed by hand makes this box stand down.

examples.title: Read combat lines into records
examples.summary: combatlog.parse turns one line of combat text into a record - a hit, a damage-over-time tick, a heal, a ward, a miss, a death - with YOU resolved to your own name; anything else is nil.
examples.code:
-- your script
local log = require("eb.ui.monitor.combatlog")
local me = "Fixturae"
local lines = {
    "YOUR Fixture Flare hits a fixture brute for 1,200 points of heat damage.",
    "A fixture brute suffers 300 points of poison damage from Fixturae's Fixture Venom.",
    "Mendwell's Fixture Mend heals Tankard for 800 hit points (150).",
    "Mendwell wards YOU against 500 points of damage.",
    "A fixture brute tries to hit YOU, but YOU parry!",
    "You have slain a fixture brute!",
    "Tankard says, 'Pull the next one.'",
}
local recs, show = {}, {}
for i, line in ipairs(lines) do
    local r = log.parse(line, { me = me, t = i * 1000 })
    recs[i] = r
    if r then
        if r.kind == "hit" then show[#show + 1] = ("hit %d %s"):format(r.amount, r.dtype)
        elseif r.kind == "heal" then show[#show + 1] = ("heal %d (+%d over)"):format(r.amount, r.over)
        elseif r.kind == "ward" then show[#show + 1] = ("ward %d"):format(r.amount)
        elseif r.kind == "miss" then show[#show + 1] = "miss " .. r.avoid
        else show[#show + 1] = r.kind end
    end
end
print(table.concat(show, " | "))

-- check
DOCS.eq(recs[1].src, me, "YOUR is your own name")
DOCS.eq(recs[1].ability, "Fixture Flare", "the ability")
DOCS.eq(recs[2].src, me, "a damage-over-time tick credits its caster")
DOCS.eq(recs[3].dst, "Tankard", "the one healed")
DOCS.eq(recs[4].dst, me, "a ward on YOU")
DOCS.eq(recs[7], nil, "a chat line is not combat")
local all = log.parseAll(table.concat(lines, "\n"), { me = me, t0 = 0, stepMs = 1000 })
DOCS.eq(#all, 6, "parseAll keeps the six combat lines")
DOCS.eq(all[2].t, 1000, "and stamps them a step apart")
examples.expect: Each combat line gives its kind, who, whom and how much; a chat line gives nil.

examples.title: Meter a fight
examples.summary: Feed stamped combat lines to a parser and read the live fight: damage per second per character, the top character's abilities, and who took damage.
examples.code:
-- your script
local Parser = require("eb.ui.monitor.parser")
local log = require("eb.ui.monitor.combatlog")
local parser = Parser.new({ me = "Fixturae", friends = { "Tankard", "Mendwell" } })

-- a saved fight: "<ms><tab><line>" (in game parse_feed.attach feeds the parser live)
local fight = table.concat({
    "1000\tYOUR Fixture Flare hits a fixture brute for 1200 points of heat damage.",
    "2000\tTankard hits a fixture brute for 1200 points of crushing damage.",
    "3000\tA fixture brute hits Tankard for 900 points of slashing damage.",
    "6000\tYOUR Fixture Flare critically hits a fixture brute for 2400 points of heat damage.",
    "11000\tTankard hits a fixture brute for 1200 points of crushing damage.",
}, "\n")
for _, rec in ipairs(log.parseStamped(fight, { me = "Fixturae" })) do parser:ingest(rec) end

local v = parser:current()
local top = v.bars[1]
print(("%d s: %d dps | %s %d (%d%%) | %s took %d"):format(v.durMs / 1000, v.dps, top.name, top.dmg, top.pct,
    v.intake[1].name, v.intake[1].dmg))

-- check
DOCS.eq(v.total.dmg, 6000, "all outgoing damage")
DOCS.eq(top.name, "Fixturae", "the top damage dealer")
DOCS.eq(v.abilities[1].name, "Fixture Flare", "the top dealer's abilities are listed")
DOCS.eq(v.abilities[1].crits, 1, "one critical")
local named = false
for _, f in ipairs(v.foes) do named = named or f:lower() == "a fixture brute" end
DOCS.check(named, "the foe is listed (names keep the case a line gave them)")
local ex = parser:export()
DOCS.eq(ex.sources.Tankard.dmg, 2400, "export: a flat record of the fight")
examples.expect: Over a 10-second fight the crew does 6000 damage (600 per second), Fixturae leads, the tank took 900.

examples.title: One fight ends, the next begins
examples.summary: A quiet gap longer than idleMs ends a fight; breakEncounter ends one on purpose (EB does on a zone change); snapshot lists the past fights, newest first.
examples.code:
-- your script
local Parser = require("eb.ui.monitor.parser")
local parser = Parser.new({ me = "Fixturae", idleMs = 5000 })
parser:setFriends({ "Tankard", "Mendwell" })            -- the crew: always friends
parser:addFriend("Sparkwick")
local function hit(t, amount)
    return parser:ingest({ t = t, kind = "hit", src = "Fixturae", dst = "a fixture brute", amount = amount })
end
hit(0, 100); hit(2000, 100)                -- fight 1
hit(20000, 300)                            -- 18 s later: fight 2
parser:breakEncounter()                    -- ended on purpose (a zone change)
local third = hit(21000, 50)               -- fight 3, live

local snap = parser:snapshot()
print(("fights %d, past %d, live fight %d"):format(snap.fights, #snap.encounters, snap.current.id))

-- check
DOCS.eq(third, 3, "ingest answers the fight a record went into")
DOCS.eq(snap.encounters[1].id, 2, "newest past fight first")
DOCS.eq(snap.encounters[2].total.dmg, 200, "fight 1's damage")
DOCS.check(parser:isFoe("a fixture brute"), "a name with a leading 'a' is a mob")
DOCS.check(not parser:isFoe("Mendwell"), "a single word is taken for a player")
local past = parser:viewEncounter(parser.history[1])
DOCS.eq(past.total.dmg, 200, "viewEncounter reads a past fight")
DOCS.check(not parser:isFoe("Sparkwick"), "a friend added by name")
parser:reset()
DOCS.eq(parser:snapshot().fights, 0, "reset forgets every fight")
examples.expect: Three fights: two split by the quiet gap, one by breakEncounter; the snapshot lists the two past fights.

examples.title: Meter the game's own combat lines
examples.summary: parse_feed.attach wires a parser to eb.events: each combat line that reaches ChatLine is read, counted and re-announced as a CombatEvent; a zone change ends the fight.
examples.code:
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
local events = w.events()

-- your script
local Feed = require("eb.ui.monitor.parse_feed")
local Parser = require("eb.ui.monitor.parser")
local parser = Parser.new({ me = "Fixturae" })
local seen, closed = 0, nil
events.on(Feed.EVENTS.COMBAT_EVENT, function() seen = seen + 1 end)
events.on(Feed.EVENTS.ENCOUNTER, function(e) closed = e.reason end)
local detach = Feed.attach({ events = events, parser = parser, combatlog = require("eb.ui.monitor.combatlog") })

-- the game delivers lines (offline: the fake host fires ISXEQ2's chat event, then the zone events)
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 3, message = "YOUR Fixture Flare hits a fixture brute for 1000 points of heat damage." })
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 3, message = "YOU hit a fixture brute for 500 points of slashing damage." })
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 8, speaker = "Tankard", message = "nice pull" })
w.frame(2)
local dmg = parser:current().total.dmg
w.host:fire("EQ2_FinishedZoning", "4")
w.frame(2)
print(("counted %d records, %d damage; fight closed: %s"):format(seen, dmg, tostring(closed)))
detach()

-- check
DOCS.eq(seen, 2, "two records announced")
DOCS.eq(dmg, 1500, "both hits counted")
DOCS.eq(closed, "zone", "the zone change closed the fight")
DOCS.eq(parser:current(), nil, "no fight is open after zoning")
examples.expect: Two combat lines are counted and announced; a plain chat line is ignored; zoning closes the fight.

examples.title: Share a fight with the crew
examples.summary: A box sends the crew one short summary per fight, never its raw lines; the shared service hands every window the same monitor.
examples.code:
-- your script
local Feed = require("eb.ui.monitor.parse_feed")
local Parser = require("eb.ui.monitor.parser")
local service = require("eb.ui.monitor.service")
local parser = Parser.new({ me = "Fixturae" })
parser:ingest({ t = 0, kind = "hit", src = "Fixturae", dst = "a fixture brute", amount = 600 })
parser:ingest({ t = 1000, kind = "heal", src = "Fixturae", dst = "Fixturae", amount = 250 })
parser:ingest({ t = 4000, kind = "hit", src = "Fixturae", dst = "a fixture brute", amount = 300 })

local line = Feed.crewLine("is1", parser:export())     -- send this over the crew relay
local back = Feed.parseCrewLine(line)                  -- what the lead reads from it
print(("%s -> %s did %d"):format(line, back.box, back.dmg))

service.setMonitor(parser)                              -- the one monitor every window reads
local shared = service.monitor()
service.publish({ app = { monitor = parser } })

-- check
DOCS.eq(back.heal, 250, "the summary carries the healing")
DOCS.eq(back.durMs, 4000, "and the fight's length")
DOCS.eq(Feed.parseCrewLine("not a summary"), nil, "anything else is not a summary")
DOCS.eq(shared, parser, "the service hands out the same monitor")
DOCS.eq(service.app().monitor, parser, "the published app carries it too")
service.reset()
examples.expect: The summary line round-trips; the service answers the monitor it was given.

examples.title: Ask an ability export what a character can do
examples.summary: Wrap an export with reader.load (or read a saved one back with reader.loadText) and ask it by name - any rank finds the line - by group, by label, or for the cast-stack shortlist. Here the export is converted from a few invented records, saved as text and read back the way a helper would read a file.
examples.code:
local reader = require("eb.exports.reader")
local util = require("eb.exports.util")

-- an export to read (offline: converted from invented records; in game take one from exporter.snapshot)
local ex0 = require("eb.exports.convert_v3").convert({ meta = { subClass = "templar" }, abilities = {
    { Name = "Fixture Mend III", ID = 103, Level = 40, SpellBookType = 0, TargetType = 1, IsBeneficial = true,
      EffectDesc1 = "Heals target for 900 to 1100 hit points" },
    { Name = "Fixture Smite", ID = 201, Level = 12, SpellBookType = 1, DoesDmg = true,
      EffectDesc1 = "Inflicts 400 divine damage on target" },
    { Name = "Fixture Calm", ID = 301, Level = 20, SpellBookType = 4, EffectDesc1 = "Increases max power by 2%" },
} }, { anonymize = true })
local text = util.serialize(ex0)                     -- what you would write to a file (off the game thread)

-- your script: read it back and ask it
local ex = reader.loadText(text)
local mend = ex:find("Fixture Mend")
local heals = 0
for e in ex:iter() do if ex:labels(e).heal then heals = heals + 1 end end
local shortlist = ex:castStackCandidates()
print(("book: %d entries, %d heal, %d on the cast-stack shortlist"):format(ex:summary().total, heals, #shortlist))

-- check
DOCS.eq(mend.name, "Fixture Mend", "found whatever the rank")
DOCS.check(ex:has("Fixture Mend II"), "a rank name finds the same line")
DOCS.check(ex:labels("Fixture Mend").heal, "its labels say heal")
DOCS.eq(#ex:abilities(), 2, "the active abilities")
DOCS.eq(#shortlist, 2, "the passive is not on the shortlist")
DOCS.eq(ex:meta().archetype, "priest", "the header")
DOCS.eq(ex:summary().aa, 1, "the passive counts as an alternate-advancement entry")
DOCS.eq(reader.load(ex0):find("Fixture Smite").topLevel, 12, "load wraps a table you already have")
examples.expect: The heal is found by a rank name, its labels say heal, the passive is left off the shortlist, and the saved text reads back the same.

examples.title: Fold per-rank ability records into an ability export
examples.summary: An ability list arrives with one record per rank. convert folds every rank of a line into one entry - the highest held rank kept, the lowest level as when the line was learned - labels it, and masks big damage numbers in the effect text. convertText does the same from JSON text with your decoder.
examples.code:
local convert = require("eb.exports.convert_v3")

-- one record per rank, in the record layout (offline: invented abilities)
local doc = { meta = { subClass = "templar" }, abilities = {
    { Name = "Fixture Mend", ID = 101, Level = 10, SpellBookType = 0, TargetType = 1, IsBeneficial = true,
      CastingTime = 1.5, RecastTime = 10, MaxRange = 25, EffectDesc1 = "Heals target for 120 to 150 hit points" },
    { Name = "Fixture Mend II", ID = 102, Level = 25, SpellBookType = 0, TargetType = 1, IsBeneficial = true,
      CastingTime = 1.5, RecastTime = 10, MaxRange = 25, EffectDesc1 = "Heals target for 310 to 380 hit points" },
    { Name = "Fixture Smite", ID = 201, Level = 12, SpellBookType = 1, TargetType = 1, DoesDmg = true,
      EffectDesc1 = "Inflicts 12,500 divine damage on target" },
} }

-- your script
local ex = convert.convert(doc, { anonymize = true })
local mend, smite
for _, e in ipairs(ex.abilities) do
    if e.name == "Fixture Mend" then mend = e elseif e.name == "Fixture Smite" then smite = e end
end
print(("%s: learned %d, held %d (%s), %s"):format(mend.name, mend.level, mend.topLevel, mend.rank,
    mend.labels.heal and "heal" or "-"))
local fromText = convert.convertText('{"abilities":[{"Name":"Fixture Ward","ID":7,"Level":5,"SpellBookType":0}]}',
    { decode = require("ebkit.jsontable").decode, anonymize = true })

-- check
DOCS.eq(#ex.abilities, 2, "two ranks folded into one line, plus the art")
DOCS.eq(mend.topLevel, 25, "the highest rank is held")
DOCS.eq(mend.level, 10, "the lowest level is when the line was learned")
DOCS.check(mend.labels.heal, "the heal is labelled heal")
DOCS.check(smite.labels.dps, "the art is labelled dps")
DOCS.has(smite.effects[1], "N divine damage", "a big number is masked in the kept text")
DOCS.eq(ex.meta.character, nil, "anonymize leaves the character out")
DOCS.eq(ex.meta.archetype, "priest", "the subclass gives the archetype")
DOCS.eq(fromText.abilities[1].name, "Fixture Ward", "convertText reads JSON with your decoder")
examples.expect: Two ranks of the heal fold into one entry labelled heal, learned at 10 and held at 25; the damage art is labelled dps and its big number is masked.

examples.title: Snapshot a character's ability book
examples.summary: exporter.snapshot asks a host for the book and each ability's details, then folds and labels them into an ability export. Asking for every ability's details is a server request: snapshot asks once (host.warm), waits a bounded while for them (host.ready), and reports how many had not arrived. Here the host is a small fake.
examples.code:
local exporter = require("eb.exports.exporter")

-- a host over the game's ability reads (offline: invented abilities; in game build it over the game layer)
local warmed = 0
local host = {
    warm = function() warmed = warmed + 1 end,
    ready = function() return true end,
    list = function() return { { id = 11, name = "Fixture Ward II", tier = 3 }, { id = 12, name = "Fixture Taunt" } } end,
    detail = function(id)
        if id == 11 then return { spellbookType = 0, targetTypeId = 1, beneficial = true, castSeconds = 1,
            classes = { { level = 30 } }, effects = { { text = "Wards target against 500 points of damage" } } } end
        return nil                                       -- this one's details have not arrived yet
    end,
    identity = function() return { character = "Fixturae", subClass = "guardian" } end,
}

-- your script: one snapshot, kept and reused (never every frame)
local ex, info = exporter.snapshot({ host = host, anonymize = true, maxWaitMs = 0 })
print(("read %d abilities, %d detail still on its way"):format(info.read, info.detailMisses))

-- check
DOCS.eq(info.read, 2, "both abilities were read")
DOCS.eq(info.detailMisses, 1, "the missing detail is counted")
DOCS.eq(warmed, 1, "the details were asked for once")
DOCS.eq(ex.meta.character, nil, "anonymize keeps the character out")
DOCS.eq(ex.meta.archetype, "fighter", "the subclass gives the archetype")
DOCS.check(#ex.meta.gaps > 0, "the export says what a live snapshot cannot read")
examples.expect: Both abilities are read, one detail is missing and counted, and the snapshot carries no character name.

examples.title: Snapshot a character's gear for a group decision
examples.summary: gearexport.snapshot reads worn gear, bags and bank through a host and builds the gear export the group loot auction and gear matching compare. Bags keep only what can be worn or is Lore, a ring's slot family becomes every ring slot, and the result is rebuilt from a field whitelist so nothing else a host attaches survives.
examples.code:
local gearexport = require("eb.exports.gearexport")

-- a host over the game's item reads (offline: invented items)
local host = {
    identity = function() return { name = "Fixturae", class = "warrior", subClass = "guardian", level = 100 } end,
    worn = function() return { chest = { name = "a fixture breastplate", stats = { stamina = 120 }, guildTag = "x" } } end,
    bags = function() return { { name = "a fixture ring", slot = "ring", stats = { agility = 30 } },
                              { name = "a fixture rag" } } end,
}

-- your script
local export, info = gearexport.snapshot({ host = host, includeBank = false })
local ring = export.bags[1]
print(("worn %d, bags %d (the ring fits %s)"):format(info.worn, info.bags, table.concat(ring.slots, " + ")))
local item = gearexport.normalizeItem({ name = "a fixture charm", slot = "charm", lore = true })

-- check
DOCS.check(export.worn.chest ~= nil, "the worn piece is kept by its slot")
DOCS.eq(export.worn.chest.guildTag, nil, "a field off the whitelist is gone")
DOCS.eq(#ring.slots, 2, "a ring competes for both fingers")
DOCS.eq(info.bags, 1, "the rag that cannot be worn is dropped")
DOCS.eq(export.archetype, "fighter", "the archetype comes from the subclass")
DOCS.eq(item.lore, true, "normalizeItem keeps the Lore flag")
examples.expect: The worn piece keeps its slot, the bag ring fits both fingers, the junk is dropped and a stray field is gone.

examples.title: Share gear exports across the crew
examples.summary: Each box's gear feed builds its own export and publishes it on the crew relay; every box takes in its peers' and holds the group table a loot or gear decision reads. Here two feeds are joined by a tiny in-memory transport standing in for EB's relay, and a tick on each shares both exports.
examples.code:
local gearfeed = require("eb.exports.gearfeed")

-- a transport pair standing in for EB's relay (in game pass opts.relay = the crew relay)
local listeners = {}
local function transport()
    return { kind = "test",
        publish = function(cmd, payload)
            for _, fn in ipairs(listeners) do fn(payload) end
            return true
        end,
        subscribe = function(fn) listeners[#listeners + 1] = fn end }
end
local function host(name, sub)
    return { identity = function() return { name = name, class = "warrior", subClass = sub, level = 100 } end,
             worn = function() return { chest = { name = "a fixture breastplate", stats = { stamina = 90 } } } end,
             bags = function() return {} end }
end
local clock = 0
local now = function() return clock end

-- your script
local a = gearfeed.new({ transport = transport(), box = "is1", me = "Fixturae", now = now,
    gearOpts = { host = host("Fixturae", "guardian") } })
local b = gearfeed.new({ transport = transport(), box = "is2", me = "Tankard", now = now,
    gearOpts = { host = host("Tankard", "berserker") } })
a:tick(); b:tick()
local names = {}
for name in pairs(a:exports()) do names[#names + 1] = name end
table.sort(names)
print("is1 holds: " .. table.concat(names, ", "))
clock = clock + 1000
local again = a:tick()

-- check
DOCS.eq(#names, 2, "box 1 holds both exports")
DOCS.check(b:exports()["fixturae"] ~= nil, "box 2 holds box 1's, by name in any case")
DOCS.eq(again, "held", "nothing changed: nothing sent")
DOCS.eq(#a:boxes(), 2, "the roster lists both boxes")
DOCS.eq(a:peerCount(), 1, "one peer heard")
DOCS.check(a:decode(a:encode(a:build())) ~= nil, "a payload round-trips")
examples.expect: Each box ends up with both exports, a re-tick with nothing changed sends nothing, and the roster lists both.

examples.title: What an ability asks for and what it does
examples.summary: The label engine reads an ability's effect lines and flags: a position it must be cast from, stealth, a stun or a group target, a threat increase. classify returns the whole picture; tags_of, tokensOf and to_json give it as text or a small table, and is_enhance / is_tradeskill sort out upgrades and tradeskill abilities.
examples.code:
local csreq = require("eb.exports.csreq")

-- two ability records in the record layout (offline: invented abilities)
local backstab = { Name = "Fixture Backstab", ID = 1, IsSingleTargetAbility = true,
    EffectDesc1 = "You must be behind your target to use this", EffectDesc2 = "You must be stealthed to use this" }
local taunt = { Name = "Fixture Roar", ID = 2, IsGroupAbility = true, IsStun = true,
    EffectDesc1 = "Increases threat to target encounter by 3,000" }

-- your script
local r1 = csreq.classify(backstab)
local r2 = csreq.classify(taunt)
print("backstab: " .. csreq.tokensOf(r1))

-- check
DOCS.eq(r1.pos, "behind", "cast from behind")
DOCS.check(r1.stealth, "only from stealth")
DOCS.check(r1:any(), "it asks something of the caster")
DOCS.has(csreq.tags_of(r2), "stun", "the roar stuns")
DOCS.has(csreq.tags_of(r2), "group", "and reaches the group")
DOCS.eq(r2.up, "e", "it raises threat across the encounter")
DOCS.eq(csreq.to_json(r1).pos, "behind", "to_json keeps the position")
DOCS.check(csreq.is_enhance("Enhance: Fixture Roar"), "an Enhance: entry is an upgrade, not a cast")
DOCS.check(csreq.is_tradeskill("Rapid Manufacturing"), "a crafting ability is a tradeskill one")

examples.title: Ability names, line keys and stable files
examples.summary: eb.exports.util holds the naming rule EB uses everywhere for "the same ability line" - the name without its rank, lower case - and a serializer that writes the same table to the same text every time, so a saved export diffs cleanly and reads back in an empty sandbox. b64encode makes any text one clean word for a transport.
examples.code:
local util = require("eb.exports.util")

-- your script
local name = "Fixture Mend IV"
print(("%s -> line '%s', rank %d"):format(name, util.lineKey(name), util.levelOf(name)))
local saved = util.serialize({ b = 2, a = { 1, 2, 3 }, note = "kept" })
local back = assert(util.deserialize(saved))
local word = util.b64encode("a line, with commas")

-- check
DOCS.eq(util.lineKey("Fixture Mend"), util.lineKey(name), "every rank shares the line key")
DOCS.eq(util.baseName(name), "Fixture Mend", "the name without its rank")
DOCS.eq(util.romanValue("XII"), 12, "a Roman numeral")
DOCS.eq(util.romanValue("Mend"), nil, "a word that is not one")
DOCS.eq(saved, util.serialize({ note = "kept", a = { 1, 2, 3 }, b = 2 }), "the same table writes the same text")
DOCS.eq(back.a[3], 3, "and reads back")
DOCS.eq(util.deserialize("os.exit()"), nil, "text that is not a table does not run as a script")
DOCS.check(not word:find(","), "base64 is one clean word")
DOCS.eq(util.b64decode(word), "a line, with commas", "and reads back")
examples.expect: Every rank of the heal shares one line key; a table round-trips through serialize and deserialize; base64 round-trips.

examples.title: Auto-cure watcher (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that keeps your group clear of one kind of detriment: when a member in this zone carries it, target them, cast your cure, then go back to the target you had.
examples.code:
-- eb_autocure.lua - keep your group clear of one kind of detriment. When a member in this zone carries it, target
-- them, cast your cure, then go back to the target you had. It reads only members EB has verified to work.
--
--   lua eb_autocure "Cure Noxious" noxious      start it (InnerSpace console): the ability, then the detriment kind
--   endlua eb_autocure                          stop it
--
-- Kinds: arcane, noxious, elemental, trauma. The whole group is read in ONE read four times a second; a cure is cast
-- only when it is ready, you are alive and you are not casting already.

local ability, kind = ...
kind = tostring(kind or "noxious"):lower()
local KINDS = { arcane = "Arcane", noxious = "Noxious", elemental = "Elemental", trauma = "Trauma" }
if not ability or not KINDS[kind] then
    echo('usage: lua eb_autocure "<cure ability>" arcane|noxious|elemental|trauma')
    return
end
local MEMBER = KINDS[kind]
local CHECK_EVERY = 0.25        -- seconds between checks (ISXLUA's wait takes seconds)

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

-- one read: whether I can cast, my target, my own id and detriment count, then every other group slot's id,
-- in-zone, dead and detriment count (Me.Group[1] .. [5]; slot 0 would be you, read through Me instead)
local function snapshot()
    local seq = { "${Me.IsDead}", "${Me.CastingSpell}", '${Me.Ability["' .. ability .. '"].IsReady}', "${Target.ID}",
                  "${Me.ID}|TRUE|FALSE|${Me." .. MEMBER .. "}" }
    for slot = 1, 5 do
        local g = "Me.Group[" .. slot .. "]"
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. g .. ".ID}|${" .. g .. ".InZone}|${" .. g .. ".IsDead}|${" .. g .. "." .. MEMBER .. "}"
    end
    return split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
end

-- the first one in this zone, alive, who carries the detriment: you first, then the group
local function whoNeedsIt(s)
    for slot = 0, 5 do
        local at = 5 + slot * 4
        local id, inZone, dead, count = tonumber(s[at]) or 0, s[at + 1], s[at + 2], tonumber(s[at + 3]) or 0
        if id > 0 and inZone == "TRUE" and dead ~= "TRUE" and count > 0 then return id end
    end
    return nil
end

local function targetId() return tonumber(IS.Parse("${Target.ID}")) or 0 end

echo(("eb_autocure: curing %s with %s - endlua eb_autocure stops it"):format(kind, ability))
while true do
    local s = snapshot()
    if s[1] ~= "TRUE" and s[2] ~= "TRUE" and s[3] == "TRUE" then
        local id = whoNeedsIt(s)
        if id then
            local before = tonumber(s[4]) or 0
            IS.Execute("Actor[id," .. id .. "]:DoTarget")
            if waituntil(function() return targetId() == id end, 1) then
                IS.Execute('Me.Ability["' .. ability .. '"]:Use')
                echo("eb_autocure: " .. ability .. " on actor " .. id)
                wait(0.5)
                waituntil(function() return IS.Parse("${Me.CastingSpell}") ~= "TRUE" end, 5)
            end
            if before > 0 and before ~= id then IS.Execute("Actor[id," .. before .. "]:DoTarget") end
        end
    end

examples.title: Buff keeper (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that keeps your own buffs up: when one of them is not maintained, is ready, and you are out of combat, standing still and not casting, it casts it.
examples.code:
-- eb_buffkeeper.lua - keep your own maintained buffs up.
--
--   lua eb_buffkeeper "Fixture Ward" "Fixture Haste"     start it (InnerSpace console): one or more buff names
--   endlua eb_buffkeeper                                 stop it
--
-- Once a second it reads, in ONE read, whether you can cast and whether each buff is ready, then (in a second read,
-- only when something is maintained) the names of your maintained spells. A missing, ready buff is cast when you are
-- alive, out of combat, standing still and not casting - one cast per check, so the next check sees the result.

local wanted = { ... }
if #wanted == 0 then
    echo('usage: lua eb_buffkeeper "<buff>" ["<buff>" ...]')
    return
end

local SEP = "~^~"
local function split(s)
    local out, i = {}, 1
    s = tostring(s or "")
    while true do
        local j = s:find(SEP, i, true)
        if not j then out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i); return out end
        out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i, j - 1)
        i = j + #SEP
    end
end

-- "Fixture Ward II" and "Fixture Ward" are the same buff at another rank
local function base(name) return (tostring(name or ""):lower():gsub("%s+[ivxlc]+$", "")) end

-- one read: can I cast at all, how many spells I maintain, and whether each wanted buff is ready
local function state()
    local seq = { "${Me.IsDead}", "${Me.IsHated}", "${Me.CastingSpell}", "${Me.IsMoving}", "${Me.CountMaintained}" }
    for _, b in ipairs(wanted) do seq[#seq + 1] = '${Me.Ability["' .. b .. '"].IsReady}' end
    return split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, SEP)))
end

-- the names of what I maintain, by base name
local function maintained(count)
    local up = {}
    count = math.min(tonumber(count) or 0, 30)
    if count <= 0 then return up end
    local seq = {}
    for i = 1, count do seq[i] = "${Me.Maintained[" .. i .. "].Name}" end
    for _, name in ipairs(split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, SEP)))) do up[base(name)] = true end
    return up
end

-- say once which names are not in the book (they are skipped)
local known = {}
local check = {}
for i, b in ipairs(wanted) do check[i] = '${Me.Ability["' .. b .. '"](exists)}' end
for i, v in ipairs(split(IS.Parse(table.concat(check, SEP)))) do
    known[i] = (v == "TRUE")
    if not known[i] then echo("eb_buffkeeper: no ability called '" .. wanted[i] .. "' in your book - skipped") end
end

echo("eb_buffkeeper: keeping " .. table.concat(wanted, ", ") .. " up - endlua eb_buffkeeper stops it")
while true do
    local s = state()
    if s[1] ~= "TRUE" and s[2] ~= "TRUE" and s[3] ~= "TRUE" and s[4] ~= "TRUE" then
        local up = maintained(s[5])
        for i, b in ipairs(wanted) do
            if known[i] and not up[base(b)] and s[5 + i] == "TRUE" then
                IS.Execute('Me.Ability["' .. b .. '"]:Use')
                echo("eb_buffkeeper: cast " .. b)
                wait(0.5)
                waituntil(function() return IS.Parse("${Me.CastingSpell}") ~= "TRUE" end, 10)
                break
            end
        end
    end
    wait(1)
end

examples.title: Follow and assist the tank (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script for a box in the crew: it asks EB to follow the tank, then keeps your target on the mob the tank is fighting, so your box's fight goes where the tank's does.
examples.code:
-- eb_assist.lua - follow the tank and fight what the tank fights.
--
--   lua eb_assist Tankard follow     start it: the tank's name, and "follow" to have EB walk after the tank
--   lua eb_assist Tankard            assist only (you walk, or something else moves you)
--   endlua eb_assist                 stop assisting (a follow EB started keeps going until EB stops or walks elsewhere)
--
-- Four times a second: ONE read finds the tank in your group and your own target; when the tank is there, a second
-- read takes the tank's target and what it is. Only a mob that is already fighting (an NPC or a named, alive, in
-- combat mode) becomes your target - the script never starts a fight and never picks anything the tank did not.

local tank, word = ...
if not tank or tank == "" then
    echo("usage: lua eb_assist <tank name> [follow]")
    return
end
local tankLow = tank:lower()

local SEP = "~^~"
local function split(s)
    local out, i = {}, 1
    s = tostring(s or "")
    while true do
        local j = s:find(SEP, i, true)
        if not j then out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i); return out end
        out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i, j - 1)
        i = j + #SEP
    end
end

if tostring(word or ""):lower() == "follow" then
    IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd follow " .. tank:gsub("[^%w']", ""))   -- EB walks after the tank over the mesh
end

-- one read: my target, then each other group slot's name and id
local function group()
    local seq = { "${Target.ID}" }
    for slot = 1, 5 do
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${Me.Group[" .. slot .. "].Name}"
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${Me.Group[" .. slot .. "].ID}"
    end
    local s = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, SEP)))
    local tankId
    for slot = 1, 5 do
        if tostring(s[2 * slot]):lower() == tankLow then tankId = tonumber(s[2 * slot + 1]) end
    end
    return tonumber(s[1]) or 0, tankId
end

-- one read: what the tank targets - its id, type, dead flag and combat mode
local function tanksTarget(tankId)
    local t = "Actor[id," .. tankId .. "].Target"
    local s = split(IS.Parse("${" .. t .. ".ID}" .. SEP .. "${" .. t .. ".Type}" .. SEP .. "${" .. t .. ".IsDead}"
        .. SEP .. "${" .. t .. ".InCombatMode}"))
    return tonumber(s[1]) or 0, s[2], s[3] == "TRUE", s[4] == "TRUE"
end

echo("eb_assist: assisting " .. tank .. " - endlua eb_assist stops it")
local lastSaid
while true do
    local mine, tankId = group()
    if tankId and tankId > 0 then
        local mob, kind, dead, fighting = tanksTarget(tankId)
        if mob > 0 and mob ~= mine and (kind == "NPC" or kind == "NamedNPC") and not dead and fighting then
            IS.Execute("Actor[id," .. mob .. "]:DoTarget")
            if lastSaid ~= mob then echo("eb_assist: on " .. tank .. "'s target, actor " .. mob); lastSaid = mob end
        end
    end
    wait(0.25)
end

examples.title: Say when a named spawns (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that looks for named mobs around you every second and says each new one in group chat once; with the word pause it also pauses the crew so nobody pulls into it.
examples.code:
-- eb_namedwatch.lua - say when a named spawns.
--
--   lua eb_namedwatch [radius] [pause]     start it: how far to look (metres, default 100), and "pause" to pause
--                                          the crew (eb all pause) the first time a named shows up
--   endlua eb_namedwatch                   stop it (a pause it sent stays until you type eb all resume)
--
-- Every second ONE query fills the script's own LavishScript index (EBH_Named: never a game object's name) with the
-- named mobs in range, nearest first, and ONE read takes their ids, names and distances. Each id is announced once;
-- an id that is gone is forgotten, so the same named spawning again is announced again.

local radius = tonumber((...)) or 100
local pauseCrew = tostring(select(2, ...) or ""):lower() == "pause"
local VAR = "EBH_Named"

local SEP = "~^~"
local function split(s)
    local out, i = {}, 1
    s = tostring(s or "")
    while true do
        local j = s:find(SEP, i, true)
        if not j then out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i); return out end
        out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i, j - 1)
        i = j + #SEP
    end
end

-- chat text: no LavishScript sequences, no line breaks
local function clean(s) return (tostring(s):gsub("%${", ""):gsub("[\r\n]", " ")) end

IS.Execute("squelch declarevariable " .. VAR .. " index:actor global")

local function nameds()
    IS.Execute(VAR .. ":Clear")
    -- the tested form: strings compared with ==, flags with = TRUE / = FALSE
    IS.Execute("EQ2:QueryActors[" .. VAR .. ", Type == \"NamedNPC\" && IsDead = FALSE && Distance <= " .. radius
        .. ", \"ByDist\"]")
    local n = math.min(tonumber(IS.Parse("${" .. VAR .. ".Used}")) or 0, 10)
    local rows = {}
    if n <= 0 then return rows end
    local seq = {}
    for i = 1, n do
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].ID}" .. SEP .. "${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].Name}" .. SEP ..
            "${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].Distance}"
    end
    local s = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, SEP)))
    for i = 1, n do
        local id = tonumber(s[3 * i - 2]) or 0
        if id > 0 then rows[#rows + 1] = { id = id, name = s[3 * i - 1], distance = tonumber(s[3 * i]) or 0 } end
    end
    return rows
end

echo(("eb_namedwatch: watching %d m for named mobs%s - endlua eb_namedwatch stops it"):format(radius,
    pauseCrew and " (the crew pauses on the first)" or ""))
local seen, paused = {}, false
while true do
    local now = {}
    for _, r in ipairs(nameds()) do
        now[r.id] = true
        if not seen[r.id] then
            local line = ("Named up: %s (%d m)"):format(r.name, math.floor(r.distance + 0.5))
            IS.Execute("eq2execute gsay " .. clean(line))
            echo("eb_namedwatch: " .. line)
            if pauseCrew and not paused then
                IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd all pause")
                paused = true
            end
        end
    end
    seen = now
    wait(1)
end

examples.title: Group-ready checker (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script for after a fight or before a pull: it waits until everyone in the group is in this zone, alive, topped up and close, says so in group chat, and resumes the paused crew.
examples.code:
-- eb_groupready.lua - wait until the group is ready, then resume the crew.
--
--   eb all pause                                 pause the crew first (in the console)
--   lua eb_groupready [health] [power] [metres] [minutes]
--                                                start it: the lowest health and power in percent (default 90 and 80),
--                                                how close everyone must be (default 30 m), and how long to wait at
--                                                most (default 10 minutes). It ends by itself.
--
-- Twice a second ONE read takes you and every group slot: name, in this zone, dead, health, power, distance. Ready
-- twice in a row (no one just dipped below) -> one line in group chat and `eb all resume`. Out of time -> it says
-- who is not ready and ends without resuming.

local HEALTH = tonumber((...)) or 90
local POWER = tonumber((select(2, ...))) or 80
local NEAR = tonumber((select(3, ...))) or 30
local MINUTES = tonumber((select(4, ...))) or 10

local SEP = "~^~"
local function split(s)
    local out, i = {}, 1
    s = tostring(s or "")
    while true do
        local j = s:find(SEP, i, true)
        if not j then out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i); return out end
        out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i, j - 1)
        i = j + #SEP
    end
end

-- one read: me, then each other slot -> the list of reasons the group is not ready (empty = ready)
local FIELDS = { "Name", "InZone", "IsDead", "Health", "CurrentPower", "MaxPower", "Distance" }
local function notReady()
    local seq = { "${Me.IsDead}", "${Me.IsHated}", "${Me.Health}", "${Me.Power}" }
    for slot = 1, 5 do
        for _, f in ipairs(FIELDS) do seq[#seq + 1] = "${Me.Group[" .. slot .. "]." .. f .. "}" end
    end
    local s = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, SEP)))
    local why = {}
    if s[1] == "TRUE" then why[#why + 1] = "you are dead" end
    if s[2] == "TRUE" then why[#why + 1] = "a fight is on you" end
    if (tonumber(s[3]) or 0) < HEALTH then why[#why + 1] = "your health is " .. tostring(s[3]) .. "%" end
    if (tonumber(s[4]) or 0) < POWER then why[#why + 1] = "your power is " .. tostring(s[4]) .. "%" end
    for slot = 1, 5 do
        local at = 4 + (slot - 1) * #FIELDS
        local name = s[at + 1]
        if name and name ~= "" and name ~= "NULL" then
            local hp, pw, maxPw = tonumber(s[at + 4]) or 0, tonumber(s[at + 5]) or 0, tonumber(s[at + 6]) or 0
            local pwPct = maxPw > 0 and (pw * 100 / maxPw) or 100
            if s[at + 2] ~= "TRUE" then why[#why + 1] = name .. " is not in this zone"
            elseif s[at + 3] == "TRUE" then why[#why + 1] = name .. " is dead"
            elseif hp < HEALTH then why[#why + 1] = ("%s's health is %d%%"):format(name, hp)
            elseif pwPct < POWER then why[#why + 1] = ("%s's power is %d%%"):format(name, math.floor(pwPct))
            elseif (tonumber(s[at + 7]) or 9999) > NEAR then why[#why + 1] = name .. " is too far away" end
        end
    end
    return why
end

local socket = require("socket")
local deadline = socket.gettime() + MINUTES * 60
echo(("eb_groupready: waiting for health %d%%, power %d%%, everyone within %d m"):format(HEALTH, POWER, NEAR))
local streak, why = 0, {}
while socket.gettime() < deadline do
    why = notReady()
    streak = (#why == 0) and (streak + 1) or 0
    if streak >= 2 then
        IS.Execute("eq2execute gsay Group ready - moving on")
        IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd all resume")
        echo("eb_groupready: the group is ready - the crew resumes")
        return
    end
    wait(0.5)
end
echo("eb_groupready: out of time, not resuming: " .. table.concat(why, "; "))

eb all pause
lua eb_groupready 90 80 30

the crew paused first (eb all pause), so it waits for the go this script gives

examples.title: Answer tells while you are away (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that answers each player who sends you a tell with your away line, once per person per ten minutes, and ignores group, raid, say and NPC lines.
examples.code:
-- eb_tellreply.lua - answer tells while you are away.
--
--   lua eb_tellreply "<your away line>" [minutes]    start it: the line to send, and how long before the same person
--                                                    gets it again (default 10 minutes)
--   endlua eb_tellreply                              stop it
--
-- The game's chat event only QUEUES each line (an event handler must not wait or read much); the main loop takes the
-- queue twice a second. A line is a tell to you when its target is your own name, it has no channel name and the
-- speaker is a player other than you - so group, raid, say and channel lines never get an answer.

local message, minutes = ...
if not message or message == "" then
    echo('usage: lua eb_tellreply "<your away line>" [minutes]')
    return
end
local EVERY = (tonumber(minutes) or 10) * 60

-- a tell's text and a name, made safe for one console line
local function cleanText(s) return (tostring(s):gsub("%${", ""):gsub("[\r\n]", " ")) end
local function cleanName(s) return (tostring(s):gsub("[^%w']", "")) end

local queue = {}
IS.AttachEvent("EQ2_onIncomingChatText", function(chatType, text, speaker, target, speakerIsNPC, channel)
    queue[#queue + 1] = { speaker = tostring(speaker or ""), target = tostring(target or ""),
                          npc = tostring(speakerIsNPC or ""):upper() == "TRUE", channel = tostring(channel or "") }
end)

local socket = require("socket")
local answered = {}            -- lower-case name -> when they were last answered (seconds)
echo("eb_tellreply: answering tells - endlua eb_tellreply stops it")
while true do
    if #queue > 0 then
        local lines = queue
        queue = {}
        local me = tostring(IS.Parse("${Me.Name}") or ""):lower()
        local now = socket.gettime()
        for _, l in ipairs(lines) do
            local who = l.speaker:lower()
            if not l.npc and l.channel == "" and me ~= "" and l.target:lower() == me and who ~= "" and who ~= me then
                if not answered[who] or now - answered[who] >= EVERY then
                    answered[who] = now
                    IS.Execute("eq2execute tell " .. cleanName(l.speaker) .. " " .. cleanText(message))
                    echo("eb_tellreply: answered " .. l.speaker)
                end
            end
        end
    end
    wait(0.5)
end

examples.title: Event watcher (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that reacts to the game's own events the safe way: each handler only queues, and the main loop logs zoning, loot windows and incoming text - and pauses the crew when a line you name appears.
examples.code:
-- eb_eventwatch.lua - react to the game's events: zoning, loot windows, incoming text.
--
--   lua eb_eventwatch ["<text>"]     start it; when a line of game text contains <text>, the crew pauses
--   endlua eb_eventwatch             stop it
--
-- THE PATTERN. An event handler runs inside the game's own callback: it must not wait and should not read the game.
-- Each handler here only puts a small record on a queue; the main loop takes the queue every frame and does the
-- work. The zone's name is read only after the load FINISHES - it already names the next zone while the load runs.
-- The loot window is read only after its event says one opened: reading it with no window up is slow.

local trigger = ...
trigger = trigger and trigger ~= "" and trigger:lower() or nil

local SEP = "~^~"
local function split(s)
    local out, i = {}, 1
    s = tostring(s or "")
    while true do
        local j = s:find(SEP, i, true)
        if not j then out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i); return out end
        out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i, j - 1)
        i = j + #SEP
    end
end

local queue = {}
local function push(kind, a) queue[#queue + 1] = { kind = kind, a = a } end      -- the handlers do only this
IS.AttachEvent("EQ2_StartedZoning", function() push("zoning") end)
IS.AttachEvent("EQ2_FinishedZoning", function(seconds) push("zoned", seconds) end)
IS.AttachEvent("EQ2_onLootWindowAppeared", function(id) push("loot", id) end)
IS.AttachEvent("EQ2_onIncomingText", function(text) push("text", text) end)

local function onZoned(seconds)
    local s = split(IS.Parse("${Zone.Name}" .. SEP .. "${Zone.ShortName}"))
    echo(("eb_eventwatch: in %s (%s) after %s s"):format(s[1], s[2], tostring(seconds)))
end

local function onLoot()
    local n = math.min(tonumber(IS.Parse("${LootWindow.NumItems}")) or 0, 8)
    if n <= 0 then return end
    local seq = {}
    for i = 1, n do seq[i] = "${LootWindow.Item[" .. i .. "].Name}" end
    echo("eb_eventwatch: loot - " .. table.concat(split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, SEP))), ", "))
end

local function onText(text)
    if trigger and tostring(text):lower():find(trigger, 1, true) then
        IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd all pause")
        echo("eb_eventwatch: '" .. tostring(text) .. "' - the crew pauses")
    end
end

echo("eb_eventwatch: watching zoning, loot and game text - endlua eb_eventwatch stops it")
while true do
    if #queue > 0 then
        local events = queue
        queue = {}
        for _, ev in ipairs(events) do
            if ev.kind == "zoning" then echo("eb_eventwatch: zoning...")
            elseif ev.kind == "zoned" then onZoned(ev.a)
            elseif ev.kind == "loot" then onLoot()
            elseif ev.kind == "text" then onText(ev.a) end
        end
    end
    waitframe()
end

endlua eb_eventwatch

examples.title: Crew status board (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that listens to every EB box's status, prints a board of the crew, and pauses the crew when a box goes quiet (its EB stopped or its game closed) - then resumes when it is back.
examples.code:
-- eb_crewboard.lua - the crew at a glance, and a pause when a box goes quiet.
--
--   lua eb_crewboard [seconds]     start it: how long a box may stay quiet before the crew pauses (default 15)
--   endlua eb_crewboard            stop it
--
-- Every EB box says who and where it is every two seconds, on the InnerSpace relay, as the event EBISX_State2 (at most
-- 40 arguments: the status's fields from the 40th on ride packed in the 40th, which this board never reads. Never attach
-- EB's old EBISX_State: an older EB sends it with 47 arguments, and ISXLUA hands a handler at most 42 safely). This
-- script finds the EB install the way EB's own start does (InnerSpace/Scripts/EBIS/boot.json,
-- read with ISXLUA's bundled cjson), loads EB's relay wire library from it, and decodes each status with
-- wire.decodeState. The event handler only queues; the main loop decodes, prints the board every ten seconds, and sends
-- `eb all pause` when a box that was heard stops talking for longer than the limit - and `eb all resume` once every box
-- is back.

local QUIET = tonumber((...)) or 15

-- EB's install, from the file EB Setup writes beside EB's start script
local home = tostring(IS.Parse("${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}") or ""):gsub("\\", "/"):gsub("/+$", "")
local f = io.open(home .. "/Scripts/EBIS/boot.json", "rb")
if not f then echo("eb_crewboard: EB for InnerSpace is not installed (no Scripts/EBIS/boot.json)"); return end
local text = f:read("a")
f:close()
local cjson = require("cjson.safe")
local boot = cjson.decode(text or "")
if type(boot) ~= "table" or type(boot.root) ~= "string" or boot.root == "" then
    echo("eb_crewboard: boot.json has no EB folder in it - run EB Setup again")
    return
end
local root = boot.root:gsub("\\", "/"):gsub("/+$", "")
package.path = root .. "/lua/?.lua;" .. root .. "/lua/?/init.lua;" .. package.path
local wire = require("eb.relay.wire")           -- EB's pure relay wire: no game reads, safe beside EB

local queue = {}
IS.AttachEvent("EBISX_State2", function(...) queue[#queue + 1] = { ... } end)

local socket = require("socket")
local boxes = {}                -- box id -> { st = decoded status, heard = seconds }
local paused, lastBoard = false, 0

local function board(now)
    local ids = {}
    for id in pairs(boxes) do ids[#ids + 1] = id end
    table.sort(ids)
    echo(("eb_crewboard: %d box(es)"):format(#ids))
    for _, id in ipairs(ids) do
        local b = boxes[id]
        echo(("  %-6s %-14s %-22s %-10s hp %3s  pw %3s%s%s"):format(id, b.st.name, b.st.zone, b.st.mode,
            tostring(b.st.hp or "?"), tostring(b.st.pw or "?"), b.st.combat and "  FIGHTING" or "",
            (now - b.heard > QUIET) and "  QUIET" or ""))
    end
end

echo(("eb_crewboard: listening to the crew (quiet after %d s pauses it) - endlua eb_crewboard stops it"):format(QUIET))
while true do
    local now = socket.gettime()
    if #queue > 0 then
        local got = queue
        queue = {}
        for _, args in ipairs(got) do
            local st = wire.decodeState(args)
            if st.box ~= "" then boxes[st.box] = { st = st, heard = now } end
        end
    end
    local quiet = {}
    for id, b in pairs(boxes) do if now - b.heard > QUIET then quiet[#quiet + 1] = id end end
    if #quiet > 0 and not paused then
        table.sort(quiet)
        IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd all pause")
        echo("eb_crewboard: no word from " .. table.concat(quiet, ", ") .. " - the crew pauses")
        paused = true
    elseif #quiet == 0 and paused then
        IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd all resume")
        echo("eb_crewboard: every box is back - the crew resumes")
        paused = false
    end
    if now - lastBoard >= 10 then board(now); lastBoard = now end
    wait(0.5)
end

    if zoned then

examples.title: Hail and answer an NPC (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that hails your target and walks a conversation by the words of each reply you want, in the speech bubble or the classic conversation window, then ends.
examples.code:
-- eb_hailreply.lua - hail your target and answer its conversation by words.
--
--   lua eb_hailreply "<words>" ["<words>" ...]    hail, then for each step pick the reply that contains <words>
--                                                 (case does not matter); it ends after the last step
--
-- An NPC talks in the speech bubble (read by its reply rows' text) or in the classic conversation window (its
-- replies listed into this script's own LavishScript index, EBH_Replies). Each step waits up to five seconds for the
-- conversation, clicks the matching reply, and waits for that reply to take. A step with no match lists the replies
-- it saw and stops - it never clicks a guess.

local wants = { ... }
if #wants == 0 then
    echo('usage: lua eb_hailreply "<words of the reply>" ["<words of the next reply>" ...]')
    return
end

local SEP = "~^~"
local function split(s)
    local out, i = {}, 1
    s = tostring(s or "")
    while true do
        local j = s:find(SEP, i, true)
        if not j then out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i); return out end
        out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i, j - 1)
        i = j + #SEP
    end
end

local BUBBLE = "EQ2UIPage[ProxyActor,Conversation].Child[composite,replies]"
local VAR = "EBH_Replies"
IS.Execute("squelch declarevariable " .. VAR .. " index:collection:string global")

-- the conversation as it stands: { kind = "bubble" | "classic", options = { texts } } or nil
local function conversation()
    local seq = {}
    for i = 1, 8 do
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. BUBBLE .. ".Child[" .. i .. "].GetProperty[visible]}"
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. BUBBLE .. ".Child[" .. i .. "].GetProperty[LocalText]}"
    end
    seq[#seq + 1] = "${ReplyDialog(exists)}"
    seq[#seq + 1] = "${ReplyDialog.IsVisible}"
    local s = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, SEP)))
    local options = {}
    for i = 1, 8 do
        if s[2 * i - 1] ~= "TRUE" then break end
        options[i] = s[2 * i]
    end
    if #options > 0 then return { kind = "bubble", options = options } end
    if s[17] == "TRUE" and s[18] ~= "FALSE" then
        IS.Execute(VAR .. ":Clear")
        IS.Execute("ReplyDialog.Replies:GetOptions[" .. VAR .. "]")
        local n = math.min(tonumber(IS.Parse("${" .. VAR .. ".Used}")) or 0, 12)
        local rows = {}
        for i = 1, n do
            rows[#rows + 1] = "${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].FirstKey}" .. SEP .. "${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].CurrentValue}"
        end
        local r = n > 0 and split(IS.Parse(table.concat(rows, SEP))) or {}
        for i = 1, n do options[i] = r[2 * i] or "" end
        return { kind = "classic", options = options }
    end
    return nil
end

local function choose(c, n)
    if c.kind == "bubble" then IS.Execute(BUBBLE .. ".Child[" .. n .. "]:LeftClick")
    else IS.Execute("ReplyDialog:Choose[" .. n .. "]") end
end

if (tonumber(IS.Parse("${Target.ID}")) or 0) <= 0 then echo("eb_hailreply: target the NPC first"); return end
IS.Execute("eq2execute hail")
for step, want in ipairs(wants) do
    local c
    waituntil(function() c = conversation(); return c ~= nil end, 5)
    if not c then echo(("eb_hailreply: step %d - no conversation opened"):format(step)); return end
    local pick
    for i, text in ipairs(c.options) do
        if tostring(text):lower():find(want:lower(), 1, true) then pick = i; break end
    end
    if not pick then
        echo(("eb_hailreply: step %d - no reply with '%s' (replies: %s)"):format(step, want, table.concat(c.options, " / ")))
        return
    end
    local chosen = c.options[pick]
    choose(c, pick)
    echo(("eb_hailreply: step %d - %s"):format(step, chosen))
    -- the reply takes when the conversation closes or changes
    waituntil(function()
        local now = conversation()
        return now == nil or now.kind ~= c.kind or table.concat(now.options, SEP) ~= table.concat(c.options, SEP)
    end, 5)
end
echo("eb_hailreply: done")
examples.expect: Hails, picks the reply containing each wanted word in turn (bubble and classic), and reports what it chose.

examples.title: Tell me when a yes/no question waits (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that notices the game's yes/no windows (a revive offer, an invite, a trade question) and says what is asked, on the console and in group chat, so you can answer it - it never clicks one itself.
examples.code:
-- eb_choicealert.lua - say when a yes/no question is waiting for you.
--
--   lua eb_choicealert [group]     start it; with "group" the question also goes to group chat (your crew's
--                                  screens), else only to this console
--   endlua eb_choicealert          stop it
--
-- The game's event for a new choice window only QUEUES; the main loop then reads the window once - its text and its
-- two answers in ONE read - and says them. It answers nothing: clicking a yes/no window is not something EB does on
-- this release, so a person decides.

local toGroup = tostring((...) or ""):lower() == "group"

local SEP = "~^~"
local function split(s)
    local out, i = {}, 1
    s = tostring(s or "")
    while true do
        local j = s:find(SEP, i, true)
        if not j then out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i); return out end
        out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i, j - 1)
        i = j + #SEP
    end
end
local function clean(s) return (tostring(s):gsub("%${", ""):gsub("[\r\n]", " ")) end

local pending = 0
IS.AttachEvent("EQ2_onChoiceWindowAppeared", function() pending = pending + 1 end)

echo("eb_choicealert: watching for yes/no windows - endlua eb_choicealert stops it")
while true do
    if pending > 0 then
        pending = 0
        local s = split(IS.Parse("${ChoiceWindow.IsVisible}" .. SEP .. "${ChoiceWindow.Text.GetProperty[LocalText]}" ..
            SEP .. "${ChoiceWindow.Choice1}" .. SEP .. "${ChoiceWindow.Choice2}"))
        if s[1] == "TRUE" then
            local line = ("Waiting for an answer: %s [%s / %s]"):format(s[2], s[3], s[4])
            echo("eb_choicealert: " .. line)
            if toGroup then IS.Execute("eq2execute gsay " .. clean(line)) end
        end
    end
    wait(0.25)
end

-- steps inside while the group holds on the tank's camp spots. Characters move only by walking the mesh.
return {
    schema = "eb.ic/1",
    zone = "Fixture Hollow",                  -- the display name
    short = "fixture_hollow",                 -- the short name the game gives the zone inside
    variants = { "[Heroic I]" },

    hub = {
        zone = "fixture_docks",               -- every box travels here first, each on its own
        difficulty = "[Heroic I]",            -- the copy the door is asked for (eb ic run fixture_hollow <difficulty> wins)
        approach = { { 10, 0, 10 }, { 20, 0, 25 } },          -- the tank's waypoints to the door; the mesh fills the gaps
        entrance = { loc = { 20, 0, 25 }, tolerance = 8 },   -- where the tank must stand to use the door

    encounters = { "hollow_skitters", "overseer_of_fixtures" },

    -- run options: an option that is ON skips its steps; type <id>=on|off after eb ic run / eb ic loop to flip one.
    -- stay_inside is on: the run ends inside the cleared copy, so eb ic loop waits out the timer THERE before it
    -- leaves by the exit and resets; eb ic run fixture_hollow stay_inside=off walks the group out at the end.
    options = {
        { id = "skip_trash", label = "Skip the skitter pack", default = false, skip_steps = { "trash" } },
        { id = "stay_inside", label = "End the run inside the cleared copy", default = true,
          skip_steps = { "to.exit", "exit" } },
    },

    route = {                                 -- the STEPS, in order
        { id = "camp.entry", act = "campspot", name = "entry", spot = { 0, 0, -30 }, who = "group" },
        { id = "to.pack", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, -10 }, { 0, 0, 5 } } },
        { id = "trash", act = "encounter", name = "hollow_skitters" },          -- the pull, then the clear
        { id = "camp.boss", act = "campspot", name = "boss room", spot = { 12, 0, 38 }, who = "group" },
        { id = "boss", act = "encounter", name = "overseer_of_fixtures" },      -- the named fight
        { id = "boss.loot", act = "loot", op = "chest" },
        { id = "said", act = "announce",
          message = "Fixture Hollow: trash {{verdict.trash}}, Overseer {{verdict.boss}}, chest {{verdict.boss.loot}}" },
        { id = "to.exit", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, -38 } } },           -- (both skipped while stay_inside is on)
        { id = "exit", act = "zoneout", via = "exit" },                        -- the tank takes the group out

    -- exit, resets the copy from outside and goes back in. max_minutes 0 = until eb ic stop (the command's minutes win).
    loop = { reset = "self", rerun_first = false, max_minutes = 0 },
