-- fixture_hollow/encounters/overseer_of_fixtures.lua - one named fight as conditions -> actions. The phases without a
-- "when" run in order; a phase with "when" + "repeat_ = true" is a REACTION, checked between phases and on every tick
-- of the fight; "once = true" fires a reaction one time per pull.
return {
    schema = "eb.ic/1",
    name = "Overseer of Fixtures",
    aka = { "the Overseer" },
    kind = "named",
    spot = { 12, 0, 42 },                                 -- where the tank fights it from

    -- the GATE: the named is up and nobody is fighting yet (else the verdict is "skipped:gate")
    when = { { actor_present = "Overseer of Fixtures" }, { in_combat = false } },

    phases = {
        -- the fight: the cast stack fights the Overseer to death; the reactions below fire on its ticks
        { id = "fight", do_ = { { engage = "Overseer of Fixtures" } } },

        -- REACTION to the emote: the floor burns - the group steps onto the safe ledge, waits it out, comes back
        { id = "floor", repeat_ = true, once = true,
          when = { { chat_seen = { match = "the floor will burn" } } },
          do_ = {
              { campspot = { name = "safe ledge", spot = { 25, 0, 50 }, who = "group" } },
              { wait = 6 },
              { campspot = { name = "boss room", spot = { 12, 0, 38 }, who = "group" } },
          } },

        -- REACTION to adds: whenever spawns are up, clear them
        { id = "adds", repeat_ = true,
          when = { { actor_count = { query = "a fixture spawn", cmp = ">=", value = 1 } } },
          do_ = { { clear_area = "a fixture spawn", radius = 25 } } },

        -- the BURN: under 30% health, cast the finisher once
        { id = "burn", repeat_ = true, once = true,
          when = { { mob_health_below = { name = "Overseer of Fixtures", pct = 30 } } },
          do_ = { { cast = "Fixture Burst" } } },
    },

    -- the WIN TEST: the fight only counts as won when the Overseer is dead (else "FAILED:done-test")
    done = { { actor_dead = "Overseer of Fixtures" } },

    -- a wipe here: say so before the walk back in
    on_death = { { announce = "the Overseer of Fixtures wiped us - walking back in" } },
}

examples.title: Loop an instance once the group is ready (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script for the tank's box: it waits until every member is in this zone, alive, healthy and rested, then types eb ic loop for you and ends. EB runs the loop: each run ends inside the cleared copy, the tank waits out the reset timer there, leaves by the exit, resets the copy from outside and goes back in.
examples.code:
-- eb_icloop.lua - start an instance loop when the group is ready: everyone in this zone, alive, health at least 90%
-- and power at least 50%. Then it types `eb ic loop <instance> <minutes>` for you (through EB's console word) and
-- ends. EB runs the loop; `eb ic stop` ends it.
--
--   lua eb_icloop fixture_hollow 120      the instance's short name and the loop's minutes (0 = until eb ic stop)
--   endlua eb_icloop                      stop waiting, before the loop has started

local zone, minutes = ...
zone = tostring(zone or ""):gsub("[^%w_/%-]", "")         -- an instance name: letters, digits, _ - /
if zone == "" then
    echo("usage: lua eb_icloop <instance> [minutes]")
    return
end
minutes = math.max(0, math.floor(tonumber(minutes) or 0))
local MIN_HEALTH, MIN_POWER = 90, 50

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

-- one read: me, then the other five group slots (Me.Group[1] .. [5]; an empty slot reads NULL)
local function groupReady()
    local seq = { "${Me.IsDead}", "${Me.Health}", "${Me.Power}", "${Me.GroupCount}" }
    for slot = 1, 5 do
        local g = "Me.Group[" .. slot .. "]"
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. g .. ".Name}|${" .. g .. ".InZone}|${" .. g .. ".IsDead}|${" .. g .. ".Health}|${" ..
            g .. ".CurrentPower}|${" .. g .. ".MaxPower}"
    end
    local s = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
    if s[1] == "TRUE" then return false, "you are dead" end
    if (tonumber(s[2]) or 0) < MIN_HEALTH then return false, "you are hurt" end
    if (tonumber(s[3]) or 0) < MIN_POWER then return false, "you are low on power" end
    for slot = 1, math.min(5, (tonumber(s[4]) or 1) - 1) do
        local at = 5 + (slot - 1) * 6
        local name, inZone, dead = s[at], s[at + 1], s[at + 2]
        local hp, pw, maxPw = tonumber(s[at + 3]) or 0, tonumber(s[at + 4]) or 0, tonumber(s[at + 5]) or 0
        if inZone ~= "TRUE" then return false, name .. " is not in this zone" end
        if dead == "TRUE" then return false, name .. " is dead" end
        if hp < MIN_HEALTH then return false, name .. " is hurt" end
        if maxPw > 0 and pw * 100 / maxPw < MIN_POWER then return false, name .. " is low on power" end
    end
    return true
end

echo(("eb_icloop: waiting for the group to be ready for %s"):format(zone))
local said
while true do
    local ok, why = groupReady()
    if ok then break end
    if why ~= said then echo("eb_icloop: not yet - " .. why); said = why end
    wait(2)
end
IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd ic loop " .. zone .. " " .. minutes)
echo(("eb_icloop: the group is ready - started eb ic loop %s %d (eb ic stop ends it)"):format(zone, minutes))
examples.expect: It waits while a member is hurt, starts eb ic loop fixture_hollow 120 the moment the group is ready, and ends; the loop then runs two laps with the reset wait inside the copy.
examples.run:
lua eb_icloop fixture_hollow 120
endlua eb_icloop
eb ic stop
needs: EB running on every box of the group; start this on the tank's box (the box that types the loop leads it)
the instance installed (the complete instance file fixture_hollow and its encounters)
every box already in the hub zone (fixture_docks)

examples.title: Food and drink keeper (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that keeps auto-consume on for your food and drink slots and warns once when a stack gets low, reading both slots in one read every five seconds.
examples.code:
-- eb_foodkeeper.lua - keep eating and drinking. Every five seconds it reads your food and drink slots in ONE read: a
-- slot whose auto-consume is off gets it turned back on, and a stack at or under the low mark is called out once in
-- the console (again only after it was refilled and ran low again). It reads only members EB has verified to work.
--
--   lua eb_foodkeeper [low]      start it; low = warn at this many left (default 5)
--   endlua eb_foodkeeper         stop it

local low = tonumber((...)) or 5
local SLOTS = { "food", "drink" }
local CHECK_EVERY = 5               -- seconds (ISXLUA's wait takes seconds)
local warned = {}

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

-- one read: each slot's item name, stack size and auto-consume switch
local function readSlots()
    local seq = {}
    for _, slot in ipairs(SLOTS) do
        local p = "Me.Equipment[" .. slot .. "]"
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. p .. ".Name}|${" .. p .. ".Quantity}|${" .. p .. ".AutoConsumeOn}"
    end
    return split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
end

local function sayOnce(key, text)
    if warned[key] then return end
    warned[key] = true
    echo("eb_foodkeeper: " .. text)
end

echo(("eb_foodkeeper: keeping food and drink on, warning at %d left - endlua eb_foodkeeper stops it"):format(low))
while true do
    local r = readSlots()
    for i, slot in ipairs(SLOTS) do
        local name, qty, on = r[i * 3 - 2], tonumber(r[i * 3 - 1]) or 0, r[i * 3]
        if name == nil or name == "" or name == "NULL" then
            sayOnce(slot .. ":empty", "nothing in your " .. slot .. " slot")
        else
            warned[slot .. ":empty"] = nil
            if on ~= "TRUE" then
                IS.Execute("Me.Equipment[" .. slot .. "]:ToggleAutoConsume")
                echo("eb_foodkeeper: auto-consume back on for " .. name)
            end
            if qty <= low then
                sayOnce(slot, ("%d %s left in your %s slot"):format(qty, name, slot))
            else
                warned[slot] = nil
            end
        end
    end
    wait(CHECK_EVERY)
end
examples.expect: Turns auto-consume back on for the slot that had it off, and warns once (not every check) about the low stack.

lua eb_foodkeeper 5
endlua eb_foodkeeper
needs: EB for InnerSpace's session (ISXEQ2 and ISXLUA loaded); EB itself does not have to run
food in your food slot and drink in your drink slot

examples.title: Sell junk at a merchant (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that waits for a merchant window and sells every listed item your bags hold through the window's own rows, once per window. It answers no question it did not cause.
examples.code:
-- eb_selljunk.lua - sell the items you name, whenever a merchant window is open. Twice a second it checks whether a
-- merchant window is up; when one opens it reads every listed item's stack and price in ONE read and sells each whole
-- stack through MerchantWindow.MyInventory["<name>"]:Sell. It sells again only after that window closed and the next
-- one opened. It never clicks a question (selling asks none it would answer) and reads only verified members.
--
--   lua eb_selljunk "<item name>" ["<item name>" ...]     start it with the exact item names
--   endlua eb_selljunk                                    stop it

local junk = {}
for _, name in ipairs({ ... }) do
    if tostring(name):find('["\\]') then
        echo("eb_selljunk: skipping a name with a quote or a backslash in it: " .. tostring(name))
    elseif name ~= "" then
        junk[#junk + 1] = name
    end
end
if #junk == 0 then
    echo('usage: lua eb_selljunk "<item name>" ["<item name>" ...]')
    return
end

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

local function row(name) return 'MerchantWindow.MyInventory["' .. name .. '"]' end

local function merchantOpen() return IS.Parse("${MerchantWindow.IsVisible}") == "TRUE" end

-- one read for every listed item (its stack in the bags - NULL when there is none - and the price), then one Sell each
local function sellListed()
    local seq = {}
    for _, name in ipairs(junk) do seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. row(name) .. ".Quantity}|${" .. row(name) .. ".PriceString}" end
    local r = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
    local sold = 0
    for i, name in ipairs(junk) do
        local qty = tonumber(r[i * 2 - 1]) or 0
        if qty > 0 then
            IS.Execute(row(name) .. ":Sell[" .. qty .. "]")
            echo(("eb_selljunk: sold %d %s (%s each)"):format(qty, name, tostring(r[i * 2])))
            sold = sold + 1
        end
    end
    return sold
end

echo(("eb_selljunk: selling %d listed item(s) at the next merchant window - endlua eb_selljunk stops it"):format(#junk))
local soldHere = false
while true do
    if merchantOpen() then
        if not soldHere then
            local n = sellListed()
            echo(("eb_selljunk: done at this merchant (%d stack(s) sold)"):format(n))
            soldHere = true
        end
    else
        soldHere = false
    end
    wait(0.5)
end
examples.expect: Sells the whole stack of each listed item in the bags when a window opens, leaves every other item, and sells again only at the next window.
examples.run:
lua eb_selljunk "Rusty Fixture Blade" "Torn Fixture Pelt"
endlua eb_selljunk

the exact names of the items to sell (only those are ever sold)
you open the merchant window yourself (hail the merchant); the script never opens one

examples.title: Pause EB when the bags are full (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that pauses EB (this box, or the whole crew) when your bags drop under a number of free slots, and resumes it once there is room again.
examples.code:
-- eb_bagwatch.lua - stop EB filling bags it cannot empty. Every two seconds it reads how many bag slots are free (one
-- read). Under the mark it sends EB "pause" through EB's console word - "all pause" with the word crew, so every box
-- stops - and once you made room (two slots past the mark, so it does not flip back and forth) it sends "resume".
-- EB answers in the console; a script hears no reply.
--
--   lua eb_bagwatch [free=<slots>] [crew]      start it (free: default 3)
--   endlua eb_bagwatch                         stop it

local low, crew = 3, false
for _, a in ipairs({ ... }) do
    local n = tostring(a):match("^free=(%d+)$")
    if n then
        low = tonumber(n)
    elseif a == "crew" then
        crew = true
    else
        echo("usage: lua eb_bagwatch [free=<slots>] [crew]")
        return
    end
end

local paused = false
echo(("eb_bagwatch: pausing %s under %d free bag slot(s) - endlua eb_bagwatch stops it"):format(
    crew and "the crew" or "EB", low))
while true do
    local free = tonumber(IS.Parse("${Me.InventorySlotsFree}"))
    if free then
        if not paused and free < low then
            IS.Execute(crew and "luacall EBISX_cmd all pause" or "luacall EBISX_cmd pause")
            echo(("eb_bagwatch: %d bag slot(s) free - paused"):format(free))
            paused = true
        elseif paused and free >= low + 2 then
            IS.Execute(crew and "luacall EBISX_cmd all resume" or "luacall EBISX_cmd resume")
            echo(("eb_bagwatch: %d bag slot(s) free - resumed"):format(free))
            paused = false
        end
    end
    wait(2)
end
examples.expect: Pauses EB once when the free slots fall under the mark and resumes it once when you made room.
examples.run:
lua eb_bagwatch free=3
lua eb_bagwatch free=3 crew
endlua eb_bagwatch

examples.title: Take loot windows by your rules (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that takes a loot window the moment the game opens one: free-for-all windows by default, never a window holding an item on your leave list, and with an only= list just the windows that hold one of those.
examples.code:
-- eb_lootall.lua - take loot windows by your rules. It does nothing until the game says a loot window opened (the
-- loot-window event; a loot window is never polled - with no window up that read is slow), then reads the window's
-- type and every item name in ONE read and decides:
--   * a window that is not free-for-all is left for you, unless you start it with the word all;
--   * a window holding an item from leave= is left for you (EB takes a window whole, so it never takes part of one);
--   * with only=, a window is taken only when it holds at least one of those items.
-- Lists are item names separated by ';' (any case).
--
--   lua eb_lootall [all] ["leave=<item>;<item>"] ["only=<item>;<item>"]      start it
--   endlua eb_lootall                                                          stop it

local takeAny, leave, only = false, {}, nil
for _, word in ipairs({ ... }) do
    local low = tostring(word):lower()
    if low == "all" then
        takeAny = true
    elseif low:sub(1, 6) == "leave=" then
        for n in low:sub(7):gmatch("[^;]+") do leave[n] = true end
    elseif low:sub(1, 5) == "only=" then
        only = only or {}
        for n in low:sub(6):gmatch("[^;]+") do only[n] = true end
    else
        echo('usage: lua eb_lootall [all] ["leave=<item>;<item>"] ["only=<item>;<item>"]')
        return
    end
end

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

-- the event handler runs in one go inside the game's frame: it only counts, the loop below does the work
local opened = 0
IS.AttachEvent("EQ2_onLootWindowAppeared", function() opened = opened + 1 end)

-- why a window stays open, or nil to take it
local function verdict(kind, names)
    if not takeAny and kind ~= "Free For All" then return "a " .. kind .. " window" end
    local wanted = only == nil
    for _, n in ipairs(names) do
        local low = n:lower()
        if leave[low] then return "it holds " .. n end
        if only and only[low] then wanted = true end
    end
    if not wanted then return "nothing on the only= list" end
    return nil
end

local function handleWindow()
    local head = split(IS.Parse("${LootWindow(exists)}|${LootWindow.Type}|${LootWindow.NumItems}"))
    if head[1] ~= "TRUE" then return end
    local kind, n = head[2], tonumber(head[3]) or 0
    local names = {}
    if n > 0 then
        local seq = {}
        for i = 1, n do seq[i] = "${LootWindow.Item[" .. i .. "].Name}" end
        names = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
    end
    local why = verdict(kind, names)
    if why then
        echo("eb_lootall: left the loot window open for you: " .. why)
    else
        IS.Execute("LootWindow:LootAll")
        echo(("eb_lootall: took %d item(s): %s"):format(n, table.concat(names, ", ")))
    end
end

echo("eb_lootall: waiting for loot windows - endlua eb_lootall stops it")
while true do
    if opened > 0 then
        opened = 0
        handleWindow()
    end
    waitframe()
end
examples.expect: Takes the free-for-all window, leaves the lottery window and the window holding a leave-list item open for you, and says why for each.
examples.run:
lua eb_lootall "leave=Cursed Fixture Idol"
endlua eb_lootall
needs: EB for InnerSpace's session (ISXEQ2 and ISXLUA loaded); EB itself does not have to run
EB's own looting off, so the two do not both act on one window

examples.title: Harvest the nodes in reach (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that harvests the nodes within reach whose names you list, nearest first: double-click, wait for the harvest to finish, again until the node is gone, then the next. It never walks.
examples.code:
-- eb_harvest.lua - harvest the nodes around you. Twice a second, when you are not fighting, casting or moving, it
-- asks the game for the interactable actors within reach (one query into this script's own index variable, then one
-- read of the rows), picks the nearest whose name holds one of your words, and double-clicks it. It waits for the
-- harvest to finish and goes again until the node is gone; a node still there after six tries is skipped.
--
--   lua eb_harvest "<part of a node name>" ["<part>" ...] [reach=<metres>]     start it (reach: default 8)
--   endlua eb_harvest                                                             stop it

local words, reach = {}, 8
for _, a in ipairs({ ... }) do
    local r = tostring(a):match("^reach=(%d+%.?%d*)$")
    if r then reach = tonumber(r) elseif a ~= "" then words[#words + 1] = tostring(a):lower() end
end
if #words == 0 then
    echo('usage: lua eb_harvest "<part of a node name>" ["<part>" ...] [reach=<metres>]')
    return
end

local VAR = "EBH_Nodes"          -- this script's own LavishScript index:actor (never named after a game object)
local MAX_TRIES = 6
IS.Execute("declarevariable " .. VAR .. " index:actor global")

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

local function busy()
    local s = split(IS.Parse("${Me.IsHated}|${Me.CastingSpell}|${Me.IsMoving}"))
    return s[1] == "TRUE" or s[2] == "TRUE" or s[3] == "TRUE"
end

local function wanted(name)
    local low = tostring(name):lower()
    for _, w in ipairs(words) do if low:find(w, 1, true) then return true end end
    return false
end

-- the wanted nodes in reach, nearest first: one query, then one read of up to 20 rows
local function nodesInReach()
    IS.Execute(VAR .. ":Clear")
    IS.Execute("EQ2:QueryActors[" .. VAR .. ", Interactable && Distance <= " .. reach .. ", \"ByDist\"]")
    local used = math.min(tonumber(IS.Parse("${" .. VAR .. ".Used}")) or 0, 20)
    if used == 0 then return {} end
    local seq = {}
    for i = 1, used do seq[i] = "${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].ID}|${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].Name}" end
    local r = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
    local out = {}
    for i = 1, used do
        local id, name = tonumber(r[i * 2 - 1]), r[i * 2]
        if id and id > 0 and wanted(name) then out[#out + 1] = { id = id, name = name } end
    end
    return out
end

local tries, skipped = {}, {}
echo(("eb_harvest: harvesting %s within %s m - endlua eb_harvest stops it"):format(table.concat(words, ", "), reach))
while true do
    if not busy() then
        local pick
        for _, node in ipairs(nodesInReach()) do
            if not skipped[node.id] then pick = node; break end
        end
        if pick then
            tries[pick.id] = (tries[pick.id] or 0) + 1
            if tries[pick.id] > MAX_TRIES then
                skipped[pick.id] = true
                echo("eb_harvest: skipping " .. pick.name .. " - still there after " .. MAX_TRIES .. " tries")
            else
                IS.Execute("Actor[id," .. pick.id .. "]:DoubleClick")
                echo("eb_harvest: harvesting " .. pick.name)
                wait(1)                                                     -- the harvest starts
                waituntil(function() return IS.Parse("${Me.CastingSpell}") ~= "TRUE" end, 8)
            end
        end
    end
    wait(0.5)
end
examples.expect: Empties the two listed nodes in reach, leaves the lever and the node out of reach alone, and stops trying a node that never goes away.
examples.run:
lua eb_harvest "ore vein" "root cluster" reach=8
endlua eb_harvest
needs: EB for InnerSpace's session (ISXEQ2 and ISXLUA loaded); EB itself does not have to run
you stand within reach of the nodes (the script never moves you)
words from the nodes' names (any part of the name, any case)

examples.title: Patrol between saved marks (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that walks you between marks you saved with eb marks set, for as many laps as you ask: it hands each walk to EB (eb marks go) and watches you arrive before it sends the next.
examples.code:
-- eb_patrol.lua - walk between your saved marks. For each mark it sends EB the line "marks go <mark>" through EB's
-- console word (luacall EBISX_cmd: EB answers in the console, a script hears no reply), then watches you: the walk has
-- started once you move, and it is over once you stood still for a second. Then the next mark, lap after lap.
--
--   lua eb_patrol <mark> <mark> [<mark> ...] [laps=<n>]      start it (laps: default 1)
--   endlua eb_patrol                                           stop it (a walk EB has started finishes on its own)

local marks, laps = {}, 1
for _, a in ipairs({ ... }) do
    local n = tostring(a):match("^laps=(%d+)$")
    if n then
        laps = tonumber(n)
    elseif tostring(a):match("^[%w_%-]+$") then
        marks[#marks + 1] = a
    else
        echo("eb_patrol: a mark name is one word: " .. tostring(a))
        return
    end
end
if #marks < 2 then
    echo("usage: lua eb_patrol <mark> <mark> [<mark> ...] [laps=<n>]")
    return
end

local START_WAIT = 4          -- seconds to see the walk start
local WALK_MAX = 180          -- seconds one walk may take
local function moving() return IS.Parse("${Me.IsMoving}") == "TRUE" end

-- one walk: EB walks it; this only watches you start and stop
local function walkTo(mark)
    IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd marks go " .. mark)
    if not waituntil(moving, START_WAIT) then
        echo("eb_patrol: no walk to " .. mark .. " (already there, no such mark in this zone, or the mesh has no way to it - EB says which in its console)")
        return
    end
    local still, spent = 0, 0
    while still < 1 and spent < WALK_MAX do
        wait(0.25)
        spent = spent + 0.25
        if moving() then still = 0 else still = still + 0.25 end
    end
end

echo(("eb_patrol: %d mark(s), %d lap(s) - endlua eb_patrol stops it"):format(#marks, laps))
for lap = 1, laps do
    for _, mark in ipairs(marks) do
        walkTo(mark)
        echo(("eb_patrol: lap %d, at %s"):format(lap, mark))
    end
end
echo("eb_patrol: done")
examples.expect: Walks to each mark in turn for the laps asked, says where it is after each walk, and ends on the last mark.
examples.run:
eb marks set alpha
eb marks set beta
lua eb_patrol alpha beta laps=2
endlua eb_patrol
needs: EB for InnerSpace running in this session (eb status answers)
each mark saved first with eb marks set <name>, standing on the spot, in this zone
a mesh for this zone (EB walks the mesh and nothing else: a mark the mesh has no route to is not walked to)

examples.title: Change an EB setting (complete script)
examples.summary: A drop-in script that changes one key in EB's settings file while EB is stopped (EB has no in-game set command yet): it checks EB's heartbeat, finds the file through EB's install, and checks the key, its kind and its range against EB's own settings catalog before it writes.
examples.code:
-- eb_setting.lua - change one of EB's settings, or read one. EB reads its settings file (eb-settings.json in the EB
-- folder) when it starts, so the file changes only while EB is stopped:
--   1. EB's heartbeat - the LavishScript variable EBISX_Beat EB rewrites several times a second - must stand still;
--   2. the EB folder comes from InnerSpace/Scripts/EBIS/boot.json (written by EB Setup), read with ISXLUA's cjson;
--   3. EB's own settings catalog (eb.ui.settings.settings, plain Lua in the EB folder) says whether the key exists, its
--      kind (on/off, a number with a range, one of a list) and its range;
--   4. the file is read, the one key changed, and the whole file written back.
--
--   lua eb_setting <key> <value>     change it (on/off for a switch; a number; one of the listed choices)
--   lua eb_setting <key>             read it

local key, value = ...
if not key then
    echo("usage: lua eb_setting <key> [<value>]")
    return
end

-- 1. EB must be stopped
IS.Execute("squelch declarevariable EBISX_Beat int64 global")      -- nothing changes when EB declared it already
local beat = IS.Parse("${EBISX_Beat}")
wait(1)
if IS.Parse("${EBISX_Beat}") ~= beat then
    echo("eb_setting: EB is running in this session - type eb stop, run this again, then start EB")
    return
end

-- 2. EB's folder
local cjson = require("cjson.safe")
local home = tostring(IS.Parse("${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}") or ""):gsub("\\", "/"):gsub("/+$", "")
local bf = io.open(home .. "/Scripts/EBIS/boot.json", "rb")
if not bf then
    echo("eb_setting: EB for InnerSpace is not installed in this InnerSpace (no Scripts/EBIS/boot.json)")
    return
end
local boot = cjson.decode(bf:read("*a") or "")
bf:close()
if type(boot) ~= "table" or type(boot.root) ~= "string" or boot.root == "" then
    echo("eb_setting: boot.json names no EB folder - run EB Setup again")
    return
end
local root = boot.root:gsub("\\", "/"):gsub("/+$", "")
local path = root .. "/eb-settings.json"

-- 3. the key, from EB's own catalog
package.path = root .. "/lua/?.lua;" .. root .. "/lua/?/init.lua;" .. package.path
local okC, catalog = pcall(require, "eb.ui.settings.settings")
local item = okC and type(catalog) == "table" and catalog.item(key) or nil
if okC and not item then
    echo("eb_setting: " .. key .. " is not an EB setting")
    return
end

-- 4. the file as it is (no file yet = every setting at its default)
local settings = {}
local rf = io.open(path, "rb")
if rf then
    local t = cjson.decode(rf:read("*a") or "")
    rf:close()
    if type(t) == "table" then settings = t end
end

if value == nil then
    local v = settings[key]
    if v == nil and item then
        echo(("eb_setting: %s = %s (the default)"):format(key, tostring(catalog.defaultOf(item))))
    else
        echo(("eb_setting: %s = %s"):format(key, tostring(v)))
    end
    return
end

-- the new value, in the key's own kind
local function asBool(s)
    s = tostring(s):lower()
    if s == "on" or s == "true" or s == "yes" or s == "1" then return true end
    if s == "off" or s == "false" or s == "no" or s == "0" then return false end
    return nil
end
local v
local kind = item and item.kind or nil
if kind == "bool" then
    v = asBool(value)
    if v == nil then echo("eb_setting: " .. key .. " is on or off"); return end
elseif kind == "num" then
    local n = tonumber(value)
    if not n then echo("eb_setting: " .. key .. " is a number"); return end
    v = catalog.snap(item, n)
    if v ~= n then
        echo(("eb_setting: %s takes %s to %s in steps of %s - set to %s"):format(key, item.min, item.max, item.step or 1, v))
    end
elseif kind == "cycle" or kind == "choice" then
    for _, c in ipairs(item.cycle or item.choice or {}) do
        if tostring(c):lower() == tostring(value):lower() then v = c end
    end
    if v == nil then
        echo("eb_setting: " .. key .. " is one of: " .. table.concat(item.cycle or item.choice or {}, ", "))
        return
    end
else
    v = tonumber(value) or asBool(value)
    if v == nil then v = value end
end

settings[key] = v
local wf = io.open(path, "wb")
if not wf then
    echo("eb_setting: cannot write " .. path)
    return
end
wf:write(cjson.encode(settings))
wf:close()
echo(("eb_setting: %s = %s - EB reads it when it starts"):format(key, tostring(v)))

lua eb_setting followDistance 12

members.name: Power
members.desc: Your power in percent, 0 to 100.

members.name: CurrentPower
members.desc: Your power points now.

members.name: MaxPower
members.desc: Your maximum power points.

members.name: IsHated
members.desc: TRUE while a fight is on you - the signal EB's combat follows.
members.notes: game.Me().inCombat. Prefer it to InCombat, which stays lit for a while after the fight.

members.name: InCombat
members.desc: The game's own in-combat flag; it stays TRUE for a while after a fight ends.

members.name: CastingSpell
members.desc: TRUE while your cast bar runs.
members.notes: game.Me().isCasting; the spell's name is GetGameData[Spells.Casting].Label (game.CastingName()).

members.name: IsMoving
members.desc: TRUE while you move.

members.name: IsDead
members.desc: TRUE while you are dead.

members.name: Grouped
members.desc: TRUE when you are in a group.

members.name: GroupCount
members.desc: How many are in your group, you included (1 when solo).

members.name: IsGroupLeader
members.desc: TRUE when you lead the group.

members.name: InRaid
members.desc: TRUE when you are in a raid.

members.name: RaidCount
members.desc: How many are in the raid.

members.name: InGameWorld
members.desc: TRUE in the world; FALSE at character select and while a zone loads.

members.name: OnMount
members.desc: TRUE while you are mounted.

members.name: IsStealthed
members.desc: TRUE while you are stealthed.

members.name: IsInvis
members.desc: TRUE while you are invisible.

members.name: AutoAttackOn
members.desc: TRUE while melee auto-attack is on.

members.name: InventorySlotsFree
members.desc: Free slots in your bags.

members.name: TSLevel
members.desc: Your tradeskill level.

members.name: Arcane
members.desc: Arcane detriments on you (also Noxious, Elemental, Trauma and Cursed, read the same way).
members.notes: game.Me().arcane and the others: the cure check.

members.name: NumAbilities
members.desc: How many abilities your knowledge book holds.

members.name: Ability[name]
members.desc: One ability by exact name (or Ability[id,N]): .ID, .IsReady, .TimeUntilReady, :Use, and .ToAbilityInfo with .Name, .CastingTime, .MaxRange.
members.cost: cheap for IsReady / TimeUntilReady; ToAbilityInfo is a server request
members.notes: Use game.AbilityReady and game.Cast: readiness of every ability you use is read in one batch a frame. The ability's name lives in ToAbilityInfo.Name, never on the ability itself.

members.name: CountMaintained
members.desc: How many maintained spells you keep up.

members.name: Maintained[n]
members.desc: One maintained spell: .Name, .Target (an actor), .TargetType, .Duration (-1 = no timer).
members.notes: game.Maintained() reads every row in one batch.

members.name: CountEffects
members.desc: How many effects are on you.

members.name: Effect[n].ID
members.desc: An effect's id. Read it once per new effect, never every frame.
members.cost: server request the first time an effect is asked about
members.notes: game.HasEffect / game.MyEffectNames keep each effect's id and name for you.

members.name: Effect[n].Type
members.desc: Beneficial or Detrimental.

members.name: Effect[n].ToEffectInfo.Name
members.desc: The effect's name.
members.cost: server request - read it once per effect id and keep it
members.notes: Never read it for every effect every frame: that floods the server.

members.name: Equipment[slot]
members.desc: A worn item by slot name (primary, chest, food, drink ...) or number: .Name, .ID, .Quantity, .IsReady, .AutoConsumeOn, :Use, :ToggleAutoConsume, and .ToItemInfo.Condition.
members.cost: cheap for the plain members; ToItemInfo is a server request

members.name: Inventory[ExactName,name]
members.desc: An item in your bags by exact name (Inventory[name] also matches part of a name): the same members as Equipment, and :Equip. Worn gear is never found here.
members.cost: cheap; ToItemInfo is a server request

members.name: GetGameData[key]
members.desc: A value the game's own interface shows, read as .Label - see the Me.GetGameData[key] entry for the keys EB has verified.

members.name: :QueryInventory
members.desc: Fill an index:item variable with your items by location: Me:QueryInventory[MyIndex, Location == "Inventory"].
members.cost: one command, then one read for the rows

members.name: X
members.desc: Your position (also Y and Z; Loc gives all three; Heading your facing in degrees).

tlos.name: Target
tlos.summary: Your current target - any actor member works on it.
tlos.when: Prefer game.Target(): it comes with the same batched read as game.Me(), so it costs nothing extra. With no target every ${Target...} reads NULL - not an error - and game.Target() answers nil. Target.Target is your target's target (the implied target).
tlos.cost: per-frame budget (shared with Me in the game layer)

members.name: ID
members.desc: The target's actor id (NULL with no target).

members.name: Name
members.desc: The target's name.

members.name: Type
members.desc: NPC, NamedNPC, PC, Corpse, Door, Special, Me ...
members.notes: A named reads Type NamedNPC: game.Target().isNamed.

members.name: Health
members.desc: The target's health in percent.

members.name: Distance
members.desc: Metres from you to the target.

members.name: Level
members.desc: The target's level.

members.name: Target
members.desc: What your target is targeting (Target.Target.Name ...).

members.name: IsDead
members.desc: TRUE once the target is dead.

tlos.name: Actor
tlos.summary: Any actor in the zone: Actor[id,N] by id (the fast, exact form), Actor[exactname,"Name"], or Actor["part of a name"] (the nearest match).
tlos.when: Use the game layer's actor functions - ActorPos, ActorDead, ActorHeading, ActorTarget, ControlCount - for one actor (one batched read per actor a frame), and NearestActor / ActorsNear / Lootables / Clickables to search; every search is one game query. Read Actor[id,N] yourself only for a member those do not return.
tlos.cost: per-frame budget (one read per actor; a search is two reads and two commands)

members.name: ID
members.desc: The actor's id.

members.name: Name
members.desc: The actor's name.

members.name: Type
members.desc: NPC, NamedNPC, PC, Pet, Corpse, Chest, Door, Special, NoKill NPC ...
members.notes: A query term too: 'Type == "NPC" || Type == "NamedNPC"' is how EB means an NPC.

members.name: Level
members.desc: The actor's level.

members.name: Health
members.desc: Health in percent.

members.name: Distance
members.desc: Metres from you.

members.name: IsDead
members.desc: TRUE once dead.

members.name: IsAggro
members.desc: TRUE when the actor is aggro on you.

members.name: InCombatMode
members.desc: TRUE while it is in combat.

members.name: IsHeroic
members.desc: TRUE for a heroic mob.

members.name: IsEpic
members.desc: How many groups an epic mob is meant for; 0 when it is not epic. A number, not TRUE / FALSE.

members.name: EncounterSize
members.desc: How many mobs are in its encounter.

members.name: ConColor
members.desc: Its con colour against you.

members.name: Target
members.desc: What the actor is targeting (Actor[id,N].Target.ID).

members.name: ThreatToMe
members.desc: How much it hates you.

members.name: Heading
members.desc: Its facing in degrees (X, Y, Z and Loc give its position).

members.name: CheckCollision
members.desc: FALSE when the line from you to it is clear; TRUE when something blocks it.
members.notes: game.Target().los and game.MobCasts() rows carry it already.

members.name: CollisionRadius
members.desc: The actor's size around its centre, for melee reach (CollisionScale scales it).

members.name: AbilityCastingID
members.desc: The id of the spell it is casting, 0 when none.
members.notes: game.MobCasts() lists the casters with their cast time (AbilityCastingTime).

members.name: IsStunnedOrMezzed
members.desc: TRUE while it is stunned or mezzed (IsFeared and IsRooted read the same way).

members.name: IsSwimming
members.desc: TRUE while it swims.

members.name: Interactable
members.desc: TRUE when it can be clicked (a door, a lever, a chest).
members.notes: A query term too; game.Clickables() uses it.

members.name: IsMerchant
members.desc: TRUE for a merchant or a mender.

members.name: NumEffects
members.desc: How many effects are on the actor.

members.name: :DoTarget
members.desc: Target it: Actor[id,N]:DoTarget. An object that cannot be targeted ignores it.

members.name: :DoubleClick
members.desc: Double-click it: open a door, loot a corpse, hail an NPC.

tlos.name: Me.Group[n]
tlos.summary: One slot of your group: Me.Group[0] is you, Me.Group[1] to Me.Group[5] the others. Any actor member works on a member who is in the zone.
tlos.when: Prefer game.Group(): it reads every slot in one batch a frame and already turns hit points into percent. A member in another zone reads ID 0 and has no distance - check InZone before you act on one.
tlos.cost: per-frame budget (one read for all five slots in the game layer)

members.name: Name
members.desc: The member's name (empty for an empty slot).

members.name: ID
members.desc: The member's actor id; 0 while the member is in another zone.

members.name: Class
members.desc: The member's class.

members.name: InZone
members.desc: TRUE when the member is in your zone.

members.name: HitPoints
members.desc: The member's health points now (MaxHitPoints is the maximum).

members.name: MaxHitPoints
members.desc: The member's maximum health points.

members.name: Health
members.desc: The member's health in percent.

members.name: CurrentPower
members.desc: The member's power points (MaxPower is the maximum).

members.name: Distance
members.desc: Metres from you; NULL when the member is in another zone.

members.name: IsDead
members.desc: TRUE while the member is dead.

members.name: Noxious
members.desc: Noxious detriments on the member (Arcane, Elemental, Trauma and Cursed read the same way).

tlos.name: Me.Raid[n]
tlos.summary: One member of your raid, the same members as a group slot.
tlos.when: Prefer game.Raid(myGroup, refreshSec): it reads the raid outside your own group at most every half second. Me.RaidCount says how many there are.
tlos.cost: per-frame budget (cached between refreshes in the game layer)

members.name: Name
members.desc: The raid member's name.

members.name: Health
members.desc: Health in percent.

members.name: HitPoints
members.desc: Health points now.

members.name: InZone
members.desc: TRUE when the member is in your zone.

members.name: IsDead
members.desc: TRUE while dead.

members.name: Class
members.desc: The member's class.

tlos.name: Zone
tlos.summary: The zone you are in: its display name and its short key.
tlos.when: ${Zone.Name} names the NEW zone as soon as a zone load STARTS, while the zone is not playable yet: never act on it until EQ2.Zoning reads 0 (game.Zoning() false) and you are in the world (game.InGame()). EB's own libraries key everything by the short name (game.Me().zoneShort).
tlos.cost: cheap (it comes with the game layer's Me read)

members.name: Name
members.desc: The zone's display name.

members.name: ShortName
members.desc: The zone's short key, the name EB's nav and data use.

tlos.name: EQ2
tlos.summary: The game itself: whether a zone is loading, and the actor query every search runs on.
tlos.when: Use game.Zoning() for the zoning check and the game layer's search functions (NearestActor, ActorsNear, Lootables, Clickables, the combat sweep) instead of running EQ2:QueryActors yourself.
tlos.cost: cheap (Zoning); a query is two commands and two reads

members.name: Zoning
members.desc: 0 when no zone is loading; anything else means a load is on. It reads -1 at character select.
members.notes: A number, not TRUE / FALSE. game.Zoning() turns it into a boolean (-1 and no answer count as zoning).

members.name: :QueryActors
members.desc: EQ2:QueryActors[MyIndex, <query>, ByDist] fills an index:actor variable with the matching actors, nearest first; read MyIndex.Used and MyIndex[n].<member>.
members.cost: one command, then one read for the rows
members.notes: Query terms are actor members with && || ! and == != < > <= >=. EB refuses a query that names a member it has not verified. The game layer's search functions do all of this for you.

tlos.name: ISXEQ2
tlos.summary: The game extension itself.
tlos.when: A stand-alone script waits for game.IsExtensionReady() (ISXEQ2 loaded and IsReady) before it reads anything. Inside EB the boot has already waited.
tlos.cost: cheap

members.name: IsReady
members.desc: TRUE once ISXEQ2 can answer game reads.
members.notes: Extension[ISXEQ2](exists) only says it is loaded; IsReady says it is ready.

tlos.name: Me.GetGameData[key]
tlos.summary: Values the game's own interface shows, read by key as Me.GetGameData[<key>].Label.
tlos.when: Only the keys below are verified; any other key is not sent. The two cast bars come with the game layer's Me read (game.CastingName(), game.TargetCasting()).
tlos.cost: cheap

members.name: Spells.Casting
members.desc: The spell on your cast bar ("" when none).

members.name: ImpliedTarget.Casting
members.desc: The spell your (implied) target is casting ("" when none).

members.name: Self.ExperienceCurrent
members.desc: Your experience on the current level, as the interface shows it.

members.name: Self.AscensionLevel
members.desc: Your ascension level.

members.name: Self.MentorLevel
members.desc: The level you are mentored to.

members.name: Self.BindLocation
members.desc: Where you are bound.

members.name: Self.Deity
members.desc: Your deity.

tlos.name: ChoiceWindow
tlos.summary: The game's yes / no popup: a rez offer, an invite, a zone-in or purchase question.
tlos.when: Use game.ChoiceWindow() (one batched read). ChoiceWindow(exists) reads TRUE or NULL. EB does not press its buttons yet: the button click is not verified, so a script must not assume a popup was answered.
tlos.cost: cheap

members.name: Text
members.desc: The question, read as ChoiceWindow.Text.GetProperty[LocalText].

members.name: Choice1
members.desc: The first button's label (Choice2 is the second).

members.name: Choice2
members.desc: The second button's label.

members.name: IsVisible
members.desc: TRUE while it shows.

tlos.name: ReplyDialog
tlos.summary: The classic NPC conversation window and its replies.
tlos.when: Use game.ReplyDialog() and game.ReplyChoose(n, d): they read the speech bubble first and this window when it is up. The replies are listed through Replies:GetOptions into a collection variable.
tlos.cost: cheap

members.name: Text
members.desc: What the NPC says.

members.name: Replies
members.desc: The replies, listed with Replies:GetOptions[MyCollection].

members.name: :Choose
members.desc: Pick reply n: ReplyDialog:Choose[n].

tlos.name: LootWindow
tlos.summary: The open loot window: its type and its items.
tlos.when: Read it only when a loot window is open: the game's loot event (eb.events LootOpened) or game.LootWindow() tells you. Asking with no window up is slow and gets slower in a long session; game.LootWindow() never asks on a quiet frame.
tlos.cost: cheap while a window is open; slow when none is

members.name: Type
members.desc: Free For All, Lotto, Need Before Greed, Leader ...

members.name: NumItems
members.desc: How many items the window holds.

members.name: Item[n].Name
members.desc: The name of item n.

members.name: :LootAll
members.desc: Take every item: LootWindow:LootAll.
members.notes: eb.economy.lootrules.decideWindow says when "lootall" is the right act.

tlos.name: RewardWindow
tlos.summary: The quest or kill reward window.
tlos.when: Use game.RewardWindow(): it tells a quest offer from a granted reward and a pick-one reward. Accepting is not verified yet, so game.AcceptReward answers false for now.
tlos.cost: cheap

members.name: NumRewards
members.desc: How many rewards it holds.

members.name: Reward[n]
members.desc: One reward row.

tlos.name: MerchantWindow
tlos.summary: An open merchant or mender window: what it sells and what it pays for your items.
tlos.when: Read it only while the window is open (IsVisible reads TRUE). Close it with game.CloseMerchantWindow().
tlos.cost: cheap

members.name: IsVisible
members.desc: TRUE while a merchant window is open.

members.name: NumMerchantItemsForSale
members.desc: How many rows the merchant sells.

members.name: MyInventory[name].Quantity
members.desc: How many of your bag item called name you hold.

members.name: MyInventory[name].PriceString
members.desc: What the merchant pays for one, as "0p,1g,20s,0c".

members.name: :Close
members.desc: Close the window: MerchantWindow:Close.

tlos.name: EQ2UIPage
tlos.summary: One page of the game's interface, read element by element: EQ2UIPage[window,page].Child[type,full.name].
tlos.when: Always name the element with its full name. Never walk a window's children by number or by type: those reads are unsafe and EB refuses them. The game layer reads the heroic wheel, the travel map, the zone picker and the Persona skills this way for you.
tlos.cost: cheap per element; batch the elements you need into one read

members.name: Child
members.desc: A named child element: .Child[page,_HUD.heroic], .Child[text,<full name>].

members.name: GetProperty
members.desc: A property of the element: GetProperty[visible], GetProperty[LocalText], GetProperty[Tooltip] ...

members.name: NumChildren
members.desc: How many children a named element has.

members.name: IsVisible
members.desc: TRUE while the page shows.

members.name: :LeftClick
members.desc: Click the element.

tlos.name: Extension
tlos.summary: InnerSpace's list of loaded extensions: ${Extension[ISXEQ2](exists)} is TRUE when ISXEQ2 is loaded.
tlos.when: Probe an extension BEFORE you read its TLO: reading the TLO of an extension that is not loaded prints an error on screen. EB's own nav checks its extension this way. Remember: (exists) reads TRUE or NULL, never FALSE.
tlos.cost: cheap

tlos.name: Session
tlos.summary: This InnerSpace session's name (${Session}, "is1", "is2" ...) - the id the crew relay knows a box by.
tlos.when: game.SessionName() reads it for you.
tlos.cost: cheap

tlos.name: Display
tlos.summary: The game window's own state.
tlos.when: game.IsForeground() reads Foreground for you.
tlos.cost: cheap

members.name: Foreground
members.desc: TRUE when this game window has the focus.

tlos.name: LavishScript
tlos.summary: InnerSpace's own information, such as the folder it runs from.
tlos.when: Never hard-code a folder: build a path from LavishScript.HomeDirectory, or from EB's own install folder (require("eb.platform").root()). Never name a LavishScript variable after a TLO - the variable hides the TLO and every script that reads it breaks.
tlos.cost: cheap

members.name: HomeDirectory
members.desc: The InnerSpace folder this session runs from.

tlos.name: EBNav
tlos.summary: EB's own mesh router, loaded as an InnerSpace extension on EB for InnerSpace. It plans routes over EB's own mesh for the zone you are in.
tlos.when: Scripts never read EBNav directly: use eb.navd (the same as require("eb.platform").nav()) or EB's walker (eb.nav). eb.navd checks that the extension is loaded before it asks anything, loads the zone's mesh off the frame, and turns every answer into plain Lua tables. When the extension is not there it says why instead of erroring.
tlos.cost: one read per question; a whole route is one read

members.name: Version
members.desc: Which version of the router answers (eb.navd checks it once).

members.name: Current
members.desc: Which zone's mesh is loaded.

members.name: LoadAsync
members.desc: Start loading a zone's mesh in the background (eb.navd.prepare does this).
members.cost: cheap; the load itself runs off the frame

members.name: Poll
members.desc: How a background load is going.

members.name: Path
members.desc: One route between two points, as a list of points (eb.navd.path / pathChained).

members.name: Page
members.desc: The rest of a very long route.

tlos.name: EBDiag
tlos.summary: EB's own diagnostics, loaded as an InnerSpace extension on EB for InnerSpace: how this session ends (where the game stopped if it went down, a freeze it never comes back from), the last freeze and where the stuck thread was, and what this PC is (the system, the processor, the memory, the graphics adapters, memory integrity).
tlos.when: Scripts never read EBDiag directly: eb fps machine, eb fps stalldump and eb debugreport show what it knows, through eb.ui.cmds.diag_native, which checks that the extension is loaded before it asks anything and keeps the answers that do not change. EB Boxer has the same built in (eb.diag).
tlos.cost: one read per question; the machine and the earlier sessions' notes are read once

members.name: Version
members.desc: Which version answers, and this process's id.

members.name: Machine
members.desc: The system and its build, the processor, the memory, the graphics adapters and memory integrity (HVCI).
members.cost: cheap; read once, the facts are gathered off the frame

members.name: Hang
members.desc: This session's last freeze: how long, whether it was EB's own frame, where the stuck thread was.
